title: cognate clustering over-merges: mega-clusters (up to 1542) pollute era-grid modern reflexes with unrelated words
description: USER QA (prod, post grid-fill): -don/-bury/-well/-bank/green etc. show MODERN reflexes full of unrelated junk words ('-don has a ton of just words', 'Grey isn't a reflex of green', 'random modern bullshit'). ROOT CAUSE: the cognate clustering (cluster-cognates-v1) over-merges. dūn (hill) cognate_id 11720 has 280 members grouping dūn with dew/deaw, dusk, Sanskrit धूम्र (dhūmra=smoke), Greek hypothymia/-thymia — totally unrelated words clustered by loose phonological/PIE-root similarity. era_reflexes (source=cluster) faithfully render the garbage cluster. SCALE: 137631 clusters, median size 2 (healthy), BUT a mega-cluster tail — 27 clusters >500 members (max 1542), 155 >200, 384 >100. Common toponym roots (dūn/burg/don) land in these mega-clusters, so the most-seen morphemes show the worst garbage. PRE-EXISTING: identical in the pre-fold bundle (/tmp/runtime-final.db) — NOT caused by wyrd-v3ow.1 folds / era-grid self-seed (wyrd-q1yp) / same-meaning merge (wyrd-j8ok). Those grid-population fixes EXPOSED it: before, these grids were empty (hiding the garbage); now they populate and show it. FIX OPTIONS: (a) re-cluster with tighter cluster-cognates-v2 (the real fix — substantial); (b) interim: filter/cap era_reflexes export to exclude implausible reflexes (cluster size cap, edit-distance/plausibility gate to the morpheme); (c) gate the self-seed/grid-fill until clustering is fixed. Owner: cognate_cluster.py + the era_reflex export.

title: Step 2: soft position-plausibility scoring from known/pre-split breakdowns (rank, never reject)
description: Add a SOFT scoring term so prospective parses of UNKNOWN toponyms are ranked by per-morpheme position frequency learned from the KNOWN (scholar-attributed / is_canonical) breakdowns. Statistically-weird positions lower a parse's rank but never disqualify it. Compose with the existing (fewest-unaccounted, fewest-morphemes) credibility score. Part of wyrd-eyjk.
notes:
DESIGN ANALYSIS (pre-implementation, 2026-06-01).

Step 1 (remove gates) cannot ship without step 2: removing _location_allows reintroduces exactly the boundary artifacts wyrd-zewx's strict-inner gate was added to PREVENT (donhole / nwydmillate — an inner morpheme matching at a word boundary). So the existing scorer (unaccounted, morpheme_count, first_pos, longer-leading) is NOT sufficient on its own; position-plausibility must compensate. 1+2 are coupled.

The fork — three sub-decisions for the soft scorer:

(A) STATS SOURCE / SCOPE. Per-(morpheme-surface, position) frequencies. Source = the KNOWN/pre-split breakdowns (is_canonical rows on toponym_decomposition + toponym_etymology element ordinals). Open: build-time-only (compute in _compute_proportions_inline from L3, score the heuristic decomposition of UNKNOWN corpus toponyms; NO bundle change, NO runtime change) — RECOMMENDED — vs also runtime (would require shipping a position-stats table in the L4 bundle so the explainer ranks the same way; larger, schema change).

(B) COMPOSITION. Position-plausibility as a soft term sorted AFTER (unaccounted, morpheme_count) — i.e. it only discriminates among equally-credible parses, never overriding a fewer-unaccounted/fewer-morpheme parse. RECOMMENDED. (Replaces/augments the current first_pos + longer-leading tiebreakers.)

(C) NEVER-REJECT. Confirmed by user: position only ranks candidates, never filters. A statistically-weird placement (don-at-front) stays a candidate, just ranked below less-weird parses.

Confining step 2 to build-time (A=build-only) avoids a bundle-schema change and keeps the runtime explainer on the simpler scorer (fine — it surfaces all readings anyway). That's the tractable path.

Step 3 (collapse -andrew/Andrew-/andrew → one morpheme; derived position into structures+buckets; retire the load_parts double-register + _matches_position bare-permissive workarounds) follows once 1+2 land.

BLOCKING QUESTION for the user: confirm (A) build-time-only + (B) tiebreaker-after-credibility + (C) never-reject, or specify a different design. Surfaced 2026-06-01; not implementing until confirmed (auto-merging a bundle-wide ranking change guessed overnight is the wrong risk).

title: Morpheme position is a match-time ENFORCER, not a derived label — corrupts prospective toponym parses
description:
The matcher treats a morpheme's stored dash-position (Meaning.location: pre/post/inner, decoded from -x / x- / -x-) as a HARD CONSTRAINT on matching. This is backwards and produces clearly-bad parses.

CORRECT MODEL (user intent / rando / D39):
1. Two toponym classes: (a) KNOWN / pre-split — scholar-attributed breakdowns; ground truth AND the source of position evidence. (b) UNKNOWN — every split is PROSPECTIVE; could be 2 morphemes, could be 15; we don't know.
2. Match morpheme STRINGS (dash-stripped) against the toponym. The trie ALREADY does this (build_morpheme_trie keys by usage.lower().replace('-','')). Position (bare/pre/post/inner) is a LABEL DERIVED from the span (sole=bare, first=pre, last=post, mid=inner), NOT a match constraint.
3. 'inner-only' is an artifact of limited evidence, not a property of the morpheme. Position-rarity is SOFT evidence against SELECTING a parse (statistical weight), NEVER grounds to REJECT it outright. e.g. don-at-front ('donhole') must remain a candidate even if attested 1x front / 50x middle — if the toponym has less-weird parses those should outrank it, but the weird one stays on the list. History/word-morphing is real.

SYMPTOMS: lone 'Andrew' matches suffix -andrew instead of bare Andrew; redundant per-position entries (-andrew / Andrew- / andrew) for ONE morpheme; saint/personal-name leak into base generation; known positions wrongly enforced on unrelated prospective parses; two-word toponyms dropped (Mount Pleasant) when a word's only form is dashed.

ROOT CAUSE SITES: trie_matcher._location_allows (DAG-walk filter), vector_name_select._matches_position (vector path twin). Both reject string-matches whose stored dash doesn't fit the span. The trie itself is NOT the bug.

This is the wyrd-5z5j parent's core defect. User: highest priority, wants it solved.
notes:
MODEL (authoritative — see DECISIONS D40 + memory 'morpheme-position-is-derived-not-matched'; corrected 5+ times across sessions):

Position is an OUTPUT of decomposition, never an input. Morpheme identity = bare surface (giles); Giles-/-giles/giles are the SAME morpheme at a derived position, not variants to match/select. Do NOT gate matching by Meaning.location.

Three layers:
1. Scholarly (is_canonical) splits → per-(morpheme,position) frequency PRIOR. Only role of position stats: a credibility tiebreaker.
2. Decompose real-town corpus by STRING match only; when several breakdowns viable, a heuristic grounded in the Layer-1 prior selects the most credible; RECORD (morpheme, derived-position) increments (Stokegiles→Stoke-(pre)+1, -giles(post)+1). A word-final morpheme records -post regardless of stored variant. These increments ARE the proportions.
3. Generation samples per-morpheme position likelihoods.

Recurring error to avoid: forcing the stored dash-location into town-name deconstruction (as a match gate or variant-selector).

String-only matching, position derived from span + recorded as (morpheme,derived-position), per-position bucket frequency, bare-surface resolution. Rate holds (English 27%), saint-leak fixed, suite green. Follow-ups: wyrd-vidi (vector-mode realism alignment), complexity/perf ticket.

title: derive-surface-in-modern ignores the reflex table — eni4 scholar reflexes don't reach decomposition
description:
The eni4 scholar-morpheme campaign raised scholar-reflex coverage from 14.7% to 81.5% (1,307 -> 7,253 scholar etymons with a mined modern reflex). But toponym CANONICAL decomposition coverage did NOT improve — it dropped 26,066 -> 25,847 after the rebuild, and surface_in_modern stayed flat (4,034 -> 4,022 elements).

ROOT CAUSE (wiring gap): period_form.py::_suffix_candidates_for_etymon builds the 'known reflex' candidate set for the suffix-anchoring alignment from (a) etymon.canonical_form, (b) cognate-cluster canonical_forms (etymon WHERE cognate_id=?), and (c) etymon_variant rows — but it NEVER queries the reflex / reflex_etymon table. So the modern reflex surfaces the eni4 campaign mined into the reflex table (e.g. OE tūn -> ton/tone/oulton) are invisible to derive_surface_in_modern. The pass instead matches modern toponym-name suffixes against OE inflectional variants (tūn/tūnas/tūne), which almost never suffix-match a modern name. Example: 'Houghton' ends in 'ton' (a reflex.surface_form) but matches nothing in tūn's variant set, so hough+ton never aligns.

EFFECT: the whole eni4 reflex investment doesn't translate into scholar-source decomposition. Candidate decompositions even grew (+56k) from the new surfaces feeding the runtime matcher, but the canonical/scholar selection can't use them, so canonical coverage went DOWN (more ambiguity, no new confident picks).

FIX: add reflex.surface_form (joined via reflex_etymon for the etymon, position='post'/'pre' as appropriate) to the candidate set in _suffix_candidates_for_etymon — for the surface_in_modern (modern-name) projection in particular, the reflex surfaces are the RIGHT input (etymon_variant OE inflections are the wrong input for a modern name). VALIDATE against the over-decomposition risk the decomposition_export.py:67 comment warns about (short reflex surfaces like 'own' could add ambiguity) and confirm canonical-decomposition coverage rises, not falls. Likely also re-run derive-surface-in-modern + re-grade.

Discovered during the 2026-06-23 post-merge rebuild. Relates to the eni4 epic (the campaign's reflexes can't pay off in decomposition until this is wired).
close_reason: Fixed by #741 (squash 5e6899cf): derive-surface-in-modern now reads reflex.surface_form via reflex_etymon for the modern-name projection, with a composite-reflex filter that keeps phonetic-reduction base forms + compares diacritic-stripped. surface_in_modern +19.7% (4022→4816) with correct boundaries.

title: Authoring loop: the week-long /loop ride (phase1 existing->senses, phase2 scholar-grounded gloss unglossed, phase3 overflow)
description:
The /loop ride on the campaign branch (own long-lived branch + single PR, NEVER merges; a human reviews + merges on return). Depends on .A rail landing first.

PER-FIRE (15-min cron, fill ~10 min, run MULTIPLE chunks if a chunk finishes early):
1. git pull --rebase.
2. PHASE 1 (existing glosses -> senses): sense-next-slice --n N -> a Task subagent does the clustering judgment (model=opus, or shell to an Ollama model — tune for quality) -> sense-validate (exit 0 or fix/drop, never bypass) -> append canonicalization/ ledgers -> commit+push. Repeat chunks to fill the interval.
3. PHASE 2 (when phase 1 next-slice empty): gloss-unglossed-next-slice -> SCHOLAR-GROUNDED gloss only (consensus over toponym-etymology glosses); PARK over-segmentation fragments + no-consensus morphemes, NEVER invent -> validate -> campaign-local gloss ledger -> then canonicalize the freshly-glossed set via the phase-1 path.
4. PHASE 3 (overflow, when 1+2 empty): same work across the FULL morpheme inventory (drop the impact>=2 restriction), still grounded + parked.
5. Track: sense-status each fire -> append epic (wyrd-u6fn.10) notes. Real readable-meaning check needs a rebuild+project (expensive) -> milestones only.

INVARIANTS (don't relax): remainder from the committed ledger not the live DB (wyrd-1rw4); author to L2 ledgers via the validate gate; park ambiguous/fragment, never guess; one PR, no merge; campaign-local gloss ledger so the eni4.3 cron never collides. Model + prompt are free knobs — adjust to improve quality, stamp provenance (D24).
notes: LAUNCHING as a fixed 5-min /loop in-session (Opus does the clustering judgment, method=opus-gloss-sense-v1). Phase 1 (existing glosses->senses) then Phase 3 (--full-inventory); Phase 2 (gloss the unglossed) is SKIPPED for now (authoring verb not built — park/skip the unglossed cohort) per owner: phase 1+3 are >1 week of work. Seed fire (9 morphemes) already on the branch. Runbook: COMPRESSED_GLOSS_CAMPAIGN.md. Branch enrichment/compressed-gloss-campaign, PR #737, never merges.

title: Rail: gloss->canonical-sense authoring pass + sense-next-slice/validate/status + projection wiring (attended build)
description:
NET-NEW engineering that MUST land (attended) before the loop runs unattended. The discipline: structural/code changes are never authored by the blind loop. Three parts, all on the campaign branch, ruff + pytest green:

(1) PROJECTION WIRING — canonicalization_projection.py. Turn on the same-sense binds the projection currently counts as skipped_unsupported (the docstring-reserved deferred slot): add "etymon_gloss" to _SUBJECT_TARGET; define a gloss ref convention (etymon natural-key + US-separator + gloss text); add an etymon_gloss branch to _resolve_binds; add a COMPOSITE-PK bind-write path in _write_projection (current path assumes a single-column id, but etymon_gloss PK is (etymon_id, gloss)). same-sense = identity (mint+bind); NO new PREDICATES entry. Tests: a same-sense bind projects onto etymon_gloss.canonical_sense_id; a polysemous morpheme yields >1 sense; D46 conflict (gloss bound to 2 hubs) left unbound + flagged.

(2) AUTHORING PASS — fork duplicate_canonical_mining.py + cli/lexicon/mine_duplicate_canonicals.py. Per morpheme: take its etymon_gloss wall, cluster into DISTINCT senses (multi-way, not the finder's pairwise A/B) and synthesize one SHORT label per sense. Deterministic gloss-token pre-screen; LLM propose -> adversarial refute; confidence-gated (>=high to author; D46 leave-separate default = collapse to ONE sense unless real polysemy evidence). Emit per cluster: mint-canonical(canonical_sense) + bind(etymon_gloss->hub, kind=same-sense) + canonical-label(canonical_sense, value=short label, stratum) into the canonicalization/ per-predicate ledgers; one audit row per judged morpheme for idempotency (model on _duplicate_canonical_audit.jsonl). LLM via OllamaClient.chat_json (gemma4:26b default; model a CLI knob). method="gloss-sense-cluster-v1", provenance quad stamped (D24).

(3) RAIL CLI — a sibling enrich-campaign-style module (add_to(parent)). sense-next-slice (reuse _band_cohort impact>=2 fast selector; remainder via ledger_refs over the COMMITTED sense ledger, NOT live DB — wyrd-1rw4; emits morpheme + its gloss wall + toponym evidence); sense-validate (shape: _type, ref resolves, >=1 sense, non-empty short label, dedup vs committed); sense-status (committed sense-coverage scoreboard over the cohort); park (campaign-local _sense_parked.jsonl, mirror the reflex park). Phase-2 verbs: gloss-unglossed-next-slice (scholar toponym-etymology gloss evidence for unglossed generation-eligible morphemes) + its validate, writing the campaign-local gloss ledger with a DISTINCT _type (NOT etymon_gloss_add). Tests for every verb.

Reusable helpers (verbatim): etymon_ref / resolve_etymon_ref (etymon_refs.py), ledger_refs (enrichment_campaign.py:621), _band_cohort (:642), fold_surface, _nfc, append_assertion / load_assertions / mint_canonical_id (assertions.py).
notes: RAIL BUILT + PR #737 (branch enrichment/compressed-gloss-campaign). Done + validated on the real 4.3GB DB: projection wiring (same-sense etymon_gloss->canonical_sense), gloss_sense clustering+authoring (monosemy-biased), gloss-campaign CLI (next-slice/validate/author/status/park), runbook + 5-min /loop prompt. next-slice 0.43s, impact-ordered (tūn=2993). Phase-1 cohort=2969 glossed impact>=2 morphemes. 115 related tests pass, ruff clean. REMAINING (not launch-blocking): phase-2 scholar-gloss AUTHORING verb (loop parks unglossed until then), A/B harness. Launch mechanism: /loop 5m with the runbook's loop prompt.

title: Band-by-band holistic morpheme uplift (loop-driven)
description:
Reframe of the scholar-morpheme campaign (supersedes the reflex-only eni4.1 loop): take the scholar-referenced morphemes (best decomposition ground-truth) and lift each to FULL capability across all dimensions, working one impact band at a time top-down. Loop OWNS reflex+tag+IPA+gloss (each authors to its L2 ledger via a validation gate); lemma-wiring+cognate+variant stay HUMAN-GATED (structural/decision-gated: wyrd-740t, over-merge bugs, lemma-wiring at 3.5%).

Rationale: the original intent was holistic per-morpheme quality, but the loop ran reflex-only for ~52 iterations. Snapshot of the impact>=2 cohort (3,118 morphemes): gloss 95%, IPA 84%, reflex(ledger) 69%, tag 52%, cognate 40%, variant 30%, lemma 3.5%. Reflexes for impact>=3 are fully done; band-by-band now front-loads the remaining dimensions (mostly tags) on the highest-impact morphemes first.

Rail (PR #727): enrich-campaign {next-slice,tags-next-slice,ipa-next-slice,gloss-next-slice} --impact N + {validate,tags-validate,ipa-validate,gloss-validate} + bands (per-band gap counts driving descent). Runbook: ENRICHMENT_CAMPAIGN.md 'CURRENT MODEL'.
notes:
CAN-IT RE-GRADE RESULT (rebuild measured locally, fire #167-era ledgers, corpus=15265 toponyms). Live DB never mutated — all rebuilds into temp DBs.

HEADLINE: rebuilding from current campaign ledgers lifts CAN-IT subset-recall 6.2% (deployed live DB) → 8.8% (rebuilt), +2.6pp / +43% relative / +404 toponyms. The rebuild IS worth deploying.

CONTROL (rebuild with _reflexes.jsonl excluded): CAN-IT = 0.0% on all metrics → reflexes are the ENTIRE matcher surface inventory; without them the 4091-morpheme trie matches nothing. Validates the campaign premise.

EXACT-SET-EQUALITY: 0.8% (live) → 0.4% (rebuilt) — a <1% noise-dominated precision metric; dips as added surfaces raise recall while diluting strict exact-equality (designed recall/precision tension, not a regression). DID-WE subset 4.8%→7.2%.

STRUCTURAL: matcher trie = 4091 morphemes regardless of bulk (skip-bulk == with-bulk) → CAN-IT is bulk-independent; --skip-bulk rebuild (20min) is a valid grading basis. Genitive priors don't affect CAN-IT (only DID-WE tiebreak).

BUG FIXED (committed 6dc390b9, PR #727): _reflex_parked.jsonl (git-tracked, non-conforming) was missing from REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS → rebuild-from-jsonl raised ReplayError AND left test_no_unhandled_nonconforming_ledgers red in CI. Fix unblocks the post-trip rebuild.

ARTIFACTS (local, ~/.wyrd/): lexicon_canit_test.db (with reflexes, priors applied), lexicon_canit_noreflex.db (control). scratch/canit_{baseline,after,control}.txt have full grades. NEXT (human): if deploying, rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment on the live DB (now unblocked) + mine-genitive-priors --apply; optional pre-session-baseline rebuild for finer per-session attribution; eyeball the exact-set dip.

title: Variant / alt-spelling uplift for accepted morphemes (the 'barthos' spread)
description: Biggest, safest uplift: 2,177 admit-cohort morphemes (69.8%) have NO variant. Each loop iteration authors the attested ALTERNATIVE surface spellings of an accepted morpheme as variants — the spread a single reflex misses (tūn: ton/tone/don; Bartholomew: barthol/bartle as realized in place-names). Grounded: every variant must appear in an attested toponym form (validate gate). Author to the spelling-variant ledger; relates to wyrd-740t (promote surface_in_modern into the D18 pool) and wyrd-gz66 (Briggs attested-form variants) — coordinate, don't duplicate. Improves recall (matcher recognizes more spellings) AND generation (worn-down forms). Decision to inherit from 740t: the toponymic-surface tag convention so variants don't leak as standalone names.

title: Rail extension: variant + tag next-slice/validate (mirror the reflex rail)
description:
Extend wyrd-eni4.1.1's enrich-campaign CLI with per-dimension primitives for the uplift track, mirroring the reflex rail:

  enrich-campaign next-slice --phase variants|tags --n N
    Next N impact-ordered admit-cohort etymons MISSING that dimension (remainder from the COMMITTED ledger: variants from etymon_variant/_<variants ledger>, tags from data/mining/_tags.jsonl), each with grounding evidence (toponyms + surface spans for variants; gloss for tags).
  enrich-campaign validate --phase variants|tags --candidates f.jsonl
    Variants: GROUNDING GUARD identical to reflexes — an alt-spelling must appear in an attested toponym form of the etymon (the 'barthos' rule). Tags: every tag is in the controlled vocabulary (44 + kinship); 'none' is a valid recorded outcome; no tag sprawl.
  Reuse next_slice/validate scaffolding from enrichment_campaign.py; per-phase remainder + grounding/vocab guard. Park support for un-authorable etymons. Tests + ruff. Blocks the variant/tag uplift phases.
notes: Tag half of the rail extension built + in PR #727 (tags-next-slice/validate/status; fast admit-CTE cohort). Variant half DEFERRED — blocked on the wyrd-740t toponymic-surface tag-convention decision, so not loop-safe unattended.

title: Accepted-morpheme quality uplift (loop-driven)
description:
Sibling track to wyrd-eni4.1 (reflex coverage). Where eni4.1 gives reflex-LESS morphemes a reflex, THIS track raises the quality of the morphemes already ACCEPTED into generation — the 'admit cohort' (_BREAKDOWN_ADMIT_MIN_TOPONYMS = 2: breakdown elements used in >=2 distinct toponyms), N=3,118. Same loop-driven, grounded, slice-at-a-time pattern; same safe-ledger + grounding-guard + park discipline.

Measured gaps in the admit>=2 cohort (2026-06-21):
- variant / alt-spelling:  2,177 missing (69.8%)  <- biggest, safest, grounded ('barthos' spread)
- cognate clustering:      1,870 missing (60.0%)  <- biggest VALUE but RISKIEST (see caution)
- tag:                     1,500 missing (48.1%)  <- controlled vocab, existing infra
- gloss:                     149 missing ( 4.8%)  <- near-complete (no dedicated ticket)
- IPA:                       ~tiny tail           <- near-complete

CAUTION (cognate): the cognate-cluster space has ACTIVE P1 over-merge bugs (wyrd-rd69, wyrd-6hbv, wyrd-vewk; epic wyrd-3vju). New binds authored unattended could worsen over-merge. The cognate uplift is therefore guarded / NOT a default blind-loop target — conservative, grounded same-morpheme binds only, parking anything ambiguous, and aware of those bugs.

Order: rail extension (variant+tag next-slice/validate, mirror the reflex rail) -> variant uplift -> tag uplift -> cognate uplift (guarded). Gloss/IPA tails are folded in as cleanup, not dedicated tickets. Existing related tickets linked: wyrd-740t, wyrd-gz66, wyrd-v3ow (variants); wyrd-t0vw, wyrd-wohr (tags); wyrd-feeq, wyrd-3vju (cognate).

title: Phase 1: author grounded reflexes for the ~7.6k reflex-less scholar etymons (impact-ordered)
description:
The coverage lever. Only 14.5% (1,296/8,939) of scholar etymons have a reflex; the matcher can only recover a morpheme that has one, which is why recall~0.205 / coverage~0.286. Each loop iteration: take the next impact-ordered slice (enrich-campaign next-slice), and for each etymon author the modern-English surface realization(s) ACTUALLY OBSERVED in its toponyms (the 'Bartholomew\'s -> barthos' / tun -> ton / lea -> ley / steinn -> stain pattern), with position, appending {_type:reflex, surface_form, position, etymon_refs:[lang:form]} to data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl. Grounded only — surface must appear in an attested toponym form (validation gate enforces). Where surface_in_modern is already populated, ingest it directly; where it is NULL, align the morpheme to the attested town spans.

Progress = (scholar etymons with a reflex ref in committed _reflexes.jsonl) / 8,939, logged to the ticket notes each batch. Periodic (nightly) rebuild+grade snapshot tracks the coverage delta. Park ambiguous/low-confidence cases (support<2, no clean residual span) rather than guessing.
notes: Iter 52: +47 reflexes / 34 morphemes, 6 parked. Coverage ~29.5%.

title: Campaign rail: scoped grounded reflex/variant writer + ledger-remainder + validation gate
description:
The harness the enrichment loop rides. A small, tested module (wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/enrichment_campaign.py + cli/lexicon/enrich_campaign.py) exposing two loop primitives:

  enrich-campaign next-slice --phase reflexes --n 20
    Emit the next N scholar etymons that still need the phase's data, IMPACT-ORDERED (descending by # of distinct toponyms the etymon appears in, so the highest-coverage morphemes go first), each with grounding evidence: lang:form, gloss(es), the toponyms it appears in (modern_name + historical_form + surface_in_modern span), current reflexes/variants/tags. 'Remaining' is computed from the COMMITTED _reflexes.jsonl (ref set), NOT the live DB (reproducibility trap, wyrd-1rw4).

  enrich-campaign validate
    Gate freshly-appended records before commit: JSONL parses; ref resolves to a real etymon (lang:form); GROUNDING GUARD — a reflex surface_form must be a substring of >=1 attested toponym form (modern_name/historical_form/surface_in_modern) for that etymon (stops invented, precision-wrecking reflexes); dedup vs existing ledger; position in {pre,post,inner}.

Writes go to data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl (reflex projection) via the SAFE scoped path — never dump_all_sources (wyrd-tg0f). Ruff-clean + a focused test or two. This unblocks every later phase.

title: Scholar-morpheme enrichment campaign (loop-driven)
description:
Loop-driven enrichment of the ~8,939 etymons referenced by the scholarly toponym breakdowns — the morphemes we have the BEST decomposition ground-truth for, and the set the grade-decomposition grader scores against. Goal: raise decomposition COVERAGE (currently recall~0.205, coverage~0.286 on 15,265 graded toponyms) by closing the reflex gap first, then a broad quality sweep.

Baseline quality of the 8,939 scholar etymons (2026-06-21): has-reflex 14.5% (THE coverage lever — matcher can only recover a morpheme that has a reflex), cognate-clustered 29.9%, tagged 33.9%, has-variant 19.3%; gloss 89.2% / IPA 72.3% already good.

Root finding: the scholar corpus ALREADY records the surface realization (toponym_etymology_element.surface_in_modern) for the highest-frequency morphemes — old-english:tun->'ton', lea->'ley', old-norse:steinn->'stain' — yet these carry NO reflex, because the only writer (mine-implied-reflexes --apply via dump_all_sources) is blocked by a durability bug (wyrd-tg0f: drops 7,327 attestation rows on rebuild). SAFE PATH (this campaign): append grounded reflexes directly to data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl (the scoped, reviewable ledger that shipped at support>=3), bypassing dump_all_sources.

Operating constraints (load-bearing): (1) compute 'remaining work' from the COMMITTED ledgers, never the live mutated DB — the live DB carries locally-applied-but-uncommitted reflexes, so a live-DB remainder is wrong + non-reproducible (wyrd-1rw4 reproducibility trap). (2) Author grounded data where safe; PARK anything needing an engineering decision (e.g. 740t tag-convention, dxtn admit-criteria) as a ticket — never guess unattended. (3) All work lands on ONE long-lived branch / ONE PR the loop keeps updating; nothing merges unattended.

Phases: P1 rail (scoped writer + ledger-remainder + validation gate) -> P1 reflex authoring (impact-ordered) -> P2 toponymic-surface variants (wyrd-740t) -> P3 quality sweep (tags / direct gloss wyrd-dxtn / IPA wyrd-32t1).

title: rebuild-from-jsonl globs audit logs into replay → from-scratch rebuild broken
description: jsonl_paths_in() globs ALL data/mining/*.jsonl into build_from_jsonl's replay, including the audit-only verdict logs. 3 of them (_cluster_reflex_audit, _descent_audit, _toponym_reflex_audit) carry a _type not registered in jsonl/log.py LIST_TYPES, and _reflex_audit.jsonl carries NO _type at all (4552 bare rows) — so from-scratch rebuild-from-jsonl raises ReplayError on the first audit file (discovered building a side DB for wyrd-xdam.5 Phase 2). Audit logs are idempotency/audit-only (effects live in _collapses/_curation/_reflexes which ARE replayed), so the fix is to EXCLUDE *_audit.jsonl from jsonl_paths_in (uniform, future-proof). _tags.jsonl stays (not *_audit). Blocks the xdam.5 side-build + breaks reconstructibility repo-wide.

title: Data bug: toponym_etymology_element.ordinal is gloss/head-first order, not modern-surface order — weakens the decomposer ground-truth corpus
EPIC: Compressed-gloss campaign (loop-driven) — gloss walls -> canonical senses + readable toponym meaning
description:
Loop-driven realization of the D50-deferred COMPRESSED GLOSS (DECISIONS D50 "Bounded by": "a short canonical label per sense — the readable 'what does this toponym mean' output — rides on the canonical_sense nodes"). Rescoped from the single-ticket u6fn.10 into a loop campaign that mirrors the eni4 enrichment-campaign machinery (ENRICHMENT_CAMPAIGN.md): own long-lived branch + single PR (NEVER merges), 15-min cron / ~10-min fires / fill-the-time-with-another-chunk / park-on-problems / remainder-from-COMMITTED-ledger-not-live-DB (wyrd-1rw4).

GOAL: render readable toponym meaning by composing ONE short token per morpheme slot ('New'+'Town'); polysemy = a small array, one label per DISTINCT sense ('wall' OR 'frog'). Today only raw etymon_gloss walls + a morpheme-side etymon_gloss_canonical VIEW exist; NO compressed/short gloss anywhere (confirmed).

SUBSTRATE (verified present 2026-06-22, mostly built): canonical_sense table (migration 0019, (id, merged_into)), etymon_gloss.canonical_sense_id FK + index, canonical_label CHECK includes canonical_sense, assertion model has canonical_sense node type + same-sense bind kind (mint prefix CS), generic mint/merge/LABEL projection paths (sense labels flow for free). clear_canonical_graph already NULLs canonical_sense_id. NET-NEW = the authoring pass + the ONE deferred projection slot (etymon_gloss bind) + the rail + presentation.

MODEL: same-sense is IDENTITY (mint a canonical_sense hub + bind etymon_gloss->hub kind=same-sense), NOT a new predicate. Per-sense canonical-label = the short compressed gloss. Monosemous wall (tun's ~20 variants) -> one sense -> one label 'town'. Polysemous -> N senses -> N labels.

PHASE LADDER (loop never idles, "do not stop"):
- Phase 1: EXISTING glosses, generation-eligible (impact>=2), impact-ordered -> cluster gloss wall into senses + short label. Park ambiguous.
- Phase 2: UNGLOSSED generation-eligible -> scholar-grounded glosses (consensus over scholar toponym-etymology glosses); PARK over-segmentation fragments, NEVER invent (D51.2 gloss-blind rule + wyrd-dxtn's finding that naive LLM glossing of the fragment-heavy unglossed set produces garbage). Then canonicalize the freshly-glossed set.
- Phase 3 (overflow): same work across the FULL morpheme inventory (~731K) once 1+2 burn down.

COEXISTENCE: campaign-local gloss ledger + a DISTINCT _type so the eni4.3 cron's gloss-next-slice (which owns _type=etymon_gloss_add in _curation.jsonl over the no-gloss cohort) never collides.

MODEL KNOB + A/B: per-fire judgment can be done by Opus (a Task subagent to keep loop context clean, stamped model=opus) OR any Ollama model on the Mac. Candidates: gemma4:26b (default), qwen3.5:9b, qwen3:8b, gemma3n:e4b, qwen2.5:7b. SKIP qwen3.5:35b-a3b (owner: "all but unusable"). A/B testing of models AND prompts is in scope — build a small eval harness over a labeled sample of gloss walls so the loop can compare variants and pick the winner. Free to tune model + prompt to improve quality; provenance stamps record which did what (D24).

Children: .A rail (attended build, THIS session) -> .B authoring loop (the week ride) -> .C presentation (human-gated renderer). Under epic wyrd-u6fn (Class B). Loop-pattern kin of wyrd-eni4.3. Folds in wyrd-dxtn as Phase 2.

Added proper-noun auto-park to speed ME/Latin bands. ~555 multi-word remain. Cron 4225a77c, PR #737.

title: Assertion schema + append-only L2 JSONL stream(s)
description: Reified edge: (subject, predicate, object, confidence, method, source, actor, rationale, timestamp). Append-only; supersede via tombstone assertion, never edit. Decide one stream vs per-predicate JSONL (lean per-predicate, mirroring _reflexes.jsonl/_element_glosses.jsonl so the rebuild-runbook + rebuild-runbook-currency-reviewer track each). Decide canonical-entity identity: synthetic canonical node (winner can change without rewriting refs — D31 UNIQUE-key lesson) vs winner-takes-redirect (current merged_into_id).
design:
ASSERTION SCHEMA + L2 STREAMS — FIRST CUT (2026-06-16). Builds on u6fn.1 taxonomy.

DECISION: SYNTHETIC CANONICAL NODES (not winner-redirect).
merged_into_id points a loser observation at a WINNER observation — three faults:
(1) conflates identity with evidence (the winner row is itself a mined observation
with its own source/citations — privileging it is what D49 says NOT to do);
(2) canonical label drifts by era (Neutune@1086 -> Newton@modern) so "the winner"
is ill-defined — winner-redirect re-points forever (D31 UNIQUE-key trap);
(3) per-stratum labels have no home.
=> Mint a synthetic canonical node per identity (canonical_morpheme / canonical_place
/ canonical_sense), declared in L2 with a STABLE id; BIND observations to it. The
node has no source of its own (derived hub). Separates identity from evidence (D21),
gives per-stratum labels a home (open #2 resolved), makes re-canonicalization a
one-assertion change, uniform across types (morphemes degenerate to node+one label —
pay indirection only where needed). Cost: extra indirection + migrate merged_into_id
clusters. All L3-rebuildable; runtime/L4 is the flattened projection (D38), no runtime cost.
REFINES u6fn.1 Family A: identity = mint-canonical + bind, one endpoint always a canonical node.

UNIFORM RECORD (one shape, all families):
{ id, predicate, subject:{type,ref}, object:{type,ref}|null, polarity:affirm|refute|retract,
  retracts:<id>|null, qualifiers:{ordinal,stratum,edge_type,kind,value,...},
  confidence:high|med|low|0..1, method:<version-stamp>, source, actor, rationale, timestamp }
Invariants: typed refs keep orthogonal axes clean; qualifiers carry ordinal/stratum/edge_type
so position/era stay DERIVED lens axes, never folded into a ref (D40/D45); append-only —
refute/retract are new records, never edits (D21/D22); full provenance quad (D24).

PREDICATE CATALOG:
 A mint-canonical (unary; node_type,node_id) | bind (observation->canonical; kind=
   same-morpheme/same-place/same-sense/inflection-of) | merge-canonical (canonical->canonical)
   | canonical-label (canonical->value; stratum,value)
 B descends-from (etymon->etymon; edge_type) | means-same-as (etymon->etymon; D28) |
   glosses-as (etymon->sense) | decomposes-into (toponym->etymon; ordinal => position derived)
   | contains (region->region; stratum) | succeeds (jurisdiction->jurisdiction) |
   located-in (place->region; stratum)
 C canonical-decomposition (toponym->sig; culture?) | decomposition-spurious (toponym_etymology row; reason)
Pairwise "looks same" from a heuristic = low-confidence bind; leave-separate default (D46)
means projection applies only above threshold — no separate proposal type.

L2 STREAM LAYOUT (per-predicate JSONL under canonicalization/, mirroring _reflexes.jsonl):
 _canonical_nodes.jsonl (mint-canonical, the stable ids) + _assert_<predicate>.jsonl (one each).
 Scoped diffs; rebuild-runbook-currency-reviewer tracks each as a discrete rebuild input
 (REBUILD.md L2 registry gets one entry per stream).

PROJECTION (u6fn.3) sketch: reads observations + _canonical_nodes + _assert_* -> L3 canonical
tables w/ per-stratum labels; observation.canonical_id (generalizes merged_into_id); relational
edge tables (generalize etymon_descent/meaning_synset/toponym_etymology_element); rollup views
(generalize *_canonical). Relational edges as mined point at OBSERVATIONS (D21); rollup via binds.
Determinism (D36.9): same L2 -> byte-identical L3.
MIGRATION (u6fn.4): each merged_into_id cluster -> one minted node + binds, method=legacy-import
low-confidence so repair revisits (esp. new->ne); cognate_id stays a PROJECTION of descends-from
closure (never identity).

WORKED EXAMPLE (Newton, real ids): mint CM-new-oe; bind 671826(niwe)/2229070(nīwe)/4631595(new);
RETRACT legacy 4631595->369498(ne) + rebind; merge-canonical CP-legacy-ne -> CM-new-oe ("ne/neu/
neuh = OCR-truncated nīwe"). decomposition-spurious on etymology row 780 (ford+botl contaminated).
mint CP-archdeacon-newton; bind toponym 5213+67841 (region 'County Durham'≡'Durham' Class-A alias).
canonical-label CP-newton-makerfield {domesday:Neutune, modern:Newton}.

OPEN -> u6fn.3: BIND GRANULARITY for places. 1725 conflates 3 places (rows 778 v./779 manor/
780 S.-of-Dalton) in one toponym row => bind at toponym_etymology-ROW granularity, not the coarse
toponym row, so the inverse (split) works. The one schema parameter u6fn.3 must confirm.
RESOLVED here: synthetic nodes (open#1), per-stratum labels on canonical node (open#2).
DOWNSTREAM: gloss A-vs-B split (open#3) is a same-sense-as vs string-norm call at use time.
close_reason: Both slices merged: L2 assertion layer (#644) + canonical_* L3 schema (#645). The L2→L3 projection is wyrd-u6fn.3.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text: u6fn.3 RESOLVED the open bind-granularity question: bind at observation-row granularity — morpheme=etymon row, sense=etymon_gloss row, place=toponym row DEFAULT with per-toponym_etymology-row OVERRIDE (override wins). Override-beats-default gives both merge (many rows->one place) and split (one row->many places, the 1725 case) with no special split predicate.

title: Design the edge-type taxonomy (identity-bearing vs relational) — the D28 fork
description: The first and most load-bearing design step. Partition predicates into IDENTITY-BEARING/collapsible (same-morpheme-as, same-place-as, variant-of, inflection-of) vs RELATIONAL/never-collapsible (descends-from, glosses-as, co-occurs-with). Conflating them recreates the D28 synset_id collision and the D42 PIE mega-component. Decide which axis each existing mechanism (merged_into_id, cognate_id, lemma_id, meaning_synset) maps onto. Nothing else in the epic proceeds until this is fixed.
design:
EDGE-TYPE TAXONOMY — FIRST CUT (2026-06-16)

TWO TESTS (apply these; families fall out):
T1 Collapsibility: "if these two nodes merged into one, would we lose info we still need?"
   No -> IDENTITY (collapsible). Yes -> RELATIONAL (never collapse).
   (Why cognate_id is NOT identity: cognate cluster = closure of descent edges;
    silly/selig are cognate but distinct now — D28.)
T2 Identity is bare + timeless (D40/D45/D44/D46/D8): identity edges connect
   stripped, position-free, era-free, inflection-free identities. Surface /
   dash-position / era-reflex / inflection are per-stratum LENSES on one identity,
   never separate identities, never identity-edge keys. Stops the D45 bug class.
Guardrails: relational axes are orthogonal (D28 — no generic related-to); all
   projects to SQLite (D42).

FAMILY A — IDENTITY (collapsible; generalizes merged_into_id). Symmetric same-entity
claims; projection unions evidence, accumulates per-stratum labels, picks canonical.
- same-morpheme-as (etymon<->etymon): ne~niwe, tun~tūn          [was merged_into_id]
- inflection-of   (etymon->lemma): cotan->cot (rolls up, D8)    [was lemma_id]
- same-place-as   (toponym<->toponym): 3 Lancashire Newtons; folds Neutune/Newton
                  name-forms into one place identity -> per-stratum label set     [new]
- same-sense-as   (gloss<->gloss): dedup gloss-sense deltas                        [new]
(Region within-stratum coding folds SUR~Surrey are NOT here — Class-A alias map, D49.)

FAMILY B — RELATIONAL (never collapse; orthogonal axes). Facts ABOUT distinct entities.
- descends-from (etymon->etymon, inh/borrow): town<-tūn<-PGmc    [etymon_descent]
- cognate-of    (etymon<->etymon peer): does NOT bridge clusters (D27)
- means-same-as (etymon<->etymon semantic): wæter~bekkr; orthogonal to identity AND
                cognate (D28)                                    [meaning_synset]
- glosses-as    (etymon->sense)                                  [etymon_gloss]
- decomposes-into (toponym->ORDERED[etymon]): Newton->[niwe,tūn]. ONLY birthplace of
                position (derived by index, D40/D43); identity edges never carry position
                                                                 [toponym_etymology_element]
- contains/within (region->region per stratum): England⊃Yorkshire⊃North Riding
- succeeds      (jurisdiction->jurisdiction): Cumberland+Westmorland->Cumbria; distinct
                extents, NEVER an identity fold (why Cumbria<->Cumberland is not an alias)  [new]
- located-in    (place->region@stratum): membership; "which Riding?" = evidence-bearing

FAMILY C — CANONICALIZATION CHOICE (assertions that SELECT among Family-B alternatives):
- canonical-decomposition: which decomposes-into is canonical, per (place[,culture])
- decomposition-spurious (corrective): flags a contaminated breakdown (ford+botl) —
  the Class-B answer to D3's neighbor-contamination gap
- canonical-label@stratum: which observed name-form is canonical at a stratum (Class-A bridge)

POLARITY (Newton trace needs all three): affirm (add ne~niwe) | refute (ford+botl
spurious) | retract (tombstone the bad new->ne merge). Every assertion carries
confidence+method+source+actor+rationale (u6fn.2). Identity-collapse defaults to
LEAVE-SEPARATE (D46 asymmetry); high bar + adversarial verify before promotion.

EXISTING MECHANISM MAP: merged_into_id->same-morpheme-as(A); lemma_id->inflection-of(A);
cognate_id->PROJECTION of descends-from closure (B, not identity); etymon_descent->
descends-from/cognate-of(B); meaning_synset->means-same-as(B); etymon_gloss->glosses-as(B)
+same-sense-as(A); toponym_etymology_element->decomposes-into(B); toponym_decomposition->
canonical-decomposition(C); region/country->Class-A labels + contains/located-in(B).

OPEN -> u6fn.2/.3:
1. same-place-as canonical: SYNTHETIC place node likely (canonical label changes by era,
   Neutune->Newton; winner-redirect would re-point endlessly — D31 UNIQUE-key lesson).
2. where per-stratum labels live (label-set on identity node vs observation edges).
3. gloss cleanup is itself A-vs-B (recursive D49): "enclosure"/"enclosure." = Class-A
   string norm; "farm, settlement"/"enclosure, farmstead" same-sense = Class-B same-sense-as.
close_reason: Edge-type taxonomy settled: graduated into DECISIONS D50.3 (identity/relational/choice families, the two sorting tests) and implemented as the PREDICATES catalog in #644 (merged). The synthetic-node refinement is D50.1.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text: Refined by u6fn.2: Family A identity is realized as mint-canonical + bind (one endpoint is ALWAYS a synthetic canonical node), NOT an observation<->observation edge. merged_into_id's winner-redirect is replaced by synthetic nodes. same-as pairwise claims are low-confidence binds resolved at projection.

title: Ingest-time region validation: fail-closed on unknown values
description: At the parser/ingest boundary, a region value that is neither in the enum nor the alias map is a HARD error (or quarantine), never a silent new row. This is the load-bearing guard that stops the mess re-accumulating after the one-time repair. Forward-looking: new mining emits canonical region only.

title: Build region alias map (mechanical code->canonical) + casing/whitespace fold
description:
The unambiguous Class-A aliases: SUF->Suffolk, LEC->Leicestershire, BUK->Buckinghamshire, SUR->Surrey, SUS->Sussex, 'County Durham'->Durham, 'Isle Of Wight'->Isle of Wight (casing). Each merges a code bucket into an already-existing spelled bucket. The alias map IS the audit trail; keep it as reviewable yaml next to the model.

SCOPE GUARD (D49): the alias map folds WITHIN-stratum, SAME-axis, SAME-level coding variants ONLY. Cross-level (Yorkshire<->North Riding), cross-axis (Danelaw), and cross-stratum (Cumbria<->Cumberland) are NOT alias entries — they are containment / membership / succession edges handled on the Class-B side (wyrd-u6fn). A blind modern->historic fold here would be a bug.

title: Region classification model: stratified multi-axis containment hierarchy (not a flat enum)
description:
Region is NOT a flat county list — it is a stratified containment hierarchy (D49 hierarchy section). Its LIVE PURPOSE is DEDUPLICATION: a tight, canonical, place-disambiguating blocking key for 'is this Newton and this Niweton the same place?' (the Class-B place-identity pass, wyrd-u6fn.7). Granularity is driven by WHAT SEPARATES PLACES, not by cultural meaningfulness.

Design the dedup hierarchy:
- CONTAINMENT depth: England -> Yorkshire -> North Riding (the flat field crams levels into one slot — Yorkshire 3023 and West Riding 102 as false peers).
- PERIOD-stratified: historic counties vs modern administrative areas are different vocabularies for different strata, not aliases.
Class-A scope of THIS ticket: node label vocabulary per stratum, the within-stratum containment skeleton, axis typing. Decide the dedup granularity the sources need (EPNS works at Riding level).

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: the cultural/linguistic-zone axis (Danelaw/Celtic/Roman) — DEFERRED generator surface, filed as wyrd-hytz, NOT a dedup key. 'England (Danelaw)' in region today is a category error: dedup wants the actual shire (migrate the Danelaw membership to wyrd-hytz's zone axis).
OUT to Class B (wyrd-u6fn.9): cross-stratum succession (Cumbria<->Cumberland+Westmorland) and ambiguous node assignment (bare 'Yorkshire' -> which Riding?).
design:
MODEL (decided 2026-06-16, user sign-off on the 3 granularity calls):

Region = forest of stratified containment trees, per country. First concrete file: data/regions_england.yaml. Each node carries: canonical label, level (country|county|subdivision), stratum (historic|modern-administrative), parent (containment edge). Axis typing: admin containment tree is the ONLY axis here; linguistic/cultural zones (Danelaw) are NOT admin nodes -> deferred to wyrd-hytz.

Dedup contract: canonical node at chosen granularity = the canonical_region blocking key for the Class-B place-ER pass (wyrd-u6fn.7). Granularity driven by what separates places, not cultural flavor.

GRANULARITY CALLS (user-decided):
1. YORKSHIRE = Riding-level leaf nodes (North/East/West Riding) under a Yorkshire county parent. The 3023 bare 'Yorkshire' rows all trace to source 'kepn' (which carries Ridings); the flattening is a KEPN-ingest bug -> Riding is recoverable from provenance, so re-coding is CLASS A (not lossy Class-B). '.4' re-codes bare Yorkshire -> correct Riding from KEPN source files.
2. SUSSEX = single historic 'Sussex' dedup node. East Sussex / West Sussex are modern-stratum labels that normalize UP to Sussex for dedup (clean non-lossy partition; safe Class-A, unlike lossy Cumbria).
3. 'Northumberland and Durham' (611 rows, all from mawer_1920_northumberland_durham combined volume) = QUARANTINE / not a valid node; fails ingest (.3), must be re-coded to a single historic county before passing (recovery from mawer source structure is a .4 concern).

CLASS-A NODES (England, historic stratum, level=county unless noted): Bedfordshire, Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Cambridgeshire, Cheshire, Cornwall, Cumberland, Derbyshire, Devon, Dorset, Durham, Essex, Gloucestershire, Hampshire, Herefordshire, Hertfordshire, Huntingdonshire, Isle of Wight, Kent, Lancashire, Leicestershire, Lincolnshire, Middlesex, Norfolk, Northamptonshire, Northumberland, Nottinghamshire, Oxfordshire, Rutland, Shropshire, Somerset, Staffordshire, Suffolk, Surrey, Sussex, Warwickshire, Westmorland, Wiltshire, Worcestershire, Yorkshire(parent) + North/East/West Riding(subdivision, parent=Yorkshire).

ALIAS TARGETS for .2 (code/casing -> canonical, within-stratum same-level): SUF->Suffolk, LEC->Leicestershire, BUK->Buckinghamshire, SUR->Surrey, SUS->Sussex, County Durham->Durham, Isle Of Wight->Isle of Wight (casing), West Riding of Yorkshire->West Riding, East Sussex/West Sussex->Sussex (normalize-up, dedup at historic stratum).

CROSS-STRATUM / CLASS-B (NOT aliases; succession edges -> wyrd-u6fn.9): Cumbria(modern, 842) = Cumberland+Westmorland(historic) lossy succession; modern metros (Bristol, Greater London, Greater Manchester, London Boroughs, Merseyside, Tyne and Wear, West Midlands) succeed historic counties.

ZONE AXIS (deferred wyrd-hytz): England (Danelaw) (130).

QUARANTINE / anomalies (fail-closed at .3): 'Northumberland and Durham' (611), 'South-West Yorkshire' (77, not a real historic Riding), 'England' (8, region=country degenerate), 'The Channel Islands' (17, not an English county -> country-level miscoding, defer to .5 country pass).

title: EPIC: Class-B universal canonicalization assertion layer (generalize the partial-but-correct collapse machinery)
description:
The collapse-with-provenance machinery already exists and does real work — merged_into_id (D22) and cognate_id (D27/D28) correctly unify tun->tūn and nīwe->niwe — but it is PARTIAL and INCONSISTENT, and the *why* is not on the edge. Concrete from the Newton trace: OE 'new' exists as TWO canonical nodes both glossed 'new' (671826 niwe, cluster 330032; 369498 ne, cluster 369500) that were never merged, so Newton decomposes differently per source; and Ekwall's 'new' was merged into 'ne' (the negative particle's node) with 2 witnesses and NO recorded rationale. Separately, a high-confidence Ekwall row (780) carries a hallucinated ford+botl breakdown on a 'new tun' entry that passed form-in-body validation (D3) because the words appear elsewhere in the paragraph.

The fix: make canonicalization a first-class, uniform, append-only ASSERTION layer — reified edges (subject, predicate, object, confidence, method, source, actor, rationale, timestamp) living in L2 JSONL, projected into the L3 collapse graph. This GENERALIZES merged_into_id/cognate_id from per-table redirect columns into one rationale-bearing, reversible, agent-augmentable model, and makes the partial-but-correct passes universal across every entity type. Edge-type taxonomy (identity-bearing same-morpheme-as / same-place-as vs relational descends-from / glosses-as) is load-bearing — conflating axes recreates the D28 synset_id collision and the D42 PIE-hairball. Merge asymmetry (D46-style): identity-collapse needs high confidence + rationale; default failure mode is leave-separate. Do NOT adopt a graph DB engine (D42 stands) — SQLite projection only.

Framed by DECISIONS.md D49 (Class-B half).

title: EPIC: Class-A controlled-vocabulary normalization at the mining/JSONL boundary
description:
Corpus dimensions drawn from closed external authorities (region, country, language code, source id, era cell) are stored inconsistently — same value, many codings — cluttering the DB with duplicate buckets that look like distinct data. Concrete: England region has SUF/Suffolk, LEC/Leicestershire, BUK/Buckinghamshire, SUR/Surrey, SUS/Sussex, County Durham/Durham all coexisting (~2,700 toponyms under code-form duplicates); country has Ireland/Republic of Ireland, Isle of Man/The Isle of Man, Brittany-as-country, 1078 nulls.

This is NOT scholarly entity resolution (that is the Class-B epic) — there is no evidence to preserve, no disagreement, no rationale. It is a CODING problem: a canonical enum + alias map enforced at ingest, fail-closed. Fix at the parser/JSONL boundary (L2 is git-tracked, so normalization is a reviewable diff, not data loss; region is not D21 etymological evidence). Getting this right produces the clean blocking keys (canonical_name, canonical_region) that make the Class-B toponym-ER pass tractable.

Framed by DECISIONS.md D49 (Class-A half). Distinct mechanism from the Class-B assertion-layer epic; they partition the corpus mess.

title: Era accretion gate (D46): morphemes must be 'in the record by then'; pools accrete, never expire
description:
USER DESIGN (2026-06-12, approved after noodling): a historical era MAY gate a morpheme out if the morpheme has no evidence as old as the period — but never if it's as old or older. 'It has to have appeared in the record by then.' Canonical example: Silicon (modern coinage) must not appear on a 1086 map; tūn appears on every map from OE onward (accretion — D44's fix stands: nothing ever expires).

ELIGIBILITY RULE (most-generous-evidence-of-age):
record_start(morpheme) = min over available signals of:
  (a) per-source-language RECORD-ENTRY year — when that language layer enters the British place-name record: old_english / celtic_mix / latin / germanic / ancient layers (akkadian, biblical, egyptian) → None (founding stratum, passes everything); old_scandinavian → 800 (Danelaw); old_french / norman_french → 1066 (Conquest); middle_english → 1100; modern_english → 1500. Unmapped fields default to None (pass).
  (b) earliest attested year across the morpheme's attested_years lists (a date can vouch a morpheme is OLDER than its stage suggests — e.g. modern_english bucket + 1086 Domesday date → passes oe-late).
Eligible at era E iff record_start is None OR E's end is None OR record_start < E.end. No evidence on either axis → pass (coverage rule, same posture as stratum/legacy era).

CONSEQUENCES:
- Open-ended eras (present-day token, the deployed default) have end=None → NO gate → full accreted pool. The wyrd-c6o1.3 -ton starvation cannot recur by construction.
- Mixed Era ('') → no era → no gate.
- Bounded historical eras gate ONLY positively-evidenced-late morphemes (Silicon class). Asymmetric failure mode: thin data errs toward inclusion.
- Pools are monotone: pool(oe-early) ⊆ pool(me) ⊆ pool(present).
- The D44 seed-level invariant NARROWS: same seed + same era → same skeleton still holds per-request, and '' vs present-day stay skeleton-identical (both ungated); but the same seed at a BOUNDED era may now differ from present-day (smaller pool). The durable invariant restates at TOWN level: a generated town's structure persists across renderings (rewind / era-map / regenerate carry the stack; they never re-draw).
- Render behavior unchanged (D44's reflex lens stands).
- Known corner (document, don't solve now): stage-level vouching is coarse — an 1817 coinage in the modern_english stage passes the early-modern (1500-1700) window via stage start 1500. All medieval eras exclude it correctly. Per-coinage dating would tighten this later.

IMPLEMENTATION: Meaning.record_start (lazy, min over (a)+(b)); EligibilityGate.era_record_cutoff: int | None (the resolved era range's END); predicate in _passes_base_gates + eligibility.admits; kenning.py/_resolve_vector_inputs + regenerate _parse_knobs derive the cutoff from the already-validated era range. DECISIONS.md: new D46 + annotate D44 ('never gates' refines to 'never gates by expiry; bounded eras gate by record entry'); update the era input_schema description + CLI help + OVERVIEW bullet; rescope/rename tests/test_kenning_era_renders_not_gates.py (ungated-pair invariance + monotonicity + an anachronism property test: bounded-era picks all have record_start < end).

description: Once the L4 ships bare-surface keys (sibling ticket): meaning_db keys = bare surfaces; Meaning._set_location stops DECODING dashes from the stored usage — location becomes an explicit constructor field (from the bundle's position metadata) used ONLY as a render/scoring hint per D39/D40; _resolve_surface/_get_stripped_index/_rank_siblings fold layers collapse to plain dict lookups; the render layer (Word/NewName/__str__) remains the SINGLE owner of positional dash decoration + case (D39). title: De-dash L4: bare-surface meaning keys + explicit position axis on proportions tables
description: Re-key the L4 runtime DB so morpheme identity is the bare surface: (1) meaning.usage_key + modern_usage become bare surfaces — the per-surface dash-variant rows ('-ton' / 'Ton-' / 'ton') merge into ONE row per surface (entries union; this also deletes the wyrd-c6o1.3 fold-union workaround for attested_languages, which becomes naturally surface-keyed); (2) proportions_usage / proportions_single_usage / bare_word_position keys become (surface, position) composite columns instead of dash-encoded position-forms; (3) runtime_db_export + bundle/_emit + bundle/_subject stop writing dashes; (4) runtime adapter + load_parts read the new shape. Schema-version bump + defensive legacy read per the proportions_attested_language precedent. Position data is PRESERVED — as an explicit column, never inside the surface string (epic wyrd-aicu / D45).
notes:
SCOPE MERGED with aicu.2 (2026-06-13). Deep analysis (Plan agent) proved aicu.1 (L4 export) and aicu.2 (runtime reader) CANNOT ship separately: the committed seed-runtime.db + exact-match schema-version gate (runtime_db.py _verify_schema_version) couple export and reader atomically. Re-exporting the seed with bare keys under today's runtime makes Meaning._set_location set every location='bare' and load_parts bucket every part as (bare,...), so pre/inner/post part pools vanish while proportions_structure still asks for them → generation collapses. _resolve_surface's fold saves surface resolution but NOT position bucketing. So this ticket now covers BOTH the L4 emit AND the runtime reader.

REAL SURFACE (3 tables need work; the rest are already de-dashed precedents):
- meaning.usage_key: dash→bare, merge up-to-5 variant rows per surface (full bundle: 79046 rows→67606 surfaces, 8965 with >1 row). LOSSLESS only if regroup-then-repick: 1100 surfaces have divergent primary_language, 918 divergent stratum across variants → re-run _pick_primary_language/_pick_unanimous_stratum over the UNIONED entries.
- proportions_usage: add position TEXT column, (surface,position) key; 22696→18595 distinct, 4101 collide → SUM weights then REBUILD cumulative (the central data landmine — _insert_cumulative assumes one row/key today).
- proportions_attested_language: fold to (culture,surface,primary_language) — 21547→11935 distinct (45% reduction; direct evidence c6o1.3 exact-key narrowing leaked). This RETIRES the c6o1.3 fold-union workaround.
Already bare (precedents, DON'T touch): proportions_single_usage (single=bare by construction; only case-twin collisions), proportions_bare_word_position (the (culture,position,usage_key) precedent), proportions_structure (location is index-derived explicit field).

DELIBERATE OUTPUT CHANGE: the weight-merge shifts the draw → names drift → tests/data/rogd10_parity.json regenerates (WYRD_REGEN_PARITY=1). Pre-launch posture, D41/D43 precedent.

KEY BREAKERS for the explicit-field swap: Meaning._set_location (meaning.py:328) accept explicit position arg; runtime/proportions.py:_location_from_form (419) delete; load_parts (449) take (surface,position); word.py:180 'Saint-' literal → fold; vector_name_select._slot_position_label (177) lockstep; meaning.py _register_inflection_shadows leading/trailing-dash wrapping.

SCHEMA: bump v2→v3 in lockstep (bundle/_emit.py SCHEMA_VERSION + runtime/runtime_db.py _EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION). Defensive legacy read (column-missing→_location_from_form fallback) modeled on _read_proportions_bare_word_positions / _read_proportions_attested_languages, lets intermediate commits stay green on the v2 seed.

PLAN (4 commits): (1) readers tolerate both shapes, green on v2 seed; (2) writers emit bare+position; (3) schema bump v2→v3, DDL position columns, re-export seed (--dev, L3 at ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db present), regen parity, fix dash-literal tests; (4) keep one defensive-read release (deleted in aicu.4 final sweep). L3 re-export needed for the COMMITTED seed (the --dev top-200 subset, fast-ish); full S3 bundle re-export is a separate deploy step.

title: EPIC: morpheme surface identity — no dashes in stored morpheme identity, ever
description:
USER DIRECTIVE (2026-06-12, verbatim intent): 'we do NOT put - in the morpheme name, *ever*, and we *never* key off of it. pre- / -inner- / -post is *only* a function of the position, and is *only* from breaking down toponyms (or from using pre-broken-down ones). It is purely something we decorate the morpheme with *at display time*.' This has recurred 5+ times (D39, D40, the wyrd-eyjk P0, the wyrd-c6o1.3 pfoo fold) because the rule was enforced at the MATCHING layer but the STORAGE layer still carries dash-marked identities — so every consumer needs fold-the-dash compat code and new code keeps keying off the stored shape.

WHERE DASHES LIVE TODAY (2026-06-12 audit):
- L3 authoring: reflex.surface_form carries dash-marked forms (seeded from the rando-port meanings.json; decomposition outputs).
- L4 runtime DB: meaning.usage_key + each entry's modern_usage are dash-marked position-forms ('-ton', 'Ton-', bare 'ton' as SEPARATE rows for one surface); proportions_usage/_single_usage keys are position-forms.
- Runtime: meaning_db keys = dash-marked; Meaning._set_location() DECODES dashes into .location; ~80 production fold/branch sites — proportions.py (32), meaning.py (9), vector_name_select.py (7), era/rewind.py (6), __init__.py (6), kenning_regenerate.py (5), bundle/_subject.py (3), kenning_rewind.py (3), trie_matcher.py (2), realism_reference.py (2), runtime_db_export.py (2), word.py/name.py/drift_runner.py (1 each).

TARGET STATE: morpheme identity = bare surface everywhere it is STORED or KEYED (L2/L3/L4/runtime). Position is (a) derived at decomposition time as an OUTPUT (D40), (b) carried as an explicit position FIELD where a table genuinely needs the axis — (surface, position) composite keys, never encoded INTO the surface string, (c) applied as dash decoration only at DISPLAY/render time (the render owns positional case + dashes, D39). The fold-the-dash compat code then deletes wholesale.

ENFORCEMENT (already landing separately): DECISIONS.md D45 records the hard rule; morpheme-surface-identity-reviewer (kenning AGENT-REVIEWERS.md) flags new violations on every PR; final child here adds the CI data-gate once storage is clean.

title: Pre-existing: _element_glosses.jsonl + _pronunciation.jsonl crash rebuild-from-jsonl (unregistered/missing _type)
description:
Discovered during wyrd-xz3g (PR #623) P1 verification. build_from_jsonl globs EVERY data/mining/*.jsonl through jsonl/log.replay_file, which raises ReplayError on a missing or unregistered _type. Two git-tracked synthetic L2 files crash it TODAY:

  - data/mining/_element_glosses.jsonl: rows have NO _type field → ReplayError 'row missing _type field'
  - data/mining/_pronunciation.jsonl: rows have _type 'pronunciation', NOT registered in LIST_TYPES/KEYED_TYPES → ReplayError 'unknown _type pronunciation'

Empirically reproduced: replay_file('data/mining/_element_glosses.jsonl') and replay_file('data/mining/_pronunciation.jsonl') both raise. So a full 'lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl' over the committed data/mining/ crashes before enrichment runs. REBUILD.md's L2-round-trip table CLAIMS both layers '✅ round-trip' — currently false. Likely latent because no full rebuild has run since these files landed.

Fix (mirror the working synthetic files _reflexes.jsonl / _merge_audit.jsonl / wyrd-xz3g _tags.jsonl): (1) register 'pronunciation' in jsonl/log.py LIST_TYPES; (2) give _element_glosses.jsonl rows a registered _type (e.g. 'element_gloss') + register it; (3) ensure BOTH files carry the mandatory canonical 'source' row as their first line (build.py:_extract_source_id requires exactly one source row per file). Their collectors (collect_element_glosses/collect_pronunciation) read the files directly, so the replay accumulation just needs to be inert. Add a build_from_jsonl round-trip test for each (pattern: wyrd-xz3g test_build_from_jsonl_accepts_tags_file).

Parent epic: wyrd-eni4 (gap-closing/coverage-quality) — same family as the rebuild-contract work.
close_reason:
Already resolved (no PR) — by wyrd-5qg7's exclusion + drift-guard work, which post-dates this ticket (2026-06-12). Verified empirically:

CRASH FIXED: rebuild-from-jsonl CLI feeds build_from_jsonl via jsonl_paths_in() (build.py:1052), which filters out REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS. Both _element_glosses.jsonl (build.py:1043) and _pronunciation.jsonl (build.py:1045) are in that set, so they're never passed to replay_file → no ReplayError. Confirmed: jsonl_paths_in('data/mining') returns 105 files, neither offending file among them.

REGRESSION-GUARDED: tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py::test_no_unhandled_nonconforming_ledgers is a bidirectional drift guard — FORWARD: every non-conforming data/mining/*.jsonl MUST be in REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS (fails CI on exactly the zhhf bug class); INVERSE: every excluded name must still exist + still be non-conforming. Both guard tests pass.

REBUILD.md ACCURATE: the '✅ round-trip' claims (lines 46/48) refer to ENRICHMENT re-derivation (read-directly via apply_element_glosses / collect_pronunciation), and lines 201-203 explicitly document both as replay-excluded. Consistent + correct.

NOTE: the ticket's encoded recipe (register 'pronunciation'/'element_gloss' types + replay inert + add source rows) is now the WRONG fix — making these files 'conforming' would trip the INVERSE drift-guard (a conforming file in REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS = 'stale exclusion'). These are read-directly ledgers, correctly excluded from generic replay. Sibling wyrd-9kh6 (lexicon enrich path) is a DISTINCT code path, untouched by this.

title: -ton has all but vanished from modern English output — core OE morpheme weighting regression
description:
-ton (OE tūn) appears in roughly 20% of real British place names, but generated modern-English output now almost never contains it. The only -ton sightings trace to the WELSH morpheme (ton = 'wave/broken ground'), not the OE one — so the OE tūn lemma is being starved somewhere in the eligibility/scoring/frequency chain.

Something is clearly wrong at the data or scoring layer. Candidate suspects (verify, don't assume):
- bundle/L4 export: did the OE tūn family lose its usage weight, frequency rows, or get folded/merged wrongly (cluster collapse, D22 merge, modern-reflex curation)?
- per-usage frequency aggregation by surface (D43 notes _apply_per_usage_frequency aggregates by surface) — a welsh/OE surface collision ('ton') mis-attributing weight?
- vector-path eligibility or baseline axis dropping the OE lemma (priors sidecar, attested-language gating).

Diagnose first: generate N=500 english/modern names, count -ton occurrences + which lemma each resolves to (morpheme_id), and compare the L4 DB's weight for the OE tūn usage vs a known-good earlier runtime DB.

Acceptance: -ton (OE tūn) frequency in modern English output is back in a plausible band relative to its corpus weight, and a regression test pins the top-N core morphemes' presence.
notes:
DIAGNOSED 2026-06-12. Two compounding defects, both fixed on branch kenning/c6o1-3-ton-era-and-homograph:

(1) ERA GATE (the regression): Meaning.attested_in_era_range required an attestation year INSIDE the era window. PR #622 (wyrd-kqyf) made era=present-day the deployed default; the english 'modern' cell is (1700, None), but OE tūn's attested_years are 709/1050/1086/1270 (scholarly attestations are inherently medieval) — so EVERY well-documented OE morpheme was filtered out of default generation, while no-data homographs passed via the no-data rule. Fix: open-ended windows (end=None, the present-day stage) pass every morpheme — place names accrete. Bounded historical windows unchanged.

(2) HOMOGRAPH LEAK (why the survivors looked welsh): wyrd-pfoo per-Meaning attested-language narrowing was keyed by EXACT usage_key; the bundle records attestation under position-forms ('-ton') but meaning_db has dash-variant keys ('ton', 'Ton-', '-ton-') which got None → filter inactive → welsh 'ton' (wave) / irish 'ton' admitted to english pool. Fix: fold-union the map to bare surface at load_proportions + fold the lookup in _native_pool.

EVIDENCE: 500-roll diag pre-fix at era=present-day: 0 picks resolve to OE tūn, all -ton hits resolve welsh:ton/irish:ton. Post-fix: 34/300 names carry -ton (11.3%), all english-family ids, zero celtic. On the committed dev seed pre-fix -ton was entirely ABSENT at present-day (no welsh bare-ton key there to fake it); post-fix 20/150 (13.3%). Regression gate: tests/test_kenning_present_day_core_morphemes.py. Diag script: scratch/c6o1_3_diag.py (gitignored).

title: SPA: toponym edits don't persist — output reverts on blur instead of reworking the underlying result data
description:
When the user alters the toponym in the SPA, the output changes while editing, but reverts as soon as focus leaves the field. The edit is only mutating the DISPLAY layer; it must rework the data the output renders from, persistently (survive blur, re-render, inspect/transform, and downstream interactions).

User framing: 'If I was using react here I would think this is a problem with redux' — i.e. the edit isn't being committed to the canonical client-side state/store that the output renders from; some component-local state is shadowing it and getting discarded.

Where to look: spa-next/src — whatever owns the result/morpheme state vs the editable toponym field; the edit path should update the same canonical structure that reroll/swap/transform read, not a transient copy.

Acceptance: edit toponym → click elsewhere → output keeps the edited form; subsequent operations (swap, transform, reroll of OTHER parts) operate on the edited data.
notes: PR #628 (branch kenning/c6o1.1-edit-persist). Root cause: reroll/reflex-swap output lived only in transient pipeline display state, never committed to appState.results[i] → reverted on re-derive. Fix (operator choice: keep stack, commit output continuously): pipeline.run mirrors bottom state → appState.results[currentResultIndex]; InspectorColumn base = select-time snapshot read via untrack (breaks the run-loop); MorphemeGrid revert/placement ref reads pipeline base (states[0]); result_modern nulled on transform / restored on revert. Verified in-browser (Flask+Vite+Playwright): swap → both columns update → switch+back persists → 2nd swap compounds; no loop. +5 unit tests; SPA suite 141 green; svelte-check clean. Awaiting review/merge.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #628 (squash c4e710d8). Reroll/reflex edits now persist: pipeline.run commits its output ($state.snapshot'd) into appState.results[currentResultIndex]; InspectorColumn base = select-time snapshot read via untrack (breaks the run-loop); MorphemeGrid revert/placement ref = pipeline base; result_modern nulled on transform / restored on revert; OutputColumn companion clause simplified. Verified in-browser (persist across switch + compounding) + 144 SPA tests + svelte-check. Review loop: all findings addressed, 0 unresolved; component-test harness deferred to wyrd-200v.

title: SPA generation-surface defects: state persistence, reroll fidelity, morpheme weighting, tag scope, structure control
description:
Umbrella for a batch of user-reported defects + one feature on the generation surface (2026-06-12, post-PR-#610 / post-D43 testing):

1. Toponym edits don't persist — output reverts on blur (state-management bug).
2. Rerolls don't respect D43 bare word placement.

Each item is its own child ticket.

The 'monster → all-animal' report that opened the epic is fully resolved (c6o1.4 one-slot --tag + ah53 culture-scoped tag offering), reroll bare-word placement (c6o1.2), -ton weighting (c6o1.3), SPA edit persistence (c6o1.1), inspector tag display (0wpd), structure allowlist (c6o1.5), and the reactive-state regression net (200v) all landed.

title: SPA per-morpheme regenerate button + kenning-regenerate-morpheme endpoint
description:
In the SPA's Inspect & Transform column, add a button in the top-right of every morpheme card. Clicking it hits a NEW API endpoint that randomly regenerates JUST that morpheme, given the context of all the other morphemes in use (same request gates — culture/era/stratum/tag hard gates; cohesion conditioned on the other slots' tags; never re-creating a Hill Hill). The new morpheme replaces the old one in BOTH the Inspect & Transform column AND the Output column (so the transformed name becomes a bookmark candidate). The regeneration is implemented as a transform-stack step, so the user undoes it by removing that item from the stack.

Decisions locked with the operator (2026-06-11):
1. Output sync: ALL pipeline transforms propagate — the Output row for the currently-inspected result live-renders pipeline.currentState, and the star bookmark captures original + pipeline (today it saves original with pipeline: []).
2. Re-click: ONE step per morpheme, re-roll in place — a second click on the same morpheme updates the existing step with a fresh seed (mirrors pipeline.setSwap update-in-place), undo goes straight back to the original morpheme.
3. Duplicate policy: the candidate pool EXCLUDES the morpheme being replaced and every morpheme already in use elsewhere in the name (fold-compare: dash-stripped lowercase) — every click visibly changes the name and can never create a Hill Hill.
4. Feature-flagged: transform tags itself flag: 'regenerate-morpheme' (WYRD_FF_REGENERATE_MORPHEME). Staging sees it via WYRD_FF_ALL; prod hides it until enabled_feature_flags adds it. No server change needed (env-driven resolution).

Process: single PR from a git worktree; pr-review-loop with AGENT-REVIEWERS.md reviewers; operator sign-off before merge.
design:
== API side ==

1. New Generator subclass KenningRegenerateMorpheme (wyrd/generators/kenning/generators/kenning_regenerate.py), name "kenning-regenerate-morpheme", multi_result=True (exactly one result; count ignored). Auto-routes as POST /api/kenning-regenerate-morpheme via the existing /api/<generator> dispatch (app.py:89-97).

2. Input schema (kenning-rewind is the precedent for morphemes-in, name-out):
   - name (string) + words (morphemes_by_word shape, as the SPA holds it)
   - word_index, morpheme_index (target slot)
   - seed (int — baked client-side at click time so pipeline re-runs/saved-workspace restores are deterministic)
   - generation-context params mirroring Kenning's: culture, tag(s), exclude_tags, mood, harshness, era, stratum, novelty, cohesion (+ vector weights where feasible), coerced like Kenning.generate.

3. Server logic:
   - Resolve each slot's Meaning from meaning_db by BARE SURFACE (D40 — string match only; reuse the rewind/stripped-index sibling-lookup pattern). Position of the target slot is DERIVED from its index in the word (sole→bare, first→pre, last→post, interior→inner per D39/D40), never from stored dashes.
   - Build RequestVector via build_request_vector (vector_kenning_adapter). Same per-lemma hard gates as a fresh roll (era/stratum/--tag OR-gate per wyrd-wv85) → tag satisfaction is preserved automatically.
   - Pool + scores: build_non_position_eligible + build_slot_base_scores (vector_name_select.py) for the derived position.
   - Cohesion context: when cohesion > 0, prior-tags = union of all OTHER slots' tags (the "context of all the others").
   - Exclusions (decision 3): drop old morpheme + all in-use folds. 4xx with a clear message when the pool is empty after exclusions.
   - Novelty blend + weighted draw, rng = random.Random(seed).
   - Render the replacement through the same surface path (D41 native canonical + modern companion; slot casing/dashes derived from the slot per D39) and rebuild the FULL name: result, result_modern, components, morphemes_by_word — the SPA replaces wholesale.
   - Validation: out-of-range indices, unresolvable usage, joiner/manorial-affix slots (not regenerable) → 4xx.

== SPA side ==

4. New transform spa-next/src/lib/transforms/regenerate.js: kind 'regenerate-morpheme', flag 'regenerate-morpheme', params {wordIndex, morphemeIndex, seed, context} where context = generation-params snapshot baked at click time (appState params for the roll). apply(state, params) POSTs state.name + state.morphemes_by_word + indices + seed + context, returns {name, morphemes_by_word}. Register in transforms/index.js. Async-transform error handling per the rewind pattern (pipeline catches, shows step error).

5. Button top-right of each morpheme card in InspectorColumn.svelte (.m-head, ~lines 204-211), gated on flagOn(appState.config, 'regenerate-morpheme') and kenning results only. Click → new pipeline helper (mirror setSwap, pipeline.svelte.js:~125): if a regenerate step exists for that (wordIndex, morphemeIndex) → updateStep with a fresh seed; else addStep with baked params + fresh seed (decision 2).

6. Undo: existing TransformStep remove control (TransformStep.svelte:18) already re-runs the pipeline without the step. Provide summary() so the step reads e.g. 'Regenerate "-ton" (word 1, slot 2)'.

7. Output propagation (decision 1): OutputColumn renders pipeline.currentState for the row at appState.currentResultIndex (native + modern companion + morpheme grid); other rows unchanged. StarToggle payload captures a snapshot of pipeline.steps instead of [] — savedStore/SavedList already restore + re-run pipelines on load.

8. api.js: new regenerateMorpheme(...) helper.

== Tests ==
- API: seeded determinism (same input+seed → same replacement); replacement never equals old fold or any in-use fold; tag-gate preservation; cohesion smoke; 4xx paths (bad index, unknown morpheme, empty pool). Fixtures/seed-runtime.db only — no live ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db (CI has none).
- SPA (vitest): transform apply with mocked fetch; update-in-place step semantics; Output propagation; star payload includes pipeline.

== Out of scope ==
- Regenerating joiners/manorial affixes; non-kenning generators; multi-slot regeneration; changing how non-inspected Output rows render.

title: era grid must always contain the rendered surface as a clickable cell (usage cell)
description: UI requirement (filed repeatedly): the era grid IS the swap menu, so the user must be able to swap to other reflexes AND BACK — which requires the actually-rendered form to be a clickable, highlighted cell. Today force-modern renders the usage but the usage often isn't a cell (modern stage holds derived reflexes like gowth/stone, not the usage), so the live form is missing from the menu and has no id. Fix (API-side, user-authorized): guarantee the rendered surface is a grid cell with an id; inject it into the render stage if absent, marked source='usage' so the central form is identifiable. active_form_id points to it.
