title: Reflex-id contract: generation must render FROM the listed reflexes and return the reflex-id used (guarantee surface ∈ reflexes)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the recurring 'X not in its own reflexes' defect cluster (staging, 2026-06-04 → ongoing; newest Hartsleigh 2026-06-09T23:30 on fc5b3fa). Per operator: the intended design was (1) every reflex carries an id, and (2) when a name is generated, the backend returns the reflexes USED (their ids) — so the rendered surface is one of the listed reflexes BY CONSTRUCTION, making 'not in its own reflexes' impossible.

wyrd-i4jd (#566) delivered only part of this: it carried the picked ETYMON id so render/grid/highlight reference the same etymon. It did NOT guarantee the rendered SURFACE is a member of that etymon's enumerated reflex set. The era/native render still SYNTHESIZES surfaces (macron'd forms, phonology-rule reflexes) outside the stored reflex list, so the surface can't be in it (see sibling wyrd-rogd.17 macron Output/Inspect mismatch — same root: rendered surface not drawn from a listed reflex).

Fix direction: unify the render path with the reflex enumeration — the generator should PICK a reflex (by id) from the etymon's reflex set and render THAT, and the API payload should return the chosen reflex-id per morpheme so the SPA grid highlights exactly the rendered form. Any surface the renderer can produce must exist as an id'd reflex in the set (synthesized forms get materialized as reflexes with ids). Composes with the era-grid data-quality cleanup (this epic) — clean reflexes + render-from-listed = the surface is always present and correct.

title: Lambda SnapStart for the wyrd API (eliminate user-facing cold-start load)
description:
Even after trimming the generation DB (wyrd-<trim>), cold containers pay init (~1.8s) + the trimmed parse. Enable AWS Lambda SnapStart (Python is supported) so the initialized container is snapshotted at deploy and restored in ~sub-second.

Requirements/caveats:
- Move the (trimmed) bundle + default-culture load into create_app()/init so the parsed Python objects are captured in the snapshot (SnapStart snapshots in-memory state).
- /tmp is NOT in the snapshot and a held SQLite connection / boto3 S3 client goes STALE across restore. Reopen the SQLite connection lazily or in an afterRestore runtime hook; do not hold a live connection across the checkpoint.
- Option to evaluate: once the generation DB is small (post-trim), BUNDLE it in the deploy zip — removes the S3 round-trip at runtime and makes SnapStart clean. Tradeoff: loses D38's 'update data without redeploy'. Decide explicitly.
- terraform: add snap_start { apply_on = 'PublishedVersions' } to aws_lambda_function.api and publish a version; point the Function URL/alias at the published version. Confirm us-east-2 + python3.12 SnapStart support.

Verify: cold-start (restore) p99 < ~1s on staging.
Refs: depends on wyrd-<trim>; terraform/main.tf (memory 1769, timeout 15).
notes:
BLOCKER found — SnapStart rollout is CROSS-STACK + needs a deploy-pipeline rework; NOT a single merge-and-auto-deploy.

Done + tested (runtime foundation, safe/neutral until SnapStart active — 4996 passed):
- wyrd/snapstart.py: preload_runtime() (gated on AWS_LAMBDA_INITIALIZATION_TYPE==snap-start, so off-SnapStart it's a no-op) + register_snapstart_hooks() (afterRestore drops the stale sqlite conn).
- runtime_db.reset_runtime_db_connection() (connection-only reset; keeps the version + lru caches so a restored container serves from memory, no 46MB re-download).
- create_app() wires both at init; pyproject adds snapshot-restore-py.

Drafted but NOT safe to auto-apply (would break the live API):
- terraform: aws_lambda_function publish=true + snap_start{apply_on=PublishedVersions}; aws_lambda_alias 'live' -> function.version; aws_lambda_function_url qualifier='live'; both cloudfront permissions qualifier='live'.

THE BLOCKER:
1. SnapStart needs a PUBLISHED VERSION, so the Function URL must target the 'live' alias. A QUALIFIED Function URL has a DIFFERENT DOMAIN than the $LATEST one.
2. CloudFront's origin for wyrd is in a SEPARATE stack — infra-frontend/terraform/modules/wyrd-cf reads data.terraform_remote_state.wyrd.outputs.lambda_function_url (env stacks production/ + staging/). The wyrd deploy.yml only applies the wyrd stack, NOT infra-frontend.
3. So applying the wyrd terraform alone replaces the unqualified Function URL with a qualified one (new domain) while CloudFront still points at the dead old domain -> live API 502s until infra-frontend is re-applied.

Rollout therefore needs (coordinated, staging-first):
- a) wyrd terraform apply (publishes version + alias + qualified Function URL) THEN b) infra-frontend apply (CloudFront origin picks up the new Function URL) — atomically/closely, staging then prod.
- deploy.yml rework: terraform apply already publishes+aliases (publish=true), but must WAIT for the published version's SnapStart snapshot to reach State=Active before it's live; remove/neuter the now-redundant update-function-code (it writes an un-aliased $LATEST). Validate the snapshot-wait on a staging deploy.
- Same coupling for Provisioned Concurrency — not avoidable for this CloudFront->FunctionURL architecture.

title: Cold start: trim generation runtime DB to the generation-relevant subset + split generation load from the full decomposition corpus
description:
Cold-start is ~14s and times out at the 15s Lambda limit. Profiled (local CPU, ~1.5-2x faster than the 1-vCPU Lambda):
- bundle_dict_from_runtime_db: 2380 ms (reads 83,439 subjects from SQLite)
- load_meanings (parse 90,492 Meaning objects): 7453 ms  <- dominant
- _load_culture proportions: 141 ms
= ~10s local, ~10-14s on the 1-vCPU Lambda, run LAZILY on the first request (via input_schema()->available_tags()->_load_meanings), so the first user request eats it and dies at the 15s timeout.

Root cause: generation only needs the per-culture eligible morphemes (~2k/culture), but it shares _load_meanings() (the FULL ~90k-meaning etymological lexicon) with the decomposition endpoints. The matcher/surface-index is already lazy; the cost is parsing the whole lexicon into objects.

COUPLING (critical): kenning-explain, kenning-era-map, kenning-rewind are registered generators the Lambda serves and they use _load_meanings() (full corpus) + find_meaning() (the matcher). So we cannot just drop the corpus from generation's load — we must SPLIT:
- Generation (Kenning, KenningCreature, KenningRender): load a TRIMMED meaning set = union of morphemes referenced by any culture's proportions + their senses (~few-k).
- Decomposition (explain/era-map/rewind): lazily load the FULL corpus (+ later the pickled matcher, wyrd-<pickle>) ONLY when those endpoints are hit.

Deliver: (a) define + build the trimmed generation runtime DB (the S3 .db the Lambda loads for generation) — see lexicon/runtime_db_export.py / runtime_db_publish.py / export_runtime_db.py; (b) make generation's _load_meanings use the trimmed set; (c) give explain/era-map/rewind a separate lazy full-corpus load so the trim doesn't break them; (d) derive available_tags() (manifest tag picker) from the trimmed subset — this also fixes wyrd-hh2m (only offer generatable tags); confirm era/stratum option coverage survives the trim. Re-emit + upload the trimmed DB to staging+prod S3. Verify cold-load drops under ~2s and warm is unchanged.

Refs: wyrd-i7uy (prior cache work), wyrd-hh2m (tag list), D38 (runtime DB on S3).
notes:
Implemented + validated the export-capability (PR on branch kenning/runtime-db-trim):
- Added --generation-subset to export-runtime-db (write_runtime_db generation_subset flag). Reuses the existing select_dev_subset filter with top_n_per_culture=None (keep ALL proportion-referenced usages, no top-N cap), real built_at/source metadata (not the dev sentinels).
- VALIDATED against the full 210MB staging corpus: 83,439 -> 12,466 subjects (14.9%), ~21MB subject JSON -> est ~48MB DB. ~77% cut. Keeps every renderable structure (no top-N drop). 63 export tests pass.
- No runtime code change needed for the trim: the Lambda loads whatever DB is at the S3 current.json pointer, so publishing the trimmed DB IS the fix. available_tags() auto-reflects the subset (also closes wyrd-hh2m). 

Breakage check (done): era-map/era-grid (active) is SAFE — it decomposes its OWN generated names (built from generation morphemes), which the trimmed DB matches. Only standalone explain (decompose arbitrary user names) + flagged-off rewind degrade — the deferred 'decomposition feature'.

REMAINING (operational, needs the L3 lexicon source DB which CI/the user has, not local):
1. Re-emit: wyrd kenning lexicon export-runtime-db --generation-subset <L3.db> <out.db>
2. Publish to staging + prod S3 (runtime_db_publish / bin/publish-runtime-db.sh) -> flips current.json pointer.
3. Verify cold-load drops ~77% on staging (CloudWatch Init+Duration; expect first-request ~2-3s vs ~14s).
Then wyrd-g1wp (SnapStart) takes the residual to sub-second, and the background DB-refresh (new ticket) picks up pointer flips without redeploy.
close_reason: VERIFIED complete. Trim already live on staging+prod since Jun 9 (v/2026-06-09T23-2xZ.db); fresh --generation-subset rebuild is byte-identical to the deployed staging DB. Generation content fully preserved: 0 proportion-referenced meanings dropped; the only diff vs the full corpus is 787 cosmetic JSON entry-ORDER differences (0 multiset content diff, 0 primary_language/stratum diff). The trim dropped exactly the 69,369 decomposition-only morphemes (79,046->9,677) that only served name dissection (not a shipping feature) - legit by design, not a bug. Cold-start (staging CloudWatch): ~13-15s with repeated 15s-timeout hits pre-cutover -> 2,864ms on the first post-cutover cold start (n=1; low staging traffic). P1 timeout resolved.

title: Tag filtering is sticky: eligible-pool cache key omits gate.required_tags (first --tag wins for the warm container)
description:
## Symptom (operator-reported)
Select a tag, generate; then select a DIFFERENT tag — output doesn't change, even though the new tag IS in the request. The first tag for a cold start is 'sticky'.

## Root cause
runtime/proportions.py NameGenerator._vector_caches builds the eligible-pool cache key WITHOUT gate.required_tags:
    cache_key = (gate.era_min, gate.era_max, gate.stratum, exclude_tags_fz, request.packs, id(pack_meaning_dbs), include_unglossed)
But build_non_position_eligible filters the pool by gate.required_tags (the --tag hard gate). So the first tag's filtered pool is cached under a key that ignores the tag; every subsequent request with a different tag (same era/stratum/exclude/packs) reuses the STALE pool.

The cache lives on the _load_culture-cached (shared, long-lived) NameGenerator, so in the deployed Lambda the FIRST tag any request uses warms the cache and sticks for every later different-tag request across ALL users on that warm container → tags are effectively broken after the first one.

## Reproduce (clear the shared cache between to see truth)
death (clean): ['Haug Quarter','Byrgen', ...]  (death morphemes)
water (clean): ['Wæter Vestr','Wætervík', ...]  (water)
death AGAIN (cache warm from water): ['Wæter Vestr', ...]  ← BUG: returns the water pool

## Fix
Add gate.required_tags (a frozenset, hashable) to the cache_key. (Note: gate.culture is implicitly keyed because each culture has its own NameGenerator via _load_culture; era/stratum/exclude_tags ARE already in the key; only required_tags was missing.) The slot_base_scores cache already keys on request_signature (which includes required_tags), but it's downstream of the stale eligible pool, so fixing the eligible key is the fix.

## Pre-existing
Not introduced by the mood rework (wyrd-4rp8) — predates it. Before wyrd-4rp8, moods ALSO routed through required_tags, so this same bug made moods sticky too; wyrd-4rp8 moved moods off required_tags (now an overlay), so this now only bites explicit --tag.

## Regression test
Warm the cache with tag A, then request tag B on the same NameGenerator → output must reflect B (different from A), not the cached A pool.

title: era-grid modern stage omits the morpheme's own form + shows wrong cognate (minster->minister, old->yule, bridge->bricg)
description: From 48 staging defect reports (wyrd-dsl5): ~40% of morpheme-instances have the morpheme's own usage/canonical form ABSENT from its era_grid, and the modern-stage cell often shows a WRONG reflex instead of the morpheme's actual modern form. Examples: usage=park -> modern 'parrock'; usage=minster -> modern 'minister'; usage=bridge -> modern 'bricg/bricge/bricgum' (un-modernized ME); usage=old- -> modern 'yule'; usage=crook -> 'croc'; usage=fair- -> 'fageran/fagere' (ME inflections). Two distinct failures: (1) the morpheme's own modern form is never guaranteed in the grid; (2) the cluster/descent reflex picker selects a wrong cognate or an un-modernized ME spelling as 'modern'. Distinct from the noise-pollution cleanup (wyrd-1wv2/pzg5 — shipped). Investigate etymon_era_reflexes tiers + the bundle modern-stage build (_collect_best_by_target / _fetch_family_era_reflexes). Investigation-first; report before changing.
notes:
PINPOINTED (supersedes the earlier clustering-only theory). The DOMINANT 'X not in its own reflexes' class is a single RENDER-SIDE bug, NOT clustering.

Chain for 'Park Grange': the morpheme is old-english:pearroc (gloss 'enclosure/paddock/park'). Its modern surface 'Park' comes from the PLACE-NAME CORPUS, not etymology: pearroc has attested modern toponym surface_forms 'Park-' and 'Paddock-' (real KEPN/Ekwall place-name elements derived from pearroc) = its modern_usage. The generator renders the morpheme as that attested modern surface ('Park'); the cognate CLUSTER separately gives the etymological modern reflex 'parrock' (a distinct archaic word; the common 'park' is the OF parc borrowing, cluster 288752, separate).

The bundle CORRECTLY carries both: pearroc's 'Park-' entry has era_reflexes modern-english=['Park-'(self), 'parrock'(cluster)] — the wyrd-mook self-seed (_seed_generated_surface) worked at build time.

THE BUG: runtime _merged_morpheme_meaning (proportions.py:380-384) applies a 'genuine-wins' filter: per language,  — if ANY non-self (cluster/descent) reflex exists, it DISCARDS the self-seeds. pearroc has 2 usages (Park-, Paddock-) so the merge fires; modern-english has genuine 'parrock' -> the self-seeds 'Park-'/'Paddock-' are dropped -> inspector shows only 'parrock' -> 'Park not in its own reflexes'. (Single-usage morphemes are exempt, line 363, which is why some morphemes look fine.)

FIX (recommended): in the merge, UNION the self-seed generated surface with genuine reflexes (don't discard) — at least for the modern stage where modern_usage lives. Makes the generated surface always appear in the grid. Resolves most of the 48 'not in own reflexes' defects in one change, render-side, no clustering/bundle change. Comment at :360 calls self-seeds 'constructed-compound artifacts' — true for connective fragments (-ning-) but WRONG for attested toponym surfaces (Park-/Paddock-); the union keeps both.

SECONDARY overlay (separate, smaller): wrong-cognate from over-merge (minster->minister cluster 44278; old->yule 98-member cluster 358585) = wyrd-h2lv cluster-splitting; and empty grids (wood/-ing 'no reflexes') = coverage gap (wyrd-32t1).
close_reason: MERGED (PR #534). Root cause was NOT clustering: the runtime morpheme-meaning merge (_merged_morpheme_meaning) applied a genuine-WINS rule that discarded self-seeds whenever a cluster/descent reflex existed — dropping the attested generated/own surface (pearroc's 'Park-') and leaving only the etymological cluster reflex ('parrock'). Fix: merge now UNIONS self-seeds with genuine; _era_grid(own_surface=) narrows the PRESENT-DAY stage to the surface the instance used (generate=generated surface=B; explain=decomposed input surface=A3) + keeps the morpheme's OWN canonical form (Gemini HIGH: no-present-day-stage families like norse/latin). Verified on bundle: pearroc/Park->[parrock,Park-]; tūn/-ton->[-ton,toun,toune,town,towne] (no ~120 flood); mynster/minster->[minister,-minster,Minster-]; hryggr own-form preserved. Runtime-only, no bundle rebuild. Reviews: generator-contract (no P1/P2, determinism stable 5 hashseeds, era-render path uses per-usage meanings not merged), test-coverage (gaps filled), Gemini HIGH fixed. Full suite 4864. SECONDARY remaining: wrong-cognate noise (minster->minister) = cluster over-merge = wyrd-h2lv. NOTE: ships with a Lambda CODE deploy (not runtime-DB publish).

title: Cognate-cluster over-merge pollutes era-grid (proto fan-out + spurious descent edges)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the recurring era-grid 'whack modern' noise, one layer above the reflex-audit (wyrd-862b). cluster_cognates' transitive closure over etymon_descent over-merges etymologically-distinct words into one cognate cluster, so a morpheme's era-grid surfaces unrelated modern forms.

TWO mechanisms (confirmed):
1. PROTO-FORM FAN-OUT HUBS (dominant): a proto-etymon with over-broad inheritance children unifies distinct words. e.g. itc-pro:*wolwumen -> {vallis(valley), vallum(wall), valgus, vulgus(crowd), vulva, volume} pulls old-french:val -> vale into the same cluster as vulva/valgus/volume.
2. SPURIOUS DIRECT DESCENDANT EDGES: e.g. old-english:hām -> 'am'/'om' inject AM/om as reflexes.

BLAST RADIUS (measured 2026-06-07, live lexicon.db):
- 21,694 / 144,510 clusters (15%) contain >=1 proto-form; they dominate oversized clusters (3,827 of 6,869 clusters with >15 members).
- era-grid: ~64% of English-family morphemes have modern reflexes; of those ~82% clean, ~12% mixed noise, ~6% all-noise (=> ~10-18% of filled cells carry some implausible reflex). Examples: hryggr->rucksack, áttján->eighteen, sewgyr->sucrose, heyra->kidney, *lente->Linse.

KEY FINDING — deterministic detection is INSUFFICIENT alone:
- Surface similarity fails: over-merged words ARE orthographically similar (val/vulva/vulgus chain).
- Gloss similarity fails: most over-merged members are GLOSSLESS in the lexicon (val: only 3 of 23 members glossed).
=> Requires LLM-semantic adjudication, mirroring the audit-reflexes pipeline (deterministic pre-screen -> Gemini arbiter -> ledger to _*_audit.jsonl -> prune -> re-cluster; LLM never re-run at rebuild).

RECOMMENDED DESIGN:
- Pre-screen: per cluster, find candidate over-merge bridges (proto hubs with multi-sense children; direct edges between dissimilar attested forms).
- Gemini arbiter: 'are these cluster-mates the same word (share form+meaning across eras/langs)?' using forms + any glosses + language.
- Prune the bad descent edges; ledger verdicts; re-run cluster-cognates; re-export; deploy.
- Consider a fast era-grid display-side plausibility filter as an interim mitigation (low-risk, reuses reflex-audit strip_surface) — deferred per user (deep fix chosen).

Discovered while landing wyrd-vewk (curated modern reflexes, PR #494): the importer's new reflexes surface correctly, but re-export would also surface this pre-existing cluster noise, so deploy is blocked on this.

title: Reflex layer links whole place-names + town-prefixes as 'reflexes' of suffix morphemes (-burnham/Belch- → hām) — root cause of era-grid town pollution
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the recurring era-grid town-name pollution across ALL toponymic suffixes (the wyrd-5olv display fix only MASKS it where a genuine reflex exists).

The reflex table (reflex / reflex_etymon, seeded from L2 data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl) records wrong links: whole place-name surfaces and town-prefix fragments are linked as reflexes of the TAIL morpheme. Confirmed for hām (cognate_id 361245) — 31 reflex rows, of which only ~6 are correct (-ham/Ham-/ham/-hamme-/Hamme-); the rest are bad:
  post (whole -ham towns): -adlam, -burnham, -denham, -isham, -kham, -leatham, -nham, -pham, -hampton  -> hām
  pre  (town prefixes):    Belch-, Daven-, Godman-, Hux-, Ight-, Marth-, Neat-, Somers-, Wickham-       -> hām
  inner:                   -esh-, -mersh-  -> hām
A reflex of hām should be a SPELLING of hām (ham/hamme/home), NOT a toponym that merely contains it. Same shape for tūn (-bolton/-newton -> tūn), and every other productive suffix.

This is the SAME CLASS as wyrd-pilc (wrong reflex_etymon links; old-english:ceole mis-linked to Kettle-). The reflex layer is seed-time (outside run_full_enrichment); fix is a SYSTEMATIC REFLEX-LINK AUDIT/PRUNE: drop reflex_etymon rows whose surface_form is not a plausible spelling of the linked etymon's canonical_form (heuristic: surface dash-stripped should ~equal the etymon canonical or a known spelling variant; a surface that STRICTLY CONTAINS the canonical-as-tail plus a leading morpheme, or a pre-fragment that doesn't contain the canonical at all, is a mis-link). Care: do NOT prune legit short derivational variants. Per user 2026-06-06: if the bad rows trace to a mining/seed pass, fixing the source data (_reflexes.jsonl) is acceptable.

How it surfaces: morpheme_id on each bundle word = the family the reflex links to (_word_morpheme_id in lexicon/bundle/_subject.py); _emit_era_reflexes self-seeds each reflex surface. So bad reflex links -> bad morpheme_id grouping -> town surfaces self-seeded into the suffix's era-grid. No prune-reflex CLI exists yet (link-reflexes only ADDS) — see wyrd-pilc notes.

title: era-grid: morpheme merge unions constructed-compound self-seeds into the parent morpheme (tūn shows 100+ town names as 'modern reflexes')
description:
Root cause of the recurring '-ton modern is whack' + 'X not in its own reflexes' defect classes.

_merge_morpheme_meanings (runtime/proportions.py via meaning.py) unions era_reflexes across every Meaning sharing a morpheme_id. Every English -ton town (-bolton/-newton/-barton/...) carries morpheme_id=old-english:tūn (Wiktionary records each town's etymology as an inheritance edge FROM tūn — bad data: a word CONSTRUCTED WITH the etymon treated as a reflex OF it). Each such entry self-seeds its OWN surface (source='self') into era_reflexes; the merge unions all 118 -> tūn's modern era-grid shows ~125 forms, almost all whole town suffixes.

Confirmed live on staging bundle 2026-06-06T04:26:05Z (reproduced Cross Gatton via POST /api/kenning). Prior fixes (#488 homograph un-merge, #491 foreign-reentry filter, #485 mook self-seed) all targeted cluster/descent/foreign noise and never touched this merge layer, so it kept recurring.

Audit: offenders are exactly the productive toponymic suffixes (tūn=71 compounds, lēah=16, hām=9, feld/hyll/dūn/healh/ford/wudu/land/ceaster/...). No arbitrary content-word surprises.

Fix (lever 1, durable, data-driven): in _merge_morpheme_meanings, per (morpheme,language): if the morpheme has any GENUINE (non-self: cluster/descent/period-form/phonology) reflex, use ONLY those; fall back to self-seeds ONLY when there is no attestation at all. Validated: -ton modern 115->10 clean, 0 morphemes emptied, -ling preserved under -ing (the explicit guardrail). Do NOT add a compound-detector (it would eat legit -ling). The all-self -ing-class residual is a separate follow-up.
notes: PR #492 (kenning/wyrd-5olv-merge-self-seed). Runtime-only fix in _merge_morpheme_meanings; validated -ton 125->10 against staging DB, -ling preserved, 4954 tests pass. Awaiting review.

title: era-grid Phase 2: cognate-cluster descent over-merge (cross-language contamination)
description: Follow-on to wyrd-6hbv (which fixed MEMBER-fold over-merges: merged_into_id/lemma_id homograph conflations like -ton→ton). This is the SECOND over-merge layer: cognate_id CLUSTERING over etymon_descent edges pulls cross-language non-cognates into a cluster (e.g. town→haw:kaona→modern-english:kaona; cid=346202 town cluster has 95+ members/27 glosses mixing real cognates with haw/ny/hi contamination). Reuse the wyrd-6hbv LLM-judge engine but over the descent-edge graph with post-cut BFS verification (failure modes: fan-in needs outbound-edge cut, multi-parent legit nodes, un-glossed proto conductors — see /home/devon/.claude/plans/snappy-juggling-dragon.md Phase-2 section + the earlier Plan-agent analysis). The descent-audit (rd69 #495 / 2wml #496) generated correct verdicts but edge-detach can't split multi-parent deep-proto clusters + judged the wrong layer — empirically 0 era-grid improvement. The WORKING fix is the per-form toponym-reflex audit (wyrd-1wv2): judge each modern era-grid reflex generically ('plausible English place-name element?'), detach non-toponymic -> 82->91% clean, no regressions. title: era-grid: clustering over-merges homographs → giant gloss blobs + garbage modern reflexes
description: Staging QA (2026-06-05). ~9 reports. Distinct homographs are collapsed into one etymon, producing 40-gloss blobs and unrelated 'modern' reflexes. Worst: -ton anchors to modern-english:ton (the WEIGHT UNIT) over-merged with 'CL tone · CL wave, billow · CL back side, bottom · CL Vale, Valley' (Goosemasston, Kettleton, Collweleston, Bushenton 'ton has no reflexes'); -ing is one etymon with ~40 glosses spanning patronymic -ingas + connective -inga- + water-meadow (ON eng) + verb 'inflection of ingān' (Ashing); -bury (Wortherbury 'bunch of just words'), Bank (Cold Bank 'random modern bullshit'), -m (Tredebm 'garbage in modern'), Venn/Green/Cove/Sandral. This is the SYSTEMIC version of wyrd-qp9c (the -don verb hand-fix): the cognate clustering + collapse ledger over-unify homographs / unrelated 'ton'/'ing' words. Needs the broader gloss-overlap edge-quality pass qp9c flagged as 'broader', plus likely splitting -ton/-ing/-bury into their real senses. Related: wyrd-c0a3 (hill/feather-down). Defect IDs: 5d0c5b70(Goosemasston -ton), 333f8c06(-bury), f3ce826a(Bank), 604cadb7(-m), 4fdb8d84(Collweleston -kaona), 0ec42f8c(Green Grey).
notes:

ROOT CAUSE pinned: ALL 4 bundle entries for usage '-ton' have morpheme_id=None + era_reflexes=[] (legacy rando-port shape: keys=meaning/modifier_tags/modifier_type/word). So 'ton has no reflexes' is LITERAL — the -ton morpheme isn't matched to its tūn etymon at export time, so no era_reflexes attach → no era grid. The 35-gloss 'blob' is the rando-port gloss UNION (legit tūn near-synonyms + leaks 'clearing or hill'/'inflection of tōh'). Same for -ing (22-gloss).

So 6hbv splits cleanly:

- RESIDUAL (gloss blobs + 'no/garbage reflexes') = NOT the over-merge and NOT redeploy-fixable. It's the morpheme→etymon linkage + era-reflex coverage layer (-ton/-ing get morpheme_id=None at export → empty era_reflexes). Overlaps wyrd-32t1 (raise era-reflex coverage) + wyrd-uumc (-ing gloss blob). Needs export-side: match the common toponym suffixes (-ton/-ham/-ing/-bury) to their promoted etymon so era_reflexes attach.

title: era-grid: morpheme's own form + modern-era reflex often missing (X not in its own reflexes)
description: Staging QA (2026-06-05, bundle built_at 05:57:55Z). ~10 defect reports: the era-grid for a morpheme shows cluster MATES but not the queried morpheme's OWN canonical form, and morphemes whose cognate cluster has no modern-english member show nothing in the modern column. Examples: Kettleton ('Kettle- doesn't have itself in its reflexes'), Roserow ('Rose- not in own reflexes' — Rose-→old-french:rose has only french/old-french reflexes, no modern), Craswell Fenton ('Cras- isn't in own reflexes' — surface 'cras' vs canonical old-english:cærse, so cærse forms show, not 'cras'), Pelmersholt(-mers-), Goldninging(-ning-), Letstone Hayes(Hayes), Bushenton(-en-), Elmoldent(-old-), Catinglington(-ling-). title: era-grid still leaks verb reflexes: folded tombstone retains stale cognate_id (violates cluster_cognates invariant)
description: Blocks the wyrd-qp9c era-grid fix from being user-visible. After qp9c folds old-english:don → old-english:dūn (merged PR #483), the bundle's -don entry (old-english:dūn) STILL shows div/do/doff/done in modern-english era_reflexes. Root cause: the don TOMBSTONE (id 345326, merged_into_id=346198) retains a stale cognate_id=345328 (the VERB cluster *dōną) with cognate_method='cluster-cognates-v2'. The export's _fetch_family_era_reflexes (bundle/_family.py) calls etymon_era_reflexes for EVERY family member and unions; it rolls the don tombstone into dūn's family and etymon_era_reflexes(345326) reads don's stale cognate_id=345328 → returns the verb cluster's reflexes → unioned into dūn's -don entry. Verified: etymon_era_reflexes(don 345326, modern-english)=[div,do,doff,done]; etymon_era_reflexes(dūn 346198)=[North Downs,deun,doon,doun] (clean). Two-sided cause: (1) clear-enrichment --stage=cognates clears canonical rows only (WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL presumably) — leaves 12 tombstones with stale cognate_id; (2) cluster_cognates writes cognate_id on canonical only and never NULLs tombstones, despite its docstring claiming 'tombstones stay NULL'. 12 tombstones corpus-wide currently violate the invariant. FIX options: (A) cluster_cognates: explicitly NULL cognate_id on all tombstones (merged_into_id IS NOT NULL) at end of apply — enforces the documented invariant, fixes all 12 + future; OR (B) etymon_era_reflexes / _fetch_family_era_reflexes: resolve the etymon through merged_into_id before reading cognate_id (resolve-on-read). (A) is cleaner. After the fix: re-enrich + re-export + deploy. STAGING DEPLOY for qp9c is PAUSED on this — the bundle (scratch/staging-runtime.db) still shows verb forms on -don. General bug: ANY folded etymon whose pre-fold cluster differs leaks its old cluster's reflexes.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #484 (merged). cluster_cognates now NULLs stale cognate_id/cognate_method on tombstones, enforcing the documented invariant. Fixes the era-grid verb-reflex leak that survived qp9c: the don tombstone's stale verb cognate_id was read by the export's per-member era-reflex union. After this, re-run cluster-cognates --apply on the live DB to clear the 12 stale tombstones, then re-export. Tests incl. end-to-end era-reflex leak→fixed.

title: era-grid: self-seed the morpheme's own form so a barren lemma always shows in its own era column
description: _era_grid (runtime/proportions.py:887) builds the col-3 grid ONLY from meaning.era_reflexes (cluster/descent reflexes) and returns [] when empty. A barren morpheme (no cognate cluster, no descent edges — e.g. Mais-, cul-) therefore renders a COMPLETELY EMPTY grid: it shows in zero era columns even though the morpheme plainly exists and was used to generate the name. The morpheme is never seeded onto its OWN grid. Fix: in _era_grid, always include the morpheme's own (primary_language, canonical_form) — parsed from morpheme_id 'lang:form' — as a baseline cell in its own era column (source='self'), seeded onto a copied Meaning so the era_reflex_for/sources_for accessors render it. Then no used morpheme is ever gridless. Runtime-only (no bundle re-emit). Surfaced by user QA on staging post-v3ow.1 (Maissing/Culend defects). Distinct from the same-language duplicate fold (wyrd-v3ow.1) and the cross-era reflex-link gap (-field missing its modern column).

title: Same-language variant FOLD: unify barren path-dependent duplicates into their rich lemma (empty-grid root fix)
description: Surfaced 2026-06-04 via staging defects after the col-3 rebuild: ~14% of generated morphemes show EMPTY era-grids (e.g. -hill, -house, -stone, -ing). ROOT CAUSE (traced): the bare-surface index returns sibling morphemes with DIFFERENT morpheme_ids; _rank_siblings picks a BARREN path-dependent duplicate as 'first' (e.g. old-english:hill id=4632179, cognate_id=NULL, 0 cluster mates, gloss=['hill']) over the RICH lemma (old-english:hyll id=418146, cognate 95911, 42 mates, gloss='A hill, a natural eminence...'), which are UNCONNECTED (0 descent edges). The era-grid uses only first.morpheme_id → empty. Same for stone/stān, house/haus. rogd.9/.15/.16 fixed the 57 CROSS-language reflex LINKs + multi-member unions but NOT these SAME-language barren duplicates (rogd.15's deferred 26 same-language FOLD cases). This is the v3ow fold, scoped to the empty-grid driver. FIX (B, operator-chosen): the SAME-language FOLD analog of rogd.15's reflex_link_detect — detect (barren etymon, rich same-language same-meaning form-similar lemma) UNCONNECTED pairs → LLM same-meaning judge → emit FOLD rows (into: rich lemma) to _collapses.jsonl → apply_collapses tombstones the barren into the lemma → rollup unifies → one morpheme_id → grid resolves to the rich reflexes. Then rebuild + re-emit + re-deploy. PLAN mirrors the rogd.15→rebuild arc. NOT a regression (these were always empty; the rebuild didn't fix them).
notes: SHIPPED to prod via #477 (same-language barren fold, 485 folds). Verified: hill/stone/wood/tre/bury etc. fold into rich lemmas.

title: era-grid: folding a reflex into a poorer-grid ancestor (rogd.9) orphans the reflex's own cluster reflexes
description: Surfaced by the col-3 rebuild re-emit (2026-06-03). rogd.9's family rollup folds a reflex into its ancestor's family (via the rogd.15 inheritance edges). The era-grid is then built from the family ROOT's cognate cluster only — _fetch_root_era_reflexes(root_id) → etymon_era_reflexes keys on the ROOT's cognate_id. When the reflex is RICHER than the ancestor, folding LOSES the reflex's reflexes instead of unioning. Concrete: ledger link old-english:green→modern-english:green; clean dev seed gives modern 'green' a 39-cell grid (its own cluster); with the edge applied, 'green' folds into OE 'green' (1-cell cluster) → grid collapses 39→1. Mirror case welsh:-bridge gains (0→3) when the ancestor is richer. Aggregate dev-seed effect: -293 era-grid cells, almost all from 'green'. FIX: era_reflexes for a merged family must UNION across ALL members' clusters (each member's cognate_id), not just the root's — i.e. wire the family-union into Phase-2's merged record as _era_grid input (the seam rogd.10 explicitly deferred: 'rogd.9 ... hook into Phase-2's merged record as _era_grid input — kept OUT of this PR'). Until fixed, re-emitting the bundle with the 57 edges REGRESSES grids for reflexes richer than their ancestor. rogd.11 (modern pollution filter) verified working independently (64→0). Lexicon currently HAS the 57 edges applied (correct data); backup at ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db.bak-prerebuild-*. The committed seed-runtime.db is UNTOUCHED (emitted only to scratch/).
close_reason: Merged #474. _fetch_root_era_reflexes → _fetch_family_era_reflexes(db, member_ids, root_language): unions etymon_era_reflexes across ALL family members (sorted, best-source dedup, rogd.11 filter preserved) instead of the root's cluster alone. Fixes rogd.9 folding orphaning a richer reflex's grid (modern 'green' 39→1; restored to 40 on re-emit). Broad-but-correct: enriches every multi-member family with distinct member clusters. Review: 4 agents (generator-contract endorsed the broad scope; complexity bounded — max 14 members; db-recon PASS) + Gemini. 1183+ tests + a union test green.

title: SPA: gate the Rewind transform behind a feature flag (default off) so prod can ship with rewind disabled

title: SPA inspector: homograph morpheme across languages picks wrong pronunciation + can't swap to non-first
description: A morpheme whose surface form exists in multiple languages (e.g. '-don' = OE don /doːn/ DOON, OF don /dun/ DUN, Celtic don /dɔ̃/ DO) is matched by BARE form string, not (language, form). Symptoms in col 3: (1) pronunciation guide always shows one fixed entry (Celtic DO /dɔ̃/) regardless of which language the morpheme came from; (2) clicking the 2nd/3rd language's 'don' row jumps back to the first — can't select them; (3) Celtic listed up top. User hypothesis: bare variant passed around (not full variant data), matcher iterates forms and picks first/last match. Fix: disambiguate pronunciation + swap by (language, form), and key swap targets on language+form not just the surface.

title: Two-word name loss: derive_positions strips whitespace, never classifies 'bare'
description:
The real cause of 'WAY fewer two-word names than original'. Source English corpus is 30% two-word toponyms, but the shipped bundle generates only 7% two-word (90% single-word) — a 23-point regression.

Mechanism: derive_positions (wiktextract_corpus_miner.py) FLATTENS each toponym and strips whitespace before classifying positions, so it can never see a word boundary — it only ever produces pre/inner/post, NEVER bare (confirmed: a full re-derive produced pre 3179 / inner 2825 / post 2025 / bare 0). A standalone word in a two-word toponym ('Foo Bar') thus looks like a suffix ('-bar'). Morphemes don't get bare reflexes; the matcher then decomposes a two-word toponym's standalone word as an attachment → a single-attachment word → ungrammatical → removed by the wyrd-zzli emit filter → the two-word toponym vanishes.

The wyrd-zzli filter is CORRECT (it drops 0 at runtime post-A; the shapes it removes genuinely are position-violating per 'position is meaningful'). Do NOT loosen it.

FIX: make decomposition / derive_positions WORD-AWARE — split a toponym on spaces and classify each morpheme WITHIN its word (a full standalone word → bare; word-initial → pre; etc.), so two-word toponyms produce GRAMMATICAL bare/positioned two-word structures that survive the filter and restore the ~30% two-word rate. Found resolving wyrd-5z5j Defect C via the new force-structure tool (forcing two-word shapes renders correctly with A+B — quality is fixed; only the rate is low).
close_reason: Verified resolved by the merged §3 (#414) + position-derived model (#424, wyrd-eyjk). VERIFICATION on the committed main seed: (1) mid-word-capital run-together symptom (ParAliKin/CornnamullacBunarath/EnAmancro) = 0 across 2400 generated names (800 english + 400 each welsh/irish/scottish/breton) — Defect A (collapse-to-bare) is bypassed by deriving position at decomposition time, Defect B (slot-authoritative case) is fixed via index-derived structure + D39 position-form casing; (2) English two-word rate = 30%, matching the ~30% source corpus (was 7% — the 23-point regression / wyrd-7nab whitespace-stripping mechanism is superseded by the now word-aware runtime position derivation). Note: lp3n (over-pooled homographs / PenBilsOne) is a separate over-pooling concern, left open.

title: Morpheme position/case model broken: names collapse to bare, slotted mid-word capitalized
description:
ROOT CAUSE behind the run-together / mid-word-capital names (ParAliKin, EnAmancro, CornnamullacBunarath) and the 'WAY fewer two-word names' regression.

The rando design: a morpheme occupies one of 4 position slots — Word (bare), Word- (pre), -word (post), -word- (inner) — decoded from dash markers by Meaning._set_location (runtime/meaning.py:274). Case rule: word-initial (Word/Word-) capitalized; non-initial (-word/-word-) ALWAYS lowercased. This lets one base form switch slots without storing 4 variants.

DATA confirms it's broken: name-tagged morphemes by position = bare 8932, pre 1, post 0, inner 0. Proper names exist almost only as bare capitalized standalone forms — no positioned variants. So generation has nothing to slot into a pre/inner/post position and drops the bare capitalized 'Buna' mid-word → caps-mid-word run-togethers; and two-word structure weight collapsed (cf the wyrd-zzli grammaticality filter removing ~47% of English structure weight).

FIX (design recorded in DECISIONS D39): the render must derive a morpheme's surface from the SLOT it fills (apply dashes + lowercase for post/inner; capitalize only word-initial bare/pre), NOT from the morpheme's stored case. Investigate Meaning render (runtime/meaning.py __str__ lowercases at :284; the case+position-marker handling is at the caller, per the variant docstring :582) and the proportions generation render. Found during wyrd-ls13 tag review.
notes:
FULL AUDIT (5 passes) — consolidated root cause. TWO independent P0 defects + one P2:

DEFECT A (data): names collapse to bare. position_pref NULL for 100% of etymons (no ingester writes it). derive_positions (wiktextract_corpus_miner.py:977) — the only positioner — is gated WHERE source_id='wiktionary-empirical', excluding the 8759 Briggs personal-name etymons. _synthesize_modern_usage (lexicon/bundle/_emit.py:257-273) defaults reflex-less families to bare CAPITALIZED form AND doesn't lowercase its pre/post/inner branches. Reflex-level name positions are healthy (pre247/post200/inner79) — model works when a reflex exists. Collapse machinery is a RED HERRING (confirmed). Fix: extend derive_positions to name-tagged etymons (union etymon_tag IN male/female/family name with the empirical-citation set) so names get pre/inner/post reflexes via the already-correct _surface_form_for_position; harden _synthesize_modern_usage to lowercase post/inner.

DEFECT B (generation, LOAD-BEARING): slot is NOT authoritative — inverse of D39. Slot-filling exact-matches stored location==slot (_matches_position vector_name_select.py:90; bucket keys proportions.py:291) so a base form fills only its one stored slot. NewName.__str__ (proportions.py:1449-1464, esp :1458 dash-strip-keeps-case, :1462 caps word-initial only) preserves STORED case → mid-word capitals (CornnamullacBunarath). _mimic_case (meaning.py:654-672) keys on stored case too. Fix: render derives dashes+case from the SLOT (post/inner ALWAYS lowercase, cap only word-initial); slot-filling accepts any dash-stripped base form for any slot, transformed to the slot. This likely fixes the symptom even with bare inventory (bare can then fill positioned structure slots).

The render must be the SINGLE owner of positional case — base forms, substituted variants (pick_variant/_pick_surface/_mimic_case), and inflections all stay raw/lowercase until the render applies slot dashes+case. Replace _mimic_case stored-case logic; add variant×position tests (variant in -word- slot must lowercase).

FIX ORDER: B (slot-authoritative render+fill; owns case for base+variants) → A (positioned reflexes for names, restores inventory + two-word weight) → re-eval C. NOTE: 'no space' half is downstream of structure-weight collapse (A), not the render. Validate-meanings hyphen guard (cli/validate_meanings.py:30) should gate the bundle to catch regressions.

title: kenning: vector scoring-mode ignores --tag + tag-only moods (blocks EoL of proportions)
description: Empirical finding (2026-05-30, EoL-proportions evaluation): in --scoring-mode=vector, semantic filters have ZERO effect. generate english --scoring-mode vector --priors-path <sidecar> produces BYTE-IDENTICAL output for: baseline, --tag water, --tag death, --mood grim (confirmed across seeds 7/13/42, -n 6+). Only phonological moods (harsh, noble — which carry a phonological vector) change vector output. Proportions mode filters all of these correctly (tag water → water morphemes sunde/skerr/pul; tag death → different set). Root cause is runtime wiring, not bundle content (proportions reads the same bundle's tags fine): the vector path (runtime/vector_name_select.select_via_vector_scoring eligibility gate + runtime/vector_kenning_adapter.build_request_vector semantic weights) is not applying (a) the D36.6 --tag HARD eligibility gate, nor (b) the tag-mood semantic-axis bias. The sem-axis contribution for a requested tag is literally 0. IMPACT: --tag (water/death/etc.) + semantic moods (grim/pastoral/devotional/mortuary) are core GM-facing proportions features; until vector supports them, proportions CANNOT be retired. FIX: wire --tag as a hard eligibility gate + thread tag-mood semantic_tags into the request vector's semantic axis in the vector path; add a regression test that vector --tag X differs from baseline. Also verify --era/--stratum gates apply under vector. Refs D36.6, wyrd-ecjp.
design:
ROOT CAUSE (scoped 2026-05-30): two distinct mechanisms, not one bug.

1) --tag is not a HARD gate. EligibilityGate (vectors/schemas.py) has fields culture/era_min/era_max/stratum/allowed_pack_tags/excluded_pack_tags — NO required-tag field. build_request_vector routes --tag only into the SOFT register.semantic_tags. build_non_position_eligible filters on era/stratum/exclude_tags/culture-attestation only. So --tag never shrinks the pool. (Note: an exclude_tags HARD path already exists; the include/required path is the missing symmetric half.)

2) The soft semantic axis is structurally powerless over USAGE selection because of the wyrd-bol9 per-usage frequency layer. In select_via_vector_scoring, score() DOES read lemma_tags=frozenset(m.tags) and sem_score fires, but _apply_per_usage_frequency composes final weight = freq[usage] × (score[meaning]/score_sum[usage]). Cross-usage weight = the PROPORTIONS freq table; the vector score only redistributes WITHIN a usage (most usages are single-Meaning). Since sem_score is non-negative (and bs<0 is filtered), the semantic axis can neither filter a usage nor re-weight across usages → zero effect on which morpheme is picked. Phonological registers (harsh/noble) DO show up only because their phon_score can go negative and drop Meanings (bs<0), changing the usage pool.

FIX (two parts):
PART A — --tag hard gate (restores the headline GM knob; small, low-risk, mirrors exclude_tags):
  * add required_tags: frozenset[str] to EligibilityGate (+ validation).
  * build_request_vector: populate gate.required_tags from the tags arg (HARD), distinct from the soft semantic_tags bias.
  * build_non_position_eligible: drop Meanings not carrying the required tag(s) — symmetric to the existing exclude_tags filter.
  * regression test: vector --tag water differs from baseline AND ⊆ water-tagged morphemes (parity with proportions filter_for_tag).
PART B — tag-MOODS soft bias at usage level (grim/pastoral/devotional/mortuary; larger/architectural):
  * _apply_per_usage_frequency must let the semantic axis re-weight ACROSS usages, e.g. usage weight = freq[usage] × f(best/aggregate sem_score for that usage), not just within-usage. Risks bit-stability + changes the vector↔proportions drift; needs tolerance-band thought.

EoL IMPLICATION: Part A alone restores --tag parity (the most-used semantic knob) and is the minimum to stop calling vector semantically-blind. Part B is required for tag-mood parity and forces a design decision: how much should vector DEFER to the empirical frequency table vs let its axes drive usage selection — the wyrd-bol9 anchoring is exactly why vector tracks proportions (KL 0.012) but also why its axes are weak. Full EoL of proportions needs both parts + a pollution pass (single-char (FR Silver) / (unglossed) fragments seen in both modes).
notes:
PARITY MATRIX COMPLETE. Verified --era/--stratum under vector (2026-05-30, converged bundle /tmp/converged-full.db): both change the pool at fixed seed and produce period/stratum-appropriate morphemes (norse-loan stratum yields -by suffixes: Keysby; oe-late era shifts to OE-period morphemes), matching proportions. No code change needed — era/stratum are gates outside vector space (EligibilityGate.era_min/era_max/stratum), threaded _generate_via_vector→build_request_vector→gate and applied in build_non_position_eligible via _matches_era/_matches_stratum; they were wired all along (unlike --tag which had no gate field). 

Vector↔proportions FEATURE PARITY now complete: base/decomposition (KL 0.012, ρ 0.86), phonological moods (harsh/noble), --tag (#390), tag-moods (#392), --era + --stratum (verified). The FEATURE blocker for EoL is cleared.

REMAINING before flipping the default + deleting proportions: (1) corpus pollution pass — single-char (FR Silver) + (unglossed) fragments hit both modes; (2) a head-to-head vector-vs-proportions equivalence/quality pass across the full knob matrix on the converged bundle to confirm no behavioral regression before changing --scoring-mode default and retiring the proportions path.

FIRST-PARTY EXPORT (no scraping/DRM). Lands in etymon/toponym/toponym_etymology/etymon_citation -> DIRECT generation lift (vs Briggs personal_name layer which has no consumer). Largely obviates the Smith pirate question (wyrd-625w) for the bulk place->element data; Smith/VEPN still unique for element-essay depth + rare-element inventory. Check KEPN reuse/licence + attribution requirement.
design:
DECISIONS (operator 2026-05-29):
1. CITATIONS: one primary source 'kepn' + one cited_source 'kepn_external'. Per element per place: always citation(kepn); when the place row has a non-empty ReferenceTitle, ALSO citation(kepn_external) with the raw ReferenceTitle string in context_snippet. No match -> shared 'personal-name' placeholder etymon keeping breakdown ordinals, raw name recorded on element (surface_in_modern/notes) -> review queue for later D25 LLM resolve. PARSER: 8-lang vocab (Celtic[abbrev C]/Latin/OE/ON/Continental-Germanic/OF/ME/ModE)+Unknown; '; '-split with language-lookahead re-join for internal-semicolon glosses; NFC-normalize; validate forms against the 5831-form canonical list (~/.wyrd/sources/kepn/elements_all.txt) -> quarantine non-matching (language-agnostic, not Celtic-specific). title: kenning: POS filter at ingest in mine-wiktextract-corpus (skip function words)
description:
Child of wyrd-smtc (fix mine-wiktextract-corpus pollution). wyrd-a106 (closed) already shipped the redirect-fallback drop + _is_derivative_gloss filter + cleanup CLI. The remaining ingest-side gap from the epic's child list is the POS filter.

ROOT CAUSE: _select_canonical_sense (wiktextract_corpus_miner.py:369) has no part-of-speech filter, so function words (prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, particles, determiners) that surface-match an unaccounted place-name fragment get ingested as wiktionary-empirical etymons — noise in a historical place-name lexicon. The epic's audit attributed a chunk of the ~11% wiktextract noise to function-word + modern_english entries.

FIX: add a POS denylist guard at the top of _select_canonical_sense (the entry dict carries a top-level 'pos' field — confirmed values include prep/conj/pron/particle/det). If entry['pos'] is in the function-word set {prep, postp, conj, pron, particle, det, article}, return None → skip the etymon entirely. Content POS (noun/verb/adj/adv/name/num/suffix/...) pass through unchanged.

This is an INGEST-time fix so a fresh re-mine produces clean data. The complementary modern_english-only drop stays at cleanup time (cleanup-wiktionary-empirical handles 'modern_english + no historical cluster mate').

CONTEXT: surfaced 2026-05-29 during the nuclear rebuild — the rebuild dropped the DB-only wiktionary-empirical layer (rebuild-from-jsonl only replays committed L1/L2; the empirical layer is written directly to the DB by mine-wiktextract-corpus). Operator decision: fix wyrd-smtc (POS filter) FIRST, then re-mine clean to restore the empirical layer de-polluted, then re-export-runtime-db + re-run after-reports. The empirical layer is deeply useful (validated: rando coverage, saints, cleanup-audit found 0 derivative pollution post-a106).

ACCEPTANCE:
- _select_canonical_sense returns None for function-word POS entries.
- Content POS unaffected.
- Tests pin: each function-word POS skipped; noun/verb/name kept; the existing redirect + derivative filters still apply.
- After re-mine: zero wiktionary-empirical etymons with a function-word source POS.

Refs: wyrd-smtc (parent epic), wyrd-a106 (closed sibling).

title: _validated_mentions crashes on non-str form/context after format='json' switch
description:
**Concrete failure 2026-05-23**: Mining started successfully under the wyrd-sj50 \`format='json'\` fix (chunks 1-2 of mawer_stenton_1930_sussex completed in 20-33s), then crashed on a later chunk:

\`\`\`
AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'strip'
File: wyrd/generators/kenning/extractors/toponym_mentions.py:442
form = _sanitize_and_count((m.get("form") or "").strip(), counters)
\`\`\`

**Root cause**: The previous format=<schema dict> mode constrained Ollama's output to the wyrd RESPONSE_SCHEMA, where \`form\` is typed as \`{"type": "string"}\`. With wyrd-sj50's switch to \`format='json'\` (Ollama 0.24+ schema-grammar regression workaround), the server now only guarantees valid JSON — not schema conformance. The LLM occasionally returns \`form\` as a dict or other non-string shape.

\`_validated_mentions\` then calls \`.strip()\` on the value, assuming string. AttributeError aborts the source.

**Why this didn't fail before wyrd-sj50**: server-side schema constraint masked the issue. Now exposed.

**Fix**: type-guard form + context fields in \`_validated_mentions\`. Drop mentions whose form isn't a string. Same for context. region_hint already has an \`isinstance(raw_region, str):\` guard so it's safe.

**Acceptance**:
- Mining doesn't crash when LLM returns non-string form/context
- Such mentions are counted (hallucinations_dropped or new counter) for operator visibility
- Regression test pins each non-str type (dict, list, int)

title: OllamaClient: switch format from JSON-Schema dict to 'json' string (schema-format hang)
description:
**Concrete failure 2026-05-22**: Ollama 0.24+ on the macbook hangs indefinitely on chat requests when \`format\` is a JSON-Schema dict (\`format: {...schema...}\`). Same model + same request with \`format: 'json'\` returns in 500ms. Mining client uses the dict form, so every chunk request times out.

**Probe results**:
- \`format: 'json'\`: 500ms ✓
- \`format: {'type':'object'}\`: timeout >90s ✗
- no format: 400ms ✓
- /api/generate (no chat structure): 285ms ✓

The schema-constrained-output path in Ollama 0.24+ appears to have a regression with gemma4:26b. User has confirmed they upgraded Ollama yesterday — so latest brew Ollama on macOS has this bug.

**Fix**: switch OllamaClient.chat_json to send \`'format': 'json'\` (legacy mode). Schema is still passed as a parameter for API compatibility and could be used for future server-side constraint when the upstream bug is fixed. Post-hoc validation in \`_validated_mentions\` already validates structure client-side, so losing server-side schema enforcement is safe.

**Acceptance**:
- OllamaClient sends format='json' in /api/chat requests
- Tests pin the new payload shape
- Mining works end-to-end against the macbook's gemma4:26b
notes: Merged via PR #341 (squash). format='json' replaces schema dict — Ollama 0.24+ schema-grammar regression workaround.

title: kenning: drop 'keep first redirect' fallback + apply derivative-gloss filter in mine-wiktextract-corpus + cleanup existing polluted etymons

title: [EPIC] kenning: fix mine-wiktextract-corpus pollution (root-cause of wyrd-hitl symptoms)
description:
Root-cause investigation 2026-05-23: the wyrd-hitl epic's symptoms (modern_english noise, derivative-only glosses, function-word entries polluting buckets) all trace back to ONE pipeline: 'mine-wiktextract-corpus'.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND:
- mine-wiktextract-corpus ingests every Wiktionary entry that surface-matches an unaccounted place-name fragment
- Bypasses the D4 ≥3-scholar-witness gate by design ('treated like rando-port')
- _select_canonical_sense in wiktextract_corpus_miner.py:369 tries to SKIP redirect senses (alt-of / form-of tags) but has a FALLBACK that keeps the first redirect anyway when ALL senses are redirects — comment says 'better than skipping the morpheme entirely', which was the wrong call
- No POS filter — function words (prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns) get ingested
- No application of our existing _is_derivative_gloss classifier

SCALE OF POLLUTION (audit 2026-05-23):
- 23% (15490 of 66837) of bundle (subject × word) entries cite wiktionary-empirical
- ~50% of those have derivative-only glosses (~7465 entries)
- ~35% are modern_english (~5459 entries — modern homographs in a HISTORICAL place-name lexicon)
- Net: ~11% of the entire corpus is wiktionary-empirical noise

CHILD TICKETS (file as work proceeds):
- Drop the 'keep first redirect anyway' fallback in _select_canonical_sense
- Apply _is_derivative_gloss filter at ingest in mine-wiktextract-corpus
- Add POS filter (skip preposition/conjunction/pronoun/particle/determiner) at ingest
- One-shot DB cleanup: DELETE wiktionary-empirical etymons matching {derivative gloss OR modern_english-only OR POS=function-word}, then re-export bundle
- Re-run wyrd-36ez semantic audit on cleaned bundle to verify noise gone

WHY THIS MATTERS:
The wyrd-hitl rank/filter pass + derivative-text suppression hide the symptoms in the SPA but don't fix the DATA. This epic fixes the data itself. Once clean, the audit should surface only LEGITIMATE suspects (real homonyms hiding as polysemy, etc.) which can then be hand-resolved.

All children shipped: redirect-fallback drop + derivative-gloss filter + cleanup CLI (wyrd-a106), POS filter at ingest (wyrd-33cv / #378), one-shot DB cleanup (−12,410 polluted etymons during the rebuild restore), and the wyrd-36ez semantic-audit re-run. title: [EPIC] kenning lexicon: corpus-quality bundle pass — Meaning ranking + filtering + classification
description:
Single epic for the 5+ corpus-data tickets surfaced during 2026-05-22 SPA QA. All trace back to the same root: Wiktionary corpus mining produces noisy multi-meaning buckets, and the SPA/CLI surface them verbatim. Fix as a coordinated bundle-rebuild pass instead of independent band-aids.

CHILDREN:
1. wyrd-ubbc (P3): 'Hill → cyln' cluster collision
2. wyrd-aizb (P2): 'alternative form of X' redirect glosses (1878 entries)
3. (P2): semantic-vs-derivative text split ('-sing- → singular imperative of singan')
4. (P2): tag-vs-meaning audit ('-y' tagged animal; 'Dar-' tagged architecture)
5. (P1): within-bucket Meaning ranking ('Green-' surfaces obsolete gree instead of OE grēne)
6. (P1): modern_english entries are noise for British place-name generation

PLAN (rough):
- Phase 1: classify all glosses in meanings.json (semantic / derivative / redirect / homograph). Adds metadata; no behavior change yet.
- Phase 2: ranking pass — when multiple Meanings share a usage bucket, rank by signal density (attested-years, tag count, era stratum). SPA's meanings_list[0] becomes the BEST Meaning, not the first-inserted.
- Phase 3: filter pass — drop modern_english Meanings when an older-stratum entry exists in the same bucket (with operator opt-in to surface modern entries for analysis).
- Phase 4: resolve alt-form chains at mining time (substitute target's meanings for 'alternative form of X').
- Phase 5: tag audit — flag morphemes whose tags don't intersect with their meanings' semantic categories.

Each phase ships as its own PR; the bundle is rebuilt at the end. SPA needs zero changes (the data quality improves transparently).

title: kenning lexicon: modern_english entries are noise for British place-name generation — drop or deprioritize when an older-stratum etymon exists
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22 (stronger framing of the wyrd-... 'Green- → step/rung' ranking issue): for British toponym generation, modern_english entries are almost always WRONG — they're modern homographs of place-name morphemes whose real etymology is OE/Norse/Celtic/OF.

The user is generating English/Scottish/Welsh/Irish/Breton TOWN names. The etymons are pre-modern. Modern English entries in the bundle add noise (obsolete dictionary senses like 'gree'=step, 'foot'=foot-measure, 'ham'=actor) that don't correspond to the place-name usage and surface in the SPA as misleading first-Meaning glosses.

RECOMMENDED FIX: at bundle-load time (or mining time), drop modern_english Meanings WHEN a same-usage bucket has any old_english / old_scandinavian / celtic_mix / old_french entry. Only when there's NO older-stratum entry (genuinely modern morpheme like a post-Conquest coinage) does the modern_english fall back to canonical.

Edge cases to handle:
- Some place names DO contain genuinely modern morphemes (Newtown, Newcastle's 'new'). These currently work because the OE 'nēowe' covers it.
- Loanwords that entered English post-Conquest and became place-name elements (rare; can audit).
- The kenning-explain CLI may want to SHOW the modern_english entries for analysis even if they're suppressed from the headline meanings — surface as 'modern English homographs (informational)'.

EVIDENCE: user observation across multiple morphemes today (Green, -y, Dar-, -sing-). modern_english entries consistently produced bad UX. The 'Green- → step/rung' case is the cleanest example: 3 etymons in the bucket (modern_english 'green'/'gree', celtic_mix 'grianán', old_english 'grēne'). The OE entry has all the right meanings + 9 tags + attested 1275. The modern_english entry surfaces FIRST and pollutes the display.

PRIORITY: P1 alongside wyrd-... (within-bucket ranking). Either fix could unblock the user; both is best.

title: kenning lexicon: rank Meanings within a usage-bucket — 'Green-' surfaces obsolete 'gree=step/rung' instead of OE 'grēne=color/village green'
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22: 'Green-' morpheme inspector shows meanings 'A step, gree or rung… To come to an understanding or agreement.' — those are the obsolete sense of 'gree' (etymologically distinct from the OE color word).

INVESTIGATION: meanings.json has THREE distinct Meaning entries all bucketed under the 'Green-' / '-green' usage key:
1. modern_english 'green' → meanings: [step/rung, to agree]. 0 tags. Maps to 'gree'/'greede'/'greeden' variants — the obsolete 'gree' etymon.
2. celtic_mix 'grianán' → meanings: [Bright, Shining, Sunny]. 1 tag.
3. old_english 'grēne' → meanings: [Green, Village green, green]. 9 tags (color/descriptive/etc), attested 1275.

The SPA's NewName.to_dict() does meanings_list[0] (first wins). The least-useful candidate (#1) is first. The user sees the wrong meaning.

ROOT: bundle iteration order surfaces the noisiest Meaning. Need to rank within a bucket. Ranking signal candidates:
- entries with attested_years > entries without
- entries with more populated tags > entries with 0 tags
- entries with broader meanings (count > 2) > narrower
- entries from era-appropriate source langs (OE for British place names) > modern-english-redirect-to-obsolete

For the SPA, a partial workaround would be to expose ALL Meaning entries (let the user see all 3 etymons) rather than just first[0] — but the real fix is at the bundle (resolve to the canonical sense for British-place-name context).

EVIDENCE: same family as wyrd-aizb (alt-form redirects). Different symptom (wrong-meaning-first vs no-meaning), shared root (Wiktionary corpus mining produces noisy multi-etymon buckets without quality ranking).

Pattern is broad enough to warrant a 'bundle Meaning quality pass' epic: alt-form resolution + semantic-vs-derivative classification + tag-vs-meaning audit + this within-bucket ranking. The compounding noise suggests these aren't independent edge cases.

title: SPA: seed input gets locked after Roll (rolls become deterministic)
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22: clicking Roll with blank seed → server picks random seed → roll.js writes envelope.seed back into appState.seed → seed input now populated → next Roll uses that seed → same name forever.

ROOT: lib/roll.js writes appState.seed = envelope.seed. Intent was to surface what seed was used for display + save + share; effect is to lock the input.

FIX: split into two fields:
- appState.seed = the INPUT VALUE (user controls; blank = random)
- appState.lastSeed = the seed the server used most recently (display + save + share)

Roll writes lastSeed only; the seed input stays blank if the user left it blank.

title: Staged miner crashes on lone-surrogate codepoints from LLM output
description:
**Symptom**: \`wyrd kenning lexicon mine-toponym-mentions-staged\` crashes with \`UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udaaa' in position 148: surrogates not allowed\` when the LLM (Ollama gemma4:26b in this case) returns a string containing an unpaired high-surrogate (U+D800-U+DBFF).

**Trace**:
- File: wyrd/generators/kenning/cli/lexicon/mine_toponym_mentions_staged.py:81 (_write)
- Pipeline: mine_toponym_mentions → on_chunk_mentions=_write → line_fn (json.dumps + utf-8 file write)

**Why this happens**: json.loads doesn't reject lone surrogates, so they enter the ToponymMention.name field unsanitized. The subsequent file write to a utf-8 stream fails.

**Concrete failure 2026-05-21**: Mining run on \`longnon_1920_noms_de_lieu_france_v2\` (French dense gazetteer) crashed mid-source around chunk ~280/396. 6,157 mentions recovered from the in-progress log via recover-inprogress-chunks; ~115 chunks of v2 tail data lost.

**Fix scope**:
1. Sanitize ToponymMention.name (and any other str field) at extraction time in toponym_mentions.py — strip lone surrogates via \`s.encode('utf-8', 'replace').decode('utf-8')\` or similar.
2. Defensive: writer (_write / line_fn) should fail soft on surrogate residue — log + skip rather than crash the whole run.
3. Add unit test feeding a mocked LLM response with a lone surrogate; assert no crash + warning logged.

**Acceptance**:
- Re-running mining doesn't crash on surrogate input.
- Surrogate-laden mentions are either sanitized into valid utf-8 or dropped with a warning, never silently lost without trace.
- Test covers the regression.
notes: Merged via PR #309 (squash). 4-round review loop: 12 agents + Gemini, 18 findings, 16 fixed in-PR, 2 deferred to wyrd-klod + wyrd-4ywt.

Likely sub-tickets (existing + future):

title: Add fantasy_morpheme to alembic + lexicon.sql so init_schema produces a complete DB (rebuild-from-jsonl is currently broken)
description:
DEFECT: ``init_schema`` produces a fresh DB missing the ``fantasy_morpheme`` table. The table is created only by ``schema.migrate_schema`` (the legacy helper path), which ``init_schema`` doesn't call. Consequence: ``rebuild-from-jsonl`` and ``diff-rebuild`` crash on any DB that has fantasy_morpheme JSONL events to replay.

DISCOVERED VIA: validation run after wyrd-fe1v (db-reconstructibility-reviewer landed) and wyrd-11zh (Briggs JSONL rework landed). The user asked for an end-to-end rebuild test; diff-rebuild crashed with::

    sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: fantasy_morpheme

at ``jsonl/build.py:565`` while replaying ``data/mining/_fantasy_morphemes.jsonl``.

ROOT CAUSE: ``fantasy_morpheme`` is the only table created exclusively by ``schema.py`` legacy helpers — every other table in the schema lives in either ``data/lexicon.sql`` or an alembic migration under ``wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/migrations/versions/``. The schema.py helpers themselves are idempotent (``if 'X' not in existing: CREATE``), so they no-op on fresh DBs that ran alembic. But for a table that exists ONLY in the schema.py helper, fresh DBs never get it.

The architectural rule (wyrd-fe1v db-reconstructibility-reviewer) says: ``rm db && rebuild-from-jsonl`` must produce a working DB. This bug breaks that rule.

FIX:

1. Add ``CREATE TABLE fantasy_morpheme (…)`` to ``data/lexicon.sql`` (fresh-install path)
2. Add a new alembic migration (e.g. ``0011_fantasy_morpheme.py``) that creates the table on legacy DBs that ran alembic but not migrate_schema. Revises 0010_briggs_personal_names.
3. Update the migration head-revision test in tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py (0010 → 0011)
4. Leave the schema.py helper in place; it's idempotent and protects DBs that ran the old code path

VALIDATE:

- ``diff-rebuild`` runs to completion against the live DB
- ``rm /tmp/test.db && wyrd kenning lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --db /tmp/test.db --skip-bulk --jsonl-dir data/mining`` produces a DB with fantasy_morpheme rows
- Existing tests still pass

title: Phase 7 bundle export changes (per-lemma phon_vector + empirical_baselines + pack manifest)
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-ecjp.8 — runtime pack overlay shipped, but the bundle-side wiring was explicitly out of scope. Required for ecjp.9 CLI integration to actually load packs from bundles instead of synthetic fixtures.

Work:
1. export_meanings emits per-lemma phonological_vector on each subject (read from lexicon.etymon_consensus.phon_vector_json which kq7w.1 populates)
2. bundle ships empirical_baselines section (per-(culture x position x tag x era) + per-(donor x recipient x position x tag x era) frequency tables — same data dump-empirical-priors already emits as a sidecar JSON; needs either embedding into meanings.json or co-shipping)
3. per-lemma pack-membership metadata + pack manifest format for the pack-catalog
4. existing bundle consumers still load

Why: ecjp.9 needs real pack data, not test fixtures.
notes:
Investigated overnight (session ending 2026-05-20). Three pieces in the ticket are deeper than safe-autonomous scope:

(1) Per-lemma phonological_vector emission has a partial wiring path: runtime/meaning.py:931 already reads word.get('phonological_vector') — the loader contract is in place. The bundle-export side needs a new path through bundle/_family.py (collect phon_vector per descendant_id from etymon.phonological_vector) → bundle/_subject.py:_word_for_reflex (aggregate across linked etymons; pick the lemma's vector or first-non-null) → emit as word['phonological_vector']. Cross-cutting through _family.py + _subject.py; need design choice on multi-etymon aggregation rule.

(2) Bundle ships empirical_baselines: design question — embed in meanings.json (changes bundle JSON shape, requires SPA + Lambda consumer updates) vs co-ship as sidecar (the sidecar form already exists via dump-empirical-priors). Sidecar is far less risky; recommend that path. Needs operator decision on bundle-build script changes.

(3) Pack manifest format: open design question — pack-catalog shape (per-pack entries declaring pack_name, template_donor, template_recipient, lemma_set_pointer, default_weight)? Bundle location? Operator design call.

Recommend operator session for: (a) multi-etymon phon_vector aggregation rule, (b) sidecar vs embedded for empirical_baselines, (c) pack manifest format. Once decided, all three pieces are straightforward implementation work.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #275 (10a: per-language phonological_vector siblings) + PR #277 (10b: priors.json sidecar + packs/ directory conventions, PackManifest schema, pack_loader module, bundled-priors fallback in vector dispatch). 36 new tests across the two PRs (15 + 21). Operator decisions: per-language siblings for phon_vector (max flexibility), sidecar for empirical_baselines (max isolation from meanings.json shape), per-pack directories for pack manifest (max flexibility for large pack collections). Authoring-side bundled priors.json + actual pack data are operator workflow steps (not code work); pack CLI wiring lives in ecjp.11.

title: Stage-1 miner loses all in-progress mentions on SIGTERM mid-source
description:
DEFECT: wyrd kenning lexicon mine-toponym-mentions-staged accumulates per-chunk mentions in memory and only writes <source_id>.jsonl atomically when the full source finishes. SIGTERM (or crash) mid-source loses ALL chunks processed so far for that source.

EVIDENCE: 2026-05-20 wyrd-x82p run was killed mid-source on joyce_1898_irish_names_vol3 at chunk 313/433 (~3h of inference work). No partial output file exists. The 313 chunks of mentions cannot be recovered; the source must be re-mined from chunk 1.

ROOT CAUSE: wyrd/generators/kenning/cli/lexicon/mine_toponym_mentions_staged.py:558-563 — atomic write happens AFTER mine_fn returns for the whole source. The per-chunk callback on_chunk_done (line 545) is progress-only; no persistence hook for mentions.

REQUIREMENT: A long-running mine MUST persist successful per-chunk mentions to durable storage as they complete, so SIGTERM/crash/power-loss leaves the work recoverable without re-running inference.

DESIGN (proposed):

1. PER-CHUNK LOG: while mining a source, write each chunk's successful mentions to data/mining/phase2/_inprogress/<source_id>.chunks.jsonl as the chunk completes. Each line: {chunk_index, mentions: [...], extractor}.

2. ATOMIC FINALIZATION: on source completion (existing path), atomic-write the canonical <source_id>.jsonl from the in-memory report, then unlink the _inprogress log. Canonical file format unchanged — backward compatible.

3. RECOVERY CLI: add `wyrd kenning lexicon recover-inprogress-chunks` that scans data/mining/phase2/_inprogress/*.chunks.jsonl and promotes each to the canonical <source_id>.jsonl (deduped, sorted). Idempotent. Operator runs this once after a crash before resuming the next mine pass.

4. MINE_FN SIGNATURE: mine_toponym_mentions.py needs a new optional callback parameter on_chunk_mentions: Callable[[int, list[Mention]], None] | None. Called per successful chunk; staged miner wires it to the chunk-log writer.

5. RESUME-FROM-FAILURES PATH: the _run_resume_from_failures function (line 341) also needs the same treatment — it currently appends-with-dedup atomically per source, same loss window.

OUT OF SCOPE for this ticket:
- mid-source resumption (skip-existing-chunks). The recovery CLI promotes incomplete-source work to a usable file; a follow-up ticket can add 'pick up where you left off' behavior on the next mine pass.

ACCEPTANCE:
- SIGTERM during mid-source mine produces a _inprogress/<source_id>.chunks.jsonl with all successfully-completed chunks up to the kill point
- recover-inprogress-chunks promotes that to a valid <source_id>.jsonl identical to what would have been written had the source completed (modulo the unfinished chunks)
- Unit test: simulate SIGTERM after N chunks → verify chunk log has N chunks → recover → verify output is the same as if mine had completed those N chunks
- Integration test: small two-chunk source mined to completion writes canonical file AND deletes the inprogress log

RELATES TO: wyrd-x82p (the killed-run-induced lesson)
close_reason: Shipped via PR #266 (merge commit ded6d70). Crash-safe per-chunk persistence + recover-inprogress-chunks CLI. 16 tests, 3 review rounds, all Gemini comments resolved, CI green. Complexity follow-up tracked in wyrd-81i3.

title: Refactor: cli.py (10239 lines) split by command family
description:
wyrd/generators/kenning/cli.py is 10239 lines and hosts ~150 click subcommands across multiple loosely-related families (lexicon mining, lexicon enrichment, lexicon dump/rebuild/diff, lexicon search/browse/report, generator rebuild-proportions / decompose, mine-fantasy-name, mine-skeat, audit-*, etc.). Every new CLI subcommand adds to the same file and every PR touching the CLI pulls 10k lines into review.

Sibling to wyrd-67fv (lexicon.py split). Surfaced 2026-05-18 in the same conversation — Devon flagged 'cli.py is also unacceptably large' immediately after the lexicon.py ticket.

Why: per the correctness-over-expediency memory, the file is large enough that PR reviewers can't reasonably hold the surface in their head. A click subcommand for project-period-forms has no business sitting next to a click subcommand for fetch-bulk-sources; they share nothing. The growth pattern is also pathological — every new feature adds ~50-200 lines to cli.py rather than to a focused subcommand module.

How to apply: file-only scope; no behaviour change. Proposed structure:
  * cli/__init__.py — the top-level @cli click group; re-exports the @lexicon sub-group so existing 'from wyrd.generators.kenning.cli import cli' still resolves
  * cli/lexicon_mining.py — mine-llm, mine-attestations, mine-skeat, mine-fantasy-name, mine-toponym-mentions-staged, etc.
  * cli/lexicon_enrichment.py — link-lemmas, project-period-forms, classify-stratum, derive-english-shaped, cluster-cognates, decompose, normalize-ocr
  * cli/lexicon_dump_rebuild.py — dump-jsonl, rebuild-from-jsonl, diff-bundle, diff-rebuild, export-meanings, fetch-bulk-sources, push-bulk-sources
  * cli/lexicon_search_browse.py — search, browse, report, stats, audit-*
  * cli/proportions.py — rebuild-proportions + helpers
  * cli/curate.py — curate-etymon, prune-toponym, prune-etymon, set-stratum
  * cli/empirical_priors.py — mine-empirical-baselines, dump-empirical-priors (filed in flight, will get its own home post-split)

Each module exposes a function add_to(lexicon_group) that registers its subcommands on the shared @lexicon click group. Top-level cli/__init__.py calls each module's add_to() at import time.

Acceptance: ruff check . && pytest is green; 'wyrd kenning lexicon --help' lists the same subcommands as before; every CLI integration test still passes (no test changes); new CLI subcommands go to the family-specific module, not the root.

Out of scope: any behavioural change. Strictly mechanical split.

Suggested sequence: (1) extract the click-group plumbing into cli/__init__.py first (smallest change, lowest risk). (2) extract one subcommand family per PR. The families with the lowest cross-family dependency (audit-*, search/browse/report, proportions) ship first; the mining families with helpers shared across commands ship last.
notes:
SLICE PLAN (revised 2026-05-19 after PR #245 clarity-reviewer finding — slice 1 narrowed to pure rename to avoid empty-stub drag-in):

1a. PURE RENAME — cli.py → cli/__init__.py only. Zero content change; git tracks as single rename so blame stays clean. PR #245 (merged). Sets up the cli/ package as a target without adding empty stubs (cli/utils.py and cli/lexicon/__init__.py defer to slice 1b when they have actual content).
1b. SHARED HELPERS + LEXICON GROUP — extract _select_parser_and_run, _load_meanings_data, _readonly_lexicon, _build_llm_client, _build_extractor_client, _DEFAULT_LEXICON_PATH, _RANDO_SOURCE etc. into cli/utils.py. Extract the @lexicon group definition into cli/lexicon/__init__.py with add_to(cli) wiring. Move FIRST family of subcommands as the proof-of-shape (recommend: top-level cli commands generate, rebuild-proportions, add-meaning, unaccounted, explain, rewind, era-map, creature, validate-meanings).
2. Lexicon read-only family (browse, audit-*, search/reverse-search/fuzzy-search, report, stats, language-report, path, era-{reflex,cell,timeline,coverage}, migrate).
3. Bulk sources + dump/rebuild/diff + operator-CSV ingest (~12).
4. Enrichment chain + curation/prune + clear-enrichment + classify/set-stratum + bridges (~18).
5. Mining + review + ingest-LLM + synsets group + export-meanings + final cleanup (~25).

PROCESS LESSONS APPLIED (from wyrd-67fv slice D + slice 1a):
- Pre-push agent sweep (template in AGENT-REVIEWERS.md) BEFORE each slice push.
- Stage files explicitly (git add <paths>) — don't let commit-and-push.sh auto-add.
- Worktree per slice (kenning/wyrd-g143-N-<descriptor>).
- Touch-it-you-own-it: adjacent docstring inaccuracies in code being moved are in-scope per no-deferrals user preference.
- Update AGENT-REVIEWERS.md as extraction lessons surface.
- (NEW from slice 1a) Don't create empty stub modules; defer module creation until the slice that has content to put in it.
- (NEW from slice 1a) Pure-rename slices CAN skip the full pre-push sweep since diff = 0 lines; the importlib-resources-reviewer is the one reviewer that still has signal on a package rename because of the path-shift class of bug (wyrd-67fv slice A).

ACCEPTANCE (unchanged from ticket original):
- ruff check + format clean on every slice
- full pytest green (3,465+ tests)
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon --help' lists every pre-split subcommand
- 'wyrd kenning --help' lists every pre-split top-level command
- 'from wyrd.generators.kenning.cli import cli' resolves
- Test-direct helper '_select_parser_and_run' importable from kenning.cli back-compat shim
