Every subcommand now lives in its own per-module file under cli/ (top-level) or cli/lexicon/ (lexicon group), plus cli/lexicon/browse/ and cli/lexicon/synsets/ nested subpackages. Shared helpers in cli/utils.py. add_to(parent) registration pattern throughout.

title: Refactor: lexicon.py (7272 lines) split by concern
description:
wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon.py is 7272 lines and mixes concerns that should not share a file. Surfaced 2026-05-18 while adding empirical_priors module for wyrd-ecjp.2 — chose to put the new module in its own file specifically to avoid making lexicon.py worse. cli.py has the parallel problem, filed separately so each can ship independently.

Current mix in lexicon.py: DB connection wrapper (LexiconDB class), schema migrations (~15 _create_*_table / _migrate_* helpers + migrate_schema orchestrator), seed-from-meanings, multiple unrelated enrichment passes (link_lemmas, reverse_search_attestations, mine_toponym_attestations, project_period_forms, backfill_citation_pages, plus matcher / fuzzy / classify / shape-english helpers), citation-and-page heuristics (parse_running_header_pages, _normalize_for_quote_match, etc.), and domain-validation logic.

This is correctness-affecting: a 7k-line file makes refactors riskier (review attention truncates), makes new contributors slower to onboard, and erodes the implicit modular contract between enrichment passes that are supposed to be independent.

Why: per the correctness-over-expediency memory, the file is large enough that PR reviewers can't reasonably hold the surface in their head; review attention degrades and design drifts. The wyrd-ami / mine-attestations / project-period-forms / link-lemmas / cluster-cognates passes are LOGICALLY independent enrichment passes that happen to share a DB connection — they don't need to share a file. Schema migration code (init_schema + the 15+ migration helpers) is structurally distinct from enrichment passes and is the file's natural extraction boundary.

How to apply: file-only scope; no behaviour change. Proposed structure (each ~500-1500 lines):
  * lexicon/db.py — LexiconDB class + connection / pragma management + low-level helpers
  * lexicon/schema.py — init_schema, migrate_schema, all _create_*_table / _migrate_* helpers
  * lexicon/seed.py — seed_from_meanings

title: EPIC: vector-driven generator architecture (scenario-pack foundation)
description:
Replace flat per-culture proportions JSONs with composable vector scoring + eligibility gates + scenario-pack overlays. Foundational infrastructure that the fantasy-language epic (wyrd-v2gm) and the narrative-translator epic (wyrd-sreb) both depend on.

Architectural decisions locked 2026-05-16:

D1. Multi-axis vector model. Four scoring axes (phonological/semantic/position/empirical-baseline), each user-tunable. Hard gates (culture/era/stratum/pack-allowlist/pack-tag-filter) live outside vector space as boolean predicates.

D2. Empirical baseline as one of the axes. Drop 'realism' concept; baseline is just another axis with continuous weight, defaulted to 1.0. Auto-blend semantics when register effects engage; pack-weight is INDEPENDENT (doesn't auto-reduce baseline).

D3. Pack lemmas inherit template's empirical baseline (OPTION B). A Khuzdul pack templated on ON->OE uses the ON->OE empirical baseline mining (wyrd-o3rh) as its baseline-axis reference. Bare '--culture english --pack neo-khuzdul' produces historically-shaped output where Khuzdul appears at the rate real Norse loans empirically appeared. Pack-weight is a multiplier on that template-baseline contribution.

D4. Slot-by-slot scoring with D17 cohesion preserved. Replace conditional weight calculation with vector scoring; keep slot structure + cohesion mechanism.

D5. Culture is a hard gate v1. Soft culture blends are future expressivity.

D6. --tag stays. Per Q6 user direction.

D7. Per (culture x position x tag x era) granularity for empirical priors.

D8. Tolerance bands deferred to Phase 6 empirical drift measurement.

Composition rule canonical form:
score(lemma) = phon_w * phon_score(lemma) + sem_w * sem_score(lemma) + pos_w * pos_score(lemma) + base_w * baseline_score(lemma, source). source=native uses empirical-baseline(culture,position,tag,era); source=pack P uses empirical-baseline(P.template_donor, P.template_recipient, position, tag, era). pack-weight scales the pack baseline contribution.

Phases 1-8. Estimated 10.5 weeks. Some phase parallelization possible.

Cross-epic deps: DEPENDS on wyrd-kq7w.1 (per-lemma vectors) + wyrd-kq7w.2 (register-effect catalog). BLOCKS wyrd-v2gm.4 (pack-build), wyrd-v2gm.5 (runtime integration), wyrd-sreb (narrative-translator).

title: Phase A: per-lemma phonological-vector schema + corpus-wide enrichment pass
description:

VECTOR SCHEMA (proposed dimensions; calibrate against phonaesthetics literature):
- cluster_density (CC- count / phoneme count)
- final_fortition (final-stop rate; final-cluster rate)
- vowel_final_bias (proportion of vowel-final syllables)
- soft_consonants (fricative + liquid + nasal share)
- polysyllabic_bias (syllable count / form length)
- palatalization (palatal phoneme share)
- sibilance (s/z/sh share)
- retroflexion (retroflex consonant presence)
- pharyngeal (pharyngeal/emphatic presence)
- vowel_height (mean F1)
- vowel_backness (mean F2)
- stop_vs_continuant (ratio)
- aspirated_voiceless (rate)

Each scalar in [-1, 1] or [0, 1]; normalized against corpus mean per-feature.

title: L2 JSONL dump doesn't capture full DB state — rebuilt bundle is 86% smaller than live
description:
Discovered alongside wyrd-pcsj when running 'lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment' against the live DB and diffing the resulting bundle against the bundle exported from the live DB.

The 'JSONL is source of truth' claim is PARTIAL. Real numbers:

Live DB → bundle:
* 8,630 subjects
* 10,187 canonical decompositions
* 244 fantasy_morphemes
* 36 MB JSON

Rebuilt-from-JSONL → bundle (same export path, same code):
* 1,181 subjects (-86%)
* fantasy_morphemes top-level key MISSING ENTIRELY
* 8,396 canonical_decompositions changed
* 2.8 MB JSON (-92%)

L2 row counts:
* live: 21,969 toponyms / 16,787 citations / 54 sources
* rebuilt: 3,950 toponyms / 7,603 citations / 53 sources
* Toponyms drop -82%, citations -55%, one source vanishes entirely.

Gaps the dump misses (so the rebuild can't recover them):

1. **Full toponym corpus**. The live DB has 21,969 toponyms; data/mining JSONL emits 3,950 on rebuild. Lots of mining sessions wrote toponyms directly to the DB without going through the JSONL dump path, OR the dump-toponym path filters more aggressively than the rebuild can reconstruct from.

2. **fantasy_morphemes pipeline**. The wyrd-vz7f / wyrd-ami fantasy creature data is in the live DB (244 morphemes shipped in the bundle) but produces ZERO output on rebuild — the entire L1+L2 layer for fantasy mining isn't in data/mining/. Probably lives in a separate table (fantasy_*) that has no _type entry in the JSONL row schema, so dump_all_sources skips it.

3. **Grandfather-class subjects**. 8,414 subjects in the live bundle are MISSING from the rebuild. Many are short-form / no-meaning rando-port carve-outs (e.g. '-ing', single-letter morphemes, archaic suffixes) that ride along on rando-port citations. The L2 dump may filter rando-port citations (per _NON_SCHOLAR_SOURCES discussion in wyrd-w3x0), and the bundle export then can't admit these without rebuilding rando-port grandfather state.

4. **One source vanishes** (54 → 53 on rebuild). Need to find which source — probably the wiktionary-empirical source row, which the L1 ingest creates as side-effect rather than dump-explicit.

5. **Citation coverage drift**. -55% on citations means the dump is dropping rows the live DB has. Could be: (a) rows attached to L1 etymons that the dump only writes per-L2-source-file; (b) dedup logic in dump_all_sources that doesn't match the rebuild's dedup; (c) the missing source's citations.

Why this matters: until the dump captures (or explicitly delegates to L1) every L2 fact in the DB, 'rebuild-from-jsonl' produces a strictly smaller bundle than the operator's live DB. A deploy from rebuild would ship a 92%-smaller bundle to production. Currently blocks wyrd-j43l (deploy refresh).

Investigation order (rough):
1. Identify the vanishing source —  between dump and live DB source IDs.
2. Audit jsonl_dump.dump_all_sources for table coverage — does it touch toponym? toponym_etymology? fantasy_*? grep for tables it reads vs the DB schema.
3. For each gap, decide: dump-completer (write the missing _type entries) or L1-pathway (treat as L1-ingest-only, no L2 dump expected — but then accept that rebuild-from-jsonl can't reproduce it without re-running mining).

Acceptance:
* Full rebuild against the live DB produces a bundle within X% of the live bundle's subject count (X negotiable; should not be 14%).
* Diff between live-bundle and rebuilt-bundle is documentable: each remaining difference is either intentionally L1-only or a known data-quality drift, not a dump-coverage gap.
* Regression test: round-trip dump-and-rebuild from a fixture that exercises each previously-missing facet.

Discovered as part of the wyrd-j43l deploy validation. Blocks wyrd-j43l.
notes:
PR #204 merged (commit 61d3f75). Dump-side attestation support landed: _attestation_source_doc_filter routes toponym_attestation rows to source dumps via SQL (O(M) per source), GLOB for case-sensitive prefix matching, NOT IN (SELECT id FROM source) enforces Python-oracle's exact-match-wins priority in SQL. 73 tests pass.

Two PR-review-driven follow-ups filed:
- wyrd-2t28: add dump-side orphan-attestation telemetry (counter/warn)
- wyrd-jr37: add toponym_attestation to DIFF_REBUILD_TABLES + extend _l2_state_snapshot

Phase A2 (operator: re-run dump + commit updated data/mining/*.jsonl files — open_domesday_hull.jsonl will grow from 1 row to ~37K) deferred until ready to validate full rebuild. wyrd-j43l (deploy refresh) still blocked on Phase A2 and wyrd-2thc (fantasy_morpheme round-trip).

title: jsonl_build._insert_etymon fails on L1+L2 etymon overlap during rebuild-from-jsonl
description:
Discovered while running full rebuild against ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db to validate wyrd-hidb against real data.

Repro: 'lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --db <path> --jsonl-dir data/mining --with-enrichment' against a full bulk-source corpus (38 wiktextract slices, ~2M entries) fails at the L2 replay step with:

  sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: etymon.canonical_form, etymon.language
  at jsonl_build.py:157, in _insert_etymon

Root cause: rebuild-from-jsonl runs L1 ingest first (8.16M forms written across 2.37M etymon rows), then L2 replay. L2 JSONL files include etymon refs that the wiktionary-empirical mining (wyrd-4hx7) created against L1-ingested etymons. When _insert_etymon tries to INSERT those L2 rows, they conflict with the existing L1 rows.

The existing _merge_etymon handles merge across multiple L2 files in memory, but the resulting merged dict is INSERTed via plain INSERT — no handling for L1-already-wrote-this-row case.

Why none of our existing tests caught it:
* Phase 3 test (wyrd-xrnw) uses synthetic fixture with no L1 ingest
* wyrd-alzd test same  
* wyrd-w3x0 diff-bundle CLI tests use --skip-bulk, so the L1+L2 overlap path is never exercised

Fix: change _insert_etymon to handle the conflict gracefully — INSERT OR IGNORE, then on conflict SELECT the existing id and UPDATE non-key scalar columns with the L2 payload (matching _merge_etymon's last-write-wins semantics for scalars). The glosses/tags INSERT OR IGNORE logic already handles row-already-exists.

Add a regression test: build a synthetic fixture that pre-populates an etymon (simulating L1 ingest) into a clean DB, then runs build_from_jsonl with JSONL referencing the same etymon ref. Should not raise; should produce a merged row with glosses/tags union and L2 scalar overrides.

Blocks wyrd-j43l (deploy refresh) — without this fix the documented one-command rebuild path is broken on real data.
close_reason: L1+L2 etymon merge fix merged in PR #203 (d276c742). _insert_etymon converted from plain INSERT to INSERT OR IGNORE + on-conflict SELECT + UPDATE non-key scalars + INSERT OR IGNORE on glosses/tags. Matches existing _merge_etymon semantics (last-write-wins for scalars, set-union for lists) extended across the L1→L2 boundary. 4 regression tests pin: merge-on-overlap, L2-overrides-L1-scalars, defensive BuildError raise on schema divergence, glosses/tags set-union dedup. 2-round review loop with 1 Gemini + 5 agents; 3 deferred refactors bundled into wyrd-0pkm.

title: JSONL-as-source-of-truth foundation (per-source × per-row-type)
description:
Strategic shift: move lexicon authoring/curation from SQLite-primary to JSONL-primary. SQLite becomes a rebuildable build artifact; JSONL files in git become the durable source of truth. Per user 2026-05-12 — pattern adapted from beads (.beads/issues.jsonl).

## Architecture (4 layers)

L1: Raw external sources (gitignored, sources/) — wiktextract dumps, Hull MDB, scraping outputs. Re-downloadable.

L2: Curated derivatives (data/mining/*.jsonl, IN GIT, SOURCE OF TRUTH):
- One JSONL file per source, e.g. data/mining/mawer_1920_northumberland_durham.jsonl
- Mixed _type discriminator per row — see schema below
- ~30-50 source files total
- Each source's contribution lives in ONE file (its complete record)

L3: SQLite DB (~/.wyrd/lexicon.db, gitignored, build artifact) — rebuilt from L2 + derived passes (decompose, project period-forms, cluster).

L4: Runtime bundle (data/runtime/meanings.json + proportions + place_names, in git) — unchanged contract for lets-roll consumers.

## Row types (v1)

Each L2 JSONL row carries a _type field:

- etymon: canonical_form, language, glosses[], tags[], ipa?, stratum?, lemma_ref?, inflection?
- citation: etymon_ref, page?, attested_year? (the etymon ↔ source link)
- toponym: modern_name, country, region
- attestation: toponym_ref, form, date_year, page?
- etymology_element: toponym_ref, etymon_ref, ordinal, inflection?, surface_in_modern?
- etymon_descent: parent_ref, child_ref, edge_type
- etymon_link: (cross-file disambiguation, future)

## Refs (cross-file identity)

Stable string keys:
- etymons: language:canonical_form (e.g. 'old-english:cot')
- toponyms: modern_name@region (e.g. 'Cottesmore@Rutland')

Build pass resolves refs → integer FKs at load.

Same key = same entity by default (cross-source auto-merge). Set-like fields (glosses, tags) union. Scalar fields (ipa, stratum) use source-priority resolution + audit-log conflicts. Homonym escalation: language:cot:1 / language:cot:2 disambiguation suffix when real collisions surface.

## Curation = direct JSONL edits

Lemma normalization, language retag, dead-rando prune are git commits editing the JSONL files. No overlay-overrides layer. Git history is the audit trail.

## Acceptance criteria

1. JSON Schema files (data/schemas/etymon.schema.json etc.) for IDE + CI lint.
2. wyrd kenning lexicon dump-jsonl — exports current DB into data/mining/<source>.jsonl per source.
3. wyrd kenning lexicon rebuild-db — fresh SQLite from data/mining/*.jsonl + derived passes.
4. Round-trip test: dump → rebuild → semantic-identical DB.
5. Commit the dumped JSONL as canonical L2 state. From this PR forward, JSONL is source of truth; new ingesters write JSONL primary.

## Out of scope (follow-up tickets)

- Convert existing ingesters to JSONL output (Domesday, scholar gazetteers, wiktextract, decompose) — per-ingester tickets.
- Lemma normalization pass against dead-rando — runs against JSONL.
- CLI inspect tooling for browsing the corpus.
- OS Open Names / Hundred Rolls / Speed / Hearth Tax ingests — write JSONL output per the new pattern.
- Cross-era surfacing in dashboard.

## Why this matters

- DB becomes disposable; corruption is recoverable (rebuild from JSONL).
- Branching workflow for risky operations = git branches on JSONL files.
- Per-source PRs naturally show what each source contributed.
- Provenance preserved at every level (which source said what).
- Eventually retiring rando-port = remove rando-port.jsonl + rebuild.

title: Generator: tighten 'inner' location semantics so inner-only morphemes don't appear at word boundaries
description:
Bug surfaced 2026-05-09 in generated output post-wyrd-eni4 bundle: names like 'donhole', 'nwydmillate', 'welsea wood', 'back houselacesranfield' contain morphemes like -don-, -hole-, -mill-, -house- (inner-only, both sides dashed) at the START or END of a word. Inner morphemes should appear strictly in the middle of compounds.

Root cause: trie_matcher._location_allows treats 'inner' as 'no anchor constraint' (matches anywhere). Original Rando-port semantics — preserved when porting to the trie. With the new 8490-subject bundle (4.5× growth post-wyrd-eni4) there are many more inner-only morphemes, so the boundary-permissive matching surfaces visibly in generation.

The cascade:
1. Matcher allows inner at position 0 / position len(word) → corpus decomposition records bad parses
2. Bad parses bake into proportions.json structures (location='inner' at boundary slots)
3. Generator replays the structures → output contains inner-leading words

Fix: tighten _location_allows so 'inner' requires start > 0 AND end < word_length. Then re-run rebuild-proportions to clean up the structures.

Effects:
- Some corpus decompositions that currently work via inner-at-boundary will fail. Per-culture perfect-rate drops slightly.
- Generation output stops producing inner-leading words.
- meanings.json bundle is unchanged (this is matcher-side); only proportions.json regenerates.

Acceptance:
- New unit test: a 4-char word where the only matching morpheme has location='inner' returns no decomposition (or at minimum, no decomposition where that morpheme is at start or end).
- rebuild-proportions for all 5 cultures completes without OOM.
- Sample generation output: 50+ generated names per culture, no '-foo-' pattern at word start (visible in description() output, not in the dash-stripped result string).
- COVERAGE.md snapshot appended with new perfect-rates.

title: rebuild-proportions OOMs on 8490-subject bundle (algorithmic scaling bug)
description:
During the wyrd-eni4 deploy chain (2026-05-08), rebuild-proportions on the post-epic bundle (8490 subjects, up from prior 1879) consumed 16+ GB resident on the Scottish corpus (~2,321 names) before being OOM-killed. That's wildly out of line with the data size — 7× memory scaling for a 5× bundle growth on a corpus of only 2K names suggests an O(N²) or O(N×M) somewhere in the decompose / score / accumulate path.

Prior data points (from COVERAGE.md):
- 2026-05-05 bundle (1697 subjects · 2831 modern_usages) ran rebuild-proportions on all 5 cultures without issue.
- 2026-05-07 bundle (1879 subjects, post-wyrd-1cjg) same.
- 2026-05-08 deploy-chain bundle (8490 subjects) OOMs on Scottish at 16+ GB.

Investigation surface:
1. cli.py:_decompose_corpus → calls Name.find_meaning(word_db) per name. The per-name matcher walk should be O(name-length × bundle-trie-depth), bounded.
2. Name.find_meaning(reduce=True) — inspects every candidate decomposition before reducing. Cartesian product of (Meanings per slot)^slots could explode if many slots have many Meanings.
3. resolved_names list accumulates ALL Name objects in memory; each carries decomposition metadata.
4. _proportions_from iterates resolved_names again — additional O(N) but doesn't accumulate.
5. The meaning_db itself (via load_meanings) registers shadow Meanings for inflected forms (wyrd-lx8). With link-lemmas adding ~6K new linkages this session, shadow-Meaning count grew. But linear in K, not problematic at K=6K.
6. Suspect: per-Meaning data structures (variants, inflections, citations, attested_years, english_shaped, original_script, transliteration, pronunciation, stratum, era_reflexes) are deeply nested dicts/lists. A bundle 5× larger may push aggregate Python-object overhead well past 16GB RES depending on the variant/inflection pool size per Meaning.
7. New since prior runs: 441K text_match rows were ingested via wyrd-vx09 mine-wiktextract-forms; export-meanings projects these into per-Meaning _variants pools. The Meaning.variants dict could now hold thousands of entries per morpheme for high-traffic Welsh/Irish lemmas, which scales by language-coverage.

Most likely culprit: the variants pool expansion from forms-mining. _variants per-Meaning was previously bounded by reverse-search/fuzzy-search outputs (~OE/ON only, low volume). After wyrd-vx09 ingested 441K rows and export-meanings projected them, every Welsh/Irish/Celtic/French/ME Meaning's variants list can be huge. The runtime decomposer doesn't actually USE variants for decomposition — they're only sampled in name generation under --spelling-variety > 0. So the memory cost is dead weight during rebuild-proportions.

Quick-test hypothesis: re-run rebuild-proportions with the wiktionary-forms variant rows EXCLUDED from the bundle (spike: filter source='wiktionary-forms' from _fetch_member_variants temporarily). If RES drops significantly, the variants-pool-size hypothesis is confirmed.

Acceptance criteria:
- rebuild-proportions runs to completion on the post-epic bundle for all 5 cultures within 8GB RES (the prior steady-state).
- Corresponding numeric output (perfect/total) matches expectations on a regression spot-check against the 2026-05-07 baseline (small lifts expected from new linkages, NOT regressions).
- A test pinning RES under a synthetic 10K-subject bundle would lock the fix.

Blocks wyrd-b7fo (which blocks the Lambda deploy step of wyrd-j43l). Bundle re-emit cannot ship until rebuild-proportions completes.
notes:
Root cause confirmed (2026-05-08): the OOM is in
trie_matcher.py:all_decompositions during canonical_decompositions
on the 58-character Welsh village name
'Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwyllllantysiliogogogoch'.

The walk() inner function memoizes ALL results per position into
``cache[pos]``. Memoization correctly bounds RECURSION depth, but
the LIST CONTENT at each position grows multiplicatively — every
match at pos i × every cached decomposition from pos j gets stored.
For a 58-char input with many overlapping morpheme matches at each
position, the cache fills with millions of decomposition lists.

Profile data:
- Welsh corpus's other 1915 names: <200 MB RES total during decomp
  (~200 KB / 50 names baseline rate).
- Single name 'Llanfairpwll...' at index 913: RES exploded from
  175 MB to 8.4 GB+ on its own (and would have continued).

Fix path: rewrite canonical_decompositions to score-prune during
the walk — at each position, keep only decompositions tied for
'best' (lowest unaccounted_chars + fewest morphemes). Don't
enumerate all alternatives just to filter at the end.

Sketch:
    def walk_best(pos: int) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], list[list]]:
        ...
        # Collect candidates from match-branches + skip-branch
        # Score each, find min, return (min_score, all_tied_at_min)
        # Memoize: cache[pos] = (best_score, best_decomps)

This bounds memory because at each position the candidate count is
small (typically 1-3 ties), not exponential. Llanfairpwll... should
produce ~1 canonical decomposition (Llan + fair + pwll + gwyn + ...)
not millions.

all_decompositions for KenningExplain still has the same explosion
risk on long inputs but that path is interactive; a length cap with
a graceful fallback ([[word]]) would keep the explainer responsive.

Workaround shipped: the village removed from welsh_place_names.json
(wyrd-v8x0 tracks restoring it post-fix). rebuild-proportions
should now complete on welsh.

Acceptance:
- canonical_decompositions on the 58-char village input completes
  in <1s with <10MB RES delta.
- all_decompositions on the same input either bails gracefully
  (returning [[word]]) or completes with a reasonable hard cap
  (e.g. 10K decompositions max).
- Test pinning the behavior added to test_trie_matcher.py.

title: Language-quality dashboard: per-language metrics + grading methodology
description:
Phase 0 of wyrd-eni4 (gap-closing epic). BLOCKS the rest of the epic: the dashboard establishes the methodology for measuring impact and the baseline against which we evaluate the gap-closing work.

== Goal ==
A reproducible CLI command (e.g. 'wyrd kenning lexicon language-report' or 'wyrd kenning lexicon dashboard') that emits a per-language quality scorecard. Same command, run before and after each phase, gives us measurable lift. Output: markdown table for human review + JSON for programmatic consumption.

== Methodology ==
English is the deepest corpus; treat its tag profile as the 'reference distribution' for what semantic classes a place-name corpus draws from. Score each other language's coverage of that profile.

Top English tags (from english_proportions.json tag_marginal — verified):
  architecture (4835), topography (4287), social (3471), descriptive (2726),
  plant (2189), agriculture (2008), water (1366), animal (1218),
  measurement (1199), geology (1169), religious (1051), tree (940), ...
Use the top-15 as the 'reference semantic profile' (covers ~95% of tag mass).

== Per-language metrics ==

A. Corpus depth (lexicon DB)
  - Total etymons in this language (etymon table)
  - Promotion-eligible (≥3 witnesses via etymon_consensus view)
  - Average witnesses per morpheme (avg consensus.witnesses)
  - Sources contributing
  - Sources with ≥10 etymons in this language (signal of robust source coverage)

B. Bundle representation (meanings.json)
  - Words with this language sibling: N (% of bundle subjects)
  - Subjects whose words contain at least one entry in this language

C. Semantic-profile coverage (vs English reference)
  - For each top-15 English tag class: does this language have ≥1 subject tagged it? Y/N + count
  - Coverage rate: M/15 = X%
  - Per-tag morpheme count vs the English count (gap visualization)

D. Inflection coverage (D8)
  - Lemmas (etymon.inflection IS NULL) in this language
  - Lemmas with ≥1 linked inflected child via etymon.lemma_id
  - % of lemmas with inflections
  - Distinct case labels present

E. Spelling-variant coverage (D18)
  - Etymons with ≥1 etymon_text_match.matched_form ≠ canonical_form
  - % of total etymons in this language

F. Era-reflex coverage (D33; the time-travel axis)
  - Family chain context (e.g. 'old-english → middle-english → early-modern → modern' for English; 'old-welsh → modern-welsh' for Welsh; note terminal-at-this-end where applicable)
  - For lemmas in this language:
    * Tier 1 (cognate cluster mate in another era): N (%)
    * Tier 2 (descent edge to younger era): N (%)
    * Tier 2-back (descent edge from older era): N (%)
    * Tier 3 (period-form projection): N (%)
    * Tier 4 (phonology-rule reachable; available post-wyrd-98cs): N (%)
    * ANY era reflex (union): N (%)
  - For each era cell (e.g. 'oe-late', 'me', 'emode', 'modern' for English): N lemmas with reflex IN that era

G. Stratum coverage (D32, where applicable)
  - Etymons classified into a stratum bucket: N (% of total)
  - Per-stratum row counts

H. Decomposition rate (per-culture; if culture exists for this language)
  - From rebuild-proportions stderr line: perfect / total / rate

I. Source-attribution depth
  - % of etymons with at least one citation
  - Average citations per etymon

== Grading rubric ==
Each axis gets a letter grade A-F via thresholds:
  A: ≥75% / strong absolute count
  B: 50-75%
  C: 25-50%
  D: 10-25%
  F: <10%
Plus an overall language grade as the unweighted mean letter grade across axes.

Each grade carries a 'next-action' hint: e.g. 'low Tier-1 cognate coverage → mine a comparative grammar' or 'low semantic-profile-coverage on water tag → seek hydrography sources'.

Treat 'terminal' designations gracefully:
  - Proto-Celtic / proto-Germanic etc.: no older-era cell expected; Tier-2-back not penalized.
  - Modern English: no younger-era cell expected; Tier-2-forward not penalized.
  - Use a per-language config to mark the historical-chain endpoints.

== Output ==
Two formats from one command:
  - Human: markdown report — one table per language + an overall summary table at top.
  - Machine: JSON snapshot of every metric + grade, timestamped, schema-versioned. Persist under wyrd/generators/kenning/data/language_quality/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json so the trend over time is preserved.

== Phasing ==
This ticket scopes the design + Phase 1 (metrics CLI emitting data + markdown). Phase 2 (grading thresholds + recommendation hints) and Phase 3 (per-mining-run hook to auto-emit a snapshot) can land as follow-ups.

Acceptance for Phase 1:
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon language-report' runs against the live DB and emits markdown + JSON for at least these languages: english, old-english, middle-english, early-modern-english, welsh, old-welsh, irish, scottish-gaelic, breton, old-french, latin, old-norse.
- Each language card carries metrics A-I (with N/A where the axis is structurally inapplicable).
- Smoke verification: numbers match what the audit (wyrd-wl35) found for English (38.7% time-travel, ~407 inflections, ~308 variants, etc.).

Audit context: wyrd-wl35.
notes:
Refinements per user 2026-05-08:

1. Promotion-eligibility threshold is PER-LANGUAGE, not global ≥3. Many languages (Welsh, Irish, Breton, Old Welsh, Old Norse) have far fewer source materials; a flat ≥3 effectively excludes them. Phase 1 metric A surfaces the language's own threshold in the output ('promotion-eligible: N/M [threshold=K]'). Requires reading wherever the existing default ≥3 is hard-coded and either (a) introducing a per-language config on the lexicon side, or (b) Phase-1: computing 'promotion-eligible at threshold K' for each of K=2,3 and reporting both, deferring the per-language config to a follow-on if it's not already present.

2. Metric C (semantic-profile coverage) — Phase 1 keeps the tag-marginal-hit-rate approach (does language have ≥1 morpheme tagged top-15 English tag X?). The richer 'per-meaning catalog' (catalog meanings INSIDE each subject so we can estimate meaning-space coverage, not just tag-class coverage) is a deliberate follow-on. Phase 1 ships the tag axis; meaning-axis is filed as a sibling ticket after Phase 1 lands.

These two memories saved: promotion-thresholds-per-language-d4-s-3-witnesses, dashboard-semantic-coverage-meanings-catalog-follow-on-for.

title: EPIC: gap-closing & coverage-quality initiative
description:
Initiative driven by 2026-05-08 end-to-end audit (wyrd-wl35). The audit found ~80 closed tickets shipped a lot of capability in code, but several major surfaces are paper-only or partially wired. This epic coordinates the close-the-gap work, gated on a per-language quality dashboard so we can both prioritize the work AND measure its impact.

The audit's headline numbers:
- 38.7% of bundle etymons can time-travel today; 61.3% gap.
- ~7-9% of bundle morphemes carry inflection / variant data, and almost all of that is OE / Old Norse — Welsh / Irish / Celtic / French inflection pools are near-zero.
- Fantasy creature pipeline: 244 etymons mined and linked, but no Generator / SPA / public CLI consumes them.
- Single biggest deploy unblock: the wyrd-j43l bundle re-emit gates 4 shipped features (KenningRewind era progression, KenningEraMap, --stratum filter, KenningExplain canonical decompositions, joiner pool).
- Highest-leverage idle capability: phonology_rules.py (4 cells shipped) is dead code — could close most of the 61% time-travel gap as a Tier-4 fallback in etymon_era_reflexes without any new mining.

Order of work:
- Phase 0 (BLOCKING): Language-quality dashboard (filed separately). Establishes the methodology + baseline so subsequent work is measurable.
- Phase 1: Bundle dict-shape migration (wyrd-c1vq) — unblocks joiners + canonical decompositions in explainer + fantasy runtime.
- Phase 2: Bundle re-emit + per-culture rebuild-proportions (wyrd-j43l + new follow-on). Unblocks SPA era progression, --stratum, KenningEraMap data, joiners-in-bundle.
- Phase 3: Phonology rules → Tier-4 era reflex (wyrd-98cs). Closes time-travel coverage gap.
- Phase 4: Fantasy runtime surface (wyrd-vz7f). Authoring complete; runtime tap.
- Phase 5 / parallel: Investigate inflection-coverage gap (wyrd-f6v4). Probably feeds into mining backlog.

Success criterion: re-run the language-quality dashboard at the end of the epic and demonstrate measurable lift on every metric we set thresholds for, especially time-travel coverage % and per-language inflection / variant pool counts.

title: End-to-end feature audit: are 80+ closed-ticket features actually wired up?
description:
User-driven audit (2026-05-08): after ~80 closed tickets across mining + features, the user wants an end-to-end perspective on what's wired up vs half-implemented vs implemented-in-principle-but-not-in-reality.

Specific questions raised by the user:
1. When breaking up probabilities of town names, are we using multiple forms of the same word? Conjugates? Does that make it forward into the randomly generated names, or are we always just picking the lemma?
2. Do all the features like using fantasy creature names work, even in the interface?
3. Can we generate real town names that can move backwards and forwards in time?
4. What percent of the original lemmas we had from rando are able to move backwards and forwards in time?
5. Other features: half-implemented, in principle but not reality.

Approach: 6 parallel investigation agents on disjoint feature axes, each returning a structured (claimed / actual / gap) report. Synthesize into a single end-to-end-state report. Agents may use bd to look at closed tickets and the lexicon DB for empirical coverage data.

Audit axes:

title: Cross-source corrupt canonical_forms in committed mining data (stray parens, OCR digit-garbage, braces)
description:
Cross-source scan of data/mining/**/*.jsonl (cycle 122) found a residual of corrupt etymon canonical_forms — distinct from the INTENTIONAL balanced Mawer/KEPN '(a)' optional-letter notation (berel(a), pæsc(e), i(s)nard, (ge)heg — ~60, stored raw BY DESIGN and handled by toponym_etymology_canonical._normalize_form's cluster-key paren-strip for COMPARISON; NOT a bug).

GENUINELY CORRUPT (surface-string-as-identity, like the Briggs fix #836 / PR #836):
- Unbalanced stray parens: kepn_gloucestershire 'H)rencga', roberts_1914 '(ge)mdr{e)' (also a brace). Briggs personal-names already fixed at the _expand_bracket_variants layer (#836); the KEPN CSV ingester (kepn_csv_ingester._process_kepn_row, form extracted ~line 229) and the LLM toponym miner do NOT strip unbalanced strays.
- OCR digit-garbage canonical_forms: mawer '6j^' '6j^=' 'm&r-deni4', smith 'va6', lindkvist '0yrr' '0ystri', skeat '*h8ema', joyce 'e6d' (~9). A canonical_form with a digit/control char is OCR noise — never a valid OE/ME etymon; should be rejected at ingestion, not stored.
- Bracket editorial-supply: lindkvist 'strea[w]', arbois 'dom-[h]arius' (may be intentional editorial notation — needs per-source review).
- Trailing whitespace: rando-port/retired 'hēa ' (trivial .strip()).

WHY MULTI-CYCLE (not a single self-contained change): spans ~15 sources / 3 ingesters (kepn_csv, briggs, the LLM toponym miner) + the LLM-mining output path; the right per-sub-class policy differs (strip unbalanced strays vs reject digit-garbage vs review bracket notation vs keep balanced raw); and it's FORWARD-ONLY — fixing the ingesters won't clean the already-committed rows, which need a coordinated re-ingest (cycle-63 committed-data carve-out).

SUGGESTED INCREMENTAL APPROACH: (1) a shared canonical_form ingestion validator — reject digit/control-bearing forms, strip unbalanced strays (reuse the Briggs _expand_bracket_variants stray-strip), strip trailing whitespace — applied across kepn_csv + briggs + the toponym miner; (2) decide bracket-supply policy per-source; (3) re-ingest to clean the ~20 committed corrupt rows. Each ingester's stray-strip is itself a tractable PR (like #836 was for Briggs).
notes: Digit sub-class SHIPPED forward via #837 (53334bd7): validate_response now rejects digit-bearing LLM element forms (form_has_digit) — the single choke point covers all 5 LLM-mined sources. Remaining: unbalanced-stray strip in kepn_csv + briggs-already-done (#836); bracket editorial-supply policy per-source; trailing-ws; the coordinated RE-INGEST to clean the ~20 already-committed corrupt rows (incl. the 8 digit forms #837 prevents going forward).

title: empirical_priors bakes single-element at position='pre' but scorer looks up 'bare' → 2376 priors mis-keyed, single-word baseline lost
description:
empirical_priors BAKES single-element words at position="pre" but the runtime scorer LOOKS THEM UP at position="bare" → 2,376 English single-element priors are stored in cells the lookup never queries → single-word generation systematically misses its position-specific empirical baseline and silently falls through to the coarse position-agnostic fallback. HIGH severity (systematic mis-score across ~16% of breakdowns), surfaced by the cycle-91 empirical_priors audit.

BAKE: empirical_priors._position_label (L155-170): element_count==1 → "pre" (the docstring calls this "this module's own convention, not inherited from legacy"). PositionLabel = Literal["pre","inner","post"] (L92) — there is NO "bare".

LOOKUP: runtime/word.py:14 _structural_position: count<=1 → "bare". This flows UNMODIFIED through proportions._flatten_struct_slots → vector_name_select._slot_position_for / _slot_weighted_pool → scoring.baseline_score_native(..., slot_position="bare", ...) (vector_name_select.py:570). The native priors lookup (scoring.py:186/248) holds only pre/inner/post cells, so a "bare" slot MISSES level-1 (exact), level-2 (era-wildcard), AND level-3 (culture,position="bare",*,* — no baked cell carries position="bare"), and silently falls to level-4 (culture,*,*,* position-wildcard, the position-agnostic max). So single-element ("bare") names never get the position-specific baseline the bake stored for those same single-element words.

BLAST (live ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db, read-only): 3,212 single-element breakdowns (~16% of 19,908); 2,376 English single-element extract rows baked at position="pre" but looked up at "bare". The (bare) structure is 16.60% / 4402 of the corpus (structure_allowlist.py:16); ships disabled-by-default in English structures.yaml but is a valid enable-able runtime structure + used in multi-word bare slots.

FIX (the runtime "bare" vocabulary is the established one — used across runtime/word.py, slots, structures — so align the BAKE to it, not vice versa): change _position_label single-element → "bare"; extend PositionLabel = Literal["pre","inner","post","bare"]; update test_kenning_empirical_priors.py::test_position_label_single_element_is_pre (currently ASSERTS the "pre" bug) → asserts "bare". The scorer already queries "bare", so after a re-derive the "bare" cells exist → lookup hits level-1/2/3. No scorer change needed.

WHY COORDINATED MIGRATION (cycle-63): the fix re-positions 2,376 committed prior rows (pre→bare cells) AND requires regenerating the committed JSON sidecar (lexicon dump-empirical-priors) + the L3 empirical_priors_native/loan tables in the shipped runtime DB. It should be done in ONE coordinated priors-rebuild PR ALONGSIDE wyrd-ckro (the merged-loser inflation, 6,789 English rows) — both touch the same extraction + sidecar, so a single re-derive that fixes BOTH axes avoids a partially-correct sidecar. Verify the re-position against the committed sidecar diff (the operator-visible "what did the corpus do" view) before swapping. D36.9 makes the re-derive routine (re-runnable, byte-identical on unchanged DB), but the committed-artifact diff is the migration.

VERIFIED CLEAN this cycle (not bugs): era-midpoint request-vs-bake convention split is consistent-by-design (degrades to era-wildcard, never a wrong key; (start+end)//2 + half-open boundary match era.era_cell); count math has no join fan-out (0 dup (etymon_id,tag) rows, per-tag counting intended); determinism/D36.9 holds (integer counts, ORDER BY + sort_keys); skip-counter partition mutually-exclusive+exhaustive (rows_emitted+Σskips==rows_scanned); native/loan split routes each ok row to exactly one cell per table.

title: committed variant-fold wrong-fold: Ede->Eve (framing-only) tombstoned a distinct name; re-screen 487 llm-variant-folds + un-tombstone
description:
The variant_fold_detect bug (fixed in the code by PR adding onomastic stopwords) ALREADY produced at least one committed WRONG FOLD in data/mining/_collapses.jsonl that needs correcting + un-tombstoning:

CONFIRMED WRONG: middle-english:Ede -> middle-english:Eve (method llm-variant-fold-v1, confidence MEDIUM). Ede (a medieval pet form of Edith / OE Ēadgifu) and Eve (Hebrew/biblical Eva) are ETYMOLOGICALLY DISTINCT names. They were folded only because both glossed "a feminine personal name" (pure entry-type framing → no meaning signal) + surface-similar (difflib ~0.67), so the LLM judged on surface alone and mis-folded. The fold set Ede's merged_into_id to Eve's id in the live DB → Ede's identity is tombstoned into Eve (corruption: a distinct morpheme lost).

AUDIT THE OTHER NAME FOLDS (verify legit vs wrong): the ledger has 3 other capitalized-name folds — old-english:Ceatwa->Ceatta (high), old-english:Godgiefu->Godgifu (high), old-english:Gōdgifu->Godgifu (high). The two Godgifu folds look LEGIT (Godgiefu/Gōdgifu are genuine spelling variants of Godgifu=Godiva). Ceatwa->Ceatta plausibly legit (high conf). But the full set of llm-variant-fold-v1 folds (487 total) should be re-screened for any that were grouped SOLELY on onomastic framing tokens (personal/feminine/masculine/saint/diminutive/patronymic) — those are the at-risk class the LLM judged with no gloss signal.

FIX (coordinated migration, cycle-63 class — re-positions committed data + needs rebuild):
1. Re-screen the 487 committed llm-variant-fold-v1 FOLD rows: flag any whose barren+lemma shared ONLY framing tokens (re-run the candidate grouping against the pre-fix vs post-fix stopword set; the post-fix set would no longer propose them).
2. For confirmed-wrong folds (Ede->Eve at minimum): change the ledger row to a reject (into:"") OR delete it, and un-set the loser's merged_into_id (un-tombstone) via a rebuild — collapse replay is last-write-wins per ref, so appending a reject row for ref=middle-english:Ede after the fold row would cancel it on replay (verify the apply path honors a later into:"" as an un-fold, or whether a full rebuild from the corrected ledger is needed).
3. Validate the re-position against the committed ledger (per determinism-fix-over-nondeterministic-data): count exactly which etymons un-tombstone, confirm no downstream assertion keyed on the (wrongly) merged identity.

Coupled to a rebuild. The CODE fix (onomastic stopwords) prevents FUTURE framing wrong-folds but does NOT un-do the committed Ede->Eve tombstone. Surfaced by the cycle-86 variant_fold_detect.py audit.

title: collapse_detect Method B: _POINTER_GLOSS_RE false-positives a sole-gloss MEANING → auto-folds a distinct morpheme (no LLM gate)
description:
collapse_detect.py Method B (_detect_pointer_parse) AUTO-APPLIES deterministic pointer-parse collapses (enrichment.apply_collapses tombstones the variant into its target — NO LLM gate). A "pure form-of etymon" is one whose EVERY gloss matches _POINTER_GLOSS_RE (is_form_of_pointer). The regex `^\s*(?:[a-zà-öø-ÿ0-9'-]+\s+){0,3}(?:form|spelling|variant)\s+of\s+\S` allows ≤3 leading qualifier words, so a genuine DEFINITION that merely starts with "<≤3 words> form/spelling/variant of <X>" is misclassified as a pointer:
  - "early form of writing" → is_form_of_pointer True, folds onto modern-english:writing
  - "earliest form of settlement" → folds onto :settlement
  - "old spelling of the name" → target "the"/"name"
  - "variant of standard usage" → folds onto :standard
These are MEANINGS, not cross-references. When such a gloss is the SOLE gloss on an etymon (passes the all()-pointer purity gate at line ~130) AND the captured tail word resolves to a live same-language lemma, Method B AUTO-FOLDS a meaning-bearing morpheme into an unrelated lemma → identity corruption (D46: wrong merge corrupts; and here there's no LLM gate to catch it). EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED: a synthetic modern-english etymon with sole gloss "early form of writing" + a live modern-english:writing lemma → _detect_pointer_parse emits {ref: someword, into: modern-english:writing}.

LATENT today: the only 2 live pure-pointer candidates (irish:lugha "superseded form of lú", old-english:arun "Northumbrian form of earon") are LEGITIMATE pointers — 0 current false-folds. The risk is a future wiktextract import of a sole-gloss "<descriptive-adj> form of <word>" MEANING.

WHY NOT A QUICK REGEX FIX: a false pointer ("early form of writing") is STRUCTURALLY identical to a real one ("superseded form of lú") — "<qualifier> form of <word>". The only difference is semantic (early/earliest/old/primitive = descriptive vs alternative/obsolete/Northumbrian/superseded = register/dialect). Distinguishing them needs EITHER (a) a curated allowlist of wiktextract form-of REGISTER qualifiers — but that risks dropping the 2 legit folds if it misses "superseded"/"Northumbrian" (a recall regression), OR (b) etymon_variant-table corroboration (but Method B is specifically for NON-variant pure-pointers), OR (c) routing pointer-parse folds through the LLM merge pass (P3) instead of auto-applying — a design change removing Method B's auto-apply. Needs deliberate design + a curated qualifier vocabulary validated against the live gloss corpus; not a tick-sized regex tweak.

RELATED (fixed in the same cycle, PR for the try-each ambiguity guard): the multi-word-qualifier mis-target (a lowercase qualifier word that resolves, "...form of west saxon burg" → folds onto `west` not `burg`) is closed by _resolve_pointer_target (fold only when EXACTLY ONE tail word resolves). The hunter's originally-reported "form of Old English burg → folds onto old-english:old" was REFUTED: resolution is case-sensitive, so the capitalized "Old" never matches the bare-lowercase canonical_form — that case was a missed fold, not a corruption.
notes: Cycle-84 review (PR #810) surfaced a SECOND false-pointer shape in the same family — fold it into this ticket's scope: TRAILING BARE PROSE after the lemma. "alternative form of burg used widely" — if `burg` is absent and a prose word ('widely') is a live lemma, the lemma region's lone resolver is the prose word → auto-folds onto it. PR #810 fixed the PARENTHETICAL variant (the lemma region is now truncated at the first '(', so a sense-gloss "(spring, well)" is never scanned), but trailing BARE prose (no delimiter before it) is indistinguishable from "[qualifier] lemma" positionally — it's a hand-written DEFINITION mis-read as a pointer, exactly this ticket's class. A resolver-count heuristic can't close it; needs the semantic/register-vocabulary or LLM-gate fix tracked here. Both shapes — (a) "early form of writing" and (b) "form of burg used widely" — are clean-template-impossible: a wiktextract form-of template emits "form of [Lang] LEMMA [(sense)]" with no descriptive prefix and no trailing bare prose.

title: merged_into_id sweep: 4 enrichment readers wrote tombstone data (phonological_vector, element_gloss, pronunciation_backfill, gloss_sense) — coordinated filter+migrate
description:
A cycle-77 systematic audit of all lexicon readers that JOIN/SELECT etymon found FOUR enrichment readers that omit the merged_into_id filter AND have ALREADY WRITTEN tombstone-derived data — the same root cause as wyrd-qdau (decomposition_grader) and wyrd-ckro (empirical_priors), but each requires a coordinated filter+migration (not a preventive one-liner like #804/#805), because committed data already references tombstones. D22 OCR-cluster merging is non-destructive (sets the loser's merged_into_id, does not re-point reflex_etymon/toponym_etymology_element/etymon_tag/etymon enrichment columns), so these readers enrich tombstones that generation can only reach via the merge winner (_family.py).

THE FOUR (each: add merged_into_id IS NULL filter/resolve + MIGRATE the already-written tombstone data to winners or clear it; verify the blast-radius against the live DB before changing, cycle-63 lesson):

1. phonological_vector_enrichment.py (HIGHEST — feeds SCORING): the where_clause omits merged_into_id; force-mode wrote phonological_vector onto ALL ~52,590 tombstones. These vectors feed the vector scorer (D36). Fix: AND merged_into_id IS NULL in where_clause; clear/migrate the 52,590 tombstone vectors.

2. element_gloss_backfill.py: grounding + apply SELECTs omit the filter; 2,254 glossed tombstones, ~1,118 wrong reflex_etymon links ALREADY COMMITTED. Fix: filter on grounding + apply SELECTs; migrate the 1,118 links to winners.

3. pronunciation_backfill.py: G2P + LLM-replay SELECTs omit the filter; 5,502 in-language tombstones, ~5,391 IPAs ALREADY WRITTEN onto tombstones (111 more a rerun would newly fill). Fix: filter both SELECTs; clear the 5,391 tombstone IPAs.

4. gloss_sense_campaign.py: _IMPACT_SQL + _INVENTORY_SQL omit the filter; 558 (Phase-1 impact>=2) / 2,253 (Phase-3) tombstones; ~1,958 same-sense binds ALREADY COMMITTED on 1,174 tombstone refs. Fix: AND e.merged_into_id IS NULL on both; migrate/retract the 1,958 committed binds.

NOT bugs (verified benign by the same sweep, do NOT filter): resolve_etymon_ref (MUST resolve to the tombstone's own id so project_canonical groups each OCR variant with its winner — 52,585/52,590 tombstones correctly carry a matching canonical_morpheme_id; filtering would orphan them); english_shaping (a tombstone's english_shaped IS reachable via the family rollup); spurious_breakdown_mining / vocab_health / descent_audit (read-only reports); synsets / etymonline_ingester (writers). Real-world scoring/generation harm is MUTED because generation routes through the merge winner, but the committed tombstone rows are real and pollute counts/scoring on any direct read. Coordinate as one rebuild-coupled batch. Already handled by preventive one-liners (clean, no committed data): tag_mining #804, pronunciation_mining #805.

title: empirical_priors._EXTRACT_SQL counts merged_into_id OCR-losers (only reader missing the merge filter)
description:
empirical_priors._EXTRACT_SQL is the ONLY lexicon reader that does NOT filter/resolve etymon.merged_into_id. It JOINs etymon e ON e.id = tee.etymon_id (the element's directly-referenced etymon) and builds lemma_ref = language:canonical_form + joins etymon_tag on that etymon. D22 OCR-cluster merging is non-destructive: it sets the loser's merged_into_id but does NOT re-point toponym_etymology_element.etymon_id, so ~18% of elements (7679/43361) point at a tombstoned variant. Of the rows that pass the England + non-NULL attested_year gates and feed the priors, ~42% (1720/4068, or 1314 by a tighter count) come from merged losers. Each loser produces a SEPARATE spurious lemma cell (latin:linum vs winner latin:linum-with-macron; old-english:an vs an-with-macron; modern-english:kye vs cow) instead of accreting onto the winner -- fragmenting the empirical baseline + injecting OCR-noise lemma_refs the scorer never legitimately sees. Feeds the vector baseline-scoring axis (D36).

FIX (known): resolve the element etymon through the merge chain to the WINNER, e.g. JOIN etymon e0 ON e0.id = tee.etymon_id then JOIN etymon e ON e.id = COALESCE(e0.merged_into_id, e0.id), so lemma_ref + tags use the winner. RESOLVE (not filter merged_into_id IS NULL): filtering would DROP the 1314 loser elements (lose evidence, D21); resolving accretes their counts onto the winner. Chains are depth-1.

WHY TICKETED not tick-fixed (cycle-68/wyrd-qdau sibling + cycle-63 lesson): the fix's effect is BROADER + cascading than a simple lemma re-bin. Measured old-vs-new on the live DB: resolving to the winner changes each merged-loser element's TAG MULTIPLICITY (loser's tags -> winner's tags), which ripples through every gate -- rows_scanned 68867->68084, rows_emitted 4068->4381 (+313), skipped_no_tag -120, skipped_country_unknown +35, skipped_year_unknown -1051; total emitted count 8136->8762 (+626). The +313 emitted priors are RECOVERED evidence (merged-loser elements that were skipped_no_tag because the sparse OCR variant was untagged, but the canonical winner is tagged) -- arguably correct (D21), but a substantial re-shaping of a committed SCORING artifact. The priors tables are re-derivable (DELETE+INSERT each run) so it is NOT an append-only-ledger reconciliation like wyrd-qdau, BUT: (a) the committed JSON sidecar (lexicon dump-empirical-priors) needs regeneration -- a large one-time diff; (b) the recovered-evidence + tag-re-attribution semantics deserve explicit sign-off (is recovering untagged-loser elements via winner tags desired?); (c) the scoring impact of +313/+626 baseline counts needs eval, not just unit tests (cycle-63: unit tests passing != data correctness). DELIVERABLE: the SQL fix + a regression test (merged loser -> winner lemma+tag cell, not a phantom loser cell or skipped_no_tag) + measure the scoring-eval delta + regenerate the committed JSON, as a coordinated step. Everything else in empirical_priors.py verified CLEAN (position derivation, era binning, culture map, native/loan split, determinism). Surfaced by a cycle-75 bug-hunter sweep.

title: load_cluster_index reads MERGED etymons → stale cluster identity feeds two writing miners
description:
decomposition_grader.load_cluster_index (and load_scholar_corpus's breakdown query) SELECT FROM etymon with NO 'WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL' filter — unlike every other index-builder in the lexicon package (collapse_merge.py:83,89; era_reflex.py:179,206,241; variant_fold_detect.py:185,328 all filter it). A merge sets merged_into_id on the LOSER but does NOT repoint its reflex_etymon / toponym_etymology_element rows; readers are expected to filter merged_into_id IS NULL (collapse_merge does). load_cluster_index does not, so cluster_of / surface_clusters read DEAD etymons. Merged losers almost always have cognate_id NULL → they yield a stale singleton key e<merged_id> (the loser's dead identity) instead of the surviving cluster c<cognate_id>.

EXACT LINES (decomposition_grader.py): :101 (SELECT id, cognate_id FROM etymon), :106-108 (reflex JOIN reflex_etymon), :146-153 (load_scholar_corpus breakdown query) — none filter merged_into_id.

LIVE-DB EVIDENCE (~/.wyrd/lexicon.db; 52,590 merged etymons): 1,193 reflex_etymon rows + 7,679 tee rows point at a merged etymon (7,673 tee → cognate_id NULL → stale singleton). 1,011 of 9,461 reflex surfaces (~11%) gain a spurious singleton cluster; for 726 of them the CORRECT (merge-target) cluster is genuinely ABSENT from the resolved set (a wrong/missed cluster, not additive noise). 5,657 distinct toponyms have a breakdown element anchored on a merged etymon. 0 true orphans (every referenced eid is a real etymon row), so this is the merged-row issue, not a missing row.

SEVERITY: corrupts IDENTITY, not metric-only. cluster_of/surface_clusters feed TWO WRITING miners: passthrough_mining.py:158,266-268 anchors composed-of (D51 passthrough) assertions on index.cluster_of[eid] — a stale key changes the (composite_cluster, constituent_clusters) identity written; implied_reflex_mining.py:193,644 builds the over-consume guard + breakdown anchors on cluster_of/surface_clusters then writes reflexes (upsert_reflex/link_reflex_etymon ~821-823). A stale singleton FRACTURES one cluster into the live cluster + a dead e<id>, splitting evidence that should pool (the tūn/ton cognate bridge) and mis-keying written assertions (D46: wrong attribution corrupts).

CLEAN (verified): fold consistency (surface_clusters keys + clusters_for both fold_surface, D45-ok); reflex-only surface_clusters is a DELIBERATE documented split (passthrough unions canonical_forms on top; implied_reflex explicitly does NOT want them); _decompose_name/grade_toponym/summarize are eval-only (gate no write) + correct; determinism holds.

FIX OPTIONS:
- Expedient: add WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL to the 3 queries. Matches the codebase invariant; D46-improvement (wrong→dropped). RISK: a reflex/breakdown that ONLY exists via a merged etymon DISAPPEARS (recall loss) — for the 726 the correct cluster stays absent (trades wrong-cluster for missed-cluster + LOSES evidence, D21 concern).
- Rigorous (preferred, best long-term): follow the merged_into_id chain to the live target and key on the TARGET's cognate_id, so the merged loser's reflex/breakdown POOLS into the surviving cluster — fixes the corruption AND preserves the 726-surface evidence (D21 mining-evidence-sacred). This is what the cluster bridge is supposed to do.

WHY A COORDINATED MIGRATION, NOT A CODE-ONLY PR (cycle-63 discipline): the fix changes ~11% of surface→cluster resolutions, and the two writing miners have ALREADY committed assertions/reflexes keyed on the stale clusters. A code-only PR fixes FUTURE mining but leaves 5,657 toponyms' committed assertions stale-keyed; the next re-mine/rebuild re-positions them uncontrolled. COMPLETE fix = (rigorous index fix) + (re-mine the affected passthrough composed-of + implied-reflex assertions) + (validate the re-position against the committed _assert_bind/_reflexes ledgers before swapping). Verify the blast-radius against the REAL ledgers (per wyrd-sf8y / determinism-fix-over-nondeterministic-data), not just unit tests. Coupled to a rebuild. Surfaced by a cycle-68 bug-hunter sweep of decomposition_grader.py.

title: identity_reflex_rows: non-deterministic position (GROUP_CONCAT order) re-emits spurious position-variant reflexes
description: cycle-63 enrichment_campaign.py audit. identity_reflex_rows (enrichment_campaign.py ~206-230) derives each identity reflex's position from the FIRST attested form in r['forms'] where the morpheme's folded canonical_form appears. r['forms'] is a bare GROUP_CONCAT(... modern_name|historical_form|surface_in_modern ..., '~') in _IDENTITY_SQL with NO ORDER BY → implementation-defined concat order (unstable across rebuilds/ANALYZE/index/SQLite-version). For the ~9% of morphemes (730/8052 live) that fold-match at >1 position, the emitted position is a coin flip. The dedup/build key is (surface_form, position, ref) with the reflex PK UNIQUE(surface_form, position) (migration 0005_reflex.py; ON CONFLICT in sql/queries/reflex.py), so a position flip on a later campaign run is NOT in the committed set → re-emits a SECOND, position-variant reflex (both persist). reflex.position also GATES productivity counting (SELECT_REFLEX_PRODUCTIVITY_COUNTS joins ep.position=r.position) + genitive_priors filtering, so a wrong position discards real observations. NON-TRIVIAL FIX (why ticketed, not a loop drive-by): the selector must pick position by FREQUENCY-MAJORITY (most-common across fold-matches, tie-broken by a fixed precedence pre>post>inner) — semantically correct (hām post 587 → post, NOT the precedence-pre which mislabels suffixes). BUT empirically (vs the real data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl) frequency-weighting re-emits 197 spurious second-position rows, precedence 425, first-match (origin/main) 3 — because the COMMITTED ledger positions were authored under the old non-deterministic first-match, so no deterministic rule reproduces them. So the COMPLETE fix = (a) change the selector to frequency-majority AND (b) reconcile the committed ledger: re-position the existing identity reflexes to the frequency-majority position (a data migration over _reflexes.jsonl) so the dedup matches and the next campaign run doesn't author 197 duplicates. Do (a)+(b) together as one coordinated change, then a clean re-mine. The frequency-weighting selector patch + a fail-before/pass-after unit test (post-majority morpheme → post; 1-1 tie → pre) were prototyped on the abandoned PR #796 branch (recoverable from its diff). Verify the spurious-re-emit count drops to ~0 against the reconciled ledger before merging.

title: kenning rewind: concatenated non-particle run matching a free particle renders lowercase
description: Found in PR #746 review (Gemini, medium; pre-existing, NOT introduced by the #746 byte-identical refactor). render_form_particle_pairs (wyrd/generators/kenning/era/rewind.py) decides title-casing in pass 2 by checking 'token in _FREE_PARTICLES' (the string), not the morpheme's is_particle flag. So a run of adjacent NON-particle forms that concatenates to a free-particle string is wrongly kept lowercase. Repro (verified): render_form_particle_pairs([('un', False), ('der', False)]) -> 'under' (should be 'Under'); render_form_particle_pairs([('on', False)]) -> 'on' (should be 'On'). Root cause: surface-string check stands in for the particle flag, which is the morpheme-identity-via-dash-shape anti-pattern in miniature (identity should come from the flag, not the rendered surface). Fix (Gemini's, sound): thread the is_particle flag through pass 1's tokens (return list[tuple[str, bool]]) and gate pass 2 on the flag: _group_pairs_into_tokens emits ('".join(pending)', False) and (form.lower(), True); _titlecase_join_tokens iterates (token, is_particle) and title-cases when not is_particle. This is a deliberate behavior change (also fixes a non-particle 'on'/'of'/'under'/'upon' to title-case), so it needs its own PR with tests asserting Under/On + that real free particles stay lowercase. Deferred from #746 to keep that PR byte-identical (its safety rests on a 32,210-case identity sweep). See PR #746 comments 3468332135 / 3468332148.

title: kenning: surface collapses-stage unresolved-ref counters in format_unresolved_warnings
description: Found in PR #744 review (Gemini, medium). The collapses enrichment stage (apply_collapses) tracks unresolved-ref/typo counters — unresolved_from, unresolved_into, unresolved_inherits, detach_unresolved_from, detach_unresolved_endpoint (enrichment.py ~1034-1093, defaults ~1272-1281) — and the result carries a 'collapses' block (~1529/1631). But format_unresolved_warnings' _UNRESOLVED_WARNING_SECTIONS does NOT include a 'collapses' section, so these silent no-ops are never surfaced to operators nor caught by --strict. This is a PRE-EXISTING observability gap (not introduced by the #744 refactor, which preserved the exact prior section set). Fix: add a ('collapses', (<counters>)) entry — but verify the EXACT result shape first (there appear to be two 'collapses' keys: collapse_state at ~1529 vs slot_counts['collapses'] at ~1631 — confirm which dict format_unresolved_warnings reads and that the counter keys live at its top level), and add van9 tests for the new section + a --strict test. This CHANGES output + --strict semantics, so it's a deliberate behavior change, out of scope for the byte-identical #744 refactor. See PR #744 comment 3468058256.

title: Canonical-morpheme top-etymon ranking regressed (ley→lēah, wick→wīc) after gloss/eni4 merge
description:
A full rebuild after the gloss-campaign (#737) + eni4 merge regressed 2 canonical-morpheme top-etymon rankings. test_bundle_canonical_morphemes[ley] and [wick] PASS on a bundle exported from the pre-merge DB but FAIL on the post-merge bundle AND on the regenerated dev seed (so it would ship on the next seed regen). main is currently clean — its committed dev seed predates the merge and CI's gate runs against that, so the regression is LATENT (only surfaces on a rebuild).

Symptom: usage 'ley' resolves to the OE ley/leye cluster (CM-623ecf...) instead of canonical lēah 'glade' (CM-2be65...); usage 'wick' resolves to the standalone 'wick' (4 glosses, no canonical_morpheme_id) instead of canonical wīc (13 glosses, CM-8970d2...).

Root cause: the merged work changed etymon gloss/sense counts (gloss-campaign sense-binds on ley/leye 7+1; gloss-adds + curation dedup shifting counts), and _rank_siblings' gloss/tag-count tiebreak now picks the wrong sibling. Underlying: ley/leye and wick sit in SEPARATE canonical clusters from lēah/wīc — they were never unified.

Fix candidates: (a) unify the ley/leye<->lēah and wick<->wīc canonical clusters so the rich canonical etymon dominates; (b) make _rank_siblings prefer the etymon carrying canonical_morpheme_id over a raw gloss-count tiebreak. 

Blocks: next seed regen / L4 deploy. Repro: export-runtime-db from a post-merge L3, run pytest tests/test_bundle_canonical_morphemes.py -k 'ley or wick' with WYRD_RUNTIME_DB set to the full bundle.

title: Ingest Macbain 1896 + Gaelic/Celtic dictionaries to corroborate the celtic rando-only bulk (523)
description:
The celtic rando-only morphemes (abh, airc, airgid, aoire, bard, bedd…) are Gaelic dictionary headwords. Smoke-test LLM leads repeatedly pointed at Macbain's *Etymological Dictionary of the Gaelic Language* (1896, public domain) — which we do NOT have ingested (we hold macbain_1922 *Place-Names of the Highlands*, a different book). 

Plan: obtain Macbain 1896 (archive.org / Wikisource), plus candidates Dwelly's Gaelic dictionary and Joyce, and run them through the existing mine-llm / ingest-* pipeline as NEW sources. Corroboration then falls out grounded (real etymon_citations validated against source text) for potentially most of the 523 celtic morphemes at once. Highest integrity + yield. Blocker: fetch the source text first. Recommended primary path.

title: Scholarly corroboration / retirement of the 816 live rando-only morphemes
description:
After wyrd-qkn0 fixed the rando-port-readiness gate, 816 live (in-bundle) morphemes are attested ONLY by rando-port (the hand-assembled Rando seed from Wikipedia + sources). They ship in the generator with no scholar/empirical backing. Snapshot: data/mining/reports/after-dedash-20260622/live-rando-only-morphemes.csv (committed #739). Per-language: celtic_mix 523, old_english 159, old_scandinavian 84, old_french 41, latin 9.

Goal: corroborate each with a real scholarly source (so it is no longer sole-rando) or deliberately retire/keep it.

Smoke-test findings (scratch/rando_corroborate_smoke.py, read-only): grounded corroboration from the EXISTING corpus is ~0 (only 5/772 via toponym_etymology_element link; a weak ~20% form-in-notes text match needs validation). The celtic bulk are Gaelic dictionary headwords. An LLM (think:false on qwen3.x) yields ~25% raw 'attested' leads but they are UNVALIDATED and title-garbled on a 9B model (e.g. 'Macbain Dictionary of the Scottish Language' vs the real 'Etymological Dictionary of the Gaelic Language') — leads, never citations. Children pursue the concrete paths.

title: Garbled-form repair via collapse (loop-approved, gated)
description:
Owner approved adding garbled canonical-form repair to the loop's work. FINDING: corrupted etymon forms (OCR/mining junk: 6j^, stdn→stān, HTML fragments, '& cetera', letter-subs) are almost all DUPLICATES of a correct etymon that already exists — so the fix is a MERGE (collapse), NOT a rename. Mechanism: a 'collapse' curation row {_type:collapse, ref:<garbled>, into:<correct-twin>} folds the dupe into its twin (replayed by enrichment.apply_collapses — reproducible, no raw DB writes).

SAFETY: collapse is a structural identity op (over-merge footgun wyrd-740t = the same class as the human-gated cognate-binds), so the loop is allowed ONLY high-confidence merges, gated by 'enrich-campaign collapse-validate' (both refs resolve to distinct etymons; rejects '#'-sense suffixes which are INTENTIONAL homograph disambiguators e.g. bol#hill, not corruption; rejects self/dup). Worklist: data/mining/garbled_etymon_forms.tsv (CORRUPTION vs INTENTIONAL_sense_suffix categories). Junk-with-no-twin + HTML fragments → leave for human triage, do NOT merge. Collapse rows append to data/mining/_curation.jsonl. Gate shipped (validate_collapse_candidates, PR #727).

title: rando-port-readiness gate is structurally blind to rando-port — always reports rando_only=0
description: _fetch_member_citations strips rando-port from the bundle's <lang>_citations field (it's a non-scholar seed), but _bundle_attestation_breakdown (the rando-port-readiness gate + language-report rando audit) detects rando_only by looking for rando-port IN that same stripped field. Result: rando_only is structurally ALWAYS 0, and real rando-only subjects are miscounted as 'uncited'. Ground truth in L3: 772 etymons cited ONLY by rando-port (1593 citations). The gate has been giving a false 'rando-only=0, retirement nearly ready' all along. Pre-existing (not the de-dash rebuild; not the #736 meanings.json port). Fix: cross-reference the committed data/mining/rando-port.jsonl (1599 citation records → de-dashed language:form set) against each bundle word's morpheme_id in _subject_citation_flags. Surfaced while running dashboards after the wyrd-aicu.8 de-dash rebuild.
close_reason: Fixed: rando-port-readiness now cross-references data/mining/rando-port.jsonl against bundle morpheme_id to surface live rando-only morphemes (816 across targets: oe 159/of 41/os 84/celtic 523/latin 9). #738 merged da45e891.

title: Presentation: wire NewName.description() to compose one compressed gloss token per slot (human-gated, NOT the loop)
description:
The readable-meaning surface — HUMAN-GATED, NOT the unattended loop (it is a code change). Do in a focused session / on return. Depends on .A projection wiring + .B having authored senses.

NewName.description() (proportions.py:2248-2291) currently emits, per morpheme slot, `head (root gloss,gloss or root2 gloss...)` — raw canonical glosses joined verbatim (siblings by " or "). Replace the per-slot emission with composition of ONE short COMPRESSED token per slot, read from the morpheme's canonical_sense label(s) (etymon_gloss.canonical_sense_id -> canonical_label): 'New'+'Town'. Polysemous morpheme -> array ['wall','frog'] -> render "Brendan's Wall" OR "Brendan's Frog". Keep the raw-gloss path available as a fallback for un-canonicalized morphemes (always-present secondary, cf. D41). Also update the structured to_dict() (proportions.py:2311) if it should carry the compressed gloss.

title: CAN-IT variant-gap completion-selector (22% of pairs)
description: Second CAN-IT lever beyond the reflex-less rail: 22.4% of scholar (toponym,morpheme) pairs are VARIANT GAPS — the morpheme HAS a reflex, but none of its reflex surfaces match THIS toponym's spelling (e.g. Bartholomew encoded as 'barthos'). These block CAN-IT even though the morpheme is 'covered'. Build a selector that, per not-yet-CAN-IT toponym, surfaces the scholar morpheme(s) whose reflexes don't substring-match the name, plus the surface span to author as a NEW grounded reflex (the span IS in the toponym, so grounding holds). Prioritize toponyms where it's the LAST unmatched morpheme (flips CAN-IT) and morphemes appearing in the most such toponyms. Authored as reflex surface_form rows (within loop remit; NOT the human-gated etymon.variants field). Diagnostic at launch: reflex-less=21.3%, variant-gap=22.4%, matched=56.2% of 43,361 pairs. Deferred so the loop launches reflex-first per owner direction.

title: Lambda: serve $LATEST directly — drop publish=true + live alias (we only want latest)
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-06-22 cost blowout (<$100/mo budget hit ~$450, projected $750). SnapStart (apply_on=PublishedVersions) + publish=true cut a NEW published version on every deploy, and staging auto-deploys on EVERY push to main (.github/workflows/deploy.yml) — so every merge/beads-sync cached a permanent 1769MB SnapStart snapshot. ~300+ staging versions accumulated, each billing snapshot storage forever → cost grew incrementally every day.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION (done 2026-06-22): (1) disabled SnapStart via CLI on both functions (apply_on=None); (2) deleted all accumulated old versions (prod → v2+$LATEST, staging → v358+$LATEST, 303 deleted); (3) Terraform change in flight to set apply_on=None permanently (keeps it OFF — a deploy re-applies TF and was re-enabling SnapStart). SnapStart STAYS OFF (cold start ~3.7s on 1769MB; prod has no users — acceptable).

ROOT-CAUSE FIX (this ticket): we only want $LATEST. Repoint aws_lambda_function_url.api + the two aws_lambda_permission.cloudfront_* from the 'live' alias (qualifier) to $LATEST (unqualified), drop publish=true and aws_lambda_alias.live. Then no versions/snapshots accumulate at all. Verify CloudFront OAC still invokes the unqualified Function URL. Also add a guard so SnapStart can't be silently re-enabled. NOTE: a final sweep should delete the 1 lingering SnapStart snapshot on staging v358 / prod v2 after the no-SnapStart deploy repoints the alias/URL.
notes: DONE 2026-06-22: staging retention added too (#734) but INACTIVE — gated on repo var ENABLE_STAGING_VERSION_PRUNE (default off; staging auto-deploys per push so it stays off until deliberately enabled, no code change). Full state: SnapStart flag-gated default-off (#732); prod retention active (#733); staging retention present+inactive (#734). To activate staging pruning later: set Actions variable ENABLE_STAGING_VERSION_PRUNE=true. ocs8 can close once staging pruning is intentionally enabled (or left as the documented opt-in).

title: Tag uplift for accepted morphemes (controlled vocab, no sprawl)
description: 1,500 admit-cohort morphemes (48.1%) are untagged. Classify each one's gloss into the controlled tag vocabulary (44 existing + kinning) — the same contract as mine-tags-llm: a mandatory 'none' outcome for genuinely-abstract glosses, NO bad matches, NO tag sprawl. Loop authors decisions to data/mining/_tags.jsonl (one per line incl. 'none'); the apply-tag-additions enrichment pass replays them for free. Relates to wyrd-t0vw (deploy/apply _tags.jsonl) and wyrd-wohr (untagged personal/saint-name homograph leak — e.g. Bartholomew empty tags). Lower risk than variants/cognate; gloss is the only input so it needs no toponym grounding.
notes: Rail ready (PR #727). Executes as loop phase 2 after phase-1 reflexes exhaust, per ENRICHMENT_CAMPAIGN.md. Cohort: admit>=2 glossed-untagged, impact-ordered; controlled TAG_VOCAB + 'none' outcome.

title: Per-language structures.yaml (sections) + refresh-merge dump w/ frequency comments
description:
Evolve the c6o1.5 structure allowlist (D48) from a single GLOBAL flat file to a PER-LANGUAGE sectioned file, and make the dump a refresh-merge so re-dumping preserves operator curation while surfacing new structures.

WHY: operators need to (a) see how COMMON each structure is to find 'trash' beyond the morphemes-per-word heuristic, and (b) curate per-language (English run-on trash != Irish patterns). Today dump-structures MERGES all cultures into one global deduped inventory (first-culture-wins), throwing away per-language frequency, and the file carries no frequency at all.

DESIGN (agreed w/ Devon 2026-06-21):
- FORMAT: one file, TOP-LEVEL CULTURE SECTIONS: 'english:\n  "<label>": {enabled: bool}  # <weight> (<pct>%)\n...' then 'scottish:' etc. (A2 = per-language ENFORCEMENT, not just visibility.)
- FREQUENCY COMMENT per row: raw proportion weight + culture-relative percent, e.g. '# 225 (0.85%)'. Comment is advisory; loader ignores it.
- SORT: ALPHABETICAL/stable within each section (NOT frequency-sorted) — so a rebuild that nudges frequencies doesn't reorder the whole file and churn the git diff; new structures appear as clean added lines. (Devon flipped the earlier freq-sort decision for diff-friendliness.)
- REFRESH-MERGE dump: read existing committed structures.yaml -> re-mine inventory per culture -> existing file's 'enabled' value WINS for any label already present (every false is sticky); a label NOT in the old file is NEW -> default (true, except single-morpheme <Bare> seeds false); a previously-disabled label no longer in the corpus DROPS OUT. Re-dump is idempotent + safe.
- STDERR SUMMARY (mining-progress convention): per culture, 'N structures (+X new, -Y dropped since last dump)' + list the NEW (and dropped) labels with freq, so operators get an explicit 'go filter these' signal independent of the git diff.
- RUNTIME THREADING: NameGenerator has per-culture DATA but no culture NAME at the filter point (is_structure_enabled(k), proportions.py ~1273). Add culture:str to NameGenerator.__init__ (self.culture), thread through load_proportions(data, meaning_db, tag_db, culture=...) and its callers, and change is_structure_enabled(struct_key, culture) -> cached.get(culture,{}).get(label, True). Absent culture/section => fail-open (all enabled).
- LOADER: load_structure_allowlist_from_text -> {culture: {label: bool}}; _load_bundled_cached -> nested MappingProxyType (read-only, wyrd-i7uy). Validate two levels (culture section is a mapping; each entry mapping w/ bool enabled). HARD-CUT the flat format (pre-launch, CLI-generated; re-dump).

description: Found during wyrd-m415. mine-element-glosses writes _element_glosses.jsonl with open(path,'w') (element_gloss_backfill.write_jsonl) — a FULL REPLACE, not a merge.
