title: Tighten mine-duplicate-canonicals propose/refute prompts to reject compound + derivation pairs
description:
Follow-up from the wyrd-u6fn.5 apply-run (PR #687). The gemma4:26b two-pass propose/refute judge has a systematic precision gap: it confirms 'same morpheme' for pairs that are NOT one lexeme, and the adversarial refute pass doesn't catch them. Opus hand-curation removed 73 of 402 raw merges across 4 rounds (final 329 authored). The false-positive CLASSES the prompts must learn to reject:

1. COMPOUND <-> CONSTITUENT: a compound is not the same morpheme as its head/constituent. Examples caught: treow≈plūm-trēow, bȳ≈kross-bý, vellir≈thingvellir, gōs≈gos(a)-wīc, gortna≈gortmore (gort+mór), bille≈da-bille. A dash in a form is a strong morpheme-boundary signal.

2. DERIVATION (asymmetric POS/affixal): noun<->verb (willa/willian), base<->adjectival-derivative (west/westerne, horu/horig), participial/gerund<->noun (ridding/ryden, wilig/wiligen), nominalized (riigan/ruga, iuo/iubhar), zero-derivation/suffixal (linden/lind), diminutive (byrgen/byrgels, chnoc/cnocan, tully/tul). Distinct from a genuine spelling/phonological variant of ONE lexeme.

3. DISTINCT NAMES / HYPOCORISTICS: Joan≈Jane, Margerie≈Meg, Gilot≈Gillota, Ellot≈Gillota, Malkin≈Mallin. BUT keep genuine single-name spelling variants (Katharine≈Katherine, Margerie≈Margery, Agnes≈Annis) — the genuine-vs-distinct distinction is the hard part the prompts must encode.

KEEP (true same-morpheme): orthographic/phonological/diacritic variants of one word (mad≈mat, mylen≈myln, wulf-pytt≈wulfpytt), inflections of one lexeme (crux≈crucis, pons≈pontem), same-root variants.

Tasks:
- Add explicit negative instructions + few-shot examples (above) to _PROPOSE_SYSTEM and _REFUTE_SYSTEM in wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/duplicate_canonical_mining.py so the LLM rejects classes 1-3 itself.
- Consider a deterministic pre-filter for the dash/compound case (detect_candidates or _maybe_pair) since it's high-precision.
- Re-run the apply (mine-duplicate-canonicals --apply); the judged-log records the 73 rejected pairs as separate (won't re-author), and a tightened run should additionally RECOVER the ~10 genuine variants conservatively dropped in the hand-curation (name spelling-variants, ð/d diacritic pairs like kaup-maðr≈kaup-madr).
- Validate on a calibration sample (the curation harness in the PR #687 history is a good oracle: the 329 kept + 73 rejected are a labeled set to score precision/recall against).

Context: D46 (wrong merge = corruption, missed merge = harmless) is why the hand-curation erred toward rejection. Parent epic wyrd-u6fn. The apply data is in data/mining/canonicalization/_assert_bind.jsonl + _assert_merge_canonical.jsonl + _canonical_nodes.jsonl + the _duplicate_canonical_audit.jsonl idempotency/labeled log.

title: D50 assertion emitters use row-id etymon/te refs (violates no-ids-in-jsonl) — switch to stable natural keys
description:
AUDIT 2026-06-20 (out of wyrd-zrce). The no-ids-in-jsonl invariant is violated SYSTEMICALLY by the D50 canonicalization-assertion emitters: every etymon (and toponym_etymology) MEMBER ref is built as str(<row_id>), not a stable natural key. etymon.id / toponym_etymology.id are reassigned on every rebuild-from-jsonl (etymon has no game_id; natural key = (canonical_form, language)), so any committed assertion orphans/mis-resolves after a corpus change. relational_projection does int(ref) -> etymon_descent, confirming row-id semantics.

THE GOOD PART: canonical NODE refs are already CORRECT — mint_canonical_id('canonical_morpheme', language, canonical_form) (deterministic hash). The fix is to key etymon/te MEMBER refs the same stable way (or the collapse/reflex convention ref='language:canonical_form'), plus a name->id resolver at projection.

EMITTER SITES (all build NodeRef('etymon'|'toponym_etymology', str(<row_id>))):
  1. lexicon/cognate_descent_mining.py:206-207   (wyrd-zrce.1 descends-from) — etymon ids
  2. lexicon/same_morpheme_mining.py:260          (wyrd-c7iz / 1a bind)       — etymon ids
  3. lexicon/canonicalization_projection.py:465   (legacy rollup bind)        — etymon ids (str(m))
  4. lexicon/passthrough_mining.py:330-331        (wyrd-h5u1 composed-of)     — etymon ids
  5. lexicon/spurious_breakdown_mining.py:214     (spurious breakdown)        — toponym_etymology ids (str(te_id))
CORRECT (keep): same_morpheme_mining.py:240, canonicalization_projection.py:440 (canonical_morpheme via mint_canonical_id).

IMPACT: committed L2 is CLEAN — none of these emitters' output is committed (no _assert_*.jsonl / _canonical_nodes.jsonl in main), so no corrupted data; the bug is LATENT. But it BLOCKS durable use of the entire D50 assertion-uplift line: zrce.1/.2 (cognate clustering), c7iz/1a (same-morpheme bind), h5u1 (passthrough composed-of), spurious-breakdown. This session's zrce evidence run produced a 1183-record _assert_descends_from.jsonl with id refs — DISCARDED, not committed.

FIX (interim natural-key approach; the long-term surrogate-UUID solution is wyrd-ihmf):
  - Make etymon/te NodeRefs emit a stable key: ref = mint_canonical_id('etymon', language, canonical_form) OR 'language:canonical_form'. Pick ONE convention repo-wide (collapse/reflex already use 'language:canonical_form').
  - Add a stable-key -> row-id resolver at projection (relational_projection + the bind projection in canonicalization_projection) — fail-closed on unresolved (one located error, not a crash).
  - Unit test: round-trip an assertion through a rebuild with REASSIGNED ids and confirm it still resolves to the same etymon.
  - Then re-run zrce.1/.2 + commit durable L2.

BLOCKS: wyrd-zrce. RELATES: wyrd-h5u1, wyrd-c7iz (already 'closed' but its bind path has the same latent bug — its 77 binds were never committed to L2 either), wyrd-ihmf (long-term UUID), the no-ids-in-jsonl invariant.
notes: PT1 MERGED via #684 (descends-from path → stable natural-key etymon refs; lexicon/etymon_refs.py shipped). PT2 MERGED via #686: the etymon BIND path — same_morpheme_mining.bind_assertions, canonicalization_projection legacy-rollup, AND duplicate_canonical_mining.same_morpheme_assertions (a 6th emitter found during review) now emit 'language:canonical_form' refs; the projection (_group_binds/_resolve_binds) resolves etymon subjects via resolve_etymon_ref (skip-on-miss) while toponym/te stay row-id; round-trip test pins id-independence. The etymon bind path that BLOCKED wyrd-zrce is now durable → zrce dependency removed. PT3 REMAINS (latent, nothing committed/projected for these yet): site 4 passthrough_mining composed-of (etymon→etymon, belongs to wyrd-h5u1 — composed-of isn't projected yet; adopt etymon_ref when it is) + site 5 spurious_breakdown_mining toponym_etymology refs (need their OWN natural-key scheme; te has no language:form key). Ticket stays open for PT3.

title: Investigate worth-gate marginal promotion (OE worð de-promoted on clean rebuild) + noisy realism bands
description:
WHAT: On a clean from-scratch rebuild, test_canonical_morpheme_top_etymon[worth] fails — the 'worth' bundle bucket has NO old-english sibling (only modern_english 'worth'), so modern 'worth' (economic) out-ranks OE worð/worþ (enclosure — the real place-name element: Worthing, Tamworth). The breton/scottish/welsh realism bands also fail. Both persist even after the three layer round-trip fixes landed (reflex br5o #673, fantasy ruvk #674, empirical x33t #677 all reproduce cleanly).

WHY IT MATTERS: blocks an all-green clean rebuild, which blocks rotating a fresh reproducible DB in as the working baseline (the active DB is the accumulated backup ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db.bak-prerebuild-20260618-0619, which passes worth).

INVESTIGATION — FOUR HYPOTHESES, ALL REFUTED by direct backup-vs-rebuild comparison:
1. Dropped toponyms (1,655 row delta): REFUTED — distinct toponym NAMES identical (68,618 both); the delta is duplicate readings.
2. Empirical citations (clean re-mine 1,870-2,676 vs accumulated 3,682): REFUTED — x33t round-tripped the full 3,682 via wiktionary-empirical.jsonl; a rebuild with 3,682 empirical STILL fails worth (no OE sibling). [Empirical was worth chasing anyway — it's a real reproducibility fix — but it is NOT the worth driver.]
3. Cognate clustering drift: REFUTED — the OE worth etymons cluster IDENTICALLY backup-vs-rebuild: weorþ→cognate 453638 (size 45), worþ→cognate 2758578 (size 2), weorð→3906870 (size 9), worð unclustered; descent edges identical.
4. Forms-variants (etymon_text_match): REFUTED — worþ has the same 7 forms (OE þ/ð-spellings: worþe/worþa/wurþ/...); it folds to usage_key 'worth' via its canonical þ→th, not via a form.

KEY FINDING: the OE 'worth' sibling etymon (worþ, id 1663380 in backup) is BYTE-IDENTICAL backup-vs-rebuild on every localizable input — citations=2, forms=7, cognate=2758578 (size-2 cluster), descent=5. Yet the backup PROMOTES it as a 'worth' sibling (so _rank_siblings Pass-1/wyrd-ywm9 favors OE over the modern homograph) and a clean rebuild does NOT.

CONCLUSION: worth's de-promotion is a GLOBAL / export-time PROMOTION effect, not a localizable data difference. worþ's tiny 2-member cluster sits right at the promotion boundary (_select_promoted_root_ids); the clean rebuild's slightly different OVERALL corpus (legitimately changed by other Claudes' merged L2 work — celtic branches/descent — since the backup snapshot) tips this marginal cluster below the bar. So it is sensitivity, not corruption.

IMPLICATIONS:
- Do NOT recalibrate the worth gate to the rebuild's result — that would encode 'modern worth beats OE worð', which is etymologically backwards.
- realism bands are a NOISY near-threshold gate, NOT a reproducibility signal: the gate-passing backup ITSELF fails the english band (~0.29 vs 0.30) when re-exported with current code; the rebuild fails scottish 0.2903 / welsh / breton, all marginal. Revisit the 0.300 morpheme_rank_correlation threshold (too tight) separately from reproducibility.

NEXT INVESTIGATION DIRECTION:
- Examine _select_promoted_root_ids (wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/bundle/_export.py) for the marginal-promotion sensitivity: does a small (size-2) cluster with scholarly citations + heavy toponym-element usage (worþ has 251 toponym_etymology_element rows for worð+worþ combined) promote on a global threshold/budget that shifts with corpus size? Goal: make legitimate historical place-name elements promote ROBUSTLY regardless of corpus-wide drift.
- Consider: the oth3 breakdown-admission path (include_toponym_breakdown, default off) would promote worð/worþ via their 251 toponym breakdowns — was gated off pending h5u1; revisit whether enabling it stabilizes worth.

REPRO: full rebuild (rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment) + Phase-2 L3 restore (scratch/phase2-noemp.sh — empirical now round-trips so skip the mine) + export-runtime-db; then 'WYRD_RUNTIME_DB=<bundle> pytest tests/test_bundle_canonical_morphemes.py::test_canonical_morpheme_top_etymon[worth] tests/test_kenning_realism_absolute.py'. Compare 'worth' siblings vs a backup-export bundle via _load_meanings()['worth'] + _roots(). Sibling wyrd-ruvk holds the original root-cause trail.
notes: RE-SURFACED + xfailed on the #719 seed refresh (2026-06-21): worth→worð de-promotion joined _XFAIL_RANKING in test_bundle_canonical_morphemes (strict, with ley/wick — aicu.7 class); breton morpheme_rank_correlation 0.21<0.30 xfailed per-culture in test_kenning_realism_absolute (strict=False — noise-dominated band + corpus mid-expansion, ip7r/fmg). Still OPEN to investigate (worth via aicu.7 ranking fix; breton band via corpus expansion).

title: Reflex layer under-reproduces on clean rebuild — orphan/seed reflexes don't round-trip (worth/fantasy/realism regress)
description:
Found by the 2026-06-18 full rebuild (the first since 2026-06-13). A clean rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment + the full Phase-2 restore produces a bundle ~8,234 promoted meanings THINNER than the accumulated pre-rebuild DB, regressing the canonical-morpheme gate (worth -> modern 'worth' instead of OE worð), fantasy morphemes (333 -> 8), and the english realism band.

ROOT CAUSE (after ruling out code + toponyms + empirical):
- CODE is correct: A/B export (pre-rebuild backup data + current code) reproduces the seed exactly (333 fantasy, worth passes). So the regressions are DATA, not the b2mf/oth3/h5u1 export changes.
- NOT toponyms: distinct toponym names are identical (68,618 both); the 1,655 row delta is duplicate readings, not missing places.
- NOT empirical citations: re-mining lifts 2,587->5,091 but cleanup nets ~2,676 and it does NOT move the bundle (red herring).
- ACTUAL root: the ORPHAN / generation-surface reflex layer. Backup reflex=24,637 (orphan=16,099); clean rebuild reflex=21,105 (orphan=12,053). The -6,437 (null)-language 'orphan-reflex' bundle meanings (place-name surfaces like Abberley/Abingdon) are the dominant gap; everything else (fantasy needs promoted constituents; worth ranking) is downstream.

WHY orphan reflexes don't reproduce:
- _reflexes.jsonl (wyrd-ned5) round-trips LINKED reflexes ONLY (dump_reflexes_to_rows; 9,081 entries, all non-empty etymon_refs). Orphan reflexes are excluded by design.
- The orphan/generation-surface reflexes are created by seed_from_meanings (one reflex per modern_usage; unlinked when the subject word has no grounded etymon — seed.py:_link_subject_reflexes) + derive_positions during enrichment.
- seed_from_meanings is marked LEGACY/superseded in _rebuild_layers.json ("reflexes now arrive via _reflexes.jsonl") and appears in REBUILD.md only as a trap-table footnote, NOT a Phase-2 step. So a clean rebuild never re-seeds them; derive_positions reproduces only ~12k of the accumulated 16k.

RECOVERY NUANCE (tested 2026-06-18): running seed_from_meanings against the FULL bundle (75,711 meanings) OVER-produces (reflex 21,105->91,776) — wrong source. The backup's 24,637 came from seeding the ORIGINAL rando meanings source, not the full bundle. So the recovery needs the correct (original rando) meanings input.

FIX OPTIONS (durable, pick one): (1) extend dump_reflexes_to_rows + jsonl/build.py replay to round-trip ORPHAN reflexes too (empty etymon_refs) — the wyrd-ned5 extension; or (2) re-document seed_from_meanings as a Phase-2 step with the correct rando meanings source + re-dump; or (3) make derive_positions deterministically reproduce the full generation-surface reflex set. Then update REBUILD.md + _rebuild_layers.json + re-rebuild clean to verify reproducibility (worth/fantasy/realism pass).

title: Uplift 1b.2: LLM cognate-ancestor proposal for the residue (adversarially verified)
description:
After wyrd-zrce.1 lands the evidence-grounded clustering, size the residue (morphemes Tiers A/B did NOT connect) and connect it via LLM-assisted cognate-ancestor proposal.

- LLM proposes the cognate ancestor / cluster for each residue morpheme (Ollama @ 10.5.2.31:11434 per workspace notes; verify model availability first).
- Emits descends-from assertions at LOW confidence by default (D50.4 leave-separate bias).
- ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION before the projection's confidence gate admits them: a verifier (LLM or rule) must confirm; unverified proposals stay below-gate and do not cluster.
- Mining-progress line per CLI convention; tests on fixtures.

Sequenced after zrce.1 because the residue size (and thus this scope) is only known once the evidence tiers run.
notes: PHASE 0 PROBE (live, read-only, 2026-06-18): the ticket's 'Roman onomastics / low yield' note was from the residue's alphabetical HEAD and is WRONG for the full set. Residue=3,071 unclustered breakdown morphemes with no clustered fold-match; they are diverse + well-glossed (hwearf 'wharf', cyln 'kiln', bærnet 'cleared-by-burning', kartr 'stony ground', crike 'creek', faba 'bean', plus OE/ON/ME/Latin/modern-English). 87% (2,698) have a candidate (shared >=4-char fold-prefix); 85% have a CLUSTERED stem-mate; only 12% (373) are truly isolated. A 4-char prefix is a weak/noisy signal by design — the LLM prunes spurious collisions to real cognates. DECISIONS: (1) scope = link residue -> EXISTING clusters only (the 85%); residue-residue new clusters deferred. (2) verification = two-pass propose + independent adversarial-refute (D50.4). Build fuses audit-descent (skeptical judge + verdict log + threshold gate) with mine-cognate-descents (authors descends-from to L2, projected by zrce.1's already-wired stage). Probe: scratch/zrce2_residue_probe.py. Model: a general Ollama model (gemma4:26b / qwen3.5) via WYRD_OLLAMA_MODEL, not the coding variant.

Phase-0 corrected the 'Roman onomastics' note — residue is diverse + 87% have candidates. Scope = existing clusters; residue-residue NEW clusters are wyrd-zrce.3.

title: Uplift 1b.1: evidence-grounded cognate-descent mining + descends-from→etymon_descent projection
description:
The high-confidence core of wyrd-zrce. Ground fact (live DB, 2026-06-17): ~98% of the 5,629 unclustered breakdown morphemes have ZERO etymon_descent edges, so cluster_cognates has nothing to walk — 1b is a mining build.

Deliver:
1. Miner mine_cognate_descents (sibling of same_morpheme_mining.py), two tiers, emitting RELATIONAL descends-from assertions (Family B, edge_type inheritance|borrowing, never bind) to L2 _assert_descends_from.jsonl:
   - Tier A (in-corpus overlap): breakdown morpheme shares gloss/folded-surface signal with an already-CLUSTERED shipped morpheme -> descends-from to that cluster's root (high confidence).
   - Tier B (Wiktionary re-mine): look up the breakdown surface in the wiktextract corpus, recover its inheritance/borrowing chain -> descends-from to its ancestor (medium-high; real Wiktionary evidence). Mining-progress line per CLI convention.
2. Relational projection descends-from -> etymon_descent (the D50.6 piece project_canonical left deferred): deterministic, idempotent, source-stamped, L2-native (survives rebuild). MUST run before cluster_cognates (step 5 of run_full_enrichment) so the rollup sees new edges.
3. Rollup: reuse cluster_cognates; verify the unclustered count drops.

Tests on tmp/fixture DBs only. Determinism (D36.9). Live re-cluster confirm defers to the one-claude rebuild. Blocks wyrd-g96o (era-reflex projection).
notes: EDGE-MODEL DECISION (zrce.1): for an unclustered breakdown morpheme X that folded-matches a clustered etymon Y whose cognate_id (= most-ancestral root) is R, emit descends-from(subject=etymon X, object=etymon R, edge_type=inheritance) — so cluster_cognates' root->down BFS (parent-but-never-child) reaches X and assigns it R's cognate_id. Connect to the ROOT R (not Y) because cross-language cognates are siblings under the proto-root, not parent-child. TIERED CONFIDENCE (homograph risk, the ton=town vs ton=wave problem): folded-match + gloss overlap -> medium; same-cluster-unique surface-only -> low; multiple candidate clusters -> prefer the unique gloss-overlapping one, else leave-separate (D46). Precision/recall is pushed to the projection's confidence gate (D50.4), not hard-coded in the miner.
close_reason: Evidence-grounded core of 1b landed in PR #666 (squash 7ecfbc68): cognate-descent miner (Tier A + in-corpus Tier B, ~45%/2,558 of the unclustered cohort) + descends-from→etymon_descent relational projection (the deferred D50.6 piece) wired before cluster_cognates + CLI. LLM residue (Roman onomastics, 55%) is wyrd-zrce.2.

title: EPIC: Branch-level Celtic language modeling (brittonic/goidelic)
description:
DECISION (2026-06-17, Devon): model Celtic at the BRANCH level — 'brittonic' (Welsh, Cornish, Breton, Cumbric, Pictish) and 'goidelic' (Irish, Scottish-Gaelic, Manx) — not as one flat 'celtic' umbrella nor as 7 fine-grained languages.

WHY: the umbrella mixes morphemes from languages that never coexisted (Brittonic tre-/llan-/pen- with Goidelic bally-/kil-/dun- → e.g. *Trekildun), which breaks the generator; but fine-grained splits a thin corpus into anemic pools (welsh=2416 etymons/0 promotion-eligible/1 source; old-welsh=71/0 sources; celtic_mix only 23% scholar-attested). Branch level keeps the ONE distinction that matters (Brittonic vs Goidelic never mix) at a corpus depth that can still generate. Nesting: zone 'celtic' (D52) ⊃ branch {brittonic, goidelic} ⊃ (optional, later) language. etymon.language + the generation pool live at BRANCH level; promote a finer language (welsh is the only candidate today) only when its evidence justifies a split.

Surfaced by a report design-review: three components disagree on Celtic granularity today — LANGUAGE_CANONICAL (umbrella 'celtic' only), language_quality.DEFAULT_LANGUAGES (fine-grained welsh/irish/breton/...), zones.yaml D52 (lists both). This epic reconciles them around the two-branch model. Caveat: requires re-tagging L2 (flat 'celtic') → branch; derivable from source/form but a mining pass, not free.

title: Mine breakdown-evidenced passthrough edges (composite surface -> constituent morphemes)
description:
SURFACED by the wyrd-oth3 grader-validated re-emit (wyrd-aicu.9 grader, 2026-06-16). With a rich morpheme inventory, the matcher's score (total unaccounted, then total morpheme COUNT — Occam, fewer wins) prefers a single coarse composite morpheme over a finer, equally-0-unaccounted decomposition into attested sub-morphemes:
  Aldington: Ald+ing+ton (3 morphemes, recovers ing + tūn) LOSES to Ald+ington (2 morphemes, one composite)
  Abberton:  abbe+r+ton -> Abb+erton ;  Alpington: Alp+ing+ton -> Alp+ington
This raised coverage but DROPPED cluster recall/precision/head on the scholarly corpus (the grader's acceptance test failed: coverage +3.4pts, recall -0.4, head -0.8, 218 regressions). The coarse parse fully accounts the string but recovers fewer of the scholar's morpheme clusters.

THE ISSUE: 'fewer morphemes' is the wrong proxy for 'better decomposition' when the extra morpheme is itself a real attested morpheme. A finer all-accounted parse whose pieces are all attested morphemes is usually MORE faithful to the scholarly breakdown than a coarse composite.

CANDIDATE FIXES (design needed): a granularity/specificity tiebreaker — among parses tied on unaccounted chars, prefer the one whose morphemes are all 'primitive' (not decomposable into other attested morphemes), or penalize composite morphemes that are themselves a concatenation of attested morphemes, or prefer MORE morphemes when all are attested+tagged. Must stay a SOFT tiebreaker (D40), validated via the grader (regression list as tripwire). Interacts with: wyrd-oth3 (admit, gated off until this lands), wyrd-myv4 (composite-form admission filter — the data-side lever), wyrd-aicu.9 (the matcher + grader). Note the composite forms partly arrive via breakdown admission, so myv4's composite filter and this matcher fix are complementary.
notes: MACHINERY LANDED in PR #670 (squash 7b16492b): the composed-of ATTRIBUTION path (not the matcher hard-key change). mine-passthroughs CLI authors composed-of edges to L2; build_passthrough_map + grade_passthrough_diff + grade-decomposition --passthroughs wire the grader to credit a matched composite (ington) with its constituents (ing+tūn) for recall/precision/head (D51.3) — coverage flat by construction. The pre-existing passthrough_mining.py logic + the grader passthrough_map hook are now wired + tested (26 tests). REMAINING before oth3 un-gates: (1) the LIVE grader net-win run with oth3 breakdown morphemes admitted in the trie (needs the rebuild/one-claude window) to confirm coverage-up + recall/head-recovered + regressions-defensible; (2) generation-side composed-of attribution (a shipped composite rendering/explaining as constituents). Decision-record: chose attribution over the matcher Occam hard-key change (the ticket's other candidate fix) — lower risk, avoids the 08m/pfoo tiebreaker branches, and is the D51 'match-but-attribute' model.

title: Occurrence-threshold tiering + junk pruning for breakdown-morpheme admission
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-oth3 (admit scholarly-breakdown morphemes). wyrd-oth3 does the SIMPLE admission; this ticket owns the occurrence-threshold / quality decision that wyrd-oth3 deliberately defers.

DATA (live corpus, 2026-06-16; net-new MATCHABLE surfaces not already in the bundle, counting reflex OR folded canonical_form, family-occurrence = distinct toponyms):
  family occurrence >=1 (all): 8,424 net-new surfaces
  family occurrence >=2:       3,434
  family occurrence >=3:       2,261
Current bundle ships ~1,424 folded surfaces, so even >=3 roughly doubles the matchable inventory.

The single-occurrence tail (>=1 minus >=2 ~ 5k surfaces) is junk-leaning: one-off mis-extractions (sc/lkr/ii/kd, dre/ire/col/ti/us short fragments) + proto-forms admitted via the canonical-form fallback. The multi-occurrence tiers (>=2/>=3) are visibly real heads/specifiers (tun/ham/by/dun/cot/feld/ford...).

WORK: decide the production occurrence threshold for breakdown admission (>=2 vs >=3 vs other), validate the chosen tier via the wyrd-aicu.9 decomposition grader (re-emit + off-vs-on, regression list as the tripwire), and prune/flag the junk tail. Confidence is NOT a usable filter (32k NULL, no 'low'). Relates to wyrd-z3me (mis-extraction audit overlaps the junk tail).

This is the '>2' work the user split out so wyrd-oth3 can refocus on just admitting the morphemes.
notes: GRADER FINDING (2026-06-16): the filter is NOT just occurrence/junk pruning — the dominant agreement-regressor is COMPOSITE FORMS in the breakdown corpus (-ington, -erton, -halton, -ingham). The grader-validated re-emit showed unfiltered admit drops cluster recall/head (coverage up but quality down) because composites let Occam pick coarse parses. So myv4 must EXCLUDE composite forms (etymons whose surface is itself a concatenation of other attested morphemes) in addition to the occurrence threshold. Complementary to wyrd-h5u1 (the matcher-side granularity tiebreaker). Validate via the grader: net agreement up AND regression list empty/defensible.

title: Admit scholarly-breakdown morphemes into the bundle (5th promotion path)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (surfaced by the wyrd-aicu.9 decomposition grader, 2026-06-16): the morpheme-inclusion gate admits a family root via four paths in lexicon/bundle/_export.py:_select_promoted_root_ids — scholar-witness threshold (>=2 since wyrd-fssn), rando-port, wiktionary-empirical, wave-2-enriched. None admits a morpheme on the strength of a scholar having DECOMPOSED a real place into it. So the specifiers scholars themselves used (alder, barlow, ...) are absent from the runtime inventory, and the matcher junk-tiles their toponyms: Aldermaston -> ['Al','Der','Ma','Ston'], Barlaston -> ['Bar','la','Ston']. Measured on the live -ston corpus: even on the COVERED subset (155/324), cluster recall is 0.083 and 93/155 have a stone head — bundle sparsity, not the homograph bug. The junk-tiled parses each dump a spurious stone count into generation proportions (part of the user-reported 'stone inflated, town starved').

PROPOSAL: add a FIFTH admission path (e): any etymon in a family that appears as an element in a scholarly toponym_etymology breakdown -> admit the root, bypassing the witness gate. Parallel to the wiktionary-empirical branch (SELECT etymon_id FROM toponym_etymology_element, roll up via root_of), behind its own flag include_toponym_breakdown (default on). Justification: a scholar-attested breakdown element is a distinct, place-name-specific evidence channel — arguably STRONGER than dictionary witnesses for place-name generation.

COMPLEMENTARY TO aicu.9: the connective+prior fix needs the specifiers present to have anything to attach to (Bishop+s+ton); the gate change makes them present. Neither fully fixes the bug alone.

RIGOR (per user 2026-06-16): add path (e) WITH a quality filter (the corpus has mis-extracted junk breakdown rows — sc/lkr/ii/kd). Candidate filters: element/breakdown confidence floor, require a real reflex surface, and/or require >=2 distinct breakdown occurrences (filters one-off mis-extractions). DERIVE the threshold from a corpus measurement (how much junk low-confidence / single-occurrence elements would admit) and bring the number to the user before flipping default-on. VALIDATE via the wyrd-aicu.9 decomposition grader (lexicon grade-decomposition): re-emit a bundle with path (e) and confirm cluster agreement rises without a junk regression.

CODE: lexicon/bundle/_export.py _select_promoted_root_ids (+ export_meanings/_collect_families signature for the new flag) + the two export CLIs (export-meanings, export-runtime-db). Needs a bundle re-emit to take effect. Related: wyrd-aicu.9 (matcher), wyrd-z3me (mis-extraction audit overlaps the junk-row filter).
notes: GRADER-VALIDATED RE-EMIT (2026-06-16): the UNFILTERED admit FAILS the acceptance test. Full-corpus grade (15,267 toponyms, connective OFF, baseline export vs +breakdown export): coverage 0.870->0.904 (+3.4pts) but recall 0.170->0.166, precision 0.165->0.162, head 0.206->0.198 ALL DOWN; 621 improvements / 218 regressions. Root cause: the breakdown corpus carries COMPOSITE forms (-ington/-erton/-halton/-ingham) and the Occam (fewer-morphemes) tiebreaker then prefers coarse Ald+ington over the finer correct Ald+ing+ton, so more toponyms fully parse but recover FEWER scholar clusters. ACTION TAKEN: flipped the include_toponym_breakdown flag DEFAULT to OFF (export_runtime_db + export_meanings CLIs + library) so a normal re-emit won't ship the regression. Opt-in until wyrd-myv4 (composite/occurrence filter) + wyrd-h5u1 (matcher granularity tiebreaker) + wyrd-7hbp (uplift clustering) make it a graded net win. CORRECTION: earlier sparsity numbers (recall 0.083 on -ston) were the committed DEV SEED (~1,424 surfaces), not the full export (~90k surfaces, coverage 0.87) — the production-scale problem is over-segmentation via composites, not sparsity.

Auto-apply only above a high threshold; queue the rest. Asymmetric failure (D46-style): a missed merge is harmless duplication, a wrong identity-collapse is corruption — default to leave-separate. Adversarial-verify: a skeptic agent tries to REFUTE each proposed merge before promotion. Regression check: does it catch the ne(369498)≈niwe(671826) duplicate?

title: Backfill rationale onto existing merged_into_id / cognate_id edges as legacy assertions
description: The existing redirect columns are method-stamped (lemma_method/cognate_method) but carry no per-edge rationale/confidence. Re-cast them as legacy assertions in the new model so the partial-but-correct machinery becomes uniform rather than parallel. Where the original method is unknown, stamp method=legacy-import with low confidence so a repair pass can revisit (e.g. the new->ne 2-witness merge).
notes: MERGED #659 (squash 50cad177, 2026-06-17). project_canonical now FOLDS today's deterministic identity clustering (merged_into_id OCR variants -> same-morpheme, lemma_id inflections -> inflection-of; reflex-link/collapse-variant members -> same-morpheme) into in-memory assertions at projection time — re-derives free on rebuild, no committed snapshot. cognate_id NOT folded (relational, D50.2). assess_identity_fidelity + --assess-fidelity gate. In-place migration on the live DB: 102,149 hubs / 255,548 binds, fidelity 102149/102149 faithful, 0 violations. Survived a 4-round pr-review-loop (full fleet + Gemini): fixed a reflex-link bind-kind mislabel, threaded an observable empty-canonical_form warning, typed FidelityReport/FidelitySample/_EtymonInfo, chunked-IN the info scan (9.8s vs 11.9s, rebuild-speed). NEXT: wyrd-b2mf = the reader/view cutover (~50 sites + cognate rollup) — makes the canonical graph AUTHORITATIVE; only then do 1a's binds (#652) + a D50-native 1b (wyrd-zrce) land in live generation.

title: Projection: rebuild L3 collapse graph from raw observations + assertions
description: The cleaned graph is a REBUILDABLE L3 projection of (raw observations L2) + (canonicalization assertions L2). Preserves D21 (evidence sacred/additive), D24 (observable), the four-layer model, and the mining-expensive/enrichment-cheap asymmetry. Generalizes merged_into_id/cognate_id rollup. SQLite only — no graph engine (D42).
design:
PROJECTION (L2 assertions -> L3 collapse graph) — FIRST CUT (2026-06-16). DESIGN, not migration.
Generalizes the D22 rollup (COALESCE(merged_into_id,lemma_id,id) chains; *_canonical = WHERE
merged_into_id IS NULL) to a clean FK-to-synthetic-node join.

BIND GRANULARITY (the D50 open item, RESOLVED): bind at observation-row granularity, layered
default+override for places.
- morpheme -> etymon row (etymon.canonical_morpheme_id)
- sense    -> etymon_gloss row (etymon_gloss.canonical_sense_id)
- place    -> toponym row by DEFAULT, with per-toponym_etymology-row OVERRIDES that take precedence.
  1725 forces this: one toponym row conflates 3 places (rows 778 v./779 manor/780 S.-of-Dalton).
  default bind handles MERGE (Archdeacon Newton 5213+67841 -> one place); etymology-row override
  handles SPLIT (778->CP-A, 779->CP-B, 780->CP-C). No special 'split' predicate — just bind precedence.

L3 DDL (projection output; columns mirror merged_into_id/cognate_id style):
  canonical_morpheme(id TEXT PK, merged_into TEXT FK self)   -- id is L2-DECLARED (stable, not derived)
  canonical_place(id PK, merged_into FK self)
  canonical_sense(id PK, merged_into FK self)
  canonical_label(canonical_type, canonical_id, stratum, value, source_assertion, PK(type,id,stratum))
  ALTER etymon            ADD canonical_morpheme_id FK
  ALTER etymon_gloss      ADD canonical_sense_id    FK
  ALTER toponym           ADD canonical_place_id    FK   -- default
  ALTER toponym_etymology ADD canonical_place_id    FK   -- override (wins)
Family-B relational edges MOSTLY EXIST already: etymon_descent (descends-from), etymon_meaning_synset
(means-same-as), etymon_gloss (glosses-as), toponym_etymology_element (decomposes-into). Projection
adds rollup-through-canonical VIEWS, not new tables. New tables only for region: region_node(id,axis,
level,stratum), region_contains, jurisdiction_succeeds, place_located_in.

ALGORITHM (deterministic; terminal stage AFTER rebuild-from-jsonl materializes observations):
 1 mint: canonical_* rows from mint-canonical (skip retracted).
 2 bind: per observation gather affirmed binds, drop retracted+refuted, keep confidence>=gate
   (default 'high', env-tunable per D43 threshold precedent), set canonical_*_id. Places: etymology-row
   override beats toponym-row default.
 3 merge-canonical: via merged_into (smallest-id-wins), flatten chains (D22 two-step, no A->B->C).
 4 labels: canonical-label@stratum, highest-confidence per (node,stratum); tie -> lowest assertion-id.
 5 relational + Family-C: region edges; apply canonical-decomposition / decomposition-spurious to
   toponym_decomposition / toponym_etymology.
 CONFLICT (D46-faithful): observation bound above-gate to TWO canonicals -> leave UNBOUND + emit
 projection warning (D24), never silently pick; the contradiction is the signal a merge-canonical is owed.
 DETERMINISM (D36.9): process assertions sorted by stable id -> same L2 = byte-identical L3.

ROLLUP VIEWS generalize etymon_consensus/*_canonical: witnesses rolled to canonical node via
e.canonical_morpheme_id = COALESCE(cm.merged_into, cm.id) JOIN, replacing the COALESCE chains.

REVERSIBILITY + REBUILD (D22 / REBUILD.md): clear-enrichment --stage=canonical drops canonical_* +
nulls canonical_*_id, fully rebuildable from L2 streams. Canonicalization streams become L2 replay
inputs in REBUILD.md registry; rebuild-runbook-currency-reviewer enforces.

NOT DONE (this is design): projection can't RUN until u6fn.2 is built (streams+writers+canonical DDL
exist — nothing to project from yet). Implementation order: u6fn.2 (streams + canonical_* DDL) ->
u6fn.3 (projection algo) -> u6fn.4 (migrate merged_into_id/cognate_id/lemma_id to legacy-import binds
so first projection reproduces today's clustering, then repairs adjust). Mutates the 4.6GB authoring DB
schema — real code PR, in that order.
notes: MERGED #656 (squash 87e68a75, 2026-06-17). The L2->L3 projection engine (project_canonical): mint/bind/merge-canonical/canonical-label, deterministic + idempotent + reversible (clear-enrichment --stage=canonical), terminal pass in run_full_enrichment, project-canonical CLI, runbook + L2_L3_BOUNDARY promoted. ADDITIVE: populates canonical_* + canonical_*_id without touching the legacy merged_into_id/cognate_id/lemma_id readers. 24 tests. Survived a 4-round pr-review-loop (full fleet + Gemini): fixed an int-ref-after-clear crash, added a transaction rollback, cross-type-merge + orphan-label + confidence-gate guards, and a real CLI bug (--confidence-gate 0.8 string-float). NEXT: wyrd-u6fn.4 = legacy-import binds (so the projection reproduces today's clustering) + cut the ~50 readers/views over to the canonical FK join. Only after u6fn.4 does the canonical graph become authoritative and 1a's binds / a D50-native 1b land in generation.

Lower priority; pattern reuse after region proves it out.

Safe to do in place BECAUSE L2 is git-tracked — original codings recoverable from history; region is not D21 evidence. Must be idempotent + re-runnable. Lands as one reviewable commit/PR.

title: aicu.9.1: per-toponym attestation genitive-marker disambiguation (the -es-/-s- signal done right)
description:
FOLLOW-UP to wyrd-aicu.9 (the genitive-s split prior). aicu.9 shipped the COGNATE-CLUSTER classifier only; the per-toponym attestation override was REMOVED before merge because the naive whole-name string marker mis-classified the protected genuine-stone set (rudston/beeston/keston read as town).

ROOT CAUSE (why the naive approach fails): the genitive prior must call the HEAD (town tun vs stone stan) of an -ston name. The string 'ston' = s+ton whether the s is genitive (Bishop's-tun) or stem-initial (rood-stan) — it is genuinely ambiguous at the surface. Worse, the toponym_attestation table largely stores the BARE MODERN NAME ('rudston'), which carries no genitive vowel, and the es+ton / Cs+ton regex matches the bare 'ston' ending, so it flips ~every -ston to split. Verified on live DB: rudston/beeston/keston -> split (WRONG) under the marker; cluster classifier -> rudston literal (RIGHT).

WHAT'S NEEDED (do it right): per-ELEMENT historical-form decomposition, not whole-name string matching. Mine the GENUINELY historical dated forms (e.g. Alfriston <- Alvricestone 1085, which shows the -es- genitive before a town stem) — distinguish them from rows that merely echo the modern name. The toponym_etymology.historical_form column may carry the -es- more faithfully than toponym_attestation. Detect the OE genitive -es- infix between specifier and a TOWN-family head stem, and require it to be unambiguous (residual stem is a town stem, not reachable as a stone stem).

PRECEDENCE: attestation is SUBORDINATE to the cognate-cluster classifier — it may only refine/break ties for cluster-ambiguous (both classes) or unclassified (neither) toponyms, OR override only when the historical genitive is genuinely unambiguous. It must NEVER override a decisive stan/tun cluster verdict. (User's original 'attestation wins' intent stands for the cases where attestation is genuinely decisive; it just is not decisive for the bare-surface -ston case.)

REGRESSION GATE (mandatory): the protected genuine-stone set must stay literal where scholars say stone — rudston (the rood-stone monolith), humberston, little ribston, etc. Build a test from these BEFORE wiring. Note that names like garston/beeston are genuinely town in SOME places and stone in others (cross-region variation) — the per-place breakdown is ground truth, so the gate is per-(name,region/etymon), not per-name.

CODE: wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/genitive_priors.py (the classifier; attestation hook goes here, subordinate to _classify). Data: toponym_attestation (form, date_year), toponym_etymology.historical_form. The dropped v1 attestation implementation is recoverable from PR #641 history (the pre-rework commit 1866f822 had attestation_verdict + the two-pass gate) as a starting reference for what NOT to do (whole-name regex).

aicu.9 is shippable WITHOUT this (cluster classifier: ston 355/23 P=0.936, ster 0/42, rudston->stone). This ticket is the quality refinement.
notes:
INVESTIGATION 1 (feasibility, 2026-06-16) — the design is FOUND and SAFE.
Data characterization (live DB, read-only):
- toponym_attestation = 86,156 rows but only 3% (3,096) differ from the modern name; 97% just echo the modern spelling. THIS is why v1 failed (the regex matched the bare modern 'ston' surface). Only 38% have date_year.
- toponym_etymology.historical_form = 5,770/19,924 (29%) — a RICHER -es- source than attestation.
- Combined, 3,405 toponyms have >=1 GENUINELY historical form (folded form != folded modern_name).

THE KEY FIX: run the -es-/-s- detector ONLY on genuinely-historical forms (folded(form) != folded(modern_name)). Validated:
- All protected genuine-stone names (rudston/beeston/keston/garston/...) -> DEFER (no genuine historical form) -> fall to cluster -> STONE. Zero false-town. Regression gate PASSES by construction.
- Kingston -> town via cyningestun/chingestone/kingestone; Alfriston -> town via alfricestun/alvricestone (real -es- + town stem). Recall confirmed where historical data exists.
- aldermaston/adbaston -> DEFER (no historical form) — no spurious signal.

DESIGN:
1. Source: UNION(toponym_etymology.historical_form, toponym_attestation.form), folded.
2. FILTER: keep only forms where folded(form) != folded(modern_name). (Eliminates the v1 modern-echo trap.)
3. Detect on those: -es-/-s- genitive + TOWN-family stem (ton/tun/tune/tone) -> 'town'; unambiguous bound stone stem (stan/stane/staun) -> 'stone'; else None.
4. PRECEDENCE: subordinate to the cognate-cluster _classify — attestation only refines cluster 'both'/'unclassified' (and may corroborate), NEVER overrides a decisive stan/tun cluster verdict.
5. Per-place granularity (toponym row), pooled like the cluster path.

REGRESSION TEST (build first): protected stone set must be stone/defer, never town; kingston/alfriston must be town. Use genuine historical fixtures (form != modern).

NEXT: implement detect_historical_genitive(forms, modern_name) + wire subordinate to _classify in genitive_priors.py; this is a SEPARATE PR from #641 (aicu.9 cluster-only).

IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-16, PR #642, branch kenning/aicu9.1-attestation, STACKED on #641). detect_historical_genitive() + pair_genitive_stems() + _genitive_ambiguous() + _load_historical_forms() in genitive_priors.py; wired SUBORDINATE via _resolve() (cluster decisive wins; attestation only resolves both/unclassified). Genuine-historical filter (folded form != folded modern) is the load-bearing fix. Source: toponym_etymology.historical_form + toponym_attestation.form. No schema change (uses existing columns). LIVE: resolved_by_attestation=15, ston 355->363 split (P unchanged 0.938), protected stone set ZERO attestation-splits (rudston/humberston/ribston->stone). 9 new tests incl the 3 safety guards (resolves-unclassified, never-overrides-decisive, modern-echo-stays-skipped). 726 tests green. Merge after #641.

title: trie_matcher: tied-best cap truncates by arbitrary DAG order before the culture tiebreaker (order-dependence)
description: canonical_decompositions caps the per-position tied-best parse set at MAX_TIED_DECOMPOSITIONS_PER_POSITION via [:cap] in arbitrary DAG/export order, BEFORE _prefer_culture_aligned runs — so a correct culture-aligned parse can be silently dropped if it sorts late. Surfaced by the aicu.3 de-dash: it reordered the L4 export, pushing OE tūn for 'Tonbridge' past the 100-cap → the welsh 'Ton' (wave) homograph leaked into english attestation. Latent order-dependence regardless of de-dash. FIX (shipped this PR): cap 100→256 (real toponyms tie >100; Tonbridge=120; trivial memory — the load-bearing OOM bound is the separate MAX_DECOMPOSITIONS_PER_POSITION=10000) + _cap_tied_decompositions sorts by _alignment_score (stable→bit-stable) before truncating when culture_languages is supplied, so culture-aligned parses survive the cap for the rare >256 set. Unit-tested (test_kenning_trie_matcher: prefers-aligned-over-DAG-order, no-culture-stable-prefix, under-limit-unchanged). Behaviorally inert on the current dashed bundle (full suite 5197 passed); de-risks the aicu.9 de-dash data regen.

title: Matcher: stop -ston(stone) eating the possessive-s of X's-tūn (town); statistical/scholarly split disambiguation
description:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, pre-existing — surfaced by the aicu.3 de-dash). The decomposition matcher mis-parses possessive 'X's-tūn' (town) place names as 'X + ston' (stone): it prefers the longer 'ston' match (0 unaccounted chars) over 'X + s(possessive) + ton' (s left unaccounted), so Occam picks stone. E.g. Bishopston (=Bishop's-tūn, a TOWN) → bishop+ston(stone). This inflates the stone morpheme's weight and starves ton(town) in generation.

GROUND TRUTH (scholarly toponym_etymology, english -ston toponyms): final element is TOWN (tūn/tun/ton) 181 vs STONE (stān) 12 — ~15:1. So -ston is overwhelmingly town, but stone is REAL ~12x (test set: Beeston, Garston, Rudston, Onston, Keston, Syston, Whiston, Humberston, Little Ribston, North/South Anston, Hunston). Must NOT blanket-force town.

DATA LIMITS found while attempting a quick fix (why it's not trivial): (1) the 'ston' surface reflex links ONLY to middle-english:ston (stone) — there is NO town/tūn meaning on the 'ston' surface to relabel to; (2) scholarly toponym_etymology_element.surface_in_modern is EMPTY (NULL) for 395/403, so we can't map which chars the tūn element covers. => the fix MUST make the matcher SPLIT Xston → X + s(possessive) + ton (ton→tūn), i.e. a possessive-s connector (counts as 0 unaccounted) + a tiebreaker that picks town vs stone.

USER'S DESIGN IDEAS (capture for design):
- Identify when ston SHOULD win via STATISTICS + PROXIES: are there statistical differences in the TAGS of the word before the -s- between town vs stone cases? (Tested naively: too noisy alone — Bishop=profession→town, Bee=plant→stone, but many pre-words have no tags. Needs a real statistical model, not a hand rule.)
- Take the KNOWN SCHOLARLY PARSES into account when splitting words (the 403 scholarly -ston breakdowns are labeled data — train/seed the split preference from them).
- FRACTIONAL / PROBABILISTIC scoring: don't pick one parse — give ston n% and ton m% of the splits (e.g. weight the proportions contribution by the scholarly town:stone ratio per context), so the corpus reflects the real distribution instead of all-or-nothing.

RELATED: the trie_matcher culture-aware-cap fix (MAX_TIED 100→256 + _cap_tied_decompositions, shipped with aicu.3) fixed a DIFFERENT homograph bug (welsh Ton leaking via the order-blind cap) — this ticket is the ston/ton possessive-s issue, separate. Also connects to wyrd-aicu.7 (case-as-identity: Ston/ston split). Test set + before-DB (/tmp/before-possessive.db) saved 2026-06-15. aicu.3 ships with test_present_day_english_keeps_oe_ton_and_excludes_celtic_homograph xfail'd referencing THIS ticket.
notes: LIVE-WIRING MERGED (#715, Path B). Connective+genitive fix is now live-on-next-export: genitive_split_prior is an ADDITIVE/optional bundle table (no schema bump; tolerant loader → {}); _compute_proportions_inline trains proportions on connective-corrected decompositions at export. word.py treats Connective as zero-cost/non-content/position-neutral; find_meaning/decompose threaded (None=bit-stable). Grader: head 0.13→0.64 on -ston, 177/8. Committed dev seed UNCHANGED (stale since #629) — its refresh is the separate Path-A follow-up; _load_genitive_prior + the bundled table are STAGED for a future live-generation/explain consumer (also filed). Remaining for the EPIC: the dev-seed refresh would let the seed reflect this; aicu.3 (de-dash) unblocks after that.

title: aicu.1 bare-surface merge demotes canonical etymon ranking (wick→wīc, ley→lēagum outranked by thin-gloss variant)
description:
Discovered fixing wyrd-aicu.6 (canonical-morpheme suite). D45/aicu.1 merges a morpheme's position-variants (post/inner/bare) into ONE bare-surface meaning_db key with entries UNIONED. For 'wick' and 'ley' this pooled a THIN-gloss variant with the canonical scholarly etymon, and _rank_siblings now ranks the thin one TOP:
  - wick: top = oe_forms=['wick'], meanings=['clearing and dwelling','dwelling']  — OUTRANKS  oe_forms=['wīc','wic',...], meanings=['A dwelling; a building... dairy farm, trading settlement...'] (the canonical wīc).
  - ley:  top = oe_forms=['ley','-ley','leye'], meanings=['clearing','field']  — OUTRANKS  oe_forms=['lēagum'], meanings=['Glade','Meadow'].
Pre-aicu.1 the post-position key (-wick / -ley) held only the canonical sibling so it ranked top (the suite passed). The position-merge changed the ranking input.

IMPACT: generation/display picks the top etymon, so wick/ley now surface the thin variant instead of the rich canonical gloss. Likely affects OTHER merged pools beyond these two (canonical suite only spot-checks ~18). NOT user-urgent (prod pre-launch), but a real quality regression.

INVESTIGATE: why does _rank_siblings prefer the thin variant in the merged pool (wyrd-emlb within-bucket ranking — witness/tag/gloss-count tiebreak?). Decide whether the merge should dedup/prefer the richer etymon, or ranking should weight gloss richness / witness count differently. This touches generation-wide ranking — needs its own review, not a drive-by.

Tracked by: test_bundle_canonical_morphemes.py marks wick+ley xfail(strict=True) referencing this ticket; removing the xfail is the fix's acceptance test.
notes: ALSO surfaced in aicu.3 PR #634 (db-reconstructibility, P3): the bare-surface de-dash preserves CASE, so ~14/9082 legacy reflex rows whose stored case diverges from the writer convention (Beck vs beck, Moel vs moel — pre=Title, inner/post=lower) (a) skip 2 genuine case-variant merges and (b) won't fold with a future mine (writer produces 'beck', stored is 'Beck' → ON CONFLICT(surface_form,position) misses → second row). Same case-as-identity root as Field/field. When aicu.7/aicu.4 decides the case model, either lowercase inner/post in storage (render owns the front-cap by slot) or normalize-on-fold. The ~14 rows are pre-existing data noise, not urgent.
close_reason: Fixed (#724): _rank_siblings sorts a tags-present signal above surface_similarity so canonical etymons outrank untagged thin mining stubs (wick→wīc, ley→leah, worth→worð). Full-corpus investigation chose this predicate (46 improvements/0 pinned regressions; the only one that also fixes ley — gloss/citation-count wrongly promote tūn). _XFAIL_RANKING emptied; ley/worth pins corrected to canonical lemmas. Seed refreshed + coupled artifacts reconciled. ~10 off-pin collateral (untagged-canonical loses to tagged off-sense) filed as a net-acceptable follow-up.

title: Tag composer offers culture-empty tags (e.g. 'monster' for english) → 'no eligible name' or silent no-op
description: The tag vocabulary is culture-agnostic (shared across all 5 cultures), so the SPA 'Customize moods & tags' composer offers tags that NO morpheme in the selected culture actually carries. Concrete: 'monster' (a fantasy/pfsrd2-corpus tag) is offered for english but 0 english morphemes carry it. Effects: bare tags=['monster'] → 'no eligible name' (raises, post-c6o1.4); combined e.g. tags=['animal','monster'] → 'monster' silently contributes nothing (OR-semantics) while 'animal' dominates. Either way the user is misled about what a tag will do. Found while diagnosing a user report ('added monster, got all-animal no-variety names') — the saturation itself is wyrd-c6o1.4 (fixed, PR #631); THIS ticket is the separate UX/data gap. title: morphemes_by_word drops picked morpheme_id → tags mis-reported by surface→meanings[0] for polysemous surfaces
description: Found while verifying wyrd-c6o1.4. In the generate output, every morpheme in GenerationResult.morphemes_by_word has morpheme_id=None, so the breakdown/inspector resolves each morpheme's TAGS by surface→meanings[0] (the first sense) instead of the sense the generator actually PICKED. For polysemous surfaces this mis-reports tags. Concrete: --tag water seed=21 'Dūnworth' — select() picked morpheme_id 'modern-english:worth' tagged [topography, water] for the post slot, but morphemes_by_word reports usage='-worth', morpheme_id=None, tags=['architecture'] (meanings[0]). The generation is CORRECT (selection-level: 60/60 names get >=1 tagged morpheme post-c6o1.4); only the reported tags are wrong. Impact: the SPA inspector grid + any tag-based UI show the wrong sense's tags, making --tag look like it didn't apply even when it did. Fix: propagate the picked morpheme_id (picked_ids already flows into NewName) through to morphemes_by_word so the breakdown resolves the picked sense by id (cf. wyrd-i4jd), not surface→meanings[0]. Broader than --tag: affects displayed tags for ALL polysemous surfaces.

title: Structure allowlist via YAML config (enabled: false filtering); fold the <Bare> special-case into it
description:

Design (user-specified):
- Dump the full structure inventory into a YAML config file (one entry per structure as mined from proportions).
- Each entry defaults to enabled: true when unspecified; the operator curates by adding enabled: false to unwanted structures.
- The generator filters its structure pool through this config at load time.
- MIGRATE the existing <Bare> special-case block to this mechanism so there is exactly ONE filtering path in code (no parallel special cases).

Implementation notes:
- Provide a CLI to dump current structures to the YAML (so the operator starts from the real inventory; rebuilds can diff new structures in as enabled-by-default).
- Decide placement: per-culture or global file; likely lives with register_effects.yaml under data/ and ships in the bundle/L4 so Lambda + CLI + SPA agree.
- Mind D43/wyrd-zzli interactions: structure filtering already happens at proportions-build time for the bare pre/post/inner-word templates — this config is the operator layer on top.
- Seeded output will change when structures are disabled — pre-launch posture per D41/D43 (bit-stability subordinate to product).

Acceptance: <Bare> blocking comes from the YAML (code special-case deleted); disabling a structure removes it from generation across CLI/Lambda/SPA; new structures from a rebuild default to enabled.

title: Rerolls don't respect D43 bare word placement (wp- buckets)
description:
Rerolling produces names that violate the D43 bare word-sequence placement model (proportions_bare_word_position / wp-pre|wp-inner|wp-post buckets, wyrd-rogd.13): e.g. structured bare words appearing at word positions they're never attested in ('Parva Wigston' shapes). Initial generation respects placement; the reroll path apparently does not.

Likely cause: the reroll path (single-slot re-pick, SPA or API side) bypasses _flatten_struct_slots' word-position derivation / the wp-bucket key extension, sampling from the un-extended bucket instead.

Where to look: the reroll/re-pick entry point vs the full-generation path in proportions.py / vector_name_select.py — make the reroll resolve the slot's word position from the struct the same way initial generation does (D43: the wp bucket, when present, is authoritative).

Acceptance: rerolling a bare slot at word position P only draws structured words attested at P (plus naked words), matching initial-generation behavior.
notes: PR #636. Root: reroll (kenning_regenerate) built its selection bucket key via _bucket_key WITHOUT the D43/rogd.13 wp- word-position extension that _flatten_struct_slots adds for bare words → re-rolled bare words sampled the un-positioned pool → landed at word-positions never attested ('Parva Wigston'). Fix: extend the reroll's bucket_key with wp-{word_position_for(wi, word_count)} for a bare slot in a multi-word name (single-word → None → no extension); NewName struct stays raw. Verified: bare last-word reroll keys ('bare','single','wp-post'). Regression test (bare→wp-extended, non-bare→none). Full suite 4933 passed. Awaiting review.

title: Export perf: skip/freeze the inline proportions rebuild (decomposes all 85,718 toponyms every emit)

title: Decomposition: build the matcher once, pickle it, upload alongside the full-corpus DB; explain/decompose load the pickle instead of rebuilding
description:
Your #2: when the decomposition path is used (kenning-explain / era-map / rewind), it loads the full ~90k corpus and the matcher. Rather than rebuild the matcher/surface-index from scratch on each cold container, build it once at publish time, pickle it, and upload it alongside the full-corpus runtime DB on S3. The decomposition load path then deserializes the pickle (fast) instead of reconstructing.

Caveats: pickle is Python-version + class-shape sensitive — version the pickle and validate against the DB's schema/bundle version on load; fall back to rebuild on mismatch. Keep it OUT of the generation load path (generation uses the trimmed DB, wyrd-<trim>).

This is the optimization layer on top of the lazy full-corpus load that wyrd-<trim> introduces for explain.
Refs: wyrd-<trim>, decomposition.py, runtime/name.py find_meaning.

title: Fix --cohesion no-op: normalize tag_cooccurrence flat-counts → nested probs at runtime
description:
--cohesion is wired end-to-end but a guaranteed no-op (byte-identical output cohesion=0 vs 1). Handoff blamed missing tag_cooccurrence data, but the data IS collected during toponym→morpheme decomposition (proportions_builder.ordered_tag_pairs) and ships in seed-runtime.db (english 1323 cells etc). Real bug: shape+units mismatch. NameGenerator.tag_cooccurrence is flat raw counts {'a|b': N} (proportions.py:981) but _cohesion_multiplier (vector_name_select.py:116-170) expects nested probs {'a':{'b':p in [0,1]}}. flat .get(bare_tag) always misses → pair_count==0 → returns 1.0 always.

Fix (runtime-only, no re-emit): build_cohesion_table(flat, tag_marginal) -> nested conditional P(b|a) at load_proportions; thread tag_marginal (already in bundle, unused) into NameGenerator; pass nested table to select_via_vector_scoring. Sort tag iteration in _cohesion_multiplier for PYTHONHASHSEED bit-stability now that path goes live. Bit-stable at default by construction (cohesion<=0 short-circuits before touching table). Related: wyrd-mj2 / D17 refinement.
notes: pr-review-loop complete (8a69f2b4). External bots unavailable today (Gemini rate-limited 24h; Cursor not configured) → ran Claude-fallback + default agents (code-reviewer, pr-test-analyzer, type-design-analyzer) + dead-code + final-verification. No P1/P2 bugs. Addressed: param rename tag_cooccurrence→cohesion_table (foot-gun), cohesion=0 fast-path restored, doc-rot, +2 tests (suppress-without-collapse, non-english diversity). Final-verification clean → exit. CI green 2/2. Ready to merge (awaiting human per no-direct-to-main). Follow-up filed: wyrd-3iln (strengthen realism lever).

title: kenning: native-render quality — clunky reconstructed/compound forms (Càrrhæferedisc, Botlstānig)
description: Surfaced by wyrd-i4jd (#566): now that the name renders the PICKED etymon's own native form (D38 + id-first), some morphemes render clunky reconstructed/compound native surfaces — e.g. scottish 'Carhafedisc'->'Càrrhæferedisc', english 'Eastan Bolstone'->'East Botlstānig', welsh 'Bodhennant'->'Bodhengestnant'. The id-first change is CORRECT (name=etymology=grid=highlight); this is the separate render/ranking-QUALITY axis: (a) is the picked etymon's native form genuinely ugly (data), (b) is the native composition concatenating badly (render bug — doubled letters / compound seams like 'hæferedisc'), or (c) is the vector scorer picking a poor etymon? Investigate a few worst cases; decide whether to gate/soften native rendering for clunky reconstructed forms, improve the native-form composition, or treat as ranking-quality. Compare old (pre-i4jd) prettier forms — those came from a DIFFERENT sibling, so the fix is honest but uglier. Spotted while reviewing the 31 parity name changes.

title: Semantic register axis is a no-op — positive tag-boost moods (grim/pastoral/devotional) don't change output
description:
## Symptom
Thematic (semantic-tag) moods have ZERO effect on generation. Measured: `mood=grim` changes **0/300** english outputs at novelty=0 (same seeds, with vs without); `mood=harsh` changes **297/300**. grim's effect is correctly defined + parsed — parse_mood_spec('grim').semantic_tags = {death:0.7, military:0.3, monster:0.5, undead:0.6, magic:0.4} — but it never reaches the rendered surface. Confirmed indirectly in the wyrd-fca0 sweep: grim-tag share under mood=grim == the no-mood baseline (0.141) at every novelty stop.

## Root cause (mechanism)
Post-wyrd-bol9 the per-slot selection has two layers (build_slot_base_scores → _apply_per_usage_frequency in runtime/vector_name_select.py):
- **cross-usage** pick weight = the empirical per-position bucket FREQUENCY (freq[usage]), NOT the composed score.
- **within-usage** weight = the D36.2 composed score ratio (phon+sem+pos+baseline) — but this only chooses among multiple SENSES of the SAME usage, which renders the SAME surface either way.
- the score additionally drops a SENSE when bs < 0 (the negative filter, line ~595).

So the composed score's only surface-affecting power is (a) within-usage sense disambiguation (no surface change) and (b) NEGATIVE-score filtering (drops a usage when all its senses go ≤0). A register that adds POSITIVE weight to desired tags (grim death+0.7, pastoral plant/water+, devotional saint+) never drops anything and never changes the frequency-driven cross-usage pick → no-op. Phonological 'harsh' works ONLY because it drives opposed (soft) morphemes NEGATIVE, dropping them.

## Impact
The thematic half of the mood system (D6/D37 grim, pastoral, devotional, mortuary, and the semantic_tags component of noble/sinister/ancient/etc.) is effectively inert. A GM asking for 'grim' / 'pastoral' names gets baseline output. Only phonological effects (harsh, and the phonological components of other moods) bite. This is a silent regression introduced by the wyrd-bol9 per-usage-frequency layer (which was added for per-usage parity with the retired proportions sampler).

## Fix directions (pick one)
1. Let the composed score modulate the CROSS-usage weight, not just within-usage — e.g. weight = freq[usage] × f(score) where f lifts above 1 for positively-scored usages (would let positive tag boosts surface their morphemes). Must preserve realism bands + bit-stability at default (no mood).
2. Make a positive semantic boost act as a soft FILTER/multiplier at the usage level (aggregate sense scores to a usage-level multiplier on freq).
3. Reconsider whether per-usage frequency should fully own cross-usage selection when a register is active (frequency for default, score-modulated when a mood/tag request is present).

## Verify
- Repro: generate english N=300 with vs without mood=['grim'] at novelty=0, same seeds → currently 0 differ; mood=['harsh'] → ~297 differ.
- After fix: mood=grim should raise the grim-tag share (death/military/monster/undead/magic) measurably above the ~0.14 baseline, without breaking test_kenning_realism_absolute or the no-mood bit-stability.

## Refs
- wyrd-fca0 (surfaced this), wyrd-bol9 (per-usage frequency layer = the cause), D36.2 (composition rule — semantic axis is SUPPOSED to contribute), D6/D37 (mood catalog), registers/effects.parse_mood_spec, runtime/vector_name_select.py build_slot_base_scores + _apply_per_usage_frequency
notes:
DEEPER DIAGNOSIS (2026-06-09, corrected — the original 'per-usage frequency cancels the semantic axis' was only HALF the story). mood=grim is a no-op for TWO compounding reasons:

LAYER 1 (primary): mood is wrongly applied as a HARD gate. build_request_vector expands mood -> gate.required_tags = {death,military,monster,undead,magic} (legacy parity with proportions' _apply_mood->filter_for_tag). In the vector path this filters the eligible pool to grim-only (~25 morphemes for english). That pool is too small to satisfy most structures (few grim morphemes have per-position frequency), so select_via_vector_scoring fails the struct and the generation FALLS BACK to the ungated pool (~496) — traced: the final picks come from a 496-pool, not the 25-pool, and are non-grim ('in','-or','-with','cross'). Net: grim output == no-mood output (0/200 differ). Per D36.6 a mood's semantic component is supposed to be the SOFT preference (the vector semantic axis); --tag is the HARD gate. So mood-as-required_tags is the design error.

LAYER 2 (secondary): even with the pool ungated, the SOFT semantic axis has no cross-usage teeth — post-wyrd-bol9 the per-usage frequency owns cross-usage selection and the composed score only re-weights WITHIN a usage's senses (no surface change). So a soft mood preference still wouldn't surface its morphemes.

COHERENT FIX (two parts):
A. Stop expanding mood into gate.required_tags — mood is a SOFT preference (D36.6), not a hard filter. Keep --tag as the hard gate. Removes the too-aggressive-gate -> fallback path; the full pool stays in play.
B. Give the semantic axis a CROSS-usage lever: modulate the per-usage frequency weight by the register's centered semantic fit (prototype: exp(beta * sem_w * (sem_score - mean_register_weight*len(tags))) — provably 1.0 for the uniform default + empty/harsh registers, so bit-stable where output already works; only thematic moods move output). Prototype lands in a worktree (kenning/semantic-axis-teeth, uncommitted) and works: grim changes 285/300 outputs.

OPEN CALIBRATION QUESTION (genuinely a product call): how STRONG should a mood be? The boost magnitude is hypersensitive — at one setting grim-share (fraction of names with a grim morpheme) rises 0.135 -> 0.147 (barely noticeable); at another it saturates to 1.000 (every name grim, monotonous). Need to pick a target (e.g. ~0.4-0.6 = clearly grim, not every-name) and tune beta/clamp there. Same lever will set the strength of ALL thematic moods (pastoral/devotional/etc.).

Bit-stability guardrails for the fix: test_kenning_realism_absolute (no-mood) must stay byte-identical; harsh (phonological, sem empty) must stay byte-identical; only thematic moods change. Both hold for part B by construction; part A needs care that removing required_tags doesn't change no-mood (it shouldn't — no mood => no required_tags today anyway).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #565 (squash). Thematic moods reworked from a broken hard required_tags gate (which fell back to ungated → no-op) into a soft 'one mood morpheme per name' overlay (operator's algo: build per-slot pools, randomly enforce mood on one mood-capable slot, others normal). grim-themed share 0.135→0.995, one accent morpheme/name. Bit-stable no-mood (realism gate untouched); full suite 4933 passed; 3 reviewers (incl. general holistic, ran the generator) approved. Multi-mood + graduated mood:0.x intensity deferred to wyrd-6xuk.
