title: Default novelty to 0.1 via env in prod + staging (WYRD_DEFAULT_NOVELTY + slider visibility)
description:
## Want
Shift the novelty default to 0.1 in BOTH production and staging, set via environment, so generated names always carry a small amount of surprise by default. (User direction 2026-06-09.)

## Mechanism already exists — this is wiring + verifying
Per CLAUDE.md SPA feature-flags: `WYRD_DEFAULT_<OPTION>` overrides an option's DEFAULT VALUE (not just visibility), resolved per-request onto /api/manifest (no redeploy needed to change the value once the var is set). Terraform maps `var.feature_flag_defaults` -> `WYRD_DEFAULT_<OPTION>` (terraform/main.tf:247-248). So `WYRD_DEFAULT_NOVELTY=0.1` is the lever; no new server code expected.

## Work
1. **Set it in terraform for both envs**: `feature_flag_defaults = { novelty = "0.1" }` (applies to prod + staging via the per-env tfvars / module call). Confirm 0.1 lands as a float through the manifest -> SPA seed -> generate path (WYRD_DEFAULT_* values are strings in env; verify the option parses '0.1' -> 0.1; generators/kenning.py does `float(params.get('novelty', 0.0) or 0.0)`, and the manifest seed should feed the SPA field its default).
2. **Slider visibility in prod**: the novelty control is gated behind WYRD_FF_NOVELTY (off in prod). Staging already shows it (WYRD_FF_ALL=true). For prod to expose the (now-default-0.1) slider, add `enabled_feature_flags = ["novelty", ...]`. (If the intent is 'apply 0.1 default but keep the control hidden in prod', skip this and document that — but 'make novelty usable' implies showing the slider.)
3. **Verify end-to-end**: with the env set, a fresh prod/staging request returns novelty default 0.1 on the manifest, the SPA slider seeds at 0.1, and an untouched generate uses 0.1.

## Coordination
- Pairs with wyrd-fca0 (graduated-novelty quality pass): 0.1 is a conservative 'a touch of surprise' default; the quality pass should specifically validate 0.1 output before/with the rollout. Sequence so we're confident 0.1 reads well.
- Depends on the slider (sibling ticket) only for the 'usable slider' half; the default-value shift works regardless of widget.

## Acceptance
- prod + staging manifests report novelty default 0.1; SPA seeds the control at 0.1; default generation uses 0.1; terraform committed + applied.

## Refs
- CLAUDE.md SPA feature flags (WYRD_DEFAULT_*, enabled_feature_flags), terraform/main.tf:239-249, wyrd/feature_flags.py, wyrd-fca0, wyrd-fcub
notes: Sequencing update (2026-06-09): prod has NO users yet — pre-first-public-release, still bug-fixing. So shipping novelty=0.1 is NOT a user-facing behavior change and is NOT gated on the wyrd-fca0 quality pass. Ship 0.1 to prod+staging now; the quality pass validates the broader range independently. (The 'related' link to wyrd-fca0 is topical, not a blocker.)
close_reason: Shipped in PR #548 (squash). Slider + terse description + novelty default 0.1 (prod+staging). The general holistic review caught that the env default was a no-op on generation (SPA omits at-default fields); fixed with server-side WYRD_DEFAULT application in _dispatch (feature_flags.apply_env_defaults) — now fixes every value-changing env default, not just novelty. CI green; full suite 4892 passed.

title: Mine a real surname corpus (etymology + formation class) into the lexicon
description:
Parent epic: wyrd-pbjv. FIRST TARGET of the surname work.

## Goal
Build the family-name corpus wyrd lacks: ingest historical surnames with their etymology and FORMATION CLASS (toponymic / patronymic / occupational / descriptive-nickname) into the lexicon, so generators (wyrd-pbjv children) and the existing morpheme machinery can use them. Mirror the toponym mining pipeline shape.

## Current state
- 0 surname/family-name/patronymic/occupational etymons in the authoring DB; only the hardcoded 39-entry norman_manorial_families.json exists.
- 8,543 male + 392 female given-name etymons already present (likely wiktextract) — the patronymic class can lean on these.

## Sources to evaluate
- Wiktextract surname entries (the ingest path wyrd-4rt already handles; surnames carry 'Surname' senses + often an etymology/formation note). Likely the cheapest large source — no new mining tier.
- PD surname-etymology dictionaries (Bardsley, Reaney, Lower 'Patronymica Britannica') via the existing LLM mining pipeline (mine-llm) — same form-in-body validator + tier model as toponyms (D2/D3). Check PD status per source.
- Cross-link toponymic surnames to existing toponym etymons (de Vere -> Ver; Ashby -> the place) via the descent/decomposition graph.

## Schema / tagging
- Add formation-class tags (toponymic / patronymic / occupational / descriptive) + a 'surname' (or 'family name') tag. Decide whether these live as etymon_tag values or a dedicated column/table. Reuse the existing tag machinery if it fits.
- Patronymic affixes (-son, Mac-/Mc-, O'-, -ez, ben-, -ovich, -sson) are a small curated set worth a sidecar like norman_manorial_families.json.

## Sensitivity / IP (D7, D11)
- Real surnames of living people / specific families: apply the D7 living-community + D11 IP rules. Bulk PD etymology dictionaries and wiktextract surname *etymons* are fine; avoid bundling targeted modern-family datasets.

## Acceptance
- A surname corpus in the lexicon with formation-class tags, queryable + exportable, and a documented INGESTION.md procedure (or a sibling-pipeline doc per wyrd-ami).
- Patronymic-affix sidecar shipped.
- Coverage report: counts per formation class per culture.

## Refs
- wyrd-pbjv (epic), wyrd-4rt (wiktextract ingest), wyrd-ami (sibling-pipeline model), D2/D3/D7/D11, OVERVIEW.md (authoring vs runtime layers)

title: Family-name (surname) corpus + generators
description:
## Motivation

wyrd has a HUGE given-name corpus — 8,543 `male name` + 392 `female name` etymons in the authoring lexicon DB (heavily male-skewed, ~22:1) — but essentially NO family-name data: `family name` / `surname` / `patronymic` / `occupational` tags are all 0 in both the DB and the runtime bundle. The only surname data anywhere is the hardcoded 39-entry `data/norman_manorial_families.json`. And there is no people-name generator at all: every Generator is toponym/creature-oriented (Kenning, KenningExplain/Rewind/EraMap/Render, wyrd-ami).

Surnames are a natural fit for wyrd's etymon/morpheme machinery because the classic formation classes are derivable from material we already have or are adjacent to:
- toponymic ('de Vere', 'Ashby', 'of <place>') -> Kenning already generates place names
- patronymic ('Williamson', 'MacDonald', 'ben-') -> given-name corpus + affixes
- occupational ('Smith', 'Fletcher', 'Baker') -> trade morphemes
- descriptive/nickname ('Strong', 'Whitehead', 'le Blanc') -> adjective/feature morphemes

## Scope (user direction 2026-06-09: all of the below, each its own ticket; the CORPUS mine is the first target)

Children:
1. **Mine a real surname corpus** (FIRST TARGET) — ingest historical surnames + etymology + formation class into the lexicon, like the toponym pipeline. The foundation the generators ride on.
2. **Family-name generator composing existing machinery** — toponymic via Kenning, patronymic via given-names + affix, occupational/descriptive via surname morphemes.
3. **Fantastical-first surname generator** — fantasy/fictional output (invented dynasties / NPC houses), register/phonology-driven; doesn't require a real surname corpus.

## Also worth addressing (cross-cutting)
- The given-name corpus is badly female-skewed (8543 vs 392) — surface as a data-coverage gap; relevant to patronymic generation balance.
- Composes with / informs wyrd-v3o9 (manorial structure) and the existing `manorial_affix` knob (Norman manorial families ARE toponymic surnames).

## Refs
- norman_manorial_families.json + _norman_manorial_subjects (the only extant surname data)
- saint_personal_names.json (_saint_personal_name_subjects sidecar) — the given-name sidecar pattern to mirror
- wyrd-ami (sibling research pipeline) — model for a non-toponym mining pipeline
- D7/D11 (sensitivity + IP rules — apply to any real surname source)

title: Migrate off Gemini Code Assist before it sunsets (2026-07-17)
description:
Gemini Code Assist (the consumer GitHub PR-review bot) is being deprecated. Per the notice on its own PR reviews:
- New org installations BLOCKED starting 2026-06-18.
- ALL code-review activity officially CEASES 2026-07-17.
- Docs: https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review

## Impact
Our pr-review-loop skill uses Gemini as the PRIMARY review bot (C1 of each round): /gemini review trigger, get-review-comments.sh, reply-to-comment.sh thread resolution. After 2026-07-17 those calls return nothing — the loop silently loses its main broad-correctness pass, leaving only the AGENT-REVIEWERS fleet + (if configured) Cursor Bugbot.

## Options to evaluate
1. **Cursor Bugbot** — already a supported bot in pr-review-loop (--cursor). Lowest-friction swap; auto-reviews on push. Verify it's installed on the repo + tune priority parsing.
2. **Lean on the agent reviewers** — the repo already configures 29 AGENT-REVIEWERS (defaults + 26 custom). These ran well on PR #498 (caught the 2 real coverage gaps Gemini missed). Could promote them to the primary signal and drop the external bot.
3. **Claude fallback** — pr-review-loop has a --claude path (claude-review.sh) that posts a PR-level review. Heavier but no external dependency.
4. Some combination (e.g. Cursor for broad pass + agent fleet for depth).

## Deliverable
Decide the replacement before ~2026-07-01 (ahead of the 07-17 cutoff), update any docs/CLAUDE.md guidance that says "Gemini is the default reviewer", and confirm the chosen path works end-to-end on a real PR. If Cursor: confirm installation + that trigger-review.sh --cursor and comment parsing work.

Context: surfaced in Gemini's own review of PR #503.

title: Revert superseded rd69/2wml descent detaches from _collapses.jsonl (rebuild-consistency)
description: The deployed era-grid fix is the per-form toponym-reflex audit (wyrd-1wv2): it detaches modern noise leaves -> 82->91% clean. The earlier descent edge-audit (wyrd-rd69 PR #495 / wyrd-2wml PR #496) also wrote detach rows to data/mining/_collapses.jsonl, but those were empirically INEFFECTIVE on the era-grid (0 noise improvement) and net-negative (delete deep proto edges for no benefit). They are NOT applied to the current live DB (reverted), so the DEPLOYED bundle (from the live export) is correct. BUT a from-scratch rebuild runs apply_collapses over ALL _collapses rows -> would re-apply the descent detaches, diverging from the deployed state. ACTION: identify the rd69/2wml detach rows in _collapses.jsonl (method tags from descent_audit) and remove them, so a clean rebuild reproduces the 91%-clean deployed state. Verify with a rebuild + era-grid noise measurement (should stay ~91%).
close_reason: MERGED (PR #499). Stripped all 2,240 llm-descent-audit-detach-v1 rows from _collapses.jsonl + re-emitted toponym detaches onto the stripped base (re-added 108 contaminated refs as pure toponym rows; net -2,240/+108). Independent validator + structural check: 0 descent rows remain, all 5,921 toponym detach EFFECTS preserved (0 missing), all historical collapse families intact, base->PR diff is descent-only (toponym grew 5805->5913, never shrank). Rebuild now reproduces the deployed 91%-clean state (live DB = baseline 1,618,062 - 12,201 toponym edges = 1,605,861, confirmed; descent detaches independently proven 0 era-grid effect). Full rebuild-sim was blocked by a backup-file lock but the structural proof + edge-count math are conclusive.

title: Descent over-merge Phase 2b: glossless-proto-conductor screen (val->vulva class)
description:
Follow-on to wyrd-rd69 Phase-2a (PR #495, the gloss-visible bridge-edge audit). The dominant over-merge case — an un-glossed proto conductor (itc-pro:*wolwumen) fanning out to etymologically-distinct GLOSSLESS descendants (vulva, valgus, vulgus) dragged into old-french:val's cluster — is NOT caught by the gloss-sense-group screen, because the polluting members carry no gloss so the cluster looks coherent (val: only 3 of 23 members glossed, all 'valley'). Confirmed 2026-06-07: detect found 0 *wolwumen/vulva candidates.

Options: (a) backfill glosses for the glossless Latin/proto members FIRST (mine-element-glosses / LLM), then re-run audit-descent (they'd become gloss-visible); (b) a high-fanout-proto degree screen: for proto/reconstruction conductors with out-degree > N, judge each child against the cluster's dominant glossed sense even when the child is glossless (the gemma judge handles 'is Latin vulva the same family as a cluster whose sense is valley?' from forms alone — validated in the 2a dry-run). Bound to avoid flooding legit cognate fan-outs (*haimaz->home/heim/ham). File from main.
close_reason: Phase-2b glossless-proto-conductor screen merged (PR #496). scope=2b added; full scope=both run landed 6,728 verdicts / 2,467 detaches (incl. val/vulva via *wolwumen). Engine complete; rollout tracked on wyrd-rd69.

title: hām (and peer suffixes) missing genuine modern reflex in cognate cluster (home/ham absent) — leaves -ham all-self so genuine-wins can't clean it
description:
Secondary to the reflex-link bug. hām (etymon 361243, cognate_id 361245, cluster size 100) has only 2 modern-english cluster members: 'AM' (junk) and 'hame' (Scots) — the real modern reflexes 'home'/'ham' are MISSING from the cluster. The OCR-variant 'ham' (id 507650) is merged_into hām and its only descent modern child is 'hyem' (junk). Compare tūn (cognate_id 346202): 14 modern members incl. town/tun/toun.

Consequence: hām has NO genuine (non-self) modern-english era_reflex, so the wyrd-5olv genuine-wins merge fix is a NO-OP for it (its fallback keeps all the self-seeded town surfaces). Same for -ing/ing (bound suffixes, inherently no standalone modern reflex). Other major suffixes (lēah, dūn, feld, hyll, healh, wīc, burg, ford, wudu, cot, stān, worð) DO have genuine modern reflexes and ARE cleaned by wyrd-5olv.

Root: the wiktextract descent/cluster ingest never linked hām -> home (modern-english), or 'home' landed in a different cognate cluster. Likely a descent-edge / cluster-cognates gap. Fix (data-side, mining-fixable per user 2026-06-06): ensure hām's cognate cluster carries its genuine modern reflex (add the inheritance edge hām->home / re-cluster). Once present, the already-deployed genuine-wins fix cleans -ham automatically. NOTE: the reflex-link prune (the P1 sibling ticket) is the more complete fix — it removes the bad town reflexes outright rather than masking them; this ticket is the belt-and-suspenders data-quality fix for the cluster gap.

title: -ton under-represented in generated names (~1 in 20-40 vs ~20% of real English towns)
description:
User observation (2026-06-06): real-world ~20% of English town names end in -ton, but the kenning generator surfaces -ton only ~1 in 20-40 names. -ton is the single most productive English toponymic suffix and should appear far more often.

This is a GENERATION-SAMPLING issue, distinct from the era-grid display fix (wyrd-5olv, which kept generated names byte-identical). Likely causes to investigate:
1. -ton's weight in the per-(culture x position) proportions tables is too low relative to its real frequency. Check proportions_usage / proportions_single_usage for english culture: what is -ton's cumulative weight share vs other -post morphemes?
2. Dilution: the bundle has 763 usage_keys ending in 'ton' (every -Xton town became its own morpheme). If the matcher/proportions split -ton's mass across all these compound keys instead of concentrating it on the -ton morpheme, -ton-the-suffix is under-weighted. (Related to the morpheme_id attribution issue — see the wyrd-5olv successor tickets.)
3. scoring_mode=vector (staging/prod default) may weight differently than proportions; check both modes.
4. Structure templates (post-wyrd-zzli filter) may under-represent the [pre + -post] shapes that -ton fills.

Investigate against the live bundle + proportions; measure -ton's empirical share vs a target (~real-world). Fix may be proportions/weighting, de-duplication of the -Xton compound keys, or vector-axis tuning. No code yet — scope first.

title: era-grid: -ing 44-gloss blob survives merge-audit (mixed glosses bridge sense-groups)
description: The 6hbv merge-audit did NOT clean old-english:-ing (still ~44 glosses spanning patronymic -ingas + hill + water-meadow + verb 'inflection of ingān'). Root cause: the audit's disjoint-sense detection (_anchor_intruders / _sense_groups in merge_audit.py) uses gloss-token union-find, and MIXED glosses on -ing members — e.g. 'sons of; or water-meadow', 'meadow, water meadow, ing' — contain tokens from BOTH senses, bridging the patronymic and meadow groups into ONE connected component, so the family isn't flagged disjoint and old-english:ing (hill/water-meadow) is never reverted off -ing. Fixes to consider: (1) gloss-suppression of the mixed/conflated glosses (etymon_gloss_suppression) then re-run audit; (2) treat -ing as an etymon-SPLIT (apply_etymon_splits) into patronymic vs topographic senses; (3) split a gloss on ';'/'or' before tokenizing in _sense_groups so a mixed gloss votes for multiple groups without bridging. -ton (the other headline) IS fixed. Found during the 6hbv staging deploy 2026-06-05.
notes: LOOP-DECISION (2026-06-20, Devon via Claude): Implement fix option 3 — split mixed glosses on ';' / ' or ' boundaries inside _sense_groups BEFORE tokenizing, so the -ing 44-gloss blob splits into coherent sense-groups instead of bridging them. Least-data, most-general of the three options. Re-run merge-audit after. Low-risk data-quality fix -> LOOP-WORKABLE. Open PR, run pr-review-loop skill (full roster, no manual triage), auto-merge on green CI.
close_reason: PR #701 merged. Fixed merge-audit disjoint-sense detection (the -ing blob): a MIXED gloss ('sons of; or water-meadow') previously bridged the patronymic + topographic sense-clusters in the gloss-token union-find, masking the topographic intruder (old-english:ing). Fix (ticket option 3): split glosses on ';'/' or ' into sub-senses BEFORE tokenizing and group at sub-sense granularity (_sub_sense_token_sets + a shared _union_find_components core; _anchor_intruders now groups via _sense_clusters where a mixed member votes for each sense without bridging, dominant = largest cluster the anchor is in with a deterministic (len, sorted-eids) tiebreak, intruders = members entirely outside the dominant sense). Scoped to merge-audit: shared _sense_groups (used by cluster_reflex_audit + descent_audit) left untouched. 3 review rounds (shared-core extraction, deterministic tie, mutation-verified tie test + ;/or/comma-boundary + non-anchor-shares-dominant coverage). Full suite 5593 passed. NEXT (operator step): re-run merge-audit to actually revert old-english:ing off -ing.

title: era-grid: wrong-etymon anchoring — surfaces resolve to unrelated etymons (Kettle→ceole, -ton→ton)
description: Staging QA (2026-06-05). Some generated-name surfaces anchor to the WRONG etymon in the bundle/matcher: 'Kettle-'→old-english:ceole (throat/gully) instead of ON ketill; '-ton'→modern-english:ton (weight unit) instead of old-english:tūn. The era-grid then renders the wrong morpheme's forms entirely. Distinct from over-merge (separate ticket) — here the surface→etymon mapping itself is wrong (decomposition/anchoring or bundle usage_key keying). Investigate Name.find_meaning / the bundle's per-usage_key primary-entry selection. Likely overlaps the over-merge ticket where modern-english:ton is both wrong-anchor AND over-merged. Defect IDs: 6cd19ade(Kettleton), 84ae6ca8(East Stanton 'fishy'), 506c39de(Row Morton pronunciation).
notes: ROOT CAUSE (2026-06-06): Kettle anchoring is a WRONG REFLEX LINK, not a merge/_rank_siblings issue. The reflex 'Kettle-' (pre) is linked in reflex_etymon to BOTH old-english:cetel (correct: kettle/deep-valley) AND old-english:ceole (WRONG: throat/channel/gorge) — and ceole is also wrongly linked to 'Kel-'. So the bundle's 'Kettle-' usage_key carries both etymons and _rank_siblings surfaces ceole. Fix mechanism: the reflex layer is L2 in data/mining/_reflexes.jsonl (canonical-state {surface_form,position,etymon_refs}); it is SEED-time, NOT part of run_full_enrichment — so a fix needs (a) edit the _reflexes.jsonl row to drop the wrong etymon_ref, AND (b) delete the corresponding reflex_etymon row in the live DB (the bundle build reads reflex_etymon), then re-export. No dedicated prune-reflex CLI exists (link-reflexes only ADDS). RECOMMEND: a systematic reflex-link audit (wrong surface→etymon links where the etymon's gloss is incoherent for the surface), against the FRESH post-(-ing/Phase-2) bundle, rather than one-off Kettle. Deferred from the -ing/Phase-2 staging deploy (2026-06-06).

title: lexicon enrich crashes on element-gloss sidecars (replay_file: row missing '_type')
description: Found during the wyrd-qp9c staging deploy. 'wyrd kenning lexicon enrich --apply' crashes immediately in collect_curation_overrides → replay_file with 'ReplayError: line 1: row missing _type field'. Root cause: cli/lexicon/enrich.py passes jsonl_paths_in(jsonl_dir) (build.py:1017 — ALL data/mining/*.jsonl, no exclusion) to the replay-based collectors (collect_curation_overrides / collect_gloss_suppressions / collect_collapses / etc.), but two sidecars use a bespoke non-event schema with no _type rows: data/mining/_element_glosses.jsonl and _element_gloss_adjudications.jsonl (consumed separately via collect_element_glosses with explicit paths at enrich.py:119-125). replay_file is strict and raises on the first such file. So 'enrich --apply' is currently unusable on main; rebuild-from-jsonl likely hits the same path. Fix options: (a) jsonl_paths_in / the enrich path-set should exclude the bespoke sidecars (the underscore files that have dedicated collectors), or (b) the replay-based collectors should skip files/rows without _type. Workaround used for the qp9c deploy: scratch/deploy_enrich.py filters the two files from the replay collectors before calling run_full_enrichment. NOTE: this means the L3 enrichment chain has not been runnable via the supported CLI since these sidecars landed — worth verifying rebuild-from-jsonl and the deploy runbook.
notes: Confirmed 3 sidecars break the replay-based collectors (all have dedicated bespoke collectors): _element_glosses.jsonl + _element_gloss_adjudications.jsonl (no _type row), and _pronunciation.jsonl (_type:'pronunciation', not in replay_file's allowed set). The deploy workaround (scratch/deploy_enrich.py) excludes all 3 from the replay collectors while still loading them via collect_element_glosses / collect_pronunciation. Proper fix: jsonl_paths_in or the enrich/build path-set must exclude the bespoke sidecars (or replay_file should skip files whose _type isn't an event type).
close_reason:
Already resolved (no PR) — by wyrd-5qg7's jsonl_paths_in exclusion (same fix that resolved sibling wyrd-zhhf), which post-dates this ticket (2026-06-05). Verified empirically:

ROOT CAUSE GONE: enrich.py:115 now passes paths = list(jsonl_paths_in(jsonl_dir)) to ALL replay-based collectors (collect_curation_overrides / collect_gloss_suppressions / collect_gloss_additions / collect_etymon_splits / collect_collapses). jsonl_paths_in (build.py:1052) excludes REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS, which contains all 3 bespoke sidecars (_element_glosses.jsonl, _element_gloss_adjudications.jsonl, _pronunciation.jsonl). The 3 sidecars are loaded separately via their dedicated collectors with explicit paths (collect_element_glosses enrich.py:122-125, collect_pronunciation enrich.py:131). This is exactly the ticket's fix option (a).

EMPIRICAL PROOF: ran all 5 replay collectors over jsonl_paths_in('data/mining') (105 files; all 3 sidecars confirmed ABSENT from the set) — every collector returned without ReplayError. So 'wyrd kenning lexicon enrich --apply' replay path no longer crashes.

REGRESSION-GUARDED: tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py::test_no_unhandled_nonconforming_ledgers (bidirectional drift guard) enforces that every non-conforming data/mining/*.jsonl is in REPLAY_EXCLUDED_LEDGERS, so any file reaching a replay collector via jsonl_paths_in is guaranteed _type-conforming — covers BOTH the enrich path (this ticket) and the rebuild path (zhhf). Plus test_jsonl_paths_in_excludes_replay_excluded_ledgers. Both pass.

OBSOLETE WORKAROUND: scratch/deploy_enrich.py (the qp9c filter) is no longer needed — the supported CLI works. (gitignored; not cleaned here.) No committed doc/runbook references the crash or workaround.

title: era-grid: -don contaminated cluster — wrong don→do inheritance edge drags in the verb
description: Post cluster-cognates-v2 (#481) + the v2 re-mine (#482), old-english:don (glossed hill/farm/dwellings — the toponym) is a 91-member cluster CONTAMINATED with the verb 'do' (do/doff/done/div) via a wrong don→do inheritance edge in Wiktionary's descent data. Because don's cluster (91) is LARGER than the clean dūn (7), it can't be folded (merge would go the wrong way), and ton→tūn-style barren folding doesn't apply (don isn't barren). The era-grid for -don shows do/doff/done in the modern column. FIX: targeted bad-edge cleanup — prune the don→do (and similar semantically-wrong) inheritance edges from etymon_descent, then re-cluster. Broader: a pass to detect/flag inheritance edges where parent and child glosses share no meaning (a quality filter on Wiktionary's descent graph). Separate from the PIE mega-cluster fix (wyrd-uq64, shipped).
notes: PR #483 (branch kenning/don-bad-edge). Root cause was a HOMOGRAPH CONFLATION, not a stray edge: OE 'don' = one (canonical_form,language) row serving both the toponym 'hill' (=dūn) and the verb 'to do'; the verb's 8 descent edges + a prior wrong-direction LLM merge (dūn→don, line 1478 of _collapses.jsonl) put the toponym into the 91-member verb cluster. Fix: new detach_parents/detach_children op on the collapse ledger (apply_collapses deletes the wrong-sense edges before the fold) + revert the dūn→don merge + fold don→dūn + suppress 'to do' gloss + new curate-collapse-etymon CLI. Verified on a DB copy: verb forms gone from the hill cluster, verb lineage intact via OE dōn. Full suite green (4899 passed). DEPLOY (enrichment re-run + bundle re-emit + publish) is the separate operator step.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #483 (merged). Homograph-conflation fix: detach op on collapse ledger + revert wrong dūn→don merge + fold don→dūn + suppress 'to do' gloss + curate-collapse-etymon CLI. Verified: -don leaves the verb cluster, verb lineage intact via OE dōn. Follow-up wyrd-c0a3 (hill/feather-down conflation). Deploy to staging pending.

title: era-grid: -field stops at ME — cross-cluster same-meaning merge (v3ow P3) with homograph handling
description:
User QA (Broomfield): -field renders OE+ME but NO modern column, though 'field' is obviously modern. Root cause: generation resolves -field to old-english:field (cognate 2832244, cluster=6) whose descent chain reaches only toponyms (Hundersfield), not the bare modern 'field' reflex. The rich lineage is old-english:feld (cognate 21044, cluster=224) → middle-english:feld → modern-english:field, spanning all eras. So old-english:field is a parallel anglicized-spelling lineage that should merge into the feld lineage for the same SENSE.

NOT a barren fold (wyrd-v3ow.1): field's cluster is 6, not <=1. This is the v3ow P3 cross-cluster SAME-MEANING merge. COMPLICATION: old-english:field is a HOMOGRAPH — glosses are BOTH 'open land, field' AND 'fold, crease (of clothing), plait, wrinkle'. A wholesale cluster merge into feld would wrongly fold the fold/crease sense. The merge must be SENSE-LEVEL (LLM-judged same-meaning on the open-land sense only), persisted to an L2 _merges.jsonl (replayed free at rebuild, per v3ow DECISION 2), then re-emit. Alternative considered: resolution-ranking (prefer richest-era-coverage morpheme per surface) — broader behavioral change, separate evaluation.

Distinct from wyrd-v3ow.1 (same-language barren fold, shipped) and the era-grid self-seed (shipped #478).

title: Investigate slow runtime-bundle export (export-runtime-db ~15+ min)
description: export-runtime-db (full bundle, ~78.7k meanings → ~210MB SQLite) takes ~15+ min single-threaded and uses ~1GB RSS; under concurrent load it was OOM-killed twice (0-byte output, no file). During wyrd-v3ow.1 this forced several serial re-emits and was the wall-clock bottleneck. Investigate where the time goes (the inline proportions rebuild + per-morpheme era_reflexes/era-grid computation are the suspects — the 'all_decompositions' trie spam suggests repeated decomposition work), and whether it can be (a) parallelized, (b) incrementalized so only changed morphemes re-emit, (c) memory-bounded so it doesn't OOM under load, or (d) cached. Owner: kenning runtime export (wyrd/generators/kenning/cli/lexicon/export_runtime_db.py + runtime/proportions.py).
notes: FIX SHIPPED (temp-table bulk prefetch): _fetch_member_attested_years was 96% of collect_families (per-family UNION/MIN over etymon_text_match + toponym_etymology, re-run for each of ~67K roots). Replaced with _bulk_attested_years — one indexed TEMP TABLE join over all 75,002 members, sliced per family. RESULT: collect_families 67,020 roots ~13min -> 31.5s (~25x); full export ~15min -> ~2-3min. VERIFIED byte-identical: full 67,020-family bulk-vs-per-root diff = 0 mismatches (2,458 year-bearing families); 3 new unit tests + 980 bundle/export tests pass. Remaining (separate, smaller): the proportions rebuild decomposes all 85,718 toponyms every emit (--proportions-dir bypasses); memory ~1GB could stream families.

title: Extend collapse job: LINK cross-era reflexes via inheritance (not just merge)
description: Finding (rogd.9 investigation, 2026-06-03): empty-grid in-use morphemes are path-dependent DUPLICATES of a reflex-rich relative that were never connected — of 79 P1 cases (empty first + rich sibling) ZERO have any descent edge between the empty root and the rich root (26 same-language variant spellings e.g. OE hill 4632179 vs OE hyll 418146; 53 cross-language/era). So the fix is NOT re-typing edges (none exist) and NOT folding cross-era pairs (folding tūn+-ton destroys the era distinction the grid shows). EXTEND the existing collapse machinery (merge-collapses / _collapses.jsonl / enrichment.apply_collapses, wyrd-6xzs/y651): (1) NEW LINK op in the ledger — {_type: collapse, ref: '<parent lang:form>', inherits: '<child lang:form>', edge_type: 'inheritance', method, confidence} — applied by INSERTING an etymon_descent inheritance edge (parent→child), keeping both etymons distinct (vs the existing 'into' fold). (2) extend candidate detection (detect-collapses) to surface cross-era reflex candidates (empty-era-grid etymon + same-gloss relative an era-step away / variant spelling). (3) extend the LLM judgment (gemma on the macbook Ollama 10.5.2.31) to classify each candidate: same-meaning variant → FOLD (into), later-era reflex-of → LINK (inherits), else reject. (4) the 26 same-language variants (hill/hyll) are FOLD candidates the v1 pass MISSED → recall improvement (existing op); the 53 cross-era are LINKS (new op). Rebuildable: link rows ride in _collapses.jsonl, replayed by apply_collapses on rebuild, content-keyed (lang:form). FEEDS rogd.9 (the rollup follows inheritance edges → the linked reflexes unify into one morpheme → empty modern surfaces inherit the canonical's era_reflexes → grids fill).
notes: DONE on branch kenning/rogd15-reflex-link (ready for PR). Mechanism + populated ledger: (1) apply_collapses gains an 'inherits' LINK op → adds an etymon_descent inheritance edge (parent=ancestor, child=reflex), keeps both era forms distinct, idempotent; collect_collapses carries it through → rebuildable replay. (2) detect_reflex_link_candidates: same-family, known era-stage, form-similar, shared-gloss, not-already-edged pairs (cell-map language→(family,rank); orientation parent=earlier). A first full run exposed that cross-family/proto labels flip orientation + identical-form cognates mislink → scoped to one lineage (579 noisy → 97 clean). (3) LLM judgment scaffolding (build_reflex_judge_prompt/parse_reflex_verdict/reflex_verdict_to_row, methods llm-reflex-link-v1 / llm-reflex-rejected-v1). (4) link-reflexes CLI (detect→gemma judge→ledger). (5) RAN on the macbook Ollama (gemma4:26b): 76 inheritance links + 20 rejections appended to data/mining/_collapses.jsonl. Validated correct: OE biscop→bishop (sc→sh), OE beacnes→modern beacon, OE acres→acres; rejects cognates/borrowings/false-form-matches (alne/lyne). 12 tests. NEXT: on rebuild-from-jsonl the ledger replays → 76 inheritance edges; rogd.9's rollup follows them → linked reflexes unify → empty grids fill (lands with Phase 2). Minor follow-up: proto-* era ranking + same-language FOLD recall (hill/hyll) for the existing detector.
close_reason: Merged #469. Reflex-LINK op extends the collapse machinery: apply_collapses 'inherits' adds an etymon_descent inheritance edge (kept distinct, idempotent, replayed from _collapses.jsonl); detect_reflex_link_candidates (same-family/era-stage/form-similar/shared-gloss/not-edged, dedup to one best ancestor per child); LLM judgment + link-reflexes CLI. Ran gemma4:26b → 57 inheritance links + rejections in the ledger (OE biscop→bishop, beacnes→beacon, acres→acres; rejects cognates/borrowings). Review: 5 agents + Gemini 3 rounds (db-recon PASS; dedup→clean ledger, perf, coverage, CLI robustness). 16 tests. The 57 links add inheritance edges on rebuild → rogd.9's rollup consumes them.

title: Bare word-sequence placement (pre/inner/post position stats for bare words)
description: Design (user 2026-06-03): some bare standalone words have a strong WORD-SEQUENCE position bias the model doesn't capture — e.g. 'Saint' is essentially always the FIRST word (Saint Albans), never the tail, yet today any bare slot can pull any bare word. Add a word-position dimension for bare words. NOTE: this is the WITHIN-NAME word position (which word slot in the multi-word name), distinct from the WITHIN-WORD morpheme position (the pre-/-inner-/-post dashes). SPEC: (1) DATA — derive at PROPORTIONS-BUILD time from the existing place-name corpora (the builder already walks each toponym's word sequence); NO new mining, stays rebuildable-from-JSONL. (2) BUCKETS — a bare word's word-position = pre (first word) / inner (interior) / post (last word). 2-word names → pre + post only; no solo case (single-word names not in the model). A word CAN have observations in multiple slots — it just carries different per-slot statistics. (3) NAKED vs STRUCTURED — below a total-observation threshold a bare word is 'naked' (eligible for ANY bare slot via the general bare distribution); at/above threshold it's 'structured' (sampled per its per-slot weights, eligible in each slot it's attested in). Threshold = build-time tuning param. (4) GENERATION — a bare slot at word-position P samples structured-bare words weighted by their P-slot stat PLUS all naked-bare words; the slot's position is derived from the sampled structure's word index. (5) SCOPE — bare only (general word-sequence position = future). (6) SEQUENCING — land AFTER wyrd-rogd.10 (both touch the proportions/usage model; build on the cleaner morpheme keying). IMPL: new per-position bare proportions stat (e.g. proportions_bare_usage keyed by (culture, position, usage_key)) + a per-bare-word total observation count to drive naked<->structured.
close_reason: Merged PR #618. Bare word-sequence placement shipped end-to-end: build-side (word_position, surface) tally over multi-word names (D40 surface identity, case-twin dedupe); raw counts in new L4 proportions_bare_word_position table (no schema bump — defensive adapter read); naked↔structured threshold at LOAD time via WYRD_BARE_POSITION_THRESHOLD (default 3, terraform var bare_position_threshold → Lambda env; deliberately not an SPA advanced option); vector path derives wp-pre/inner/post bucket keys from struct word order with legacy fallback. Validated on a full live export: parva 27/27 post-only, saint never post; 800-seed placement check 0 violations; realism + canonical gates green; legacy DBs bit-stable. Documented as D43. pr-review-loop: 5 rounds, 26 findings, 23 fixed. Activation (re-export + S3 publish) tracked in wyrd-oet8.

title: era-grid modern-english stage polluted by cluster tier (foreign cognates, anthroponyms, toponyms)
description: Part of defect ff022ea4. source='cluster' cells dump the etymon's whole modern-attested cluster into the modern-english stage: cross-language cognates (Ouest [FR], Düne/Zaun [DE]) landing in the ENGLISH family's modern stage (a plain language-misassignment), derived personal names (Wesley, Alaric, Derek, Hank), and multi-word toponyms (West Ham, Westbourne, Coldingham, Notting Hill). ~235/400 sampled morphemes affected. The morpheme's genuine modern reflex is buried or absent. FIX: the modern-english stage should carry the morpheme's modern English reflex form (or be empty), filtering foreign-family cognates, derived anthroponyms, and multi-word/Capitalized toponym examples out of the cluster tier's modern assignment.
notes: ROOT: the modern-english pollution is the descent graph's DERIVATION edges to compounds/derived names — OE tūn derives into Pemberton, Pinkerton, Scruton, Crichton, Symington, Tunstall, etc., and the cluster/descent tier surfaces all of them as 'modern reflexes'. Same for West→West Ham/Westbourne/Wesley. The intent-correct rule is 'reflexes = the morpheme's own continuation (inheritance lineage), NOT new words derived from it', but edge_type is unreliable (tūn→-ton is 'derivation', tūn→Pendleton is 'inheritance'), so the filter needs form-based signals too (multi-word/Capitalized toponym, cross-family cognate, anthroponym) not just edge_type.
close_reason: Merged #471. _fetch_root_era_reflexes (+ fantasy_export's parallel loop) now drops, for MODERN-stage target languages only, era reflexes whose form is multi-word or initial-capitalized — stripping derived toponyms (West Ham, Coldingham), anthroponyms (Wesley, Derek), and mistagged capitalized foreign cognates (Düne, Ouest) from the modern stage, keeping the morpheme's lowercase common-noun reflex (or empty). edge_type unreliable so form-gated. Cleans BOTH the era-grid display AND the forms_by_lang merge (generator can't sample 'West Ham'). Historical stages untouched. Real-lexicon probe: ~31% of modern stages cleaned. Review (4 agents + Gemini): caught the fantasy_export consistency gap + whitespace robustness. 10 tests + 575 regression green. Ships on re-emit with rogd.9/.15.

title: Key morphemes by stable id; connective form references it (retire _resolve_surface string-derivation)
description: Root data-model issue (user, 2026-06-03): the connective/surface form IS the morpheme key. proportions_usage stores only usage_key (a string like -ing-); proportions_structure is positional only ({location:pre/post}); the meaning table is PRIMARY KEY usage_key (the connective string). The runtime re-derives the morpheme by dash-stripping the connective string and matching it back into meaning_db (_resolve_surface). Consequences: (1) one morpheme is fragmented across connective-form rows — ing has THREE rows (-ing-, -ing, Ing-); (2) eras/spellings of the same word are separate morphemes (stan vs stone never link); (3) era_reflexes are owned per-string-row, so coverage is whatever surface-variant happened to catch them (Stan- has reflexes, no ing row does). FIX: introduce a morpheme entity keyed by a stable id (etymon/game_id); the connective form (proportions usage) carries a direct morpheme_id used purely for weighted sampling + placement; runtime follows usage→morpheme_id→record. Retire the dash-strip string match. Touches: proportions builder, L4 export schema (meaning keyed by id; proportions_usage gains morpheme_id), runtime resolver, migration/back-link of existing usage strings→ids. Position stays a pure OUTPUT (never a match key) — see morpheme-position-is-derived memory.
design:
PLAN (grounded; full detail in session 2026-06-03).

KEY UNLOCK: the morpheme entity already exists implicitly — bundle/_export.py rolls etymons to a family root_id (merged_into_id→lemma_id→self) and the export ALREADY sorts by the stable tuple (root_canonical_form, root_language) because root_id is autoincrement/unstable. But root_id is dropped in _subject.py before reaching the word. Surface a content-addressed id from that tuple.

STABLE ID: morpheme_id = 'm:' + sha1(f'{root_language}\x1f{root_canonical_form}')[:16]. Deterministic + JSONL-rebuildable (root identity is sourced; the rollup incl. collapse ledger replay is deterministic build logic). NOT the autoincrement etymon.id.

SCHEMA (L4, bump SCHEMA_VERSION/_EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 2→3):
- NEW morpheme(morpheme_id PK, root_language, root_canonical_form, primary_language, stratum, data BLOB= merged family entries/era_reflexes/IPA/vectors). idx on primary_language.
- meaning keeps usage_key PK (back-compat thru Phase 2) + nullable morpheme_id col.
- proportions_usage / proportions_single_usage gain morpheme_id col (per-row → disambiguates homographs; NULL only for un-mappable drift).
- No separate surface→morpheme table (morpheme_id rides each proportions row).

PHASES (each lands behind tests, parity-gated):
0. Parity harness (test-only): fixed seeds × 5 cultures → (gen,params,seed)→output + col-3 era-grid sample, anchored on --dev seed-runtime.db. Oracle for every later phase.
1. Compute+emit morpheme_id alongside string key, DORMANT. Carry root_language/root_canonical_form onto each word in _subject.py; morpheme_id_for() helper; runtime_db_export.py emits morpheme table (merging the family's connective rows = the unfragmenting) + morpheme_id cols on meaning + proportions; proportions_builder emits usage→morpheme_id map. Runtime still uses _resolve_surface (col unread). Checkpoint: generation byte-identical; --dev seed re-snapshot diff = only the additive col/table.
2. Runtime FOLLOWS the id. Adapter reads morpheme table; _resolve_morpheme(morpheme_db, id); route the 4 era-grid call sites + _era_grid (proportions.py ~1992/2189/2286/2401→2337/2427) to resolve usage.morpheme_id → merged record. Keep _resolve_surface as NULL-fallback (logged). ALSO route realism_reference.py:124 + kenning_rewind.py:287 (other _resolve_surface consumers) or they re-fragment. Position stays output-only (load_parts keeps bucketing by _location_from_form; sampling/keep/tag still gate by bare surface — correct). Checkpoint: names byte-identical; era-grid coverage INCREASES (intended delta — -ing-/-ing/Ing- now share one grid, ton links tūn lineage).
3. Retire string-derivation. Assert every proportions row has non-NULL morpheme_id at export (fail-loud); delete _resolve_surface/_surface_index_for/_clear_surface_index_cache + wiring in kenning/__init__.py. meaning table stays (matcher keys by modern_usage) — only era-grid morpheme resolution stops using it. Checkpoint: suite green; grep 0 _resolve_surface.

SPA COMPAT: rogd.7 cell ids f'{lang}:{index}' + _cellId derive from the resolved record's era_reflexes ordering → indices change in Phase 2. schema bump forces bundle re-download; pre-v3 col-3 swap share-links NOT forward-compatible (generated names from saved seeds unaffected — Phase 2 is byte-stable). Producer: _era_stage proportions.py:797.

ROGD.9/.11 SEAM: this ticket changes KEYING ONLY, not reflex content. rogd.9 (walk lineage UP from leaf for span) + rogd.11 (filter derivation-vs-inheritance pollution) hook into Phase-2's merged record as _era_grid input — kept OUT of this PR.

RISKS: (1) id stability — derived from the tuple export already trusts; collapse-ledger root moves carry the id with the morpheme; build-time assert on 16-hex prefix collision. (2) noisy edge_type — out of scope here. (3) homograph mis-merge — per-root id keeps senses distinct; ambiguous usage→morpheme recorded deterministically + logged. (4) seed contract — Phase-2 byte-identical-output gate.

CRITICAL FILES: bundle/_subject.py, lexicon/runtime_db_export.py, data/runtime.sql, runtime/proportions.py, runtime/runtime_db_adapter.py (+ runtime/meaning.py load_meanings, realism_reference.py, generators/kenning_rewind.py).
notes: PHASE 2 NOW ACTIVE IN THE BUNDLE (col-3 rebuild merged #475, 2026-06-04). The committed seed-runtime.db was re-emitted from the lexicon (which has the 57 rogd.15 reflex edges applied) with rogd.9/.11/.16 merged → meaning rows now carry morpheme_id, the runtime's _resolve_morpheme follows it, green grid restored 1→40, pollution removed, ~8 reflexes folded. So Phase 2's coverage effect is live + verified (full suite 4853 green). Phase 3 is now UNBLOCKED but its scope needs the rogd.16-era correction (see earlier note): the literal 'delete _resolve_surface' conflicts with it being the generation matcher; the REAL Phase 3 = remove the era-grid 'or first' string-derivation fallback + a non-NULL morpheme_id guard (note: morpheme_id lives on MEANING rows not proportions rows, and some meanings are legitimately un-attributable/NULL like -'s, so the guard must tolerate those). Backup lexicon at ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db.bak-prerebuild-* (3.3G, removable).
close_reason: Merged #476 — all phases complete. Phase 0: parity harness. Phase 1: morpheme entity + content-addressed morpheme_id (emitted dormant). Phase 2: runtime resolves the era-grid via morpheme_id (_resolve_morpheme merges the family's connective rows). Phase 3: era-grid made morpheme_id-authoritative — dropped the dash-strip string-derivation fallback ('or first'); a surface with no morpheme_id (un-attributable) gets no grid. RE-SCOPED the literal 'delete _resolve_surface / grep 0': _resolve_surface is the load-bearing generation MATCHER (usage→meaning/tags/siblings/location across proportions + realism_reference + kenning_rewind) and STAYS — only the era-grid stopped using string-derivation, matching the design's own 'meaning table stays, matcher keys by modern_usage'. Activated by the col-3 rebuild (#475) which put morpheme_ids in the bundle. Reviews: generator-contract + code-reviewer (PASS/approve) + Gemini. 4854 suite green.

title: Audit in-use morphemes with no era-grid + source their era-span (rebuildably)
description: Defect ff022ea4 (-ing-, -ton): in-use morphemes show an EMPTY era-grid because their era_reflexes bag is empty (ing/ton/ham), while others (stan) render. The model ALLOWS a morpheme to span eras — but we must NOT inject a synthetic self-anchor cell at runtime: everything is rebuildable from sourced data and a morpheme's era-span must be SOURCED, not fabricated. So the work is: (a) audit which morphemes that are actually IN USE (appear in generated names) have no grid — usage-weighted so high-frequency gaps surface first; (b) determine how to SOURCE their ability to span eras (which tier/source — cluster/descent/period-form/phonology-rule, attestations, etymonline/wiktextract mining) and why ing/ton got nothing. Supersedes the earlier runtime self-anchor idea (rejected: unsourced + not the rebuildable model).
notes: IMPLEMENTED + simulation-validated. _build_family_rollup now walks 'collapse'-sourced inheritance edges (rogd.15 reflex-links) to the oldest ancestor → reflex joins ancestor's family → inherits era_reflexes. KEY FINDING: following the raw 709K Wiktionary inheritance edges over-merges catastrophically (largest family 14→1174, ~440K families collapse, 20% of roots change) → MUST scope to curated collapse-source only. Simulation w/ the 57 ledger links against the live 3.3G lexicon: exactly 57 controlled family merges, 0 unresolvable, spot-checks pass (bishop→biscop, acres→acres, hoyle→ME hole). 6 unit tests + 572 regression green. PR open on kenning/rogd9-rollup (incl Phase 2 cherry-pick). REMAINING: full bundle parity (names byte-identical + grids grow) runs on rebuild-from-jsonl, which applies the 57 edges → rogd.9 follows them; that's the deploy gate.
close_reason: Merged #470. _build_family_rollup now follows curated 'collapse'-sourced reflex-link inheritance edges to the oldest ancestor → a later-era reflex joins its ancestor's family + inherits era_reflexes (empty-grid fix). Scoped to collapse-source ONLY (following raw 709K Wiktionary inheritance over-merges: largest family 14→1174). Review (6 agents + Gemini, 2 rounds) caught + fixed a CRITICAL double-emission bug (consensus branch now routes through root_of so a reflex that is its own consensus lemma promotes its ancestor's root, not standalone+folded → preserves byte-identity), lemma-key asymmetry, content-key tie-break, SQLite 999-param chunking. 9 rollup tests + 594 regression green. Simulation w/ the 57 ledger links: 57 controlled merges, spot-checks pass. Bundles rogd.10 Phase 2 (runtime era-grid via morpheme id). Empty grids fill on rebuild-from-jsonl (applies the 57 edges → rollup follows them).

title: Variant highlight collides — needs a stable cell id, not surface-fold matching
description: User defect 2026-06-03: clicking one variant highlights TWO cells/words. Cause: isCurrent/cellForSurface match by accentFold(surface) — accent+dash+now-also-* folded — so two cells that fold to the same key (e.g. 'stān' vs 'stan', or '*ur' vs 'ur' after wyrd-rogd.6's *-strip) BOTH highlight, and a repeated morpheme surface across positions collides too. FIX (user-requested): give each era_grid cell a STABLE id (backend: e.g. family:language:index, emitted on the cell), record the SELECTED cell's id on swap (pipeline/_cell), and drive the highlight (isCurrent) by id equality — not surface re-matching. Removes the fold-collision double-highlight + the homograph ambiguity zw1f deferred. cellForSurface stays for the no-swap initial highlight (best-effort) but the post-swap current is the recorded id.
close_reason: Merged #467. rogd.7: each era_grid cell carries a stable lang:index id (backend _era_stage); swaps record the chosen cell on morpheme._cellId, grid highlights by id (cellForSurface honours the id pin, fold fallback only for the initial state) — fixes defect f0a1e5c7 (bǣre/bære double-highlight), verified on a live græs/græs collision (one cell lights). Closes the dup-form unreachability generator-contract flagged on #466. rogd.8: name cards pinned, only .morphemes scrolls (scoped flex). Review: Gemini 3 rounds + frontend-logic/generator-contract/test-coverage agents, all clean (one Gemini era.js guard held as a verified false-positive). 14 py + 72 vitest pass.

title: Strip reconstructed-form '*' markers from era-grid surfaces (leaking into names)
description: Regression (user 2026-06-03): the '*' scholarly reconstructed/unattested-form marker is rendering in col 3 again — era_grid cells show forms like '*ur'/'*bearwe' (35 cells/60 rolls; NOT just phonology-rule — many are source=cluster reconstructed canonical_forms), and swapping grafts the '*' into the active name ('Tray*bearwe'). rendered surfaces are already clean (0 with '*', stripped by the era-render path wyrd-q1np), so the leak is the NEW era-grid (zw1f/qc0g). FIX (frontend, works on existing payload — no re-emit): strip '*' in accents.js graftPosition (covers grid cell display via withPlacement AND the swap target) + accentFold (so '*ur' matches 'ur' for highlight/pron). Add tests.
close_reason: Merged #466. Strip '*' reconstructed marker: backend _era_form_cell emits clean form + resolves pron via the original starred key + strips '*' from reader/ipa; frontend graftPosition/accentFold strip '*'. Verified 0 starred fields/80 rolls + clean names on swap. Gemini 3 rounds + 3 agents.

title: Reconcile lexicon drift before re-emitting a gloss seed (blocks rogd.1)
description: The committed seed-runtime.db (769 meanings, last built at PR #424) and the current ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db are out of sync: a fresh canonical 'export-runtime-db --dev' from the local lexicon yields only 659 meanings — overlap 643, DROPS 126, adds 16. The 126 dropped are concentrated in celtic_mix (58), modern_english (26), old_english (21), None (10), old_scandinavian (6), old_french (4), akkadian (1); the 16 added are celtic_mix (9), None (6), old_english (1). So the local lexicon is NOT the state the committed seed came from — it appears to have lost a chunk of Celtic (and some English/Norse/French) mining data since #424. ACTION: investigate where the Celtic+English corpus went (lexicon rebuilt/pruned? mining data lost? a richer pre-#424 lexicon?) and restore/rebuild the canonical lexicon so a re-emit ADDS gloss without dropping the 126 meanings. Only THEN re-emit the seed with gloss (wyrd-rogd.1's code, already verified working: 2050 gloss entries on a --dev build). User decision 2026-06-03: hold rogd.1, reconcile the lexicon first.
close_reason: Investigated per user hypothesis: NOT data loss. All 12 sampled dropped forms exist in the lexicon (dal 25 etymon rows, der 21, eg 17, all 20, ...). The 769->659 meaning drop is the dev-seed top-N-per-culture SAMPLE shift + proportions<->bundle drift (the van9 'usage has no Meaning, skipping' lines), not lost mining data. The committed seed is a capped dev/CI fixture; prod uses the full S3 runtime DB. User decided 2026-06-03 to proceed with the re-snapshot. The structure-prune (#420) only drops structures, not meanings. Residual minor signal (proportions reference some missing usages) is benign — re-emit rebuilds proportions inline.

title: Re-enable Rewind in prod once the new col-3 renderer lands
description: Part of the col-3 redesign (wyrd-rogd). Rewind is currently flagged OFF in prod (wyrd-nwpa) due to era-rendering bugs. The fresh, placement-consistent renderer + carried-over strip logic should resolve the visible bugs.
