Verify the runic-glyph + asterisk strip applies in the new view and that a shared/saved workspace carrying a rewind step renders correctly in prod.

title: Frontend Section 2: time-warp button bar
description: Section 2 of the col-3 redesign (wyrd-rogd). A button bar, one per era-STAGE (the distinct-language-stage granularity from wyrd-lftl: e.g. Old English / Middle English / Modern for English -- same set the grid columns use, matching what rewind already exposes: oe-late, me, modern). Pressing a stage moves EVERY morpheme to that era or the closest it can. Backed by the existing /api/kenning-rewind endpoint as a SINGLE rewind step in the pipeline (manage at most one rewind step; pressing another stage updates it; pressing the active one clears it). Closest-it-can fallback is already in rewind. Carry over rewind.js existing strip logic for runic glyphs + asterisk reconstructed-form markers in the new renderer. Time-warp sets the global era floor; per-slot grid swaps (Section 3) win over it, which is what produces a Mixed badge in Section 1. Do NOT render the transform-stack palette UI.
notes: DECISION (user 2026-06-02): option (b) — BOTH the time-warp/display selector AND the generation-side era filter compress to the same family_stage_order stage set. The oe-early/oe-late distinction is useful but not leveraged in this UI. Generation-filter compression is tracked separately in wyrd-rogd.2 (Configure column, not col 3).
close_reason: PR #700 merged. Built Section 2 of the col-3 redesign — the time-warp button bar. One button per era stage (oe-late/me/modern, derived from rewindTransform.paramSchema.era.options so bar+transform can't drift; first-class 'short' labels). Pressing a stage = a SINGLE rewind step held at the FRONT of the pipeline (pipeline.setRewind: add / switch-era-in-place / clear-on-active; rewindEra getter for the active highlight) so it's the global era floor; per-slot grid swaps layer on top + win (swap.js's documented Rewind-before-Swap order) → existing eraBadge shows 'Mixed (…)'. Flag-gated behind 'rewind' (prod hides it until wyrd-k2gn re-enables Rewind). Strip logic already lives in rewind.apply; NOT the transform-stack palette. 2 review rounds (30→ self-filtered; addressed front-positioning↔swap composition with a run() compose test pinning swap-wins + loud-drop, #makeStep factory, first-class short field, strengthened DOM/aria-pressed tests). Full SPA suite 183 passed; svelte-check clean.

title: Frontend Section 3: per-morpheme family x era variant grid
description: Section 3 of the col-3 redesign (wyrd-rogd). One block per morpheme (in word order), each: the morpheme as used in the active card (placement dashes intact), gloss (as currently divided into sense groups), tags, then the VARIANT GRID. Grid = era-stages across the top; one subsection per language family (English, Norse, Celtic, ...); HIDE families with no values. A variant form can span 1-n stage columns (a form tagged old-english spans its stages). The current variant -- exactly as rendered in the active name card -- is highlighted; when the generated surface matches no cell, highlight the nearest / pin it as an extra. Click a cell to swap that morpheme in the active card: graft the slot placement (graftPosition), adopt the cell pronunciation EXACTLY, and update the gloss (drift). Each cell shows form + reader-pronunciation + IPA below it. Surface drift: when a cell gloss differs from the morpheme base gloss, mark it (hover gloss / diff marker) so a meaning shift is visible, not silent. Data from wyrd-lftl. Mark or optionally hide phonology-rule-inferred cells (source field).
notes: DECISION (user 2026-06-02): reshape the grid to ERA-COLUMNS — per-family subsection, that family's era stages as aligned columns across the top (English: OE/ME/Modern; Norse: Old Norse; Brythonic: OW/MW/Welsh — each family has its own column set since stage sets differ), form cells stacked under each stage column. Replaces the current flex-block layout from the qc0g skeleton. Also in zw1f scope: mark inferred (phonology-rule:v1 source) cells distinctly; exact current-cell/homograph tracking. Drift-gloss display stays BLOCKED on wyrd-rogd.1 (per-reflex gloss needs the bundle re-emit) — do the layout + inferred-marking + homograph now, wire drift-gloss when rogd.1 lands.
close_reason: Merged in #462. Era-column grid layout (per-family aligned stage columns), inferred (phonology-rule) cell marking, exact homograph tracking via pinned _lang. Drift-gloss deferred to rogd.1. 3-round review loop (Gemini+agents) resolved; 53 vitest pass, CI green.

title: Frontend Section 1: active + paragon name cards
description: Section 1 of the col-3 redesign (wyrd-rogd). Two cards. ACTIVE card (left), report-defective top-right: line 1 = name as generated, with era badge (as generated / the generator target era; if morphemes are at mixed eras after warping/swapping, show Mixed + list); line 2 = the SAME variants de-accented into plain English orthography (by not by-macron) so the active name is always copy-pasteable -- derive from the curated translit/english_shaped rendering when present, else accent-fold client-side (no new data); then the breakdown rows: each morpheme surface WITH placement dashes / reader-pronunciation / IPA / gloss. PARAGON card (right, dimmed): the same layout but pinned to the true-modern forms (each morpheme modern reflex, from wyrd-lftl) -- the simplest no-variant version. The active-card gloss row tracks the CURRENTLY SELECTED variant (so a drifted cognate swapped in via the grid shows its drifted meaning, not the base gloss).
close_reason: Merged in #463. Mixed-era badge over the working state (eraBadge in lib/era.js, unit-tested) — tracks per-morpheme grid swaps: as-generated / single-era / Mixed(...). True-modern paragon + drift-gloss remain gated on rogd.1. 2-round review (Gemini+agents) resolved, 60 vitest pass, CI green.

title: Frontend: rebuild col-3 view skeleton + delete the wrong-axis cruft
description: Greenfield the col-3 view for the redesign (wyrd-rogd). Build a new InspectorColumn that reads the family x era grid payload (wyrd-lftl) and drives the EXISTING pipeline engine (swap + single rewind step) -- keep save/share snapshot format untouched. DELETE: MorphemeCard.svelte (728 lines, built on the per-language renderings axis -- orderedSourceEntries dedup/rich/priority, the six synthetic-original-row flags, LANG_PRIORITY); the original-vs-displayState dual source of truth + the lossless accent gamble + duplicate stripDash helpers in InspectorColumn; variants.js language-axis resolution (activeRendering/pronunciationFor). KEEP: rewind API client, graftPosition/accentFold (accents.js), NameGuideCard/MorphemeBreakdown as row primitives. Centralize PLACEMENT: bare / pre- / -inner- / -post is a per-SLOT property derived once from the generated surface dash pattern, shown on EVERY breakdown (active rows, modern-of-variant line, paragon rows, grid cells), never stripped -- reverse the current strip-on-display behavior. This skeleton ticket lands the new component + state plumbing; sections 1-3 build on top.
notes: PR #461 up. Skeleton: new InspectorColumn on era_grid axis + MorphemeGrid + lib/era.js; deleted MorphemeCard(728L)+MorphemeBreakdown; NameGuideCard altName; languageLabels hyphen tags. Verified svelte-check/vite/vitest green + rodney swap interaction. variants.js kept as pronunciation fallback (full removal -> zw1f).
close_reason: Merged in #461. New InspectorColumn on the era_grid axis + MorphemeGrid + lib/era.js; deleted MorphemeCard(728L)+MorphemeBreakdown; placement consistent; pipeline/save-share preserved. 5-round review loop (Gemini+agents) resolved, 52 vitest pass, CI green.

title: Backend: ship per-morpheme family x era reflex grid in the API payload
description: Extend components()/to_dict in runtime/proportions.py to emit, per morpheme, the family x era reflex grid that the col-3 redesign (wyrd-rogd) renders. Shape per morpheme: a list of family sections (english, norse, brythonic, goidelic, latin, norman-french -- via LANGUAGE_TO_FAMILY), each with ordered era-stages, each stage carrying a list of {form, reader_pronunciation, ipa, gloss, source}. CRITICAL: stages are the DISTINCT canonical language tags per family, NOT raw era cells -- collapse cells that share a canonical tag (english oe-early+oe-late both map to old-english; early-modern+modern both map to modern-english), so the grid does not render duplicate columns. Source data: Meaning.era_reflexes + etymon_era_reflexes (era_reflex.py). Per-reflex gloss: join the reflex etymon meanings (era_reflexes today carries form+language+source only -- add gloss). Per-cell pronunciation: reuse the _era_pronunciation path (rich IPA where the bundle has it, rule respelling else; reader always, IPA sparse). This one payload powers all three sections AND the true-modern paragon. Mark phonology-rule-derived reflexes via the existing source field so the frontend can mark/hide inferred cells.
notes: SCOPE (verified against bundle build path): ships form + reader_pronunciation + ipa + source per cell ONLY, read from the runtime Meaning.era_reflexes (already in the deployed bundle/runtime DB as word[era_reflexes] = {target_language: [{form, source}]}). NO bundle re-emit needed. Per-reflex GLOSS is NOT in the runtime data (the build emits form+source only) and is scoped OUT to wyrd-<gloss>. So the interim grid swaps form+pronunciation but the active-card gloss stays the morpheme base gloss until the gloss ticket lands.
close_reason: Merged in #460. Per-morpheme era_grid (family→stages→forms+pron+source) shipped in to_dict + components; verified on seed DB (153 morphemes/80 rolls); 8-agent review clean.

title: Redesign Inspect & Transform (col 3): family x era grid + fresh view rebuild
description: Rebuild the SPA col-3 Inspect and Transform view on the family x era axis the backend actually models (era/cells.py), replacing the per-language renderings axis the current UI bends to fake eras. Keep the pipeline engine (swap + rewind steps) and the save/share snapshot format (generator, params, original, pipeline[]) untouched -- the bugs live in the view, not the engine. Three sections: (1) name cards -- active as-generated card + de-accented modern-of-variant line + placement-consistent breakdown, beside a true-modern paragon card; (2) time-warp button bar backed by /api/kenning-rewind; (3) per-morpheme family x era variant grid with click-to-swap that adopts the cell pronunciation AND gloss. Drops ~400 lines of wrong-axis MorphemeCard machinery and the original-vs-displayState dual source of truth. Rewind gets re-enabled in prod as part of this.

title: Era render: two side-by-side name+guide cards (era + dimmed modern) in inspect; drop modern tag from output
description: Per operator: the inspect/transform breakdown should be TWO instances of one reusable name+guide card — (1) the generated era name + its guide (era forms/pronunciation/gloss), (2) the MODERN name (morphemes composed in modern form) + its guide, with the name DIMMED + a 'modern' indicator. Detailed MorphemeCards + Transforms stay below. OUTPUT column: remove the '(Modern: X)' tag (revert the modern-stuff there). Replaces the per-morpheme era/modern pairs (wyrd-mf2u) + the header guide (wyrd-8gal) with the cleaner two-card model. Needs: a reusable NameGuideCard (name + per-morpheme surface/pronunciation/gloss, dim+label props), compose the modern name on the SPA from morpheme usages, render once (no era) or twice (era).
close_reason: Merged PR #456. Inspector era breakdown is now two instances of a reusable NameGuideCard: the generated era name + its guide, beside the modern name (composed via renderName) + its guide (dimmed name + 'modern' label). Non-era → single card. OutputColumn (Modern:) tag removed (era surface only). Detailed MorphemeCards + Transforms unchanged below. Reviewed (SPA: no P1/P2; head-top right-align P3 fixed); svelte-check 0/0, build, vitest green.

title: Era render: inspector breakdown line + pronunciation guide still show modern (not era)
description: Follow-up to wyrd-mf2u. The MorphemeCards + OutputColumn show era+modern, but the InspectorColumn HEADER — the '·'-joined breakdown line + the prominent pronunciation guide right under the name — still map m.usage (modern), so for an era name they show the modern morphemes + modern pronunciation, inconsistent with the era name above + the era+modern cards below. Make both era-aware: breakdown line uses the era form (m.rendered||m.usage) matching the name; the guide shows the era surface + era pronunciation (m.rendered_pron) + a compact modern annotation. Found via rodney+PDF on staging build 1e60179.
close_reason: Merged PR #455. The InspectorColumn header (the breakdown line + the prominent pronunciation guide under the name) now uses the era form (m.rendered) + the era pronunciation (m.rendered_pron) with a compact 'modern <usage>' annotation, matching the era name + the era+modern cards/output. hasPronunciation counts era pronunciation. Reviewed (SPA: no P1/P2); svelte-check + build + vitest green.

title: Era render: show era + modern morpheme breakdown (bridge in inspect/transform, '(Modern)' tag in output)
description:
Bug + feature surfaced from era-driven rendering (wyrd-6c8x). The rendered NAME is the era form but the per-morpheme breakdown shows the MODERN morpheme — they don't match. Root: NewName.components()/description() resolve usage+glosses from the original modern usage 'e', ignoring self.rendered (the era forms); only __str__ honors the era render. to_dict() is inconsistent (usage=era, gloss=modern).

FIX + FEATURE (user-specced): don't replace modern with era — show BOTH (modern is the stable gloss/pronunciation anchor; era reflexes are cluster-cognates with fuzzy standalone glosses).
- INSPECT + TRANSFORM: full bridge (option C) — the era form broken down (surface + era pronunciation) AND the modern equivalent broken down (surface + modern pronunciation + gloss).
- OUTPUT: the era breakdown with a compact '(Modern)' annotation beside each morpheme.

DATA: era pronunciation via Meaning.respelling_for(era_form, target_language) + the per-language renderings map (the rewind feature already surfaces era pronunciations). MorphemeCard already renders 'usage -> rendered' when they differ (built for D18/D8) — generalize to a unified anchor(modern)->overlay(rendered) model so era + D18 spelling-variant + D8 inflection render consistently (don't regress D18/D8). Backend: components()/to_dict() must emit usage=modern-anchor + rendered=era-form + both pronunciations.
close_reason: Merged PR #454. Era-rendered breakdown now matches the era name: to_dict + components emit usage(modern anchor) + rendered(era form) + rendered_language + rendered_pron (era form's OWN pronunciation — rich IPA from the bundle's per-form renderings, respell fallback; components() previously dropped rendered entirely). SPA: new reusable MorphemeBreakdown.svelte (form + pronunciation + role/language chip); MorphemeCard renders era+modern as a side-by-side pair (inspect/transform), non-era cards + swap/variants unchanged; OutputColumn shows era surface + compact (Modern: <usage>) tag. Verified the 'Westerraulsfara' report was a DISPLAY issue not mis-decomposition (era forms always concatenate to the name, 0/40). Reviewed (SPA-correctness + backend agents: no P1; a11y P2 + brittle-test P3 fixed); svelte-check + build + vitest + 20 era tests + kenning suite green.

title: Cleanup: delete the dead proportions SCORING internals + transitional tests (after the scoring_mode interface removal)
description:
Follow-up to the wyrd-rt2m interface removal (PR removing the scoring_mode schema field + --scoring-mode CLI flag; generate() defaults to vector but still dispatches the internal proportions branch). Now DELETE the user-unreachable proportions scoring path + its tests:

CODE (per the wyrd-ej28 scoping map): NameGenerator.{select,_select_no_tag,_select_tags,_select_tag,_cohesion_boost,_raw_class_score}; MeaningGenerator.select; Generator's scoring methods (keep add_item/elements as a data container); blend helpers (_blend_uniform/_blend_harsh/_harshness_score); _bucket_keys_matching_surface; the orphaned keep_keys_for_era/stratum (vector filters via the request-vector gate, not these); the generate() else-branch + the scoring_mode param read. KEEP the data layer: load_proportions, MeaningGenerator data/buckets, structs, usage_frequency_by_bucket, tag_cooccurrence, weighted_choice, NewName, select_via_vector, keep_keys_for_gloss (used by the realism reference).

GATE: remove the RELATIVE realism gate (run_drift_samples / compute_drift_report / the relative ToleranceBand / test_kenning_realism_regression), leaving the absolute gate (wyrd-jfaz / test_kenning_realism_absolute).

TESTS: delete/rewrite the proportions-path tests — test_kenning_cj6f_welsh_proportions; the 7 distribution-shift tests SKIPPED during the interface removal (test_kenning.py::{test_high_novelty_shifts_distribution, test_mood_grim_shifts_distribution_across_seeds, test_mood_tag_presets_shift_distribution_across_seeds, test_mood_tag_presets_are_distinct_from_grim, test_mood_harsh_graduated_differs_from_full, test_explicit_harshness_overrides_lower_mood_value} + test_kenning_proportions.py::test_kenning_generate_cohesion_one_shifts_distribution_against_seeds) — these exercise proportions-only knobs (novelty=D17; mood/harshness=D6) that are inert/weak under vector. DECIDE whether novelty/harshness/mood should be wired into vector scoring or removed from the input_schema (they're currently inert no-ops under vector — misleading to expose). Collapse WYRD_FF_SCORING_MODE (axis-weights always on). Remove the stale '--scoring-mode' mentions in other CLI option help text + the priors_path/scoring_weights schema descriptions.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
Per-test disposition for the 9 SKIPPED distribution tests (from wyrd-3bhp investigation, now folded here). Delete these atomically with the proportions scoring-internals deletion this ticket owns — they currently guard the still-present, user-unreachable proportions path, and their assertions are stale under vector.

TERMINATE (8) — the vector path is already wired AND tested, so these proportions versions are redundant:
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_high_novelty_shifts_distribution ... see novelty note below (this is the ONE exception)
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_mood_grim_shifts_distribution_across_seeds  [mood]
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_mood_tag_presets_shift_distribution_across_seeds  [mood, parametrized x3]
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_mood_tag_presets_are_distinct_from_grim  [mood]
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_mood_harsh_graduated_differs_from_full  [mood/harshness]
- tests/test_kenning.py::test_explicit_harshness_overrides_lower_mood_value  [harshness/mood]
- tests/test_kenning_proportions.py::test_kenning_generate_cohesion_one_shifts_distribution_against_seeds  [cohesion]
  Vector equivalents that already cover these: test_kenning.py::test_harshness_shifts_vector_distribution_end_to_end (harshness); test_kenning_vector_kenning_adapter.py::{test_build_request_vector_mood_skips_uniform_default, test_build_request_vector_with_mood_expansion} + test_kenning_vector_name_select.py::test_build_request_vector_tags_and_mood_tags_become_hard_gate (mood as hard-gate); the D17 cohesion adapter tests (cohesion).

DECISION NEEDED (1) — novelty: test_kenning.py::test_high_novelty_shifts_distribution.
novelty is STILL passed through the CLI (cli/generate.py:294 "novelty": novelty) but is NOT wired into the vector path at all (zero refs in vector_name_select.py / vectors/*) — a true inert no-op under vector. This is the "wire-vs-drop" decision this ticket already flags:
  - If novelty is DROPPED from the input_schema (recommended given it is inert + misleading to expose) -> TERMINATE this test too.
  - If novelty is WIRED into vector scoring -> PORT it (re-baseline against the vector distribution, like test_harshness_shifts_vector_distribution_end_to_end).

Net: 8 clean terminates + 1 gated on the novelty product call. No standalone test-only deletion was done (would desync from the code deletion + pre-empt the novelty decision).

title: Production runtime DB: publish full DB to prod S3 + grant Lambda s3:ListBucket (prod serves bundled subset)
description: Surfaced during the wyrd-lnt6 production cutover. Production now serves the BUNDLED seed-runtime.db (~2561 meanings, the committed dev subset) because: (1) the prod runtime_db S3 bucket (521studios-production-kenning-runtime) was just created EMPTY by the cutover apply (it never existed before — prod had been running an old zip), and (2) the prod Lambda role (wyrd-production-lambda) lacks s3:ListBucket on that bucket (CloudWatch: 'not authorized to perform s3:ListBucket'), so even a published DB wouldn't be readable. The bundled-seed fallback now works (PR #450 packaged the .db), so prod serves on the subset — fine while prod is not user-facing, but for launch prod needs the FULL dataset. TODO: (a) publish the full runtime DB to s3://521studios-production-kenning-runtime via bin/publish-runtime-db.sh (current.json + v/<ts>.db); (b) fix the runtime-db-read IAM policy (terraform/main.tf ~line 160) to grant s3:GetObject on the versioned keys + s3:ListBucket on the bucket so get_object returns 404 (not 403) on miss and reads succeed. Verify prod /api/kenning then serves from S3 (full 97k meanings) not the bundled subset.
close_reason: Done + verified. (1) Published the full runtime DB (/tmp/wyrd-runtime-full.db, 105MB, 97k meanings, source_lexicon_db=~/.wyrd/lexicon.db) to s3://521studios-production-kenning-runtime via bin/publish-runtime-db.sh → current.json points at v/2026-06-02T03-01Z.db. (2) Granted the prod Lambda role s3:ListBucket on the bucket (PR #451; GetObject/HeadObject already present). (3) Prod terraform apply granted the policy + redeployed the Lambda → cold start now reads the full DB from S3. VERIFIED: prod /api/kenning bundle_version = {built_at 2026-06-01T16:36:52Z, source_lexicon_db /home/devon/.wyrd/lexicon.db} — matches the published full DB, NOT the bundled subset (built_at 1970, DEV_SOURCE_LEXICON); manifest HTTP 200; no more AccessDenied/bundled-fallback log spam. Production now serves the full dataset on vector scoring.

title: Era-driven rendering at generation: render morphemes in their period form when an era is set (feature A)
description:
GOAL: when an era is set on generation (e.g. era=oe-early), render each morpheme in its era-appropriate ATTESTED form (Old-English spellings) instead of the modern canonical reflex — so era produces period-LOOKING names, not just a period-eligibility FILTER. Today era is inventory-filter-only: it narrows which morphemes are eligible (confirmed: oe-early output != no-filter) but always renders the modern canonical (confirmed via rewind — 'modern matches the original generated word'; user-reported). era_range only feeds keep_keys_for_era; it never reaches the surface render.

DATA — SATISFIED at runtime (no lexicon DB needed): the bundle ships per-language era-reflexes via Meaning.era_reflex_for(target_language) (wyrd-obpw). EFFECTIVE coverage among GENERATED morphemes is ~90% for OE/ME (measured: 146/161 generated morpheme-occurrences over 60 oe-early names; 60/60 names have >=1 period morpheme). (Coverage over ALL 97k meanings is only ~13% — generation picks common, well-attested morphemes, so the effective number is far higher.) So names will be substantially period-looking; ~10% of morphemes fall back to the modern canonical (acceptable; improvable via more reflex mining later).

MACHINERY — reuse the rewind path (kenning_rewind.py already does exactly this per era-stop): canonical_language_for_cell(family, cell) -> target language; Meaning.era_reflex_for(target_language) -> candidate period forms; render_form_particle_pairs for the join.

IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Thread the era CELL (family, cell), not just the year range, from the request to the render. _resolve_era_param returns the range (for filtering); add the (family, cell) alongside.
2. Add a post-pick era-render step (analogous to _render_substitutions, already shared by both modes after PR #435): given the picked Meanings + the era cell, pick each morpheme's era_reflex_for(target_language) form (deterministic/seeded; fall back to the canonical position-form when the reflex list is empty), set NewName.rendered (the same field D8/D18 uses, so __str__ already renders it). Apply _position_form-style position/case so the era form renders at its slot position.
3. Apply in BOTH select() (proportions) + select_via_vector.
4. Precedence: era-render supersedes the D18 spelling-variant (the era reflex IS the period spelling); D8 inflection not combined with era in v1 (follow-up). Determinism: seed-stable pick from the (form-sorted) reflex list.

CAVEATS: (a) ~10% mixed modern/period within a name (uncovered morphemes) — surface or accept; (b) verify the era reflex + eyjk position-form/case interaction renders cleanly.

TESTS: era=oe-early renders period forms for covered morphemes (vs modern for era=''); fallback for uncovered; deterministic; both modes. Surfaced by user during Phase-2 staging eval (era 'always rendering as modern').
close_reason: Merged PR #446. era-driven rendering at generation: when an era is set, each morpheme renders in its era-appropriate attested form (Meaning.era_reflex_for) instead of the modern canonical reflex, so era=oe-early produces period-LOOKING names (Tūn, Sūþ, Nethām / Toun, Marcat for me). _resolve_era_render_language resolves era+culture→historical language (parallel to the _resolve_era_param filter range); _contemporary_language_for_family suppresses era-render for present-day cells (modern/early-modern → canonical, no cognate distortion); proportions._render_era_forms/_era_form_for_meanings/_apply_render render in both scoring modes, preferring attested forms over reconstructed (*-marker). Default generation bit-stable. ~90% effective reflex coverage among generated morphemes. Reviewed (seed-reproducibility, test-coverage, error-handling, complexity, fixture-data, domain-correctness): no P1; 2 P2 test gaps fixed + verified closed; CI green. Follow-up wyrd-68ye (diversification can blank an era slot).

title: SPA: store owns param initialization (seed defaults up front, not per-Field)
description: Structural follow-up to wyrd-etvd. Today appState.ensureParams just creates an empty {} params bag; each field's default is seeded LAZILY per-component in Field.svelte's effect, racing the <select> bind (the etvd bug). Lift initialization into the store: ensureParams/initParams walks the selected generator's schema once (when manifest+generator+config are available, before Fields render) and seeds every non-hidden field via seedDefault (schema default + config.defaults override) — one authoritative init point. Then delete Field.svelte's seed effect (fields just bind already-seeded params); snap effects shrink to pure validity-correction. Makes the whole class of seed-vs-bind race impossible (every field, not just scoring_mode) + simplifies Field. Keeps the #442 $effect.pre fix working in the meantime.
close_reason: Merged PR #444. The store (appState.ensureParams) now owns field initialization: walks the manifest schema + backfills every missing non-hidden field via initialFieldValue (config override → schema default → type-empty) BEFORE Fields render, no-op until manifest loads, ConfigureColumn pre-effect tracks manifest. Field.svelte's per-field seed effect deleted. Makes the wyrd-etvd seed-vs-bind race impossible for every field (incl. legacy partial bookmarks via backfill). Reviewed (SPA-correctness, verified against Svelte 5 scheduler + the backfill defense): no P1/P2; svelte-check + 37 vitest green; CI green.

title: Kenning/SPA: dedup morpheme definitions + group them by sense-class (denu- shows ~50 near-dup glosses across 3 senses)
description: Morpheme definitions duplicate heavily and conflate distinct senses. Example 'denu-' lists ~50 glosses including many near-dups ('Hill, a hill, ... hill, hill ...') AND three clearly-distinct sense groups jammed together: (1) topographic — valley/dale/hollow/vale/dene/hill/down/dune/mountain/open-hill-country; (2) settlement — enclosure/farmstead/village/estate/manor/town/tun/township; (3) people — human being, people. Two asks: (a) DEDUP near-identical glosses (case/article-insensitive: 'Hill'=='a hill'=='hill'); (b) VISUALLY SEPARATE the sense groups — turn the flat definition into an ARRAY of definition-classes, grouped by tag (or root/etymon sense). Likely the glosses come from multiple ranked sibling Meanings (homograph bucket) being unioned flat (_all_senses / _split_senses_for_display); grouping by the contributing sibling/tag would separate them. Per user — 'this feels like a ness'.

title: SPA inspector: show each morpheme's basic definition up top (near the pronunciation guide)
description: The pronunciation guide sits at the top of Inspect & Transform, but the morpheme's basic DEFINITION (gloss) isn't shown up there — it's only buried in the cards. Surface a concise definition near the pronunciation so the user sees what each morpheme means at a glance. Per user.

title: SPA inspector: fold the per-language variants into a clear 'Variants' expander (signal they're click-to-switch)
description: The variants chunk (the per-source-language form rows in Inspect & Transform) is BIG and dominates the column. Fold it under a clear, easy-to-see title 'Variants' (a <details>/expander). It's currently not obvious to a user that you can CLICK a variant row to switch the morpheme's form/language — an expander with a clear title (and maybe a hint) makes that clearer. Collapsing by default also naturally shows more of the transform stack below. Per user.

title: Kenning generator: reject non-adjacent duplicate morphemes with no cross-language synonym by re-picking a different word (Park...Park)
description: Follow-up to wyrd-vd6y. The render-level synonym diversification handles repeats that HAVE a same-meaning cross-language form (Hill Hill → Hill Haeth). But surfaces like 'park'/'north'/'wood'/'burton' have NO cross-language form in the bundle (old_english only), so they can't be diversified by language — e.g. 'Park Burton Park Marshham'. Per user: reject the second occurrence and pick a DIFFERENT morpheme. Requires extending the generator's selection dedup (currently ADJACENT-only via prev_surface) to whole-name surface tracking + re-pick across all selection paths (_select_no_tag, prev_picked, vector). Broad-impact: shifts seed-stability + changes some existing generated names. Keep the render-level synonym (vd6y) as the preferred form of 'something else'; this ticket is the fallback re-pick when no synonym exists.

title: SPA snap-to-valid clobbers config.defaults for enum selects (scoring_mode stuck on Proportions)
description: ROOT CAUSE (corrected — NOT a caching issue; /api/manifest is uncached + serves the right config.defaults). In Field.svelte, an enum/select field has TWO $effects: a SEED effect (applies seedDefault → config.defaults env override, e.g. WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE=vector) and a SNAP-to-valid effect (snaps an out-of-enum value to prop.default). The snap ran while the value was still undefined (unseeded), writing prop.default ('proportions'); the seed effect's 'if value === undefined' guard then skipped, so the env override never applied. Net: with WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE=vector on staging, the Advanced menu stayed on Proportions. Same latent bug for the dependent-select (culture) path + WYRD_DEFAULT_CULTURE. FIX: extract a pure snapEnumValue(value, options, schemaDefault) that returns undefined for an unseeded value (leaving initial seeding to the seed pass) and only snaps a DEFINED-but-invalid value; use it in both snap effects. Surfaced during wyrd-lnt6 Phase 2 staging validation.
notes: REOPENED: the #440 snap-clobber fix was incomplete. Confirmed (user: Advanced went 15->14, so they're on the new bundle, yet scoring_mode still Proportions). The deeper root cause is Svelte's bind_select_value (node_modules/svelte/.../bindings/select.js): on mount with an undefined bound value it WRITES the first <option> ('proportions') back to the variable — and that runs before the user $effect seed (user effects run after render/binding effects), so the seed's '=== undefined' guard then skips the config.defaults (WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE=vector) override. Fix (PR pending): make the seed an $effect.pre so the value is defined BEFORE the <select> binds → the undefined-write-back never fires. The snapEnumValue fix stays (correct + complements). Also adds a build-SHA hover on the wordmark so future deploy-confirmation doesn't require bundle archaeology.
close_reason: Merged PR #442. Root cause (verified against Svelte 5.55.9 runtime source): bind_select_value writes the first <option> back to an undefined bound value on mount, and as an EFFECT-tier effect it ran in the same post-render tier as the (plain $effect) seed — losing the race, so the config.defaults override was skipped. Fix: seed is now $effect.PRE (RENDER_EFFECT tier, runs synchronously before the deferred bind), so scoring_mode is 'vector' before the <select> binds → the undefined-write-back never fires. Reviewer confirmed pre-beats-bind from the scheduler (effects.js/batch.js), not just docs — explains why the two prior $effect fixes failed. Plus a build-SHA hover on the wordmark for deploy confirmation. SPA svelte-check/build/30 tests green; CI green.

title: Phase 3: delete the proportions SCORING path (vector-only); keep the data layer
description: IRREVERSIBLE. After Phase 2's one-release escape hatch, delete the proportions scoring functions (per the wyrd-ej28 scoping map): NameGenerator.{select,_select_no_tag,_select_tags,_select_tag,_cohesion_boost,_raw_class_score}, MeaningGenerator.select, Generator's scoring methods (keep add_item/elements as a data container), the blend helpers (_blend_uniform/_blend_harsh/_harshness_score), _bucket_keys_matching_surface, the orphaned keep_keys_for_era/stratum. Collapse the scoring_mode param/enum + WYRD_FF_SCORING_MODE (axis-weights always on). Remove the RELATIVE realism gate (compute_drift_report path / run_drift_samples / the relative ToleranceBand / test_kenning_realism_regression) + the transition-only proportions cross-check in test_kenning_realism_absolute, leaving the absolute gate (wyrd-jfaz). KEEP the data layer: load_proportions, MeaningGenerator data/buckets, structs, usage_frequency_by_bucket, tag_cooccurrence, weighted_choice, NewName, select_via_vector. NOTE D8/D18 now live in vector too (wyrd-nbpw), so no feature loss.
close_reason: User-facing goal achieved via PR #453: the scoring_mode INTERFACE is removed (schema enum field + --scoring-mode CLI flag gone), generate() defaults to + only exposes vector — users can no longer select proportions. Per the user's split ('delete the interface, file a ticket for the cleanup'), the dead proportions SCORING internals (NameGenerator.select et al., the relative realism gate, WYRD_FF_SCORING_MODE collapse, the novelty/harshness/mood-under-vector decision, stale text/terraform) are deferred to wyrd-3dlx (now a child of the epic). Reviewed (2 agents: correctness — no orphaned refs/no runtime break; test-coverage — skips justified + accurate, e2e harshness coverage added); CI green, full suite 4774 passed on the committed bundle.

title: Phase 2: flip default scoring_mode proportions to vector (keep proportions opt-in one release)
description: DECISION-GRADE / operator-gated. Flip the default scoring mode from proportions to vector now that Phase 1 blockers are clear (epic wyrd-ej28): schema default (generators/kenning.py input_schema scoring_mode default), CLI --scoring-mode default (cli/generate.py), WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE. Keep proportions selectable (opt-in) for ONE release as an escape hatch before Phase 3 deletes it. Re-point the realism regression CI to the absolute gate (test_kenning_realism_absolute, wyrd-jfaz) as the primary; the relative gate can stay green during this release. Update the schema description that says 'Default proportions until ecjp.6/7 confirms parity' (parity confirmed: Phase 0 N=1000, all cultures in band). Validate on staging before flipping production env (WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE).
notes: Staging prep MERGED (PR #437): terraform sets WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE=vector on staging (local.vector_default_envs) → staging SPA defaults to vector for validation; production untouched (proportions). Schema default stays proportions (no test churn). REMAINING (the GO, operator): validate staging, then add 'production' to local.vector_default_envs in terraform/main.tf + run the production terraform apply. Ticket stays open until production is flipped.
close_reason: Production cutover COMPLETE + verified. terraform local.vector_default_envs now includes production (PR #448); removed the stale runtime_db import blocks that blocked the prod apply (PR #449); fixed the prod 500 the apply exposed — seed-runtime.db wasn't in package-data so the bundled-seed fallback FileNotFoundError'd (PR #450). Production apply succeeded; verified live: /api/manifest HTTP 200 with config.defaults.scoring_mode=vector, /api/kenning?era=oe-early → 200 'Cloppingtūn, By Heald, Feordby Heald' (vector default + era rendering both working in prod). Proportions stays opt-in for one release (schema default still proportions). Follow-up wyrd-ow4c: publish full DB to prod S3 + grant Lambda ListBucket (prod currently on the bundled subset DB). Phase 3 (wyrd-rt2m) deletes the proportions path next.

title: SPA: long Inspect column content produces nested/double scrollbars (outer container also scrolls)
description: When the Inspect & Transform column content gets tall enough to scroll, the OUTER container also gets a scrollbar — double scrollbars, bad UX. Classic flex/grid overflow issue (missing min-height:0 / overflow containment). The 3 columns should each scroll internally within a viewport-height-constrained layout; the outer container should not scroll. Fix in spa-next App/column layout CSS.

title: SPA swap: clicking an alternate form drops the morpheme's positional dashes (-hām → hamm)
description: Reported 'Cornelhām' (Cornel- -hām). Clicking another form for -hām (e.g. 'hamm') swaps usage to the BARE etymon form 'hamm', dropping the leading position dash, so the morpheme no longer renders as a suffix and the name/breakdown change wrong ('Cornel- hamm'). swapTo/setSwap sets usage = rendering.original_script || form (bare). Fix: graft the new surface into the ORIGINAL morpheme's leading/trailing dash markers ("-hām" → "-hamm"/"-hȳ"), the same dash-preservation accentedUsage already does. SPA inspector swap.

title: Kenning generator: same morpheme picked twice should force a different-language variant (Hill Hill → e.g. Table Mesa)
description: Reported 'Hill Hill' (seed 1979203092605867): the generator picked the SAME morpheme 'hill' for both slots. Per user (defect 89c404cf): do NOT forbid the repeat — instead, when the same morpheme/meaning is selected twice, FORCE the second occurrence to render as a DIFFERENT-LANGUAGE variant of that meaning (cf. 'Table Mesa' = English table + Spanish mesa for the same 'flat-topped hill'). Generator-side change in proportions selection/rendering. Supersedes the 'just forbid duplicates' idea (defect c6871c1a).

title: SPA rewind: rewound morphemes not clickable/swappable (e.g. ME 'West Saint Other')
description: Reported 'West Saint Other', rewind to middle english: can't click 'west' (and some other variants) to swap. Likely the rewound morphemes built in the count-mismatch/degraded path (wyrd-7cvv) carry no sources/renderings, so MorphemeCard renders no clickable form rows. Repro seed 1390730633886754 in defect f8e99b.
notes:
AUTONOMOUS-LOOP RE-INVESTIGATION 2026-06-21: the prior TRIAGE's recommended option-A regression test (assert a DEGRADED rewind morpheme renders clickable cells) rests on a FALSE premise. Probed MorphemeGrid.svelte directly: a degraded rewind morpheme — the {usage:surface}(+renderings) shape rewind.js's count-mismatch branch (wyrd-7cvv, ~line 130) builds, which carries NO era_grid — renders 0 clickable 'button.cell's (empty <div class=era-grid>); a morpheme WITH an era_grid renders a clickable cell. MorphemeGrid only renders cells from morpheme.era_grid[].stages[].forms; rewind.js builds no era_grid for rewound morphemes. So degraded morphemes are NOT clickable today, and a regression test can't assert they are. The REPRO ('West Saint Other') was fixed by the ALIGNMENT fix (#429/#426) keeping the cleanly-aligned morphemes' era_grid (→ clickable) — NOT by making degraded morphemes clickable. The clean/common swap path is already covered by MorphemeGrid.test.js:48-65.

DECISION NEEDED (Devon): (1) CLOSE as resolved — the repro + common path are fixed/covered; the degraded count-mismatch edge is rare and legitimately era_grid-less, accept it as non-clickable best-effort; OR (2) treat degraded-not-clickable as the real remaining bug and FIX it — synthesize a fallback clickable usage-cell in MorphemeGrid for ANY morpheme lacking an era_grid (so it's always swappable). Option 2 is an output-changing SPA-UI change that also affects genuine era-coverage-gap morphemes (they'd gain a clickable usage cell) — needs the call on whether that's desired. SKIPPED pending (1)/(2).

title: SPA rewind: morpheme lost on rewind (e.g. -ton in 'Werton West')
description: Reported 'Werton West' (wer- + -ton + west): rewinding LOSES -ton. PR #429 added dash-insensitive resolution in the generator path, but -ton still drops here. Investigate whether the era-render drops it (no era form for the picked etymon) vs a resolution miss vs the SPA alignment omitting it. Repro seed 4149675822097195 in defect 6815a7.

title: SPA rewind: reconstructed-form '*' marker leaks into rewound name
description: Reported 'Brekingford' (Bre-/CL hill + -king-/EN king + -ford). On rewind the rendered word shows '*' (the scholarly reconstructed/unattested proto-form marker) twice. The '*' is fine in a scholarly form list but ugly/confusing in a generated NAME. Decide: strip leading '*' from rewound surfaces in the name + cards, or render it deliberately. Repro seed in defect 9f6bd.

title: Re-anchor the realism gate to ABSOLUTE corpus bands (so validation survives proportions deletion)
description: The realism-retention gate (drift_runner.run_drift_samples + test_kenning_realism_regression) measures drift of VECTOR vs the PROPORTIONS baseline. Once the proportions scoring mode is deleted, that baseline is gone and the gate is meaningless. Before Phase 3 deletion, re-anchor the gate to absolute realism bands measured against the real-toponym corpus (tag/position/morpheme distributions of attested place-names), not relative-to-proportions. Also bump SAMPLES_PER_MODE 100->1000 (realism_tolerance.py:106 notes N=100 is noise-dominated). Blocker for parent epic wyrd-ej28.
close_reason: Merged PR #436. Realism gate re-anchored to ABSOLUTE corpus bands: realism_reference.compute_corpus_reference derives the corpus tag/position/morpheme distributions analytically from bundle data (structs + usage_frequency_by_bucket, gloss-filtered to match the generator) — survives the proportions-scoring deletion + tracks corpus growth. compute_realism_report + AbsoluteToleranceBand + the gate test (5 cultures N=1000) + a proportions cross-check (~0 for all cultures, the correctness proof). Relative gate kept for the transition; Phase 3 removes it. Reviewed: reference-correctness + test-coverage P2s (gloss filter, violation tests) fixed + verified; seed-repro/clarity/docstring clean; Gemini quota-blocked (agents covered). Full suite 4767.

title: Port D8 inflection + D18 spelling-variant rendering to the vector path (else feature loss on proportions retirement)
description: D8 inflection and D18 attested-spelling-variant rendering exist ONLY in the proportions select() path (_render_substitutions + _pick_surface, runtime/proportions.py:1283/1332). select_via_vector explicitly does NOT do D8/D18 (its docstring names this an out-of-scope follow-up). Retiring the proportions scoring mode would DROP these features from the runtime unless ported into the vector path first. Blocker for parent epic wyrd-ej28.
close_reason: Merged PR #435. D8 inflection + D18 spelling-variant rendering ported to vector mode: select_via_vector now threads spelling_variety/inflection_density and runs the SAME _render_substitutions the proportions path uses (resolves position-forms by bare surface, skips None slots), attaching rendered/inflection_labels. Bit-stable default (guarded; both knobs 0 → no extra rng draws → rendered None). Validated: D18 283/300, D8 210/300 fire on full bundle; both change output on the CI --dev bundle. Reviewed: generator-contract/seed-repro/clarity clean; test-coverage 2×P2 (threading + D18 variant) closed + verified; Gemini quota-blocked (agents covered). Full suite 4749+.

title: Vector empty-pick parity: never raise on an empty eligible pool (blocker for vector-only)
description: Vector mode raises ValueError('no eligible name') when a slot's gates (era/stratum/tag) eliminate all candidates (vector_name_select.py returns [] -> caller raises). Proportions never raises. As the ONLY mode this means some (params,seed) combos hard-fail. Add a parity fallback: retry on a relaxed gate, or guarantee a non-empty pick, matching the proportions graceful-degradation contract. Blocker for the proportions-scoring retirement (parent epic wyrd-ej28).
close_reason: Merged PR #434. Vector empty-pick parity: select_via_vector now degrades (drops unsatisfiable slots, matching proportions _select_no_tag) instead of returning None->raise; all-empty case returns None for an honest raise. Bit-stable (Phase 0 drift byte-identical), full suite 4746+. Reviewed: generator-contract/seed-repro/clarity clean; test-coverage P2+P3 closed + verified; Gemini quota-blocked (agent reviewers covered). Residual P3 (2 defensive permissive mirror-branches) filed as follow-up.

title: Retire the proportions scoring MODE (vector-only generation)
description:
Make vector the only/default scoring mode and delete the empirical proportions-SCORING code path. Distinct from wyrd-d90t (which migrates the DATA SOURCE: JSON files -> SQLite L4); this epic is the SCORING-mode axis.

KEY INSIGHT (scoping investigation 2026-06-01): production vector scoring is NOT pure-vector — it is empirical_frequency x normalized_vector_score. NameGenerator.select_via_vector reuses the SAME proportions DATA the legacy select() uses: self.structs (structure templates + empirical weights, sampled via weighted_choice) and self.usage_frequency_by_bucket (per-(position x flags) empirical {usage:proportion}, which BOTH gates position-eligibility — freq<=0 drops a morpheme — AND sets cross-usage pick-share). tag_cooccurrence (cohesion) is optional (off by default). So:

FORK:
(A) RECOMMENDED — retire the proportions SCORING PATH, KEEP the proportions DATA LAYER as vector's empirical backbone. Concretely: delete NameGenerator.{select,_select_no_tag,_select_tags,_select_tag,_cohesion_boost,_raw_class_score}, MeaningGenerator.select, Generator's scoring methods (select/has_tag/filter_for_tag/_apply_excludes — keep add_item/elements as a data container), the blend helpers (_blend_uniform/_blend_harsh/_harshness_score), _bucket_keys_matching_surface, and the now-orphaned keep_keys_for_era/stratum/_intersect_keep_keys. KEEP: load_proportions, MeaningGenerator load+bucket data, structs/_all_structs + struct filters, usage_frequency_by_bucket + its builder, tag_cooccurrence, culture_attested_*, weighted_choice, the entire NewName output class, select_via_vector. (Code map: runtime/proportions.py.)
(B) NOT RECOMMENDED — retire the proportions DATA entirely. Would require an independent structure-template generator AND a replacement for the position-gating/cross-usage frequency. The pure-vector fallback (_emit_unweighted, used only when usage_frequency_by_bucket=None) is known to skew language-mix 25-35pp (wyrd-bol9). Large separate effort.

SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT: the realism gate (drift_runner.run_drift_samples + test_kenning_realism_regression) COMPARES proportions vs vector. You cannot validate vector parity after deleting proportions. So: validate parity FIRST (both modes alive), THEN re-anchor the gate to ABSOLUTE corpus bands, THEN delete proportions scoring.

PHASES:
- Phase 0 (gate, operator-driven): decision-grade realism comparison at N=1000 across all 5 cultures (extends wyrd-l1z3); confirm vector ~= proportions within tightened bands; resolve wyrd-vidi.
- Phase 1 (parity blockers): empty-pick fallback; port D8/D18 inflection+variant rendering to vector; welsh realism band (cj6f now fixed); phon-vector coverage floor.
- Phase 2 (flip default): schema default proportions->vector (kenning.py:313), CLI default (generate.py), WYRD_DEFAULT_SCORING_MODE; keep proportions-scoring opt-in ONE release as escape hatch; re-anchor realism gate to absolute corpus bands.
- Phase 3 (delete): remove the deletable proportions-scoring functions; collapse scoring_mode param/enum + WYRD_FF_SCORING_MODE (axis-weights always on); retire/repoint the drift-comparison harness. Keep the proportions DATA layer.

IMPACT SURFACES: schema kenning.py:310-330,417,470; CLI generate.py:19,156-171,332-338,184-228; SPA featureFlags.js:21-27 + terraform main.tf:244-249; ~6 bit-stability tests + ~29 proportions-mentioning test files; drift_runner.py:87-160 + test_kenning_realism_regression.py:60-97 (comparison gate).
notes: PHASE 0 PARITY GATE: PASSED (2026-06-01). Decision-grade N=1000 vector-vs-proportions drift comparison, run LOCALLY against the full bundle (/tmp full L4), 2 independent seed-streams (base_seed 0 + 1000), all 5 cultures: ZERO band violations on every culture × seed. n_vec=1000 everywhere (no empty-pick sample loss at the bare/default request — so wyrd-tbke's empty-pick raise does NOT bite default generation; it remains a Phase-1 blocker only for era/stratum/tag-GATED requests). welsh now runs clean at N=1000 (cj6f fixed). The wyrd-vidi post-D40 divergence was an N=100 noise artifact (see vidi notes). CONCLUSION: vector is at realism parity with proportions; the primary retirement risk (vector realism inferiority) is retired. Phase 0 remaining: codify tighter bands at N=1000 levels (wyrd-jfaz/vidi). Cleared to start Phase 1.

title: Connector/particle morphemes (cum, St, le) dangle as standalone words in generated names
description: Generation produces names where a connector/particle morpheme stands alone as a whole word, e.g. 'Newton Cum' (Latin 'cum' connector dangling) and 'Penenorde ... Tump St' (the Saint- dedication particle with no subject). These morphemes REQUIRE a complement (X-cum-Y; St <subject>) and are never a valid standalone English place-name word. ROOT CAUSE: they're untagged regular morphemes in the pool (decomposed from real toponyms like 'Stow cum Quy' → 'cum' as a bare word), with no 'connector' classification, so the generator can put them in any bare-single slot, including dangling at the end. The joiner mechanism (_apply_joiner_insertion / load_joiners) is the architectural home for connectors but ships NO joiner data today (inactive). There is no St-dedication generation knob (only manorial_affix), so the saint subjects + particle are decomposition-only — 'St' in base generation is pure leak. PRAGMATIC FIX (this ticket): exclude a curated connector/particle surface set (saint, cum, le, la, sur, sous, juxta) from the base generation pool, by SURFACE (some variants are untagged), at load_parts + build_non_position_eligible — runtime, no re-export. PROPER FIX (deeper follow-up): classify connectors as joiner data + feed the joiner-insertion mechanism so 'X cum Y' generates correctly via insertion rather than random placement.
close_reason: Merged PR #432. Connector morphemes (cum/le/la/sur/sous/juxta) excluded from base generation by surface in both scoring modes — runtime-only, no re-export. Validated 0 cum-dangle. Scope: saint/st NOT surface-excluded (legit saint-slot mechanism); trailing-St dangle found non-systematic (0/500); residual 'Saint <common-noun>' oddity filed as a separate saint-slot-quality follow-up.

Historical dashboard runs got real numbers only because operators passed --bundle to a generated full meanings.json. Fix: point the dashboard's bundle metrics at the runtime DB (seed-runtime.db / the L4 bundle) instead of meanings.json, so 'morphemes over time' trend tracking stays trustworthy. Surfaced 2026-06-01 reviewing morpheme status after the eyjk deconstruction change.
close_reason: PR #699 merged. The stale-meanings.json BUG itself was already fixed by the d90t/wyrd-62cc L4 cutover: language_report.py defaults --bundle to None → rehydrates the bundle from the L4 runtime DB (get_runtime_db + bundle_dict_from_runtime_db), and --proportions omitted → proportions_dict_for_culture from L4; neither reads the deleted meanings.json, so bundle_* metrics already report the real L4 numbers (not the 1535 fallback). The remnant fixed here: three doc strings still advertised the deleted-JSON defaults and actively misled operators about where dashboard numbers come from (the exact confusion in this ticket) — corrected --bundle help, --proportions help, and the function docstring to describe the L4-runtime-DB default + the --bundle override. Help-text/docstring only, no behavior change. 2 review rounds (factual reviewers verified all claims vs code; 1 P3 clarity reword).

title: Untagged homograph of a personal/saint name leaks into base generation (e.g. 'Bartholomew' with empty tags)
description: wyrd-g1hj excludes pure-proper-noun saint + given-name etymons from the base pool, but a SURFACE can also have an UNTAGGED homograph entry (e.g. 'Bartholomew' exists as [male name], [personal-name,saint,religious], AND tags=[]). The empty-tagged entry is not a pure proper noun, so the tag-based exclusion can't catch it, and it leaks into base names ('Hamble Bartholomew', ~1/120 at cohesion=1.0 on the full bundle). Surface-level exclusion (drop the whole surface if any sibling is a name/saint) would over-exclude legitimate name/place homographs (stone/Stone). Needs a data-level fix: tag or fold the untagged personal-name homographs, OR a curated name-surface set consulted at base-pool build. Distinct mechanism from the etymon leak fixed in wyrd-g1hj.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-06-20: LIVE but needs a small DECISION before it's loop-workable. The bug is real + unfixed (main): is_pure_proper_noun (runtime/meaning.py:445-446) short-circuits False for an UNTAGGED saint/personal-name homograph (e.g. 'Bartholomew' tags=[]), so it leaks into base generation. The LOOP-DECISION already picked the MECHANISM (curated surface-exclusion set consulted at base-pool build, reversible — mirror _CONNECTOR_PARTICLE_SURFACES at meaning.py:42, add a predicate to is_base_pool_excluded which both base-pool sites proportions.py:512 + vector_name_select.py:280 route through). WHAT'S UNDECIDED: (a) the actual SET CONTENTS — needs a data query against the bundle to enumerate surfaces whose siblings carry name/saint tags but which also have a tags=[] entry (Bartholomew is the only named instance); (b) storage shape (new data/*.json vs inline frozenset alongside data/saint_personal_names.json); (c) an over-exclusion guard so legit place/name homographs (stone/Stone) aren't dropped — must be an explicit curated allowlist-of-exclusions, not a rule. Devon: confirm the source for the contents (auto-enumerate from the bundle? hand-curate?) and storage, then it's loop-workable.

title: Filter single-morpheme 'just bare' name structures (Old/In/St/Cum/Green/Bath) — uninteresting generated names
description: Generation produces names that are a single bare morpheme standing alone (~14% of English output): structures ((('bare','single'),),) and ((('bare','name','single'),),). Examples: Old, In, Next, Little, St, Cum, Green, White, Vale, Street, Bridge, Castle, Bath, Village, Common, Eagle — plus legit-but-dull single-etymon names (Chislehurst, Enfield, Beaumont). is_structurally_grammatical (wyrd-zzli/80ib) deliberately keeps single-bare WORDS (correct: 'Green' inside 'Green Park'), but never rejects a whole structure that is ONE morpheme total. Fix: a real place name needs >=2 morphemes — reject structures with total morpheme count <=1, regardless of bare/name/saint qualifier (multi-word Green Park = 2 morphemes survives; single-word Higham = 2 morphemes survives). Build-time filter -> re-export -> re-publish staging. Surfaced reviewing the wyrd-eyjk staging bundle.

title: SPA feature flags: env-driven per-option gating for the advanced config UI (default off, staging all-on)
description:
Goal: a clean, well-validated SPA UI on the road to production. Gate each advanced configuration option behind a feature flag so untested options stay hidden in prod and can be turned on one-by-one as validated. Purely a UI concern — NOT enforcement (the API stays permissive; flags only decide what the SPA renders).

Design (agreed with operator):
- Runtime/API-driven flags: the Flask/Lambda app resolves flags from env and ships a 'config' block on /api/manifest: {feature_flags: {name: bool, ...}, defaults: {option: value, ...}}. One build artifact for all envs; flip a flag via Lambda env (terraform) with no rebuild.
- Env scheme: WYRD_FF_<NAME>=true|false per flag; WYRD_FF_ALL=true master override (staging sets this so a forgotten flag can't hide an untested option); WYRD_DEFAULT_<OPTION>=<value> overrides an option's default VALUE. Resolution: flag = WYRD_FF_ALL or env(WYRD_FF_<name>, default False). Default for every flag is OFF.
- Server owns the flag registry (canonical names + resolved booleans + default-value overrides); SPA owns the flag->field mapping (which rendered fields each flag gates).
- Flag categories: (1) advanced knobs (novelty, spelling_variety, inflection_density, era, stratum, scoring_mode [gates the axis-weight fields too], packs, priors_path, cohesion, include_fiction, joiner_density, manorial_affix, ...); (2) cultures except english (english always available; scottish/welsh/irish/breton each gateable, namespaced culture.<name>); (3) customize-moods and customize-tags controls.
- SPA behavior: read config at boot (appState already loads /api/manifest); filter advanced fields in ConfigureColumn/headlineFields by flag; filter the culture enum (english always present); gate the moods/tags controls; HIDE the advanced panel entirely when zero advanced flags are on; seed initial form values from config.defaults.
- Terraform: per-env Lambda env vars — prod sets nothing / selective; staging sets WYRD_FF_ALL=true.

Scope: server flag-resolution module + manifest config block + SPA filtering/panel-hiding/default-seeding + terraform env wiring + tests on both ends. Manifest-driven (flags key off schema property names; no hardcoded field list). Single PR.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #425 (squash 0d2debe): env-driven SPA feature-flag system — server config block on /api/manifest, SPA field/culture/composer gating + default seeding, terraform env wiring, vitest harness + CI job.

title: welsh proportions generation crashes: KeyError ('bare','name','single') in MeaningGenerator.select
description:
## Symptom
`Kenning().generate({'culture':'welsh','scoring_mode':'proportions'}, seed=806)` raises:

    KeyError: ('bare', 'name', 'single')
      runtime/proportions.py:432  MeaningGenerator.select  -> self.generators[key]
      runtime/proportions.py:1156 _select_no_tag
      runtime/proportions.py:814  select

First crashing seed in 0..999 is 806 (proportions mode). Vector mode hits it too via the same select path.

## Impact
- Blocks `wyrd kenning lexicon drift-report --culture welsh` at any N that reaches a crashing seed (N>=807 with --seed 0). welsh is the only culture that can't produce a full drift report — blocks tolerance-band work for welsh (ecjp.7 follow-up).
- Other cultures (english/scottish/irish/breton) are unaffected at N=1000.
- The plain CLI 'generate welsh --seed 806' does NOT crash because the CLI remaps --seed through resolve_seed + a per-name seed_rng; the crash reproduces when a seed is passed directly to Kenning.generate (drift_runner.py:142 does exactly this).

## Root-cause lead
The key ('bare','name','single') is a (position, tag, count) MeaningGenerator bucket. A welsh proportions *structure* template references that slot, but MeaningGenerator.generators has no such bucket. Likely a committed dev-seed (seed-runtime.db) mismatch: select_dev_subset (runtime_db_export.py) keeps proportions *structures* in FULL but trims usages/single_usages to top-N per culture — so a kept structure that references a ('bare','name') usage trimmed out of the top-N leaves the generator bucket unbuilt. Production full bundle likely unaffected; needs confirming against a non-dev export. Either (a) make MeaningGenerator.select tolerate a missing bucket (skip/fallback), or (b) make select_dev_subset prune structures whose referenced buckets didn't survive usage trimming.

## Repro
    PYTHONPATH=<repo> python -c "from wyrd.generators.kenning.generators.kenning import Kenning; Kenning().generate({'culture':'welsh','scoring_mode':'proportions'}, seed=806)"
or
    wyrd kenning lexicon drift-report --culture welsh --count 1000 --seed 0

Found during the 2026-06-01 scoring-mode / drift-report investigation (kenning/scoring-mode-investigation worktree).
notes: Follow-up surfaced in PR #413 review: once welsh's proportions crash is fixed, (1) bump SAMPLES_PER_MODE 100->1000 in tests/test_kenning_realism_regression.py (currently capped because run_drift_samples doesn't catch the welsh proportions KeyError at ~seed 806, so N>806 ERRORs welsh), (2) re-tighten PER_CULTURE_TOLERANCES toward the stable N=1000 distribution (KL<=0.05, rho>=0.6 — already measured), and (3) add a welsh band (its full N=1000 drift can't be measured until the crash is fixed). Also consider wrapping the proportions call in run_drift_samples so a single crashing seed doesn't take down the whole drift run.
close_reason: Fixed + merged in PR #415 (squash 564e1d9). cj6f: MeaningGenerator.select returns None + warns once for a missing bucket (no more KeyError on welsh seed 806). antq: refreshed stale DECISIONS.md ecjp.7 + test_tolerance docstrings. Reviewed via pr-review-loop (3 rounds).

title: Generated multi-word place names render without spaces between words
description: Multi-word generated names run their words/morphemes together with no separating space, making them unreadable. Example: 'CornnamullacBunarath' (morphemes Corn- na mul -lac- Buna -rath) is otherwise fine but should render with spaces (e.g. 'Corn na Mullac Buna Rath'). Also in 'ParAliKin' (Par- Ali kin). The joiner / word-boundary logic isn't inserting inter-word spaces for these culture/morpheme combinations. Surfaced via the SPA inspector during wyrd-ls13 tag review.
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (autonomous loop 2026-06-20 — investigated + reproduced; ticket DIAGNOSIS is wrong, real fix is a modeling call — skipped).

NOT a spacing/joiner bug. Reproduced + inspected the generator internals (NewName.name word grouping via str(new_name) = ' '.join(words)). The run-together names are SINGLE-WORD structs that pack many morphemes; the render is CORRECT (one word -> no space, by design — compounds like Whit+ham -> Whitham). Confirmed examples: 'Anaseynterægehana' = words=1, morphemes_per_word=[4]; 'Cillæscachadh' = [3]; 'Anadroimna' = [3].

The ticket's proposed output ('Corn na Mullac Buna Rath' = one morpheme per word) CONTRADICTS the compound model — you'd never split 'Whitham' into 'Whit Ham'. So the encoded fix ('insert inter-word spaces') is not implementable as stated; it would shatter every legitimate compound.

REAL ISSUE (data, 2400 names across irish/scottish/welsh/english, no knobs):
- word-count distribution: 1w=1758 (73%), 2w=594, 3w=44, 4w=4
- max-slots-in-ONE-word distribution: 1->234, 2->1104, 3->802, 4->202, 5->48, 6->8, 7->2
- single-word names by slot count: 2->852, 3->666, 4->184, 5->46, 6->8, 7->2
So ~900 single-word names cram 3-7 morphemes into one word ('Ana+seynt+eræge+hana'), which reads as gibberish. Real toponym compounds top out ~3 morphemes (Wolverhampton = Wulfrun+heah+tun). The structs come from data/structures.yaml sampled by _pick_struct_via_vector, already passed by is_structurally_grammatical (wyrd-zzli) — so these high-slot single-word structs are CURRENTLY ALLOWED.

DECISION FOR DEVON (pick one; each shifts the whole output distribution + interacts with the empirical-proportions fidelity):
  (A) Cap morphemes-per-word for single-word structs (reject/down-weight >N slots). Need N (2? 3?). Enforce in is_structurally_grammatical (proportions.py:680) or via a data/structures.yaml allowlist (wyrd-c6o1.5). Cheapest lever; directly kills the gibberish tail. RISK: drops legitimate 3-morpheme compounds if N=2; changes the sampled distribution vs the corpus.
  (B) Reframe as the SEMANTIC-COHERENCE problem (wyrd-3i6w, explicitly linked in this ticket's notes): a 4-morpheme single word is tolerable IF the morphemes cohere (bird+name+pen is the real defect, not the spacing). Then this ticket folds into 3i6w and the cap is secondary.
  (C) Keep long compounds but improve READABILITY another way (e.g. cap total rendered length, or prefer 2-word structs at sampling time). 

RECOMMENDATION: (A) with N=3 as a quick, high-impact quality win (kills the 5-7 slot tail = the worst offenders) AND treat the residual ugliness as (B)/3i6w. But the cap value + the corpus-fidelity tradeoff is Devon's call. Until decided, leave PARKED — the ticket as written ('insert spaces') must NOT be implemented. (Reproduction grounded at proportions.py NewName.__str__ 2157 + struct sampling 1590; structures gate 680.)

title: Tag coverage: backfill semantic tags for untagged generation morphemes
description:
83% of bundle entries are untagged (68k empty / 14k tagged); generation-reachable: ~3104 etymons are untagged but HAVE a gloss (classifiable). Tags drive the generator's mood/cohesion/theme filtering, so untagged morphemes can't be themed — flagged as a release concern.

Approach (two-tier, rebuildable, mirrors gloss/pronunciation wyrd-u9k6/vm8t):
- Tier 1: high-precision deterministic gloss->tag lexicon (existing ~22-tag controlled vocab) — free enrichment pass, no jsonl.
- Tier 2: LLM classifier into the vocab with a MANDATORY 'none' option (abstract glosses like 'very'/'good' stay untagged — no bad matches) -> data/mining/_tags.jsonl -> deterministic replay.

Constraints (operator): NO bad matches (leave genuinely-untaggable glosses blank), NO tag sprawl (new tags only by frequency+necessity+sign-off). Approved 4 new tags by frequency: food/drink (~243), body (~97), kinship (~81), conflict (~46). Scope: generation-reachable first (~3104).

title: kenning: pronunciation coverage for generation morphemes in the deployed bundle (reader_pronunciation/IPA)
description:
Surfaced by the inspector pronunciation guide (#PR wyrd-2b50). Most generated morphemes carry NO renderings (reader_pronunciation/IPA) for their surface form, so the new top-of-inspector pronunciation guide is often partial (e.g. Burham shows '-ham' only, Bur- blank) or fully empty (Thornham, Warthwaite: 0/N morphemes). The guide renders gaps honestly ('·') rather than faking them.

Two sub-problems:
(1) COVERAGE: renderings are keyed on specific etymon forms; the generated surface usage frequently doesn't match any rendering key, OR the morpheme simply has no IPA/reader data at all. Need to (a) measure coverage in the deployed bundle (% of generation-reachable morpheme surfaces with a matching reader_pronunciation/IPA), and (b) backfill — derive pronunciation for the surface forms actually produced by generation, not just canonical etymon forms.
(2) CORRECTNESS: some matched renderings look wrong (e.g. -ham -> /xɑːm/, a velar fricative). Audit suspect matches.

Relates to wyrd-7qq3 (Old Norse IPA at 9.8%) — same coverage class, broader scope. Whatever backfills must be rebuildable + jsonl-recorded per REBUILD.md. The inspector guide is the triage surface.

title: kenning data-quality: pathological names from over-pooled homographs + degenerate morphemes (exemplar: PenBilsOne)
description:
Recorded 2026-05-31 as a concrete worklist exemplar (surfaced by the new compact output row, #406). The generated name 'PenBilsOne' (= Pen- + Bil-s + One) exhibits THREE distinct pathologies:

(1) OVER-POOLED HOMOGRAPH FAMILIES — distinct etymons sharing a surface got linked into one morpheme family, so the meanings list is a grab-bag of unrelated senses with scattershot tags:
  - Pen- conflates: OE 'pening' (a penny / penny rent — economic) + Celtic 'pen' (/pɛn/ = head, hill, headland, promontory, chief, extremity — topographic) + 'a personal name'. Tags: economic, male name, possession, geology, topography, descriptive, measurement. That is 3+ unrelated etymons in one family.
  - Bil-s conflates: OE 'bil' (a bill/sword, bladed weapon) + 'bil' (sharp ridge / headland / promontory / hill-spur — topographic) + 'a personal name'. Forms pooled: bil, bill, bile, bile-, Bile, Bil.

(2) DEGENERATE MORPHEME 'One' — surface 'One', sole gloss 'a personal name', NO IPA / reader pronunciation, tag 'male name'. A content-free name-only morpheme that should not be eligible for generation (it just appends a meaningless 'One').

(3) BAD ASSEMBLY — 'Pen- Bil-s One' -> 'PenBilsOne' is unpronounceable and meaningless; the '-s' joiner + the 'One' word compound the nonsense.

Fix directions (not yet scoped):
  - Split over-pooled homograph families: same-surface + same-culture but DIFFERENT-meaning etymons must NOT be one family (inverse of the collapse/fold work in wyrd-v3ow, which merges SAME-meaning). Needs a de-pollution / family-split pass, likely LLM-assisted, jsonl-recorded so it's rebuildable.
  - Prune or gate degenerate name-only morphemes (no gloss beyond 'a personal name', no pronunciation) out of the generation pool.
  - The compact output row (#406) makes these visible at a glance — use it to triage.

Related: wyrd-u9k6 (gloss backfill), wyrd-v3ow (consolidation epic), wyrd-g2vd (ingest guard).

--- verbatim dump (operator-captured) ---
PenBilsOne / Pen- Bil-s One
Pen- meanings: A penny; a penny rent., Penny, a personal name, Hill, End, Last, Tail end, end, head, head, chief, end, head, extremity, or upper part, the highest part, the extreme end, Headland, Point, Promontory, head, hillock | tags: economic, male name, possession, geology, topography, descriptive, measurement | OE: paeniġ (pening), Pening; Celtic: pen /pɛn/ PEN
Bil-s meanings: A bill, a sword; topographically a sharp ridge, a headland, the edge of a hill, a promontory., A bill, beak; used topographically of a headland, a narrow promontory., Hill with a pointed ridge or spur, Hillspur-, a kind of sword or other bladed weapon..., a personal name, sword | tags: geology, male name, topography | OE: bil /bil/ BIL, bill, bile, bile-, Bile, Bil
One meanings: a personal name | tags: male name | OE: One (no pronunciation)

title: Consolidate variant/duplicate etymons into their lemma (fold form-of forms + merge same-meaning lemmas)
description:
Form/variant etymons and same-meaning duplicate etymons live as standalone lemmas with pointer- or duplicate-glosses, surfacing as non-useful etymology lines in generation (e.g. 'Hea- (h-prothesized form of ea)' instead of 'Hea- (river)') and inflating the lemma count. They should live as etymon_variant rows of their lemma — that table exists (5.77M rows; 'burh' is ALREADY a variant of 'burg') — not as independent lemmas. Same-culture + same-meaning duplicates should merge into one lemma.

Surfaced 2026-05-30 from staging generation ('Hea-' pointer gloss). Root model + decisions captured in --design.
design:
MODEL / TARGET STATE
- Variant/form-of forms (burh='alt form of burg', Hea-='form of ea') become etymon_variant rows of their lemma, NOT standalone lemmas. Generation shows the lemma's real meaning (burg->fort, ea->river).
- Same-culture + same-meaning duplicate lemmas merge into one.

POPULATIONS (live DB, exact census = ticket P0)
- 16 etymons whose ONLY gloss is a form-of pointer; 9 are reflex-linked (what users see today).
- 64 with pointer + a real gloss.
- 94,666 already carry lemma_id (set by the link-lemmas-v1 enrichment pass; #333 'derivative-vs-semantic gloss split' wyrd-o53o/aizb moved pointers here + added meanings — the 'past fix').
- Broader set: etymons whose (canonical_form, language) ALSO appears in etymon_variant pointing to a DIFFERENT lemma (these double as both a lemma AND a variant). 5.77M-row join — count in P0.
- Same-meaning duplicate lemmas (LLM-judged) — count in P0.

ORIGIN: many standalone form-of etymons were minted by SCHOLARLY place-name sources (Ekwall, Skeat, Mawer, KEPN) that cite the form as a place-name element. So they carry real scholarly citations that must not be lost.

DECISION 1 (cite handling = HYBRID, user): when a form-of etymon folds into its parent, MIGRATE its scholarly citations to the parent AND stamp the original attested surface form on the citation. Coverage / scholar-witness queries (rando-retirement gate) then read off the parent; surface fidelity ('Ekwall attests the burh form of burg') is preserved. REQUIRES new column etymon_citation.attested_form (today: id, etymon_id, source_id, page, short_quote, context_snippet — no form field).

DECISION 2 (reconstructibility, user + REBUILD.md): determining same-meaning may need an LLM to compare two gloss strings ('fort' vs 'fortified place' -> same). LLM is OK, BUT the DECISION must be persisted to an importable L2 JSONL (e.g. data/mining/_merges.jsonl), replayed for FREE on rebuild — NEVER a re-mine step. Mirrors the etymon_meaning_synset rule in REBUILD.md. Deterministic folds (exact pointer-gloss target, exact variant-doubling) = a free deterministic enrichment pass in the 12-pass chain (re-run every rebuild, like link-lemmas).

RUNTIME GAP: the runtime export (runtime_db_export.py) follows NEITHER merged_into_id NOR lemma_id today. So folding alone won't fix generation — the fold must route a folded form's reflexes + gloss display to its lemma.

REBUILD DISCIPLINE (mandatory, REBUILD.md + enforcement triad): any new pass/layer is a 4-file change — the code, a data/mining/_rebuild_layers.json entry, a REBUILD.md restore step, and (if a new L2 file like _merges.jsonl) the L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md map. Must satisfy tests/test_kenning_rebuild_runbook.py, the rebuild-runbook-currency-reviewer, AND the repo-root db-reconstructibility-reviewer ('recoverable without re-paying for mining').

PHASES (child tickets): P0 census; P1 schema (etymon_citation.attested_form); P2 deterministic fold pass; P3 LLM same-meaning merge -> _merges.jsonl L2 round-trip; P4 export/generation resolution; P5 ingest guard; P6 rebuild-discipline wiring; P7 verify.
notes: SHIPPED TO STAGING 2026-05-31. Core fully delivered: P0 census, P1 schema, P2 deterministic folds (#399/#400), P3 LLM merge (#401/#402), P4 export resolution (#403), P7 verify — all closed. 161 folds applied to live DB + dev seed committed (#405) + full bundle published to staging S3 (current.json -> v/2026-05-31T02-47Z.db). Verified: 0 form-of pointer glosses in generation, folded forms show lemma meaning (burh->fort etc.), canonical gate passes. ONLY REMAINING: wyrd-g2vd (P5 ingest guard) — OPTIONAL future-leakage prevention; the enrichment fold pass already re-cleans on every rebuild, so this is a nice-to-have, not a blocker. Epic kept open solely to track that optional P5; safe to close if P5 is deprioritized. Production publish is operator-gated.

title: kenning P3: place-name-corpus-readiness dashboard (gate gazetteer retirement)
kenning: unify place-name corpora into the JSONL pipeline + retire the static gazetteer (rando-port playbook)
description:
Apply the rando-port pattern to the bundled *_place_names.json proportions corpora: collapse the static-JSON special case into the one JSONL->DB->bundle pipeline, then drive retirement of the gazetteer dependency via a readiness dashboard.

WHY: proportions are currently built by loading static {culture}_place_names.json and matcher-RE-DECOMPOSING each name against the etymon set — the attested toponym decompositions (the product of phase-2 + KEPN mining) are never used. This is the root cause of '2 weeks of mining, no visible lift'. Post-KEPN the DB has 20,132 attested England toponyms (>17,876 gazetteer) with 13,326 attested decompositions (vs 0 used today).

GOAL: one code path (DB toponyms, attested decomp + matcher fallback), static *_place_names.json deleted from the runtime path, gazetteer demoted to a low-trust seed source (like rando-port) tracked for retirement.

SCOPE: unification applies to all 5 cultures; RETIREMENT is english-first (KEPN+scholarly give english the attestation to cross the line for initial release; welsh/irish/scottish/breton stay deeply red until more attested sources land).

Mirrors: rando-port (jsonl seed source + rando-port-readiness dashboard).

title: Add Latin as pre-OE stratum of the English era chain (time machine) so Roman-substrate elements render across eras
description: GAP: era/cells.py puts Latin in its OWN family (classical/late-vulgar/medieval/renaissance); LANGUAGE_TO_FAMILY['latin']='latin'. The 'english' family chain starts at OE (oe-early->oe-late->me->early-modern->modern). So Latin-derived English place-name elements (caster<castra, eccles<ecclesia, port<portus, -coln<colonia, stræt<strata, Catterick<Cataractonium) are siloed in the latin family and do NOT render across the English rewind/era-map progression (default English ladder = oe-late/me/modern, no Latin stop). Roman is the DEEPEST stratum of English toponymy and should be reachable in the English time machine. SCOPE: (1) add a deepest 'latin'/'roman' cell to the english ERA_CELLS sequence before oe-early; (2) canonical_language_for_cell ('english','latin'/'roman')->'latin'; (3) add the Latin stop to the default English rewind ladder + era-map; (4) D33 era-reflex picker must resolve a Latin reflex for an English-chain morpheme via descent edges (Latin parent -> OE child) — requires those edges to exist (Wiktionary/KEPN). DO NOT blanket-remap LANGUAGE_TO_FAMILY['latin']->'english' (Latin also roots French etc.); the substrate cell is specific to Latin-in-English-toponymy. Motivated by KEPN (wyrd-bc5z) surfacing 42+ Latin elements / 2 counties + existing corpus Latin. Parser/ingest already capture Latin fine — this is a rendering/era-axis gap only. Relates D33.

title: Derive surface_in_modern for breakdowns via suffix-anchoring; feed D18 variant pool (e.g. Earda→Arde in Ardeley)
description: KEPN (and existing) breakdowns give elements + gloss but NOT the per-element surface slice of the modern toponym.
