title: kenning mining: extract high-signal toponyms from cross-scholar disagreements (914 candidates)
description:
The lexicon report ('wyrd kenning lexicon report') surfaces 914 toponyms with conflicting breakdowns across scholars — different historical-linguistics references give different morpheme decompositions for the same modern surface. These are an under-mined high-signal source.

The disagreement set is interesting for THREE reasons:

1. **Scholar count is the entry gate.** A toponym appearing in two scholarly sources at all is rarer than appearing in one — getting cited at all means the name was worth a researcher's attention. Disagreement specifically means MULTIPLE scholars cared, which raises the prior.

2. **The disagreement encodes uncertainty in the morpheme assignment** — when Skeat says 'Barton = bere + tūn' and a later authority says 'Barton = beorh + tūn', either reading is corpus-attested somewhere. The disagreement itself is data — it tells us the morpheme picker should hedge here, not pick one and lock in.

3. **The 914 candidates are scholar-sourced, not rando-port-grandfathered.** Already past the C1 / C3 readiness criteria as a class.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Audit-side: a 'wyrd kenning lexicon report-disagreements' command (or extend existing 'report') that dumps the 914 toponyms with all their conflicting breakdowns side-by-side, sortable by per-name disagreement-count.

2. Mining-side: for each disagreement, walk the etymological CHAIN behind each scholar's decomposition (toponym_etymology_element rows) and ensure all root etymons are ingested. Pre-this, only the WINNING parse's elements get the citation chain — the LOSING parse's morphemes might be cited in the disagreement but lack the toponym_etymology link.

3. Resolution policy: pick one of (a) admit both readings as alternate canonical_decompositions, (b) prefer the most-recent scholar, (c) prefer the scholar most frequently cited across the corpus. Option (a) is the highest-fidelity but requires runtime changes to handle multi-parse Meanings.

CONTEXT (from 2026-05-29 dashboard audit):
The lexicon report's disagreement examples list starts with Skeat's 1901 Cambridgeshire entries (Barton, Carlton, Chesterton, Clopton, Coton, Croxton, Drayton, ...) — these all have one or more newer authorities giving different breakdowns. That's the easy starting tranche.

Related: wyrd-eni4 (coverage-quality epic), wyrd-sfdj (semantic-coherence audit — disagreements feed into the split-tool surface).

title: kenning mining: extract English single-letter joiners (-s-, -e-, -i-) from toponym corpus
description:
Post wyrd-m2ym (#372) the trie matcher no longer blocks English single-character morphemes — phonogram-only filter is precise to Egyptian/Akkadian/Sumerian sources. The bundle still lacks legitimate English joiners (genitive '-s-' in Kingsbury, linking vowels '-e-' / '-i-' in Tunbridge / Wakefield), so words like 'Kingsbury' currently decompose with the joiner consumed into an unaccounted fragment ([King-, sbury]) instead of [King-, -s-, -bury]. That data is lost from proportions training and shows up as low-quality decomposition in the explainer.

WHY MINING (vs manual seed): the manual-seed pathway works for a small known set but doesn't surface joiner frequencies per language / period / position. Mining gives us empirical attestation from the toponym corpus (Watts, Mills, Ekwall) — which lets us weight joiner-bearing decompositions correctly in proportions training and validates the morpheme set against real-world citations.

DELIVERABLE:
1. Joiner extraction pass over the toponym corpus that detects single-char connector patterns in attested decompositions (e.g. 'Kingsbury → King(s)bury' annotations in Watts Cambridge dictionary).
2. Joiner morphemes land in the lexicon DB with:
   - canonical_form: 's' / 'e' / 'i'
   - language: 'modern-english' (or 'old-english' for genitive '-es-' patterns from OE; 'old-norse' for ON linking morphemes)
   - position_pref: 'inner' (forces dash-marked inner-position usage)
   - sources: citation-attested via the mining source the joiner came from
3. Bundle export carries them through. Trie matcher includes them (filter doesn't block — they have English-family sources).
4. Proportions training picks them up automatically as inner morphemes in 3-morpheme decompositions.

ACCEPTANCE TESTS:
- After mining: 'Kingsbury' canonically decomposes as [King-, -s-, -bury] (3 morphemes, no unaccounted fragment).
- 'Tunbridge' decomposes as [Tun-, -bridge] (no joiner) but 'Eshalpe'-shape names with linking vowels surface them.
- Proportions empirical table for 'pre → inner → post' transitions shifts to include joiner-bearing patterns at corpus-weighted frequency.

RELATED:
- wyrd-m2ym (#372, merged 2026-05-28) — phonogram-only filter that unblocks English single-chars.
- wyrd-bol9 (#366, merged 2026-05-28) — per-bucket frequency-weighted proportions pool that will absorb joiners transparently.
- wyrd-eni4 (epic) — coverage-quality initiative this fits under.

GOTCHA TO WATCH:
The wyrd-m2ym filter rule is 'pure phonogram-only'. If mining adds spurious English-family citations to Egyptian phonograms (e.g. a scholar's source cites Egyptian 's' as influential in English genitive 's' evolution), the filter stops dropping those Egyptian surfaces — they become mixed-source. The mining pass should NOT add English citations to non-English etymons unless the citation genuinely supports an English-language attestation, not just etymological influence.

title: language-report dashboard: 'avg witnesses' metric reports 0.0 for modern-english (rounding or counting bug)
description:
The language-quality scorecard's per-language detail section reports 'avg X.XX witnesses across N sources' for each language. modern-english is showing:

> A. Corpus depth: 22883 generator-eligible etymons (17077 eligible lemmas) of 1336698 raw etymons (1260760 raw lemmas in DB); 33 promotion-eligible at threshold ≥2, **avg 0.0 witnesses across 38 sources**.

That can't be right. modern-english has 33 promotion-eligible etymons at ≥2 — meaning at least 33 of them have ≥2 citations. The avg-witnesses should be > 0 for any language with > 0 promotion-eligible count.

Compare to old-english in the same report:
> A. Corpus depth: 12414 generator-eligible etymons (7128 eligible lemmas) of 71192 raw etymons (57291 raw lemmas in DB); 273 promotion-eligible at threshold ≥3, **avg 0.078 witnesses across 43 sources**.

old-english shows 0.078 — also suspiciously low (273 promoted should imply ~273 × 3 = ~800+ citations against ~12k etymons → avg should be ~0.06, so this is in range).

modern-english's 0.0 likely comes from one of:
1. The metric is dividing by raw-etymon count (1.3M) rather than eligible-etymon count (22.8k). 33×2 / 1336698 ≈ 0.00005 → rounds to 0.0.
2. The metric uses INTEGER division somewhere upstream.
3. A SQL aggregation is silently casting NULL → 0 for un-cited rows in a way that breaks the average.

## Repro

```bash
wyrd kenning lexicon language-report 2>/dev/null | grep -A1 '^### modern-english'
```

Should show a non-zero avg witnesses given the 33 promotion-eligible count.

## Likely fix

Locate the metric computation in `wyrd kenning lexicon language-report` (likely `lexicon/reporting/language_report.py` or similar). Check:
1. Divisor: should be `eligible_etymon_count` (generator-eligible filter applied) not the raw-etymon count.
2. Type: float division throughout; no integer truncation.
3. NULL handling: `COUNT(DISTINCT source_id)` per etymon, then `AVG(witness_count)` across etymons. Etymons with 0 citations should count as 0 in the average, not be excluded.

## Why P2

This is a published-data correctness bug — the dashboard's primary trust signal is the witness depth. A miscalibrated avg-witnesses number undercuts confidence in every downstream policy decision (including wyrd-fssn's tiered threshold). The fix is small and localized.

## Related

- wyrd-eni4 — dashboard is Phase 0 of the gap-closing epic

title: Witness-threshold policy: tier by rando-port origin (≥1 corroborator for rando lemmas, ≥3 for net-new)
description:
Current rule (D4): a morpheme promotes to the live inventory when it has ≥3 independent mining witnesses.

This rule was designed for the bootstrapped case: discovering a brand-new morpheme from scratch via LLM extraction, where independent corroboration is the only signal we have. It applies the same gate to rando-port lemmas, which is over-restrictive given their provenance.

PROPOSED TIERED POLICY:
- Rando-port lemma + 0 mining witnesses → 'rando-only' (quarantine, current behavior)
- Rando-port lemma + ≥1 mining witness → 'corroborated rando' → promote (NEW)
- Non-rando lemma + ≥3 mining witnesses → 'attested' → promote (current behavior)

The argument for the lower threshold on rando lemmas:
- Rando lemmas were curated by Wikipedia editors as place-name elements. That's already 1 layer of human signal — not bootstrap-from-nothing.
- ≥1 mining hit corroborates an existing claim rather than discovering a new one. The confidence boost from 0 → 1 mining witness on a rando lemma is qualitatively different from the boost from 0 → 1 witness on a no-baseline new morpheme.
- The wyrd-4453 toponym retirement work already adopted this stance: 'as long as it's attested in one source, I'm fine with town names getting promoted' (per the ticket close note from 2026-05-18).
- Keeping rando lemmas hostage to ≥3 witnesses keeps the rando-port corpus quarantined as second-class data even when scholars HAVE cited the form.

The argument against:
- 1 mining witness could still be a hallucination or low-quality extraction. Mitigation: this proposal only LOWERS the threshold for rando lemmas (where there's a curated baseline); never below 1.

CONCRETE EXAMPLE (surfaces in wyrd-nxhh context): modern-english:-chester has 0 mining witnesses today (rando-port only). modern-english:chester has 1 mining witness. Under current ≥3 policy both stay quarantined. Under tiered policy, -chester stays quarantined (0 corroborators) but chester (the bare/non-suffix form) promotes (1 corroborator).

Implementation hooks:
- bd promote-* commands need a tier-aware threshold. Concretely a per-source-class threshold (rando-port=1, net-new=3).
- etymon_consensus view (or the queries that materialize it) needs to expose the source-class breakdown so the policy can apply.
- Audit needed: how many rando lemmas have 1-2 mining witnesses today? That's the actionable lift from this change.

Related: wyrd-eni4 (gap-closing epic), wyrd-j2bv (retire rando-port as primary attribution source — already closed), wyrd-nxhh (bundle export cognate resolution — separate but compose with this), wyrd-4453 (toponym version of this rule, closed). Per OVERVIEW.md, current rando-port lemma count is ~1600, of which ~114 are promotion-eligible at ≥3 witnesses today — this change should lift that number meaningfully.

title: Bundle export: resolve modern surface form via cognate cluster / descent layer, not just reflex_etymon
description:
When a canonical etymon promotes on D4 witness count (e.g. old-english:ceaster, 5 witnesses) but has no reflex_etymon row, the bundle export currently drops it from the modern-surface mapping. The runtime then either omits the morpheme entirely or renders it in its archaic form (e.g. 'ceaster' instead of 'chester'/'-cester'/'-caster').

The data is already there at L3:
- Cognate cluster (D27/D28): ceaster shares cluster 3617 with 9 middle-english surfaces (Chestre, Chestere, Chestir, Chestr, Chestur, Chestyre, Cæstre, Cestre, Chæstre), modern-english chester / -cester / -caster / Colchester, latin:castra, old-french:Cestre.
- Direct descent (etymon_descent inheritance edges): ceaster → Chester / -chester / -cester / -caster / Colchester.
- Toponym attestations (9 in toponym_etymology_element): Binchester, Chesterton, Chichester, Bellister, Taddecastre, etc.

What's missing: a bundle-export pass that walks the cognate-cluster + descent-layer to populate the modern surface mapping for promoted etymons, mirroring what etymon_era_reflexes already does at runtime.

Validation: re-emit the bundle and confirm:
1. old-english:ceaster appears as a Meaning in the English meaning_db
2. Its modern_usage surfaces are -chester / -cester / -caster
3. Generated names include Manchester / Winchester / Chichester / Doncaster shapes

Concrete example surfaced during wyrd-bol9 follow-up: chester family was missing from the English bundle entirely despite ceaster having 5 witnesses + a 16-member cognate cluster reaching the modern forms. The lexicon has the data; the bundle doesn't carry it because reflex_etymon is the only bridge in use today.

Related: wyrd-j43l (bundle re-emit umbrella), wyrd-eni4 (gap-closing epic). This is a sibling concern that the re-emit needs to address.

title: Vector sem_score axis amplifies OE picks even after per-Meaning culture filter (wyrd-pfoo follow-up)
description:
After wyrd-pfoo (PR #364) shipped the per-Meaning attestation filter at the vector runtime, Welsh vector OE-share dropped from 67% → 63% — much smaller than the gap to proportions' 34%. Remaining ~30pp gap is a scoring-axis amplification, not an eligibility-pool concern.

## Root cause

The vector path's per-slot scoring composition is

  score = phon_w * phon + sem_w * sem + pos_w * pos + base_w * baseline

With default request (no mood, no harshness, empty priors via the dev seed):
- phon_score ≈ 0 (no register weights → dot product against all-zero phon vector is 0)
- pos_score ≈ 0 (no position bias in default request)
- baseline ≈ 0 (no priors in the dev seed)
- sem_score = dot product of Meaning.tags against register.semantic_tags

The default request register has no semantic_tags weights set (just culture + no mood). So sem_score reduces to a simple presence sum: every Meaning gets score = len(intersection(meaning.tags, request_tags)).

But the per-Meaning eligibility pool admits MULTIPLE Meanings per usage_key (especially after wyrd-pfoo where both OE and Celtic senses survive when both have attestation). Within a slot, weighted_choice picks one weighted by score. OE Meanings consistently win because OE has DENSER tag enrichment than Celtic:

- OE morphemes typically carry 3-6 semantic tags (kq7w.1 corpus enrichment was OE-focused)
- Celtic morphemes typically carry 1-2 tags
- → OE Meanings get higher sem_score → higher weighted_choice probability

Validation trace from scratch/vector-validation/trace-scoring.py confirms: in 45 Welsh-attested dual-Meaning usages, mean OE-Celtic sem_score delta is +0.73 with default request. phon/pos/baseline deltas are 0.

## Why proportions doesn't have this issue

Proportions mode samples USAGES from per-culture proportions tables (weighted by corpus frequency), then picks within the usage by separate logic that doesn't favor OE Meanings over Celtic. It never scores Meanings against each other within a usage.

Vector picks USAGES via per-Meaning eligibility pool (uniform after gating) then scores each Meaning. The scoring asymmetry compounds the pool composition: even when Celtic and OE Meanings co-exist in the pool, OE wins the per-slot pick because it scores higher on the tag-dense sem axis.

## Possible fixes (not chosen — design needed)

1. **Tag-density normalization**: divide sem_score by len(meaning.tags) so a Meaning with 6 tags isn't weighted 3× over a Meaning with 2 tags. Lower-density Meanings (Celtic) compete on equal footing.

2. **Per-language tag enrichment**: aggressive Celtic / Welsh / Irish / Breton tagging pass to bring tag density up to OE's level. Closes the gap at the data layer rather than the scoring layer. Sister concern to the 8 untagged-but-plausible Celtic Meanings flagged in wyrd-pfoo investigation (-bad-, Bod-, Hen-, Nant-, Tir-, Wal-, -side, -ant).

3. **Pool-uniformity → frequency-weighted**: make vector's eligibility pool weighted by per-culture corpus frequency (the same data proportions samples from). Aligns vector with proportions' frequency-aware pool composition; scoring then operates on a pool that's already culture-shaped.

4. **Cohesion / mood injection**: vector mode's full strength shows when register/mood weights are non-trivial — the sem_score amplification only dominates in the no-register default case. Could be an operator-education concern more than a scoring bug.

## Validation methodology

Same as wyrd-pfoo: scratch/vector-validation/gen-post-merge.sh + compare-pfoo-impact.py + check-pool-skew.py + trace-scoring.py. Re-run after any candidate fix lands; aim for Welsh vector OE to track proportions (~34-40%) rather than 63%.

## Priority

P2. The wyrd-pfoo fix closed the wrong-sense leakage (the biggest correctness concern). The remaining OE-amplification is a quality/aesthetics concern — Welsh names that DO admit to Anglo-Welsh elements (which is realistic — Welsh place-names contain many anglicized elements) just admit them too aggressively. Users probably accept the current state but would notice a fix landing.

title: Vector mode over-picks OE across all cultures (Welsh vector 67% OE on 18%-presence pool)
description:
Post-merge validation (wyrd-80ib + wyrd-izcr) shows vector mode picks OE far beyond what the culture-attested pool composition would suggest:

| culture | attested OE presence | proportions picks OE | vector picks OE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| english | 44% | 73% | 87% |
| scottish | 32% | 53% | 70% |
| welsh | 18% | 34% | 67% |
| irish | 22% | 33% | 60% |
| breton | 16% | 28% | 64% |

Proportions roughly tracks pool composition (Welsh attested-weighted celtic 54% → proportions picks 53%). Vector is 2-4× more OE-skewed than proportions, even though both modes draw from the same per-culture attested-usages pool (post-wyrd-361).

Hypothesis: the culture-attested filter (wyrd-361, runtime.proportions.NameGenerator.culture_attested_usages) operates at the usage_key level — it decides which usages are eligible. But within an attested usage (e.g. -ham is attested in Welsh), the meaning_db carries multiple Meaning entries (OE, modern_english, etc.). Vector scores each Meaning independently and picks the highest. OE-tagged Meanings consistently win because they have the richest enrichment data: phonological_vector (kq7w.1 was OE-focused), attested_years, stratum classifications, citations. So even with culture=welsh, when an attested usage has both an OE Meaning and a Celtic Meaning, vector picks OE.

Proportions sidesteps this — it samples USAGES from per-culture proportion tables (which encode per-culture frequency), then picks within the usage by separate logic that doesn't favor the OE Meaning over the Celtic one.

User-facing effect: users requesting --culture welsh get names that read as Anglo-Welsh, not Welsh. Vector mode's culture-purification (Egyptian eliminated, good) flipped into culture-erasure (Welsh now mostly OE, bad).

Validation data + analysis scripts in scratch/vector-validation/ (gen-post-merge.sh, compare-post-merge.py, check-pool-skew.py).
design:
# PR plan: matcher tiebreaker for culture-aligned tagged Meanings

## Scope (one PR)

Matcher API + splitter wiring + bundle regen are tightly coupled. Splitting would leave a "feature flag" state with no caller. One PR.

## Files & sequence

### 1. runtime/trie_matcher.py — accept the tiebreaker hint

```python
def canonical_decompositions(
    word: str,
    trie: TrieNode,
    *,
    culture_languages: frozenset[str] | None = None,
) -> list[list[Meaning | str]]:
```

When `culture_languages` is None → preserve current behavior bit-for-bit. When set, after the existing `(unaccounted_chars, morpheme_count)` reduce, apply a third tiebreaker on remaining ties:
- `alignment_score(parse) = count of Meanings whose primary_language ∈ culture_languages AND len(tags) ≥ 1`
- Keep only parses with max alignment_score
- If still tied, fall back to the existing list-index tiebreaker

Pure function; no state.

Cache key for `canonical_decompositions` (per wyrd-p8ve fix) must include `culture_languages` to avoid serving a Welsh-tiebroken parse to an English caller.

### 2. runtime/name.py — thread the hint through

```python
def find_meaning(self, word_db, reduce=True, joiners=None, *, culture_languages=None)
```

Forward to `canonical_decompositions`. Default None preserves existing callers (KenningExplain, KenningRewind, KenningEraMap).

### 3. lexicon/proportions_builder.py — define CULTURE_LANGUAGES + use at split site

```python
CULTURE_LANGUAGES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {
    "english":  frozenset({"old_english", "modern_english", "old_scandinavian", "old_french"}),
    "scottish": frozenset({"celtic_mix", "old_english", "old_scandinavian"}),
    "welsh":    frozenset({"celtic_mix"}),
    "irish":    frozenset({"celtic_mix"}),
    "breton":   frozenset({"celtic_mix", "old_french"}),
}
```

Hand-curated for clarity; can be auto-derived from per-culture `place_names.json` language distributions later.

### 4. cli/rebuild_proportions.py + lexicon/runtime_db_export.py — pass culture through

Find every `name.find_meaning(word_db, ...)` call site that operates on a per-culture corpus. Add `culture_languages=CULTURE_LANGUAGES[culture]`. Both sites currently know the culture they're processing — pure plumbing.

### 5. data/seed-runtime.db — regenerate

`lexicon export-runtime-db --dev --output ...` regenerates the committed dev seed with the culturally-correct decompositions. Binary diff in PR but expected.

## Tests

### Unit — trie_matcher (`tests/test_kenning_trie_matcher.py`)

- `test_canonical_decompositions_no_culture_is_bit_stable_with_prior_behavior`: synthetic 2-Meaning corpus, no culture hint → output matches pre-PR matcher exactly.
- `test_canonical_decompositions_prefers_culture_aligned_tagged_meaning`: corpus with OE-tagged + Celtic-tagged Meanings for `-ton`; `culture_languages={"celtic_mix"}` → Celtic wins.
- `test_canonical_decompositions_skips_culture_aligned_untagged_meaning`: OE-tagged "town" + Celtic-but-empty-tags "tone"; `culture_languages={"celtic_mix"}` → OE wins (the tag gate).
- `test_canonical_decompositions_culture_match_only_on_ties`: parses with different unaccounted → unaccounted wins regardless of culture.
- `test_canonical_decompositions_cache_separates_culture_variants`: cache key includes culture_languages (regression for the cache-pollution risk).

### Unit — Name.find_meaning plumbing

- `test_find_meaning_forwards_culture_languages_to_matcher`: monkeypatch `canonical_decompositions`, verify kwarg flows through.

### Integration — proportions splitter

- `test_rebuild_proportions_welsh_attests_celtic_meaning_over_oe_homonym`: synthetic Welsh corpus where the matcher would ambiguously split via OE or Celtic; verify `proportions_usage` reflects the Celtic attestation, not OE.

## Validation

After landing:
1. Regenerate `seed-runtime.db` (committed in PR)
2. Re-run `scratch/vector-validation/gen-post-merge.sh` + `compare-post-merge.py`
3. Expected: Welsh vector OE drops from 67% → ~35-40% range. Same shape for Irish + Breton.
4. Verify junk-shape counts still 0/N (wyrd-80ib + wyrd-izcr guarantees)
5. Spot-check Welsh output for Pen-/Tir-/Hen-/Nant- prefixes increasing.

## Risk / open questions

- Bit-stability for explainer paths (KenningExplain, KenningRewind, KenningEraMap): they don't pass culture_languages → keep current behavior. Verify no implicit leak via generator class hierarchy.
- Trie-matcher cache (wyrd-p8ve): key must include culture_languages.
- Cultures missing from CULTURE_LANGUAGES (pack-overlay, future cultures): default None → no tiebreaker → existing behavior. Documented as safe fallback.

## Estimated diff

- Runtime: ~50 LOC (matcher tiebreaker + name.py plumbing)
- Lexicon: ~30 LOC (CULTURE_LANGUAGES + splitter wiring, 2 call sites)
- Tests: ~200 LOC (6 new tests across 2 files)
- Bundle: 1 binary regen
- Total: ~300 LOC + 1 binary

## Out of scope (file as follow-ups when wyrd-pfoo closes)

- Celtic-Meaning tag enrichment for 8 untagged-but-place-relevant Celtic Meanings (`-bad-`, `Bod-`, `Hen-`, `Nant-`, `Tir-`, `Wal-`, `-side`, `-ant`) — converts them from OE-fallback to Celtic-correct attestation.
- Auto-deriving CULTURE_LANGUAGES from per-culture corpus stats.
- Pool-uniformity vs frequency-weighting (vector picks uniformly from attested pool, proportions weights by frequency) — separate concern even after this fix.
notes: PR #364: https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/364. Ships matcher culture tiebreaker + per-Meaning attestation pipeline end-to-end. Validation: Welsh -4pp / Irish -2pp / Breton -3pp OE-share. Remaining OE-bias is sem_score axis amplification (OE has denser tag enrichment than Celtic) — separate ticket.

title: Filter single-word [pre]/[post] structure templates (1-morph affix-rendered-alone names)
description: The wyrd-zzli grammatical-structure filter exempts every single-word structure ('A single-word structure is always grammatical' early-return in runtime/proportions.is_structurally_grammatical). But [pre] and [post] single-word templates fill the only slot with a bare prefix/suffix morpheme, which renders as a standalone word with the hyphen stripped — producing names like 'Bridge', 'Green', 'South', 'End' that aren't real place-name compounds. Same defect class as the multi-word 'By Green' / 'Ton North' bugs wyrd-zzli originally fixed, just in single-word shape. Bundle has 566 weight (6.7%) of [pre] / [post] templates with no qualifier-word flag; matches the empirical 14/200 (7%) 1-morph junk in the validation 200-name run for both proportions and vector modes. Fix: drop the len(struct_key) <= 1 early-return so the existing _is_ungrammatical_word_template predicate applies to single-word structures too. title: kenning: explainer tiebreaker picks semantically-wrong parse when context favors a different sense
description:
Multiple etymons share a usage_key in the bundle and the canonical-decomposition picker chooses by list-index order (D29) rather than by semantic fit. Real examples surfaced during user QA:

* 'Eastmoter' → 'East + mot[word, Old French] + er' wins. But 'mot' also has an OE 'mōtere' [Assembly/Council/Meeting place] sense in the bundle, which is what English place-names with -mote/-moot actually mean (folkmoot, witenagemot). The matcher picked the French/modern-English row instead of the OE place-name sense.
* 'Tallage Tres' → 'Tall-' rendered as 'there' (Celtic). May be technically correct for Celtic but doesn't read as 'tall' in an English-speaker context.
* See also wyrd-v4rc: 'Mine-' picks slope over mineral-extraction.

Root cause: D29 trie matcher's canonical_decomposition (singular) tiebreaker is 'list-index of the first matched element; ties beyond that fall back to meaning_db insertion order'. There's no context-aware ranking — e.g., 'when generating English-flavored names, prefer the OE / wiktionary-EN-attested sense over the wiktionary-FR sense'.

Fix options:
1. Cohesion-aware tiebreaker: per-culture preference (English generation → favor OE/EN over OF/FR ties). Requires the picker to know the generation culture context, which it doesn't today.
2. Surface alternatives in the explainer: instead of picking ONE parse, show the top 2-3 with confidence markers so the user can pick.
3. Per-morpheme curation list: 'Mot- in English place-name context → Assembly, override the tiebreaker'.

Captured during user QA pass on the post-d90t generator. Connects to wyrd-m2ym (single-char) + wyrd-v4rc (Mine-) as part of a broader decomposer/explainer quality theme.
design:
IMPLEMENTATION DESIGN (position-partitioning, investigated 2026-05-29)

== Root cause (confirmed in code) ==
Meaning._set_location (runtime/meaning.py:259-265) classifies BARE keys (no
dashes) as 'post' via its else-branch. So bare keys and genuine post-keys are
INDISTINGUISHABLE. Because the trie's _location_allows treats post as
'end==word_length' (trie_matcher.py:258), and a single full-word match
satisfies end==word_length, post-shaped keys (e.g. '-park') match standalone
single-token words. get_lone_samples (word.py:64-70) then adds them to the
single-word proportion bucket → the sampler can pick '-park' (suffix form) for
a standalone word slot.

== Blast radius — WHY this needs a proportions rebuild ==
Meaning.key() (meaning.py: key=[self.location]+...) and Word.get_structure()
(word.py:72-83) BOTH bake .location into:
  (1) the MeaningGenerator bucket keys (generators dict, proportions.py:227+)
  (2) the structure encoding that drives which structures get sampled
These are PERSISTED in the per-culture proportions tables / L4 runtime DB.
Changing _set_location to emit a distinct 'bare' location changes every bare
key's bucket key ('post'→'bare') AND the structure tuples for bare words.
The existing proportions tables were built with bare==post, so post-change the
generator would look for ('bare',) buckets/structures that don't exist in the
current tables → generation falls back / breaks. ANY change to bucket contents
(even just filtering get_lone_samples to bare-only) likewise shifts the tables.
=> The code change is COUPLED to a full proportions regeneration
   (rebuild-proportions per culture) + L4 runtime DB rebuild. Operator-owned.

== Two-site code change ==
1. runtime/meaning.py _set_location: add 4th branch — bare (no dashes) →
   location='bare' (new), distinct from 'post'.
2. runtime/trie_matcher.py _location_allows: 'bare' → return True (valid at any
   position); pre/post/inner unchanged. (_location_for default stays 'inner'
   for synthetic fixtures lacking .location.)
3. Builder partitioning (word.py get_lone_samples / get_samples OR the
   proportions_builder populate loop): single buckets accept ONLY bare-shape;
   pre/inner/post buckets match their location. Likely falls out naturally once
   'bare' is its own location (single words are bare → ('bare','single')
   bucket; '-park' is post → can't land in the single/bare bucket).
4. Verify Meaning.key()/get_structure() now separate bare from post cleanly.

== Sequencing (the decision) ==
Because output changes, the safe sequence is:
  a. land code change behind the new 'bare' location
  b. operator runs rebuild-proportions for ALL cultures + rebuilds L4 DB
  c. validate generation: spot-check that standalone words no longer get
     suffix-form morphemes (the '-park' case), and run drift-report /
     diff-bundle to confirm no broad regression vs the pre-change baseline
  d. CI tests pin the partition invariants (bare valid anywhere; dash-marked
     rejected from single buckets) against fixtures, independent of the rebuild

== Tests to add ==
- _set_location: bare→'bare', pre/post/inner unchanged.
- _location_allows: 'bare' returns True at start/mid/end.
- builder: a post/inner usage matching a single-token word does NOT enter the
  single/bare bucket; a bare usage does.
- Meaning.key()/get_structure(): bare word encodes ('bare',) not ('post',).

Files: runtime/meaning.py, runtime/trie_matcher.py, runtime/word.py,
runtime/proportions.py, lexicon/proportions_builder.py. Tests:
test_kenning_proportions.py, test_kenning_runtime_db_proportions.py, +
new test_kenning_location_partition.py.
notes:
User caught a deeper architectural issue: SPA already consumes morphemes_by_word from generation (added by wyrd-cp2d, plumbed through InspectorColumn / pipeline / rewind / swap / snapshots — confirmed via grep). So the SPA isn't re-deriving via trie for the morpheme display; it's faithfully reporting whatever the GENERATOR picked. Which means the wrong picks ARE coming from the proportions sampler itself, not from the explainer. Bug is upstream — the generator picks position-incorrect dash-shaped keys (e.g. '-park' for a standalone single-word generation).

Same architectural fix needed at both sites because both consult the same position-mismatched bundle data:

1. Generator side (rebuild-proportions emit): partition morphemes by dash-shape (bare / pre- / -post / -inner-); reject cross-shape membership in proportion buckets. Single_usages should ONLY contain bare-form keys. Per-structure-position usages should match the location annotation (pre→pre-marked or bare, post→-post-marked or bare, inner→-inner- only).

2. Runtime trie (Name.find_meaning): same partitioning, consult only the position-appropriate partition based on where in the input we are. Bare-shape keys are valid at any single-token position; dash-marked keys are valid ONLY at their corresponding position. This is a build-time partitioning change on the trie input set, not a runtime ranking change.

The dash convention is already explicit + machine-checkable in every morpheme key. This is plumbing, not a hard correctness call.

title: kenning: explainer should tag personal-name morphemes (Giles, etc.) instead of empty-gloss
description:
'Gileston' decomposes as 'Giles + ton' where 'Giles' surfaces with empty gloss + empty language attribution. Should instead be flagged as a personal name (Latin Aegidius via Norman French; common in saint-dedicated places + manorial holdings — 'Giles' family or 'St Giles' dedications).

Norman manorial families synthesis (wyrd-8s71) handles this for Norman surnames (Cary, Lacy, Mandeville, etc.) but Giles isn't in that list — it predates Norman conquest as a saint's name (Saint Giles / Aegidius).

The bundle currently has 'Giles-' as a morpheme with empty meaning + empty language. Two fix paths:
A. Mine personal-name etymologies separately and tag them as such (Saints + Norman families + Anglo-Saxon personal names). The explainer surfaces 'Giles [personal name: Saint Giles / Aegidius, Latin]' instead of empty.
B. Simpler: maintain a hand-curated saint/personal-name list (like norman_manorial_families.json) and have the explainer prefer that classification over an empty-meaning morpheme.

User caught: 'Gileston has Giles- ton. presumably giles is a name, it doesn't call that out'.

title: kenning: Mine- morpheme conflates 4 unrelated etymologies + missing modern 'mine' (extractive)
description:
The 'Mine-' / '-mine' / 'mine' morphemes in the bundle have 4 distinct etymologies grouped or stacked confusingly:

  1. 'Mint' (plant) — OE 'minte'
  2. 'a slope / inflection of mīn / my' — OE 'mine' — THE 'mīn' (possessive 'my') and 'mine' (slope) senses are conflated into one Meaning row — distinct etymologies wiktionary lumped together
  3. 'smooth field' — Celtic 'mine' (Joyce 1898/1913)
  4. 'Estuary / mouth of a river' — Old Scandinavian 'mynni'

Modern English 'mine' (mineral extraction, from Old French mine ← Gaulish *mēnā) is NOT in the corpus. So a user asking why 'Mine-' parses as 'slope' has no good answer.

Two fixes:
A. Data: mine the modern English 'mine' (extractive) etymology + add it as a separate Meaning. Disambiguate the OE 'mīn' / 'mine' conflation in the source row (probably a wiktionary-empirical multi-sense merge).
B. Explainer: when multiple unrelated meanings stack on one usage_key, surface the disambiguation rather than rendering them as a comma list ('a slope / inflection of mīn: / my').

User context: this came up when a generated name 'Mineingeler' surfaced 'mine = slope' which doesn't match the English-speaker expectation.

title: kenning: single-char ASCII morphemes pollute decompositions ('Clifts' → 'Clift + s [Egyptian]')
description:
The bundle has 430 single-character morphemes, including bare-ASCII Egyptian phonograms (s, t, n, m, h, j, p, w, z) and Akkadian (u, ī). Every English word containing those characters at a position boundary picks up a phantom morpheme attribution. Example: 'Clifts' decomposes as 'Clift + s' where 's' is an Egyptian etymon with empty gloss; 'Lift' decomposes as 'l + ift' etc.

The data is correct upstream (Egyptian hieroglyphs ARE single-consonant signs per wave-2 wiktextract mining) but the runtime trie matcher (D29) doesn't filter for it.

Fix options:
1. At trie-build time: exclude morphemes <2 chars whose canonical form is bare-ASCII Latin script. Keeps non-Latin single-char morphemes (Sanskrit Devanagari, Hebrew niqqud).
2. At bundle-export time: skip single-char morphemes from Egyptian/Akkadian whose canonical_form contains only [a-z] (transliterations that collide with English).
3. At canonical-decomposition picker: penalize parses containing <2-char morphemes during the tiebreaker.

Option 2 cleanest — drops ~30 collision-prone morphemes from the bundle. Option 1 most flexible. File for reviewer call.

title: kenning: replace meanings.json bundle with SQLite-on-S3, download on Lambda cold start
description:
# Replace meanings.json + proportions JSON files with a SQLite runtime DB shipped via S3

**Trigger**: post-wyrd-wz82 bundle re-emit grew meanings.json from 54MB → 113MB, exceeding GitHub's 100MB push limit. Growth driven by `*_phonological_vector` fields landing on every form (wyrd-kq7w.1 enrichment). Decision: the JSON-bundle era for kenning runtime data is over.

This work jettisons ALL JSON data files from the kenning runtime path (meanings.json + 5 per-culture proportions.json) and replaces them with a single SQLite DB downloaded from S3 on Lambda cold start.

## Why SQLite-on-S3 (not other options)

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| Keep JSON, use git-lfs | Doesn't fix cold-start parse cost, growing memory footprint, or queryability. Pure size workaround. |
| SQLite bundled in Lambda container image | Couples data updates to code deploys — the exact problem we're solving. |
| DynamoDB / NoSQL | Network hop per request, schema gymnastics, $ per read; wrong shape for static read-only data. |
| Aurora / RDS | VPC cold-start penalty, ENI management, ops overhead; overkill for read-only generator data. |
| EFS mount | Lambda cold-start mount cost, throughput limits, more infra. |

SQLite-on-S3 is the **pfsrd2-data-api pattern** already in production at 521 (see top-level CLAUDE.md). Same shop, same problem class, working solution. Decouples data lifecycle from code lifecycle.

## L4 schema (canonical)

Two design principles:
- **Blob columns where the row IS the unit of consumption** (meanings, fantasy morphemes, decompositions). No payoff to normalizing internal structure when the runtime always fetches the whole row.
- **Normalized columns where SQL operates on the values** (proportions sampling, statistics lookups). Cumulative sums precomputed at emit time for O(log n) weighted random.

```sql
-- ===== Meanings (denormalized blob) =====
CREATE TABLE meaning (
    usage_key        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- modern_usage, e.g. '-ham-'
    primary_language TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'old-english', 'old-norse', ...
    stratum          TEXT,                    -- nullable; some morphemes lack one
    data             BLOB NOT NULL            -- JSON: full Meaning payload (forms, IPA, vectors)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_meaning_language ON meaning(primary_language);
CREATE INDEX idx_meaning_stratum  ON meaning(stratum);

CREATE TABLE fantasy_morpheme (
    usage_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    data      BLOB NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE canonical_decomposition (
    toponym_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    culture      TEXT NOT NULL,
    elements     BLOB NOT NULL,               -- ordered JSON list of elements
    PRIMARY KEY (toponym_name, culture)
);

-- ===== Proportions (normalized, SQL-sampled) =====
-- Three sampled distributions. Cumulative precomputed at emit time so
-- runtime weighted-random is an O(log n) index seek: roll a random
-- integer in [1, MAX(cumulative)], index-seek first row whose
-- cumulative >= roll.

CREATE TABLE proportions_usage (
    culture    TEXT NOT NULL,
    usage_key  TEXT NOT NULL,
    weight     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cumulative INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (culture, cumulative)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_proportions_usage_by_key ON proportions_usage(culture, usage_key);

CREATE TABLE proportions_single_usage (
    culture    TEXT NOT NULL,
    usage_key  TEXT NOT NULL,
    weight     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cumulative INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (culture, cumulative)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_proportions_single_usage_by_key ON proportions_single_usage(culture, usage_key);

CREATE TABLE proportions_structure (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    culture    TEXT NOT NULL,
    template   BLOB NOT NULL,                 -- JSON: nested 'words' template
    weight     INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cumulative INTEGER NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (culture, cumulative)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_proportions_structure_sample ON proportions_structure(culture, cumulative);

-- Two statistics tables: point lookups, no sampling.
CREATE TABLE proportions_tag_marginal (
    culture TEXT NOT NULL,
    tag     TEXT NOT NULL,
    weight  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (culture, tag)
);

CREATE TABLE proportions_tag_cooccurrence (
    culture TEXT NOT NULL,
    tag1    TEXT NOT NULL,
    tag2    TEXT NOT NULL,
    weight  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (culture, tag1, tag2)
);

-- ===== Operational =====
CREATE TABLE bundle_metadata (
    key   TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    value TEXT
);
-- Rows: schema_version, built_at, source_lexicon_db_hash, source_corpus_hash, emitter_version, ...
```

## Sampling pattern (replaces Python random.choices on loaded dict)

```python
def sample_weighted(conn, table, culture, rng):
    total = conn.execute(
        f"SELECT MAX(cumulative) FROM {table} WHERE culture = ?",
        (culture,),
    ).fetchone()[0]
    roll = rng.randint(1, total)
    row = conn.execute(
        f"SELECT usage_key FROM {table} "
        f"WHERE culture = ? AND cumulative >= ? "
        f"ORDER BY cumulative LIMIT 1",
        (culture, roll),
    ).fetchone()
    return row[0]
```

Two index seeks per sample. No data loaded into Python beyond the sampled row. Memory footprint is just SQLite page cache for hot pages. NameGenerator init becomes cheap — the DB IS the lookup table.

## Loader contract

```python
# wyrd/generators/kenning/runtime/runtime_db.py
def get_runtime_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Process-wide read-only connection. Lazy. Reused across warm Lambda
    invocations. First-call resolution order:

      1. WYRD_RUNTIME_DB env var (absolute local path) — local dev / tests
      2. /tmp/wyrd-runtime.db if present AND HEAD on s3://... shows matching ETag
      3. Download s3://{WYRD_RUNTIME_DB_BUCKET}/{key from current.json pointer}
         to /tmp/wyrd-runtime.db, record ETag in /tmp/wyrd-runtime.etag
      4. Repo-shipped seed DB (wyrd/generators/kenning/data/seed-runtime.db)
         as last-resort fallback for tests + dev without AWS creds.
      5. Open with file:...?mode=ro URI, return.
    """
```

Key invariants:
- **Lazy**: import-time is free; first runtime call triggers connection.
- **Idempotent + warm-reuse**: once opened, connection lives for container's lifetime.
- **Read-only**: `file:/tmp/wyrd-runtime.db?mode=ro` URI; physical guarantee.
- **ETag-checked every cold start**: HEAD on S3 (~10ms), download only if /tmp mismatches.

## S3 layout

```
s3://521studios-{env}-kenning-runtime/
├── current.json                          # {"key": "v/2026-05-24T05Z.db", "etag": "..."}
└── v/
    ├── 2026-05-24T05Z.db                 # immutable, versioned
    ├── 2026-05-25T11Z.db
    └── ...
```

Versioned keys give:
- Rollback = `aws s3 cp current.json` from prior version
- A/B = staging on v+1 while prod stays on v
- History = past versions queryable for forensics

## Local dev story

**Mixed model:**
- **Seed DB** committed to repo at `wyrd/generators/kenning/data/seed-runtime.db` — small (~5-10MB), schema-correct, sufficient for unit tests + default `wyrd kenning generate` without AWS creds.
- **WYRD_RUNTIME_DB env override** points at any full DB (typically `~/.wyrd/runtime.db` after `wyrd kenning sync-runtime`) when serious local work needs the full corpus.

Seed DB regeneration: a `lexicon export-runtime-db --dev` flag emits a fixed-criterion subset from the local lexicon.db (top N usages per culture by weight, plus all referenced meanings, plus all fantasy_morpheme + canonical_decomposition deps). Deterministic so re-running yields the same output; CI can verify the committed seed matches.

Unit tests use the seed DB directly (no S3, no env var). Existing tests-use-fixtures convention is preserved — fixtures can construct ad-hoc runtime DBs in tmp_path when they need to test specific shapes.

## PR sequence

| # | What | Notes |
|---|------|-------|
| 1 | L4 schema + `lexicon export-runtime-db` emitter | Schema CREATE statements; emitter reads lexicon.db + 5 proportions JSON files + canonical_decompositions, writes the L4 DB. Tests round-trip a known meaning + sampled proportion. No consumers yet. |
| 2 | `lexicon export-runtime-db --dev` flag + commit seed DB | Deterministic dev-subset emit; commit the resulting `seed-runtime.db` to repo. Tests verify committed seed matches a fresh `--dev` emit (drift detection). |
| 3 | `bin/publish-runtime-db.sh` uploader | Per-env S3, versioned keys, updates `current.json` atomically. Manual CLI. Mirrors `pfsrd2-automation/bin/pf2_build_index` shape. |
| 4 | `runtime/runtime_db.py` loader | Lazy connection, ETag cache, env override, seed-DB fallback. Tests mock S3 + use tmp-path DB. |
| 5 | `load_meanings` SQLite path + feature flag | Behind `WYRD_USE_RUNTIME_DB=1` initially. Existing meaning tests parametrize over both backends, assert identical Meaning objects. |
| 6 | NameGenerator / proportions SQL-sampled refactor | Convert `random.choices` calls to SQL-sampled. Same feature flag. Validate determinism with same seed → same name across both backends. |
| 7 | Staging vector validation | Run vector-mode generation in staging against the SQLite path. Compare to proportions baseline. **This is the original goal — testing vectors in AWS.** |
| 8 | Default-on cutover + delete JSON bundles | Flip feature flag default, remove meanings.json + 5 proportions.json from build-lambda.sh, delete from repo, update terraform for S3 read perms on the Lambda role. |

PR 8 is the irrevocable one. PR 7 is where the decision-grade evaluation happens.

## Decisions locked

1. **All JSON data files jettisoned** (meanings.json + 5 proportions.json) — not just meanings.
2. **Schema split**: blobs for row-as-unit-of-consumption (meaning/fantasy_morpheme/canonical_decomposition); normalized columns for SQL-sampled distributions (proportions_*).
3. **Cumulative precomputed at emit time** for O(log n) weighted random sampling.
4. **ETag check every cold start** (HEAD on S3, ~10ms).
5. **Local dev = seed DB in repo + WYRD_RUNTIME_DB env override** for full DB.
6. **Cold-start budget 1-2s** accepted for in-region 113MB download.
7. **S3 layout = versioned keys + current.json pointer** for rollback / A/B.

## What this does NOT cover (filed elsewhere if needed)

- **SPA bundle delivery**: if the SPA loads meanings.json directly today, that's a parallel cutover (CloudFront-served runtime DB or different format). Check before PR 8.
- **Phonological vector queries**: vector cosine similarity stays Python-computed for now (vectors are in the JSON blob alongside the form they describe). If we ever want SQL-driven vector queries, that's a future schema migration.
- **Mining DB updates**: orthogonal — mining still flows into lexicon.db, which feeds the L4 emitter.

title: kenning: semantic-coherence audit CLI (phase 1 of audit epic)
description:
Phase 1 of the semantic-coherence audit epic. Build a CLI that scans the bundle and produces two suspect CSVs for human review.

SCOPE:
- New file: wyrd/generators/kenning/cli/lexicon/audit_semantic_coherence.py
- CLI: 'wyrd kenning lexicon audit-semantic-coherence --output-dir audit/'
- Reads meanings.json from the bundled location (or --meanings flag override)
- Uses Ollama embeddings (default http://10.5.2.31:11434, model nomic-embed-text; --ollama-url + --model overrides)
- For each subject's words, embed the gloss list as a single doc per (subject, source_lang) entry
- Per modern_usage bucket: compute pairwise cosine sim across siblings; per sibling, avg sim to bucket-mates
- Per entry: compute pairwise cosine sim across glosses; avg intra-entry coherence
- Homonym signal: for each entry, list other source-language lemmas in the same bucket
- Emit two CSVs sorted asc by similarity:
  - cross-sibling-suspects.csv: bucket pollution candidates
  - intra-entry-suspects.csv: internally-incoherent entries
- Progress reporting per the project's mining convention (every ~10 records, final summary, s/entry rate)

NON-GOALS for this PR:
- No auto-split, no bundle modification
- No SPA changes
- The audit produces reports; the operator reviews; later phases act on the reports

DELIVERABLES: CLI, 2 CSVs ready to eyeball, sample run on current bundle showing top-20 suspects per CSV

title: [EPIC] kenning lexicon: semantic-coherence audit + future split tool
description:
User-asked 2026-05-22 after wyrd-hitl shipped: how do we systematically catch other cluster-pollution / mismatched-meaning cases like 'Hill→cyln'?

Surface-similarity audit (proposed) was discarded in favor of SEMANTIC coherence — sound changes (Grimm's Law, Great Vowel Shift, Norman s/c/k flips) make surface unreliable. 'Ceaster→chester' is a real cognate surface-similarity barely catches; conversely two surface-similar words can be unrelated.

DESIGN (full thread):

Phase 1 — semantic-coherence audit CLI (THIS EPIC, child ticket below):
- Per-bucket pairwise cosine similarity over meaning-gloss embeddings
- Inter-sibling audit: which siblings in a usage bucket don't fit
- Intra-entry audit: which entries have semantically distant glosses (potential undetected homonymy)
- Homonym signal column: same_surface_other_lemmas (distinguishes split-homonym-already-correct polysemy like 'beran=carry/birth/tolerate' from undetected-homonym like a missing 'bera' for animal-bear)
- Decision matrix:
  - low coherence + non-empty other-lemmas → polysemy within already-split homonyms; LEAVE
  - low coherence + empty other-lemmas → likely missing homonym; SPLIT (with help, manual)
  - high coherence → coherent entry; LEAVE
- Embeddings: Ollama nomic-embed-text on user's macbook (10.5.2.31:11434)
- Output: CSV per audit, sorted asc by similarity (lowest = most suspect)
- Report-only first pass — no auto-split, no auto-suppress

Phase 2 — split-subject tool (separate ticket, depends on phase 1 review):
- Operator-driven CLI takes a suspect entry ID + gloss-partition assignment
- Emits two new subject entries with the same surface key + different source-lemma assignments
- Deprecates the original

Phase 3 — regression-test suite (separate ticket, parallel to phase 1):
- Pin ~15 canonical morphemes (Hill, Town, Bridge, Ford, Stone, Green, Wood, Ham, etc.) with expected top-ranked etymons
- CI test that bundle regen produces the expected etymon for each
- Cheap insurance against future regens accidentally undoing today's wins

title: Revert OllamaClient num_ctx default from 16384 back to 8192 (mining-throughput regression)
description:
**Reverts the round-3 bump from PR #327 wyrd-dyf8.**

**Concrete failure 2026-05-22**: After PR #327 shipped with num_ctx=16384 (Gemini round-3 P2 to cover hypothetical truncation on the single-tier miner's 20000-char chunks), staged miner throughput regressed from ~33s/chunk (8K context, pre-outage) to ~102s/chunk (16K context, post-fix). 2-3x inference cost — gemma4:26b's KV-cache scan scales with allocated context. Mining at 102s/chunk projects to ~5 days for the remaining 23 sources vs ~2 days at 8K.

**Why the bump was over-cautious**:
- Staged miner uses 3000-char chunks (~750 tokens). Its actual context usage maxes around 2000 tokens. 8K is right-sized.
- The single-tier \`mine-toponym-mentions\` CLI defaults to 20000-char chunks but is NOT used for production mining. Its hypothetical truncation concern was Gemini's speculation, not a current issue.
- A caller with known-large chunks can override at OllamaClient construction time.

**Fix**: revert num_ctx default to 8192. Update docstring + test assertion. The single-tier caller's hypothetical truncation concern is documented in the docstring as a known limitation; if it becomes a real production issue, a future PR can make num_ctx CLI-configurable per-caller.

**Acceptance**:
- num_ctx default is 8192
- Test asserts 8192 in the request payload
- Docstring acknowledges the trade-off (right-sized for staged miner; single-tier callers may need to override)
notes: Merged via PR #332 (squash). num_ctx default 16384 → 8192 restored. Empirical pace was 102s/chunk at 16K, expected ~33-48s/chunk at 8K.

title: kenning structure: slot constraints not respected — suffix morphemes (-by) placed in prefix slot, produces ungrammatical two-word names ('By Green')
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22 in SPA testing with scoring_mode=proportions (default — vector mode is wyrd-t70w broken):

EVIDENCE: result 'By Green' decomposed as '-by · green-'.
- '-by' is the Old Norse settlement suffix (Whitby, Grimsby, Selby, Derby). Leading dash = suffix slot only.
- 'green-' has trailing dash = prefix slot only.
- Composed with the WRONG slot ordering → 'By Green' as two words instead of 'Greenby' as one word.

SCOPE OF BUG (need to confirm in code):
- Are slot constraints encoded in the morpheme data (the dash position is the canonical signal) but the structural composer ignores them?
- Or is the composer slot-agnostic by design (picks N morphemes for N slots without per-morpheme constraint matching)?
- Are 'two-word names' a deliberate structure type? Genuine British place names can be two words ('Stoke Mandeville', 'Newton Abbot', 'Burton upon Trent') but those have specific patterns; '-by' is never word 1.

LIKELY ROOT: structures.yaml (or wherever structure templates live) picks morphemes from pools without filtering by slot. Need to filter prefix-slot morphemes (trailing dash) to prefix positions and suffix-slot morphemes (leading dash) to suffix positions per structure template.

WORKAROUND: none from user side; produces ungrammatical names.

RELATED: wyrd-hitl corpus-quality epic. The data-quality fixes for Meanings won't fix this — it's a structural-composition bug, separate code path. But once data is clean, structural bugs become more visible (no longer hidden by the 'meaning shown is wrong anyway' noise).

title: wyrd: seed precision lost over JSON — copy/paste seed from result yields different name
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22: copying the seed displayed in the result meta + pasting into the Header's seed input → next Roll produces a DIFFERENT name. Should reproduce the exact result.

ROOT: wyrd/app.py:90 generates seeds via seed_rng.randrange(2**63) — up to ~9.2×10^18. JSON Number → JS Number has only 2^53 (~9×10^15) safe-integer precision. The displayed seed is already truncated on receive; copying back sends a different value.

FIX OPTIONS:
A. Server: cap seeds at 2**53 (safe for JS Number). Simplest; no API change; still ~9 quadrillion possibilities (plenty).
B. Server: send seed as string (preserves precision; SPA parses BigInt on display).
C. SPA: BigInt handling throughout (display + input + payloads).

RECOMMEND A — cap at 2**53 — no API change, smallest blast radius.

Surfaces in BOTH the seed-copy UX AND the wyrd-tz35 share-link / wyrd-34tn save-load flows (loaded saves with pre-cap seeds would reproduce wrong).

Likely root: tags are assigned at cluster level (all etymological-cluster mates share tags) but cluster members have heterogeneous semantic categories. OR an automated tagging pass got noisy.

EVIDENCE: third user-observed corpus-data issue today (after wyrd-aizb alt-form redirects + wyrd-... semantic-vs-derivative split). Cumulative signal that the meanings.json data needs a tag-quality audit.

PROPOSAL: audit pass that flags tag-vs-meanings mismatches. Heuristics:
- If tags include 'animal' but no meaning contains animal/mammal/bird/etc words → suspect
- Tag clusters that span unrelated semantic domains → suspect
- Cross-reference morpheme tags against the tags of the words containing each meaning (if Wiktionary categorizes those)

Could be a lexicon CLI tool: 'wyrd kenning lexicon audit-tags' that emits a report of suspect morphemes for hand-review.

title: kenning lexicon: separate semantic-meaning text from morphological-derivative text
description:
User-reported 2026-05-22: morpheme '-sing-' shows meaning 'singular imperative of singan' — that's a morphological derivation (grammatical conjugation pointing at the lemma), not a semantic gloss. Same family as wyrd-aizb (alt-form redirects).

Wiktionary glosses for inflected/derived forms commonly include both:
- the SEMANTIC meaning ('sing', 'song', 'to sing')
- the MORPHOLOGICAL derivative text ('singular imperative of singan', 'past tense of run', 'genitive of dom')

The corpus miner ingests them verbatim into one meanings[] list. SPA / CLI / explainer all show the verbatim mix.

FIX: at mining time, classify each gloss as semantic vs derivative:
- 'singular imperative of X', 'past tense of X', 'genitive of X', 'inflection of X', 'alternative form of X' (wyrd-aizb), 'plural of X', etc → derivative
- everything else → semantic
- For SPA display: prefer semantic glosses; fall back to (or supplement with) the derivative text resolved through the lemma reference X.

Schema delta: meanings[] → { semantic: [...], derivative: [...] } OR a per-gloss type tag. Backwards-compat path: keep flat meanings[] but add derivatives[] alongside.

Related to wyrd-aizb (alt-form redirects — same rabbit hole, different gloss pattern). Both should probably ship together as a 'normalize meaning text' bundle pass.

title: OllamaClient should set explicit num_ctx in options (config drift hazard)
description:
**Problem**: \`OllamaClient.chat_json\` in \`wyrd/generators/kenning/extractors/llm.py\` only sets \`temperature\` in the request's \`options\` dict. It doesn't override \`num_ctx\`, so the actual context window allocated for inference depends on whatever Ollama loaded the model with — which is environment-dependent (Ollama version, env vars, prior requests, model defaults).

**Concrete failure 2026-05-22**: A macbook reboot caused Ollama to reload gemma4:26b with \`num_ctx: 262144\` (the model's absolute max). Our chunks are ~750 tokens. Inference time degraded from ~33s/chunk (healthy) to ~90s/chunk (2.7x slower) because every inference traversed a 262K KV cache instead of the previously-allocated smaller one. Mining throughput halved overnight without any code change.

**Fix**: Set \`options.num_ctx\` explicitly. A safe value for our use case is 8192 (accommodates 3000-char chunks + system prompt + headroom; covers all current sources). The value should probably be a constant/CLI flag rather than a magic number.

\`\`\`python
"options": {
    "temperature": self.temperature,
    "num_ctx": 8192,
},
\`\`\`

**Acceptance**:
- OllamaClient sends \`num_ctx\` on every request
- Mining throughput is stable across Ollama restarts / version changes
- A regression test asserts \`num_ctx\` is in the request payload
- INGESTION.md documents the chosen value + rationale

**Why P2**: silent throughput halving with no operator-visible cause is a real ops hazard. The wall-clock cost of the current outage is hours of mining time on a ~4-day run.
notes: Merged via PR #327 (squash). 4-round review loop with convergent findings from 6 agents + Gemini.

title: Staged miner promotes 0-byte canonical file when all chunks fail (chunks_processed=0)
description:
**Symptom**: When every chunk of a source fails (e.g. provider unreachable for the duration), the staged miner's atomic-write merge step at the end of \`_run_fresh_mining\` produces a 0-byte canonical file at \`data/mining/phase2/<source>.jsonl\`. On the next run, \`--skip-existing\` treats this file as "done" and skips the source — the 0 mentions are now the permanent record for that source.

**Concrete failure 2026-05-22**: Ollama on the macbook (10.5.2.31:11434) lost power mid-run. The staged miner advanced through 12 sources (slices 31-42 of the corpus queue) with every chunk failing "No route to host" / errno 113. All 12 produced 0-byte canonical files. The 13th (slice 43) was caught with an empty inprogress before promotion. Mining was killed and the 13 empties were deleted by hand so a restart picks them up correctly.

**Reproduction**:
1. Disable network to the provider
2. Run \`wyrd kenning lexicon mine-toponym-mentions-staged --skip-existing\`
3. Observe that sources where every chunk fails produce 0-byte canonical files
4. Re-enable network, restart with --skip-existing
5. The empty-source-jsonl is treated as "done" and skipped — silent data loss

**Fix scope**:
1. In \`_run_fresh_mining\` (\`mine_toponym_mentions_staged.py\` around line 555 — the \`tmp_path.replace(out_path)\` atomic-write site), skip the atomic-write entirely if \`report.chunks_processed == 0 AND report.mentions is empty AND no pre-existing canonical file existed\`. Keep the inprogress around so the operator sees the failure state.
2. OR: write a sentinel/marker on the canonical path that --skip-existing recognizes as "needs retry" (less ideal — more complex).
3. Either way: emit a per-source warning so operators see "this source had 0 successful chunks" rather than a silent zero.
4. Add a regression test: mock client that raises on every chunk; assert the canonical file is NOT created OR is recognizably-incomplete.

**Acceptance**:
- A source where every chunk fails leaves no 0-byte canonical file behind.
- The next \`--skip-existing\` run retries that source.
- Operator-visible warning surface (CLI summary mentions the gap).

**Why P2**: pre-existing silent data loss whenever the provider has any sustained outage. The current crash-safety (wyrd-w7i3) protects against per-process interruption but not provider unreachability.
notes: Merged via PR #327 (squash). 4-round review loop with convergent findings from 6 agents + Gemini.

title: kenning: deterministic IPA → reader_pronunciation field in to_dict()
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-cp2d. The JSON continuity flow now carries IPA per morpheme (round 3 of PR #305), but most non-linguist readers can't parse '/xɑːm/' or '/byrjj/'. The bundle's english_shaped field is defined in the schema but has ZERO populated entries for British place-name morphemes; the irish_anglicizations.json sidecar only covers ~10 Irish prefixes.

FIX: deterministic IPA → reader-friendly pronunciation mapping. New helper anglicize_ipa(ipa: str) -> str | None covering the OE/ME/Welsh/Celtic/OF phonemic inventory:
- x → KH, θ → TH, ð → DH, ʃ → SH, ŋ → NG, ɬ → LL (Welsh)
- t͡ʃ → CH, d͡ʒ → J, ǰ → J
- length marker ː → repeat vowel
- ɑ → AH, æ → A, y → I, œ → EU, ɨ → I, ə → UH
- syllable separator . → ignore; stress markers ˈˌ → ignore
- bracket strip // and []

Surface as new 'reader_pronunciation' key alongside 'ipa' in the renderings slot. Sparse — only emit when ipa is present.

SAMPLES (target output):
- /xɑːm/ → KHAHM
- /wyrm/ → WIRM
- /kumb/ → KUMB
- /byrjj/ → BIRJ
- /æ͜ɑː/ → AH
- /ɬɨ̞n/ → LLIN

User name choice from 2026-05-22 demo session: 'reader_pronunciation' (over say_as / simplified / pronunciation_guide).

title: kenning: --json output for generated names + --from-json input for rewind/era-map (continuity of morpheme picks)
description:
Observed during 2026-05-22 demo: 'Cranwith' generated by the generator. When the user passes the rendered string back to rewind, the trie matcher re-decomposes 'Cranwith' from scratch and picks 'Cran' → OE 'corn' (etymological cluster), producing 'Cornlandian' at OE rather than the actual lemmas the generator used. The morpheme picks the generator made are thrown away when we render to a string.

ARCHITECTURAL FIX: capture the generator's morpheme picks in a JSON document. Downstream steps (rewind, era-map) accept the JSON so they don't have to re-decompose. Webapp side gets the same continuity.

PROPOSED JSON SHAPE (one object per name):
{
  "name": "Cranwith",
  "culture": "english",
  "seed": 100,
  "words": [
    [
      {"usage": "Cran-", "tags": [...], "meanings": [...], "sources": {"old_english": ["crān"]}},
      {"usage": "-with", "tags": [...], "meanings": [...], "sources": {"celtic_mix": ["gwydd"]}}
    ]
  ]
}

CLI CHANGES:
- kenning generate --json: emit JSON instead of text (one JSON object per line, newline-delimited).
- kenning rewind --from-json FILE (or stdin): bypass trie decomposition, use the pre-picked morphemes directly. Anchor + era-reflex pipeline stays the same.
- kenning era-map --from-json: same.

NEW HELPER:
- NewName.to_dict() returning the dict shape (per-word morpheme lists).
- rewind_from_morphemes(words, db, eras) in era.rewind — new entry point that skips the Name + find_meaning step; takes pre-picked morpheme metadata, looks up each in meaning_db by usage, runs the existing _render_morpheme_at_era pipeline.

TESTS:
- generate --json: verify the JSON shape contains per-word morpheme lists with usage + sources.
- rewind --from-json with mismatched name: error loudly.
- rewind --from-json correctly bypasses re-decomposition (use a name where re-decomposition would pick different lemmas, like 'Cranwith' → 'corn' vs the generator's actual 'crān' pick).
- End-to-end: generate --json | rewind --from-json produces a clean ladder for the actual picks.

3. Modern cell picks wrong cognate ('el-ter-ell' for Lowterell — same wyrd-8qbi bug; modern should round-trip 'Lowterell')
4. No surface-form dedup or triple-letter collapse

ROOT CAUSE: KenningRewind.generate_all in wyrd/generators/kenning/generators/kenning_rewind.py is a PARALLEL implementation that doesn't call into era.rewind.rewind_name. It has its own renderer at line 123:
  rendered = '-'.join(m.strip('-') for m in rendered_morphemes if m)

This is the pre-wyrd-085k hyphenated-join. The SPA-facing rewind API (KenningRewind) and the CLI-facing rewind module (era.rewind) duplicate the morpheme-walk + render logic with different implementations, so all 4 recent rewinder fixes (#297, #298, #299, #300) bypass the SPA path.

DOWNSTREAM IMPACT: era-map command (wyrd-381) calls KenningRewind.generate_all internally, so era-map inherits all the old bugs even though rewind CLI has been fixed.

FIX: refactor KenningRewind.generate_all to delegate to era.rewind.rewind_name. Wrap the returned Rewind dataclass back into the GenerationResult list shape KenningRewind expects. Single source of truth for morpheme-walk + render.

OR: keep parallel implementations but factor out the rendering layer into a shared helper that both call.

The first option (delegate) is the cleaner long-term shape; less code duplication.

TESTS:
- Add an integration test that exercises KenningRewind.generate_all and asserts the output matches era.rewind.rewind_name's output for the same input.
- Verify era-map command output uses smart-join + title-case + modern-cell round-trip post-fix.

title: kenning generate: collapse 3+-letter runs at morpheme-join boundaries (Killlen / Alllas / Bronferrrhedyn)
description:
Demo sweep 2026-05-22 across 5 cultures × 50 seeds × 10 names surfaced 12 names with 3+ identical consecutive letters from morpheme-join concatenation:
- Alllas, Balllagh, Ballland (Kill + l-, Ball + l-)
- Bank Vellley, Billley Hill (vell- + l, bill- + l)
- Bonallliesstone (ll + l + ie + ss; double-bug: triple l AND double s join)
- Bronferrrhedyn (rr + r)
- Castleeek, Killlen Baltown, Les Langan Maen Alllac, Millleglan, Nettton

ROOT CAUSE: NewName.__str__ concatenates morphemes by raw string-join (post-wyrd-3xdb's title-case fix). When morpheme A ends in 'll' and morpheme B starts with 'l' (e.g., 'Kill' + 'len' → 'Killlen'), the join produces a triple-letter run that English orthography normally elides ('Killen' is the natural form).

FIX: at the within-word concat step in NewName.__str__, collapse any run of 3+ identical letters down to 2. This is a conservative orthographic normalization that:
- Matches real English/Celtic place-name convention (Killarney NOT Killlarney; Newcastle NOT Newccastle)
- Doesn't affect double-letter morphemes alone (Kill, Ball stay intact)
- Doesn't affect across-word boundaries (the space separates them naturally)
- One regex: re.sub(r'(.)\\1{2,}', r'\\1\\1', joined)

ALTERNATIVE: per-morpheme boundary-aware join (drop one letter when A's last == B's first). More precise but harder to reason about — the 3+-collapse is simpler and gives the same result for the observed cases.

TESTS:
- New: 'Kill' + 'len' → 'Killen' (not 'Killlen')
- 'Ball' + 'l' → 'Ballla' becomes 'Balla'
- 'Newcastle' (already correct) stays 'Newcastle' (no triple)
- Cross-word boundaries: 'Bank Vellley' → 'Bank Velley'
- Sweep: 50 seeds × 5 cultures → zero triple-letter outputs.

title: kenning generate: avoid adjacent slots picking the same morpheme (duplicate-word names like 'North North' / 'Green Green')
description:
Bug observed during 2026-05-22 demo sweep. Running 'wyrd kenning generate <culture> -n 10 --seed <S>' across 5 cultures × 50 seeds surfaces names where the same word repeats in adjacent slots:

- english: 'East East', 'Green Green'
- welsh: 'Pentre Pentre'
- scottish: 'North North'

(More likely across more seeds; the pattern is cardinal directions, descriptors, and language-specific modifier-words like Welsh 'Pentre' = 'village'.)

ROOT CAUSE: NameGenerator picks each slot independently from its bucket. When a structure has 2 adjacent slots that can both hold modifier-words (e.g. [pre, post] = [modifier, modifier-or-head]), the sampler can independently choose the same morpheme for both, producing 'North North'-style outputs. Real medieval place names use modifier repetition (Stratford-on-Avon, Newcastle-upon-Tyne) only for prepositional joins; 'X X' adjacent duplicates aren't attested.

POSSIBLE FIXES (in increasing scope):
(a) Post-render filter: detect adjacent-duplicate words in NewName.__str__ output; elide one or re-render. Hides the symptom.
(b) Per-slot filter at fill time: when sampling slot N, drop morphemes whose modern_usage equals the morpheme just picked at slot N-1. Bounded retry if filter empties the bucket.
(c) Cross-slot cohesion (D17.5 wyrd-mj2 territory): the cohesion knob already biases against tag-incompatible adjacents; extend to anti-bias against identical-morpheme adjacents.

Option (b) is the smallest contained change and the most honest. Adds a one-line filter to the slot-N sampling step plus a fallback (if dedup empties the bucket, fall back to original — better to ship a duplicate than crash).

TESTS:
- Pin that across 50 seeds × 5 cultures, no -n 10 output contains adjacent-duplicate words.
- Unit test: NameGenerator slot N's bucket excludes the morpheme picked at slot N-1.

title: kenning rewind: at modern cell, bypass smart-join to preserve operator's input shape
description:
Post-PR #298 + #297, running 'wyrd kenning rewind Helon Mortborough' now produces:
- english/oe-late  Helde on Mortbyrgen *  (smart-join particle 'on' separated)
- english/me       Helde on Mortburȝen *
- english/modern   Hel on Mortborough *  <-- WRONG (operator typed 'Helon', not 'Hel on')

The OE / ME cells correctly smart-join because that's the historical scribal pattern (Stratford ON Avon style). But the modern cell already short-circuits to canonical (wyrd-8qbi) — the smart-join layered on top splits the operator's input shape.

FIX: at the modern-english target in _render_morphemes_as_name (or a dedicated modern renderer path), concatenate morpheme forms within each word WITHOUT particle-separation. Each space-separated WORD still gets title-cased; the particle logic only applies to OE/ME cells.

Two reasonable implementations:
(a) Add a 'use_smart_join' bool flag to _render_morphemes_as_name, default True; pass False when rendering the modern stop.
(b) Pre-render the modern stop directly in rewind_name (skip the helper).

Option (a) is cleaner — one parameter, threads through cleanly.

EXPECTED post-fix:
- english/modern  Helon Mortborough  (round-trip matches operator input)

TESTS: pin the round-trip-at-modern invariant for inputs with embedded particles ('Helon' -> 'Helon' at modern; 'Stratfordonavon' -> 'Stratfordonavon' at modern). OE / ME cells still smart-join (existing tests cover that path).

title: kenning generate: title-case the first letter of each space-separated word in generated names
description:
Demo run 2026-05-21 showed every -n 10 sample contained at least one all-lowercase output:
- 'ward green'
- 'castle'
- 'holmrwood common'
- 'holes'
- 'end Bargorton'

These are proper-noun place names rendered with the source morphemes' case preserved verbatim — when the picked morphemes happen to all be lowercase suffixes / modifiers (no initial proper-noun morpheme slotted into the first position), the result reads as broken.

ROOT CAUSE: NewName.__str__ in wyrd/generators/kenning/runtime/proportions.py concatenates morpheme strings within a word and joins words with spaces, preserving each morpheme's bundle-source case. The bundle stores pre-modifiers cap'd ('Whit-', 'Ash-') and post-modifiers / inner-modifiers lowercase ('-ham', '-ton', '-ward'). A word constructed entirely from lowercase morphemes lands lowercase in the output.

FIX: title-case the first letter of each space-separated word at the __str__ boundary. Names are proper nouns; they should ALL start with caps. The current behavior leaks bundle-implementation detail.

BEFORE / AFTER:
- 'ward green' -> 'Ward Green'
- 'castle' -> 'Castle'
- 'holmrwood common' -> 'Holmrwood Common'
- 'Hunlock Forest' (already-cased) -> 'Hunlock Forest' (unchanged)

Touch one method (NewName.__str__) at one site. Tests: add a focused unit test pinning the title-case behavior; existing generator tests that assert specific outputs need a sweep to see if any rely on the lowercase-leaked behavior.

This is the symptom-level fix for the broader wyrd-6gj design question (positional bias for modifier words) — wyrd-6gj would prevent these structures from being picked at all; this PR makes the picked structures READ as proper nouns regardless.

title: kenning rewind: modern cell should round-trip the input, not pick cognate mates
description:
Observation from the 2026-05-21 demo: running 'wyrd kenning rewind Elmton' produced:
- english/oe-late  Elmtūn
- english/me       Elmtoun
- english/modern   Amherstton  <-- WRONG

The OE / ME cells are correct (modern Elm -> OE elm -> ME elm). The 'modern' cell, however, runs the cluster-mate picker against modern-english cognates and surfaces 'Amherst' (a place-name derived from 'elm') instead of 'elm' itself. Same pattern across the demo run:
- Bradton -> Bradmoreton
- Cauldlow -> Elbeel
- Whitby -> Whitbournby

ROOT CAUSE: at the modern cell, the morpheme already has its modern form (Meaning.usage = the modern reflex). Running the cognate-cluster picker for modern adds noise rather than information — it picks sibling cognates that happen to share an OE root but aren't the morpheme operator just typed.

FIX: in _render_morpheme_at_era, when target_language is modern-english, short-circuit to the morpheme's canonical (modern_usage with dashes stripped). Skip cluster query. fallback=False (we have a confident answer).

OE / ME / EModE cells stay on the cluster picker — that's where the morpheme's modern form doesn't have era-appropriate data so the cluster lookup IS load-bearing.

EXPECTED post-fix output:
- english/oe-late  Elmtūn
- english/me       Elmtoun
- english/modern   Elmton  <-- round-trips the input cleanly

For invented names too — operator types 'Newburywater', each morpheme's canonical IS the modern form, so the round-trip stays clean.

TESTS:
- Existing test_rewind_renders_morphemes_at_each_era_stop currently asserts modern=='white' (cluster pick); update to whatever canonical resolves to for the test fixture's morpheme.
- New test pinning the modern-cell short-circuit: invented input -> modern cell == join-of-canonicals.

title: kenning rewind: render historical forms as names (smart join: preserve prepositions as separate words)
description:
Today `wyrd kenning rewind` outputs analytical hyphenated morpheme strings like 'helde-on-Mort-byrgen' or 'elm-tūn'. That's right for the explainer use case but not for the operator who asked 'what did this name look like in 1100'. Real medieval scribes wrote single-word compounds with prepositions / particles as separate words: 'Helde on Mortbyrgen', 'Elmtūn'.

DESIGN: smart join, preserves prepositions as separate words (selected from 3 options on 2026-05-21).

ALGORITHM:
- Walk morpheme form list with position info from each morpheme.
- Treat a morpheme as a particle IF its lowercased form is in {on, upon, under, of} AND its position is 'standalone/free' (no leading/trailing hyphen markers in modern_usage). Skip 'by' (ambiguous: preposition vs ON settlement suffix), 'in' (rare in place names), 'at' (rare).
- Particles space-separate; non-particles concatenate directly.
- Title-case first letter of each space-separated token; particles stay lowercase.

BEFORE / AFTER:
- elm-tūn -> Elmtūn
- helde-on-Mort-byrgen -> Helde on Mortbyrgen
- hēafod-croft-west -> Hēafodcroftwest
- mil-worthig-byrgen -> Milworthigbyrgen

The original analytical hyphenated view is still available via 'wyrd kenning explain' (separate command, different use case).

TESTS: existing rewind tests need updating to match the new join style. Add focused tests for: simple two-morpheme join (no particles), preposition-detection ('on' between morphemes), proper-noun morpheme cap-preservation through join, leading-particle edge case.
