title: kenning: commit phase2 mining JSONL artifacts to main + gitignore _inprogress/
description:
## Why this exists

Phase 3a Stage 1 (ollama gemma4:26b) mining is producing per-source JSONL artifacts in data/mining/phase2/. These are durable evidence files that the db-reconstructibility-reviewer rule says MUST be committed (DB reconstructible from JSONL + scripts, no re-mining).

Currently 19+ phase2 sources have completed and their .jsonl outputs sit uncommitted in the main checkout. They need to be committed to main via a PR.

ALSO: the staged-miner crash-safety code (wyrd-w7i3) writes per-chunk fsync'd logs to data/mining/phase2/_inprogress/<source>.chunks.jsonl. These are TRANSIENT artifacts (promoted/discarded by recover-inprogress-chunks). They MUST NOT be committed. A recent accidental commit (e694565, force-push-reverted in this session) included one of these, demonstrating the risk.

## What needs to be done

In a worktree (not main checkout):

1. Add data/mining/phase2/_inprogress/ to .gitignore so the crash-safety logs are never accidentally tracked.

2. Commit the completed data/mining/phase2/*.jsonl artifacts:
   - Use `git add data/mining/phase2/*.jsonl` (NOT -A — that picks up too much)
   - Verify with `git status` that no _inprogress files are staged
   - Commit + PR

3. After PR merges, mining will continue adding new completed sources to data/mining/phase2/. Those can be committed in subsequent PRs at natural milestones (e.g. when a slice batch completes).

## Pointers

- AGENT-REVIEWERS.md db-reconstructibility-reviewer section for the rule
- data/mining/phase2/_inprogress/ for the transient logs
- data/mining/phase2/*.jsonl for the durable artifacts

## Acceptance

- _inprogress/ in .gitignore
- All currently-complete phase2 sources committed to main via PR
- No _inprogress files in the PR's diff

## Followup of

The recovery from the bad e694565 push during the PR #281 review loop.

title: EPIC: real-world loan-profile templates (Latin/Norse/Norman/Mongol/Sanskrit/...) for scenario-pack baselines
description:
Cluster of 14 'real-world loan-profile' tickets that document specific donor → recipient empirical patterns (Old Norse → Old/Middle English, Latin → OE, Norman French → ME, Mongol → Russian, Sanskrit → Hindi/English, Quechua → Spanish, etc.).

Each profile becomes a template for scenario packs: a pack templated on (donor='old-norse', recipient='old-english') inherits ON→OE empirical baselines per D36.4 Option B. The runtime + bundle conventions (ecjp.4 baseline_score_pack + ecjp.10 packs/ manifest format) already accept these; this epic tracks the corpus + template authoring work.

Sub-tickets are the per-profile cards:
- Norse → OE (Danelaw)
- Latin → OE (Roman + ecclesiastical)
- Celtic → OE (substrate)
- Norman French → ME (manorial overlay)
- Mongol → Russian (steppe, Dothraki real-counterpart)
- Sanskrit → Hindi/English (Indo-religious)
- Quechua → Spanish (Andean)
- Algonquian → American English (New England coastal)
- Bantu → Afrikaans/English (Southern African)
- Polynesian → English (Hawaii)
- Slavic → Germanic (Pomerania/Mecklenburg/Brandenburg)
- Akkadian/Semitic → English (Adûnaic dependency)

Doing them as standalone tickets loses the shared-infrastructure pattern; doing them as epic surfaces what the unifying authoring template needs to look like.

title: kenning: add init_schema → build_from_jsonl regression test for fantasy_morpheme
description:
## Why this exists

The wyrd-rrse bug (fantasy_morpheme missing from init_schema-produced DBs) shipped under 848 green tests. The reason: existing fantasy_morpheme tests in tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py use a hand-rolled _build_fixture_db() that creates fantasy_morpheme directly via CREATE TABLE, bypassing init_schema entirely. And the existing test_diff_rebuild_zero_deltas_on_self_rebuild fixture uses only source+etymon JSONL, never triggering INSERT INTO fantasy_morpheme. So the exact crash scenario was untested.

pr-test-analyzer flagged two HIGH gaps on PR #281 review:

1. test_init_schema_creates_tables (tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py:101) doesn't include fantasy_morpheme / personal_name / personal_name_toponym_attestation in its expected set. The expected.issubset(tables) assertion means a future migration could drop these tables entirely and the test would still pass.

2. No end-to-end pin on the actual crash scenario: init_schema fresh DB + build_from_jsonl with a fantasy_morpheme row.

## What needs to be done

### Test 1: enumerate the new tables in test_init_schema_creates_tables

Open tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py:101 and add fantasy_morpheme, personal_name, personal_name_toponym_attestation to the expected set so a future migration that fails to create them fails this test.

### Test 2: end-to-end init_schema + build_from_jsonl pin

Add tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py::test_build_fantasy_morpheme_via_init_schema (or similar name). Test body:

  1. fresh_db via init_schema(tmp_path / "lexicon.db")
  2. Write a _fantasy_morphemes.jsonl with one fantasy_morpheme row
  3. Run build_from_jsonl(conn, [the jsonl path])
  4. Assert one row in fantasy_morpheme, exit code clean

This is the literal crash scenario that broke before PR #281.

### Test 3 (optional): case-insensitive UNIQUE dedup pin

Add a test that pre-populates {"input_name": "Angel", ...} then sends JSONL with {"input_name": "angel", ...} and asserts INSERT OR IGNORE preserves the original casing. Pins the COLLATE NOCASE invariant that PR #281 round-1 added to tables.py.

## Pointers

- wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl/build.py — build_from_jsonl
- wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl/build.py:535-570 — _insert_fantasy_morpheme path
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/schema.py:46 — init_schema
- tests/test_kenning_jsonl_build.py:132 — hand-rolled _build_fixture_db (the gap this addresses)

## Followup of

wyrd-rrse (PR #281)

title: kenning: add SA MetaData ↔ alembic-head parity test (autogen drift canary)
description:
## Why this exists

PR #281 (wyrd-rrse) shipped a fix for two separate cases of the same drift class: alembic migration <-> lexicon/sql/tables.py MetaData going out of sync. The wyrd-uzoh / PR #276 case (personal_name + personal_name_toponym_attestation) went undetected for an entire PR cycle. The wyrd-rrse case (fantasy_morpheme + a residual COLLATE NOCASE drift introduced in the same PR) was caught only by manual audit and skeptic review.

There is no automated check that flags this. Alembic provides one: alembic.autogenerate.compare_metadata returns the set of diffs between a SA MetaData and a live schema. Empty diff = parity.

## What needs to be done

Add a test that builds a fresh DB via init_schema(tmp_path), connects to it, calls alembic.autogenerate.compare_metadata(MigrationContext.configure(conn), tables.metadata), and asserts the returned diff list is empty (or, if pre-existing drift exists across older migrations, allowlist it explicitly with a TODO referencing this ticket).

The test must run on every PR via CI so any new Table() addition that drifts from the matching alembic migration trips immediately.

## Pointers

- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/tables.py — the MetaData source of truth
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/migrations/versions/ — alembic migration chain (currently head=0011)
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/schema.py:46 — init_schema (use for the fresh-DB step)
- tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py head-pin tests at lines 284-313 — same fixture shape this test would use

## Acceptance

- Running the new test against current main passes (zero drift after wyrd-rrse landed).
- Deliberately introducing a drift (e.g. removing the COLLATE NOCASE on fantasy_morpheme.input_name) makes the test fail with a clear diff message naming the affected column/table.

## Followup of

wyrd-rrse (PR #281)

title: Briggs ingest: emit JSONL artifacts + reconstruct from rebuild-from-jsonl (wyrd-uzoh follow-up)
description:
Per the new db-reconstructibility-reviewer (wyrd-fe1v, PR #278), the Briggs ingest path must satisfy the architectural rule:

- The lexicon DB at ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db can be blown away at any time.
- Operators must be able to ``rm db && wyrd kenning lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl`` to restore state.
- No mining (no pdftotext, no re-LLM-calling, no PDF re-fetch) is acceptable as part of reconstruction.

PR #276 shipped the Briggs ingester DB-direct. The .txt source is staged outside the repo; if the DB is wiped, the operator must re-run ingest-briggs-personal-names against the staged PDF→txt extract. Gap.

SCOPE (Option B — single-CLI emit-then-load, matching the future-better pattern in the new reviewer):

1. Extend ``wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl/log.py``:
   - Add ``personal_name`` to KEYED_TYPES (ref = headform)
   - Add ``personal_name_toponym_attestation`` to LIST_TYPES
   - Update ``ReplayState.to_canonical_rows`` for the new types

2. Extend ``wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl/build.py``:
   - Add ``_insert_personal_name`` + ``_insert_personal_name_toponym_attestation`` inserters
   - Wire into pass-2 keyed + pass-3 list dispatch
   - Provide ``personal_name_id_by_headform`` FK lookup map
   - Add to counts dict + the ``DIFF_REBUILD_TABLES`` list

3. Extend ``wyrd/generators/kenning/jsonl/dump.py``:
   - Round-trip personal_name + personal_name_toponym_attestation rows out of the DB so dump→wipe→rebuild→dump is identity for the new tables

4. Refactor ``wyrd/generators/kenning/briggs_personal_names_ingester.py``:
   - The ``ingest_briggs_index`` function now: parse → emit JSONL events to ``data/mining/briggs_2024_personal_names_index.jsonl`` → load that JSONL into DB via the shared build_from_jsonl path
   - JSONL is the on-disk artifact; DB is the queryable index
   - SIGTERM/crash mid-ingest leaves a partial JSONL file that's still loadable (since the JSONL is written linearly + flushed per entry)

5. Update CLI:
   - ``wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-briggs-personal-names <txt> [--db PATH] [--jsonl-out PATH]``
   - Default ``--jsonl-out`` to ``data/mining/briggs_2024_personal_names_index.jsonl``

6. Validate the reconstruction recipe:
   - ``rm ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db && wyrd kenning lexicon init && wyrd kenning lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl`` produces the same DB state, with no .txt re-parse

OUT OF SCOPE (still tracked in wyrd-jac1):
- Tests (parser unit tests, schema parity, idempotent re-ingest assertions, etc.)
- Silent-skip counter plumbing
- Complexity refactor of _parse_entry / _parse_attestations / ingest_briggs_index

RELATES TO: wyrd-uzoh (the shipped DB-direct ingester this PR converts to the JSONL-first pattern), wyrd-fe1v (the new reviewer enforcing the rule), wyrd-jac1 (the test follow-up).
close_reason: Shipped via PR #279. Briggs ingest now JSONL-first; rebuild-from-jsonl restores the rows from the on-disk artifact alone. Satisfies db-reconstructibility-reviewer (which approved this PR on first deployment + caught the unknown-county filter bug at C3).

title: Add db-reconstructibility-reviewer to AGENT-REVIEWERS.md
description:
Architectural rule that has been violated multiple times:

- The lexicon DB MUST be reconstructible at any time from JSONL files + scripts that act on that data
- The DB itself can be blown away — no mining should be required to rebuild it
- All mining MUST leave durable JSONL artifacts (mining is expensive; losing it to a DB blow-away is the failure mode this prevents)
- ``rebuild-from-jsonl`` is the canonical reconstruction path

Recent violations:
- wyrd-uzoh PR #276: Briggs ingester writes directly to DB with no JSONL emission. If the DB is wiped, the Briggs rows are gone unless ``ingest-briggs-personal-names`` is re-run on the staged .txt.

Fix scope:
1. Add a new reviewer section to /home/devon/521Studios/wyrd/AGENT-REVIEWERS.md, e.g. ``db-reconstructibility-reviewer``.
2. The reviewer flags:
   - Any new code path that writes to the lexicon DB without emitting a corresponding JSONL artifact (or without being itself loadable from JSONL events that rebuild-from-jsonl can replay).
   - Any mining/ingest CLI whose output is DB-only.

title: Read + position: Bender et al. 2021 Stochastic Parrots as field's missing keystone
description:
Bender et al. 2021 'On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots' (FAccT 2021) is the canonical critical-AI text on LLM cultural harms. The wyrd-kz2b.17/.18/.21 reading clusters confirm it is SYSTEMATICALLY ABSENT from the citation graphs of both LLM-conlang generation papers AND cultural-bias-audit papers — even Visual Orientalism, which cites Birhane/Crawford/Said, omits Bender.

This is now a structural finding across three clusters, not a sampling artifact. The manifesto's positioning move: cite Stochastic Parrots from 'field's missing keystone' position. Wyrd's manifesto is the bridge between conlang-LLM critique and cultural-bias-audit work, with Stochastic Parrots as the shared theoretical anchor neither side currently uses.

WHAT TO READ:
- Bender, E.M., Gebru, T., McMillan-Major, A., Shmitchell, S. (2021). On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big?. Proceedings of FAccT 2021, pp. 610-623.
- URL: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3442188.3445922
- The 'famous paper that got Timnit Gebru fired from Google' — read with awareness of its institutional history

WHAT TO EXTRACT:
1. **Their specific argument structure** — what claims does it make about LLM cultural harms?
2. **The hegemonic-viewpoint argument** — LLMs encode dominant-group worldviews silently
3. **The environmental cost argument** — secondary to wyrd but worth knowing
4. **The audit-evasion argument** — LLMs are too big to audit. Wyrd's three-tier audit is exactly the audit-tractable alternative.
5. **Citations they make** — what's THEIR theoretical foundation? May surface additional reading.

OUTPUT: notes file at ~/.wyrd/papers/bender_2021_stochastic_parrots.md per template.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- Cites Bender from 'field's missing keystone' position is a STRONG manifesto move
- Anchors wyrd's claim that rule-based + scholarship-traced is the audit-tractable alternative to 'too-big-to-audit' LLMs
- Bridges the conlang-LLM-critique cluster and the cultural-bias-audit cluster

ESTIMATED TIME: 2-3 hours (FAccT papers are ~14 pages but dense).

CITATION CONSEQUENCES: this paper becomes a centerpiece of wyrd's manifesto positioning. Read carefully.

CROSS-REFERENCES:
- wyrd-x8r2.1 (Manifesto) — primary consumer
- wyrd-kz2b.12 (Paper D) — secondary cite
- wyrd-kz2b.5 (BibTeX) — required entry
notes:
Completed 2026-05-19 via agent pass. Notes deposited at:
- ~/.wyrd/papers/bender_2021_stochastic_parrots.md

KEY FINDINGS:
1. CRITICAL: wyrd was OVER-CLAIMING alignment with Bender et al. The "Bender implicitly calls for symbolic alternatives" framing is a STRETCH; she calls for smaller statistical models with documentation discipline, NOT symbolic alternatives.
2. Softened framing required (drafted in wyrd-x8r2.1 notes).
3. Adopt "documentation debt" (Bender's exact coinage §4.4) as the load-bearing term. Replaces "audit-evasion" / "too big to audit."

title: META-EPIC: scholarly-grounded procedural worldbuilding — field-creating research program
description:
The 10-year field-creating research program of which wyrd-2166 (REGISTERS.md), wyrd-ecjp (vector-driven onomastics), wyrd-kq7w (phonaesthetic registers), and wyrd-kz2b (publication path) are the proof-of-method exemplars.

UNIFYING THESIS:

Every layer of a fictional world should emerge from real scientific / scholarly process, with reproducible code and citation-traced audit trails. The integration architecture — not any individual domain implementation — is the load-bearing methodological contribution.

Layers (each a sub-epic, each its own publishable paper):

1. ONOMASTICS — vector-driven, citation-bearing name generation with three-tier UNIVERSAL/IE-CONVENTIONAL/IDENTITY-MARKING audit. (proof-of-method, currently shipping via wyrd-ecjp + wyrd-kq7w + wyrd-2166; publication path is wyrd-kz2b)
2. PLATE-TECTONICS GEOLOGY — procedural terrain via simulated mantle convection + plate movement; cite geomorphology / mantle-dynamics literature; heightmap + plate-boundary + rock-age metadata for downstream consumers.
3. CLIMATE / HYDROLOGY — atmospheric circulation + ocean currents + rainfall + river networks + biome distribution over the geology layer; cite climate science (GCM literature, Köppen-Geiger).
4. GENERATIVE ECONOMICS — agent-based economic simulation over resource distribution from geology+climate; settlement patterns, trade routes, regional specialization; cite economic-history + agent-based-model literature.
5. CULTURAL GEOGRAPHY — language-family migration, religious-syncretism zones, kinship-system distributions, over the economic-geographic substrate; this is the layer that lets onomastics know WHERE Brittonic substrate is and WHERE Norman influence reaches.
6. INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE — the cross-domain audit-trail format + downstream-consumable schemas that hold the stack together. THIS is the field-defining methodological move; this is the manifesto paper.

STRATEGIC PATH (Path B per 2026-05-19 conversation):

Field-creator + seeder. Goal is not to be the world expert in any single domain — geomorphologists, climatologists, agent-based economists, historical linguists all exist as established subfields with deep expertise. Goal is to publish DEFENSIBLE-ENOUGH-TO-CITE implementations of each domain, with the integration architecture and audit-trail methodology as the load-bearing contribution.

\"Even if my plate tectonics model is crap, if it's published it can be cited and built upon.\" The publication is the territory-stake; subsequent collaborators deepen each domain.

RATIONALE FOR THE FIELD'S EXISTENCE:

Closest existing fields all miss the unique cross-section:
- Computational creativity (ICCC, JCC): generative systems, no scholarship audit trail
- Digital humanities: computation → humanities-study, rarely reversed
- Procedural content generation (FDG): algorithms + player experience, scholarship trace unasked
- Onomastics + applied phonaesthetics (Kawahara Pokémonastics): empirical study of naming, not generative methodology
- Worldbuilding studies (Mark Wolf, Trammell, Boraman): textual-critical, not methodological/generative
- Hard-SF integration (Niven, Forward): single-author, no reproducible pipeline
- Dwarf Fortress: cross-layer simulation but proprietary, no scholarship trace, no methodology paper

The unclaimed methodological territory is REPRODUCIBLE + AUDITABLE + INTEGRATED scholarly-grounded worldbuilding.

EXECUTION SEQUENCE:

Phase 0 (now → +6 months): ship onomastics to publication-grade. wyrd-kz2b is the active publication epic. Lands as arXiv preprint + JOHD data paper + ICCC 2027 paper.

Phase 1 (+6 → +18 months): write the field-defining manifesto paper. After onomastics ships, the manifesto has a proof-of-method exemplar. Without it, the manifesto is hand-waving. With it, the manifesto is 'here is a working exemplar; here is the program for extending it to N more domains.' Target venue: a theoretical / methodology venue (MIT Press Open, Cosmos & History, Mark Wolf's Worldbuilding book series, or a new venue established for this purpose).

Phase 2-5 (+18 months → +5-10 years): each domain epic ships as its own paper + integration into the stack. Order is flexible; geology naturally comes first because it's the foundation of climate which is the foundation of biomes which is the foundation of economics. Cultural geography is the integration layer that ties everything back to onomastics.

ANTI-PATTERN: do not try to publish the integration manifesto BEFORE onomastics ships. The manifesto without a working exemplar is hand-waving and reviewers will reject. The manifesto AFTER onomastics ships is 'here is proof; here is the proposed research program.'

REALITY CHECK: this is a 5-10 year arc. Solo-build the architecture + onomastics + a hacky low-fidelity integration prototype showing all 6 layers running end-to-end at minimal quality. The integration prototype demonstrates FEASIBILITY; once published, attracts the collaborators who want to deepen each domain. By year 5, you should be co-authoring with at least 3 academic collaborators across the domains.

OUT OF SCOPE for this epic: any specific publication output (those are separate sub-epic tickets). The job of this meta-epic is to hold the strategic context so it doesn't get lost.

title: Rando-toponym retirement workflow using corpus mining attestations
description:
Use the wyrd-x82p corpus mining output to retire synthetic 'rando' toponym entries, same playbook as the meanings retirement.

PROMOTION (auto, no operator review):
- Any rando-classified toponym with >=1 attestation in the attestations table after the corpus mining stages land → bulk re-class rando → attested.
- User confirmed 2026-05-17: 'as long as it's attested in one source, I'm fine with town names getting promoted'.
- Each historical spelling variant counts as an attestation (the DB-side dedup key is (toponym_id, form, date_year, source_doc) — anti-collision, not anti-duplication — so Bedlington / Bedlingtun / Bethlingtun all preserve their evidence chain).

TRIAGE (operator review):
- Rando toponyms with ZERO attestations after a broad corpus pass.
- These could be: (a) genuinely synthetic (a generated -ham/-ton compound no scholar ever cited), (b) a small/obscure place attested only in primary sources outside our corpus, (c) a spelling variant we haven't matched to its canonical form.
- Do NOT auto-prune. Operator decides per case.

INPUTS:
- data/mining/phase2/*.jsonl (corpus mining outputs from staged cascade — wyrd-srd2)
- ingest-toponym-mentions populates the attestations table from those JSONL
- rando-port-readiness CLI for baselining

ACCEPTANCE:
- A new CLI command (or extend rando-port-readiness) that:
  - Reports: rando-with-attestations count, rando-without-attestations count
  - Has a --promote-attested flag that bulk re-classes rando → attested in one DB transaction, with audit-trail JSONL events (matches the curation event pattern)
  - Has a --emit-triage flag that dumps the zero-attestation set with a fuzzy-similarity score to known toponyms, for operator review
- prune-toponym command works for the operator-confirmed-synthetic residual (already exists per kenning CLI command listing)
- Documentation in INGESTION.md or similar covering the full retirement workflow

PRE-REQS:
- wyrd-srd2 corpus mining stage 1 (gemma4) complete + stages 2+ as needed (residual cascade)
- All attestations ingested via ingest-toponym-mentions
- dump-jsonl applied to keep the L2 facts rebuild-safe

PRIORITY: P2 — not blocking but unblocked once corpus mining lands.
notes:
2026-05-17: design clarified per user direction.

STREAMING PROMOTION (run anytime, idempotent forward ratchet):
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon retire-rando-toponyms --promote-attested'
- Finds every rando-classed toponym with >=1 toponym_attestation row.
- Bulk re-class rando → attested in one transaction.
- Audit JSONL of promotions.
- Safe to re-run after each ingest batch.

BATCH TRIAGE + ARCHIVE (run ONCE after corpus mining + ingest complete):
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon retire-rando-toponyms --emit-triage <file>'
- Dump zero-attestation rando set + fuzzy-match suggestions to known toponyms.
- Operator review.
- 'wyrd kenning lexicon retire-rando-toponyms --commit-triage <triage-file>'
- For each operator decision:
  - 'skip' → leave rando-classed in DB (still synthetic, no change)
  - 'attest' → re-class as attested + write the operator-confirmed
    citation as a synthetic attestation row
  - 'retire' → DELETE from active DB tables AND append full row data
    to data/mining/retired/rando-toponyms-retired.jsonl tombstone
    (mirrors the wyrd-j2bv etymon retirement pattern)

ARCHIVE PATTERN (mirrors wyrd-j2bv):
- Tombstone path: data/mining/retired/rando-toponyms-retired.jsonl
- Lives OUTSIDE the data/mining/*.jsonl glob walked by rebuild-from-jsonl
  → retired entries don't bounce back on rebuild
- Excluded from dump-jsonl too (preventing accidental round-trip)
- Source row at top documents the tombstone purpose
- Preserves toponym + toponym_etymology + toponym_etymology_element rows
  + any pre-existing attestations (none for true synthetic rando, but
  in principle for completeness)
- Revivable: future passes can read the tombstone to un-retire if a
  later corpus mining finds the place attested somewhere

USER-CONFIRMED THRESHOLDS (2026-05-17):
- Promotion: >=1 attestation auto-promotes (no cross-source ceremony)
- Pruning: gated behind operator review, not automatic
close_reason: Promotion-path / report-only deliverable merged to main via PR #223 (squash) 2026-05-18. 3-round review loop + R3 verification, 29 tests. Final state: report-wikipedia-backfill CLI command reads the 5 *_place_names.json files + lexicon DB; reports per-region backfill stats (total/in_db/attested/gap/%_attested) with --as-json + --verbose + --language modes. Key contracts: rando-port source_doc filtered (defensive scholar-only), NFC normalization on both sides, UnknownLanguageError narrows CLI exception scope. Live baseline at merge: English 49% attested, Scottish 5%, Welsh 6%, Irish 1%, Breton 0% (corpus mining ongoing). Deferred to future bd ticket: bulk-promote rando→attested workflow + tombstone archive for retired entries (the actual retirement action, beyond the report).

title: Staged cascade mining: --capture-failures + --from-failures for operator-paced multi-model extraction
description:
Today's mine-toponym-mentions-tiered does per-chunk primary→fallback inline. For corpus-scale work + cost-tier shopping (Mawer probe 2026-05-17 showed gemini-flash gets 98% of sonnet's yield at 10× lower cost, but 12% per-chunk failure rate), the operator-paced staged cascade is more useful.

Design:

NEW FLAG --capture-failures FILE on mine-toponym-mentions (single-tier):
- For every chunk where the provider raises (transport, JSON parse, schema mismatch), append a row to FILE:
  {"source_id":"…","chunk_idx":N,"chunk_body":"…","error":"…","model":"provider:model"}
- Orthogonal to existing behavior (chunks_failed is still counted in the report).

NEW INPUT MODE --from-failures FILE on mine-toponym-mentions:
- Mutually exclusive with --sources-dir / --source.
- Reads pre-chunked rows from FILE, processes those chunks with the configured provider, writes mentions to --output-dir/<source_id>.jsonl (appending if file exists for that source).
- Same provider flags (--provider, --model). Same report shape.

WORKFLOW:
- Stage 1: mine-toponym-mentions --sources-dir sources/ --provider ollama --model gemma4:26b --output-dir data/mining/phase2/ --capture-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage1.jsonl
- Inspect stage1.jsonl
- Stage 2: mine-toponym-mentions --from-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage1.jsonl --provider gemini --model gemini-2.5-flash --output-dir data/mining/phase2/ --capture-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage2.jsonl
- Inspect stage2.jsonl
- Stage 3: mine-toponym-mentions --from-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage2.jsonl --provider anthropic --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --output-dir data/mining/phase2/ --capture-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage3.jsonl
- Stage 4 (optional sonnet on residual): mine-toponym-mentions --from-failures data/mining/phase2_failures/stage3.jsonl --provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-6 --output-dir data/mining/phase2/

Each stage is operator-inspectable. The phase2 output JSONLs accumulate mentions across stages with the model attribution preserved in each row (so analysis can see who extracted what).

Output append semantics: dedup by (source_id, chunk_idx, form, date_year, region_hint) so re-running a stage is idempotent.

Acceptance:
- --capture-failures captures one row per failed chunk including the chunk body verbatim
- --from-failures resumes the failed chunks, writes to the correct per-source output, idempotent
- Tests covering single-tier with failure-capture, single-tier with from-failures input, idempotent re-run
- Documentation update: replace or augment the mine-toponym-mentions-tiered docs to point operators at the staged workflow for cost-tiering
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #221 (squash) 2026-05-17. 4-round PR review loop with 14 agent fanout per round + Gemini iteration. Final state: mine-toponym-mentions-staged CLI command with --capture-failures + --from-failures + operator-paced cascade workflow. 130 unit/CLI tests covering: schema validation (type-check + null/empty rejection), atomic-write resume + malformed-row purging, dedup, idempotency, failure isolation across sources, non-monotonic indices, --limit per-source, capture-failures stale-records warning, UTF-8 replacement warning, U+FFFD detection, callback exception propagation. Won't-fix follow-ups deferred: client_box → dataclass, mine_fn injection removal, oversize-warning suppression in resume, 3-stage cascade end-to-end, FailureRecord dataclass.

title: Extend push-bulk-sources to S3-sync data/mining/phase2/ (corpus-scale mining artifacts)
description:
Currently data/mining/phase2/<src>.jsonl (the durable LLM-mining output) lives only in git per PR #220 (Mawer 1920). Fine at 2.6 MB/book, but at 48 books × ~3 MB = ~150 MB this becomes borderline for git.

Convention to mirror: push-bulk-sources/fetch-bulk-sources already round-trips ~/.wyrd/sources/ to S3 with content-addressing. Extend that mechanism (or build a parallel one) to also round-trip data/mining/phase2/.

Acceptance:
- A command (probably push-bulk-mining-artifacts or extend push-bulk-sources) uploads data/mining/phase2/*.jsonl to s3://521studios-{env}-wyrd-mining/phase2/
- Symmetric fetch command for a fresh checkout
- Manifest tracks (source_id, file_hash, schema_version, mining_run_ts) — gives audit trail of which gemma4/anthropic versions produced which artifacts
- README or CLAUDE.md note explaining the lifecycle: phase2 = expensive LLM output, S3 = durable, git = small-scale only
- When this lands, remove phase2/ from PR #220 (or whatever's been committed by then) and migrate to S3
- BUT: keep canonical data/mining/<src>.jsonl in git (small, rebuild-safe L2 facts)
close_reason: Won't fix — user directive 2026-05-17: 'as noted, if the rest of mining is mostly in git, we can just add it to git. I just want it to be durable.' Existing convention (data/mining/*.jsonl with 30+ source files like ekwall_1922_lancashire.jsonl, duignan_1902_staffordshire.jsonl, etc.) is git-tracked. phase2/ follows that pattern. If corpus-scale mining ever bloats the repo past acceptable size, file a fresh ticket to migrate. For now: just commit.

title: Add hallucination-triggered Anthropic fallback with union merge to mine-toponym-mentions-tiered
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-pe4g Gemma 4 26B viability evaluation (2026-05-16). With Gemma 4 26B as primary, the smoke test (3 chunks of Mawer 1920) showed 93% of Anthropic Sonnet's mention yield + 1.3% form-hallucination rate + free + completes every chunk. The tiered command should opportunistically re-extract chunks where the primary hallucinated with Anthropic as fallback, then UNION the mentions (don't discard the primary's good mentions from those chunks).

Implementation:
* New flag on `lexicon mine-toponym-mentions-tiered`: `--hallucination-fallback-threshold N` (default: disabled / 0 = off). When set, chunks where primary's `hallucinations_dropped >= N` get re-extracted by the fallback client.
* Merge strategy: union of (primary's surviving mentions) + (fallback's mentions) deduped by (form, date_year, region_hint) tuple. Don't replace primary's chunk output — preserve everything primary saw correctly.
* New counter on the report: `chunks_hallucination_rescued` (matches existing `chunks_recovered_by_fallback` style).
* Tests: pin the threshold trigger, the union-not-replace behavior, the dedup, and the new counter.

Cost calibration: at 1.3% hallucination rate × ~130 chunks/book × 48 sources × ~$0.06 Anthropic per chunk = ~$5-10 corpus-wide. Same Anthropic call rate as a 'replace' strategy; the difference is what's kept.

Acceptance: re-run smoke on Mawer 1920 with --primary-provider ollama --primary-model gemma4:26b --fallback-provider anthropic --hallucination-fallback-threshold 1 --hallucination-fallback-merge union. Verify chunks_hallucination_rescued > 0 (the smoke had 1 hallucination across 3 chunks), output mentions count >= primary-only count, and the union dedupes correctly.

Threshold calibration: needs full-Mawer benchmark first (currently incomplete due to mid-run macbook outage) to see real hallucination distribution across the whole 130-chunk book.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #219 (squash) 2026-05-17. 7-round PR review loop with 14 agent fanout each round + Gemini iteration. Final state: hallucination-triggered Anthropic fallback with union merge, dual counter (attempted/succeeded), context-inclusive dedup with internal-fallback-duplicate handling, opportunistic continuation on fallback error, click.IntRange(min=0) at CLI boundary, halluc_rescued=succeeded/attempted in summary lines. 60 tiered tests passing. Follow-ups: wyrd-kg22 (further extract primary-fail-fallback block), wyrd-oaq5 (delta-return ValidationCounters from both extract helpers).

title: Fix Gemini schema dialect for mine-toponym-mentions (JSON Schema → Gemini OpenAPI subset)
description:
The toponym extraction RESPONSE_SCHEMA in wyrd/generators/kenning/toponym_mention_extractor.py:160 uses JSON Schema 2020-12 dialect (`additionalProperties: False`, nullable unions like `type: ["string", "null"]`). GeminiClient.chat_json forwards this schema as-is to Gemini's API, which uses an OpenAPI-3.0 subset that doesn't accept either feature. Every `mine-toponym-mentions --provider gemini` call therefore returns HTTP 400 with `Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name 'additionalProperties'` and `Proto field is not repeating` on the union type. Confirmed by direct test 2026-05-16: 0 chunks succeeded, 3 chunks failed for Mawer 1920.

Pattern: the etymology extractor's existing GEMINI_RESPONSE_SCHEMA in gemini_extractor.py:42 is already hand-translated to the Gemini dialect; the new toponym schema added in PR #213 wasn't given the same treatment. Fix: add RESPONSE_SCHEMA_GEMINI sibling in toponym_mention_extractor.py + dispatch by isinstance(client, GeminiClient) in extract_toponym_mentions_from_chunk.

Acceptance: `wyrd kenning lexicon mine-toponym-mentions --provider gemini --source mawer_1920_northumberland_durham --limit 3 --chunk-size 5000` produces a non-empty JSONL with no chunk failures. Tests cover both schema variants and assert correct dispatch by client type.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #218 (squash) 2026-05-16. 7-round PR review loop with 14 agent fanout each round + Gemini iteration. Final state: schema_dialect ClassVar dispatch via _DIALECT_TO_SCHEMA dict, ValueError + JSONDecodeError + UnicodeDecodeError wraps on all 9 transport sites, 202 tests passing. Follow-ups: wyrd-9air (urlopen E2E for gemini), wyrd-rmc6 (parse_transport_json helper extraction).

title: Phase 0: Unify --mood system into phonaesthetic-vector register-effect catalog
description:
Foundational refactor: the existing MOODS dict in __init__.py (grim, harsh, pastoral, devotional, mortuary) is a less-generalized form of the phonaesthetic-vector primitive (per [[phonaesthetic-vector-design-refinement-2026-05-16-user]]). Unify them: every register effect becomes a triple of (phonological_feature_weights, semantic_tag_weights, position_bias) keyed by name in a YAML catalog.

Why foundational: Phase 2 (fantasy-pack schema) and Phase 3c (adaptation-template schema) both need to reference register effects. Defining the catalog up-front means downstream schemas can speak the same vocabulary.

Subsumes (does NOT break) existing --mood behavior:
- 'grim' stays as a registered effect with the same tag weights it has today
- 'harsh' stays as a registered effect with the same phonological biases
- 'harsh:0.5' colon-suffix graduation still works (becomes weight in the vector)
- Composition (multiple --mood flags) becomes vector sum/clamp, equivalent to today's tag-union + max-harshness
- Bit-stable at default (no --mood specified) since vector is zero-vector

Steps:
1. Define register_effects.yaml schema and migrate the 5 current MOODS to it
2. Replace MOODS dict reads with YAML catalog loads in NameGenerator
3. Document custom-effect contribution path
4. Round-trip test: existing --mood test cases produce identical output post-refactor

Acceptance: full test suite passes; phonaesthetic-vector catalog is loadable; new register effects can be added by editing YAML without touching code.

Blocks: wyrd-v2gm.2 (fantasy-pack schema needs vocabulary), wyrd-v2gm.3.3 (adaptation-template schema needs semantic_register reference).
close_reason: Superseded by wyrd-kq7w (rip-and-replace epic). Phase B of new epic (wyrd-kq7w.2) covers the catalog YAML migration originally scoped here; new epic adds the per-lemma vector enrichment + runtime rip-and-replace + audit work that was out of scope for the original soft-refactor framing.

title: wyrd-x82p Phase 2b.3: operator-review tool for new-toponym candidates
description: Two-step bulk-edit workflow: prepare-toponym-candidates adds fuzzy suggestions to raw candidates JSONL; operator hand-edits action field; commit-toponym-candidates applies decisions (create new toponym row / map to existing / skip / defer). Triages the 238 new-toponym candidates from Phase 2 pilot + the full set from Phase 2b.2 multi-source runs.

title: Shavian Phase 1b: OOV + proper-name pronunciation via Bedrock fallback
description:
Pure G2P fallback fails badly on the words that matter most for TTRPG use: proper nouns. 'Worcestershire', 'Cholmondeley', 'Siobhan', 'Geoffrey' break rule-based G2P; fantasy names ('Drizzt', 'Gygax', 'Xythraqq') get phonetic guesses that diverge from how players actually say them. Since campaign documents are saturated with proper nouns, this is the single biggest forward-pipeline quality lever after the heteronym work.

THREE-TIER OOV RESOLUTION:

TIER 1 — Lexicon hit (ReadLex). Free, zero-latency. Already handled by Phase 1.

TIER 2 — G2P (CMUdict-backed via g2p-en). Free, zero-latency. Phase 1 baseline. Adequate for ordinary common-noun OOV; bad on names.

TIER 3 — Bedrock pronunciation lookup (cheap, per-call latency).
- Triggered when the token is OOV AND (a) tagged NNP/NNPS by the POS tagger, or (b) has phonotactic features suggesting an unusual or foreign origin (Phase 0 decides the trigger rule).
- Prompt: 'How is the English word "<token>" pronounced? Reply in ARPABET with stress markers. If you do not know a standard pronunciation, give your best phonetic guess and prefix with "?".'
- Parse ARPABET response → phoneme sequence → Shavian glyphs (same phoneme→Shavian map as the G2P path).
- Mark low-confidence (prefixed '?') results in the component breakdown so the SPA can flag them.

WHY ARPABET (not IPA): the Shavian generator's phoneme→glyph map is built from CMUdict, which is ARPABET. Asking the LLM for ARPABET avoids an IPA-to-ARPABET translation step. If Phase 0's model can't reliably emit ARPABET, fall back to IPA + a deterministic IPA→ARPABET mapping.

CACHING: aggressive caching makes this cheap in practice. Campaign documents reuse the same proper names hundreds of times. In-process LRU keyed on the raw token string (no context needed — pronunciation of 'Drizzt' doesn't depend on neighbors).

TESTS:
- Curated list of known-hard proper names (real + fantasy): assert each gets a plausible Shavian rendering (exact match for well-known names, plausible-phonetics for invented ones).
- Cache hit-rate test: re-translate the same paragraph twice in a warm container; Tier-3 calls should be 0 on the second pass.
- Cost regression: average Bedrock calls per 200-word fantasy-flavored paragraph stays under a recorded threshold.

DEPENDS ON: Phase 0 (Bedrock model + IAM), Phase 1 (forward pipeline + G2P baseline).

title: Phase 6: Neo-Khuzdul pilot scenario-pack — end-to-end integration target
description:
The integration validation. Build a real Neo-Khuzdul pack from public Aaberg + Tolkien Appendix E sources, run it through Phase 1-5 end-to-end:

1. Source: Neo-Khuzdul lemma list with glosses (geology/architecture/social tag-dominated)
2. Template choice: Khuzdul -> OE-pre-1100 (primary) + Khuzdul -> ModE (secondary for modern-feel variant)
3. Run pack-build (Phase 4); surface culturally-absent prompts for bird/sea/food tags
4. Bundle into meanings.json fragment
5. Generate sample English town names with --fantasy-pack neo-khuzdul.yaml
6. KenningRewind a generated name through eras to validate phonology chain

Acceptance: 25 generated town names with Khuzdul loan-flavor, all rendering OE-shaped through ModE-shaped via KenningRewind, operator-graded as 'feels dwarven' >=80%.

This is also the validation that the whole epic's design works end-to-end. Failures here surface upstream issues.

title: Phase 5: generator runtime + KenningRewind integration
description:
Wire fantasy-pack-built meanings.json fragments into the generator runtime. Mostly verification work since by design fantasy packs emit STANDARD bundle entries (D18 variants, era_reflexes, modifier_tags) — runtime should not need new code.

Verification checklist:
- 'wyrd kenning generate english --fantasy-pack neo-khuzdul.yaml' produces town names where Khuzdul reflexes appear
- KenningRewind walks Khuzdul-loaned names through OE/ME/EModE/ModE eras correctly via existing phonology chain
- --spelling-variety knob samples among the loan-reflex variants from the variants pool
- --era filter respects the loan-era declaration in the pack
- --mood + --cohesion knobs compose orthogonally with fantasy packs

If runtime IS untouched, this phase reduces to: write integration tests + verify KenningRewind output on Neo-Khuzdul sample.

title: Phase 4: interactive scenario-pack-build — culturally-absent vs augment vs fill prompts
description:
New CLI: 'kenning pack build <fantasy_pack.yaml>' walks the (donor × recipient × era) template proportions; for each tag in the template profile, checks user's lemma pack for coverage; surfaces gaps with 3-way operator prompt:

1. **Fill** — operator wants to supply more lemmas for this tag; pack-build pauses, operator edits pack, resumes
2. **Culturally absent** — operator confirms 'this culture has no concept/vocabulary for this tag'; renormalize template proportions excluding the absent tag
3. **Augment** — operator says 'this culture has rich vocabulary for a tag the template underweights' (e.g., Khuzdul material/craft); operator supplies custom proportion weight

Output: meanings.json fragment ready for merge into the bundle, plus pack-build audit log.

Composable with multiple template choices (e.g., Khuzdul can be built into both OE-era and ME-era reflexes in one pass).

title: Phase 3h: kenning pack review-adaptation — operator review tool
description:
New CLI: 'kenning pack review-adaptation <template>' renders an operator-facing review surface:
- Shows the rules in the template (3c shape)
- Adapts 20 sample lemmas (from the fantasy pack) through 3e, displays variants with their strategy_chain + ipa_trace
- Shows the calibration-set precision number from 3f
- Lets operator: tweak a rule + re-render; accept variants from alternative strategies; approve-and-lock the template

Last human-in-the-loop checkpoint before a fantasy pack is built into bundle entries.

Acceptance: operator can iterate Neo-Khuzdul -> OE template in <30 minutes to a state they're happy locking.

title: Phase 3g: kenning pack propose-adaptation — Gemini Flash drafts template
description:
New CLI: 'kenning pack propose-adaptation <source_phonology> <recipient> <era>' calls Gemini Flash with:
- Source-phonology YAML (3a) for the fantasy lang
- Recipient-era schema (3b)
- Real-loan calibration set from 3d as grounding examples
- Scholarly citations as prompt context (Townend 2002 patterns for ON->OE, Pope 1934 for NF->ME, etc.)
- 'Extrapolate the substitution + cluster + prosody rules for this novel donor at this era'

Output: draft adaptation-template YAML (3c shape) for operator review.

This is the genuinely creative step where empirical rules get extrapolated to fantasy donors that have no historical attestations. The grounding-in-real-loans makes the proposals principled rather than free invention.

Acceptance: produces a Neo-Khuzdul -> OE-pre-1100 template that 3h's 20-sample render looks plausible enough to lock.

title: Phase 3f: kenning adaptation-eval — >=80% precision gate on calibration set
description:
New CLI: 'kenning adaptation-eval <template> <calibration_set>' runs adaptation-runtime (3e) against each (donor, expected_recipient) pair in the calibration set; reports precision (recipient_attestation present in adaptation runtime's N variants).

Precision gate: a template scoring <80% on its calibration set fails the gate and cannot be locked for production (operator must iterate 3g or hand-tune 3c).

This is what gives us empirical grounds for trusting Khuzdul->OE outputs (which we can't directly score) — calibrate on ON->OE first, then trust the same algorithm on Khuzdul.

Acceptance: ON->OE-pre-1100 template scores >=80% precision; <80% blocks Phase 6 sign-off.

title: Phase 3e: kenning adaptation-runtime — pure-Python adapt(lemma, template, n_variants)
description:
The heart of phase 3. Pure-Python function 'adapt(lemma, template, n_variants=5) -> List[AdaptedReflex]' that:
1. Walks the source-phonology lemma form
2. Applies phoneme_map substitutions (with positional conditions)
3. Applies cluster_rules with sample-weighted strategy selection (per design: variety for the variants pool)
4. Applies prosody rules (stress shift, vowel reduction)
5. Applies morphophonology (i-mutation/breaking/palatalization) if template.morphophonology_apply
6. Returns N weighted-variant reflexes for writing into the bundle's D18 variants pool

Output shape: [{form, weight, strategy_chain, ipa_trace}] — strategy_chain + ipa_trace are for operator review in 3h.

Deterministic given (lemma, template, seed). Sample-weighted with PCG-stable RNG so pack-build reruns produce identical variants.

Acceptance: 3a Neo-Khuzdul lemmas + 3d-derived ON->OE-pre-1100 template produce reasonable-looking OE-shaped reflexes for 'khazad', 'tharkun', 'mazarbul', 'baruk'.

title: Phase 3d: lexicon mine-loan-adaptations — extract real-loan substitution patterns from corpus
description:
New CLI: 'lexicon mine-loan-adaptations <donor> <recipient> [--era ERA]' walks toponym_etymology_element + etymon_descent + attested_year, extracts (donor_form, recipient_attestation, era) triples, aligns them phoneme-by-phoneme, emits:
- per-phoneme substitution frequency table
- per-cluster repair pattern table (epenthesis/simplify/preserve weights)
- prosodic pattern observations
- calibration set: JSONL of (donor, expected_recipient, era) for grading runtime adaptations

Source data:
- ON->OE pairs: ~91 pre-1100 + 531 ME-recorded
- Latin->OE: 222 pre-1100
- NF->ME: 75 1100-1499

Output dual-purpose: (1) seed for empirical adaptation templates per 3c (rules derived from real data); (2) calibration set for the >=80% precision gate in 3f.

Acceptance: emits ON->OE-pre-1100 template + calibration set; spot-check 10 pairs show plausible alignments.

title: Phase 3c: adaptation-template schema (donor × recipient × era)
description:
YAML schema for the (donor × recipient × era) adaptation rules:
- phoneme_map: source IPA -> recipient IPA with positional conditions
- cluster_rules: source clusters -> repair strategies (epenthesis/simplify/preserve) with empirical weights
- prosody: stress mapping rules, vowel reduction in unstressed syllables
- morphology: target inflection class for borrowed roots + integration suffixes
- semantic_register: tag prior (favored/disfavored tags) for slot composition
- morphophonology_apply: bool — apply breaking/palatalization/i-mutation (true for OE-era, false for ME+ per design)

Schema instances are produced by 3d (empirical extraction) and 3g (LLM propose). 3e consumes them.

Acceptance: schema validates an ON->OE-pre-1100 template derived from real data via 3d.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-06-21 (autonomous loop): LIVE but blocked-in-practice + needs decision. Skipped (same class as wyrd-v2gm.3.1). Unstarted; authors a new donor×recipient×era adaptation-template schema (phoneme_map, cluster_rules, prosody, morphophonology_apply, semantic_register) + one ON→OE instance. BLOCKED-IN-PRACTICE: acceptance requires the template be derived from real data via sibling 3d (unstarted), and the schema's consumer is 3e's adapt() (unstarted). Same 3 decisions as 3.1: (a) acceptance references unbuilt siblings; (b) schema shape should be co-designed with 3e's adapt() contract; (c) the ON→OE instance is empirical-linguistics content needing sourcing/vetting. Foundational Phase-3 architecture for Devon to shape. Work the 3e/3d contracts (or an explicit standalone-design OK) before this is loop-workable.

title: Phase 3b: recipient-era phonology schemas (OE/ME/EModE/ModE)
description:
Write recipient-language phonology files for English at each loan-era stop:
- old-english-pre-1100.yaml (Alfredian/Late West Saxon norm; /æ ɑ e i o u y/ vowels; CC- initial limited; i-mutation + breaking productive)
- middle-english-1100-1499.yaml (post-Conquest; /v z ʒ/ phonemicized; clusters relax; i-mutation no longer productive)
- early-modern-english-1500-1699.yaml (GVS in progress; loss of /x/; consonant inventory near-modern)
- modern-english-1700plus.yaml (post-GVS; final inventory)

References to consult (not bundle): Hogg 1992 (OE phonology), Campbell 1959 (OE Grammar), Jordan/Crook 1974 (ME phonology), Lass 1994.

This is the piece most likely to be wrong-the-first-time per design discussion. Expect iteration. Acceptance: real ON->OE pairs in calibration set (from 3d) parse cleanly against these schemas.

title: Phase 3a: source-phonology YAML schema + Neo-Khuzdul instance
description:
YAML schema for documenting a source-language (fantasy or real) phonological inventory:
- phonemes (consonants + vowels) with IPA + romanization
- phonotactic constraints (allowable clusters, syllable shape)
- stress pattern (fixed/weight-sensitive)
- morphological notes (inflection classes if any)

First instance: Neo-Khuzdul phonology file, sourced from Magnus Aaberg + Tolkien Appendix E + Etymologies. Includes /x/ (kh), /q/, /z/, glottal stop, weight-sensitive stress, CV(C)C+ syllable shape with rich medial clusters.

Schema reuse: same shape works for Sindarin, Quenya, Dothraki, High Valyrian source files. Acceptance: YAML round-trips through adaptation runtime (3e) cleanly.
notes:
TRIAGE 2026-06-21 (autonomous loop): LIVE but NOT autonomously workable as written — needs Devon's call on 3 points. Skipped.

1. ACCEPTANCE UNMEETABLE: the stated acceptance is 'YAML round-trips through the adaptation runtime (3e) cleanly', but 3e (wyrd-v2gm.3.5) does NOT exist (this ticket BLOCKS it; epic v2gm.3 is 0/8). So full acceptance can't be verified now. Either (a) rescope this ticket's acceptance to a STANDALONE round-trip-parse test (load YAML → model → dump → reload, structure-stable), with the 3e integration verified later in 3e; or (b) keep it gated until 3e's adapt() contract exists.

2. SCHEMA-SHAPE RISK (design-before-consumer): this is the FOUNDATIONAL schema for the Phase-3 adaptation engine, but its real consumer — adapt(lemma, template, n_variants) in 3e, plus the donor×recipient×era template schema in 3.3 — isn't designed yet. Authoring the phonology schema in a vacuum risks the wrong field shape (it must serve the adaptation algorithm + template join). Recommend sketching 3e's adapt() contract + 3.3's template shape FIRST (or at least concurrently) so this schema is driven by what the engine needs, not guessed. Devon: design standalone now and accept rework risk, or sequence after the 3e/3.3 contracts?

3. SPECIALIZED CONTENT NEEDS SOURCES: the Neo-Khuzdul instance is to be 'sourced from Magnus Aaberg + Tolkien Appendix E + Etymologies' (/x/ kh, /q/, /z/, glottal stop, weight-sensitive stress, CV(C)C+ medial clusters). I don't have those sources; reconstructing a conlang phonology from training memory would produce PLAUSIBLE-BUT-UNVERIFIED data — against the project's evidence ethos (D21, 'evidence sacred'). Needs the sources provided, or Devon's authored/vetted phonology, or an explicit OK to draft-from-memory-then-vet.

Net: foundational greenfield architecture for a fantasy-source-language adaptation engine — Devon's vision to shape, not autonomous review-debt. Until 1-3 are resolved, leave PARKED. Same applies to sibling wyrd-v2gm.3.3 (template schema).

title: Phase 3: phonotactic adaptation engine (sub-epic)
description:
The genuinely-new algorithmic work in the fantasy-lang epic. Take a Khuzdul lemma + era + recipient lang, produce N weighted-sampled OE-era-shaped reflexes, written into the bundle's existing D18 variants pool.

Sub-tickets 3a-3h cover:
3a. Source-phonology YAML schema + Neo-Khuzdul phonology file
3b. Recipient-era phonology schemas (OE pre-1100 / ME / EModE / ModE)
3c. Adaptation-template schema (donor × recipient × era)
3d. lexicon mine-loan-adaptations: extract real-loan substitution patterns from corpus
3e. kenning adaptation-runtime: pure-Python adapt(lemma, template, n_variants=5)
3f. kenning adaptation-eval: gate >=80% precision on calibration set
3g. kenning pack propose-adaptation: Gemini Flash drafts template grounded in calibration set + scholarly citations
3h. kenning pack review-adaptation: operator review tool

Estimated 5 weeks elapsed for Phase 3 with Neo-Khuzdul pilot.

Architectural payoff: adaptation is offline; runtime sees standard bundle entries (just more variants per Meaning).

title: Phase 2: scenario-pack YAML schema
description:
YAML schema for a fantasy-language pack. Per-fantasy-lang file containing:
- Source phonology inventory (phonemes + clusters + stress + morphology)
- Lemma list with glosses + semantic tags (from corpus tag vocab)
- Optional inflection paradigm
- Choice of loan template: (donor_template, recipient_lang, ingest_era) tuple
- Per-tag weight overrides (for the 'culturally augmented' bucket)
- Per-tag 'absent' markers (for the 'culturally absent' bucket)

A single fantasy lang can declare multiple (recipient × era) variants of itself (e.g., Khuzdul-into-OE and Khuzdul-into-ModE both shipped).

Pack-format draft for review before sub-phase 3a starts.

title: Phase 1: lexicon profile-loan-shape CLI
description:
New CLI: 'lexicon profile-loan-shape <donor_lang> <recipient_lang> [--era OE|ME|EModE|ModE]' emits tag/position/inflection vector for the empirical donor->recipient->era profile from toponym_etymology_element + attested_year. JSON output. Reusable infrastructure for all fantasy packs in this epic.

Empirically validated profiles available:
- old-norse -> old-english: 1,220 element appearances across 858 toponyms (Khuzdul template)
- celtic -> old-english: 3,514 / 2,032 (Sindarin template; richest dataset)
- latin -> old-english: 492 / 343 (Quenya template; OE-era dominant)
- norman-french -> old-english: 135 / 114 (High Valyrian template; ME-era dominant)
- old-english (native baseline): 5,519 / 3,067

Per-era buckets validated: ON peaks in ME records (531), NF clusters ME (75), Latin clusters OE (222).

Output shape: {tag_distribution, position_distribution, inflection_rate, mean_morpheme_length, suffix_inventory, ...}

Foundational dependency for the epic.

title: EPIC: scenario-pack town-name generation (fantasy + counterfactual + speculative-future; Neo-Khuzdul pilot)
description:
Generate town names with cultural influence from fantasy languages (Neo-Khuzdul, Sindarin, Quenya, Dothraki, High Valyrian) by templating against empirical loan-shape patterns in the real corpus. The core insight: we know what English ingestion of loans looks like at each era (OE pre-1100 / ME 1100-1499 / EModE / ModE), so we can create fake English loan words with fantasy roots that obey the same empirical phonotactic + tag-distribution + position-bias patterns as real loans from that era.

Architecture: adaptation runs offline at pack-build time, outputting standard meanings.json entries (using existing D18 variants pool for sample-weighted reflex variety). Runtime stays untouched. Neo-Khuzdul is the first pilot (fan work, no IP issues).

Design choices locked:
- Stratified sourcing: empirical rule-derivation from corpus + LLM-extrapolation for fantasy + operator-review
- Calibration: score >=80% precision on real-loan calibration set before trusting on fantasy lang
- Sample-weighted at pack-build time -> variants pool; deterministic at runtime
- Apply morphophonology (breaking/palatalization) for OE-era loans; skip for ME+
- Scholarly references (Townend 2002, Hogg 1992, Campbell 1959, Pope 1934, Jordan/Crook 1974) used as LLM grounding, not bundled

Composes with existing infrastructure: D33 era-reflex, D32 stratum tags, D18 variants pool, KenningRewind, phonology_rules forward chain, attested_year era-anchoring.

title: Shavian Phase 4: Generator class + manifest + SPA wiring
description:
Wire the Shavian transliterator into the wyrd plugin framework so the SPA picks it up automatically via /api/manifest, and confirm the Lambda deploy budget is intact.

DELIVERABLES:

  - 'components': per-token breakdown (English word, POS, Shavian, sense if disambiguated) — same style as kenning's component list.

LAMBDA DEPLOY CHECK:

- If size budget is exceeded, decide whether the heavy deps (POS tagger / G2P) need to move behind '[shavian]' optional-dep group and the runtime degrades gracefully, OR whether the lexicon-only path is sufficient for in-Lambda use (since ReadLex covers most common English).

TESTS:
- API test (similar to existing generator API tests) hitting the manifest endpoint and asserting the Shavian generator is present with the correct schema.
- API test invoking 'forward' and 'reverse' modes via the dispatcher.

DEPENDS ON: Phase 1 (forward pipeline) at minimum. Phase 3 (reverse) for full functionality. Phase 2 (semantic heteronyms) is integrated transparently — no new surface changes needed.

title: Shavian Phase 3: reverse pipeline (Shavian → English) with homophone resolution
description:
Build the reverse transliteration path: Shavian text → English text.

KEY INSIGHT: heteronyms have *distinct* Shavian forms (different pronunciations → different glyphs), so they're trivial in this direction. The mirror problem is HOMOPHONES: English words that sound identical and therefore share one Shavian spelling. Recovering English requires picking the right one from context.

Common collapses:
- to / too / two
- their / there / they're
- your / you're
- its / it's
- bear / bare, hear / here, etc.

PIPELINE:
1. Tokenize Shavian input.
2. Inverse-map each Shavian word via ReadLex → list of candidate English spellings.
3. Single candidate: emit it.
4. Multiple candidates (homophone set): two-tier resolution (below).
5. Punctuation + whitespace passthrough.

TWO-TIER HOMOPHONE RESOLUTION:

TIER 1 — Curated disambiguation rules (free, zero-latency).
- Hand-authored rule table per homophone set, encoding syntactic + lexical cues:
  - 'to' before infinitive verb; 'too' near {also, very, much}; 'two' near digits or quantifier context.
  - 'their' before noun; 'there' near {is, are, was}; 'they're' is contraction-like.
- Implement as POS + neighbor-word checks against the chosen POS tagger from Phase 0.
- Frequency prior as Tier-1 tie-breaker (most common spelling wins absent any cue).

TIER 2 — Bedrock LLM fallback.
- For homophone sets that the rules don't cover, or where Tier-1 confidence is low (no rule fires, frequency prior is close to 50/50), batch into a single Bedrock call.
- Same cheap-model + constrained-output pattern as Phase 2.
- Same in-process LRU cache.

PUBLIC SURFACES:
- 'wyrd shavian untransliterate "𐑖𐑱𐑝𐑾𐑯 𐑑𐑧𐑒𐑕𐑑"' CLI.

TESTS:
- Sentence pairs exercising the common homophone collapses, asserting correct English recovery.
- Round-trip accuracy test: take a curated English corpus, forward → reverse → assert word-level recovery (target >95%, recorded as Phase 6 baseline).
- Instrumentation: same per-request metrics as Phase 2 (tier1_hits / tier2_calls / cost).

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Capitalization recovery beyond Phase 5's namer-dot handling.
- OOV Shavian (not in inverse map) — emit phoneme-based English spelling, tag low-confidence.

title: Shavian Phase 2: semantic heteronym disambiguation (curated table + offline LLM audit)
description:
Resolve the ~20% of heteronyms that POS tagging can't distinguish — where both senses share a part of speech and only lexical context disambiguates. Examples: bow (ribbon vs bend), bass (fish vs instrument), tear (eye vs rip), sow (plant vs pig), dove (bird vs verb), wound (injury vs past of wind).

TWO-TIER RUNTIME RESOLUTION:

TIER 1 — Curated context-word table (free, zero-latency, deterministic).
- Hand-authored 'semantic heteronym context table' shipped as JSON in 'wyrd/generators/shavian/data/'.
- Each entry: word + the two pronunciations + a context-word list per sense.
  Example: tear → {/tɪər/: [eye, cry, drop, weep], /tɛər/: [rip, page, fabric, hole]}.
- At transliteration time, when a tagged token is in this table, score each sense by counting context-word hits in a window (±5 tokens). Pick higher score; tie → goto Tier 2.
- Cover the 'big 15' semantic heteronyms initially (Phase 0 audit produces the actual list).

TIER 2 — Bedrock LLM fallback (cheap, per-call latency).
- For tokens that are ambiguous AND either (a) not in the curated table, or (b) Tier 1 returned a tie, call the Bedrock model chosen in Phase 0.
- Prompt format: 'In: "<sentence>". Which sense of <word>? A) <gloss-a>, B) <gloss-b>. Reply A or B.' Constrained to 1 output token.
- Batch all ambiguous tokens in a paragraph into a single Bedrock call where possible (one prompt enumerating each ambiguity, structured output).
- Cache resolved (word, sense_options, context_hash) → sense in in-process LRU. Same paragraph translated twice in a warm container hits the cache.

INSTRUMENTATION:
- Emit per-request metrics: tokens_total, tier1_hits, tier2_calls, cache_hits, total_bedrock_cost_cents. Log to CloudWatch. Phase 6 evaluates these.

TESTS:
- Adversarial sentence pairs for each Tier-1 curated heteronym (must pass without LLM).
- A held-out test set the curation didn't see — Tier-2 LLM fallback must lift accuracy above the Tier-1-only baseline.
- Cost regression test: average Bedrock calls per 200-word paragraph on the eval corpus stays under a recorded threshold.

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Replacing the deterministic POS path with LLM — that would 100x cost for no win.
- Caching across containers (in-process LRU only for Phase 2; revisit in Phase 4 if needed).

title: Shavian Phase 1: deterministic forward pipeline (English → Shavian, POS-disambiguated)
description:
Build the core English → Shavian transliteration pipeline using only deterministic components. No LLM. Handles POS-distinguishable heteronyms; semantic-only cases (Phase 2) are scope-deferred.

PIPELINE:
1. Tokenize input English text (preserve whitespace + punctuation as passthrough tokens).
2. POS-tag tokens (using the tagger chosen in Phase 0).
3. For each word token, look up (lowercase, POS) in ReadLex.
4. If found: emit the lexicon's Shavian spelling.
5. If not found (OOV): fall back to G2P → phoneme sequence → phoneme→Shavian glyph map.
6. Preserve original capitalization (Shavian doesn't case, but track for the namer-dot work in Phase 5; for now just record).
7. Pass punctuation and whitespace through unchanged.

PUBLIC SURFACES:
- 'wyrd shavian transliterate "some english text"' CLI command (click group, will auto-mount).
- Module entry point usable by the Generator class in Phase 4.

TESTS (these are the acceptance bar):
- Fixture set of POS-distinguishable heteronym minimal pairs:
  - 'a minute detail' (adj /maɪˈnjuːt/) vs 'one minute later' (n /ˈmɪnɪt/)
  - 'record the song' (v) vs 'a clean record' (n)
  - 'present a gift' (v) vs 'a present moment' (adj)
  - 'permit me' (v) vs 'a parking permit' (n)
  - 'wind the clock' (v) vs 'a strong wind' (n)
  - 'lead the way' (v) vs 'lead pipe' (n)
  - 'an object' (n) vs 'I object' (v)
- Expected Shavian strings asserted exactly.
- OOV fallback exercised on at least 5 made-up words.

OUT OF SCOPE (deferred to later phases):
- Semantic heteronyms (bow, bass, tear) — Phase 2.
- Reverse direction — Phase 3.
- Generator class + SPA — Phase 4.
- Namer dot for proper nouns, numerals, abbreviations — Phase 5.

title: Shavian Phase 0: scope + deps decision (ReadLex audit, POS tagger, G2P)
description:
Establish the technical scope and dependency choices before any code lands. Output: a DECISIONS.md entry (or epic-design doc) covering the five open questions below.

DECISIONS NEEDED:

1) Lexicon source. ReadLex (Thomas Reed's Read Lexicon, maintained for Shavian heteronym disambiguation) is the obvious starting point. Confirm:
   - License is compatible with wyrd (CC-BY or similar, vs anything copyleft that would force re-licensing).
   - Distribution format (JSON / TSV / SQLite).
   - Heteronym coverage: count of POS-tagged heteronym entries and how many are semantic-only.
   - Vendor into repo as a data file vs fetch-at-install. Kenning data lives in 'wyrd/generators/<gen>/data/' — likely the same pattern.

2) POS tagger choice (Lambda size-budget sensitive):
   - spaCy 'en_core_web_sm' (~50MB wheel + model) — accurate, mature, well-tested.
   - NLTK perceptron tagger (~10MB) — lighter, slightly less accurate on edge cases.
   - Custom rule-based for the ~20 heteronyms that matter — smallest, but brittle.
   Pick based on actual measured impact on the Lambda zip size. Document the measurement.

3) G2P fallback for OOV words:
   - g2p-en (pure Python, CMUdict-backed, ~30MB) — established choice.
   - phonemizer (espeak-ng wrapper) — needs a binary, problematic for Lambda.
   - Phonetic ruleset only — minimal, accuracy hit on unusual words.
   Pick the one that fits Lambda + gives acceptable accuracy on a 100-word OOV sample.

4) Bedrock model for runtime disambiguation fallback. The runtime can call Bedrock when curated rules don't resolve an ambiguous token. Decide:
   - Model: Nova Micro (cheapest, ~$0.000035/1k input), Nova Lite, or Haiku 4.5 (smartest of the cheap tier). Benchmark all three on a curated 50-case heteronym/homophone set; pick the smallest model that hits >95% accuracy.
   - Bedrock IAM permissions: confirm the existing wyrd Lambda role can be granted 'bedrock:InvokeModel' for the chosen model, or whether a separate role/policy is needed.
   - Cost ceiling per request: pick a target (e.g. <$0.001 for a 200-word paragraph) and verify the chosen model + expected LLM-call rate stays under it.
   - Region availability: confirm the model is available in the wyrd Lambda's deploy region.

5) Caching strategy. Lambda has limited persistent state between invocations. Decide:
   - In-process LRU per warm container (zero infra cost, lost on cold start).
   - DynamoDB-backed cache keyed by (word, context_hash) — durable across containers.
   - Skip caching entirely if measured LLM-call rate is low enough to not matter.
   Recommendation: start with in-process LRU; revisit only if cost becomes a problem.

DELIVERABLES:
- DECISIONS.md (or generator-local design doc) entry covering all five.
- Empty 'wyrd/generators/shavian/' directory skeleton with a README stub citing the decisions.
- A 50-case benchmark CSV (heteronyms + homophones) used to compare Bedrock models, kept in 'wyrd/generators/shavian/data/'.
- File any follow-up tickets that surface during the audit.

NO CODE BEYOND THE SKELETON in this phase.

title: EPIC: Shavian transliterator generator (English↔Shavian, heteronym/homophone aware)
description:
Add a 'shavian' generator to wyrd that transliterates English text into Shavian (and back), producing runic/foreign-looking text usable as in-game prop documents for TTRPG campaigns.

THREE HARD PROBLEMS:

1) Heteronyms in forward direction. Words like 'minute' (n /ˈmɪnɪt/ vs adj /maɪˈnjuːt/), 'record', 'wind', 'lead', 'bow', 'tear'. Split into:
   - POS-distinguishable (~80%): resolved by POS tagger + POS-keyed lexicon.
   - Semantic-only (~20%): resolved by curated context rules + LLM fallback.

2) Homophones in reverse direction. Heteronyms back-translate cleanly (distinct Shavian → distinct English), but homophones (to/too/two, their/there/they're) collapse to one Shavian form and need context to recover. Same curated-rules-plus-LLM-fallback shape.

3) OOV proper names. Campaign documents are saturated with proper nouns; G2P chokes on them ('Worcestershire', 'Drizzt'). LLM fallback for pronunciation is needed specifically for the proper-name path.

THREE-TIER ARCHITECTURE (each problem resolved the same way):
1. Lexicon path (free, zero-latency, deterministic): ReadLex (word, POS) → Shavian. Handles the bulk of common English.
2. Curated rule path (free, zero-latency, deterministic): small hand-authored tables for the most common ambiguous cases.
3. Bedrock LLM fallback (cheap, per-call latency): when Tiers 1–2 don't resolve, call a cheap Bedrock model (Nova Micro / Lite / Haiku — Phase 0 picks). Constrained, often single-token outputs. In-process LRU cache.

Lambda runtime CAN call Bedrock at request time — it's a normal AWS SDK call. Tiers 1–2 keep cost down by handling the common cases for free; LLM is the long-tail fallback. Expected LLM rate on real text: a small fraction of tokens.

PHASES:
- Phase 0: scope + deps decision (ReadLex audit, POS tagger size budget, G2P lib choice, Bedrock model + IAM + cost ceiling).
- Phase 1: deterministic forward pipeline (English → Shavian), POS-disambiguated heteronyms. No LLM.
- Phase 1b: OOV + proper-name pronunciation via Bedrock fallback.
- Phase 2: semantic heteronym disambiguation (curated rules + Bedrock fallback).
- Phase 3: reverse pipeline (Shavian → English) with homophone resolution (curated rules + Bedrock fallback).
- Phase 4: Generator class + manifest + SPA wiring; 'use_llm_fallback' option; cache wiring.
- Phase 5: polish — namer dot, numerals, abbreviations, punctuation, round-trip preservation.
- Phase 6: evaluation harness (corpus, round-trip accuracy, heteronym accuracy, LLM-call rate, cost).

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
- 'wyrd shavian transliterate' produces correct Shavian for a curated heteronym test set (target: 100% POS-distinguishable + >95% semantic with LLM fallback).
- Proper-name rendering matches expected pronunciation for a curated name list (>95%).
- Round-trip (forward → reverse) on the eval corpus recovers >95% of words.
- Bedrock cost per 200-word paragraph stays under $0.001 with default model.
- Lambda bundle size stays under the existing deploy budget.
- SPA exposes the generator via manifest with no client changes.
