title: fantasy_morpheme: add dump + build round-trip
description:
Discovered alongside wyrd-6gpy: the fantasy_morpheme table (1,308 rows in live DB) has neither dump-side nor build-side support in the JSONL pipeline.

The bundle's fantasy_morphemes top-level field (244 entries shipped) is populated by collect_fantasy_morphemes(db) from lexicon.py — reads from the fantasy_morpheme table. On a full rebuild-from-jsonl, the table is empty (no JSONL events to populate it) → bundle export emits no fantasy_morphemes field → 244 fantasy morphemes vanish from the rebuilt bundle.

Schema (live DB):
CREATE TABLE fantasy_morpheme (
  id, input_name, input_description, usable, etymon_id, bar_reason,
  resolution_method, approach_version, confidence, citation, reasoning,
  unapproved_language, unapproved_form
);

This is part of the wyrd-vz7f fantasy creature pipeline. The table is operator-mining-fed: 'lexicon mine-fantasy-name' adds rows. Dump-side missing entirely; build-side missing entirely.

Scope:
1. jsonl_dump: add fantasy_morpheme dump path. Likely lives in a non-per-source file (the table has etymon_id FK but no source attribution) — could be data/mining/_fantasy_morphemes.jsonl similar to _curation.jsonl.
2. jsonl_build: add a Pass 1 reader for the fantasy_morpheme row type + Pass 2 inserter. etymon_id resolves via the etymon_id_by_ref map.
3. Tests: round-trip a fantasy morpheme through dump → rebuild → verify bundle export contains it.

Separate from wyrd-6gpy (toponym + attestation round-trip) because fantasy_morpheme is a different table with no source attribution. Both are L2 dump coverage gaps but they're independent fixes.
notes:
PR #206 merged. Phase A (code + tests) complete. The fantasy_morpheme table now round-trips through dump → JSONL → build with full field fidelity (all 12 scalar columns + etymon_ref FK resolution).

Key design notes:
- _fantasy_morphemes.jsonl carries a synthetic 'fantasy-mining' source declaration (mirrors _curation.jsonl pattern); the live DB has no fantasy-mining row, but rebuilt DBs do
- fantasy-mining added to DEFAULT_BULK_EXCLUDED_SOURCES so dump_all_sources doesn't emit a competing per-source file on rebuilt DBs
- INSERT OR IGNORE on (input_name, approach_version) UNIQUE for idempotency; counter tracks actual inserts via rowcount (silent-failure-hunter caught the original bug where NOT NULL violations were swallowed)
- Three-branch orphan/null distinction in _insert_fantasy_morpheme_rows:
  * no etymon_ref field → insert NULL etymon_id (barred morpheme)
  * etymon_ref present but unresolved → orphan + skip (don't silently null)
  * etymon_ref resolved → insert with FK

Phase A2 (operator: dump → commit _fantasy_morphemes.jsonl with ~1308 rows) still TODO.

title: Dashboard attestation round-trip: language-report numbers must survive dump/rebuild/re-export
description:
Phase 3 (wyrd-xrnw, PR #200) pins that the bundle JSON round-trips byte-identically. The wyrd-hidb parent ticket also requires that 'the dashboard's bundle-attestation numbers survive the round trip' — a strictly stronger contract because the dashboard reads from BOTH the bundle (for attestation-breakdown classification) and the rebuilt DB (for corpus depth, citation depth, inflection coverage, era-reflex coverage, stratum coverage, IPA coverage). A round trip that preserves bundle bytes but loses lexicon-side provenance would silently drift the dashboard.

Background
==========

The dashboard is the 'lexicon language-report' CLI command (cli.py:7166), backed by language_quality.py. Per-language scorecard with sections:

* Corpus depth (_corpus_depth, language_quality.py:881) — DB-side
* Citation depth (_citation_depth, language_quality.py:1158) — DB-side
* Inflection coverage (_inflection_coverage, ~957) — DB-side
* Variant coverage (_variant_coverage, ~1000) — DB-side
* Era-reflex coverage (_era_reflex_coverage, ~1018) — DB-side
* Stratum coverage (_stratum_coverage, ~1142) — DB-side
* IPA coverage (_lexicon_ipa_coverage / _bundle_ipa_coverage) — both
* Bundle attestation breakdown (_bundle_attestation_breakdown, ~514) — bundle-side. The acceptance-named one. Bins subjects into scholar_attested / empirical_only / rando_only / uncited per the wyrd-lc94 rule.

What this ticket adds
=====================

An integration test (likely tests/test_kenning_hidb_dashboard_round_trip.py or extending the existing Phase 3 round-trip file) that:

1. Builds the same synthetic fixture used by wyrd-xrnw's round-trip test (tests/test_kenning_hidb_phase3_round_trip.py::_populate_round_trip_fixture).
2. Runs run_full_enrichment(apply=True, curation_state={}) on the pre-DB and exports the bundle.
3. Computes the language_quality scorecard against (pre-DB, pre-bundle). Call this dashboard_pre.
4. Dumps JSONL → wipes → rebuilds DB → re-runs enrichment → re-exports bundle.
5. Computes the scorecard against (rebuilt-DB, rebuilt-bundle). Call this dashboard_rebuilt.
6. Asserts dashboard_pre == dashboard_rebuilt for every section AND, specifically, the _bundle_attestation_breakdown bin counts match (the named acceptance criterion).

Likely shape of the helper:



Acceptance
==========

* New CI-runnable test passes against the synthetic fixture.
* On a deliberately introduced provenance loss (e.g. dropping etymon_citation rows during dump/rebuild), the test fails loudly with a structured diff showing WHICH section / WHICH language drifted.
* The bundle_attestation_breakdown bin counts (scholar_attested / empirical_only / rando_only / uncited) match exactly between pre and rebuilt.
* Test runtime stays comparable to the existing Phase 3 round-trip test (~2-3s).

Why this is separate from wyrd-w3x0
====================================

wyrd-w3x0 is the operator-runnable real-data bundle byte-diff. This is the CI-runnable dashboard-numbers structural diff. Different surface, different signal:

* wyrd-w3x0 catches drift in the SHIPPED bundle's bytes vs the committed file (release-decision-relevant).
* This ticket catches drift in the DASHBOARD's signal vs the in-DB ground truth (provenance-loss-relevant).

Both are needed before wyrd-hidb closes.

Related
=======

* wyrd-hidb (parent) — the dashboard-attestation acceptance criterion that's not yet met
* wyrd-xrnw (✓ closed) — the byte-identical bundle test that's a prerequisite (the dashboard reads the bundle)
* wyrd-w3x0 — the operator-runnable real-data complement to wyrd-xrnw
close_reason: Dashboard attestation round-trip test merged in PR #202 (909de76). Pins that compute_report's scorecards are byte-stable across dump → wipe → rebuild → enrich → re-export — strictly stronger than Phase 3's bundle-byte test because the dashboard reads from BOTH the bundle AND the lexicon DB. 11 tests covering: broad round-trip invariant, attestation breakdown specifically (with sanity guards + rando-port etymon for non-vacuous bin coverage), negative drift detection, 5 _format_dashboard_drift branch tests (no-drift, top-level scalar, truncation, duplicate-language guard, dict-aware per-key diff), helper unit test, JSON serializability. 4-round Gemini loop + 8 agent reviewers, all threads resolved.

title: lexicon diff-bundle: operator-runnable real-data round-trip drift check
description:
Phase 3 of wyrd-hidb (PR #200, merged as 4053cf5) shipped a CI-runnable round-trip invariant test using a synthetic fixture. That catches pipeline-level non-determinism (iteration order, datetime stamps, RNG leaks) but does NOT catch real-data drift between the committed wyrd/generators/kenning/data/meanings.json bundle and what a fresh rebuild would produce from the operator's live ~/.wyrd/sources/ + S3 wiktextract + data/mining/ JSONLs.

This ticket adds the missing operator-runnable check.

Background
==========

The existing 'lexicon diff-rebuild' command (cli.py:3057) only compares L2 table row counts between current DB and a rebuild, not bundle output. It's the right scaffolding to extend, but adding a --bundle-diff flag mixes two concerns. Cleaner: a new 'lexicon diff-bundle' command.

Per wyrd-j2bv finding: rebuild-from-jsonl from L2 alone produces ~24% of the canonical bundle because wiktionary-empirical citations live in L1 wiktextract slices that require S3 fetch + ~/.wyrd/sources/ population. So diff-bundle must invoke the L1 ingest path before the L3 enrichment chain, OR document that the operator must have ~/.wyrd/sources pre-populated.

Proposed shape
==============



Workflow:
1. Optional: fetch bulk wiktextract slices from S3 to ~/.wyrd/sources (--fetch-bulk).
2. Rebuild a temp DB from JSONL + bulk slices.
3. Run run_full_enrichment(apply=True, curation_state=collect_curation_overrides(paths)).
4. Run export_meanings (with the same min_witnesses / lang_thresholds the CLI default uses) + collect_canonical_decompositions + collect_fantasy_morphemes.
5. Serialize via 'json.dumps(bundle, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)' — the EXACT format the CLI 'lexicon export-meanings --output' writes.
6. Read the committed bundle file.
7. Diff:
   - If bytes-identical: exit 0, print 'No drift'.
   - If different: produce a structured summary — total bytes diff, first divergence location with ±100 char window, subjects-added / subjects-removed / subjects-changed counts (parse both as JSON for the structural diff). Exit 1.

Acceptance
==========

* 'lexicon diff-bundle' runs end-to-end against the operator's live data and the committed bundle file, exits 0 when round-trip is clean, exit 1 + readable summary when drift exists.
* The first-divergence window is helpful, not a 30 MB blob dump.
* The command's contract is documented in L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md as the pre-release drift check (alongside the existing 'diff-rebuild' which stays for the row-count-only check).
* Optional: a Makefile target or CI gate that runs diff-bundle on main and fails the release if it's not clean. (Out of scope for THIS ticket; file a follow-up for the gate.)

Why operator-runnable, not CI
============================

CI runners don't have ~/.wyrd/sources (4.6 GB of wiktextract slices) and the cost of pulling them on every CI run is prohibitive. The synthetic-fixture test on CI catches the deterministic-pipeline class of regression; this command catches the data-coupled class (bundle stale relative to JSONLs, witness-gate threshold drift, etc.). Operators run it before each bundle re-export.

Related
=======

* wyrd-hidb (parent) — closes when this lands + dashboard-attestation work
* wyrd-0vj3 — bulk-data storage; --fetch-bulk hooks into the S3 path it defines
* PR #200 / wyrd-xrnw — Phase 3 synthetic round-trip test (the CI-side complement to this)

title: Restore 'one-command rebuild': L1 wiktextract ingest + L3 derivations in rebuild-from-jsonl
description:
Context
=======

Today `lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment` does:
1. Wipe + init schema
2. Replay every data/mining/<source>.jsonl
3. Run normalize-ocr + link-lemmas L3 passes (the wyrd-ilam orchestrator)

It does NOT run:
* L1 wiktextract bulk ingest (`ingest-wiktionary` per slice)
* L3 derivations not yet migrated: decompose, cluster-cognates, classify-stratum, derive-english-shaped, project-period-forms

Operators must run these manually before/after rebuild-from-jsonl. Discovered in the wyrd-j2bv Latin lift session: rebuild-from-jsonl from L2 only produces a bundle with ~24% the subject count of the canonical bundle because wiktionary-empirical citations are missing — visible immediately in `lexicon rando-port-readiness` showing 0 empirical attestation across all languages.

Why it matters
==============

The 'JSONL is source of truth' claim depends on a one-command rebuild. Without that:
* Recovering from DB loss requires multi-hour operator-driven pipelines.
* Round-trip invariants (dump-jsonl → wipe → rebuild → dump-jsonl → diff) can't be tested cleanly.
* Bundle export drift is hard to detect — there's no canonical 'fresh rebuild' to compare against.

Dependencies
============

This work depends on the bulk-data-storage-strategy decision (companion ticket). The wiktextract ingest path depends on where the .jsonl slices live.

Scope (after the storage decision lands)
========================================

1. Wire each missing L3 pass into the canonical enrichment chain in `enrichment.py:run_ocr_lemma_enrichment` (or successor). Canonical order:
   * L1 ingest (per storage decision) — only if dest table empty
   * L2 replay (current behavior)
   * normalize-ocr
   * link-lemmas
   * apply-curation-overrides
   * decompose
   * cluster-cognates
   * classify-stratum
   * derive-english-shaped
   * project-period-forms

2. Add an integration test: dump-jsonl → wipe DB → rebuild --with-enrichment → export-meanings → byte-diff against committed bundle. Diff should be empty (or documented if any pass is non-deterministic).

3. Update L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md to remove the 'operators still run those manually post-rebuild' caveat.

Acceptance
==========

* `lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl --with-enrichment` followed by `lexicon export-meanings --output wyrd/generators/kenning/data/meanings.json` produces a bundle byte-identical (or documented-diff) to main.
* CI integration test catches drift.
* The dashboard's bundle-attestation numbers survive the round trip.

Linked to wyrd-eni4 (terminal 'JSONL is source of truth' goal). Companion to bulk-data-storage-strategy ticket.

title: Bulk-data storage strategy for wiktextract slices and similar large extracts
description:
Context
=======

The wyrd-eni4 epic moved per-source mining to a JSONL-as-source-of-truth pattern (data/mining/<source>.jsonl). The migration is incomplete: bulk-data sources remain in sources/ (gitignored).

Inventory of sources/ — 4.6 GB total across ~50 wiktextract slices:
* wiktextract_english.jsonl                  2.8 GB
* wiktextract_arabic.jsonl                   476 MB
* wiktextract_ancient_greek.jsonl            277 MB
* wiktextract_irish, _old_english             ~112 MB each
* wiktextract_sanskrit                        98 MB
* (~40 smaller slices)                       totalling ~700 MB
* os_opennames/                              1.8 GB (already gitignored; operator-CSV pattern)

Compression ratios (sampled):
* gzip jsonl → ~10% (4.6 GB → ~460 MB)
* zstd -19 jsonl → ~7.4% (4.6 GB → ~340 MB)

Problem
=======

`lexicon rebuild-from-jsonl` doesn't re-ingest L1 wiktextract. Operator must manually run `ingest-wiktionary` per slice before rebuilding the bundle. If both `~/.wyrd/lexicon.db` AND `sources/` are lost, the wiktionary-empirical tier can't be reconstructed without re-mining Wiktionary upstream — a multi-hour pipeline.

So the 'JSONL is source of truth' claim is partial: scholar mining + manual curation + Phase 3 ingesters round-trip cleanly, but the bulk wiktextract layer doesn't.

Decision options
================

Pick one (or hybrid):

**1. Status quo — gitignored sources/, scripts re-ingest each rebuild**
  Pros: zero disk/git cost.
  Cons: bus-factor problem; rebuild requires hours of upstream mining.
  Cost: 0 MB committed; hours per checkout.

**2. Commit raw .jsonl slices to git**
  Pros: maximum reproducibility; vanilla `git clone` is enough.
  Cons: ~4.6 GB in git history; slow clones; may exceed repo-size norms.
  Cost: ~4.6 GB (or ~700 MB-1 GB for ship-only subset).

**3. Commit gzip/zstd-compressed .jsonl.{gz,zst} slices to git**
  Pros: ~10x smaller (340-460 MB); vanilla checkout; modify ingest-wiktionary to read transparently.
  Cons: still significant repo growth; compressed blobs churn poorly in git history.
  Cost: ~340-460 MB committed.

**4. Store .jsonl slices in ~/.wyrd/sources/ (local cache, not in git)**
  Pros: git stays lean; lexicon DB + sources travel together as a 'lexicon environment'.
  Cons: doesn't solve bus-factor; needs documented re-mining/download flow.
  Cost: 0 MB committed.

**5. Git LFS for .jsonl slices**
  Pros: git-native; LFS handles big files; vanilla clone still works (with LFS).
  Cons: LFS server + bandwidth quota; team adoption.
  Cost: ~4.6 GB on LFS; GitHub LFS quota.

**6. External object store with manifest in git (S3 / GCS / R2)**
  Pros: bulk data outside git; manifest + checksums versioned; `lexicon ingest-wiktionary --from-manifest` auto-fetches.
  Cons: infra setup; per-contributor read access; manifest schema design.
  Cost: small manifest in git; cloud bucket storage.

**7. Separate data-only git repo (precedent: pfsrd2-data in this workspace)**
  Pros: workspace precedent (see /home/devon/521Studios/CLAUDE.md pfsrd2-data); decouples data churn; schema-versioned branches.
  Cons: two-repo coordination; ingester needs configurable path.
  Cost: separate repo growth.

**8. DVC (Data Version Control)**
  Pros: purpose-built; integrates with git; pluggable remotes.
  Cons: DVC adoption / learning curve.
  Cost: small DVC metadata in git; storage in chosen remote.

**9. Hybrid: gitignored sources/ + automation downloads from upstream**
  Pros: zero data in git; upstream (Kaikki.org) is source of truth.
  Cons: external dep on Kaikki; bandwidth per checkout; license/etiquette concerns.
  Cost: 0 MB committed; hours per checkout.

Acceptance
==========

* Operator picks an option (possibly hybrid).
* Update DEFAULT_BULK_EXCLUDED_SOURCES policy in jsonl_dump.py and the rebuild-from-jsonl path to integrate chosen storage.
* Document in wyrd/generators/kenning/L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md.
* Unblocks the 'one-command rebuild' ticket (companion).

Linked to wyrd-eni4 (terminal 'JSONL is source of truth' goal).
design: Implementation plan: docs/plans/wyrd-0vj3.md (region us-east-2, bucket 521studios-staging-wyrd-lexicon-bulk via 521-Staging-Admin profile, ~/.wyrd/config.toml local config, two-PR phasing — PR A infra + ingest plumbing, PR B (wyrd-hidb) wires into rebuild-from-jsonl)
notes:
Operator preference (2026-05-13): S3 is available; OK with storing
bulk .jsonl slices in S3 and a fetch script populating
~/.wyrd/sources/ on demand. This is a hybrid of options 4 (local
cache) + 6 (external object store with manifest).

Concrete shape worth scoping:
* S3 bucket layout: s3://<bucket>/wiktextract/<version>/<slice>.jsonl(.zst?)
* Manifest in git: data/mining/_bulk_manifest.json with {slice, s3_uri, sha256, version}
* Fetch CLI: `lexicon fetch-bulk-sources` reads manifest, downloads missing/stale slices to ~/.wyrd/sources/ (gitignored), validates checksums
* rebuild-from-jsonl behavior: optionally auto-fetch if --fetch-bulk passed, or fail loudly with a hint to run fetch-bulk-sources first
* zstd compression on the S3 side (~7.4% ratio) — keeps bucket size + bandwidth low; ingest reads transparently via zstd python lib

Open sub-decisions:
* Public-read bucket vs IAM-gated (lets-roll-style AWS profiles already exist in workspace)
* Per-slice versioning vs whole-corpus snapshot version
* Whether to also store the OS Open Names CSV here (same pattern, different schema)
close_reason:
Closed via ride-along on PR #202 (wyrd-alzd). All acceptance criteria + open sub-decisions resolved:

1. Operator picked the strategy (option 4+6 hybrid: S3 + ~/.wyrd cache + manifest in git) — decision recorded 2026-05-13.
2. Infrastructure shipped: bulk_sources.py module (PR #195), fetch/push/verify-bulk-sources CLI commands, --fetch-bulk flag threading through rebuild-from-jsonl, manifest seeded with all 38 wiktextract slices (PR #197), zstd compression on S3 side.
3. L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md now documents the rebuild operator workflow with --fetch-bulk + the four design decisions from docs/plans/wyrd-0vj3.md (IAM=single-user-dev, versioning=S3+sha256, CI=none, migration=operator-driven push-bulk-sources).
4. os_opennames CSV corpus declared out of scope (separate operator-CSV pattern, gitignored, no pressure to move) — documented inline.

Implementation plan in docs/plans/wyrd-0vj3.md remains as the durable design doc. Anything truly new about bulk-data storage (e.g. hosting os_opennames in S3) can land via fresh tickets.

title: Phase 3a: Re-mine scholar gazetteers to extract ALL place names mentioned (not just etymon-attributed)
description:
Current scholar-mined toponyms (4,783 rows pre-Domesday) come from etymon-attributed entries — when Mawer 1920 etc. explicitly decompose a toponym. But these gazetteers ALSO mention place names in passing ('as found in Birmingham', 'compare Suttone (Domesday)', cross-references between entries).

Re-mining pass: walk each scholar source, extract every place name reference (not requiring etymon decomposition). Emit as 'toponym' + 'attestation' events to the source's L2 JSONL.

Expected lift: substantially more ME-era forms from existing work, without re-paying LLM extraction cost. Also fills gaps in the toponym corpus that the Wikipedia scrapes miss.

Each source: Mawer 1920, Ekwall 1922, Joyce 1898, etc. — one PR per source family ideally.

title: Phase 3b: OS Open Names ingest (~1M GB place names, OGL v3)
description:
Per user 2026-05-12: existing english_place_names.json (~20K Wikipedia scrapes) under-represents villages and hamlets. OS Open Names (Ordnance Survey, Open Government Licence v3 — commercial-friendly) provides ~1M GB place names with grid refs.

Tractable in our L2 JSONL pattern? At 1M rows × ~200 bytes = 200MB. Too large for git. Two paths:
(a) Keep OS Open Names file in sources/ (L1), regenerate L2 on demand by parsing slice
(b) Only commit to L2 the SUBSET that gets used in decomposition or attestation

Path (a) is consistent with how wiktextract is treated. The L2 JSONL becomes a per-toponym 'attestation' for places that decompose into morphemes; the master list stays L1.

Acceptance:

title: Ingest Open Domesday (1086) place-name corpus + period-form attestations
description:
Per user 2026-05-12: pulling the Domesday Book gives us four overlapping wins:

1. **Toponym corpus expansion** — ~13,500 settlements with 1086 attestations
2. **rando-port validation** — OE morphemes that look 'dead' in modern Wikipedia probably appear in Domesday spellings (-tun, -ham, -aecer, etc.)
3. **Period-form data (Tier 3 era reflex)** — every Domesday entry IS a period-form attestation; F.Tier-3 for English jumps from ~60 to ~13K
4. **attested_year backbone** — 1086 is a solid early benchmark for the English chain

Source: Open Domesday (opendomesday.org) — Williams-Erskine translation, CC-BY. Provides CSV/JSON export with county, hundred, Domesday name, modern equivalent (where known), holder, value, population.

- New `domesday_ingest` CLI command (under `wyrd kenning lexicon`)
- Source row `domesday_book_1086` added to `source` table

title: Dashboard: --source / --tag filters for diagnostic slices (rando-port, fantasy, single scholar source)
description:
Per user 2026-05-12, operators want to view the dashboard restricted to a specific seed slice — e.g.:

- 'How are rando-port grandfather words doing?' → seed = etymons cited by source 'rando-port'
- 'How are fantasy / monster / creature words doing?' → seed = etymons tagged 'fantasy' (or 'monster', 'creature')
- 'How are the Mawer 1920 attestations doing?' → seed = etymons cited by source 'mawer_1920_northumberland_durham'

The wyrd-bfv1 eligible-set machinery already supports a parameterized seed. Extend populate_eligible_etymon_table:

- source_filter: str | None — when set, step (1) cited becomes 'cited by this source' instead of 'cited by any source'; step (3) fantasy skipped
- tag_filter: str | None — when set, step (1) cited skipped; step (3) tagged-with-this-tag only

Descent + lemma rollup STILL apply from the restricted seed (so the rando-port view includes the OE/ME context of grandfather words, not just the rando-port-citation rows themselves).

CLI: --source SOURCE_ID and --tag TAG, mutually exclusive. Dashboard header shows active filter so the operator knows what slice they're looking at.

Acceptance:
- --source rando-port renders a dashboard restricted to rando-port-cited etymons + descent neighbors + lemma children
- --tag fantasy renders a dashboard restricted to fantasy/monster/creature-tagged etymons + descent + lemma
- --source mawer_1920_northumberland_durham renders a single-source dashboard
- Header notes the active filter

- COVERAGE.md updated

title: Dashboard denominators: restrict to generator-eligible etymons (1-hop)
description:
Dashboard's per-language metrics currently divide by every etymon row in the DB (e.g. modern-english 1.4M denominator). That's mostly the wyrd-dxu2 Kaikki wiktextract dump — raw corpus material for future mining, NOT what the kenning name generator can actually use. So every coverage % is denominator-collapsed.

Per user 2026-05-12: the dashboard should report on 'words the name generator would use'. Eligible set definition:

Generator-eligible etymon = ANY of:
  1. Has ≥1 row in etymon_citation (rando-port OR scholar source)
  2. 1-hop parent or child via etymon_descent of a cited etymon
  3. lemma_id points to an eligible etymon (within-language inflection rollup)
  4. Tagged 'fantasy' / 'monster' / 'creature' in etymon_tag (the explicit fiction exception)

1-hop ONLY (not transitive) — the wiktextract Kaikki ingest built lateral descent edges (English ← Latin ← Greek ← PIE) that connect ~70% of the corpus to some cited node somewhere via transitive closure, which defeats the intent. 1-hop captures 'one era step more modern / more eldritch' — the user-stated grain.

Reduction sizes (1-hop):
  - modern-english: 1.4M → 21,892 (-98.4%)
  - middle-english: 62K → 8,885 (-85.8%)
  - old-english:    72K → 13,407 (-81.5%)
  - welsh:          27K → 3,011 (-88.8%)
  - irish:          34K → 2,162 (-93.7%)
  - scottish-gaelic:17K → 706    (-96.0%)
  - latin:          29K → 928    (-96.8%)

Affected metrics (every per-language coverage %):
  - A. Corpus depth: split into raw + eligible
  - C. Tag coverage (lexicon side): denom → eligible
  - D. Inflection: denom → eligible lemmas
  - E. Variants: denom → eligible
  - F. Era reflex (lex side): denom → eligible
  - G. Stratum: denom → eligible
  - H. IPA (lex side): denom → eligible
  - I. Citation depth: denom → eligible
  - Tier-4 phonology walk: restrict to eligible (also massive speedup, 1.4M → ~22K)

Side effect: Tier-4 dashboard walk drops from ~3 min modern-english to <5s.

Bundle-side metrics (B, B₂, C₂, F₂ bundle, H bundle) unchanged — those use bundle-side denominators which are already correct.

COVERAGE.md updated with rationale; the metric definitions doc updated to call out eligible-set.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #172. Dashboard's per-language metrics now restrict denominators to generator-eligible etymons (cited ∪ 1-hop descent ∪ lemma rollup ∪ fantasy-tagged). ModE denominator drops from 1.4M to 22K; every coverage % rises to operator-meaningful levels. Full dashboard run drops from 12 min to 43 s (Tier-4 walk also restricted).

title: Thread sense-category → tag extraction through full wiktextract ingest
description:
The full ingest-wiktionary path (wiktextract_ingester._process_entry) extracts etymology, descent, pronunciation, original_script, transliteration — but NOT tags. The corpus-miner path (wiktextract_corpus_miner._write_one + _select_canonical_sense + _map_categories_to_tags) does extract tags from sense categories, but only touches etymons whose surface matches a place-name fragment.

Consequence: the wyrd-dxu2 modern-english slice ingest (PR #164) created ~1.4M new modern-english etymon rows, all of them tag-less. Dashboard now shows modern-english at C 2/15 (13.3%) reference-tag hits despite the slice having rich categories. Modern-english is 29.2% of bundle words — biggest single language — so this tag gap suppresses generation quality for the most-used language.

Fix path:
1. Promote _map_categories_to_tags to a shared module (or import it into wiktextract_ingester from wiktextract_corpus_miner)
2. In wiktextract_ingester._process_entry, after the etymon upsert, iterate senses and:
   - Apply _map_categories_to_tags to each sense's categories
   - db.add_tag(etymon_id, tag) for each mapped tag (INSERT OR IGNORE so re-runs are idempotent)
3. Add a 'tags_added' counter to the per-run summary
4. Re-run ingest-wiktionary --apply on the English slice (and ideally all other ingested slices for consistency)

Acceptance:
- modern-english tag coverage in DB jumps from 0.0% to a meaningful % (target: 30%+ on lemmas with senses+categories)
- Bundle's C row for modern-english jumps from 2/15 to 12+/15 reference-tag hits
- Per-run summary surfaces 'tags_added' counter
- Existing corpus-miner path's _write_one still adds tags (no double-counting; INSERT OR IGNORE handles it)
- 2232+ tests still pass
- Re-exported bundle's modifier_tags + per-language modifier_tags fields reflect the new tag coverage

Trade-off: full ingest writes tags on 1.4M English etymons; many of those have no senses (just etymology-template placeholders). Those rows would still be tag-less but the entries WITH senses would all get tagged. That's the right behavior.

title: Backfill IPA via ingest-wiktionary on existing European wiktextract slices
description:
The corpus-miner path (mine-wiktextract-corpus) only touches etymons whose surface matches an unaccounted place-name fragment — ~1% of OE etymons (4858 of 73871 after the wyrd-69s5 backfill in PR #159). The wiktextract slices already on disk (OE, ON, OF, ME, welsh, irish, scottish-gaelic, old-irish, middle-irish, breton, cornish, manx, proto-celtic) contain IPA in their sounds arrays for many entries the corpus miner never touches.

The FULL ingest path (wyrd kenning lexicon ingest-wiktionary <slice>) walks every entry in the slice via wiktextract_ingester._process_entry — which already extracts and writes pronunciation_ipa via _extract_pronunciation since wyrd-ha9q. It also handles etymology templates and descent edges.

Running ingest-wiktionary on the existing slices should:
1. Backfill IPA on existing etymons via COALESCE on upsert
2. Create new etymons for entries the corpus miner skipped
3. Add etymon_descent edges

Acceptance:
- Run ingest-wiktionary --apply on at least the OE + ON + OF slices
- Verify per-language IPA coverage jumps significantly in the lexicon table:
    target: OE from 1.0% to 50%+
    target: ON from 0.1% to meaningful %
    target: OF from 0.9% to meaningful %
- Re-export bundle so renderings.ipa surfaces the new IPA
- Dashboard rerun shows the lifts in Section H

Operational cost estimate:
- OE slice ~73K entries × ~50ms = ~1 hour per slice
- ON / OF similar
- All ~12 slices: several hours total, but can be incremental

Risk: full ingest does MORE than backfill IPA — it also writes descent edges. That may create new cluster connections that affect family rollup behavior elsewhere (e.g. the wyrd-vn09 grandfather audit). Worth doing dry-runs first to size the impact.

Separate from wyrd-dxu2 which is specifically about ACQUIRING a new modern-english wiktextract slice (since one isn't on disk).

title: IPA / pronunciation: 0% coverage on every shipped language; bundle ships empty renderings
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09: user expected pronunciation data in generator output, found 'renderings: {}' on every component. Investigation shows the lexicon DB has zero IPA for every European / ancient language we ship:

    old-english:      0/73,871   0.0%
    middle-english:   0/54,250   0.0%
    irish:            0/34,204   0.0%
    welsh:            0/27,040   0.0%
    modern-english:   0/21,175   0.0%
    scottish-gaelic:  0/17,403   0.0%
    old-norse:        0/14,696   0.0%
    latin:            0/14,694   0.0%
    proto-germanic:   0/13,408   0.0%
    old-french:       (similar)

The 5% global IPA coverage is concentrated in non-European langs we don't ship (Arabic 23.6%, Persian 59.3%, Hebrew 19.5%). 

The data path is fully wired — etymon.pronunciation_ipa column exists, load_meanings parses it, NewName.components() emits a 'renderings' slot with an 'ipa' subslot, the SPA reads it. The pipe is empty all the way back to the source.

Causes to investigate (in priority order):

1. wiktextract ingest skipping the 'sounds' field on European-language entries. The mining path probably drops it. Fix: thread IPA through mine-wiktextract-corpus / mine-wiktextract-forms upserts.

2. Modern English Wiktionary has IPA on most entries — should give us 90%+ for modern-english. Lower-hanging fruit.

3. Old English / Latin / Old Norse on Wiktionary often DO have reconstructed IPA or at least 'pronunciation' notes — extracting these takes more parsing care but is doable.

4. SPA-side rendering: even with empty renderings, the panel should show 'pronunciation: not attested' or similar so the user knows it's a data gap, not a UI bug. Currently the empty {} is invisible.

- Spot-check 10 generated names from a re-emitted bundle: most components carry non-empty 'ipa' for modern-english parts.

title: Generator: drop citations from description() text — they're already in components for the SPA
description:
Bug surfaced 2026-05-09: NewName.description() inlines citation lists into the human-readable explanation text, producing dense walls like:

    -don- ( To do, perform (an activity) or CL contraction of do + an or EN dwellings...; cited by mawer_1920_northumberland_durham, wiktionary-empirical) -hole- ( hole or EN Dale, Hollow, Vale, Valley...; cited by ekwall_1922_lancashire, mawer_1920_northumberland_durham, mawer_stenton_1927_worcestershire (+4 more)) ...

The SPA already renders citations in a structured expandable component (the components() output carries 'citations' per part). The description() text should be the COMPACT human-readable summary — gloss block only, no citations.

Fix: strip the '; cited by ...' tail from NewName.description() output.

Sketch (proportions.py around line 762-780):
    # current:
    if citations:
        cite_block = f'; cited by {_format_citations_for_description(citations)}'
    else:
        cite_block = ''
    results.append(f'{head} ({gloss_block}{cite_block})')

title: Generator: prevent same usage from being picked for adjacent slots within a name
description:
Bug surfaced 2026-05-09 in generated output post-wyrd-eni4 bundle: names like 'port port', 'les les Betton Kergan', 'Lowmall Lowy' have the SAME morpheme picked twice in adjacent slots (within a word, or across words). Independent per-slot sampling allows duplicates and the larger bundle has heavily-skewed buckets that surface dupes more often.

Root cause: proportions.NameGenerator._select_no_tag / _select_tags pick each slot independently via meaning_gen.select(...). No tracking of prior-slot usage. With the new bundle, certain buckets (especially location='inner' under the existing too-permissive semantics — see related ticket on inner) are dominated by a few high-frequency entries, so adjacent picks dupe.

Fix: track the prior slot's usage and re-roll if the new pick equals it. Cap re-rolls (e.g., 3 attempts) so tiny buckets don't infinite-loop.

Sketch:
    prev_usage = None
    for w in struct:
        for key in w:
            for attempt in range(3):
                picked = meaning_gen.select(...)
                if picked != prev_usage or picked is None:
                    break
            keys.append(picked)
            prev_usage = picked

Apply consistently across _select_no_tag, _select_tags. Determinism: re-rolls share the same RNG so seed-stability holds; the sequence of RNG calls changes vs prior, which is a one-time bit-shift acceptable for a quality fix.

Acceptance:
- New unit test: structure [(K,), (K,)] with a 1-element bucket — generator either re-rolls cap times then accepts the dupe, or returns one None. Document the chosen behaviour.
- Sample generation output: 100+ names per culture, no adjacent-identical-usage patterns.
- Tag-cooccurrence stats unaffected (proportions are corpus-derived; this fix is generator-only).

title: Dashboard: add bundle-level decomposition/attestation metric alongside DB-level
description:
The current language-quality dashboard (lexicon language-report) measures DB-level state — every etymon mined including unpromoted. This is useful as a curation signal ("50K rows of mining residue to consolidate") but misleading as a runtime-quality signal: the bundle is post-promotion, so what actually ships is a small well-attested subset.

Concrete confusion seen 2026-05-09 (post-wyrd-eni4 epic): user looked at dashboard, saw "many morphemes with almost no observations", then looked at actual generated output and found morphemes with 14-15 scholarly citations (-stone-, -curry). The dashboard alarm didn't match the empirical experience because they measure different layers.

Fix: add a parallel bundle-level metric alongside the DB-level one. Per-language report should include:

* DB level (current): total etymons, witnesses distribution, % below threshold
* Bundle level (NEW): subjects in bundle, citation distribution per subject, % rando-port-grandfathered, % wiktionary-empirical, % scholar-witnessed

The bundle-level metric is what tells you 'is your runtime output well-attested'. The DB-level metric tells you 'how much mining residue you have to clean up'. Both useful, currently conflated.

Implementation sketch:
- After lexicon export-meanings runs, compute bundle-level stats by walking subjects + citations
- Emit them in the JSON dashboard output under a 'bundle' key alongside 'lexicon'
- Markdown rendering: separate columns 'bundle subjects', 'bundle scholar-attested rate', 'rando-port grandfather %' alongside the existing DB columns

Acceptance:
- language-report --json has both 'lexicon' (existing) and 'bundle' (new) sections per language
- markdown view distinguishes the two
- a re-run after a bundle re-emit reflects the new bundle-level numbers (not stale)

title: Upgrade bundle era_reflexes schema to carry source tag (unblock Tier 4 in SPA)
description:
Surfaced by general-review BLOCKING finding on PR #146 (wyrd-98cs). Tier 4 (phonology-rule) era reflexes are currently filtered OUT of the bundle export at _fetch_root_era_reflexes because the bundle's era_reflexes field is shaped {lang: [form, ...]} — set semantics, no source tag. If we let Tier 4 reflexes through today they'd reach KenningRewind / SPA indistinguishable from human-vetted Tier 1 cluster mates.

To unlock the projected ~22pp time-travel coverage lift on the bundle / SPA, upgrade the schema:

Bundle field shape:
- Old: era_reflexes: {target_language: [form, ...]}
- New: era_reflexes: {target_language: [{form, source}, ...]}

Loader-side (meaning.py:load_meanings + Meaning.era_reflex_for):
- Detect shape (string entries = legacy, dict entries = new).
- Internal storage carries (form, source) tuples.
- era_reflex_for(target) keeps returning list[str] (back-compat).
- Add era_reflex_for_with_sources(target) → list[(form, source)] for source-aware consumers.

Export-side (lexicon.py:_fetch_root_era_reflexes + _emit_era_reflexes):
- Drop the Tier 4 filter at line 5895.
- Stamp full {form, source} dicts onto the bundle's era_reflexes field.
- Merge across linked families: dedupe on (form, source); when same form has multiple sources, keep the higher-quality source ('cluster' > 'descent' > 'period-form' > 'phonology-rule:v1').

Consumer-side (Phase 2 follow-on, OK to defer):
- KenningRewind / KenningEraMap surface source visually (e.g. italic for inferred forms; tooltip explaining 'derived via phonology rule').
- SPA component reads source field if present, falls back to plain form display otherwise.

Test plan:
- Loader handles legacy list-of-strings input correctly (back-compat).
- Loader handles new list-of-dicts input correctly.
- Bundle export emits new shape when Tier 4 fires.
- KenningRewind continues to render correctly with both shapes.

Audit context (wyrd-98cs review): blocks the user's headline 'real town names move forward and backward in time' question reaching the SPA. CLI path already works via direct etymon_era_reflexes calls; this ticket bridges to the bundle/SPA path.

title: Surface lexicon etymon_tag data into the bundle for languages without dedicated siblings
description:
Audit follow-up from wyrd-wzwa dashboard (2026-05-08): the bundle export drops semantic-tag data for languages without dedicated bundle siblings. Concrete: middle-english has 182 etymons with tags hitting 13/15 reference tag classes (architecture, topography, plant, animal, tree, water, etc.), but 0/15 of those reach the runtime bundle because there's no 'middle_english' sibling field. Same shape for modern-english (5 tagged etymons, 3/15 hit, 0/15 in bundle), early-modern-english, norman-french, old-irish, scottish-gaelic. Whatever bundle subject each of these etymons could attach to either doesn't exist (no rollup target) or strips the tag at export boundary.

Two implementation paths to scope (pick one in design):

Path A — schema additions: extend bundle subject shape to carry per-language tagged-etymon data. Add middle_english / modern_english / etc. siblings whose presence triggers the same subject-tag visibility logic that old_english enjoys today. Larger schema change but architecturally clean.

Path B — promotion-threshold relaxation for tagged etymons: if an etymon carries a tag in etymon_tag AND has a citation, surface it in the bundle as a tagged contribution to the relevant subject regardless of witness count. Smaller bundle export change. Risk: noise from low-quality tags polluting the runtime tag-cooccurrence statistics.

Acceptance:
- After fix + bundle re-emit (gated on wyrd-j43l), the language-quality dashboard's bundle_tag_hit_rate for middle-english reaches at least 13/15 (matches the lexicon-side reading).
- modern-english, old-irish, scottish-gaelic show non-zero bundle_tag_hit_rate.
- No regression on bundle subject count (the existing 1879 subjects stay).
- Tag co-occurrence proportions don't get poisoned by sparse-witness tag data — measure via test that compares pre/post tag_cooccurrence row counts and flags 10x+ growth.

This is part of the cleanup epic wyrd-eni4 (gated on the bundle dict-shape migration wyrd-c1vq + bundle re-emit wyrd-j43l).

title: Per-culture rebuild-proportions BETWEEN bundle re-export and Lambda deploy
description:
When meanings.json is re-exported (wyrd-j43l), the per-culture proportions JSONs (english_proportions.json, scottish_proportions.json, welsh_proportions.json, irish_proportions.json, breton_proportions.json) are derived from the bundle + place-names corpus. They MUST be regenerated to reflect the new morpheme inventory + tag distributions, otherwise the runtime samples from a stale empirical distribution.

```
  .venv/bin/wyrd kenning rebuild-proportions "$c" \
    "wyrd/generators/kenning/data/${c}_place_names.json"
done
```
Each run regenerates {culture}_proportions.json + emits a 'culture=… perfect=… total=…' progress line on stderr that should be appended to COVERAGE.md as a new snapshot.

This ticket covers:
1. Run rebuild-proportions for all 5 cultures.
2. Append the new snapshot to COVERAGE.md (date + commit + table).
3. Verify tag_marginal + tag_cooccurrence are populated in each output (they're consumed by --cohesion).
4. Quick spot-check: post-rebuild perfect-rates should be ≥ pre-rebuild rates (more morphemes in the bundle → more decompositions land).

Gated on wyrd-j43l (bundle re-emit must land first; this is the proportions-side follow-up).

title: Fantasy creature pipeline: runtime surface (KenningFantasy generator + SPA + CLI)
description:
The wyrd-ami fantasy creature pipeline is paper-only at the runtime layer: 1,308 fantasy_morpheme rows mined, 244 with full etymon_id linkage and descent chains (Angel→OE, Archon→ancient-Greek, Daemon→Latin), but no Generator class / SPA UI / public CLI consumes the data. Authoring works; the tap is closed.

Per D30's design intent: 'no new generator class needed — same temporal-axis machinery just works'. Architecturally correct, but the user has no way to invoke the flow. Three minimal moves to surface it:

1. Add KenningFantasy Generator class (or --mode=creature flag on existing Kenning). Reads fantasy_morpheme + etymon descent. Composes with KenningRewind for era-rendered creature names.
2. Bundle export path for fantasy_morpheme rows (subjects keyed by creature input_name, etymon_id linkage retained).
3. Public CLI: 'wyrd kenning render-creature Harpy' or similar.
4. SPA dropdown entry exposed via the manifest.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): one of the highest-impact half-shipped surfaces in the project. Runtime layer is absent; backend is complete.

title: Bundle migration: array-shape → dict-shape to unblock joiners + canonical_decompositions
description:
meanings.json is currently array-shaped (legacy). Two shipped features are unreachable because of this:

1. wyrd-q0g6 joiners pool: Phase 1 schema + Phase 1.5 insertion code wired in proportions.py, but bundle export never populates the dict 'joiners' key. joiner_density knob is silent no-op.

2. wyrd-h8k1 canonical decompositions: Phase 3b shipped (PR #140) and KenningExplain projects canonical_decompositions when bundle is dict-shape, but load_canonical_decompositions returns {} on array-shape input.

The dict-shape pattern is the right forward-compat: emit dict-shape only when new fields have data, keep list-shape otherwise. Each loader (load_joiners, load_canonical_decompositions) defensively returns empty for list-shape input.

Approach:
1. Update lexicon.py:export_meanings to emit dict-shape {subjects: [...], joiners: {...}, canonical_decompositions: {...}} when joiners pool or canonical decompositions are present.
2. The runtime loaders already handle dict-shape (per the wyrd-h8k1 PR #140 work).
3. Bundle re-emit (wyrd-j43l) surfaces the change to SPA + Lambda.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): two shipped features blocked on this migration. Re-using the dict-shape forward-compat pattern (memory: bundle-dict-shape-forward-compat).

title: Wire phonology_rules into etymon_era_reflexes as Tier-4 fallback
description:
The phonology rules library (wyrd/generators/kenning/phonology_rules.py) ships 4 complete sound-change cells (OE→ME, ME→EModE, EModE→ModE, OW→ModW) via PRs #131/#135/#141/#143 but is dead code — apply_rules() is never called outside the test suite. Integrating it as a Tier-4 fallback after period-form projection in etymon_era_reflexes() could close most of the current 61.3% time-travel coverage gap on bundle etymons WITHOUT any new mining. Highest-leverage idle capability surfaced by the 2026-05-08 end-to-end audit (wyrd-wl35).

Approach:
1. In lexicon.py:etymon_era_reflexes, after Tier 3 (period-form projection) returns empty, fall through to Tier 4: take the etymon's modern_canonical, route through apply_rules(form, language, from_era, to_era, mode='inverse') to surface ancestral forms; for forward-walking, route through mode='forward' to surface descendants.
2. Tag the result with source='phonology-rule:v1' so consumers can distinguish projection-from-real-attestation vs projection-from-rule.
3. Add quality dimension: phonology-rule-derived forms are weaker evidence than cognate-cluster mates; KenningRewind explainer should mark them differently.
4. Bundle re-emit needed (wyrd-j43l) to surface the new coverage to SPA.

Audit context (wyrd-wl35): 2026-05-08 audit found 38.7% of bundle etymons have era data today (Tier 1 cognate 27.2% + Tier 2 descent 10.9% + Tier 3 period-form 0.6%). Phonology-rule integration could plausibly raise this toward ~80-90% on the four cells covered (OE/ME/EModE/ModE chain + OW/ModW).

title: wyrd-08m Phase 3b: KenningExplain canonical surfacing via bundle projection
description:
Phase 3a (PR #136) wired the canonical pick into rebuild-proportions and the unaccounted miner. KenningExplain (Lambda / SPA path) was deliberately excluded because the Lambda has no DB access — the canonical decomposition lives only in the lexicon DB.

To surface canonical in KenningExplain (the user-facing decomposer), one of these has to happen:

(a) Project canonical_signature (and optionally canonical_source) into the bundle's per-name structure at export-meanings time, so the Lambda can read it without a DB. Cost: bundle size grows by 40 hex chars + a small label per toponym × ~7000 toponyms = ~300KB.

(b) Add a canonical-aware decomposition function that runs in the bundle context — but this requires the bundle to carry enough scholar/etymology data to compute canonical at runtime, which it does not.

Option (a) is the right call. Implementation:
1. Update lexicon export-meanings to emit a 'canonical' block per toponym carrying decomposition_signature + canonical_source for any toponym with a canonical pick.
2. Update KenningExplain.generate_all to honour the canonical block when present: sort the candidates dict so the canonical-signature reading appears first (or marked visually); show alternates as 'also possible'.
3. Tests: bundle export emits canonical for toponyms with a pick; KenningExplain marks canonical when bundle carries it; falls back to current heuristic-by-unaccounted-count sort when bundle lacks canonical.

Acceptance: KenningExplain output for a toponym with a canonical pick highlights the canonical reading and orders alternates beneath it.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #140. Bundle projects canonical_decompositions; KenningExplain marks + front-loads canonical reading; GenerationResult + envelope carry canonical/canonical_source fields.

title: wyrd-08m Phase 3: wire canonical pick into rebuild-proportions / unaccounted / explainer
description:
Phase 3 of wyrd-08m (parent ticket): consumer integration that turns the Phase 1 schema + Phase 2 refactor (wyrd-zpi9) into actual user-facing value.

Today the matcher's reduce=True heuristic still feeds:
- rebuild-proportions: counts morpheme frequencies via the heuristic pick → false-hits inflate frequencies, false-gaps under-count.
- unaccounted miner: surfaces fragments via the heuristic pick → false-gaps appear as 'corpus gaps' that authoring effort would target.
- KenningExplain: shows decomposition via the heuristic pick.

Phase 3 wires the canonical decomposition (toponym_decomposition.is_canonical=1) into all three:
1. rebuild-proportions reads the canonical pick when available; falls back to the heuristic when canonical is unset (e.g. multi-zero-tied not yet tiebreaker'd).
2. unaccounted miner reads the canonical pick — fragments that appear ONLY in the canonical decomposition's unaccounted_fragments are real gaps.
3. KenningExplain surfaces canonical visually (e.g. a marker) but shows alternates too — operators see the canonical pick + the disagreement context.

Acceptance criteria (from the parent wyrd-08m ticket):
- Coverage and gap reports use canonical-only counts.
- Re-running rebuild-proportions after a 'decompose --apply' run produces stable counts (no churn from arbitrary tiebreaks).

Dependencies:
- Requires Phase 1 + Phase 2 + the eventual rule (c) tiebreaker (Phase 4) for full coverage. Phase 3 can ship with rule (c) deferred; canonical-set just won't cover multi-zero ties until then.
notes: Phase 3a shipped via PR #136 (d86336b): rebuild-proportions + unaccounted miner --db wiring. KenningExplain canonical surfacing carved out to wyrd-h8k1 (needs bundle-side projection — Lambda has no DB access). Follow-ups: wyrd-8m87 (region plumbing), wyrd-0see (shared _decompose_corpus helper refactor).
close_reason: Phase 3a shipped via PR #136; explainer carved to wyrd-h8k1. Parent wyrd-08m remains open for rule (c) tiebreaker.

title: wyrd-4i6 Phase 2: ME→EModE→ModE cells + sporadic-weight rules
description:
Phase 2 of wyrd-4i6 (parent ticket): extend the sound-change rules library beyond the OE→ME cell shipped in Phase 1 (PR #131).

Cells to add:
- (english, middle-english, early-modern-english): roughly the Great Vowel Shift block (Sweet 1888 covers; ~20-30 rules).
- (english, early-modern-english, modern-english): post-GVS settling, final-e loss, modern orthography.
- (welsh, old-welsh, modern-welsh): ~20 rules per Morris-Jones 1913 / Lewis & Pedersen.

Plus refinements deferred from Phase 1:
- Sporadic-weight rules (weight<1.0) for transitions that aren't universal. Phase 1 framework supports them; Phase 2 mining surfaces the actual frequency data.
- Environment constraints (regex-based 'before front vowel', 'word-initial', 'in stressed syllable'). Phase 1 used literal patterns; ME→EModE has more context-dependent rules where this matters.
- Phase 1 limitation pinned in test docstring: short y → i fires on suffix-introduced y (e.g. -ley → -lei). Add a terminal-suffix protection mechanism so once -ley appears it stops further char-level rewrites.
- Attestation-weighted priors for inverse-mode 50/50 split. Phase 1 splits uniformly; Phase 2 mining could surface 'when ME has X, OE was Y 73% of the time' priors.

Acceptance criteria from parent ticket:
- 30+ rules for OE→ME→ModE forward chain.
- Inverse application of OE→ModE chain on 20 known test toponyms produces the attested OE form within top-3 candidates for >70% of cases.
- A test confirms apply_rules('Bridgewater', 'old-english', 'modern-english', mode='inverse') includes 'brycgwæter' or close variant in the candidate set.

Phase 1 (PR #131) shipped: framework + OE→ME cell + 28 rules + 55 tests. Phase 2 chains the cells together so 'modern-english' can route through ME via composition.
notes: Phase 2.3 (OW→ModW Welsh cell) shipped via PR #141. Phase 2.1 (ME→EModE) shipped via PR #135. Phase 2.2 (EModE→ModE) and Phase 2.4 (sporadic-weight rules + env constraints + restoration of dropped Phase 2.1 rules) remain. Phase 2.2 lower-priority (most place-name orthography stable by EModE).

title: wyrd-q0g6 Phase 1.5: generator-side joiner insertion (compose-time)
description:
Generator hook deferred from PR #130 (wyrd-q0g6 Phase 1):

Phase 1 shipped the matcher-side hook (Joiner sentinel + matcher-time consumption). The complementary GENERATOR-side hook lets compose-time output insert one joiner between adjacent picked morphemes, probability-gated like manorial_affix.

Concrete surface:
- New input_schema knob: `--joiner-density` (0..1, default 0).
- In Kenning.generate / NameGenerator structure walk: between adjacent picked morphemes whose families share a populated joiner pool, with probability=joiner_density, pick one joiner (weighted by attestation) and insert it between the morpheme surfaces. Emit a component for the joiner with location='joiner' so KenningExplain can round-trip it.

Caveats / scope:
- Lang-field selection: when the two adjacent morphemes share one lang_field, that's the pool. When they don't, defer (no joiner inserted) — cross-language joiner insertion is more nuanced than Phase 1.5 wants to handle.
- Bit-stable at joiner_density=0 (default).
- Bundle effect at ship time: zero (no joiners populated until wyrd-semi audit lands). Pin this with a test.

Pairs with wyrd-semi (Phase 2 audit) — without that, this is also plumbing-only. But the two are independently shippable: matcher hook lives in Phase 1, generator hook lives here, audit lives in wyrd-semi. All three converge once data arrives.
notes: SHIPPED via PR #134 (squash-merged 2026-05-08). Compose-time joiner insertion: joiner_density knob (0..1, default 0), _load_joiners runtime cache wired into coupled-clear chain, _apply_joiner_insertion post-processes NewName to insert joiners between adjacent morphemes sharing populated lang_field pools. 66 tests, 1931 full-suite. Real bug caught + fixed in review: _weighted_joiner_choice empty-pool crash; KenningExplain round-trip overclaim tightened. Bundle effect at ship time: zero (no joiners populated until wyrd-semi audit).

title: wyrd-q0g6 Phase 2: audit 149 short subjects + populate joiners pool
description:
Phase 2 of wyrd-q0g6 (parent ticket): triage the 149 bundle subjects with 1-2 char modern_usage, classify each as:
- Real grammatical morpheme (stays a subject; no change)
- Pure phonological joiner (migrates to bundle's joiners field)
- Spurious entry (e.g. 'um' with empty meaning — drop)

Manual triage required — gloss is the deciding evidence per the parent ticket. Auto-classifying by length-only mis-categorizes real short morphemes (OE genitive -en-, ON -by, Welsh -y- etc).

Phase 1 (PR #130) shipped the schema + matcher hook + Joiner sentinel. The bundle's joiners field is empty until this audit fills it. Once populated, the matcher hook starts producing correct unaccounted counts immediately.

Output: an updated meanings.json bundle in dict shape with `subjects` + `joiners` populated. Re-emit via lexicon export-meanings (CLI changes to support dict-shape output may be needed).

Acceptance criteria:
- Each of the 149 short subjects classified (real / joiner / spurious) with rationale.
- Joiners populated with attestation weights derived from corpus audit.
- Bundle re-emit produces dict-shape meanings.json with the new joiners field.
- Empirical English perfect rate measured against pre-Phase-2 baseline (target: at minimum recover the 6.1pp drop seen when ALL <3-char usages are removed).

title: wyrd-08m Phase 2: split pick_canonical_decomposition + add cross-product cap
description:
Phase 2 follow-ups deferred from PR #126 (wyrd-08m Phase 1):

1. **Refactor pick_canonical_decomposition**: ~80-line function fails the and/or test (loads rows + rebuilds slot candidates + runs rule (a) + runs rule (b)). Extract:
   - _build_slot_candidates_per_row(rows, word_db) -> list of slot lists
   - _try_rule_scholar(...) -> matching rows (or None)
   - _try_rule_unique_zero(...) -> matching row id (or None)
   Will become more important in Phase 2 when rule (c) tiebreaker lands and the function would otherwise grow another ~30 lines.

2. **Cross-product memory cap in compute_decompositions**: _cross_product_decompositions materializes the full Cartesian product before persisting. For multi-word toponyms with many per-word options the product can explode. Before the operator runs decompose --apply against the production 1.4M-row corpus, add either:
   - A per-toponym cap (e.g. 256 combos max; emit a warning + sample the rest)
   - OR streaming yield instead of materialize + persist incrementally

3. **Optional: log on _scholar_form_sequences silent drops**: today an etymon with an unmapped language code or NULL canonical_form is silently dropped from the scholar sequence. A one-line warning would surface the failure mode the next time it bites.

Phase 2 also wires the canonical pick into rebuild-proportions, the unaccounted miner, and the explainer (per the wyrd-08m parent ticket).
notes: SHIPPED via PR #132 (squash-merged 2026-05-08). Refactor + cap + log. Critical bug caught + fixed in review: original early-termination of cross-product loop emitted prefix-only combos. New per-word capping ensures all combos full-length. 49 tests, 1908 full-suite passing. Phase 2 consumer integration (rebuild-proportions / unaccounted miner / explainer adopting the canonical pick) deferred to a fresh ticket.

title: toponym_attestation projection: derive per-etymon period forms
description:
Deferred from PR #114 (wyrd-rni Phase 3.1). The era-reflex picker covers 24% of OE toponym etymons via cognate-cluster + 4% via direct descent fallback (PR #110); ~72% remaining have neither cognate_id nor descent edges. Demo-name fallback rate is ~58% of morpheme×era slots.

Closing the gap via projection:
- toponym_attestation already carries 1,476 dated historical spellings keyed to 669 toponyms (PR #108 mining output).
- toponym_etymology_element gives per-toponym element ordering with surface_in_modern.
- For each toponym_attestation row, project the historical form's segments back onto the canonical breakdown's elements via prefix/suffix anchoring (last morpheme aligned to historical-form suffix).
- Aggregate across toponyms: each etymon gets a list of (historical_form, year, source) entries representing its surface at attested points in time.

Schema option A: new etymon_period_form table (etymon_id, form, date_year, source_doc).
Schema option B: extend etymon_variant with attested_year column.

Picker integration: extend etymon_era_reflexes with a Tier 4 fallback that consults projected period forms when cognate-cluster and descent both miss. Sort by year ascending; pick the form whose date_year falls in the target era cell's range.

Quality gates:
- Last-morpheme suffix-anchoring is high-precision (Hadenham → -ham, Bradford → -ford).
- First-morpheme prefix-anchoring is medium-precision.
- Middle-morpheme alignment is low-precision; skip for v1.

Empirical baseline: 1,476 attestations × ~2 segmentable morphemes ≈ ~3000 projected period-form rows. Coverage of the 1,507 isolated OE etymons probably reaches ~30-50% (the productive toponym suffixes show up everywhere).

Parent epic: wyrd-lm5m
Related: wyrd-4i6 (phonological-rule fallback — orthogonal path; rules are forward-derived, projection is backward-derived from attestations)

title: EraReflexProvider abstraction + bundle plumbing for SPA-side rewind
description:
Deferred from PR #114 (wyrd-rni Phase 3.1). The CLI rewinder works against a LexiconDB handle directly; the SPA needs an EraReflexProvider protocol abstraction so the same primitive can run on bundled data.

Why this is needed:
- wyrd/generators/kenning/rewind.py:rewind_name() takes a LexiconDB and runs raw SQL in two places (anchor lookup + era-reflex query).
- The Lambda runs on bundled data (importlib.resources). The lexicon DB is 673MB — won't fit in a Lambda layer.
- For SPA integration, era-reflex data must ship as part of the bundle.

Scope:
1. Define an EraReflexProvider protocol with two methods:
   - resolve_anchor(meaning: Meaning, sources_pref: tuple[str, ...]) -> Anchor | None
   - era_reflexes(anchor: Anchor, family: str, cell: str) -> list[EraReflex]
2. Implement LexiconDBProvider (current behavior, wraps lexicon.etymon_era_reflexes) — used by CLI.
3. Implement BundleProvider that reads era-reflex data from per-Meaning sibling fields on the bundle. Requires:
   - Bundle export: emit <lang>_era_reflexes per word entry with etymon_id + cluster_lang_form pairs
   - Runtime: parse the sibling into Meaning.era_reflexes; expose Meaning.era_reflex_for(family, cell) accessor
4. Refactor rewind_name to take an EraReflexProvider instead of LexiconDB; CLI passes LexiconDBProvider, SPA passes BundleProvider.
5. Register a Generator subclass (e.g. KenningRewind) using BundleProvider so the SPA's /api/generators endpoint surfaces the rewinder.

Best designed once wyrd-381 has shipped — both demos consume the same era-reflex shape, so the protocol's contract becomes evident once we have two callers.

Parent epic: wyrd-lm5m

title: wyrd-lr4 Phase 4d — manual stratum hand-correction CLI
description:
Phase 4d (the last Phase 4 follow-on per the umbrella). The classifier family (Welsh / French / OE / ON via Phase 4a-c) covers the bulk-classification path; Phase 4d is the operator escape hatch for high-stakes etymons the heuristic misclassifies.

## Design

New 'lexicon set-stratum' CLI subcommand:

  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --etymon-id 12345 --stratum latin-loan
  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --canonical-form caer --language welsh --stratum latin-loan
  wyrd kenning lexicon set-stratum --etymon-id 12345 --clear

Inputs (mutually-exclusive identification):
- --etymon-id INT — direct row identifier
- --canonical-form + --language — pair lookup; must resolve to exactly one row

Stratum specification:
- --stratum STR — must be in ALL_STRATA (union of WELSH/FRENCH/OE/ON tuples) for typo protection
- --clear — sets stratum to NULL (--stratum and --clear are mutually exclusive)

Output to stderr:
- 'etymon N <canonical_form, language>: <old_stratum> → <new_stratum>' so the operator can verify

## Validation

- Exactly one of {--etymon-id, --canonical-form+--language} required
- --stratum and --clear mutually exclusive (one required)
- Stratum value validated against ALL_STRATA frozenset (catches typos)
- Cross-family strata (e.g. setting 'native-welsh' on a french etymon) are NOT blocked — operator's responsibility; these may legitimately surface during edge-case correction
- Canonical-form ambiguity (multiple matches across languages with the same form) → error listing candidates
- Missing etymon → error

## Out of scope

- Bulk corrections file (operator can script multiple --etymon-id calls)
- Audit trail / log of changes (stderr line is the audit trail)
- wyrd-j3gy validator + SPA culture gating (separate ticket)

## Tests

~12 tests:
- set by id (happy path)
- set by canonical-form + language (happy path)
- both id and form+lang → error
- neither → error
- form-only without language → error
- canonical-form ambiguity → error with candidates
- etymon doesn't exist → error
- unknown stratum → error
- --clear sets to NULL
- --clear + --stratum mutex → error
- previous-stratum reported in stderr line
- --apply path for full DB stratum write doesn't blow this away (idempotency check)

Estimated 250-300 lines.

Parent: wyrd-lr4.
close_reason: Phase 4d shipped via PR #115. Manual stratum hand-correction CLI (lexicon set-stratum) added. ALL_STRATA frozenset registry in strata.py for typo protection. Three helper functions extracted from the main command for one-screen-rule compliance: _validate_set_stratum_identification, _validate_set_stratum_value, _resolve_set_stratum_target. Includes warn-and-proceed for merged-cluster losers. 22 new strata tests cover happy paths, all error paths, --clear semantics, end-to-end idempotency, cross-family writes, merged-row warning. Family-aware validation deferred to wyrd-j3gy as noted in that ticket.

title: wyrd-lr4 Phase 4a — French within-language stratum classifier
description:
Phase 4 of wyrd-lr4. Phases 1-3 covered Welsh (schema + classifier) → bundle export → generator filter. Phase 4 fills in classifiers for the other major language families: French (4a), Old English (4b), Old Norse (4c).

This ticket is just the French slice.

## Plan

title: wyrd-lr4 Phase 3 — generator --stratum filter consumes the loaded data
description:
Phase 3 of wyrd-lr4 (within-language stratum tagging).

Phase 1 (PR #105) shipped the schema/classifier/CLI. Phase 2 (PR #107) plumbs stratum through the bundle export so Meaning.stratum_for(lang_field, form) returns the tag at runtime. Phase 3 wires the generator filter so users can actually use it.

Plan, mirroring the established --era filter pattern (D5-2 / wyrd-lyp):

1. Meaning.in_stratum(stratum: str | None) -> bool — analogous to attested_in_era_range. Returns True when stratum is None (no filter), when self.stratum is empty (treated as 'always include' — same convention as era for 'no data → pass'), or when any of self.stratum.values() contains the requested tag for any form.

2. MeaningGenerator.keep_keys_for_stratum(stratum) -> frozenset[str] | None — mirrors keep_keys_for_era. Cache by stratum tag. Returns None when stratum is None or when the keep-set covers the full meaning_db (full-coverage fast path, same bit-stable invariant as era).

3. Proportions.select gains a stratum: str | None = None param. Compose era_range + stratum keep_keys: if both are non-None, frozenset intersection; if one is None, use the other. Threaded down to Generator.select via the keep_keys arg unchanged.

4. CLI: add --stratum to wyrd kenning generate (cli.py near --era around line 262). Validate against the loaded vocabulary at runtime so a typo fails loud.

5. Kenning.generate (or whatever orchestrator sits between cli.py and Proportions.select) needs the param threaded through.

6. Tests:
   - Meaning.in_stratum: present (in lang's stratum dict) / missing-from-lang / missing-from-form / empty-stratum-data passthrough / None-filter passthrough.
   - keep_keys_for_stratum: returns None on None input; returns None on full-coverage; returns subset on partial; cache hit.
   - Proportions.select: stratum-only filter; era + stratum intersection; stratum=None bit-stable with no-arg.
   - CLI: --stratum welsh:native-welsh actually narrows the bundle pool (smoke test against rebuild-proportions or a fixture).

Granularity caveat (same as era): filtering happens at the USAGE level, not the SENSE level. A usage with two senses (one in-stratum, one out) stays in the pool; the downstream pick at NameGenerator._pick_surface picks meanings[0]. Documented for era; carry forward verbatim.

Out of scope for Phase 3:
- Per-form filtering within a Meaning (would need NameGenerator._render_substitutions reworked).
- French / Old English / Old Norse classifiers (Phase 4).
- Manual hand-correction CLI for misclassified etymons.

Estimated 200-300 lines including tests. Worktree-isolation per PR-recipe in /tmp/wyrd-handoff-2026-05-07.md.

title: wyrd-ami: capture IPA pronunciation + derive English-shaped renderings for non-Latin etymons
description:
Per user 2026-05-06: when an etymon comes from a non-Latin-script language (Hebrew, Arabic, Egyptian, Sanskrit, etc.), the canonical_form alone is insufficient for English town-name generation. We need both the academic transliteration AND an English-phonotactic rendering so generated names are pronounceable to native English speakers.

Two-phase implementation:

## Phase 1: Capture IPA at ingest time (cheap)

Wiktextract entries already contain a 'sounds' array with IPA strings, e.g.:
  {'sounds': [{'ipa': '/d͡ʒɪnː/', 'tags': ['Modern Standard Arabic']}, ...]}

The current wiktextract_ingester.py discards this. Plumb it into the etymon table.

Schema change:
- Add etymon.pronunciation_ipa TEXT (nullable). Optionally also a pronunciation_dialect TEXT to distinguish multiple IPA variants when present (Modern Standard Arabic vs. Egyptian Arabic, Old vs. Middle Egyptian, etc.).
- Migration: nullable so existing rows don't need backfill.

Ingester change:
- wiktextract_ingester.py picks the most authoritative IPA from the sounds array (first one with no dialect tag, falling back to the first overall).
- Empirical mining helpers (lexicon mine-wiktextract-corpus) plumb the same.

## Phase 2: English-shaped derivation (the harder part)

For each non-Latin-language etymon with IPA, derive an English-spelled rendering using English phonotactic rules. Roughly:

1. Map IPA phonemes to closest English phonemes:
   - Arabic ʿayin /ʕ/ → silent or 'a'
   - Arabic ḍād /dˤ/ → 'd'
   - Hebrew ḥet /ħ/ → 'h' or 'kh'
   - Egyptian aleph /ʔ/ → silent
   - Sanskrit retroflex ṭ /ʈ/ → 't'
   - etc.

2. Map English phonemes to English spellings using mainstream conventions:
   - /ʤ/ → 'j' (initial), 'g' (before e/i)
   - /k/ → 'c' (before a/o/u), 'k' (before e/i, finally)
   - Long vowels → magic-e or doubled-vowel patterns
   - /ʃ/ → 'sh'
   - etc.

3. Output the English-shaped form alongside the canonical academic transliteration.

Examples from PR #83's wave-2 entries:
  Arabic jinn /ʤɪnː/         → 'Jinn' (English-shaped) + 'jinn' (academic) — same in this case
  Arabic ʿifrīt /ʕifriːt/    → 'Ifrit' (English-shaped, ʿayin silenced) + 'ʿifrīt' (academic)
  Egyptian inpw /ɪnpw/       → 'Anpu' or 'Anep' (English-shaped, vowels guessed) + 'inpw' (academic)
  Hebrew gōlem /ɡoːlɛm/       → 'Golem' (English-shaped) + 'gōlem' (academic)
  Sanskrit rakṣasa /rɐkʂɐsɐ/ → 'Rakshasa' (English-shaped retroflex→s) + 'rakṣasa' (academic)

Generation pipeline integration:
- Realistic-mode names: prefer the English-shaped form (modern register).
- Archaic/scholarly mode: use the academic transliteration.
- Could expose both as a generation option ('register=english_modern' vs 'register=scholarly').

## Caveats

- IPA → English-phoneme → English-spelling has many-to-many mappings; needs heuristic + confidence rating. Some etymons probably need a hand-curated override.
- For Egyptian especially (no native vowels in hieroglyphs), Wiktionary's IPA may be conjectural. Mark these with lower confidence.
- For Sanskrit / Arabic / Hebrew, the established English forms (rakshasa, jinn, golem) should win over rule-derived forms. Could load a small known-form lookup table that overrides the rule output for canonical creature names.
- Already-Latin-script languages (Latin, Greek, OE, etc.) probably don't need this — Latin → English orthography is well-known and the canonical_form is usually fine. Scope this to non-Latin-script source languages.

## Scope clarification

NOT included in this ticket:
- Phonotactic-aware joining for compound town names (different concern; town-generation has its own pipeline).
- Full TTS synthesis (out of scope; we only need the spelling).

User-facing impact: town names like 'Anpu Hollow', 'Jinn Reach', 'Rakshasa Crossing' read natively to English readers, while the underlying etymological provenance is still preserved in the academic transliteration field.
notes: Phase 2b started 2026-05-07: english_shaped derivation rules + CLI backfill, on branch wyrd-ami/english-shaped-derivation. Generator + SPA integration deferred to later PRs.

title: wyrd-ami: re-ingest wiktextract for Semitic / Egyptian / Indo-Iranian language slices
description:
Part of EPIC wyrd-ialp (wave-2 language etymon corpus expansion). FIRST to implement per user 2026-05-06.

The wiktextract_ingester (wyrd/generators/kenning/wiktextract_ingester.py) already supports any language code — codes pass through as-is. The bottleneck is operational: the slices we actually RAN it against were targeted at British Isles place-name ancestry (Germanic, Celtic, Romance, Greek/Latin). The wave-2 dumps were never ingested at scale.

What to do:

1. Download the relevant wiktextract slices from kaikki.org. Each language has a per-language extract:
   - Hebrew: kaikki.org/dictionary/Hebrew/kaikki.org-dictionary-Hebrew.jsonl (or similar)
   - Arabic: kaikki.org/dictionary/Arabic/...
   - Persian: kaikki.org/dictionary/Persian/...
   - Akkadian: kaikki.org/dictionary/Akkadian/...
   - Egyptian (Ancient Egyptian): kaikki.org/dictionary/Egyptian/...
   - Aramaic: kaikki.org/dictionary/Aramaic/...
   - Middle Persian / Pahlavi: kaikki.org/dictionary/Middle_Persian/...
   - (Sanskrit already has 12,456 — verify it doesn't need re-ingestion.)

2. Run lexicon mine-wiktextract or whichever ingester is current against each dump. Verify _WIKTIONARY_LANG_CODE_MAP correctly canonicalizes the codes (he, ar, fa, akk, egy, arc, pal — should all pass through correctly per the existing 'unmapped passes through' contract).

3. Re-mine the pfsrd2 corpus (with --skip-resolved disabled or via approach_version bump) and verify previously attested_but_not_in_corpus entries (Jann, Kanya, Anpw, etc.) now resolve usable via descent_walking_lookup.

Expected impact: should rescue most of the ~140 attested_but_not_in_corpus rows from the 2026-05-06 mine. Each language probably grows from ~few-hundred to ~10k+ entries (matching the IE language coverage).

Caveats:
- Wiktionary's coverage of these languages is uneven. Hebrew likely good (lots of biblical scholarship), Egyptian probably weakest (small Wiktionary editor pool).
- Some lemmas may need transliteration normalization. The ingester should handle this transparently but verify e.g. that 'jinn' in Latin script and 'جن' in Arabic script both land correctly.
- No new ALLOWED_LANGUAGES code change needed — PR #83 already approved these.

Trust level: HIGH — same authoritative data source as the rest of our corpus.
notes: PR #94 opened. Wave-2 wiktextract ingest yielded etymon counts of ar 709->64698, fa 752->20242, he 425->15220, egy 131->4343, arc 227->2696, akk 217->1614, pal 384->1005. Rescue mine of 210 attested_but_not_in_corpus rows recovered 26 (12.4%) -> fantasy_morpheme usable 218->244. Remaining 143 are anchor-form mismatches (Phase 2 wyrd-ha9q target). Added 16 precursor/postcursor codes per user 2026-05-06 sign-off.

description:

The wiktextract ingester (wiktextract_ingester.py) supports these
