2. New table etymon_period_form (or a date_range column on reflex) so the SAME etymon carries its surface variants across periods, not just per-toponym.
3. Period taxonomy — coarse first: 'old-english' (pre-1066), 'middle-english' (1066-1500), 'early-modern' (1500-1700), 'modern' (1700+). Fine-grained later if useful.
4. Generator gains a 'period' or 'era' input parameter. For an unattested compound, derive the period-specific form by looking up each etymon's surface variants for that period. Where multiple variants attested, sample weighted.
5. For periods where an etymon has no attestation, optionally fall back to phonological rules (OE -tūn → ME -tun → -tone → -ton) — but this is much later work; coverage from attestations should be high.

The toponym_attestation table is the raw input to (2). For etymon-level period forms we'd also want to mine the variant historical spellings the books print throughout each entry.

Pairs naturally with the historical-vs-modern register knob we already discussed (currently just 'register: modern' as the default).
notes: Phase 3.0b shipped via PR #110 (6d3540d, 2026-05-07). Adds the cognate-cluster era-reflex picker — the lexicon-side primitive that wyrd-rni / wyrd-381 will consume. New: era.canonical_language_for_cell((family, cell)), era.era_cell_for_input(input, default_family) -> (family, cell), lexicon.etymon_era_reflexes(db, etymon_id, target_language=... or target_family_cell=...) returning EraReflex(etymon_id, form, language) tuples. CLI: 'wyrd kenning lexicon era-reflex <id> --era me|1086|english/me'. Two-path lookup: cognate-cluster (high-quality, 24% OE coverage) then direct etymon_descent fallback (recovers 67 more OE etymons with descent edges, including core toponym suffixes halh/burne/leah/dun/ham/tun/hoh/side). Remaining ~72% gap (no edges at all) needs phonological rules (deferred per ticket) or toponym_attestation projection. Out of scope deferred to wyrd-rni/wyrd-381: bundle plumbing, runtime Meaning.era_reflex_for accessor, generator render-path integration.

title: Build alphabetical-dictionary parser for non-Skeat books
description: Mawer, Ekwall, Johnston, Joyce, Watson — all in alphabetical-entry format rather than Skeat's TOC+suffix-section format. Current parser returns 0 entries on these. Need a generic alphabetical parser: detect headword (capitalized at paragraph start), extract entry body up to next headword. Then feed to the same LLM extractor. Covers the remaining 27 books in sources/.
notes:
Starting work — pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham 1920 first, then test against Ekwall and Johnston for format coverage.
Phase 1 done: pilot on Mawer Northumberland-Durham succeeded. Parser handles Skeat-format AND alphabetical-dictionary format with auto-detection. Working well on: Mawer NorthDur (838 entries), Ekwall Lancs (499), Duignan Staffs (337), Harrison Liverpool (215), Watson Ross (652), Watson Celtic (474), Joyce vol 3 (606), Morgans (~830), Macbain (178), Gillies Argyll (155).

Still problematic (deferred):
- Taylor 1893: parser grabs back-of-book index entries (toponym + page number, no etymology body). Needs back-matter / index detection.
- Joyce vol 1: thematic chapters not alphabetical — wrong shape entirely. Skip; vol 3 is the dictionary.
- Lindkvist, Wyld/Hirst, Mawer 1922/1924/Stenton: small/methodological volumes with mixed content — low yield expected.
- Watson 1926 has some 3-letter false-positive headwords leaking through (Ady, Ann, Arch, Bede).

title: Sonnet/Haiku second pass for low-confidence LLM extractions
description: Qwen 9B leaks modern forms ('king' instead of 'cyning', 'mill' instead of 'myln', 'town' instead of 'tun') on some entries, and misreads attestation fragments as etymons (Croxton: 'estone'). Add a review CLI that picks toponym_etymology rows with confidence in (medium, low) and notes containing 'extracted_by:llm:qwen', re-runs them via the Anthropic API (Haiku first, Sonnet for residue), and inserts new rows from the better extractor. Old rows stay; consensus view shows where they agree/disagree.
notes:
Pivot to Gemini for second-pass review — user has GEMINI_API_KEY configured but no Anthropic key. Less bureaucratic: free-tier covers expected volume, paid pricing for 2.5-flash is very cheap (~$0.075/M input). Will build as a parallel client to OllamaClient with the same extract_one signature, then add --provider {ollama|gemini} flag on mine-llm.
Implemented as 'wyrd kenning lexicon review <source_dir>' command. Dry-runs by default; --apply to insert new toponym_etymology rows tagged with extracted_by:gemini:<model>. Idempotent — skips toponyms that already have a Gemini row. Filters by --book / --confidence / --limit. Tested end-to-end against the in-progress DB (3 Cambridgeshire entries, ~36s for 3 calls). Ready to run for real after the current Ollama mining job finishes.
close_reason: Implemented as 'wyrd kenning lexicon review'. 128 Gemini-reviewed Mawer rows written this session. Bug fixed mid-run: bare TimeoutError now caught in both extractors.

title: Populate reflex.productivity counts
description: reflex.productivity is currently always 0. Should be the count of distinct toponyms that use this (surface_form, position) reflex, derived from toponym_etymology_element joins. Drives generator weighting later.

title: Capture word-level positional bias for modifier words
description: Single-word modifiers like 'Great', 'Long', 'Old', 'Little' are pre-only ('Great Bevvy' yes, 'Bevvy Great' no). Cardinal-direction words like 'North', 'South' are flexible (both 'North Stoke' and 'Stoke North' attested). Current schema captures intra-word morpheme position (pre/inner/post within a compound) but NOT inter-word position (which word slot in a multi-word name). Need either: (a) new name_modifier table with per-word-position counts derived from observed toponyms; (b) an inter_word_position field on something. The generator currently treats single-word modifiers as positionally free, which produces unnatural names.
close_reason: Already resolved (no PR) — implemented as D43 / wyrd-rogd.13 (PR #618, 2026-06-11, after this ticket's 2026-04-30 filing). Per-WORD-position stats for bare words: word.py word_position_for (first→wp-pre / interior→wp-inner / last→wp-post), tallied via proportions.py:111-121, persisted in L4 table proportions_bare_word_position (runtime_db_export.py:739-758), loaded proportions.py:526-585, scored vector_name_select.py:599-622. The ticket's exact examples (Great/Long/Old/Little single-word modifiers, North/South directionals) are covered; a WYRD_BARE_POSITION_THRESHOLD gates structured-vs-free. Only D43-noted future work is COMPOUND multi-morpheme word-sequence position — not this ticket's single-word scope.

title: Move confidence from toponym_etymology to per-element
description: Scholars hedge per-element ('the prefix is clearly X; the suffix may be Y'). Currently we record one confidence per breakdown. Move confidence to toponym_etymology_element; keep an aggregate on the parent for back-compat queries.

title: OCR ligature normalization for etymon canonical_form
description: Skeat OCR consistently mangles æ→cs, æ→ce, ð→§. Etymons end up as 'hcsdan' (should be 'hædan') or 'hy§' (should be 'hyð'). Add a normalize_ocr_form() pass that maps these back, applied at upsert_etymon() time. Pairs with the lemma work (variants under one lemma).
notes:
Implemented normalize_ocr_form() and cluster_ocr_variants() with dry-run/apply modes. Tested. Will run as a post-mining pass.
Lexicon README + arch note added at wyrd/generators/kenning/README.md covering data model, authoring flow, key invariants, module map, and CLI cheatsheet. Helps future-us stay oriented.
close_reason: OCR ligature normalization applied: 43 variant-pairs merged. Sat upstream of the lemma pass and let it work on cleaned forms.

title: Add lemma_id self-FK on etymon for variant collapse
description: Inflected forms (Hæda/Hædan) and OCR/macron variants (hām/hamm/ham) currently become separate etymon rows, breaking consensus counts. Add etymon.lemma_id (nullable self-FK) so variants point at a canonical lemma. Update etymon_consensus view to roll up to lemma. Backfill via clustering pass over canonical_form within each language.
close_reason: Schema migrated, inflection-strip linker shipped. 50 lemma links applied; cross-witnessed etymons rose from 113 to 133. Known false-positive class (OE adj↔noun) tolerable for now.

title: Design: should era-reflex surfaces enter a reflex-LINKED family's draw pool (scope-aware)?
description:
Cycle-135 investigation: _word_for_reflex (the reflex-LINKED bundle path) builds the generator draw pool (forms_by_lang) from the member-descendant walk only, so the cluster-carried era-reflex surfaces merged into fam['forms_by_lang'] by _merge_era_reflexes_into_forms_by_lang (wyrd-nxhh) are absent from a reflex-linked family's pool. The reflex-LESS path (_synthesize_word_for_family) reads fam['forms_by_lang'] wholesale and DOES include them.

This is NOT a simple bug: PR #841 tried a blanket union of fam['forms_by_lang'] into the reflex path and it broke test_export_meanings_reflex_linked_to_inflection_only_emits_that_inflection — a reflex linked to a specific INFLECTION (cotan) must emit ONLY that inflection's descendant scope, NOT the whole family (cot/cotes). The reflex-linked path is INTENTIONALLY descendant-scoped (linking to an inflection != covering the whole morpheme).

OPEN QUESTION (needs design analysis, not a blanket fix): should the cluster-carried era-reflex surfaces enter a reflex-linked family's draw pool ONLY for WHOLE-MORPHEME links (reflex linked to the family root/lemma) and NOT for inflection-scoped links? Or is their absence entirely intentional (they're emitted separately via _emit_era_reflexes into the era_reflexes field, and reach the draw pool only via the synthesize/reflex-less path by design)?

If a fix is warranted, it must respect the reflex-link scope: detect whether the linked etymon(s) cover the whole morpheme (root/lemma) vs a specific inflection, and only fold era-reflexes for the former. The cotan inflection-scoping test and a root-linked era-reflex test must BOTH pass.

Filed as a deferred design question — the loop's per-cycle blanket fix was wrong (closed PR #841).

title: Add round-trip regression tests for SPA workspace share/save serialization (shareLink/savedStore/workspaceSnapshot)
description:
Cycle-130 hunt verified the SPA workspace serialization CLEAN: both save->load via savedStore and encode->decode via shareLink round-trip every field, including falsy values seed:0/count:0/novelty:0/cohesion:false/packs:empty/explanation:empty. But the round-trips are UNTESTED. shareLink.js and workspaceSnapshot.js have NO test file; savedStore.test.js only covers importJSON.

This is a user-DATA seam (a saved/shared workspace). The classic latent regression is a truthiness gate: someone later writes if-seed instead of if-seed-not-undefined and silently drops a seed:0/count:0 on restore -- exactly the falsy-loss the hunt confirmed is currently handled but unguarded. Other untested-but-correct behaviors: shareLink Unicode round-trip via TextEncoder/TextDecoder, base64url padding-restore, schema_version mismatch -> null, malformed-base64 -> null never throws, savedStore corrupt-JSON/future-schema -> empty degrade, the JSON deep-clone.

SUGGESTED: new spa-next/src/lib/shareLink.test.js (encode->decode round-trip incl Unicode + falsy + schema mismatch + malformed) + extend savedStore.test.js with a save->load round-trip asserting falsy fields survive + workspaceSnapshot.test.js pinning the captured field set. vitest, pure serialization fns.

Out of the refactor/bugfix loop per-cycle scope (test-coverage addition, not refactor or bug fix). No bug exists today; regression-prevention on a user-data path.

title: build_family_rollup _lemma_root (nested) vs the 'byte-equivalent' flat COALESCE claim (_export.py:231) diverge on 85 dual merged+lemma rows
description:
A cycle-88 reviewer (PR #813) found that build_family_rollup's _lemma_root in wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/bundle/_export.py is NESTED — _lemma_root(eid) = lemma_by_id.get(target_by_id.get(eid, eid)) or target_by_id.get(eid, eid), i.e. resolve merged_into FIRST, then lemma-of-the-merge-target. But the comment at _export.py:231 claims the "legacy COALESCE(merged_into_id, lemma_id, id) columns — byte-equivalent". These are NOT equivalent DB-wide: flat COALESCE(merged_into_id, lemma_id, id) picks merged_into_id if non-null (ignoring a further lemma hop), while nested _lemma_root resolves merged THEN lemma. Measured on ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db: 1505/2.37M rows differ; 85 rows have BOTH merged_into_id AND lemma_id non-null (the exact case where they diverge — e.g. 4613076 schele: merged_into 3119644, whose lemma is 3093187 → flat=3119644 vs nested=3093187).

INVESTIGATE: does build_family_rollup actually USE the flat COALESCE columns anywhere (the "legacy COALESCE columns" the comment refers to) ALONGSIDE the nested _lemma_root? If the rollup mixes the two root definitions, a family root computed one way (flat) could disagree with one computed the other way (nested) on those 85 dual merged+lemma etymons → a split/mis-rooted family (latent identity bug). If build_family_rollup uses the nested _lemma_root CONSISTENTLY everywhere and the flat-COALESCE comment merely describes a superseded approach, then it is only an INACCURATE COMMENT (cosmetic) — fix the comment to stop claiming byte-equivalence. Determine which.

Scope: read _export.py build_family_rollup end-to-end; find every place a "root" is computed (flat COALESCE SQL vs _lemma_root vs root_of); confirm they agree on the 85 dual rows or fix the inconsistency. Did NOT affect duplicate_canonical_mining (#813) — that fix only excludes CHILD-roots and the one divergent endpoint there is a parent. Surfaced by the cycle-88 dupcanon reflex-link review.

title: descent_audit reads MERGED etymons (no merged_into_id filter) — inert today; filter re-positions 14 committed verdicts (migration)
description:
descent_audit.py reads cognate-clustered etymons + within-cluster descent edges WITHOUT a merged_into_id IS NULL filter — the recognized merged_into_id-omission pattern (sibling of wyrd-qdau/ckro/xqz3). Exact lines: descent_audit.py:86 (SELECT id,language,canonical_form,cognate_id FROM etymon WHERE cognate_id IS NOT NULL), :100 (gloss join WHERE e.cognate_id IS NOT NULL), :121 (_load_cluster_edges WHERE e1.cognate_id IS NOT NULL AND e1.cognate_id=e2.cognate_id). Every sibling index-builder filters merged_into_id — including variant_fold_detect.py:210, the very module descent_audit imports _gloss_tokens/_sense helpers from — so descent_audit is the genuine outlier.

CURRENTLY INERT (verified, cycle-87 audit, live ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db): only 5 merged etymons still carry a cognate_id; 16 unique within-cluster edges touch one. ALL 16 have the merged etymon as the modern-english CHILD (casefold tombstones: isle->Isle, ram->RAM, ...), glossed and in the cluster's DOMINANT sense-group. So 2b skips them (gidx.get(c)==unique_dom) and 2a never fires (these clusters collapse to a single sense-group with or without the tombstone). 0 of the 16 are ever screened (0/16 in data/mining/_descent_audit.jsonl); 0 applied detaches in _collapses.jsonl. The omission causes NO wrong detach + NO cluster corruption TODAY — the merged member only enlarges the already-dominant group by 1, never injects a spurious second group, never causes a GOOD edge to be screened.

WHY A MIGRATION, NOT A BYTE-IDENTICAL CODE FIX (cycle-63 discipline): adding the filter REMOVES 14 candidates (all from the isle cluster 376088) — dropping the tombstone shrinks that cluster's dominant group 2->1, so max_size>=2 fails and 2b stops firing for its 14 glossless-child fan-out edges (gmw-pro:insulā->osx:*insula, etc.). All 14 are ALREADY committed verdicts in _descent_audit.jsonl (12 KEEP no-ops + 2 high-conf DETACH, the 2 DETACHes not yet applied to _collapses.jsonl). So the filter ORPHANS 14 committed verdicts -> a ledger re-position with the reproducibility hazard the determinism-fix-over-nondeterministic-data memory flags. NOT slip-in-able to an unrelated PR expecting byte-identity.

DOWNSTREAM note: if a merged-touching edge WERE ever detached, it would NOT be inert — cognate_cluster.py:182 rolls tombstone edges up via COALESCE(merged_into_id,...), so DELETE-ing the raw etymon_descent row affects re-derivation. That path is unreachable today (no such edge is screened) but is why the filter is correct in principle.

FIX (bundle with the next deliberate _descent_audit.jsonl migration): add WHERE merged_into_id IS NULL to the 3 queries (matching every sibling), then re-screen the isle cluster + reconcile the 14 orphaned verdicts against the committed ledger before swapping. Verify the re-position against the REAL ledger, not just unit tests. Low priority — inert today. Surfaced by the cycle-87 descent_audit.py audit, which otherwise verified the module CLEAN (detach polarity correct end-to-end, verdict parse fail-closed, empty-token glosses excluded from sense-splitting, determinism holds, _is_proto/fan-out correct).

title: reflex_link_detect: latin/vulgar-latin link direction can be backwards (era-rank collapses 3 non-contiguous Latin cells)
description:
reflex_link_detect._LANGUAGE_ERA_RANK is built by first-seen enumeration over CANONICAL_LANGUAGE_FOR_CELL.items(): for each (family, cell)->language, setdefault(lang, index). This orders eras correctly WITHIN a family ONLY when each family's canonical-language tags appear once, in era order. That holds for english/welsh/irish/french/norse — but NOT for latin: the latin family's cells are classical->latin (index 13), late-vulgar->vulgar-latin (14), medieval->latin (13 again, setdefault no-op), renaissance->latin (13 again). So `latin` collapses classical+medieval+renaissance into rank 13, and `vulgar-latin` (the 200-700 late-vulgar cell, chronologically BETWEEN classical and medieval) ranks 14 — AFTER all the latin cells.

CONSEQUENCE: a (latin, vulgar-latin) cross-language pair is eligible (cross-language, same family, ranks 13 != 14), and _eval_reflex_pair makes latin (rank 13) the PARENT of vulgar-latin (rank 14, larger). If that `latin` row represents medieval/renaissance Latin, the true direction is the reverse (vulgar-latin 200-700 is earlier). On an LLM YES this writes a BACKWARDS inheritance edge into the descent graph (which cognate_cluster + era_reflex consume). Confirmed with a constructed pair: parent=latin:castellum, child=vulgar-latin:castellu. This contradicts the module's own comment (lines ~27-34) that the rank "orders eras correctly WITHIN a family".

SEVERITY: LOW-MEDIUM + currently latent. LLM-gated (a backwards proposal corrupts the graph only if the judge says YES). Does NOT surface on the current live DB — there are no qualifying latin/vulgar-latin reflex pairs (the 61 live candidates are all english/goidelic). But it is a genuine latent direction-swap, NOT documented design (the comment actively claims latin is safe).

FIX OPTIONS: (a) give _LANGUAGE_ERA_RANK a real chronological order for latin (vulgar-latin BEFORE medieval/renaissance latin) — but the rank derives from CANONICAL_LANGUAGE_FOR_CELL ordering, shared with era_reflex etc., so reordering that constant has wider blast-radius; safer is a small explicit per-language era-order override map in reflex_link_detect for the non-contiguous-tag families (just latin today). (b) or detect the collapsed-rank case and emit the latin/vulgar-latin pair as direction-ambiguous (skip, D46 leave-separate) rather than guessing. Either way add a regression test (latin/vulgar-latin pair → correct direction or skipped). Verify no other family has non-contiguous repeated canonical tags (audit CANONICAL_LANGUAGE_FOR_CELL). Surfaced by the cycle-80 reflex_link_detect.py audit; PR #807 fixed the separate determinism bug in the same file.

title: cognate_cluster: contested-node tiebreak is smallest-id (arbitrary) over 164k nodes, not 'rare' — re-validate vs nearest-root
description:
cognate_cluster._assign_cognate_clusters resolves a node reachable from MULTIPLE distinct roots by "smallest root id wins" (BFS over roots in ascending id order, skip-if-assigned — D22-style deterministic tiebreak). The docstring justifies this as a RARE case ("happens when scholars disagree on the chain"). That premise is empirically FALSE by ~5 orders of magnitude: against the live ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db, 164,065 nodes are reachable from >=2 distinct roots, and the competing roots are frequently genuinely UNRELATED families — e.g. majem/dutch is reachable from Proto-Semitic *māy, Ancient-Greek μῖμος, AND French mémé; it is assigned to the Proto-Semitic root purely because its id is numerically smallest. Smallest-id is deterministic but ARBITRARY — it does not prefer the closest/genuine immediate ancestor, so a contested node and its whole subtree can be clustered behind an etymologically-wrong root, feeding era_reflex (Tier-1 cluster mates) and the vector scorer a mismatched cognate set.

NOT a code bug (the BFS, edge filtering inheritance+borrowing-only, PIE blocklist, cycle handling, determinism, merged_into all verified CLEAN in the cycle-79 audit) — this is a DESIGN question: is smallest-id acceptable at 164k contested nodes, or should the tiebreak prefer the nearest/deepest reaching root?

WHY TICKETED not tick-fixed: (a) the precise mis-cluster rate is UNQUANTIFIED — the "how often does smallest-id beat a CLOSER root" job over 750k edges timed out; needs measuring first. (b) switching the tiebreak to nearest-root re-clusters up to 164k contested nodes → re-positions committed cognate_id at scale + cascades to every consumer (era_reflex, decomposition_grader, same_morpheme_mining, meaning_merge_detect) — the cycle-68/wyrd-qdau coordinated-migration class, not a code-only PR. DELIVERABLE: (1) measure the fraction of the 164k where the nearest reaching root differs from the smallest-id winner (+ how many cross IE-family); (2) if material, switch to nearest/deepest-root tiebreak and re-cluster as a coordinated rebuild step with downstream re-validation; (3) if smallest-id is deemed acceptable at this volume, just keep it (the docstring is being corrected separately to drop the false "rare" premise). Surfaced by the cycle-79 cognate_cluster.py audit.

title: same_morpheme_mining: broaden _GENERIC_GLOSSES placeholder set (inert variants + safe predicate)
description: PR #797 fixed the 2 LIVE wrong same-morpheme binds resting on a placeholder gloss (_GENERIC_GLOSSES = {a personal name, personal name}). Both reviewers confirmed those are the ONLY placeholders causing a wrong bind in the current DB (0 missed today). BUT the breakdown-etymon gloss pool has many other zero-identity '<x> name' placeholders NOT in the set — 'masculine personal name.'(44), 'a feminine personal name'(196), 'name'(23), 'river name'/'river-name'(~13), "man's name"(6), "person's name"(5), 'feminine personal name.', "saint's name", 'personal name.', 'personal name (saint)', 'personal name element'. Glosses normalize via .strip().lower() only (no period/article folding), so these are distinct strings outside the 2-element allowlist. They are INERT today (none is the sole overlap of a unique medium bind), but a future mining batch making one a sole overlap would silently slip a WRONG bind (identity-collapse) through. TASK: broaden the placeholder coverage SAFELY. Options: (a) curate a fuller literal set of the observed '<x> name' placeholders; (b) a predicate (e.g. normalized gloss matches '(a |the )?(masculine |feminine )?(personal )?name([. ]|$)' or ends in 'name'/'name.') — BUT must NOT over-suppress the REAL morpheme glossed 'name' (OE nama, meaning 'name'), so a bare 'name' needs care (placeholder 'a personal name' vs real 'name'). Verify any broadened set/predicate against the live miner: it must still drop 0 REAL-gloss binds (byte-identical on the 48 real-gloss medium binds) + the broadening itself is inert today (byte-identical on live data). Low priority (no current wrong bind beyond the 2 fixed).

title: canonicalization D46 conflict/refute keys on un-normalized ref (dash-variant bypass) + 12 dash-stored etymons unresolvable
description: cycle-61 canonicalization_projection.py audit (hunter, no ACTIVE bug — both latent). FINDING 1 (D46 bypass): _group_binds (line 313 grouping key) and _bind_key (172, used for the refute set at 285/295) key on the RAW subject.ref, but _resolve_obs_key→resolve_etymon_ref (etymon_refs.py:81) DE-DASHES the form (normalize_morpheme_surface, D45). So two binds whose refs differ only in boundary dashes ('celtic:-ach' vs 'celtic:ach') sit in SEPARATE groups but resolve to the SAME etymon row. Each group sees one root → the per-group D46 conflict check (_resolve_binds:380-384) never fires → both emit a BindWrite for the same (table,key_cols,key_vals) → _write_projection runs two UPDATEs, last-writer-wins SILENTLY (a genuine identity conflict masked, not flagged+left-unbound as D46 requires). Symmetrically a dash-variant refute fails to suppress its affirm. REPRO: author binds refs '<lang>:-<form>' and '<lang>:<form>' to two distinct minted hubs vs one bare-form etymon → conflicts:[], warnings:[], silent CM-1 wins. LATENT: every emitter today (same_morpheme_mining:276, duplicate_canonical_mining:410, _legacy_identity_assertions:553, gloss_sense:287) builds the ref from the already-de-dashed stored canonical_form, so no dashed ref is produced — defense-in-depth gap, not active corruption. FIX OPTIONS: (A) normalize the ref form (normalize_morpheme_surface) in _bind_key + the grouping key so dash-variants merge into one group (reuses existing per-group conflict machinery); (B) detect conflicts on the RESOLVED (table,key_cols,key_vals) post-resolution in _resolve_binds (more robust, but needs to track (subj_type,subj_ref) alongside each BindWrite for Conflict reporting + bound counting). Both are non-trivial changes to identity-critical code for a non-triggered case → deliberate, not a loop drive-by. Byte-identical on current data either way (no dashed resolvable refs exist). FINDING 2 (related, stored-data): 12 of 200k stored etymon.canonical_form values have TRAILING NON-ASCII dashes (e.g. '*bʰres‑' U+2011, '*senh₂‐' U+2010) that normalize_morpheme_surface strips. resolve_etymon_ref de-dashes the REF but matches WHERE canonical_form=<de-dashed>, while the STORED form keeps the dash → no match → these 12 PIE-root etymons are UNREFERENCEABLE in the canonical graph (D45-in-stored-data violation; the ingest/normalize path that stored them dashed missed these non-ASCII dash codepoints, OR they predate the rule). Rebuild-coupled to fix the data; consider a normalizer pass. Verify: sqlite3 ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db "SELECT canonical_form FROM etymon WHERE canonical_form GLOB '*[‐‑‒–—―−﹘﹣－]'" (non-ASCII dashes).

title: strata _ancestor_walk_proposals counts ALL descent edge_types (no loan-only filter)
description: Surfaced in PR #793 review (cycle-59 strata.py audit). _ancestor_walk_proposals (strata.py ~544-551) pulls every parent language via etymon_descent with NO edge_type filter, so a stratum like 'english-loan' means 'has an English-mapped parent by ANY edge' (borrowing/derivation/inheritance/calque/compound). For CROSS-FAMILY ancestors (Latin, English → Welsh) this is correct by construction — no inheritance is possible across families, so any edge IS a loan (the en-ear/enm-wmi/en-GB additions in #793 are all borrowing/derivation; the one enm-wmi flip 'siom' is a genuine loan). BUT it's worth scrutiny generally: e.g. modern-english→welsh has 501 'inheritance' edges in the live DB (etymologically odd for cross-family — possible etymon_descent edge_type data-quality issue), all currently bucketed english-loan. QUESTION: should the classifier filter to loan-type edges (borrowing/derivation/calque) and exclude inheritance, OR is the all-edges behavior intended? If filtered, the modern-/middle-/old-english entries' inheritance children would re-classify. Investigate the 501 modern-english inheritance edges (real cross-family loans mis-typed as inheritance, or genuine noise?) before deciding. Pre-existing; not introduced by #793.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIXED at source (PR #794, cycle 60): the odd cross-family 'inheritance' edges (501 modern-english→welsh, etymologically impossible) were NOT a classifier issue — they were the wiktextract parser (_descendant_edge_type) ignoring raw_tags, where the 'borrowed' marker actually lives. 16,177 borrowed descendants across the English slice were mis-typed inheritance. Parser fixed (reads tags + raw_tags). The remaining wyrd-fljy question (should the strata classifier filter edge_types?) is now LOWER priority: future ingests feed correctly-typed edges. Stored ~16k edges still need a re-ingest/rebuild-from-jsonl to correct. Re-evaluate the classifier-filter question AFTER a rebuild — it may be moot.

title: _fetch_member_variants: bare matched_form in GROUP BY is non-deterministic (1780 case-collided groups, reaches generation)
description: cycle-56 _family.py audit. _fetch_member_variants (bundle/_family.py ~874) selects a BARE non-aggregated matched_form under GROUP BY etymon_id, LOWER(matched_form). The fold collapses case-variant spellings (Chimaera/chimaera, Anti-Christ/anti-Christ) into one row; the bare column then surfaces an ENGINE-DEFINED arbitrary row's casing. 1780 such collided groups in the live lexicon. The casing REACHES GENERATION: member_variants -> _absorb_member_variants (_subject.py:457) inserts variant_form as a per-language surface-form randomization-pool key. So a SQLite-version/query-plan change would silently shift generated names = a byte-reproducibility hole. FIX is a casing-POLICY decision + rebuild (not byte-identical): MAX(matched_form) drifts 987/1780 groups from today's bare pick (uppercase-leading -> lowercase-leading); most-attested-casing diverges from MAX in only ~19 groups (rest count-ties). Pick a deterministic aggregate, regen the live bundle, and validate realism/parity. ABANDONED PR #791 attempted MAX but mis-claimed byte-identity (the verification used a bare column ALONGSIDE MAX in one SELECT, which SQLite forces equal via the MIN/MAX-row rule — a false drift=0). To verify any candidate: run the ORIGINAL bare-column query and the aggregate query as SEPARATE statements and diff.

title: brittonic-keyed empirical priors unreachable via _lemma_ref_for (celtic_mix→celtic collapse)
description: Found during cycle-55 audit of vectors/scoring.py. The english-culture empirical_priors contain ~19 lemma_refs keyed 'brittonic:<form>' (extract_priors uses etymon.language verbatim: empirical_priors.py:341). At runtime _lemma_ref_for (vector_name_select.py) maps the bundle 'celtic_mix' field to the single representative 'celtic' (_BUNDLE_FIELD_TO_L3_LANG), and there is no 'brittonic' value in that reverse map; brittonic-substrate morphemes land in celtic_mix. So those ~19 brittonic priors are never hit — their baseline silently degrades to 0 (graceful, per the documented degrade contract). MINOR: 19 of ~1500 english priors; non-english cultures have no priors at all so are unaffected. The bulk celtic case IS consistent ('celtic'(20) priors ↔ celtic_mix→'celtic'). FIX (rebuild-coupled, hence not done in-loop): either add a brittonic→field/reverse mapping, or collapse brittonic→celtic in extract_priors so the priors key matches the runtime lookup; then re-emit the bundle + re-validate realism/parity. Verify the live distribution with: sqlite3 ~/.wyrd/dashboard-bundle.db "SELECT data FROM empirical_priors;" | grep -oE '"brittonic:[a-z-]+'.

title: Dedup the two _coerce_date_year copies into one shared helper
description: toponym_mention_ingest.py and toponym_candidate_review.py each carry a byte-identical-semantics _coerce_date_year (JSONL date_year → int|None). #772 fixed the isdigit→isdecimal crash in BOTH copies; the 'kept in sync' comment is now a MANUAL invariant (guarded only by both test files asserting the superscript cases). Retirement tool: scripts/wyrd_j2bv_rando_retirement.py (splits data/mining/rando-port.jsonl → retired/rando-retired.jsonl tombstone). title: LLM-leads rando corroboration pipeline with a source-validation gate (long tail)
description:
For morphemes not covered by dictionary ingestion (wyrd ticket A), use an LLM to ROUTE each morpheme to a likely published source + a claimed quote — NOT to author citations. Hard gate: a lead becomes an etymon_citation ONLY if validated against real ingested source text; never blind DB writes (an LLM is a research lead, not a scholarly source). Emit a reviewable leads file (no L3/L2 writes) for human approval first.

Use a capable model — gemma4:26b local or paid Gemini/Anthropic; the 9B smoke garbled titles. ollama on 10.5.2.31; qwen3.x are thinking models so pass think:false (else response is empty — see scratch/rando_corroborate_smoke.py). Raw lead rate ~25%, unvalidated.

The command errors out-of-the-box. title: Move the proto/reconstruction '*' marker out of etymon.canonical_form into a 'reconstructed' boolean field
description: Split out of wyrd-aicu.8 (deferred — too big to bundle). Same philosophy as the dash/position de-dash: '*' (reconstructed vs attested) is a QUALITY of the etymon, not part of the identity TEXT. Move it to a 'reconstructed' boolean column; strip '*' from canonical_form. SCALE + WRINKLE (measured): 65,229 leading-'*' etymons (mostly proto langs: PIE, proto-germanic, gmw-pro, proto-celtic). Stripping '*' collides the language:canonical_form natural key with attested forms — 14,052 within-language (lang,bare) groups mix a reconstructed + an attested member (e.g. old-english:*Banna vs old-english:Banna — DISTINCT evidence, must NOT merge). So this needs: (a) a 'reconstructed' boolean column + the UNIQUE widened to (canonical_form, language, reconstructed) [SQLite table-rebuild], (b) a ref strategy that keeps the two distinct — recommend keeping a '*' SIGIL in the etymon_ref derivation (language:*form) while the COLUMN is bare + the boolean carries truth (the L2 _assert_descends_from streams already carry 1,026 language:*form refs, so they resolve unchanged), (c) CM-hash re-mint for any canonical node minted off a '*' form, (d) L4 morpheme_id reconstructed encoding (keep the '*' sigil so the dash-gate stays valid). Detailed analysis in the wyrd-aicu.8 planning session (2026-06-21). Do AFTER aicu.8's boundary-dash de-dash lands.

title: Cognate-cluster uplift for accepted morphemes (GUARDED — active over-merge bugs)
description: 1,870 admit-cohort morphemes (60.0%) have no cognate_id. Binding them into cognate clusters lets variant spellings bridge across cognates and is high-VALUE for the grader (it compares by cluster). BUT this is the RISKIEST uplift: active P1 over-merge bugs (wyrd-rd69 cross-language contamination, wyrd-6hbv homograph blobs, wyrd-vewk; epic wyrd-3vju) mean a careless bind worsens conflation. Therefore NOT a default unattended-loop target. Constraints: conservative same-morpheme/same-language binds only (the _assert_bind.jsonl 'same-morpheme' path, actor opus), grounded in shared gloss + lemma, PARK anything cross-language or ambiguous, and respect the over-merge fixes. Sequence AFTER rd69/6hbv land, or run human-in-the-loop. Relates to wyrd-feeq (keep-vs-drop low-confidence edges).

title: aicu.7 collateral: ~10 pools where an untagged canonical loses to a tagged off-sense sibling
description: From wyrd-aicu.7 PR #724 (data-quality review). The tags-present term in _rank_siblings (correctly promotes canonical over untagged thin stubs: wick→wīc, ley→leah, +46 improvements) has ~10 collateral pools where the CANONICAL toponymic etymon is itself UNTAGGED + exact-surface, and a thinly-tagged OFF-SENSE sibling now outranks it: ach (tagged kinship beats the canonical toponymic 'field/marshy land/place'), fair (to-watch beats isthmus), ell (gell colour, surf 0.857, beats exact-surface 'ell' 1.0). 0 PINNED-canonical regressions (the 18-pin suite is green); these are off-pin pools. Root cause = a DATA gap: the canonical toponymic etymon lacks tags. The reviewer's suggested 'gate the tags-term below exact-1.0 surface' does NOT work — it would revert the wick fix (the wick stub IS the exact-1.0 match; the canonical wīc is 0.857). Two fix axes: (a) TAG the ~10 untagged canonical toponymic etymons (data — then they win on the tags-term too), or (b) a finer ranking signal (e.g. toponymic-sense weight, or scholarly-witness count as a secondary). Enumerate the full ~10 (investigation found them full-corpus) + decide. Net-acceptable to ship aicu.7 as-is (the reviewers approved net +46/-10).

title: Re-vet structure curation for non-english languages (group rules over-cull anglicized toponyms)
description: The english structure-curation rules (wyrd-6o0a: 4+word, multi-[name], single-word>=4-morpheme, bare-heavy multi-word, all <=1%) do NOT transfer to the other languages. Applying them broadly dropped irish morpheme_rank_correlation 0.30->0.199 (test_kenning_realism_absolute[irish]) because anglicized Irish (and welsh/breton) place-names legitimately use more multi-word / bare-string patterns ('Carrick on Shannon', 'Ballina'). Group 1 (single word >=4 morphemes — run-on gibberish) is likely safe everywhere; group 2 (bare-heavy >=3-word) is the over-cull. DECISION (Devon): per-language curation pass with realism re-checked after each, OR a gentler rule for non-english. PARENT: wyrd-c6o1.

title: Curate english structures.yaml: cull run-on / boring / multi-name structures (operator triage)
description:
Operator-driven curation of the per-language structure allowlist (wyrd-hzqs), english section only. Devon triaged english generation structures and culled the low-quality tail by rule:
- 4+ WORDS and <=1% (run-on multi-word names)
- >=2 [name] tags and <=1% (multiple personal-names read weird; zero such structures are >1%)
- single word with >=4 morphemes (the Anaseynteraegehana run-on-compound class)
- >=3 words with >=2 bare words (boring dictionary-word strings)
KEPT: 2-bare-word names ('(bare) (bare)' etc. — reasonable), 3-morpheme single words (Wolverhampton-shapes), single-[name] compounds.
Result: english 376/480 disabled, 104 enabled. Other languages left at baseline (group rules over-cull irish — morpheme_rank_correlation 0.30->0.199 — because anglicized non-english toponyms legitimately use more multi-word/bare patterns; deferred, see follow-up).
Also: fixed a pre-existing brittle request-isolation test (water tag-coverage is ~0.78 at BASELINE, not a regression; the 0.9 absolute proxy held only by seed luck at n=8 — retargeted to test isolation warm-vs-cold) + regenerated the rogd10 parity golden snapshot (curation intentionally changes english output). PARENT: wyrd-c6o1.
close_reason: PR #721 merged. English structures.yaml curation: 376/480 disabled (104 enabled) — culled 4+word ≤1%, multi-[name] ≤1%, single-word ≥4-morpheme run-ons, and bare-heavy ≥3-word dictionary-strings; kept 2-bare-word names, Wolverhampton-shape 3-morpheme single words, single-[name] compounds. Pure true→false flips (drift-guard green). Non-english left at baseline (group rules over-cull anglicized toponyms — irish realism 0.30→0.199 — deferred to the re-vet follow-up). Test consequences (not regressions): retargeted a brittle request-isolation test to exact warm==cold isolation (water ~0.75 is baseline behavior, not caused by the cull; Gemini-endorsed ==); regenerated the rogd10 parity golden (curation intentionally changes english output). 2 review rounds, full suite 5710.

title: G2P/phonemizer chokes on proper & fantasy place names (Phase-1b)
description:
Surfaced by dream-mining (2026-06-21, cluster c015/c057). Grapheme-to-phoneme libraries mishandle non-compositional proper names — 'Worcestershire', 'Cholmondeley' — and fantasy names with no English orthographic basis ('Drizzt'). This matters for the per-lemma phonological vectors that feed vector scoring: a bad G2P → bad phonological vector → bad phonaesthetic/mood scoring for those names.

Flagged as a Phase-1b concern for TTRPG use, where fantasy/invented place names are common inputs. Not blocking current English-toponym generation (the committed corpus is scholar-attested), but a known accuracy gap for user-supplied or fantasy-pack names.

Scope to investigate:
- which G2P path(s) are in use and where (phonological vector build)
- failure characterization on a small proper/fantasy-name probe set
- options: pronunciation-dictionary lookup first, fallback heuristics, or accept-and-flag low-confidence vectors

No action required yet — this is a captured backlog concern, not a regression.

title: Refresh the stale committed seed-runtime.db from a clean rebuild baseline
description: The committed dev seed wyrd/generators/kenning/data/seed-runtime.db was last regenerated at #629 (wyrd-aicu.1), before dozens of merges (zrce, de77, f233, 65jh, aicu.9 connective wiring, era-map #713, ujyo surface_in_modern, …). Surfaced during aicu.9 (PR for the connective live-wiring took Path B = additive table + no bump to avoid this).

Ran full REBUILD.md Phase 2; verified rebuilt-vs-live (0 delta on glosses/country/forms; caught a missing import-modern-reflexes that would've dropped 145 modern-english glosses). Seed now carries the aicu.9 connective fix (25 genitive pairs + corrected proportions). Coupled artifacts regenerated; worth/breton clean-rebuild signals xfailed + tracked in wyrd-8vfo/aicu.7.

title: Auto-regen structures.yaml on rebuild-proportions + CI drift-guard
description:
Follow-up to the per-language structures.yaml refresh-merge dump. Keep structures.yaml in sync with the proportions automatically.

WHY (Devon): new structures appear after decomposition/proportions rebuild; the allowlist should be regenerated each time so we never forget to surface new structures for filtering.

DESIGN:
- HOOK the refresh-merge dump as a TAIL STEP of rebuild-proportions (the authoring step that recomputes proportions after decompose), writing the WORKING-TREE data/structures.yaml. NOT at L4 runtime generate (read-only bundle / Lambda / per-request perf — forbidden).
- DO NOT auto-COMMIT: regen updates the working file + leaves the git diff for operator review (the whole point is the human filters NEW structures before they ship). The refresh-merge keeps existing falses, so the diff is just new/dropped structures.
- CI DRIFT-GUARD test: fail if committed data/structures.yaml != a fresh refresh-merge over the current bundle (catches 'rebuilt but forgot to re-dump/commit'). Mirrors the existing c6o1.5 drift-guard pattern.
- Keep the discrete dump-structures CLI for manual runs.

DEPENDS ON the core per-language refresh-merge bead (must land first).
notes:
DRIFT-GUARD HALF SHIPPED via PR #716 (test_committed_structures_yaml_in_sync_with_bundle): asserts the committed structures.yaml byte-equals a fresh refresh-merge over the committed seed-runtime.db (skips when WYRD_RUNTIME_DB[_BUCKET] redirects to a full-corpus L4). Catches a bundle re-export that adds/retires structures without a re-dump.

AUTO-REGEN HOOK HALF — REMAINING, with CORRECTED design (original spec's 'rebuild-proportions' target was WRONG: that command only emits proportions JSON to stdout, it does NOT rebuild seed-runtime.db). The real bundle build is 'wyrd kenning lexicon export-runtime-db --dev' (cli/lexicon/export_runtime_db.py — the canonical 'regenerate the committed seed-runtime.db' invocation). It ALREADY post-writes a decomposition-matcher sidecar via _build_matcher_sidecar (points WYRD_RUNTIME_DB at the just-written DB, resets runtime caches, builds, resets again) — that's the EXACT precedent the structures.yaml auto-regen should mirror: after write_runtime_db in --dev mode, regen structures.yaml from the just-written DB (read committed file as merge base, _build/_render, write to output_path.parent/'structures.yaml'), do NOT auto-commit (leave the working-tree file for operator review). DECISIONS to confirm (Devon, light): (1) hook on --dev only (the committed-seed build) vs also full/generation exports; (2) write target = sibling of --output. Testing note: end-to-end needs a live lexicon DB (absent in CI) — test the regen helper in isolation against the committed seed-runtime.db (point at it, write to tmp, assert == committed) like the drift-guard does.
close_reason: FULLY DONE. Both halves shipped: (1) CI drift-guard PR #716 — committed structures.yaml must byte-equal a fresh refresh-merge over the committed seed; (2) auto-regen hook PR #717 — export-runtime-db --dev (the canonical 'regenerate the committed seed-runtime.db' invocation) now regenerates structures.yaml next to the DB via _regen_structure_allowlist. Reads the just-written L4 via runtime_db._open_readonly (read-only; no raw sqlite3 in cli/lexicon per package-boundary); refresh-merges over the WORKING-TREE sibling structures.yaml (Gemini HIGH fix: not the importlib.resources/installed copy, so non-editable installs don't silently drop curation), falling back to bundled on first dump; writes the working-tree file for operator review (NEVER auto-commits); prints +new/-dropped to stderr. Original spec's rebuild-proportions target was wrong (corrected to export-runtime-db --dev). Decisions taken (defensible defaults): --dev-only + sibling write. 3 review rounds (P2 sticky-false test + Gemini HIGH addressed). Full suite 5713.

title: Mine implied reflexes at support>=2 + impoverished-cluster over-consume (wyrd-65jh follow-on)
description: From wyrd-65jh. Shipped the support>=3 band (105 implied reflexes, ~90% precision). Two extensions: (1) the support==2 tail (~150 more) is ~78-85% precise — mostly anchor-surface errors the guard can't catch; needs a precision pass (e.g. anchor-validity check) before it's committable. (2) Residual impoverished-cluster over-consume leaks the cluster-aware guard can't fully reach when an etymon's cluster is a NULL-cognate_id singleton whose cognate variant lives in a separate cluster (the (language, fold(canonical_form)) grouping catches the macron/ASCII tun/tūn case but not all). Also: 65jh extract is non-idempotent against a DB already carrying its own applied reflexes (the already-known guard skips them) — re-mining for the remainder must start from a clean rebuild baseline (the reproducibility trap), not the post-apply live DB.

title: Deliver implied-reflex surface_in_modern safely + fix dump_all_sources data-loss
description: Follow-up from wyrd-65jh. The implied-reflex miner (mine-implied-reflexes) ALSO computes toponym_etymology_element.surface_in_modern (1383 elements for support>=3), but its --apply persists it via dump_all_sources, which (a) re-dumps EVERY per-source L2 JSONL (~40 files, 121k-line diff — unreviewable) and (b) emits a data-loss WARNING: 7327 toponym_attestation rows have source_doc that routes nowhere (neither matches a source.id nor a registered _ATTESTATION_DOC_PREFIX_TO_SOURCE prefix) and 'will be lost on rebuild'. So surface_in_modern was DEFERRED from the 65jh PR (only the reflex + canonical-label outputs shipped). Two tracks: (1) FIX dump_all_sources to not silently drop the 7327 unrouted attestations (register the missing prefixes or fail loud) — a real durability bug; (2) make the implied-reflex apply write surface_in_modern via a SCOPED per-touched-source dump (not dump_all_sources), so it's a small reviewable diff. Until then surface_in_modern stays 100% NULL.

title: Promote toponymic surfaces (surface_in_modern) into the D18 spelling-variant pool
description: GENERATIVE follow-on to wyrd-ujyo (which derived surface_in_modern). Now promote those per-element toponymic surfaces into the D18 spelling-variant pool of the name etymon, so generation can emit worn-down name forms as they appear in place-names — e.g. Earda gains surface 'Arde-'. Insert into etymon_text_match (or the variant pool) tagged toponymic-surface (NOT a standalone name), reading toponym_etymology_element.surface_in_modern (populated by derive_surface_in_modern). NEEDS A DECISION: the tag-convention pick (how 'toponymic-surface' variants are flagged + how generation gates them so they don't leak as standalone names) — that's why wyrd-ujyo deferred this half. Parent epic: wyrd-eni4.

title: Unglossed admit etymons need a DIRECT gloss path — element_gloss_backfill targets reflexes, not etymons
description: From wyrd-m415. The ticket assumed element_gloss_backfill could gloss the ~116 unglossed >=2-toponym admit ETYMONS. It can't: apply_element_glosses links unglossed REFLEXES to already-glossed etymons (reflex_etymon), only for prefix/suffix positions, and only reaches generation surfaces (proportions_usage). Census of the admit cohort: of 113 unglossed admit etymons, 62 are NOT generation surfaces (tool can't see them), ~25 have no grounding consensus, and the ~26 reachable produce mostly co-occurrence-noise or fragment glosses (verified via gemma4:26b adjudication: 'to'->tun, 'Es'->west, 'aco'->oak, 'par'->park; only ~1-2 like egles->church are correct, and even those fail to apply — standalone position is unmapped in _POSITION_TO_REFLEX and 'egles' has no reflex row). ROOT CAUSE: many unglossed admits are over-segmentation FRAGMENTS that shouldn't be admitted as morphemes (an upstream decomposition/admission-quality issue), and the genuine ones need a DIRECT etymon-gloss path (consensus over (lang,normform) toponym-etymology glosses written to etymon_gloss), not the reflex-linking tool. Two sub-tracks: (1) tighten admit criteria to exclude fragments; (2) build/extend a direct etymon_gloss backfill for real unglossed admit etymons.

title: Regenerate path: apply era-fashion midpoint to single-slot re-roll (wyrd-3tvd follow-up)
description: wyrd-3tvd wired the priors-baseline era_midpoint into the MAIN generation path (kenning._generate_via_vector → select_via_vector). The per-morpheme regenerate path (kenning_regenerate.py, flag-gated 'regenerate-morpheme', OFF in prod) scores its single-slot re-roll via name_gen._build_vector_pools + _weighted_pool_with_fallback, which do NOT thread era_midpoint (baseline lookup defaults to 0). So a re-rolled morpheme ignores era-fashion while the rest of the name (generated via the main path) leaned toward it — a minor inconsistency. Scope: thread era_midpoint (= _request_era_midpoint(_resolve_era_param(era, culture)) — already computed analogously in regenerate at kenning_regenerate.py:400 where era_record_cutoff is derived) through _weighted_pool_with_fallback → the baseline fill so the re-roll scores against the same era cell. Zero prod impact (flag off). Small.
close_reason: PR #712 merged. wyrd-3tvd follow-up: threaded the priors-baseline era_midpoint through the per-morpheme regenerate path (kenning_regenerate, flag 'regenerate-morpheme', OFF in prod). _parse_knobs derives era_midpoint=_request_era_midpoint(era_range) (mirroring era_record_cutoff from the same resolved range); _weighted_pool_with_fallback threads it into BOTH _slot_weighted_pool calls (keyed + bucket-miss fallback). No _build_vector_pools change — it returns an empty lazy slot_base_scores cache so the era cell applies on first build (same as the main path). Now a single-slot re-roll under a bounded era leans toward that period's naming fashion, consistent with the rest of the name. title: Align matcher fold + synthesis fold to clean OE/ON letters (æ/þ/ð/ø) from rendered surfaces
description: From wyrd-f233 PR #702 review (morpheme-surface-identity). f233 cleaned macron/proto from the reflex-less synthesis fallback but DELIBERATELY left OE/ON letters (æ/þ/ð/ø) unmapped, because the runtime matcher fold (genitive_priors.fold_surface, proportions._grid_match_key) maps them its OWN inconsistent way (þ→th, ð→d, ø dropped, ǣ dropped but plain æ→ae) — so ASCII-mapping them only at synthesis would make a synthesized surface fold-differently than its canonical and break self-binding (wyrd-mook 'surface not in its own reflexes'). ~218 reflex-less admits still render with OE letters (e.g. Þorp, Ðæc); ~47 keep raw macron-ligatures (ǣ). To clean these from RENDERED surfaces, the matcher fold and the synthesis fold must be aligned to ONE canonical OE-letter mapping (decide: þ→th, ð→th-or-d, æ→ae, ø→o; fix fold_surface's ǣ-drop-vs-æ-expand inconsistency too), then synthesis can ASCII-map safely. D45-sensitive (changes matching identity for þ/æ families across the system) — needs its own review + a rebuild durability check.

title: Cognate-descent: decide keep-vs-drop for low-confidence surface-only edges in committed L2
description: From wyrd-zrce PR #691 data-quality review. _assert_descends_from.jsonl commits ~1182 LOW-confidence surface-only fold-match edges (from cognate_descent_mining._place, no semantic/LLM gate) alongside the realized medium edges. They are GATED OFF at projection (medium gate) so they don't affect clustering, and are honestly labeled confidence=low (D50 evidence-sacred pattern). BUT they contain clear homograph garbage (exotic-script + dash-root) and bloat the committed L2 by ~60%. DECISION NEEDED: (a) keep (honest low evidence, a future better tiebreaker might use them); (b) stop emitting/committing low surface-only edges (only commit medium+); (c) commit but document that low = unverified-surface-only so downstream gates on confidence. Relates: the evidence miner's emit-all-with-confidence behavior is established, so changing it is a behavior decision.

title: Cognate-descent: exotic-script LLM false positives slip past adversarial verify
description: From wyrd-zrce PR #691 data-quality review. ~3-5% of the REALIZED (medium, LLM-confirmed) cognate-descent edges are cross-script homographs the propose+verify LLM (gemma4:26b) wrongly confirmed — e.g. brittonic:fawr -> ar:فوران, old-english:sūðan -> ar:سودان (Sudan), old-english:Gobán -> ja:碁盤 (Go board). Surface-prefix fold-match + the LLM rubber-stamps a spurious cross-family link. FIX OPTIONS: (a) a language-family plausibility gate (reject cognate edges between implausible family pairs — e.g. a non-IE script root for an English/Celtic morpheme) applied before/after the LLM; (b) strengthen the verify prompt to reject cross-script/family pairs; (c) require the bridge/root to share a plausible ancestry family. Needs tuning + its own review. Adversarial verify already rejects 257/1055 proposals (75.6% confirm rate), so this is the residual tail.

title: kenning matcher/grader type-design: ConnectiveKind StrEnum + tuple[Connective] inventory + MatcherConfig dataclass
description:
Split from wyrd-gzjo (items 1 + 2) — the two genuine type-design REFACTORS, deferred from the gzjo PR (which did the low-risk shared-util promotions + cleanups 3-6) because these ripple through load-bearing matcher/grader signatures and deserve their own focused review.

Bundle into a frozen MatcherConfig dataclass. Touches those 3 signatures + the internal _decompose_name/_match helpers + call sites (decomposition_grader 374/451/452/481/491, cli/lexicon/grade_decomposition.py:198) + tests/test_kenning_decomposition_grader.py. Behavior-preserving (kw-only today, 'not a rule violation' — ergonomic).

Both advisory ('consider') in the original review; non-blocking. Do as two separate commits.
notes: VETTED LOOP-WORKABLE 2026-06-21. MEDIUM, approach fully specified in ticket (two behavior-preserving commits). (1) ConnectiveKind(StrEnum) in connective.py (keep GENITIVE/FORMATIVE/LINKING as member aliases — StrEnum==str keeps existing ==GENITIVE comparisons valid), retype Connective.kind, change ConnectiveInventory/DEFAULT to tuple[Connective,...], fix the (surface,kind) destructure in trie_matcher._connective_candidates. PLR0913 isn't in this repo's ruff select, so the 3-field grouping was chosen for semantic cleanliness over param-count. 3 review rounds (15-agent round 1 → 2 P2 fixes → 2 verification rounds clean). title: JSONL dump merged_into_id follow-to-winner is single-hop — multi-hop merge chains resurrect a mid-tombstone
description:
Surfaced by db-reconstructibility-reviewer on PR #690 (wyrd-q6ro). All three jsonl/dump.py follow-to-winner sites use single-hop COALESCE(ref.merged_into_id, ref.id): _dump_cited_etymons, _dump_citations (both wyrd-q6ro), and _dump_fantasy_etymons / _dump_fantasy_morpheme_rows (wyrd-ruvk).

Single-hop only resolves ONE merge hop. The OCR auto-collapse path can't form chains (_apply_variant_fold resolves 'into' via _resolve_live_etymon, which excludes merged_into_id IS NOT NULL). BUT the curation path _apply_curated_merge (enrichment.py ~186-217) resolves merged_into_ref via the tombstone-agnostic _resolve_etymon_id (guards only self-reference), so a curation batch can set loser.merged_into_id = mid where mid is itself a tombstone (mid.merged_into_id = winner) — a 2-hop chain. Single-hop COALESCE then emits mid (still a merged loser); build_from_jsonl drops merged_into_id, so mid resurfaces as a live unmerged etymon = the exact D22 violation q6ro closes, one hop deeper.

Latent today (requires a specific curation order to build a chain).

Fix options (reviewer): (a) recursive winner resolution — a CTE or find_canonical-style walk — shared by ALL dump-path sites (cited, citation, fantasy); OR (b) a curation-time / rebuild-time invariant that flattens merged_into_id chains so it always points to a TERMINAL winner (then single-hop COALESCE stays correct everywhere + the dump comments' 'winner is unmerged' claim becomes true). Option (b) is likely cheaper and fixes the root cause once. wyrd-q6ro softened its comment to note the single-hop assumption + cross-ref this ticket rather than overstating the guarantee.
notes: VETTED LOOP-WORKABLE 2026-06-21 with DEFAULT = ticket's option (b). Multi-hop merge chains resurrect mid-tombstones because dump.py uses single-hop COALESCE(ref.merged_into_id, ref.id) at ~6 sites (219/257/386/903 + descent 296-301) and enrichment._apply_curated_merge (_resolve_etymon_id, no merged_into_id IS NULL filter) can point a loser at a tombstone. DEFAULT FIX (b, ticket-preferred, cheaper, fixes root once): add a chain-flatten invariant at curation/rebuild time so merged_into_id always points at the terminal winner; single-hop COALESCE then stays correct + the dump comments become true. (Alt (a): shared recursive winner-resolver across dump sites — more churn.) Add a multi-hop parity test. Pure DB/Python, in scope.
close_reason: PR #706 merged. Multi-hop merge-chain resurrection fix (db-reconstructibility, surfaced on PR #690). Option (b): enrichment.flatten_merge_chains — idempotent, cycle-safe, tombstone-only scan — re-points every etymon.merged_into_id to its TERMINAL winner, hooked into _run_curation_slot_passes (curation-only gate; the sole chain-former). Plus a read-only fail-loud guard (assert_merge_chains_flat + MergeChainError) in the dump-jsonl CLI, since that path can't enrich — catches any residual chain/cycle (a tombstone targeting a tombstone) before emitting a D22-violating dump. Dump comments rewritten to be honest (enrichment flattens on rebuild; dump asserts). 3 review rounds (14-agent round 1 → P1 dump-gap + Gemini-high perf + cycle + coverage + docs fixes → 2 verification rounds clean, mutation-tested). New pass added to REBUILD.md + L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md. Full suite 5634 passed. Follow-up noted (not filed, non-blocking): a shared resolve_merge_terminal util unifying _terminal_merge_winner + bridges/_common._resolve_canonical (divergent cycle semantics).

title: _dump_descent_edges + element dump lack merged_into_id follow-to-winner (same latent orphaning as wyrd-q6ro)
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-q6ro (PR for cited-etymon channel). q6ro made _dump_cited_etymons + _dump_citations follow merged_into_id to the surviving winner so a re-dump after an OCR-cluster merge emits the winner, not the tombstone, and the citation witness isn't orphaned on rebuild.

The same latent ref-orphaning shape remains in the other two per-source etymon-ref emitters in jsonl/dump.py:
- _dump_descent_edges (JOIN etymon pe ON pe.id=d.parent_id / ce ON ce.id=d.child_id) — emits loser refs if an endpoint is a merge loser.
- the element dump inside _dump_etymology_elements (JOIN etymon e ON e.id=el.etymon_id) — emits loser refs for merged element etymons.

Both refs feed the same referenced-id union in _dump_cited_etymons, so after q6ro the etymon dump emits only winners while these two still emit loser refs → orphaned on build_from_jsonl (etymon_descent_orphans / element-ref drop) = reconstructibility/evidence loss.

Fix: apply the same COALESCE(ref.merged_into_id, ref.id) winner resolution (pattern: _dump_fantasy_morpheme_rows LEFT JOIN etymon w ON w.id=COALESCE(e.merged_into_id,e.id)).

DESIGN SUBTLETY for descent: following BOTH endpoints to winner can collapse an edge to a self-loop (parent==child) when a descent edge connects two members of the same OCR cluster that later merge. Decide: skip self-edges on dump, or let build INSERT OR IGNORE a self-loop (current build _insert_descent has no self-edge guard). This subtlety is why it was split out of q6ro. Latent today (0 current merge-losers).
close_reason: Done in PR #690 (wyrd-q6ro) — code-reviewer reframed the descent/element deferral as a regression, so _dump_descent_edges + the element dump now follow merged_into_id to the winner (with a descent self-loop skip), with regression tests. Multi-hop chains remain tracked in wyrd-lpxq.

title: LLM cognate-descent verdict cache (_cognate_descent_audit.jsonl) stores endpoint row-ids — make durable
description:
From wyrd-c6wu pt1 review (PR #684). mine-cognate-descents-llm's verdict cache _cognate_descent_audit.jsonl stores cluster_root + morpheme_ref as etymon ROW-IDS (cognate_descent_llm.py:316-318, 363-364: edge_from_log does int(row['morpheme_ref'])/int(row['cluster_root'])). The cache is replayed (free) to avoid re-running the LLM. After a rebuild reassigns etymon ids, replaying a cache mined against a different corpus resolves STALE ids -> wrong/dropped edges. pt1 mitigated the OUTPUT (the authored _assert_descends_from.jsonl uses natural keys, and the CLI now skips edges whose stale ids don't resolve in the current DB) but the CACHE itself is still id-keyed, so a cross-corpus replay silently loses verdicts.

FIX: store the morpheme/root NATURAL KEYS (language:canonical_form) in the audit log instead of ids; edge_from_log resolves them to current-build ids (resolve_etymon_ref) instead of int(). Migrate existing logs (id->natural-key) or accept a one-time re-judge. Same D50.1 principle as wyrd-c6wu.

RELATES: wyrd-c6wu (the assertion-output fix), wyrd-zrce.2 (the LLM residue pass that consumes this cache), the no-ids-in-jsonl invariant.
close_reason: LLM cognate-descent verdict cache now stores natural keys (language:canonical_form) not row-ids; PR #697 merged. ClusterCand.root_ref resolved via etymon_refs_for in build_candidates; ResidueItem.ref=etymon_ref(language,form); audit_log_row writes keys; edge_from_log(row,*,conn,...) resolves keys->current ids via resolve_etymon_ref (None->skip+rejudge); resolve_etymon_ref made total over str|int. Operator-artifact log => legacy id-keyed rows gracefully fail to resolve (one-time re-judge). 3 review rounds (re-id durability test, type-honesty widening, root_ref source assertion, resource-leak fix, honest 2-row stale CLI test).

title: Dedup ~820 true-duplicate toponym_etymology rows (prereq for natural-key te refs)
description:
Prereq for keying toponym_etymology by a stable composite natural key (wyrd-c6wu's 5th emitter, spurious_breakdown_mining). Audit 2026-06-20: toponym_etymology has NO unique natural key — 820 rows still collide on (toponym_id, source_id, COALESCE(page,''), element-signature) where element-signature = ordered '<ordinal>:<etymon natural-key>' of toponym_etymology_element. These are true duplicates distinguishable only by row-id.

TASK: dedup/merge the 820 collision rows so (toponym, source, page, element-sig) becomes UNIQUE, then add a UNIQUE index (Alembic migration) so the composite key is enforced + safe to use as an L2 ref. Use natural keys throughout (no row-ids): toponym natural key = (modern_name, country, region) per idx_toponym_unique; element natural key = etymon (language:canonical_form) per wyrd-c6wu. Preserve evidence (D21) — merge, don't delete; keep distinct historical_form/confidence/notes if they differ (those may be REAL distinct breakdowns, in which case add a discriminator instead of merging).

Investigate first: are the 820 genuinely identical (safe merge) or do they differ in historical_form/attested_year/confidence (real alternatives needing a discriminator)? Query: GROUP BY (toponym_id,source_id,page,elem_sig) HAVING count>1, inspect the differing columns.

BLOCKS: the toponym_etymology portion of wyrd-c6wu (spurious_breakdown ref fix). The 4 ETYMON emitter sites in c6wu do NOT depend on this. RELATES: wyrd-ihmf (long-term UUID surrogate — the alternative to deduping).

title: Stable UUIDs on all referenceable elements (durable L2 JSONL identity)
description:
DO NOT ACT YET — backlog. Filed 2026-06-20 out of the wyrd-zrce investigation.

PROBLEM: L2 JSONL must not use ephemeral row-ids (etymon.id is reassigned on every rebuild-from-jsonl; etymon has no game_id). Today we work around this with natural-key refs (language:canonical_form), as the collapse/reflex assertions do. But natural keys are awkward and can be ambiguous (homographs; same surface across senses; surface drift by era/canonicalization), and not every referenceable entity has a clean natural key.

PROPOSAL: give every referenceable element a STABLE UUID (or ULID) column — etymon, and the other entities that get referenced in L2 assertions/streams (canonical nodes, toponym, reflex, morpheme, etc.). Properties:
  - Generated once at element creation/mining time; PRESERVED across rebuilds by round-tripping through L2 (the UUID is part of the L2 record, not derived from row position).
  - L2 JSONL refs use the UUID instead of row-id or natural key, so assertions stay valid across corpus changes + rebuilds.
  - Distinct from game_id (pfsrd2's content-addressable citation hash): this is a kenning-internal durable surrogate key, not content-derived (so it survives label/surface drift by era — cf D50 synthetic-node identity).

SCOPE (when actioned): Alembic migration adding uuid columns (+ unique index); generation at ingest/mining; L2 round-trip (dump/build must read+write the uuid, never regenerate); update assertion emitters + resolvers (relational_projection, canonicalization streams) to key on uuid; backfill uuids for existing rows on a one-time migration.

INTERIM (near-term, separate from this ticket): the wyrd-zrce miner fix uses natural-key (language:canonical_form) refs — the established collapse/reflex convention — to unblock cognate-descent durability without waiting on this. This ticket is the proper long-term identity fix that retires the natural-key workaround.

Relates: wyrd-zrce (the id-ref bug that surfaced this), the no-ids-in-jsonl invariant, D50 synthetic-canonical-node identity (separates identity from evidence/surface).

title: Index reflex_etymon.etymon_id + toponym_etymology_element.etymon_id to speed up tag_mining.select_targets
description:
PR #681 (round-2 Gemini, reclassified P3) surfaced that tag_mining.select_targets is a heavyweight query. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db shows the cost is structural, not about the breakdown subquery form:

- Outer: full SCAN of etymon (2,383,451 rows).
- CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 1 (reflex EXISTS): SCAN re — reflex_etymon has NO index on etymon_id.
- CORRELATED SCALAR SUBQUERY 2 (breakdown count): SCAN el — toponym_etymology_element (43,361 rows) has NO index on etymon_id; only the PK auto-index (toponym_etymology_id, ordinal) exists.

Both correlated subqueries full-scan per candidate etymon. Adding indexes:
  CREATE INDEX idx_reflex_etymon_etymon ON reflex_etymon(etymon_id);
  CREATE INDEX idx_tee_etymon ON toponym_etymology_element(etymon_id);
should turn the SCANs into SEARCHes and materially speed up mine-tags-llm target selection (the full select_targets query ran for minutes on the 4.8GB authoring DB).

Must go through a new Alembic migration under lexicon/sql/migrations/versions/ (per alembic-migration-discipline-reviewer) + sync lexicon/sql/tables.py. Out of scope for the wyrd-jrwc tag-backfill PR. Verify the index helps with EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN before/after.

Note: Gemini also suggested an EXISTS(... GROUP BY te.toponym_id LIMIT 1 OFFSET N-1) short-circuit for the count(DISTINCT) — a micro-opt dominated by the missing indexes; reconsider only if profiling shows subquery-2's temp-b-tree is hot after indexing.

title: Decompose dithematic OE/Norse personal-name morphemes into name-elements (composed-of, onomastics)
description:
Surfaced by the wyrd-zrce.3 Phase-0 probe (2026-06-18, scratch/zrce3_group_probe.py), which found the residue-residue stem-mate cohort (~1,234) is DOMINATED by dithematic Old English/Norse PERSONAL NAMES sharing a protheme: beor- (Beornwulf, Beorhthere, Beorcol), leof- (Leofric, Leofwig, Leofgar), plus wulf-/ceol-/thor-/sige-/aedel-/eald- (8 of the 12 largest prefix-groups). These are NOT cognates (zrce.3 closed on that basis) — they are COMPOSITES: Beornwulf = beorn ('warrior'/'bear') + wulf ('wolf').

Opportunity: mine composed-of edges (D50.3 Family B) decomposing these name morphemes into their two name-elements (protheme + deuterotheme), so a dithematic name is ATTRIBUTED to its constituents (which are often already shipped/clustered: beorn, wulf, leof, sige...) rather than left as an opaque unclustered singleton. This is ONOMASTIC morphology — a level BELOW wyrd-h5u1 (which mines toponym composite-surface -> constituent morphemes but stops at the personal name as a single constituent; cf its in-progress passthrough work). Coordinate with ingest-briggs-personal-names (the existing OE personal-name pipeline) for the element inventory + breakdown evidence.

Distinct from cognacy (the zrce axis) and from h5u1's toponym-level composed-of. Element-sharing toponym COMPOUNDS the same probe surfaced (burh-tun/burh-weard/burh-ware = burh+X) belong to h5u1, noted there. The ~12% truly-isolated residue (373) legitimately stay singletons.
notes:
DEFERRED (planning Phase 0, 2026-06-18). Mapping found name-element decomposition is fully GREENFIELD: no name-element inventory, no protheme/deuterotheme storage, no name-segmentation logic exists — personal names are stored only as whole-name etymons (tag male/female name, gloss 'a personal name'). Three blockers to building now:
1. NO EVIDENCE SIGNAL: the clean cross-scholar coarse-vs-fine signal that made wyrd-h5u1 sound does NOT exist for name-internal elements — toponym breakdowns treat Beornwulf as ONE element; no scholar splits it into beorn+wulf in the corpus. Pure surface-tiling (Beornwulf->beorn+wulf against the morpheme set) is the gloss-blind segmentation D51 explicitly forbids (barton tiles bar+ton but means bere+tūn).
2. NO CURRENT CONSUMER: the composed-of edges would sit unused — the decomposition grader never splits names internally (no recall gap to recover, unlike h5u1), and generation uses personal names as WHOLE slot-fillers. The real payoff is a FUTURE name-element RECOMBINATION generator (procedurally building new dithematic OE names from protheme+deuterotheme) — a feature that does not exist yet and is not this ticket.
3. BUILD COST: any rigorous path is large — ingest a scholarly OE/Norse name-element dictionary (+ mint/tag element etymons) OR an LLM propose+verify pass (reusing zrce.2). Greenfield inventory + tiler + validation for edges nothing consumes yet.

DECISION (operator, 2026-06-18): defer until a name-recombination feature wants this. Keep open as a FOUNDATION ticket; revisit when that consumer is scoped. Reusable when built: h5u1's passthrough_assertions (composed-of emission) + the cohort tags (etymon_tag male/female name). Map: see the 7hbp.1 planning Explore.

title: Uplift 1b.3: form NEW cognate clusters among residue morphemes (residue-residue)
description:
Deferred from wyrd-zrce.2 (which links residue -> EXISTING clusters only). The Phase-0 probe (2026-06-18) found ~40% (1,234) of the 3,071-morpheme residue have a residue-residue stem-mate — morphemes that are cognates of EACH OTHER but not of any already-clustered etymon (e.g. arrius/arria/arrianus -> one new Latin-gens cluster). These cannot be handled by zrce.2's link-to-existing-cluster approach: there is no existing anchor, so the LLM must additionally (a) decide the set forms a genuine cognate group, (b) pick/propose the MOST-ANCESTRAL member as the cluster root, and (c) author the descends-from edge directions among them. Riskier to adversarially gate (no existing cluster to verify against) and a bigger build than zrce.2.

Approach sketch: candidate groups = residue morphemes sharing a fold-prefix; LLM groups + names the ancestral root; adversarial verify each proposed edge; emit descends-from edges (Family B) among them so cluster_cognates forms the new cluster (rooted at the LLM-chosen ancestor). Reuses zrce.1's descends-from->etymon_descent projection + cluster_cognates rollup. Sequenced after zrce.2 (measure how much residue remains once existing-cluster links land). The ~12% truly-isolated residue (373) legitimately stay singletons (leave-separate).
close_reason: PREMISE INVALIDATED by Phase 0 (group probe, 2026-06-18, scratch/zrce3_group_probe.py). The residue-residue stem-mates (1,234) are NOT cognates of each other: 8 of the 12 largest prefix-groups (and most of the volume; max group=21, 29 groups >=5) are DITHEMATIC OLD ENGLISH/NORSE PERSONAL NAMES sharing a protheme (beor- Beornwulf/Beorhthere; leof- Leofric/Leofwig; wulf-/ceol-/thor-/sige-/aedel-/eald-) — distinct names, not one word-family. The non-name remainder is mostly element-sharing COMPOUNDS (burh-tun/burh-weard/burh-ware = composed-of, D50.3, not cognacy). Genuinely-cognate residue-residue sets (weales/weallas) are a small scattered size-2 tail. Cognate-clustering this cohort would be wrong; an adversarial gate would correctly refute nearly all of it → near-zero yield for heavy LLM spend. Personal names also already have ingest-briggs-personal-names. The real signal (composites needing composed-of decomposition) is filed as a follow-up. zrce epic complete at .1 (evidence core) + .2 (LLM residue→existing clusters).

title: b2mf debt: export silently falls back to legacy rollup when canonical graph unpopulated
description:
The wyrd-b2mf reader cutover made _build_canonical_rollup (lexicon/bundle/_export.py) fall back to the legacy merged_into_id/lemma_id rollup — with a UserWarning — when canonical_morpheme_id is unpopulated, instead of hard-requiring the projection to have run. Forced by CI: a guard-RAISE broke ~15 existing export tests that build multi-member fixtures and call export_meanings without projecting, and would make the export unusable on any unprojected dev/test DB.

It is CORRECT (legacy is full clustering, byte-identical to canonical today, so the fallback never under-clusters; it only misses not-yet-applied 1a binds, which an unprojected DB has none of) and production always projects (rebuild --with-enrichment terminal pass). But it is GROSS tech debt:

1. Export correctness depends on an out-of-band projection step, enforced only by a warning — a soft contract. A caller that exports an unprojected DB in production-like flow would silently ship legacy clustering.
2. Dual rollup paths (legacy _build_family_rollup + canonical _build_canonical_rollup) coexist; the fold/1a-miner/verifier keep legacy by necessity (circular), so the duplication is load-bearing, not removable yet.
3. The rep-collision .extend (Gemini-flagged) degrades a hub-split legacy family to the legacy grouping because the int-rep export contract can't represent sub-legacy splits.

Better long-term: have the export pipeline guarantee/trigger the projection (or assert freshness) so the fallback is unreachable in real builds, and/or collapse to a single authoritative rollup once the fold no longer needs legacy. Revisit at/after the full rebuild. Reverses the original b2mf decision-2 ('guard, not fallback'); operator agreed it's the right call but flagged as debt. See PR #663.

description:

1. connective.py (type-design-analyzer): ConnectiveInventory = tuple[tuple[str,str],...] is stringly-typed for a concept already modeled by the frozen Connective dataclass — a transposed (kind,surface) entry is a silent bug. Consider tuple[Connective,...]. And Connective.kind: str over the closed set {genitive,formative,linking} — a typo'd kind silently skips the genitive tiebreak; consider StrEnum/Literal. (Pre-existing connective core; ripples through trie_matcher._connective_candidates.)

2. decomposition_grader (complexity-reviewer / PLR0913): the 4-field config cluster (culture_languages, connective_inventory, genitive_prior, passthrough_map) is threaded through grade_toponym/grade_configuration/grade_corpus_diff. Consider a MatcherConfig dataclass. (Kw-only today, not a rule violation.)

3. genitive_priors._fold (import-reviewer): now a de-facto shared surface-fold util imported by decomposition_grader + passthrough_mining (3 consumers) as a private name with no __all__. Promote to a public name (e.g. fold_surface) or a small shared normalization module.

4. passthrough_mining._aggregate_pairs (complexity-reviewer): indent depth 4 at the accumulation block; consider hoisting lines into a small _record helper.

5. decomposition_grader.diff_grades (pr-test-analyzer): the trade-off case (a toponym that improves one dimension AND regresses another — 'lands on both lists') is untested; add coverage.

Source: PR #649 review threads (comment ids 3424805376, 3424805501, 3424810143, 3424811934, 3424812223, 3424809603, 3424808399). Each thread replied 'Out of scope - tracked here'.
