title: Mine implied reflexes/conjugations from modern-name <-> breakdown-element surface alignment
description:
OBSERVED (user, 2026-06-16) while building the passthrough miner (wyrd-h5u1). The cross-scholar coarse/fine pairs — and more generally aligning a toponym's MODERN name to its OE breakdown elements — reveal IMPLIED REFLEXES/conjugations for the surface spans not covered by known reflexes:
  Houghton  -> hoh + tun   => hough == reflex of hōh
  Winterborne -> winter + burna => borne == reflex of burna
  Ouinton/Xinton -> ing + tun  => inton/ington surface maps to ing+ton
The alignment trick (anchor with KNOWN reflexes, attribute the residual span to the remaining element) yields NEW modern reflex surfaces AND can begin populating the empty toponym_etymology_element.surface_in_modern (NULL for ~98% of rows — the gap aicu.9/z3me hit).

VALUE: directly feeds wyrd-f233 (uplift 3: derive modern reflex surface+position for reflex-less admitted morphemes) — these implied reflexes ARE that data, mined from scholarly evidence (gloss-correct, not surface-guessed). Also a partial answer to the surface_in_modern gap.

MODEL (post-D50): a modern reflex form of a morpheme is a per-stratum label/form — D50 canonical-label@stratum on the morpheme's canonical node, OR a reflex/reflex_etymon row. Evidence-backed (cross-scholar / breakdown alignment), confidence = support, append-only. Reuse the wyrd-h5u1 stream-1 alignment machinery. Related: wyrd-h5u1 (same alignment source), wyrd-f233 (consumer), wyrd-z3me (surface_in_modern/ordinal data gaps), wyrd-aicu.3 (reflex de-dash).
notes: SCOPE NOTE (from wyrd-c7iz 1a, 2026-06-16): the cognate-but-different-surface breakdown morphemes (a shipped morpheme's reflex/era variant attested under a different surface) overlap this ticket — a different modern surface for the same cluster IS the implied-reflex signal. 1a deliberately did NOT bind them (different surface != same-morpheme identity); they belong here (per-stratum canonical-label / reflex) and/or 1b (cognate clustering). Cross-confirm with 1a's same_morpheme_mining (which found ~77 same-surface identity dups) to avoid double-handling.

title: Place & jurisdiction identity across time: succession + ambiguous node assignment (dedup-serving)
description:
The Class-B half of the region/place DEDUP story (D49). Two identity operations the flat region field can't express, both serving deduplication / place identity:
- SUCCESSION across strata: same jurisdiction under changing names/boundaries (Cumberland+Westmorland -> Cumbria; hundred reorganizations). Same reflex-vs-identity discipline as D44/D46 — identity persists, label is per-stratum.
- AMBIGUOUS node assignment: bare 'Yorkshire' -> which Riding for THIS place? needs evidence; sharpens the dedup blocking key.

title: explain/matcher over-generates spurious readings for etymologically-opaque (pre-English) names — e.g. London → 'blackbird + hill'
description:
`wyrd kenning explain "London"` confidently returns folk decompositions like `Lon` ("moose / blackbird", CL) + `don` ("hill", EN/FR/CL) — i.e. it back-fits the productive OE hill-element `-don` (as in Wimbledon/Hambledon) onto a name that is NOT an OE compound.

London is a pre-English substrate name (pre-Celtic / early Brittonic), opaque by the time English speakers arrived: Roman *Londinium* < reconstructed Celtic `*Londinjon` (Coates 1998: from pre-Celtic *Plowonida, a Thames hydronym; or Schrijver 2013: `*lond-` 'flood' + `*-injo-`). Its `-don` has nothing to do with OE 'hill'. The matcher has no way to know that, so it offers a plausible-looking-but-wrong reading with the same visual weight as a genuine compound.

WHY IT MATTERS: misleads the user/SPA inspector into thinking the system 'knows' London = blackbird + hill. There is no confidence/plausibility/ranking signal separating a real OE compound reading from a coincidental letter-match, and no flag for opaque/loanword/substrate names.

IMPORTANT — do NOT 'fix' this by gating matches on position or etymology. String-only matching is intentional (D40/D45; position is a DERIVED output, never a gate — enforced by morpheme-surface-identity-reviewer). The fix space is RANKING / CONFIDENCE / PRESENTATION:
  - score readings by plausibility (element frequency in the real corpus, attested co-occurrence, family coherence) and rank/threshold rather than dumping all string-matches equally;
  - and/or mark a name as low-confidence / likely-opaque when no reading clears a plausibility bar, instead of presenting the top coincidental match as if authoritative.

Observed via the live lexicon during a user etymology query (London / Londinium). Affects `wyrd kenning explain` and any SPA breakdown that surfaces the same matcher readings. Real-name ANALYSIS path, not generation.

title: Committed L2 (data/mining/*.jsonl per-source files) is ~1 month stale vs the live L3
description: DISCOVERED during aicu.3 PR B (de-dash _reflexes.jsonl). title: De-dash morpheme_id / etymon.canonical_form — affix-markers vs LEGITIMATE hyphens (needs analysis, NOT a blanket fold)
description:
Split out of wyrd-aicu.3. The dashed morpheme_id content key (language:canonical_form, e.g. celtic:-ach — ~742 in L4) comes from etymon.canonical_form, which has ~105.9k dashed rows in L3. CRUCIAL: those dashes are MOSTLY LEGITIMATE etymological hyphens, NOT position decoration: 'Eid al-Adha, 's-Hertogenbosch, '14-'18, 'Phags-pa. A blanket replace('-','') would CORRUPT them (al-Adha→alAdha). Only the AFFIX-MARKER dashes (-ach, -ar-, leading/trailing on bound suffixes/infixes) are identity-decoration in the D45 sense.

So this is NOT a mechanical migration like reflex.surface_form (aicu.3). It needs analysis: (1) classify which canonical_form dashes are affix-markers (bound-morpheme position decoration) vs legitimate hyphens-in-the-form; (2) decide whether morpheme_id should be de-dashed AT ALL (it's a CONTENT KEY = the scholarly etymon form; a legit hyphen belongs in it) — arguably D45 covers MORPHEME SURFACE identity, and morpheme_id is the etymon content key, a different scheme; (3) if affix-markers are folded, handle content-key COLLISIONS (celtic:-ach vs celtic:ach). The L4 morpheme table is DORMANT (no runtime reader), so this is low urgency. Decide scope before touching. Discovered during aicu.3 exploration 2026-06-13.
close_reason: De-dash of etymon.canonical_form / morpheme_id landed in 2 PRs: #730 (write/ingest de-dash: normalize_morpheme_surface at the upsert choke + all write paths; * sigil + interior hyphens kept; junk dropped) and #735 (read-path sweep + rebuild-not-migrate cutover). Realized via clean rebuild-from-jsonl: etymon.canonical_form boundary dashes 105906->0, 7296 collisions folded via the UNIQUE conflict (no migration), ~734 junk dropped; bare seed re-exported, morpheme_id CI gate flipped to form-level (boundary dash only — language prefix + interior hyphens exempt). The * -> reconstructed boolean is deferred to wyrd-qoy8.

title: Production deploy will 500 on v3 schema unless a v3 runtime DB is published to prod S3 FIRST
description:
ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-06-13 staging outage: PRs #629/#630 bumped the L4 runtime DB schema v2→v3. Push-to-main auto-deploys STAGING only (deploy.yml), shipping v3 Lambda code while staging S3 still served a v2 DB → _verify_schema_version raised RuntimeDBVersionMismatch → 500 on every request (/api/manifest etc). Fixed staging by rebuilding a full v3 DB (export-runtime-db --db ~/.wyrd/lexicon.db) and publishing via bin/publish-runtime-db.sh --env staging (current.json now → v/2026-06-13T14-51Z.db).

PRODUCTION IS NOT YET BROKEN (deploy-production is manual workflow_dispatch only, so prod still runs v2 code + v2 DB). But the NEXT production deploy of current main will 500 identically unless, BEFORE/with that deploy, a v3 DB is published to prod S3:
  bin/publish-runtime-db.sh --env production --source <fresh v3 export>
(profile 521-Production-Admin). Rebuild with the same plain full export REBUILD.md Phase 3 documents.

PROCESS GAP: deploy.yml ships CODE but never publishes the runtime DB, so any schema bump needs a hand-coordinated publish. Consider: (a) document the ordering in REBUILD.md / a DEPLOY runbook, and/or (b) have the deploy job publish a freshly-built DB when the schema version changed, so code+data can't drift apart. The strict version gate is correct (fail-closed) — the gap is the missing data-publish step in the pipeline.
notes:
DECISION (2026-06-13, user): DURABLE automated-publish fix is OUT OF SCOPE / low prio. The durable fix (deploy.yml builds + publishes the runtime DB so code+data can't drift) requires CI to reach the L3 lexicon — but L3 is a local 4.6GB SQLite (~/.wyrd/lexicon.db), and we're not paying for Postgres/RDS to host it. So there's no cheap way to automate the build-in-CI.

ACCEPTED APPROACH = the documented MANUAL cutover (cheap, already prepped): a v3 DB is pre-staged in prod S3 (v/2026-06-13T15-31Z.db); the next prod v3 deploy just flips current.json to it (procedure above). Low prio because: only push-to-main auto-deploys STAGING (prod is manual-dispatch only), prod is pre-launch (no users), and the schema-mismatch RuntimeError is self-diagnosing if anyone forgets ('Re-run export-runtime-db ... and re-publish'). 'Only staging broke, not a huge miss.'

STILL TRUE: the next production v3 deploy MUST be paired with the pointer flip or prod 500s — but that's a documented one-liner, not the massive change. If the local L3 changes before that deploy, rebuild + re-stage first (the pre-staged DB is from the Jun-8 L3).

Cheap drift-resistance option if ever wanted (no infra cost): make runtime_db.py fall back to the BUNDLED v3 seed on an S3 schema-version mismatch instead of 500ing — degrades to the small committed seed rather than a hard outage. Tradeoff: serves the tiny dev subset silently. Not doing now; noting for the backlog.

title: Investigate tag-coverage backfill for the 31% untagged morphemes (cohesion lift)
description:
Successor to wyrd-3iln (closed: both its levers — max-coherence weighting and tag-vocab enrichment — empirically unjustified on the current corpus). The one actionable signal that surfaced: ~31% of the 2227 shared-bundle morphemes carry NO tags, so they contribute zero cohesion signal (cohesion_raw=0) and get suppressed at high cohesion. This is a tag-COVERAGE gap (backfill missing tags on existing morphemes), distinct from and cheaper than wyrd-3iln lever #2's tag-VOCABULARY enrichment (inventing more discriminating tag types).

Hypothesis: backfilling tags on the untagged 31% raises realized attested-pair coherence more than either wyrd-3iln lever, because it adds cohesion signal where there is currently none (vs reshaping signal that already discriminates — current co-occurrence CV is already ~1.6-2.0).

Approach: (1) characterize the untagged morphemes (which languages/positions/usages dominate the 31%); (2) source tags (Wiktionary sense categories already feed etymon_tag — see wyrd-vsvi; the gap is bundle-side coverage, not the pipeline); (3) re-emit + measure with the fixed-yardstick cohesion-ramp harness from wyrd-3iln (scratch/cohesion_ramp_probe.py + tag_spread_diag.py).

Note: tag vocabulary is SHARED across all 5 cultures (culture-agnostic meaning_db), so coverage backfill is a global realism change, not per-culture.
design:
RECREATABLE BACKFILL ARCHITECTURE (data mutation must round-trip per L2/L3
boundary + REBUILD.md; LLM involvement -> new L2 JSONL).

Tags are added by deriving from the GLOSS (etymon_gloss, L2) -- a NEW gloss->tag
path complementing the existing wiktextract category->tag path (_map_categories
_to_tags, wyrd-vsvi), which produced nothing for these tag-poor Celtic/OF/OE
entries. etymon_tag is L2 (dumped as the row's `tags` array), so ANY added tag
must land in L2 to survive a wipe.

Two passes, deterministic-first to MINIMIZE the paid LLM surface:

1. DETERMINISTIC gloss->tag rule table (free, re-runnable). A keyword->tag map
   (hill|ridge|valley|mound|hollow|mountain->topography; spear|arrow|dart->
   military; hair|horn|skin|follicular->anatomy; lock|fold|enclosure->
   architecture; ...). Handles the unambiguous bulk. Multi-label by design.
   Emits curation rows into L2 JSONL (regenerable by re-running the rule pass).

2. LLM ADJUDICATION for the ambiguous residue only (multi-sense glosses;
   keywords like 'lock' canal-vs-hair; 'part/share' scaffolding-vs-real).
   PAID -> verdicts MUST persist to L2 JSONL so rebuild replays, never re-pays
   (D21 / REBUILD.md). Exact pattern of _collapses.jsonl /
   _element_gloss_adjudications.jsonl / _pronunciation.jsonl.

Both write tag-addition events to a NEW L2 file data/mining/_tag_backfill.jsonl
applied by a new `apply-tag-additions` enrichment pass (INSERT OR IGNORE on
etymon_tag), mirroring the existing `apply-gloss-additions` (gloss-add-v1)
curation slot in run_full_enrichment. Free + idempotent on rebuild.

FOUR-FILE CONTRACT (REBUILD.md enforcement): apply-tag-additions pass +
_rebuild_layers.json entry + REBUILD.md restore step + L2_L3_BOUNDARY.md map.
Gated by rebuild-runbook-currency-reviewer. Then re-emit bundle + re-measure
with the cohesion-ramp harness (scratch/cohesion_ramp_probe.py) to confirm the
lift hypothesis (adds signal where there's currently NONE).
notes:
STEPS 1-4 COMPLETE + REVIEWED — PR #623 (kenning/xz3g-tag-backfill). Awaiting merge.
pr-review-loop ran to convergence: 4 substantive rounds, all findings posted+replied,
CI green, Gemini clean on HEAD, all agent reviewers clean on re-review.

Review fixes landed:
- P1: _tags.jsonl crashed rebuild-from-jsonl (unregistered _type) → registered 'tags'
  in LIST_TYPES + synthetic source row. Found pre-existing twin bug → filed wyrd-zhhf.
- P2: select_targets Cartesian product duplicated glosses (EXISTS not JOIN).
- HIGH: API failures wrote sticky error rows that skip-resolved away → now not recorded
  (retryable) + consecutive-failure abort.
- mediums: as_uri() db open; existing_refs tag-only resume keys; apply_tag_additions
  O(N) per-etymon query (not N+1); deterministic gloss order (sorted subquery).
- docs: 44-existing+kinship count; L2_L3_BOUNDARY pass table 13→16 in run-order.
Won't-fix (P3, reasoned): applier placement (mirrors apply_gloss_additions); 2 type-design
dict-shape nits (peer-consistent).

NEXT (operator-run, step 5): merge PR #623, then run mine-tags-llm over ~3104 targets on
the macbook (WYRD_OLLAMA_URL=http://10.5.2.31:11434), commit _tags.jsonl, enrich, re-emit
bundle, re-measure cohesion lift (scratch/cohesion_ramp_probe.py). Needs operator go-ahead.

title: Export memory: stream families to the writer instead of materializing the full list (~1GB RSS, OOM under concurrent load)
description: Split out of wyrd-4zyb. The export holds the corpus + word_db + the full families list in memory → ~1GB RSS; OOM-killed twice under concurrent load (0-byte output, no file) during wyrd-v3ow.1. _iterate_families_with_progress materializes ALL ~67K families into a list before the writer consumes them. OPTION: stream/yield families to the subject assembler + writer instead of building the whole list, capping peak memory. Composes with the PR #613 bulk attested-years prefetch (small map, doesn't add to the list). Lower priority than the proportions follow-up.
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (autonomous loop 2026-06-20 — skipped, not workable as encoded):

The encoded OPTION ('stream/yield families to the subject assembler + writer ... capping peak memory') does NOT cap peak memory as written. Traced the code:
- _collect_families -> _iterate_families_with_progress builds the ~67K family list, then the SOLE consumer is _group_families_into_subjects (_subject.py:59).
- That assembler is NOT a streaming writer — it GROUPS families by (modifier_type, glosses, tags) signature, which is an inherent FULL-CORPUS BARRIER: it must buffer every family (a matching signature can appear anywhere in the stream) into 'groups' before it can emit any subject.
- 'groups' holds every family dict BY REFERENCE (groups[key].append(fam)), so converting _iterate_families_with_progress to a generator only eliminates the intermediate LIST CONTAINER (~67K pointers, <1MB) — NOT the ~67K fat family dicts (forms/glosses/tags/reflexes + ~10 per-member maps incl. member_phonological_vector_by_id; nearly all consumed by _subject.py via fam.get()). Peak is unchanged.

To ACTUALLY cap peak, pick one (each a real tradeoff — your call):
  (A) Two-pass 'group-keys-first': pass 1 computes ONLY the cheap group key per root (modifier_type + glosses + tags) and buckets root_ids (small memory); pass 2 gathers full family data per group, builds the subject, releases the group's dicts. Peak drops to (largest group's fat dicts + accumulated compact subjects). COST: re-fetches glosses/tags in both passes (~2x those queries) and forces restructuring the wyrd-4zyb bulk-attested-years prefetch (currently ONE global prefetch that was 13min->tens-of-sec; per-group would regress wall time). RISK: must stay byte-identical to satisfy the u6fn.4 fidelity gate — reordering the gather could perturb determinism. Moderate-large rewrite on a fidelity-gated path.
  (B) Slim the family dict — REJECTED: grep shows nearly every field (incl. all member_*_by_id maps) is consumed by the assembler; negligible win.
  (C) Mitigate OOM out-of-band instead of in this code: bound export concurrency, or run export in a subprocess with an RSS cap. Cheapest; doesn't touch the fidelity-gated path.

QUESTION FOR DEVON: accept the (A) wall-time/complexity/fidelity risk for the memory win, or prefer (C) operational mitigation? Until decided this stays P3/open. (Confirmed single-consumer; analysis at _export.py:160-170, _subject.py:59-90.)
close_reason: Decision made (Devon, 2026-06-20): option (C) operational mitigation, NOT the (A) two-pass rewrite. The ticket's 'stream families' approach was shown not to cap peak — _group_families_into_subjects groups by signature, a full-corpus barrier that holds all ~67K fat family dicts live at once (streaming only frees the cheap list container). The (A) peak-capping rewrite trades the wyrd-4zyb bulk-attested-years wall-time win and risks the u6fn.4 fidelity gate, so it's deferred unless a hard memory ceiling forces it (would be its own focused ticket). PR #698 merged: documented the operational guard in INGESTION.md Stage 8 (export-meanings peaks ~1GB RSS; provision ~1.5GB+; don't run concurrently with other heavy passes; or subprocess + RSS cap). 2 review rounds (full roster self-filtered to N/A on the docs-only diff; runbook-currency + docstring-grep verified all claims; one P3 figure-reconciliation fixed).

title: Strengthen cohesion realism lever: tag-vocab enrichment / max-coherence weighting
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-e2b4 (PR #576). The slot-relative D17 cohesion multiplier now measurably raises attested-pair coherence, but the lift is modest (~3-7% in most cultures; welsh flat) because it's corpus-bound: tag-level co-occurrence has limited spread, and a morpheme's coherence is AVERAGED across all its tags (plant/food/tree), diluting any single strong signal.

Two levers to get more punch from the knob:
1. Weight by the STRONGEST coherent tag-pair (max) rather than the mean across a morpheme's tags, in vector_name_select._cohesion_raw — so a morpheme with one strongly-attested tag isn't washed out by its weak ones. Cheap; needs re-validation of the coherence ramp + diversity across all 5 cultures + bit-stability.
2. Enrich the tag vocabulary so co-occurrence has more spread (more discriminating tags). Bigger data-side effort.

Validate against tests/test_kenning_realism_absolute.py + the coherence-ramp probe used in PR #576. Keep diversity-safe (no pool collapse) and bit-stable at cohesion=0.
notes:
BOTH LEVERS TESTED — NEITHER JUSTIFIED. Closing (2026-06-12). Successor: wyrd-xz3g.

Premise of this ticket ("cohesion lift is modest ~3-7%, corpus-bound") is
OVERTAKEN BY CORPUS GROWTH. Fresh fixed-yardstick measurement (mean generator
= production, mean ruler) shows realized attested-pair coherence lift of
+6-55% at the deployed cohesion=0.6 and +12-92% at 1.0 — well above the stale
3-7%. Per-culture @1.0: english +11.9, scottish +15.5, welsh +24.8, irish
+21.1, breton +92.1.

LEVER #1 (max instead of mean in _cohesion_raw): TESTED, NEGATIVE.
Implemented + ran a fixed-yardstick A/B (scratch/cohesion_ramp_probe.py;
harness validated — reproduces PR #576 diversity to the exact name, english
291/300 @1.0; bit-stable @cohesion=0 by construction). Each generator just
optimizes its OWN ruler (max-gen wins max-ruler, mean-gen wins mean-ruler;
deltas 1-3 lift pts). The faithful realism metric is the MEAN ruler
(attested-pair fidelity = a name's pairs are GENERALLY attested, not that its
single best pair is); on it max-gen is consistently SLIGHTLY WORSE across all
5 cultures. Optimizes the proxy at a small cost to the goal. Reverted.

LEVER #2 (tag-vocab enrichment): NOT JUSTIFIED. Its premise — co-occurrence
has 'limited spread' because tags are coarse — is FALSE on the current corpus
(scratch/tag_spread_diag.py): co-occurrence CV is 1.6-2.0 (heavy-tailed; the
table already has strongly-discriminating pairs), tag entropy 0.82 (rich),
top-5 share 44% (moderate). Also structurally misframed: the tag VOCABULARY
is SHARED across all 5 cultures (culture-agnostic meaning_db: identical 2227
morphemes / 45 tags everywhere) — so lever #2 is a GLOBAL realism change, not
a per-culture knob-strengthener. And welsh, lever #2's original 'flat'
motivating case, is now the 2nd-strongest culture (+24.8%).

THE ONE ACTIONABLE SIGNAL (different lever, filed as wyrd-xz3g): 31% of
morphemes carry NO tags → zero cohesion contribution, suppressed at high
cohesion. That is a tag-COVERAGE gap (backfill missing tags), distinct from
and cheaper than lever #2's tag-VOCABULARY enrichment. Higher leverage if any
intervention is wanted: it adds signal where there's none, vs reshaping
signal that already discriminates.

Artifacts (gitignored scratch/): cohesion_ramp_probe.py, tag_spread_diag.py,
ab_mean.txt, ab_max.txt. Code tree clean (lever #1 reverted).
close_reason: Both levers empirically unjustified on current corpus (lever #1 negative A/B; lever #2 premise false — co-occurrence already discriminates, CV 1.6-2.0). Premise overtaken by corpus growth (lift now 6-55% at deployed default, not 3-7%). Actionable residue filed as wyrd-xz3g (tag-coverage backfill).

title: Recover warm cost: scope vector pool per-request (across the count loop), not per-name
description:
wyrd-i7uy removed cross-request caching of the vector eligibility pool but scoped it per-NAME (per generate() call). For count=5 that rebuilds the pool 5x. On the 1-vCPU Lambda that is ~200ms/request of avoidable work (warm count=5 is ~500ms; per-name sample includes the rebuild).

Scope the pool per-REQUEST: build once per HTTP request, reuse across the count's N names, discard at request end. Stays within the 'never cache above a request' rule (per-request is the allowed ceiling). Thread a per-request cache object from app._dispatch's count loop through generate() -> select_via_vector -> _build_vector_pools (the plumbing deferred in wyrd-i7uy). Keep _build_vector_pools fresh-per-call when no request-cache is passed (CLI/tests).

Refs: wyrd-i7uy, no-caching-above-a-request memory.
close_reason: Duplicate of wyrd-dag4 (both: scope the vector eligibility pool per-request across the count loop, not per-name). Consolidating on wyrd-dag4; implementing there.

title: Recover warm per-request cost: scope the vector pool per-request (across the count loop), not per-name
description:

On the 1-vCPU Lambda that's ~200ms/request of avoidable work (warm count=5 is ~500ms; sample_ms ~100-140/name includes the rebuild).

Scope the pool per-REQUEST instead: build once per HTTP request and reuse across the count's N names, discarding at request end. This stays within the 'never cache above a request' rule (per-request is the allowed ceiling). Requires threading a per-request cache object from app._dispatch's count loop through generate() -> select_via_vector -> _build_vector_pools (the plumbing deferred in wyrd-i7uy). Keep _build_vector_pools fresh-per-call when no request-cache is passed (CLI/tests).
Refs: wyrd-i7uy, no-caching-above-a-request memory.

title: Empty eligible-pool from a valid-but-unsatisfiable request raises generic ValueError (→ opaque 500); map to a 4xx/422
description:
Surfaced during wyrd-i7uy review. When a request's gate filters the eligible pool empty (e.g. an API caller passes a --tag with zero eligible morphemes, or an over-restrictive era/stratum/tag combo), the vector path raises a bare ValueError('vector scoring produced no eligible name …') at wyrd/generators/kenning/generators/kenning.py:~493. The web layer can't distinguish this 'valid request, no data' case from a genuine internal error, so both become an opaque 500.

The SPA constrains tags to a valid enum, so UI users can't trigger it today — but the API is permissive (per the feature-flag note), so a direct API caller CAN, and gets a 500 instead of a clean client error.

Proposed: introduce a dedicated exception (e.g. class EmptyEligiblePool(KenningError)) raised for the valid-but-unsatisfiable case, and have app.py map it to a 422/4xx with an operator-readable message, reserving 500 for genuinely unexpected errors. Keep the loud-fail behavior; just make it classifiable.

Note: wyrd-i7uy added test_empty_tag_pool_raises_instead_of_reusing_a_warmed_pool (tests/test_kenning_request_isolation.py) which locks the current ValueError behavior — update it when the exception type changes.

Refs: wyrd-i7uy (the cache fix that unmasked this), error-handling + test-coverage review of PR #575.
close_reason: Empty eligible-pool now raises EmptyEligiblePool(KenningError) -> app maps to 422 (not opaque 500); CLI friendly error; unified the regenerate sibling (NoEligibleReplacementError now 422 too) + fixed drift_runner catch. PR #693 merged. 2 review rounds.

title: Mood-catalog review: mystical is theme-inert in english (no magic morphemes); ancient uses too-generic tags
description:
Validating all 12 catalog moods after wyrd-4rp8 (the one-mood-morpheme overlay) found every mood now changes output, but two are weak — and both are CATALOG/COVERAGE issues, not overlay bugs.

## mystical — theme-inert in english (0.00 -> 0.00 grim-style theme share)
mystical's mood tags are magic:0.6, fantasy:0.4, monster:0.2. The english eligible pool has 0 'magic', 3 'fantasy', 3 'monster' morphemes (vs death 57, undead 23, military 45, religious 165, plant 206). So _choose_mood_slot finds no mood-capable slot and the overlay correctly no-ops; mystical's PHONOLOGICAL component still shifts output (94% of names change). Net: a user asking for 'mystical' english names gets a phonetic shift but no magical theme — because English place-names have no magic morphemes.
Options:
- Document mystical as PACK-DEPENDENT (it themes once a fantasy pack/culture supplies magic/fantasy morphemes — exactly the packs use case); and/or
- add a handful of magic/fantasy-tagged morphemes to the english (or a shared) corpus; and/or
- re-scope mystical's tags toward something english HAS (e.g. lean on its phonological component).

## ancient — themes via the 3 most common tags, so no distinctive feel (0.81 -> 1.00)
ancient's tags are topography:0.3, geology:0.2, descriptive:0.2 — the three MOST common tags in the corpus (466/240/234 eligible morphemes). ~every name already carries them, so 'ancient' as a SEMANTIC theme adds almost nothing distinctive; it leans on its phonological component for the actual effect. Consider re-scoping ancient to more distinctive tags (or treating it as phonological-led), so it reads as a real theme.

## Acceptance
A decision per mood: keep / re-tag / mark pack-dependent / phonological-led. Update register_effects.yaml + REGISTERS.md accordingly. (No overlay code change — the wyrd-4rp8 mechanism is correct; this is catalog content.)

## Data (english eligible-pool tag counts)
death 57, undead 23, military 45, monster 3, magic 0, fantasy 3, saint 2, religious 165, plant 206, animal 96, water 157, topography 466, geology 240, descriptive 234

## Refs
wyrd-4rp8 (the overlay this validates), D6/D37 (mood catalog), data/register_effects.yaml, REGISTERS.md, wyrd-6xuk (multi-mood/intensity semantics)

title: Define multi-mood composition + graduated intensity (mood:0.x) semantics under the one-mood-morpheme model
description:
## Why
wyrd-4rp8 reworks moods from a (broken) hard tag-gate into a 'one mood-appropriate morpheme per name' overlay (the user's algo: build per-slot pools → pick one slot that can carry a mood tag → enforce mood there → others normal). That model is clean for a SINGLE mood at full strength, but it leaves two semantics under-defined that the old register-composition model answered differently — we need to decide them deliberately.

## Q1 — Multiple moods (e.g. --mood grim --mood pastoral, or grim+harsh)
Under the old model moods COMPOSED into one register vector (sum-then-clamp, D37.1). Under the one-morpheme model, what does requesting 2+ thematic moods mean?
Options to weigh:
- UNION the tag sets and enforce ONE morpheme from the combined set (a name gets one grim-OR-pastoral morpheme).
- One morpheme PER mood (a 3-morpheme name with grim+pastoral gets one grim + one pastoral morpheme — needs ≥2 mood-capable slots).
- Weighted blend (pick which mood to enforce per name by relative weight).
- Note: harsh is PHONOLOGICAL (not tag-themed) and composes orthogonally on the phon axis — it's unaffected; this is specifically about 2+ SEMANTIC moods.

## Q2 — What does mood:0.x (0<x<1) mean now?
Old model: the colon-suffix SCALED the register effect's weights (grim:0.5 → death 0.35, etc.) — a direction-strength on a soft axis. Under the one-morpheme model that scaling is meaningless (we enforce a morpheme or we don't). Candidate redefinition:
- **Probability**: x = fraction of names that get a mood morpheme (grim:0.5 → 50% themed, 50% plain). Clean + interpretable; this is the natural intensity knob for the new model.
- Or x scales WITHIN-mood tag emphasis (keep the per-tag weights as a soft tiebreaker among mood morphemes), separate from a probability.
- Decide how x interacts with multiple moods (per-mood probability? shared?).

## Acceptance
- A short decision (DECISIONS.md D-entry or ticket note) fixing: multi-mood semantics (Q1), the meaning of mood:0.x (Q2), and how the two interact. Then wire it (wyrd-4rp8 ships single-mood @ full strength = always one morpheme; this ticket adds graduated + multi-mood on top).

## Refs
- wyrd-4rp8 (the one-mood-morpheme rework this builds on), D6/D37 (mood catalog + the old sum-then-clamp composition), registers/effects.parse_mood_spec (colon-suffix scaling), D36.6 (--tag hard vs mood soft)
notes:
Empirical evidence for Q1 (multi-mood), measured on the shipped wyrd-4rp8 overlay (english, N=300):
- grim alone: grim-share 0.99
- pastoral alone: pastoral-share 0.94
- grim+pastoral: grim-share 0.22 (≈ the 0.15 incidental baseline — grim is CROWDED OUT), pastoral-share 0.90.

So today multi-mood = UNION of mood tags → ONE enforced themed morpheme, and that single slot SKEWS to whichever mood has more corpus coverage (pastoral's plant/animal/water = 200+/96/157 morphemes swamp grim's death 57 / undead 23). Net: stacking 2 semantic moods does NOT give one-of-each; it gives one-from-the-union dominated by the better-represented mood. This is the concrete failure the Q1 decision must fix — likely 'one morpheme PER mood' (needs ≥1 mood-capable slot per mood) rather than union, OR a per-mood probability so the rarer mood isn't crowded out. Phonological-mood components are unaffected (they sum on the phon axis; grim+harsh stacks correctly).

title: Reword the novelty option description: terse, accurate, user-facing
description:
## Want
Rewrite the novelty `description` to tersely + accurately tell a user what the knob does. (User direction 2026-06-09: '0 is purely statistically derived, 1 is purely random' — but accurate.)

## Current copy (generators/kenning.py:139, verbose + implementation-leaning)
'Lexical-surprise dial (wyrd-fcub). Blends the per-slot score distribution toward uniform: 0 samples by score (common morphemes like ...) ; 1 samples every eligible morpheme equally ... Applied after tag/mood/harshness scoring.'

## Accuracy note (so the rewrite is correct, not just terse)
At 1 it is NOT 'purely random' over all morphemes — it's UNIFORM over the per-slot ELIGIBLE pool (every hard filter still applies: culture, era, stratum, exclude_tags, base-pool class exclusions, name/saint qualifier, and the per-position empirical-frequency filter that drops freq-0 morphemes). What 1 erases is the FREQUENCY/score PREFERENCE among eligible morphemes, not eligibility. Copy should imply 'ignores how common a morpheme was', not 'anything goes'.

## Draft candidates (pick/refine one)
- 'Surprise vs. typicality (0–1). 0: morphemes chosen by how often they're historically attested (most typical). 1: every eligible morpheme equally likely, ignoring frequency (most surprising).'
- 'How adventurous the name is (0–1). 0 follows attested frequency; 1 gives every eligible morpheme an equal shot, surfacing rare ones as often as common ones.'

Keep it one or two sentences, user-facing (no wyrd-fcub / 'per-slot score distribution' jargon). The schema description propagates to CLI help, SPA field help, and Lambda input docs, so one edit covers all surfaces.

## Acceptance
- New terse, accurate description on the novelty schema; no internal jargon; reads correctly for a GM.

## Refs
- generators/kenning.py input_schema (novelty), wyrd-fcub, wyrd-fca0
close_reason: Shipped in PR #548 (squash). Slider + terse description + novelty default 0.1 (prod+staging). The general holistic review caught that the env default was a no-op on generation (SPA omits at-default fields); fixed with server-side WYRD_DEFAULT application in _dispatch (feature_flags.apply_env_defaults) — now fixes every value-changing env default, not just novelty. CI green; full suite 4892 passed.

title: SPA: render bounded-proportion knobs (novelty etc.) as a slider, not a number input
description:
## Want
novelty is conceptually a proportion in [0,1]; it should be a SLIDER in the SPA, not a free-number field. (User direction 2026-06-09.)

## Current state
`spa-next/src/components/Field.svelte` renders `type: 'integer' | 'number'` as `<input type="number" min max step>` (Field.svelte:191-197). The novelty schema (generators/kenning.py:134) is `{type: number, minimum: 0.0, maximum: 1.0, default: 0.0}` — all the bounds a slider needs are already present.

## Approach
- Render a range slider for bounded proportions: a `number` field that has BOTH `minimum` and `maximum` (and isn't an integer count). Add a live numeric readout next to the slider + min/max end labels, and a sane `step` (e.g. 0.05).
- Keep it manifest-driven (SPA guideline): drive off the schema, not a hardcoded field list. Prefer an explicit opt-in hint over auto-converting EVERY bounded number — e.g. a schema annotation like `"ui_widget": "slider"` (or `"format": "range"`) on the option, so a future numeric knob can still choose a plain box. Add the hint to the novelty schema.
- Other bounded-proportion knobs are slider candidates too (cohesion, harshness, spelling_variety, inflection_density, the vector axis weights phonological/semantic/position/baseline) — scope THIS ticket to the slider mechanism + novelty; note the others for a follow-up sweep.

## Acceptance
- novelty renders as a slider with a visible current value; emitted param is still a float in [0,1]; existing Field number behavior for non-slider numbers unchanged. Field.svelte unit/test coverage updated.

## Refs
- wyrd-fca0 (graduated-novelty quality pass), wyrd-fcub (novelty impl), Field.svelte, generators/kenning.py input_schema, SPA manifest-driven guideline (CLAUDE.md)

title: Graduated-novelty quality pass (validate output across novelty 0->1, decide prod-flag enablement)
description:
## Why
The --novelty knob (wyrd-fcub, vector path) has NO quality validation across its range — the only novelty-specific test is the manorial canary at novelty=1 (wyrd-57d8). It ships flag-gated off in prod (WYRD_FF_NOVELTY). Before anyone flips that flag we want to know what graduated novelty actually produces and where the useful range is.

## What novelty mechanically does (grounded 2026-06-09, so the tester isn't guessing)
novelty does NOT change slot eligibility. The per-slot candidate pool is built + filtered FIRST, then novelty re-weights the survivors toward uniform via _blend_uniform_by_novelty: weight = (1-novelty)*(score/total) + novelty*(1/n); novelty=1 -> pure uniform 1/n.

The per-slot pool survives FOUR constraints BEFORE novelty, none of which novelty touches:
1. Hard eligibility gates (build_non_position_eligible): culture, era, stratum, exclude_tags, base-pool class exclusions (saints / given-names / manorial / connectors).
2. Name/saint qualifier gate (qualified slots only).
3. Negative-score filter (a register actively opposing a morpheme drops it).
4. **Per-position empirical-frequency filter** (_apply_per_usage_frequency, live NameGenerator path): a morpheme with freq <= 0 in this position bucket is dropped (vector_name_select.py:677). This is the data-driven 'which morphemes appear in this position' restriction that replaced the old hard position gate post-D40.

So increasing novelty flattens the RELATIVE PREFERENCE among morphemes that are already eligible + attested-in-this-position — both the four score axes (phon/sem/pos/baseline) AND the empirical position-frequency weighting. Effect: a morpheme attested RARELY in this position becomes as likely as a common one; an off-register-but-eligible morpheme becomes as likely as a well-matching one. It does NOT surface morphemes that are gated out or never attested in the position (freq 0 -> already filtered). (Note: novelty's role in the wyrd-57d8 leak was INDIRECT — it made degenerate repeats like 'corner corner' likely, which triggered the separate diversification re-pick that had no frequency filter; the scored pick itself correctly excluded the manorial subject.)

## The pass
1. Generate N (>=1000 for signal, per wyrd-vidi's N=100-is-noise lesson) per culture at novelty in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0}; eyeball + measure.
2. Metrics worth capturing:
   - decomposition/realism drift vs novelty (reuse drift_measurement / realism_tolerance primitives) — how fast does plausibility fall off?
   - repeat rate vs novelty (degenerate same-surface picks that lean on diversification) — quantify the diversification load high novelty creates.
   - register/mood retention vs novelty: does --mood harsh/grim still have teeth at novelty=0.7, or does the uniform blend wash the register axis out? (novelty vs register is a real tension — both modify the same weighted distribution.)
   - any OTHER low-frequency-morpheme surprises analogous to Malet that read as wrong (not just manorial — saints/given-names are gated, but rare topographic/loanword morphemes in odd positions).
3. Recommend a USEFUL novelty range / default and whether to cap the SPA slider below 1.0 (novelty=1 = pure uniform = maximally unrealistic by construction).
4. Decide + record: enable WYRD_FF_NOVELTY in prod or keep gated. (enabled_feature_flags = ['novelty'] is the flip; no redeploy.)

## Acceptance
- A short findings note (quality at each novelty stop, the metrics above) + a recommended default/range + a go/no-go on the prod flag. Add graduated-novelty regression coverage if the pass surfaces a defect.

## Refs
- wyrd-fcub (novelty re-wire onto vector path; _blend_uniform_by_novelty), wyrd-57d8 (novelty=1 manorial leak, fixed), wyrd-vidi (N=1000 not N=100), D17 (original novelty), D36/D37 (vector scoring + register), CLAUDE.md SPA feature flags (WYRD_FF_NOVELTY)
notes:
FINDINGS (graduated-novelty quality pass, N=1000/cell, 5 cultures × novelty {0,.25,.5,.75,1}; harness in scratch/novelty_quality_pass.py):

Key metric = morpheme_rank_correlation ρ (Spearman of sample morpheme ranks vs the corpus reference; 1=corpus-faithful, lower=flatter). Degrades monotonically with novelty, as designed:
  english : .615 .569 .397 .302 .252
  scottish: .680 .639 .463 .329 .234
  welsh   : .626 .459 .334 .300 .200   (most novelty-sensitive)
  irish   : .788 .667 .510 .481 .299
  breton  : .703 .605 .533 .493 .400   (most gradual)
tag-TV/KL (semantic drift vs corpus) rises with novelty the same way; welsh drifts most, breton least.

Robustness across the whole range:
- decomposition_rate = 1.000 at EVERY stop, all cultures — novelty never produces undecomposable junk; it reorders morpheme frequency within the eligible+attested pool.
- position-TV stays low + flat — novelty does NOT distort name STRUCTURE (per-position frequency filter survives), only within-slot morpheme choice. Confirms the mechanism.
- within-name duplicate-morpheme rate ≤1.1% even at novelty=1 — diversification holds; the wyrd-57d8 manorial-class path does NOT blow up at high novelty.
- variety (uniq surfaces/N) is already high at novelty=0 (.80–.91); novelty adds only +.05–.13. novelty trades realism for surprise, NOT for variety — the generator is already diverse at 0.
- eyeball: names at every stop read as plausible (nov=1 english: 'Gata Tūn Lēagum Heg', 'Forest Wearghús', 'Lanu Henakr') — more archaic/exotic, not broken.

The knee is ~0.25–0.5: novelty ≤0.25 stays close to the novelty=0 baseline (corpus-faithful 'a touch of surprise'); 0.5 roughly halves ρ; 1.0 washes out most corpus-rank structure (ρ .2–.4) = maximally surprising by construction, but still well-formed.

RECOMMENDATION:
- Default 0.1 is VALIDATED — it sits well inside the corpus-faithful zone (realism ≈ novelty=0). The shipped prod/staging 0.1 is a good, safe default.
- Useful range ≈ 0–0.5 for 'realistic with flavor'; 0.5–1.0 is the deliberately-weird zone (legitimate, just atypical).
- No slider cap needed: novelty=1 is SAFE (decomposable, no junk, no repeat blowup). 0–1 is fine; the low end is the realistic zone (could add UI guidance later, no code change).
- Prod flag: already shipped ON at 0.1 — confirmed safe. No change. (Item 4 'decide enablement' resolved by the wyrd-7f22 ship.)

NO novelty DEFECT surfaced (so no novelty regression test required by acceptance; a graduated-novelty smoke pinning decomp=1.0 + low dup across {0,.5,1} is an optional guard).

SEPARATE FINDING (filed as follow-up): the SEMANTIC register axis is a no-op. mood=grim changes 0/300 outputs at novelty=0 (mood=harsh changes 297/300). grim's effect is correctly defined+parsed (semantic_tags death/military/monster/undead/magic) but positive tag boosts can't surface morphemes: post-wyrd-bol9 cross-usage selection weight = empirical freq[usage]; the composed score only disambiguates WITHIN a usage's senses (no surface change) or drops a sense via bs<0. So only NEGATIVE-direction effects (harsh) bite; thematic moods (grim/pastoral/devotional/mortuary) are effectively inert. Independent of novelty.
close_reason: Done. Graduated-novelty quality pass complete: swept 5 cultures × novelty {0,.25,.5,1} N=1000; findings + recommendation recorded (0.1 default validated, useful range ~0-0.5, no cap, prod flag fine). Smoke regression shipped in PR #560 (well-formed/has-effect/no-repeat-blowup/mid-stop-graduated). Surfaced a separate P2 — semantic register axis no-op — filed as wyrd-4rp8.

title: Mitigate the male skew in the given-name corpus (source-class artifact, not real variability)
description:
## Observation
The authoring lexicon has 8,543 `male name` vs 392 `female name` etymons (~22:1). This is NOT because male names had less variability — historically female given-names had MORE variability — it's a SOURCE-CLASS artifact.

## Diagnosis (grounded 2026-06-09)
Top sources for the name-tagged etymons:
- male:   briggs_2024_personal_names_index 8503, pase 2846, dlv 1690, kepn 1497, kepn_external 1464, anglo_saxon_charters 170 (lang: old-english 7762)
- female: briggs_2024_personal_names_index 378, pase 140, kepn 37, kepn_external 36, dlv 32, rando-port 15 (lang: old-english 289)

Every top contributor is a male-biased DOCUMENT CLASS: charters, Domesday (dlv), place-name keys (kepn = toponym-derived), and prosopography (pase) record landholders / witnesses / clergy — overwhelmingly men. Women's names that existed are under-recorded in property/legal/administrative sources, so the corpus inherits that bias. The skew is real *about these sources*, not about historical name variability.

## Mitigation directions
1. **Ingest female-name-richer source classes** that aren't property/charter records:
   - Wiktextract given-name categories (gender-tagged; attested given names across genders, not document-derived) — likely cheapest, reuses wyrd-4rt ingest.
   - Hagiographies / saints' lives, religious-house (nunnery) records, literary sources, dedicated onomastic dictionaries of female names (PD; D2/D3 mining pipeline).
2. **Decouple generation from attestation** for the generator use case (esp. fantastical/fictional, wyrd-2cz5): female given-names can be generated from morpheme/phonology pools even where direct attestation is thin — don't gate female output on the (biased) attestation count.
3. **Surface gender balance as a coverage metric** (counts per gender per language/era) so progress is visible, and document the source-bias caveat so future readers don't misread the skew as historical truth.

## Notes
- Tagging check: verify unisex names get both tags and that 'female name' isn't simply under-applied during ingest (a cheaper fix if it's partly a tagging gap rather than pure source gap).
- Relevant to patronymic generation balance (wyrd-pbjv / wyrd-44qo): a patronymic arm drawing from an 8543:392 pool will be near-exclusively male-derived.

## Refs
- wyrd-pbjv (surname epic — patronymic balance), wyrd-2cz5 (fantastical gen — attestation-decoupled), wyrd-4rt (wiktextract ingest), D2/D3 (mining tiers + validator)
design:
Gendered morphology / conjugation correctness (user note 2026-06-09): fixing the skew is NOT just 'add more female names' — the generation + conjugation layer must produce gender-correct forms, or we'll emit malformed names.

Things that must conjugate/agree by gender:
- **Gendered given-name endings**: Latin -us/-a, Slavic -ov/-ova & -sky/-skaya, Italian/Spanish -o/-a, Greek -os/-a, etc. A morpheme pool can't be gender-blind — the same root takes a different surface by gender.
- **Patronymic gender agreement** (cross-cuts wyrd-44qo): the affix agrees with the BEARER's gender, not the parent's — -son/-dóttir (ON), -ovich/-ovna (Slavic), Mac-/Nic- (Gaelic), ben-/bat- (Hebrew), -ez (Iberian, frozen), -sson/-sdóttir (Icelandic). Patronymic also takes the parent name in the GENITIVE in several languages (the D8 inflection machinery is relevant here).
- **Surname agreement**: in some languages family names themselves inflect for the bearer's gender (Slavic Novák/Nováková).

Implication: 'gender' needs to be a first-class attribute on the name pools + a parameter threaded through the patronymic/surname arms, with per-language gendered-affix + gendered-ending tables (a sidecar set, like the patronymic-affix sidecar in wyrd-oh30). Don't model gender as a post-hoc filter on a male-shaped pipeline. Decide the model (binary tag vs. per-language gendered-form sibling, à la D8 inflections / D26 sibling fields) as part of this work.

Cross-refs: wyrd-44qo (patronymic arm — the main consumer of gender agreement), wyrd-oh30 (corpus: capture gender + gendered variants at ingest), D8 (inflection/genitive), D26 (per-form sibling-field pattern).

title: Fantastical-first surname generator (invented dynasties / NPC houses)
description:
Parent epic: wyrd-pbjv.

## Goal
A surname generator tuned for FANTASY / FICTIONAL output — invented noble houses, NPC family names, dynasties — register/phonology-driven rather than historically faithful. Does NOT require a real surname corpus (wyrd-oh30); pulls morphemes + register effects directly.

## Design notes
- Lean on the D36/D37 vector + register machinery: 'noble', 'sinister', 'ancient', 'exotic', 'martial' moods already exist and map naturally onto house-name flavor (House Blackmoor, von Grausen, Asheforth).
- Compose surname-shape templates (descriptive+place 'Blackmoor', particle+root 'von Grausen', double-barrel 'Ravensworth') with morpheme draws; the manorial/locative-particle vocabulary (de/von/of/le) is reusable.
- Pack-friendly (D11 user packs): a fantasy world supplies a morpheme/register pack and gets coherent house names.
- Seed-reproducible; Generator ABC + CLI + SPA.

## Relationship to siblings
- Independent of wyrd-oh30 (corpus) — can ship without it.
- Shares the surname-template + class-weight machinery with wyrd-44qo (the compositional generator); whichever lands first should factor the shared template layer so the other reuses it.

## Acceptance
- A fantasy-surname Generator (registered + CLI + SPA) producing coherent invented family/house names driven by register/mood + morpheme packs, seed-stable.

## Refs
- wyrd-pbjv (epic), wyrd-44qo (shared template layer), D36/D37 (vector scoring + register catalog), D11 (user packs), wyrd-ami (fantasy-flavor precedent)

title: Family-name generator composing existing machinery (toponymic/patronymic/occupational/descriptive)
description:
Parent epic: wyrd-pbjv.

## Goal
A surname Generator that produces historically-plausible family names by COMPOSING what wyrd already has, one arm per formation class:
- **toponymic** ('de Vere', 'Ashby', 'Atwood') -> drive the existing Kenning place-name generator, optionally prefix a locative particle (de/of/at/von).
- **patronymic** ('Williamson', 'MacDonald', "O'Brien") -> draw from the 8,543-strong given-name corpus + a patronymic affix (sidecar from wyrd-oh30).
- **occupational** ('Smith', 'Fletcher', 'Baker') -> trade/occupation morphemes (from wyrd-oh30 corpus, or curated).
- **descriptive/nickname** ('Strong', 'Whitehead', 'le Blanc') -> adjective/feature morphemes.

## Design notes
- Fits the Generator ABC + register() pattern; CLI subcommand + SPA generator (generator-contract-reviewer applies).
- Class weights should be GM-tunable (e.g. mostly-occupational vs mostly-toponymic culture). Could learn empirical class proportions from the wyrd-oh30 corpus.
- Reuse vector scoring / register effects (D36/D37) for phonological flavor; reuse seed-reproducibility contract.
- Toponymic arm composing Kenning is the strongest immediate win — it needs little/no new corpus (the manorial families ARE this pattern; see wyrd-v3o9 + manorial_affix).

## Dependency
- Occupational/descriptive arms need surname morphemes from wyrd-oh30 (the corpus mine). Toponymic + patronymic arms can prototype before wyrd-oh30 lands (Kenning + given-names already exist).

## Acceptance
- A FamilyName (or Surname) Generator registered + CLI + SPA, with per-class arms and tunable class weights, seed-stable, composing existing generators/corpora.

## Refs
- wyrd-pbjv (epic), wyrd-oh30 (corpus, soft dep), wyrd-v3o9 (manorial structure), D36/D37 (vector scoring + register), generator-contract-reviewer

title: Learn manorial <base> <family> structure from the corpus (proportions build excludes manorial subjects)
description:
## Problem

The proportions build (`_compute_proportions_inline` in `lexicon/runtime_db_export.py`) decomposes each culture's toponyms against `word_db = load_meanings({'subjects': export_meanings(db, ...)})`. `export_meanings` (`lexicon/bundle/_export.py`) is the L3-DB projection and does NOT include the four runtime sidecars — the synthesized Norman manorial subjects, saint personal names, Irish anglicizations, curated senses — which are unioned in only at runtime by `__init__._load_meanings()`.

Consequence: a real manorial toponym (Shepton Mallet, Stoke Mandeville, Castle Cary) has its family-surname token (Mallet/Mandeville/Cary) match NO morpheme in the build word_db, so `count_unaccounted() != 0` and the name is dropped from `good_names` → it contributes nothing to proportions. The two-word `<base> <family>` manorial STRUCTURE is therefore never learned into `proportions_structure` (and the manorial-affix position never appears in `proportions_usage`). Empirically: 0 of 708 distinct proportions usage keys in seed-runtime.db match any of the ~40 Norman family tokens.

Today manorial layering is produced ONLY by the dedicated `manorial_affix` probability knob (wyrd-obu, kenning.py:~513), which appends a family post-generation — not from learned corpus statistics.

## Goal

Let the build-time proportions decomposer see the manorial subjects so manorial toponyms decompose fully and contribute (a) their two-word structure to `proportions_structure` and (b) the manorial-affix position bucket to `proportions_usage`. Optionally, let generation produce manorial layering from learned structure as an alternative/complement to the `manorial_affix` knob.

## Fix direction

- Fold the manorial subjects (at minimum) into the word_db that `_compute_proportions_inline` decomposes against — mirror what `__init__._load_meanings()` already does at runtime (or reuse it). Decomposition is string-match-only (D40), so this is safe — it's exactly what KenningExplain already does.
- Ensure the derived position is `manorial-affix` (the existing D36.1 position label / kenning.py location), not bare, so the learned structure slot is the manorial slot.

## Critical interaction with wyrd-57d8 (just merged, PR #538)

Manorial subjects are now base-pool-excluded via `Meaning.is_base_pool_excluded()` (kept out of the scored pool, the load_parts frequency-weight pool, AND the diversification re-pick). That exclusion is the RIGHT default for BARE/base slots. If we learn manorial structure and want generation to USE it, the manorial subject must be selectable in a manorial STRUCTURE slot while staying excluded from bare slots — i.e. the Rando-style key/qualifier segregation (cf. proportions `word_to_key` name/saint qualifiers; add a 'manorial' qualifier). Do NOT simply un-exclude manorial subjects globally — that reintroduces the wyrd-57d8 leak. Decomposition word_db membership (string match) is orthogonal to generation-pool eligibility, so adding them to the decomposer does not by itself re-open the leak; surfacing them in generation is the part that needs the slot/qualifier gate.

## Also reconcile

- `decomposition_export.collect_canonical_decompositions` deliberately SKIPS manorial-final toponyms (so the runtime manorial-affix detector wins the canonical pick). That skip is about the canonical PICK, not proportions — but a structure-learning change should be checked against it so the two stay coherent.

## Acceptance

- Manorial toponyms decompose fully (count_unaccounted==0) in `_compute_proportions_inline`; the `<base> <family>` template appears in `proportions_structure` with the family in a `manorial-affix`/manorial-qualified slot.
- Base/bare generation still never emits a manorial subject (wyrd-57d8 canary stays green).
- Decide + document whether learned manorial structure REPLACES or COMPLEMENTS the `manorial_affix` knob.

## Refs
- wyrd-57d8 (base-pool exclusion; PR #538) — the exclusion this must not regress
- wyrd-8s71 (`_norman_manorial_subjects` synthesis)
- wyrd-obu (`manorial_affix` knob)
- D36.1 (position vocabulary incl. manorial-affix), D39/D40 (position is derived; string-match decomposition)

title: novelty=1 surfaces Norman manorial subjects in base output (render-injection, not pool exclude_tags)
description:
Pre-existing bug in the vector generation path, SURFACED by wyrd-fcub (re-wiring novelty). At novelty=1 (uniform blend over the eligible pool), synthesized manorial subjects (tagged 'manorial'/'norman', e.g. 'Malet') appear in BASE generation output ('Corner Malet') even though manorial_affix is off and exclude_tags should filter them.

## Diagnosis (from wyrd-fcub investigation)
- The synthesized manorial subjects ARE in the english meaning_db, tagged ['manorial','norman'] (confirmed: the 'Malet' Meaning carries those tags).
- generate() sets exclude_tags = (_FICTION_TAG,) for non-fiction; this is threaded correctly to select_via_vector_scoring.
- The NON-position pool path (build_non_position_eligible, vector_name_select.py:312/351) DOES apply exclude_tags.
- But the per-slot scoring path `build_slot_base_scores` (vector_name_select.py:414) does NOT take or apply exclude_tags. So tagged subjects in a position slot's base_scored pool are never filtered.
- Adding an exclude_tags filter at the pick point (the weighted-building loop, ~line 777) did NOT catch it either — strongly implying build_slot_base_scores emits position-form Meaning wrappers whose `.tags` no longer carry the original manorial tags. So the exclusion must happen at the SOURCE (when building the slot pool from non_position_eligible, using the original tags), not at pick time.

## Why it normally hides
Without novelty the subjects have near-zero vector score, so they're ~never picked across small seed ranges — the test passed by luck. novelty=1 flattens to uniform 1/n and surfaces them deterministically. (fiction-tagged morphemes likely leak into slots the same way — verify.)

## Fix direction
Thread exclude_tags into build_slot_base_scores (or filter non_position_eligible against exclude_tags before building slot pools), using the ORIGINAL meaning tags. Confirm the realism gate + seed-stability hold after (excluding morphemes re-normalizes slot pools). Then restore the novelty=1.0 canary in test_synthesized_manorial_meaning_does_not_break_kenning_generate.

Context: tests/test_kenning_manorial_explain_roundtrip.py::test_synthesized_manorial_meaning_does_not_break_kenning_generate (its docstring already names novelty=1.0 as the canary). wyrd-fcub deferred this — its novelty=1.0 config is temporarily dropped from that test pending this fix.
notes: Fix implemented in PR #538 (branch kenning/manorial-base-pool-leak). Two layers: (b) Meaning.is_base_pool_excluded() centralizes the request-independent base-pool class exclusions incl. new is_manorial_subject(); wired into all three base-pool sites (vector_name_select._native_meaning_eligible, proportions.MeaningGenerator.load_parts, proportions.NewName._collect_repick_pools). (a) the diversification re-pick now applies it. Restored novelty=1.0 canary + added direct unit tests (predicates, repick branch carve-out, vector-pool exclusion). Full suite 4875 passed; CI green; 2 agent-review rounds clean. Awaiting merge.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #538 (squash b724417). Synthesized manorial subjects now excluded from all three base-generation pools via Meaning.is_base_pool_excluded(); novelty=1.0 canary restored + direct unit tests added. Full suite 4875 passed; CI green; 2 specialist agent rounds + 1 general holistic review, all clean.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text: From PR #509 review (pr-test-analyzer): the manorial leak test's remaining default+cohesion configs only SMOKE-test now — manorial subjects have near-zero vector score so they're ~never picked without novelty's uniform flattening. The only config that deterministically exercised the leak was novelty=1.0 (dropped pending this fix). So when fixing: (1) make the slot scorer apply exclude_tags at the source (using original tags, not position-form wrappers — confirmed the pick-point filter doesn't catch it because position forms drop tags), and (2) restore the novelty=1.0 canary in test_synthesized_manorial_meaning_does_not_break_kenning_generate so the guard is deterministic by construction.

comments.author: Devon Jones
comments.text:
CORRECTION to the diagnosis — the original 'build_slot_base_scores ignores exclude_tags' premise is WRONG. Investigated deeply (wyrd-57d8 branch, since discarded):

Reproduced: generate({culture:english, novelty:1.0}, seed=13) -> 'Corner Malet' (Malet = a Norman manorial subject). But:
- build_non_position_eligible DOES honor exclude_tags on current main (the wyrd-8uvi C901 refactor extracted _native_pool which applies it). Traced: with exclude_tags={fiction,manorial}, the built pool has NO Malet.
- Adding 'manorial' to generate()'s exclude_tags makes the pool exclude Malet — BUT the output STILL contains 'Corner Malet'. So exclude_tags is NOT the lever.
- _weighted_choice fires exactly twice (the 2 bare-word slots) and Malet is in NEITHER candidate pool. The slot picks are ['corner','corner'] (structure ['bare','bare']) — yet the rendered surface is 'Corner Malet' with explanation 'Malet (FR Norman manorial family: Malet)'.

CONCLUSION: the manorial subject is injected POST-PICK, somewhere in the render / NewName-assembly / decomposition-explanation path (NOT the eligible-pool sampling). exclude_tags can't reach it. The fix needs to trace where _norman_manorial_subjects / modifier_type='Manorial' entries enter rendering and gate them out of base generation there. Only manifests at novelty=1 (an advanced knob, off by default via WYRD_FF_NOVELTY in prod) — so low user impact. Recommend re-scoping/repricing accordingly; the exclude_tags approach (and the manorial-test canary restore) was abandoned as ineffective.

title: Investigate: semantic moods (grim etc.) appear inert in vector output
description:
Surfaced during wyrd-3dlx review (PR #506). Empirical finding: generating english names with mood=['grim'] produces the SAME output set as no mood across 30 seeds — i.e. a semantic mood does not visibly shift the generated distribution end-to-end under vector-only generation. Harshness (phonological axis) DOES shift it (test_harshness_shifts_vector_distribution_end_to_end passes).

The mood MECHANISM is wired + tested (test_kenning_vector_kenning_adapter.py: mood expands to register effects, the request vector shifts), but the semantic-axis bias is apparently too weak to change the argmax morpheme picks for english.

## Investigate
- Is this expected (semantic bias is meant to be subtle / a soft preference) or a wiring weakness (semantic_weight too low, or the gate/scoring path drops the semantic contribution)?
- Does a stronger semantic_weight or a different culture/seed range surface a shift?
- If semantic moods are meant to meaningfully affect output, add a real end-to-end vector test once they do (the test-coverage reviewer wanted one in PR #506; it couldn't be written truthfully because grim is currently inert end-to-end).

This is the mood analog of the novelty finding (wyrd-fcub). Not a blocker — the mechanism + adapter coverage exist; this is about whether the effect is actually felt.

title: Re-wire novelty (lexical-surprise dial) into the vector scoring path
description:
wyrd-3dlx dropped the `novelty` input (schema field + --novelty CLI flag) because it was inert under vector-only generation. This ticket restores the capability in the vector path.

## What novelty did (proportions path, now deleted)
A frequency-flattening / lexical-surprise dial implemented in proportions._blend_uniform:
    blended_weight = (1 - novelty)*(empirical_freq/total) + novelty*(1/n)
Per morpheme bucket it interpolated between the EMPIRICAL frequency distribution (novelty=0: common morphemes like -ton/-ham dominate) and a FLAT uniform one (novelty=1: rare morphemes equally likely → deliberately unusual names). Intermediate = graduated "make this weirder". It composed multiplicatively after harshness, applied LAST.

## Why it went inert
Vector scoring picks by axis fit (phonological/semantic/positional/baseline) against the request vector via register effects — there is no "flatten the frequency distribution toward uniform" step for novelty to hook into.

## Implementation options (pick one)
1. **Map novelty -> baseline_weight.** The baseline axis IS the empirical-frequency signal; novelty=1 -> baseline_weight≈0 (de-emphasize "common=likely"). Smallest change, but NOT equivalent: it reweights an axis across the whole score rather than interpolating a per-bucket distribution toward uniform, and isn't seed-for-seed comparable to the old behavior.
2. **Post-score pool-uniform blend.** Re-introduce the _blend_uniform interpolation in select_via_vector_scoring: after computing per-candidate scores per slot, blend the score-derived distribution toward uniform-over-the-eligible-pool by `novelty`. Closest to the original semantics; localized to the vector selection step.

Recommend option 2 (faithful) unless option 1's approximation is judged good enough. Either way: re-add the schema field + --novelty CLI option + params passthrough, and add a vector distribution test (mirror test_harshness_shifts_vector_distribution_end_to_end) proving novelty shifts the output distribution under vector.

Context: created during wyrd-3dlx (proportions scoring-mode retirement). The old _blend_uniform + its tests are in git history at the pre-wyrd-3dlx commit if you want the reference implementation.

title: Add vulture dead-code gate to CI
description:
PR #498 added [tool.vulture] config to pyproject.toml so `uvx vulture` (no flags) gives a reproducible dead-code report. Turn that into a CI gate so NEW orphaned code can't land unnoticed (the repo grew to ~83kloc before the first audit).

## The baseline problem
A bare `uvx vulture` currently reports 41 pre-existing candidates (see wyrd-r87f). A naive `vulture && exit-nonzero` gate would red the build on day one. Two viable designs:

1. **Triage-first (preferred):** land wyrd-r87f first so the report is near-empty, then make the gate fail on ANY finding. Cleanest end state. → this ticket depends on wyrd-r87f.
2. **Whitelist/baseline now:** generate `vulture --make-whitelist > vulture_whitelist.py`, commit it, and run `uvx vulture wyrd vulture_whitelist.py` in CI so only NEW findings fail. Lets the gate land immediately; whitelist shrinks as wyrd-r87f progresses.

## Implementation notes
- Add a step to the existing CI workflow (alongside ruff/pytest). Use `uvx vulture` so no env/dep changes are needed — it reads [tool.vulture] from pyproject automatically.
- Confidence floor is already 60 in config; the gate inherits it.
- Keep it fast — vulture is static-only, runs in ~1-2s over wyrd/.
- Decide failure mode: hard-fail (block merge) vs. soft annotation. Recommend hard-fail once baseline is clean (design 1).

Related: wyrd-r87f (triage the 41), PR #498 (config + first removals).

title: era-grid over-merge residue: no-bridging-parent stale-attachment class (~9%)
description: After wyrd-1wv2 (toponym audit, 82->91% clean), the residual ~9% mixed/pure-noise era-grids are dominated by modern reflexes that have NO cuttable in-cluster bridging parent (e.g. hām->AM, mont->'mons pubis'/'Mons'). Edge-detach can't orphan them because _bridging_parents finds no bridging in-edge in the cluster -> after clear+recluster they persist. Likely a stale/odd attachment (a non-bridging or cross-resolution edge, or a cognate_id assigned without a traceable bridging path). Investigate how these leaves remain clustered with the morpheme despite no bridging parent; may need a different orphaning mechanism (direct cognate_id reassignment for confirmed-noise leaves) or a deeper cluster_cognates fix. Lower priority — the visible/common morphemes (tūn, hām, val) are clean.
close_reason: Form-filterable portion DONE + MERGED (PR #500). Extended _is_derived_name_pollution (bundle modern-stage era-grid filter) to drop single-char fragments + closed-class function words/pronouns + non-alphabetic artifacts, with a CI-enforced disjointness invariant vs PROTECTED_ELEMENTS. Measured on shipped bundle: 84.5->87.3% clean (mixed 11.3->8.1%); 27 distinct junk forms dropped, zero legit elements. Reviewers (test-coverage + generator-contract + Gemini): contract-safe (additive forms_by_lang merge, deterministic, modern-stage-only), HIGH non-alpha gap fixed. DIAGNOSIS UPDATE: the ticket's 'no-bridging-parent' framing was the RAW-query view; in the BUNDLE the proper-noun class was already filtered (rogd.11) and the remaining residue is (a) junk fragments [now fixed] + (b) deep cross-cluster real-word over-merge [filed as wyrd-h2lv — needs cluster-splitting, not form-filtering]. Code-only; ships on next bundle rebuild+publish.

title: era-grid: clean all-self morphemes (no attestation) — e.g. -ing keeps mis-segmentations (Birl-/Cather-) next to legit -ling/-ning
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-5olv (PR #492). The genuine-wins merge fix cleans morphemes that HAVE genuine (cluster/descent/period-form/phonology) reflexes (tūn, lēah, hām, etc.). It can't clean ALL-SELF morphemes — those with zero attestation, where the only era_reflexes are self-seeds. -ing is the canonical case: its modern reflexes fall back to self-seeds, which mix legit derivational suffixes (-ling, -ning, -ting, -inge) with mis-segmentations (Birl-, Cather-, Ching-, Kip-, Sit-, Ulling-).

A merge-time compound-detector is explicitly OFF the table: it can't distinguish a real suffix (-ling) from a constructed compound (-bolton) and would eat both (user guardrail). Real fixes need either (a) genuine attestation for these morphemes (so genuine-wins has something to filter to), or (b) a proper morpheme split à la #490's -ing/-ling work, or (c) fixing the upstream morpheme_id attribution so mis-segmentations like Birl-/Sit- don't get morpheme_id=old-english:ing in the first place. Lower priority — the dominant -ton pollution is fixed; this is the long tail.
notes: Reframed: this all-self residual is largely a symptom of wyrd-862b (bad town reflexes linked to suffix morphemes) + wyrd-862b-sibling (hām-class missing genuine modern reflex). For -ing specifically (a bound suffix with no standalone modern reflex), genuine-wins can't help; needs the reflex-link prune (wyrd-862b) to drop the -Xing town reflexes while keeping -ling. See wyrd-862b.

title: era-grid: hill dūn cluster conflated with feather-down (duvet) via Wiktionary descent
description: Surfaced while fixing wyrd-qp9c. After detaching the verb lineage and folding don→dūn, the -don toponym morpheme correctly leaves the verb cluster, but the dūn hill cluster it lands in also contains the feather/eiderdown sense (duvet, ON dúnn/dýnn, OF dumet) — OE dūn 'hill' (PIE *dʰuhnom / Celtic *dūnom) and 'down (feathers)' (ON dúnn ← PIE dʰew-) are different roots that Wiktionary's descent graph links under a shared proto-germanic node. The era-reflex picker then chose 'duvet' as the modern reflex over the correct 'down'/'downe'. Separate, pre-existing descent-graph quality issue (NOT the verb contamination wyrd-qp9c targets). Likely same class as the broader 'detect inheritance edges whose parent/child glosses share no meaning' quality pass noted in wyrd-qp9c. Lower priority — 'down'/'downe' (correct hill reflex) is still in the cluster; only the picker's representative-reflex choice is off.
notes: Update: the duvet/feather-down reflex was an ARTIFACT of my broad family-reset during verification, NOT the real enrichment. On the live DB after the proper qp9c enrichment, dūn lands in the clean 7-member dusnaz hill cluster (doun/down-/North Downs/doon), and era reflexes are all hill forms — no duvet. The underlying Wiktionary descent link between hill-dūn and feather-down still exists in the graph (could resurface if clustering changes), so keeping this open as a latent-quality note, but it is NOT currently user-visible. Lower urgency than first thought.

title: Era render: diversification can blank an era slot back to the modern form
description: Follow-up from PR #446 (wyrd-6c8x) domain review. _diversify_repeats runs lazily inside NewName.__str__/to_dict, AFTER _apply_render has set the era-rendered forms. On a REPEATED surface within a name it either (a) grafts a cross-language synonym's raw .form (proportions.py ~1822, NOT era-rendered) or (b) re-picks and sets self.rendered[wi][ei]=None (~1833), which makes that one slot emit the canonical MODERN surface inside an otherwise-period name. So era=oe-early names with a repeated morpheme can show a stray modern token. Rare (only on repeats) and degrades gracefully (still a valid name), so deferred from #446. Fix options: make _diversify_repeats era-aware (re-render the grafted synonym / re-picked slot via _era_form_for_meanings using the active era_render_language), which means threading era_render_language onto NewName or into the diversify path. Low priority — period purity polish.
close_reason: PR #729 merged. _diversify_repeats is now era-aware: the cross-language synonym graft (site a) + the re-pick (site b) render the resolved repeat slot via _era_form_for_meanings(self.era_render_language), so an era=oe-early name with a repeated morpheme no longer shows a stray modern/native token. GATED on era render (era_render_language None → prior raw/native form → non-era bit-stable; realism+parity all non-era, unaffected, no snapshot regen). Identity/seen/picked_ids still key on the raw form so the D44 era-INVARIANT skeleton + modern_name() are unchanged. Fallback when no reflex at that era → prior form (the dominant path, tested). 2 review rounds (7 personas + Gemini, 0 P1/P2; +no-reflex-fallback test). Full suite 5716.

title: Saint-dedication quality: 'Saint <common-noun>' oddities + rare trailing-St (saint slot should pair a saint NAME)
description: Vector mode produces ~0.6% 'Saint <common-noun>' names (Saint Combe, Saint West, Saint Port) — the saint-qualified slot is followed by a generic word, not a saint NAME, because the saint SUBJECTS are excluded from the base pool (wyrd-eyjk) so the trailing name-slot fills with a non-subject morpheme. The user-reported trailing-'St' dangle (...Tump St) is non-systematic (0/500 vector seeds). ROOT: there is no St-dedication generation knob (only manorial_affix); the saint subjects are decomposition-only + base-excluded, so 'Saint X' structures fill X with whatever name/common morpheme is eligible. PROPER FIX: either (a) gate saint-qualified structures behind a dedication knob that injects a real saint-name subject (like manorial_affix injects manorial families), or (b) drop saint-qualified structures from base generation entirely (no knob = no St dedications). title: CI/deploy: serialize staging deploys with a concurrency group (avoid Lambda/tfstate races)
description:
Observed 2026-06-01: two near-simultaneous pushes to main triggered overlapping 'Deploy wyrd' staging runs that raced on the shared wyrd-staging Lambda + tfstate. One run failed at Terraform apply with 'UpdateFunctionCode ... StatusCode: 409 ResourceConflictException: An update is in progress for resource: wyrd-staging' (run 26764647263, commit 48e07ac). Harmless here — a later deploy (ae47fe6) reconciled state and went green — but it produces spurious red deploys and could leave a half-applied state in worse timing.

Fix: add a GitHub Actions concurrency group to .github/workflows/deploy.yml so deploys to the same environment serialize instead of overlapping, e.g.:
  concurrency:
    group: deploy-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ inputs.environment || 'staging' }}
    cancel-in-progress: false
(cancel-in-progress: false so an in-flight terraform apply / Lambda update finishes rather than being cancelled mid-apply; a queued run then runs after.) Scope to the staging auto-deploy job at minimum; consider a per-environment group covering the production dispatch job too. Also a candidate: terraform's own state lock already exists (DynamoDB/S3) but the Lambda UpdateFunctionCode step is outside tfstate locking, so the workflow-level concurrency group is the right guard.

Affected file: .github/workflows/deploy.yml. Low priority — cosmetic-red + rare-timing, not a correctness bug.

title: dev seed: prune unrenderable structures in select_dev_subset so welsh stops rendering empty names
description:
Follow-up to wyrd-cj6f / PR #415. The crash is fixed (MeaningGenerator.select returns None + warns once for a missing bucket), but the committed dev seed (wyrd/generators/kenning/data/seed-runtime.db) still contains one orphaned welsh structure whose only slot is the ('bare','name','single') bucket. That bucket has no surviving usage in the --dev seed, so the rare seeds that pick the structure (~0.15% of welsh structure weight; e.g. the old crash seed 806) now render an EMPTY name instead of crashing.

Scope: dev-seed-only. The full PRODUCTION bundle populates that bucket (welsh personal/saint names), so no empty names ship to users. This is cosmetic and only affects local/test generation against the committed dev seed.

Root cause: select_dev_subset (wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/runtime_db_export.py) keeps proportions *structures* in full while trimming *usages* to top-N per culture. A structure referencing a bucket whose populating usage(s) fell outside top-N is left orphaned — renderable in production, empty in the dev subset.

Fix:
1. In select_dev_subset, after computing the kept-usage set, drop any structure whose slots cannot ALL be satisfied by a kept usage's bucket key (i.e. prune structures that reference a (position, tag, count) bucket with no surviving usage). Mirror the existing usage-trimming determinism (sorted, weight-stable) so the seed stays byte-reproducible.
2. Re-export the committed dev seed: `wyrd kenning lexicon export-runtime-db --dev --output wyrd/generators/kenning/data/seed-runtime.db` (per data/seed-runtime.README.md), and verify welsh seeds no longer emit empty names (tests/test_kenning_cj6f_welsh_proportions.py: the range test's non-empty count should hit 120/120; tighten that assertion afterward).

Observability already in place: MeaningGenerator.select logs a one-time wyrd-cj6f warning when this orphan path is hit, so the condition is visible in the meantime.

Note: do NOT just re-export without the select_dev_subset change — re-export alone reproduces the same orphan (the subset rules are what create it). And keep the runtime select()->None tolerance regardless; it is the production-safety guard for any future structure/usage drift, independent of the dev-seed subset.
close_reason: Implemented + merged in PR #420 (squash 6eab30f). Standing guard _prune_unrenderable_dev_structures in select_dev_subset drops trimming-orphaned structures (would render empty names) on every --dev export, per-culture, warning once. Dev-export-only; no-op on current data (wyrd-5z5j already populated welsh's bucket); committed seed unchanged. Reviewed via pr-review-loop (Gemini + silent-failure-hunter + code-reviewer clean; pr-test-analyzer order/per-culture hardening applied).
