title: language-report dashboard: distinguish 'loan-attributed zero' vs 'data-gap zero' for bundle coverage
description:
The dashboard's bundle-representation column treats two semantically-different cases identically:

1. **Loan-attributed zero**: Latin shows 0 (0.0%) bundle coverage. This is NOT a data gap — Latin loans into English get attributed to the receiving language at bundle export time (a borrowing edge `latin:castra → old-english:ceaster` lands ceaster as old-english in the bundle, with no separate latin entry). The 0 here is a deliberate attribution choice.
2. **Data-gap zero**: Breton's 92 variants (56.4%) but 0 inflections and 0 promotion-eligible at ≥3 reflects a genuine corpus thinness — we don't have enough mined material yet.

Today both surface as the same numeric '0' with no distinguishing flag. An operator reading the dashboard can't tell which languages have a 'should-fix' gap (do more mining) vs an 'expected-by-design' zero (loans are receiver-attributed; that's correct).

## What to add

### 1. Attribution-mode tag per language

In the per-language detail section, surface the attribution mode:

- `donor-only` (Latin, Greek, Akkadian, Egyptian, Hebrew, Arabic, Persian, Sanskrit, Aramaic, Armenian): loans surface as the receiving-language; zero bundle coverage is expected.
- `receiver` (modern-english, old-english, modern-french, etc.): primary bundle attribution. Coverage > 0 expected.
- `both` (old-norse, old-french, norman-french): some loans receive (gaelic-substrate in ON) AND some donate (ON → OE). Coverage > 0 expected from the receiving direction.

Mode lives somewhere already (the bundle-field mapping in `vector_name_select._BUNDLE_FIELD_TO_L3_LANG` is one source; `language_focus` in the source table is another; the descent graph is the ground truth).

### 2. Coverage delta interpretation

For donor-only languages, the dashboard should either omit bundle-coverage from the summary table OR display 'donor-only (n/a)' instead of '0 (0.0%)'.

For receiver languages with 0 bundle coverage but ≥1 promotion-eligible lemma, surface as 'data-gap; N promotable lemmas await bundle re-emit'.

For receiver languages with 0 promotion-eligible AND 0 bundle coverage (today: Welsh / Irish / Breton / etc.), surface as 'corpus-thin; N rando lemmas await tiered-policy promotion (wyrd-fssn)' or 'corpus-thin; expand mining backlog'.

## Why this matters

Without the distinction, the dashboard reads as 'Latin has 0 bundle coverage' — which prompts the wrong question ('why aren't we shipping Latin?') instead of the right one ('which receiver languages have promotable Latin loans the bundle re-emit doesn't carry?'). The Latin case in particular is concrete: it has 7 ≥2-promoted etymons and 21,057 descent edges into English-family — far from a 'zero data' state.

## Related

- wyrd-eni4 — Phase 0 of the gap-closing epic
- wyrd-g7n6 — sibling dashboard improvement (tiered-policy lift surfacing)
- wyrd-nxhh — bundle export should carry receiving-language attributions from cognate-cluster paths
notes: VETTED 2026-06-21: NEEDS one small decision, then LOOP-WORKABLE. The dashboard renders bundle coverage uniformly (reporting.py:92-94) with no donor-only/receiver flag; NO attribution-mode classification exists anywhere. Plumbing is SMALL (~60-100 LOC): add ATTRIBUTION_MODE map + scorecard field (models.py), set in compute_scorecard (audits.py), branch the bundle cell/detail in reporting.py (donor-only→'donor-only (n/a)'; receiver-zero→data-gap-vs-corpus-thin using existing promotion_eligible + rando family counts). DECISION (only blocker): how to source the donor/receiver/both classification. RECOMMEND a hand-curated static map (mirrors RECOMMENDED_LANG_THRESHOLDS/ERA_CHAINS curated-constant pattern; practically only the few donor-only langs in DEFAULT_LANGUAGES need entries) over deriving from the descent graph (needs a new query + undefined threshold). Pick static-map and it's loop-workable.
close_reason: PR #725 merged. language-report dashboard now distinguishes donor-only (n/a) vs data-gap vs corpus-thin zero. ATTRIBUTION_MODE static map (donor-only: latin/greek/akkadian/egyptian/hebrew/arabic/persian/sanskrit/aramaic/armenian; both: old-norse/old-french/norman-french; default receiver) + attribution_mode_for() + LanguageScorecard.attribution_mode field set in compute_scorecard; reporting.py branches the summary cell + detail. donor-only renders 'donor-only (n/a)' ONLY when bundle_word_count==0 (a >0 anomaly shows the real count — Gemini review); receiver-zero → 'data-gap (N promotable)' or 'corpus-thin'. Output-stable (dashboard only). 3 review rounds (2 P2 test-vacuity fixes + 3 Gemini mediums on the donor-only count-gate). Full suite 5711.

title: language-report dashboard: surface tiered-threshold lift (wyrd-fssn) + per-source-class rando breakdown
description:
The language-quality scorecard (`wyrd kenning lexicon language-report`) currently reports promotion-eligibility under a single threshold per language, which is ad-hoc inconsistent (modern-english / old-norse / norman-french / latin / celtic use ≥2; most use ≥3; Welsh / Irish / Scottish-Gaelic / Breton / old-irish / old-welsh / middle-english / old-french all sit at 0 promotion-eligible under ≥3).

Once wyrd-fssn lands (tiered threshold: rando-port + ≥1 corroborator promotes; net-new mining-only needs ≥3), the dashboard should surface the policy delta directly so operators can see the lift without rerunning the audit.

## What to add

### 1. "Promo (tiered)" column

Adjacent to the existing "Promo (≥thr)" column. Shows the promotion-eligible count under the tiered policy: rando lemmas with ≥1 corroborator + net-new lemmas with ≥3 witnesses. The delta vs the current column is the wyrd-fssn lift per language.

### 2. K (rando-port grandfather) row — expand the breakdown

The existing K row shows `pure-grandfather (rando, no corroborator) / mixed (rando + ≥1)`. Expand to:

`rando-only (0 corroborators) / rando + 1 / rando + 2 / rando + ≥3 (already promoted)`

So the audit's bucket distribution surfaces per language. Concrete numbers from the 2026-05-28 audit:

- Total rando lemmas: 1599
- rando-only: 1156
- rando + 1: 194
- rando + 2: 109
- rando + 3+: 140

Per-language lift (audit identified +303 total under tiered policy): old-english +158, celtic +98, old-norse +42, norman-french +4, biblical +1.

### 3. Sortable / filterable on the lift column

Operators want to see "which languages benefit most from the policy change" at a glance. Sort by `Promo (tiered) - Promo (≥thr)` descending highlights Celtic-family languages where the lift is the largest relative to a current value of 0.

## Why this matters for vector retirement

wyrd-bol9 closed the lang-mix parity gap between vector and proportions. The remaining quality gap is bundle coverage — Welsh / Irish / Breton vector pools are thinner than proportions in absolute terms because the underlying lexicon has 0 promoted lemmas in those languages. wyrd-fssn's tiered policy unlocks promotion for those languages without new mining; the dashboard updates here make the impact legible per-PR / per-bundle-re-emit.

## Related

- wyrd-fssn — the policy whose impact this dashboard surfaces
- wyrd-eni4 — Phase 0 of the gap-closing epic; this dashboard IS that Phase 0 deliverable
- wyrd-nxhh — sibling concern about bundle export carrying the promoted lemmas through to the runtime
notes:
K-ROW CORROBORATOR BREAKDOWN SHIPPED via PR #728 (the bead's blessed-salvageable standalone half): section K now splits the rando+corroborated 'mixed' bucket by corroborator count (rando-only/corr_0 = retirement tail; +1/+2/+≥3 = already promotion-eligible at the deployed ≥2-witness gate). _classify_grandfather_families refactored to a corroborator-count branch (multi-element-grandfather-safe, Gemini); +3 scorecard fields; K detail render. Output-stable, 3 review rounds.

STILL OPEN (deferred): the '#1 Promo (tiered) lift column' + #3 sortable-on-lift. Per the prior SKIP analysis these are STRUCTURALLY 0 under the deployed wyrd-fssn and need a Devon DECISION (A/B/C, encoded in the older NOTES): (A) reframe to the rando_min_corroborators 0→1 RETIREMENT impact (= the corr_0 count this PR now surfaces); (B) define a fixed net-new ≥3 threshold decoupled from the ≥2 gate; (C) re-run the audit for live numbers first. The closed PR #709 has the lift-column machinery to revive once decided.

title: Vector path occasionally produces split-affix 2-word names ('Port All' = Port- + -all)
description: Even with wyrd-zzli + wyrd-80ib structure filters in place, the vector scoring path produced 1/200 'split-affix' 2-word output ('Port All' = Port- + -all) during the wyrd-80ib validation run. Both Port- and -all are bare-affix morphemes (no name/saint flag) — the structure that resolved them must be one of the surviving qualifier-bearing multi-word structures (e.g. [[pre+saint], [pre+name]] weight 11) where the vector path filled the saint/name slots with non-qualifier morphemes. Likely a fallback path in select_via_vector_scoring when the saint/name-flagged bucket is empty or sparse. Investigate the vector-path bucket-resolution to confirm whether it should honor the structure's qualifier flags strictly.
notes: PR #363: https://github.com/521-studios/wyrd/pull/363. Root cause: NameGenerator.select_via_vector flattened struct to bare position labels via [key[0] for ...], dropping name/saint flags. title: kenning: etymon_add + citation_reassign event types — celtic:finn creation + Joyce 1875 reassignment
description:
Follow-up from wyrd-wz82 — the simpler half (etymon_gloss_add for OE finn + OE corn personal-name glosses) shipped in PR #349. The deeper half is still deferred:

For OE finn (etymon id 5573):
- The Celtic *finn 'bright, clear (water)' sense is currently mis-attached to the OE row because canonical_form happens to match. Joyce 1875 Irish Names vol1 cites it for Finglas / Rosenallis / Finnihy (Goidelic toponyms).
- Clean fix: create a Celtic etymon row (probably celtic:finn or per-Goidelic-language) carrying the Joyce citation; then reassign the Joyce citation from old-english:finn → celtic:finn.

For OE corn (etymon id 250):
- Same shape: the 'corn, a grain or seed' sense (productive in place-names; cf. Cornard in Skeat 1913) coexists with a personal-name sense (Mawer 1920 cites Corn as a personal name for Cornsay). The current row conflates them — wyrd-wz82 surfaced the personal-name as a separate gloss, but the citations are still all attached to the parent.
- Clean fix: split corn into corn (grain) + corn#name (personal), then reassign Cornsay's element to the personal-name child, leaving Cornard on the grain side.

Required new event types:
1. etymon_add — currently no curation event type can create a brand-new etymon row. The wyrd-wz82 add-gloss event requires the etymon to already exist. The celtic:finn row needs to come from somewhere.
2. citation_reassign — move an etymon_citation row from one etymon_id to another. Disambiguator: (source_id, page) or maybe (source_id, page, short_quote). Per D21 evidence-preservation, this is a move (UPDATE), not a delete + insert.

Both event types should mirror the wyrd-kutx/wyrd-wz82 pattern:
- KEYED_TYPES entry in jsonl/log.py
- Collector in jsonl/build.py
- Applier in enrichment.py with provenance method version
- CLI subcommand in cli/lexicon/curate_*.py
- Plumbed through enrich + rebuild_from_jsonl + diff_rebuild + diff_bundle
- format_unresolved_warnings section
- Tests covering collector / applier / CLI / run_full_enrichment threading

Scope guess: similar to wyrd-wz82 (~500 LOC + tests), maybe slightly larger because citation_reassign needs to handle the source_id disambiguator carefully when an etymon has multiple citations from the same source.

After event types land, the data work itself is small (1 etymon_add + 1-2 citation_reassign events for finn; 1 etymon_split + 1-2 citation_reassign events for corn).

Originally captured as a NOTE on wyrd-wz82.

title: kenning: wyrd-kutx polish — suffix charset validation + non-zero exit on unresolved-ref counts
description:
Surfaced during wyrd-kutx PR #343 review verification round (2026-05-23).
Two lower-priority items that aren't blocking the wyrd-kutx merge but
are worth addressing in a follow-up:

1. **Suffix charset validation on etymon-split children.** The CLI accepts
   any non-empty string as a split-suffix. If an operator writes
   `--into 'suffix=weir:foo|...'`, the resulting canonical form
   becomes `gear#weir:foo` and the ref becomes
   `old-english:gear#weir:foo`. The ref resolver's `split(":", 1)`
   happens to survive (lang=old-english, form=gear#weir:foo), but
   downstream naive parsers would break. Add a charset guard in
   `cli/lexicon/curate_gloss.py` (something like
   `re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9_-]+", suffix)`) and surface a
   `counts["invalid_suffix"]` in the applier for hand-edited JSONL
   bypasses.

2. **Exit-warning on unresolved-ref counts.** `apply_gloss_suppressions`
   and `apply_etymon_splits` surface `unresolved_etymon`,
   `unresolved_gloss`, `glosses_missing` counters via the markdown
   formatter, but the calling CLI command (`lexicon enrich --apply`)
   exits 0 regardless. An operator typo on a ref or gloss results in
   a silently-no-op event that the operator only notices if they read
   the markdown output. Either:
   - Make `lexicon enrich` exit 1 when any of the counts are non-zero,
   - Or add a `--strict` flag that triggers the error exit,
   - Or print a stderr warning ("X unresolved curation refs — review
     the markdown output above") so the operator can't miss it.

Both items are defense-in-depth / ergonomic improvements; the CLI's
existing happy-path is correct. Filed by code-reviewer (round 2) and
type-design-analyzer (round 2) on the PR review.

title: kenning: disentangle finn — Celtic *finn 'bright' vs OE personal-name Finn
description:
The etymon old-english:finn (id 5573) currently conflates three senses across two languages:

1. Celtic *finn 'bright, clear (water)' — cited by Joyce 1875 Irish Names vol1 for Finglas, Rosenallis, Finnihy (Goidelic). Etymologically Celtic, not OE; surfaces on this row because the canonical_form happens to match.
2. OE personal-name Finn — cited by Roberts 1914 Sussex for a -dene compound. Not currently captured as a gloss.
3. (Suppressed in wyrd-kutx) Modern-English 'fin' (fish-fin) — Wiktionary contamination, removed.

Clean fix requires:
- A Celtic etymon row for *finn 'bright/clear' (probably celtic:finn or per-Goidelic-language) carrying the Joyce citation
- A 'personal name' gloss added to the OE row (we don't currently have an add-gloss curation event — would need a new event type, or upstream link-personal-names work)
- Citation reassignment of Joyce 1875 from old-english:finn → celtic:finn (we don't have citation-reassign tooling yet either)

Filed during the wyrd-kutx walkthrough — see commit history around the audit batch for context.
notes:
Additional case surfaced during wyrd-kutx batch 2C: OE corn (id 250) has the same shape as finn:

- Real productive sense: 'corn, a grain or seed' (the generic-grain sense; cf. Cornard in Skeat 1913)
- Personal-name sense: cited by Mawer 1920 for Cornsay (Northumberland-Durham) — Mawer identifies 'Corn' as a personal name (genitive of strong form). Gemini extraction agrees: 'many English place-names in Corn- and their etymology is by no means clear'.

Same deferred-cleanup pattern: needs add-gloss to surface the personal-name as a distinct gloss, plus citation reassignment (Cornsay → personal-name child; Cornard → grain child).

Tracking under wyrd-wz82 rather than a new ticket — both cases need the same future tooling (add-gloss event, citation-reassign event).

title: kenning: merge tūn / tun / ton OE town-etymon fragmentation
description:
The OE 'town/enclosure/settlement' etymon exists in three separate rows in the live lexicon:

- old-english:tūn  (id 716)  — 8 citations, canonical-spelling form
- old-english:tun  (id 2274) — 24 citations, unmarked spelling (most-cited)
- old-english:ton  (id 1615) — 11 citations, post-vowel-shortening / modern-spelling form

These are the same etymon at different spelling-drift points and should roll up to a single canonical via merged_into_id curation events (D22). The normalize-ocr auto-pass didn't catch them — likely because the macron / no-macron drift falls outside its OCR-ligature heuristics.

Recommended action: pick tūn (or tun, the most-cited) as canonical and merge the other two via wyrd-2jhs etymon_curation events. After merge, all three surface forms surface in the variant pool weighted by attestation; the consensus rollup unifies the witness count.

Surfaced during the wyrd-kutx audit walkthrough — see commit a8e170b and the misattribution noted on OE tin (3987) where 'yard, grange' was incorrectly conflated with the town sense.
notes:
Resolved by auto-clustering during the wyrd-kutx enrichment passes (PR #343-345). Live DB shows tun (id 2274) and ton (id 1615) both merged_into_id → 716 (tūn, the canonical). No manual curation event needed.

The auto-clustering picked tūn (8 cits) as canonical rather than the ticket-recommended tun (24 cits) — likely an alphabetic / lemma-link heuristic. End state is correct: all 43 OE town citations roll up through tūn via the consensus view.

Shipped bundle (meanings.json) still reflects the pre-wyrd-kutx fragmented state; will be cleared on the next bundle re-emit (deferred per PR #347 commit notes).

title: OllamaClient: end-to-end smoke test verifying num_ctx+keep_alive against live Ollama
description:
**Out-of-scope follow-up from PR #327 wyrd-dyf8 review (pr-test-analyzer + error-handling-reviewer P3).**

PR #327 verifies the OllamaClient sends \`num_ctx\` (in options) and \`keep_alive\` (at payload top level) via mocked-request inspection. The mocked tests confirm the wyrd CLIENT sends the right shape, but don't verify that a real Ollama SERVER actually honors them (i.e., the loaded model's \`/api/ps\` reflects the requested context_length, and the model stays loaded past the default keep_alive).

**Acceptance**:
1. An integration-test marker (\`pytest.mark.live_ollama\`) that gates on \`WYRD_OLLAMA_URL\` being reachable.
2. Test that constructs an OllamaClient with num_ctx=8192, makes a chat_json request, then queries /api/ps and asserts the loaded model's \`context_length == 8192\`.
3. Test for keep_alive=-1: chat_json then sleep > 5 min, query /api/ps, assert the model is still loaded.

**Why P3**: PR #327's mocked tests already pin the client-side contract end-to-end. This is incremental confidence against an Ollama server behavior change, not regression coverage of wyrd code. Requires a live Ollama for CI which the repo doesn't currently have.

title: Integration test: surrogate input through staged-CLI file writer end-to-end
description:
**Out-of-scope follow-up from PR #309 wyrd-8wa4 review (pr-test-analyzer criticality 4/10).**

PR #309 added \`test_mine_toponym_mentions_sanitizes_surrogate_in_failure_message\` that exercises the FailedChunk-write contract end-to-end through \`mine_toponym_mentions\`, asserting the same \`json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')\` round-trip that the real CLI writer performs.

A true integration test would drive the staged CLI's actual file writer (\`mine_toponym_mentions_staged.py\`'s \`inprogress_sink.write(line_fn(...))\` + the atomic-write merge to \`out_path\`) with a mocked client emitting surrogate-bearing JSON, and assert the resulting JSONL files are well-formed utf-8.

**Why not done now**: \`tests/test_kenning_toponym_mention_tiered.py\` doesn't currently have infrastructure for running the chunk writer through a real \`tmp_path\` sink with mocked LLM responses. Building that fixture is a larger refactor than the wyrd-8wa4 surface justifies.

**Acceptance**: integration test in \`tests/test_kenning_toponym_mention_staged.py\` (or extend tiered) that:
1. Constructs a temp output dir
2. Drives the CLI with a mocked client returning surrogate-bearing JSON
3. Asserts the resulting per-source JSONL is valid utf-8 + the surrogate became U+FFFD in the persisted output
4. Asserts \`surrogates_sanitized\` counter is correctly surfaced in the summary line

**Why P3**: PR #309's in-band assertion (via \`mine_toponym_mentions\`) is already strong regression coverage. A live-file integration test is incremental confidence, not bug prevention.

title: Defense-in-depth: errors= on utf-8 file-open writes in mining CLIs
description:
**Out-of-scope follow-up from PR #309 wyrd-8wa4 review (error-handling-reviewer P3).**

Across the three mining CLIs (`mine_toponym_mentions.py`, `_tiered.py`, `_staged.py`) there are 8 \`open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8")\` sinks that write LLM-derived data without an \`errors=\` argument. The in-band sanitizer (PR #309) and FailedChunk.error sanitizer (also PR #309) jointly handle every known surrogate path, but a future code path that constructs a ToponymMention or FailedChunk bypassing these guards could re-introduce a wyrd-8wa4-style crash.

**Asymmetric trade-off**: Python's utf-8 encoder with \`errors="replace"\` substitutes ASCII \`?\` rather than U+FFFD, so the output quality between in-band sanitizer (clean U+FFFD) and file-open backstop (ugly \`?\`) would be uneven. The backstop is strictly better than a crash, but the asymmetry is a small operator-visible signal that something escaped the in-band guard.

**Acceptance**:
1. Add \`errors="replace"\` to the 8 file-open writes
2. Add a test (or fault-injection harness) that confirms a surrogate slipping past sanitization writes \`?\` rather than crashing
3. Document the asymmetry as intentional ("if you see \`?\` in the output, the in-band guard was bypassed somewhere")

**Why P3**: PR #309's in-band fix is sufficient for the known crash classes. This is hardening against hypothetical future regressions, not addressing a current bug.

description:
PR #286 (wyrd-jaur) closed the name-set drift for indexes and views but pr-test-analyzer round-0 review flagged two remaining body-shape drift classes:

## 1. Expression-index body drift (MEDIUM, criticality 6)

The schema has 4 COALESCE-padded unique indexes:
- idx_etymon_citation_unique
- idx_pn_toponym_dedup
- idx_toponym_unique
- idx_attestation_unique

These use sentinels like COALESCE(page, '') / COALESCE(date_year, 0). A migration that changes the sentinel (e.g. '' to ' ') would silently change uniqueness semantics — same shape of bug as wyrd-rrse (collation) — and the existing name-set parity test would NOT catch it.

Proposed: test_alembic_head_expression_index_bodies_pin_to_snapshot — for each of the 4 expression-unique indexes, snapshot the normalized sqlite_master.sql DDL into a hardcoded dict, assert byte-equality after whitespace normalization. Same brittleness profile as _EXPECTED_VIEWS (intentional pin).

## 2. View body drift (LOW/MEDIUM, criticality 5)

_EXPECTED_VIEWS pins view NAMES only. A migration that rewrites a view's SELECT body (changing projected columns or WHERE filter) would silently ship. For canonical-projection views consumed by downstream code, body drift is plausibly bug-worthy.

Proposed: test_alembic_head_view_bodies_match_snapshot — pull sqlite_master.sql for each view, normalize whitespace, compare to a hardcoded snapshot dict.

## Pointers

- tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py — existing wyrd-jaur parity tests
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/migrations/versions/0008_views.py — view definitions
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/migrations/versions/0001_sources.py through 0010 — expression-unique index definitions

## Acceptance

- Tests pass on current main (zero drift)
- Drift simulation: changing a COALESCE sentinel from '' to ' ' makes test_alembic_head_expression_index_bodies_pin_to_snapshot fail
- Drift simulation: changing a view's SELECT projection makes test_alembic_head_view_bodies_match_snapshot fail

## Followup of

wyrd-jaur (PR #286)

title: kenning: extend wyrd-hd28 parity to server_default, sqlite_where, expression-index, VIEW, UNIQUE constraints
description:
Round-0 pr-test-analyzer review of PR #284 flagged five additional MetaData ↔ alembic-head drift classes that wyrd-hd28's first three parity tests (structural, collation, ondelete, CHECK) do not catch. Same risk shape as the bugs that motivated wyrd-hd28 — adding canaries for these closes more of the silent-drift surface.

## Drift classes to cover

1. **server_default drift** (MEDIUM): MigrationContext.configure currently has compare_type=True but compare_server_default=False (default). Schema has ~15 server_default=text(...) declarations. Try enabling compare_server_default=True and see if the filter needs extension.

2. **sqlite_where (partial index) drift** (MEDIUM): Schema uses sqlite_where=text("is_canonical = 1") partial indexes. SA reflection of partial indexes is inconsistent. Direct DDL parity for index WHERE clauses.

3. **Expression-index drift** (MEDIUM): COALESCE-padded unique indexes (e.g., text("COALESCE(page, '')")). SA can't reflect these on SQLite — every parity run produces warnings. Need direct DDL comparison.

4. **VIEW drift** (LOW): Per tables.py docstring, views live only in migrations. compare_metadata ignores them entirely. Need separate VIEW DDL parity test.

5. **UNIQUE constraint vs unique-index normalization** (LOW): UniqueConstraint vs CREATE UNIQUE INDEX produce different reflection shapes that the current filter doesn't handle robustly.

Plus a P3 from test-coverage-reviewer:

6. **Helper-function unit tests for _filter_sqlite_reflection_artifacts**: The three filter branches (FK pairs, PK nullable, modify_type collation) are exercised incidentally via the live-schema integration test. If a future schema change stops producing one of the three diff shapes, the corresponding filter branch silently rots. Direct unit tests for each branch with hand-crafted diff lists would harden the helper.

## Pointers

- tests/test_kenning_lexicon.py — the parity test family added in PR #284
- wyrd/generators/kenning/lexicon/sql/tables.py — MetaData under test
- AGENT-REVIEWERS.md — alembic-migration-discipline-reviewer Rule 3

title: Add pytest-time package-boundary check for kenning/lexicon/
description:
AGENT-REVIEWERS.md lexicon-package-structure-reviewer enforces 'no DB I/O outside lexicon/' but only at PR-review time (via reviewer agents). There's no pytest-time test that asserts the boundary, so the rule has to be re-litigated by humans + agents on every PR forever. Per the agent-reviewers-mandatory bd memory (missed across 6 PRs once), this is a known gap.

Surfaced by the wyrd-5a11 retrospective pr-review-loop fanout (PR #252).

Proposal:
- tests/test_kenning_package_boundary.py
- AST-walks every wyrd/generators/kenning/*.py at the top level (excluding lexicon/, cli/, generators/, runtime/, era/, registers/, vectors/, jsonl/, bundle/ subpackages once they exist).
- Fails if any such file:
  * Contains 'import sqlite3' at top of file
  * Contains a 'CREATE TABLE' / 'CREATE INDEX' / 'CREATE VIEW' string literal
  * Imports LexiconDB from anywhere
- Skip-list keyword for legitimate exceptions (probably empty post-wyrd-xgd4 epic; possibly never).

Companion AST check: walk every cli/lexicon/*.py and assert no lexicon-DB-touching helpers DEFINED there (they should import from lexicon/ instead of redefining locally).

Defers to AFTER wyrd-5bvw / wyrd-7cg7 / wyrd-ifsx / wyrd-a83i / wyrd-0ay4 / wyrd-pggx / wyrd-1hgm ship — until those package extractions land, the boundary check would have a long skip-list of legitimately-out-of-place files. Cleanest to add the check ONCE the layout stabilizes.

title: Capture wyrd-g143 cli.py refactor lessons in AGENT-REVIEWERS.md
description:
wyrd-g143 (cli.py 10367 → 110 lines across 5 slices) surfaced several patterns worth documenting in wyrd/generators/kenning/AGENT-REVIEWERS.md alongside the wyrd-67fv lessons. Either as new reviewer rules or as practice notes.

Lessons to add:

1. **CROSS-MODULE HELPER IMPORTS** (slice 5). When a helper is shared between two extracted commands, the import graph must stay cycle-free. Pattern that works: each per-command module imports helpers from sibling modules (cli/lexicon/mine_llm.py imports _build_llm_client from cli/lexicon/review.py). Pattern that BREAKS: any submodule reaching into cli/__init__.py. Reviewer rule: flag any 'from wyrd.generators.kenning.cli import X' in a per-command module.

2. **TEST MONKEYPATCH ON CONSUMER MODULE, NOT SHIM** (slice 5). Tests that did monkeypatch.setattr(cli_mod, '_helper', stub) broke after extraction because the consumers had local-bound references to the original function. The fix is to patch the consumer module's namespace directly. Reviewer rule: when a test patches '_helper' on the cli shim, verify the actual consumer in the slice's diff resolves '_helper' through the patched path; otherwise the test silently runs against the unmocked original.

3. **AUTO-DETECTED RANGES CAN OVERFLOW INTO HELPERS** (slice 3 + slice 4). The 'next @lexicon.command anchor' heuristic for finding a command's end-line included orphan helpers from the NEXT command (diff-bundle grabbed _append_remove_event; classify-stratum grabbed set-stratum helpers). Practice: after auto-detecting ranges, scan each block for trailing 'def _' definitions and decide if they belong to the preceding command, the following command, or a shared utils.

4. **LAMBDA ASSIGNMENTS TRIGGER E731** (slice 5). ruff config rejects '_stub = lambda x: ...'. Use 'def _stub(x): return ...' instead. Reviewer rule: any '_stub = lambda' in a test fixture is an E731 latent.

5. **PER-COMMAND CONSTANTS GO WITH THE COMMAND** (slice 5). _RANDO_SOURCE was a module-level constant in cli.py used only by lexicon-build. Per-module extraction moved it next to build.py, not cli/utils.py. Pattern: shared-by-N constants → cli/utils.py; single-consumer constants → the consumer's module.

6. **NESTED SUB-GROUPS GO IN THEIR OWN SUBPACKAGES** (slice 2 browse + slice 5 synsets). Same pattern as the parent: __init__.py owns the @click.group def + add_to hook + per-sub-command add_to() calls; sub-command modules each expose add_to(parent=<group>). Reviewer rule: a NEW @click.group in a per-command module body is a structural error — promote to a subpackage.

Recommend a doc-only PR adding these to AGENT-REVIEWERS.md (either as new reviewer rules under explicit headings or as practice notes under the existing pre-push-extraction-sweep section).

title: Tier-filtered generation: operator restricts weight pool to UNIVERSAL / IE-CONVENTIONAL / IDENTITY-MARKING subsets
description:

- For non-IE worldbuilding settings (Mesoamerican fantasy, West-African mythology, sci-fi alien cultures), the IE-CONVENTIONAL weights actively harm the output — they encode English-speaker register conventions that don't transfer

title: Phonotactic-legality post-generation filter (Ćwiek 2022 phonotactic-failure constraint)
description:
Implement a phonotactic-legality post-filter for the generator output. Ćwiek 2022 ('The bouba/kiki effect is robust across cultures and writing systems') established that sound-symbolic effects FAIL when stimuli violate the target language's phonotactic rules. Generated names like 'Tkrxv-' overshoot — they pass wyrd's scorer but no English speaker would judge them as place-name-shaped.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- Per wyrd-kz2b.17 synthesis: Ćwiek 2022 found bouba-kiki replication FAILS when stimuli violate target phonotactics (Syuba: /kh/ illegal word-medially; /u/ illegal word-final in disyllables → 11/24 effect failure rate)
- Generated names that violate English phonotactics will rate as 'gibberish-shaped' by human raters in wyrd-kz2b.2
- Without this filter, Paper A's empirical evaluation has a confound: generator-output phonotactic violations vs. genuine register-effect failures

WHAT IT DOES:
- Takes a generated name (string of phonemes/graphemes)
- Returns: (is_phonotactically_legal, list_of_violations) tuple
- Violations include: illegal onset clusters, illegal coda clusters, illegal vowel sequences, illegal syllable structures
- English-targeted in v1; multi-language schema extensible

IMPLEMENTATION OPTIONS:
1. RULE-BASED (preferred — methodologically aligned with wyrd):
   - Encode English phonotactic constraints from established phonology (Hammond 1999 'The Phonology of English'; Hayes 2004 'Phonotactic Constraints')
   - Per-language constraints in YAML (similar to register_effects.yaml shape)
   - Validator function checks each generated name against the constraint set
2. STATISTICAL (alternative):
   - Train a small n-gram model on the EPNS corpus
   - Reject names with phoneme-sequence probabilities below threshold
   - Less interpretable but cheaper

RECOMMENDATION: rule-based for v1 (matches wyrd's audit-trail principle); statistical as a complementary backup.

PIPELINE INTEGRATION:
- Hook into generator output BEFORE returning to caller
- Generator can reject + retry, or return with phonotactic-violation flag
- Adjustable: 'strict' mode (only legal names returned) vs 'permissive' (legal + flagged-violations returned)

ALSO RELEVANT to Paper B (era-staged etymology):
- Phonotactic constraints DIFFER across eras (Old English allowed certain coda clusters that Modern English doesn't)
- Era-specific phonotactic-legality is a valid output of the era-staged transformation engine
- Coordinate with wyrd-v2gm.3.x adaptation templates

WHAT GOES INTO REGISTERS.md / Paper D:
- Document the phonotactic-legality filter as a precondition for the sound-symbolic effect
- Cite Ćwiek 2022 + Styles & Gawne 2017 (bouba-kiki failures track phonotactic illegality)

CITES:
- Ćwiek et al. (2022). The bouba/kiki effect is robust across cultures and writing systems. Phil Trans R Soc B.
- Styles & Gawne (2017). When does maluma/takete fail? i-Perception.
- Hammond (1999). The Phonology of English. Oxford UP.
- Hayes (2004). Phonotactic Constraints.

title: Audit-trail metadata exporter: per-name provenance bundle output
description:
Currently the wyrd generator returns scored names; for Paper A's central claim ('every generated name carries an audit trail through a three-tier UNIVERSAL / IE-CONVENTIONAL / IDENTITY-MARKING taxonomy') to be LOAD-BEARING, the output needs to actually emit the provenance bundle.

WHY THIS MATTERS:
- Paper A's headline contribution claim is that the generation pipeline is audit-traceable
- Reviewers will (correctly) ask: 'show me an example of an audit trail.' If the system only emits 'York', the claim is hand-waving. If it emits 'York + provenance bundle showing which weights contributed and which scholarship-trace tier each weight is in', the claim is concrete.
- This is the ONE feature that distinguishes wyrd architecturally from ConlangCrafter and IASC. Make it ergonomically demonstrable.

THE PROVENANCE BUNDLE per generated name:
```json
{
  "name": "Eoforwic",
  "decomposition": [
    {"morpheme": "Eofor", "position": "pre", "lemma_ref": "old-english:eofor:boar"},
    {"morpheme": "wic", "position": "post", "lemma_ref": "old-english:wic:settlement"}
  ],
  "score_breakdown": {
    "phon_score": 0.62,
    "sem_score": 0.45,
    "pos_score": 0.30,
    "baseline_score": 0.55,
    "aggregate_score": 0.47
  },
  "register_effects_composed": ["grim", "harsh"],
  "weights_consulted": [
    {"register": "harsh", "feature": "stop_vs_continuant", "value": 0.6, "tier": "UNIVERSAL", "citation": "Whissell 1999; Fort 2015"},
    {"register": "harsh", "feature": "cluster_density", "value": 0.6, "tier": "IE-CONVENTIONAL", "citation": "Mooshammer 2024"},
    ...
  ],
  "era": "old-english",
  "culture": "old-english",
  "seed": 42,
  "wyrd_version": "0.1.0"
}
```

IMPLEMENTATION:
- Extend the generator's output dataclass to include a `provenance` field
- During scoring, each weight access logs (register, feature, value, tier, citation) to a thread-local accumulator
- After scoring completes, accumulator is bundled into the provenance field
- Provenance is OPTIONAL via a flag; off by default for performance, on for audit/paper-demonstration use cases

title: Adversarial language-identity scrubber for empirical three-tier taxonomy validation
description:
Implement the adversarial language-identity scrubbing method (per Sharma et al. 2025, arXiv:2512.12245) as an empirical validation step for wyrd's three-tier UNIVERSAL / IE-CONVENTIONAL / IDENTITY-MARKING audit taxonomy.

WHY: the three-tier taxonomy is currently a LITERATURE-BASED assignment (we tag weights as UNIVERSAL because Blasi 2016 says so, etc.). The Sharma 2025 adversarial method converts this into an EMPIRICALLY-TESTABLE property — a stronger claim that's actually falsifiable.

THE TEST:
- Train a discriminator network on (phoneme features → language identity)
- Train a separator that maximizes phoneme→semantic-category prediction while MINIMIZING discriminator success
- Effects that SURVIVE adversarial scrubbing are language-identity-independent (UNIVERSAL)
- Effects that DISAPPEAR after scrubbing are language-conventional (IE-CONVENTIONAL)
- Effects that CORRELATE with language identity are IDENTITY-MARKING

WHAT IT TESTS for wyrd specifically:
- Per-weight tier verification: does the literature-assigned tier (in REGISTERS.md) match the empirical-survival tier?
- Discrepancies = research-publishable findings ('Weight X assigned UNIVERSAL by Blasi 2016 cite but adversarial-survival shows IE-CONVENTIONAL behavior — suggests catalog refinement')

IMPLEMENTATION:
- Small PyTorch network (few hundred lines): encoder + label predictor + adversarial discriminator with gradient reversal
- Input: bag-of-phoneme features per lemma + (semantic_category, language_identity) pairs
- Training: gradient-reverse the language-identity branch
- Evaluation: per-weight Δaccuracy under language-identity scrubbing
- Output: a CSV mapping (weight, literature-tier, empirical-survival-tier, discrepancy-flag) per register-effect feature

DATA:
- 27-language adjective dataset from Sharma 2025 (check if released; otherwise contact authors)
- wyrd's own multi-language corpus once wyrd-ialp expansion lands
- Multi-language coverage REQUIRED — single-language adversarial test is meaningless

PROVIDES:
- Empirical foundation for Paper D's three-tier claim
- Methodological contribution distinguishable from the Sharma 2025 paper (we apply the method to a generative-system audit, not just a typological analysis)
- Catalog-refinement signal for REGISTERS.md

DEPENDS ON:
- wyrd-ialp wave-2 corpus expansion (multi-language data)
- Existing PhonologicalVector schema

CITES:
- Sharma et al. 2025 (arXiv:2512.12245) for the method
- Blasi 2016 PNAS for the underlying cross-cultural-universal claim being validated

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Replicating Sharma 2025's adjective-size-domain study (different data)
- Cross-modal extensions (visual/auditory bias auditing)

title: Zipf cross-validation: corpus vs generator output rank-frequency analysis
description:
Empirically validate the implicit-Zipf-by-construction claim that wyrd preserves the source-corpus morpheme-frequency distribution. Two phases:

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
PHASE 1: QUICK SANITY CHECK (~1-2 hours, immediate)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

Goal: confirm the implicit-Zipf-by-construction claim is real before Paper A drafting depends on it.

Steps:
1. Extract terminal-position morpheme frequency from current EPNS-mined corpus (wyrd-srd2 output to date)
   - Top-20 morphemes by rank
   - Expected: '-ton' (OE *tūn*) and its derivatives ('-ington', '-tone', '-don') dominate ranks 1-5
   - Compute Zipf α via MLE (approximate; full rigor in Phase 2)
2. Generate a sample of 1000 names using wyrd's current generator at base_w=1.0, default register settings
3. Extract terminal-position morpheme frequency from generator output
4. Compare distributions visually (log-log rank-frequency plot, corpus vs generator)
5. Spot-check that top-5 ranked morphemes match between corpus and generator

PASS CRITERIA: corpus's top-5 terminal morphemes appear in generator's top-10, with overlapping rank positions. Distribution shapes visually similar on log-log.

FAIL CRITERIA: if generator's distribution is markedly different from corpus, that's a bug in the empirical-baseline axis. Investigate before drafting Paper A's Zipf claim.

OUTPUT: a single notebook + plot + one-paragraph note in ~/.wyrd/papers/2026-XX-XX_zipf_sanity_check.md.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
PHASE 2: RIGOROUS CROSS-VALIDATION (after Phase 1 passes, part of wyrd-kz2b.3)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

Required for Paper A's empirical evaluation. Operationalized in wyrd-kz2b.3.

Analyses:
- MLE α estimation with bootstrap confidence intervals (per Piantadosi 2014)
- Multi-metric Zipf (rank-frequency + word-distance + length distributions, per Manaris 2006)
- base_w sweep: α-vs-base_w degradation curve from 0.0 to 1.0
- Per-tier breakdown (UNIVERSAL / IE-CONVENTIONAL / IDENTITY-MARKING) — does α vary by tier?
- Statistical significance tests: generator output ≠ random baseline AND ≈ attested corpus

PHASE 2 BLOCKED ON: Paper A's evaluation harness scaffolding (wyrd-kz2b.3). Phase 1 is unblocked and should ship first.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
WHY THIS MATTERS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

Phase 1 PASS turns the implicit-Zipf claim from 'we think this is true' to 'we've shown it empirically.' It validates a NUMBERED contribution in Paper A.

Phase 1 ALSO makes a great 1-paragraph blog post / Twitter thread for preprint marketing later: 'Open-source procedural place-name generator preserves the rank-frequency distribution of its training corpus by construction — here's the plot.' Goes viral risk-free.

- wyrd-kz2b.5 — Zipf 1949 + Piantadosi 2014 + Manaris 2006 BibTeX

title: Read + extract ideas: Zipf methodology for place-name analysis (Manaris, Piantadosi)
description:
Two Zipf-methodology papers that gate the Zipf-of-place-names contribution in Paper A.

PAPERS:

1. **Manaris et al. 2006 — 'Investigating Esperanto's Statistical Proportions Relative to other Languages using Neural Networks and Zipf's Law'**
   - NOT on arXiv. Venues: search semantic scholar / academia.edu / wli-zipf.upc.edu.
   - Authors: Bill Manaris, ...
   - Method: 283 books in 6 languages (English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Esperanto), Zipf-based metrics (word/word-distance/bigram/trigram/word-length distributions), ANN classification 86-98% accurate.
   - Key finding: 'Esperanto's statistical proportions are similar to those of other languages.'

2. **Piantadosi 2014 — 'Zipf's word frequency law in natural language: A critical review and future directions'**
   - Venue: Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, Vol. 21, 2014.
   - DOI: 10.3758/s13423-014-0585-6
   - PubMed: PMID 24664880
   - Not on arXiv; available via Springer / PubMed.
   - 817+ citations per SciSpace as of 2026; the modern critical review of Zipf.

WHAT TO EXTRACT per paper:

1. **Manaris** — methodology for applying Zipf to constructed/non-natural languages. The precedent for the Zipf-of-place-names move. Critically: their methodology includes multiple Zipf-based metrics (not just word frequency — also word distance, bigram, trigram, word length) — Paper A can adopt this multi-metric approach for richer statistical baseline comparison than Diamond Genlangs's single-correlation-r approach.

2. **Piantadosi** — modern critical review of Zipf. Critical for METHODOLOGICAL RIGOR. Tells us:
   - Why Pearson correlation is insufficient (need MLE of α)
   - What confidence-interval methods to use
   - What Zipf-deviations are meaningful (Piantadosi argues there's complex structure ABOVE Zipf's law)
   - How to avoid the methodological pitfalls Diamond Genlangs falls into

WHY MEDIUM URGENCY (not HIGH):
- Only read IF Paper A includes Zipf-of-place-names analysis (which it should per wyrd-kz2b.17 synthesis finding #4 — uncontested ground)
- If skipping Zipf entirely, these can be deferred to later or skipped
- If pursuing Zipf, BOTH are required reading before the wyrd-kz2b.3 baseline-comparison harness implementation

WHAT THE RIGOROUS ZIPF-OF-PLACE-NAMES CONTRIBUTION LOOKS LIKE:
- Compare attested EPNS-derived place names (treated as a corpus) against generated place names (varied register settings) AND a baseline (random morpheme combinations)
- Multi-metric Zipf: rank-frequency + word-distance distribution + length distribution (per Manaris)
- MLE-based α estimation with confidence intervals (per Piantadosi)
- Statistical significance test that generated names ≠ random baseline + ≈ attested names
- Per-tier (UNIVERSAL/IE-CONVENTIONAL/IDENTITY-MARKING) breakdown: do the tier-stratified results vary?

This would be a substantively stronger Zipf result than any existing genlang-Zipf paper.

OUTPUT:
- Per-paper notes at ~/.wyrd/papers/manaris_2006_esperanto_zipf.md and ~/.wyrd/papers/piantadosi_2014_zipf_review.md
- Updated methodology section in wyrd-kz2b.3 (baseline-comparison harness)
- Cross-reference back to Diamond Genlangs as the weak-statistics predecessor

ESTIMATED TIME: ~4-5 hours total.

CITATION ETHICS: if Paper A claims to do Zipf-of-place-names rigorously, the Piantadosi citation is essential (acknowledges modern methodological standards) and Manaris is essential (acknowledges the conlang-Zipf precedent).
notes:
Completed 2026-05-19 via agent pass. Notes at ~/.wyrd/papers/.

KEY FINDINGS:
1. Diamond Genlangs (.17) used statistically inadequate methodology — Pearson-r on log-log scatter is artifact-laden per Piantadosi 2014. The conlang-Zipf literature is ~10 years behind cognitive science methodologically.
2. THIRD OVER-CLAIM CAUGHT: wyrd's "implicit Zipf preservation by construction" claim needs softening. Asymptotic yes; finite-sample only approximate; structure-above-Zipf not preserved by i.i.d. sampling.
3. Adopt Manaris 5-metric scaffold (word + word-distance + bigram + trigram + word-length) — joint 10-D fingerprint.
4. Layer Clauset-Shalizi-Newman 2009 on Piantadosi's binomial-split (the modern power-law gold standard neither paper cites).
5. Adopt "near-Zipfian, not Zipfian" framing.

Closing this ticket; cascaded actions to .27, .3, .7, .5.

title: Follow-on reading from wyrd-kz2b.17: citations from ConlangCrafter / IASC / Genlangs worth chasing
description:
The three LLM-conlang papers reviewed in wyrd-kz2b.17 cite ~15 additional works. This ticket ranks the unread ones by urgency for the wyrd publication path, with justification per paper. Read in priority order; don't read all of them.

Per-paper notes deposited in ~/.wyrd/papers/ once read, following the same template as the .17 cache.

HIGH URGENCY — read before Paper A / Paper B preprints
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

1. **Kallini et al. 2024 — 'Impossible languages'**
   Cited by both ConlangCrafter AND IASC. Likely defines what makes a generated language plausible vs implausible (e.g. typological-feature combinations that don't occur in natural language). DIRECTLY relevant to Paper A's evaluation: 'does our generated output stay within plausible typological space?' is exactly the question Kallini answers.
   
   Likely arXiv: search 'Kallini 2024 impossible languages' on arXiv
   Find via ConlangCrafter's reference list (in arXiv:2508.06094 PDF)
   
   READ FOR: Paper A evaluation methodology; Paper A related work; potential evaluation-metric to borrow.

2. **Blevins 2004 — 'Evolutionary Phonology' (book)**
   IASC cites this as a foundational historical-phonology framework. Paper B (through-time etymology) MUST engage with Blevins — she's the canonical reference for explaining WHY certain sound changes happen and which are natural. Without her framework, Paper B can be flagged by reviewers as 'where's the theoretical grounding?'
   
   Source: Cambridge UP book, not arXiv. Library / interlibrary loan / used copy.
   
   READ FOR: Paper B theoretical foundation; verification that our forward-projection rules align with Blevins's typology of natural sound changes.

3. **Beguš et al. 2025 — 'LLM metalinguistic abilities'**
   Cited by both ConlangCrafter and IASC. Beguš is the senior author of ConlangCrafter — and our highest-priority Paper A co-author candidate (wyrd-x8r2.7.3). Reading his most recent work BEFORE the cold-email outreach lets the email cite his work specifically + sounds informed.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
MEDIUM URGENCY — read IF doing Zipf-of-place-names analysis
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

4. **Manaris et al. 2006 — 'Investigating Esperanto's statistical proportions relative to other languages using neural networks and Zipf's Law'**
   Cited by Diamond Genlangs. THE precedent for applying Zipf's law to constructed languages. If Paper A includes Zipf-of-place-names analysis (which is uncontested ground per wyrd-kz2b.17 synthesis finding #4), this is the methodological predecessor to cite + position against.
   
   Source: search 'Manaris 2006 Esperanto Zipf' — likely a non-arXiv venue.
   
   READ FOR: Paper A's Zipf-of-place-names methodology; tells us what kind of statistical sophistication to apply (we want to do better than Diamond Genlangs which only reports correlation r).

5. **Piantadosi 2014 — 'Zipf's word frequency law in natural language: A critical review and future directions'**
   Cited by Diamond Genlangs. Modern critical review of Zipf's law applications + their pitfalls. Required reading IF Paper A uses Zipf analysis; tells us where the methodological gotchas are (Pearson r is insufficient; need MLE, confidence intervals, alpha exponent, etc.).
   
   Likely arXiv (Piantadosi posts regularly): search 'Piantadosi 2014 Zipf review'.
   
   READ FOR: Paper A Zipf analysis rigor; immunize against reviewer 'is your Zipf analysis sound?' pushback.

6. **PhonologyBench (Suvarna et al. 2024)**
   Cited by IASC. Likely a benchmark suite for evaluating LLM phonological knowledge. Useful as a comparison point: 'PhonologyBench scores LLMs on phonology comprehension; our system instead produces phonology generatively with audit trail.'
   
   Find on arXiv 2024.
   
   READ FOR: Paper A related work; useful contrast for the LLM-as-authority vs rule-as-authority framing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
LOW URGENCY — reference-only, do not pre-read
═══════════════════════════════════════════════

7. **WALS (Dryer & Haspelmath 2013)** — World Atlas of Language Structures. Database, not paper. Used by ConlangCrafter for typological feature classification. Cite as reference; no reading required.

WHO: Shigeto Kawahara, Professor at Keio University Institute of Cultural and Linguistic Studies. Founded Pokémonastics — the applied-phonaesthetics subfield studying sound-symbolic patterns in Pokémon character names. Most-cited applied-phonaesthetics researcher in our adjacency.

WHY WYRD CARES: REGISTERS.md's universal-tier phonaesthetic claims (Ohala 1994, Whissell 1999, Fort 2015, Blasi 2016) sit directly in Kawahara's intellectual neighborhood. He's done multi-paper work showing sound-symbolic patterns are robust signals; wyrd's contribution is the GENERATIVE-side complement (his work is analytical).

LEVERAGE TYPES (ranked by ask-difficulty):
- AMPLIFY (easiest) — share work on Twitter, blog, conference talks
- CITE — cite wyrd in his own future Pokémonastics papers
- ENDORSE — arXiv endorsement for cs.CL (he should already have access)
- ADVISE — feedback on Paper D draft, methodology consultation
- CO-AUTHOR (hardest) — co-author Paper D or the manifesto

KEY PAPERS TO ENGAGE WITH:
- arXiv:2301.01948 (Random forests + Pokémon evolution, 2023)
- arXiv:2512.12245 (Adversarial cross-family probing, Dec 2025)
- His Google Scholar profile likely has ~10+ relevant non-arXiv papers (linguistics journals)

APPROACH STRATEGY:
1. Read his Pokémonastics body of work (pending — wyrd-kz2b.18)
2. After Paper D is on arXiv: cold email with subject line 'Wyrd: applied phonaesthetics for procedural naming — extension of your Pokémonastics framework'
3. Open with: 'Your Pokémonastics work showed sound-symbolic patterns are robust ENOUGH to support classification of attested names; we extend this to generative naming with a citation-bearing audit trail. Would value your feedback on Paper D's evaluation methodology.'
4. Attach Paper D preprint or REGISTERS.md
5. Asks (escalate gently): feedback → cite → arXiv endorsement → advisory → co-author

EMAIL: kawahara [at] icl.keio.ac.jp (verify on his Keio page before contact)

STATUS: not_contacted

OUTREACH AFTER: preprint #3+ on arXiv (Paper D ideally; gives him something concrete + flattering to engage with)
notes:
COLD-EMAIL CV CONTEXT UPDATE 2026-05-19:

Kawahara is in linguistics; will NOT recognize PCGen / PFSRD / OpenForge by name. But the STRUCTURAL signal still works: "20-year open-source-systems architect" is a credible-entry-into-academia signal that "indie developer" is not.

REVISED COLD-EMAIL OPENING (replaces earlier draft, foregrounds CV signal):

> "Dear Professor Kawahara,
>
> I am an open-source-systems architect with two decades of experience building citation-bearing reference systems and procedural-generation tools for tabletop role-playing and worldbuilding communities (PCGen open-source character builder, est. 2002; the Pathfinder open-content reference document; OpenForge open-source 3D-printable terrain system with Patreon-supported community at scale). Wyrd is the formalization of this two-decade arc, applied to computational onomastics — a citation-bearing rule-based generative naming system grounded in the phonaesthetic literature, with a three-tier UNIVERSAL / IE-CONVENTIONAL / IDENTITY-MARKING audit taxonomy.
>
> Your 2021 Frontiers paper with Godoy and Kumagai contains an observation I have been thinking about: that English speakers can infer Pokémon types from sound symbolism, but 'none of the sound symbolic effects are visible in the existing English Pokémon names.' Section 4 acknowledges this gap but does not resolve it — the analytical-only framework cannot.
>
> Wyrd is the engineering response. [continue with prior draft]"

KEY CHANGE: the opening paragraph establishes the AUTHORITY before delivering the killer quote + ask. Kawahara reading 'open-source-systems architect with two decades of experience' positions Devon as a peer to engage seriously, not as a hobbyist with an unconventional CV.

DON'T NAME-DROP — DON'T expect recognition. The phrasing is "as a CV signal" not "as a famous project list."

Your three-tier UNIVERSAL/IE-CONVENTIONAL/IDENTITY-MARKING taxonomy IS a critical-theoretic move applied to generative systems. Engage with this paper as the closest critical-theory parallel.

title: Read + extract ideas: neural diachronic modeling (Letters From the Past, Deep Sound Change, Cognate Transformer)
description:
Read the three neural-diachronic competitor papers for Paper B. Extract: methodology differences, ways to differentiate the rule-based scholarship-traced approach.

PAPERS:
- arXiv:2205.08256 — Letters From the Past: Modeling Historical Sound Change Through Diachronic Character Embeddings
- arXiv:2011.05463 — Deep Sound Change: Deep and Iterative Learning, CNNs, and Language Change
- arXiv:2310.07487 — Cognate Transformer for Automated Phonological Reconstruction and Cognate Reflex Prediction

WHAT TO EXTRACT per paper:

1. METHODOLOGY: What's their input? What's their output? What's the learning approach (PPMI embeddings vs GAN vs Transformer)? Catalog the methodological-lane distinctions.
2. EVALUATION DATA: What corpora do they use? (Danish historical texts for Letters From the Past; cognate sets for Cognate Transformer.) Your Paper B can use English-historical attested-form pairs (Ekwall River Names, Briggs PN attestation chains) as a complementary evaluation corpus.
3. CITATION CHAINS: What historical-linguistics literature do they cite? Reuse their bibliographies as source-finder for your own historical-phonology citations.
4. WHAT THEY DON'T DO: None generate forward-projected names from proto-forms via cited sound-change rules. None target place names specifically. None provide audit trails per transformation step. Each gap is a contribution-claim for your Paper B.

CRITICAL DISTINCTION: Cognate Transformer reconstructs BACKWARD from observed cognates to proto-form. Your Paper B projects FORWARD from proto-form to modern surface forms. These are inverse operations and complementary; cite Cognate Transformer favorably as 'the inverse-direction analog.'

OUTPUT: notes file with methodological-lane diagram showing where rule-based scholarship-traced sits vs neural embedding/GAN/Transformer approaches.

ESTIMATED TIME: ~3-4 hours.

OUTPUT BLOCKS: Paper B (wyrd-kz2b.10).

title: JOSS (Journal of Open Source Software) paper for the wyrd codebase
description:
JOSS submission — a peer-reviewed, low-effort publication specifically for research software. Provides an EXTRA publication in the stack at very low effort, AND boosts the credibility of the open-source code as a research artifact.

WHY JOSS:
- Peer-reviewed venue (real DOI, real citation)
- Lightweight: ~2-page paper describing what the software does + what's reproducible
- Reviewers focus on code quality + documentation, NOT novelty — the bar is 'is this software useful and well-documented enough that other researchers could use it?'
- Free to submit
- ~2-month review cycle
- Specifically welcomes indie / non-affiliated researchers

PAPER SHAPE (~2 pages):
- Summary: what wyrd does (citation-bearing procedural-name generation with scholarly grounding)
- Statement of Need: why this exists; the unclaimed methodological territory
- Architecture: brief overview (full details in arXiv preprint wyrd-kz2b.1)
- Reproducibility: minimum-viable example + how to verify it works
- Acknowledgments + funding (if any)

REVIEWER CHECKS (built into JOSS process):
- The software installs cleanly per README
- Tests run + pass
- Documentation is sufficient
- The paper accurately describes the software
- The repository has a LICENSE + ongoing maintenance

DEPENDS ON: wyrd-kz2b.15 (repo polish: LICENSE + Zenodo + CITATION.cff + README hardening). The repo must be in good shape for JOSS reviewers.

CROSS-CITATION WITH OTHER PAPERS:
- wyrd-kz2b.1 (arXiv preprint): the architectural reference; JOSS paper says 'see X for the full methodology'
- wyrd-kz2b.6 (JOHD data paper): JOSS paper is for the SOFTWARE; JOHD for the DATA. Both can cite each other.
- wyrd-kz2b.7 (Paper A, ICCC): JOSS paper provides the citable software DOI that ICCC paper references

OUTPUT: JOSS publication + DOI; one more peer-reviewed paper added to the stack at ~1-2 weeks of writing effort.

VENUE: Journal of Open Source Software (https://joss.theoj.org/). Submit via the JOSS website. Accepts immediately if code + docs are ready; rejects only if standards aren't met (rare for well-prepared submissions).
notes:
AUTHOR-CV FRAMING UPDATE 2026-05-19:

JOSS readers are open-source-research-software people. PCGen and OpenForge may have name recognition in this audience (CS-adjacent, OSS-aware community). At minimum, the structural signal (20-year OSS-architecture track record) is highly credible in this venue.

USE FULL MASTER AUTHOR BIO including project names — JOSS values demonstrated OSS-maintainer experience explicitly.

> "Devon Jones is the founder of 521 Studios and an open-source-systems architect with two decades of experience in community-grounded computational tooling for tabletop role-playing games and worldbuilding. He is the architect of PCGen (open-source Pathfinder character builder, est. 2002), author of the Pathfinder Open Reference Document, and founder of OpenForge (open-source 3D-printable tabletop terrain system, with thousands of contributors and Patreon patrons). Wyrd is the formalization of this two-decade arc."

This is exactly the bio that JOSS reviewers want to see. Their concern is "will this person maintain the software long-term" — the bio answers that with concrete evidence.

title: Repo polish for academic citability: LICENSE + Zenodo + CITATION.cff + README hardening
description:
One-time repo polish to make wyrd a citable academic artifact. Low effort (few hours), high leverage — gates the JOSS submission AND provides DOIs that every subsequent paper cites.

REQUIRED STEPS:

1. Verify LICENSE file in repo root.
   - Should be MIT or Apache 2.0 (standard academic-friendly software licenses)
   - This is the CODE license — separate from CC-BY-SA which is the PAPER license
   - If missing or non-academic-friendly (GPL is fine for code but adds friction for academic uptake), commit a proper LICENSE file

2. Create CITATION.cff in repo root.
   - YAML format; specified by https://citation-file-format.github.io/
   - GitHub natively reads it; shows a 'Cite this repository' button in the right sidebar
   - Includes: title, author(s), URL, ORCID, version, date-released
   - First version uses 'preprint pending' for the citation reference; updated once arXiv preprint is up

3. Set up GitHub ↔ Zenodo integration.
   - Sign up at https://zenodo.org with a GitHub account (NOT institutional email; the GitHub account is the auth)
   - GitHub: Settings → Integrations → Zenodo. Flag the wyrd repo as tracked.
   - From now on, every GitHub Release auto-creates a Zenodo deposit with its own DOI
   - The 'concept DOI' (always points to latest) + version DOIs (each pinned to a specific release) are both auto-generated
   - Free; ~10 min setup

4. Tag first release as v0.1.0 to trigger first Zenodo deposit.
   - Confirms the integration works end-to-end
   - Use semantic versioning: v0.X.Y for pre-1.0, v1.0.0 when API-stable
   - First release notes summarize: 'Initial public-citable release of the wyrd computational onomastics framework. Includes vector-driven generation (wyrd-ecjp), scholarly-grounded registers (wyrd-2166), empirical priors mining pipeline (wyrd-srd2). Companion preprint pending.'

5. README hardening.
   - Minimum-viable example: 'pip install ...' or equivalent + a 5-line example showing the generator producing a name
   - Architecture diagram OR link to the arXiv preprint (wyrd-kz2b.1)
   - Citation block at the top OR bottom: 'If you use wyrd in research, please cite: <Zenodo DOI> + <arXiv preprint when posted>'
   - Link to REGISTERS.md for the methodology grounding (so academic readers find it from the repo entry point)
   - Link to documentation if there is any; otherwise inline key concepts

OUTPUT:
- wyrd repo has DOI; every release future-cite-able
- Academic readers landing on the repo find the methodology trail
- JOSS submission ticket is unblocked

DEPENDS ON: nothing. Can start immediately.

BLOCKS: JOSS submission (wyrd-kz2b.16); enables citation from all subsequent papers.

title: arXiv preprint-blanket strategy: cadence, citation discipline, license
description:
Strategic-context ticket capturing the publication strategy decided 2026-05-19. Not a single writing task; a meta-ticket that defines the rhythm.

STRATEGY: preprint-blanket-first, peer-review-curated-subset-after. arXiv every substantive milestone; route a curated subset (~3-5) through peer review for credibility anchoring.

CADENCE:
- Target ~1 preprint per 2-4 weeks at maintained build pace
- ~12 preprints over 18-24 months
- Each preprint = a substantive milestone with a clean standalone contribution
- 'Substantive milestone' filter: a new architectural layer / methodology / domain implementation. NOT every commit or bugfix.

ORDERING (sequence-of-operations):
1. arXiv preprint #1 (framing — wyrd-kz2b.1) — establishes architectural reference. POST FIRST.
2. Paper D (registers — wyrd-kz2b.12) — independent, already-written-content, ready fast. ~Month 1-2.
3. JOHD data paper (wyrd-kz2b.6) — once corpus stable + Briggs ingest done. ~Month 2-4.
4. Paper A (generation — wyrd-kz2b.7) — once ecjp.5 lands. ~Month 3-4. ICCC 2027 submission target.
5. Paper B + Paper C (etymology + cross-language) — after v2gm.3.x lands. ~Month 4-6, parallel drafting.
6. Manifesto paper (wyrd-x8r2.1) — after 4 exemplars on arXiv. ~Month 12-18.
7. Domain papers (geology, climate, economics, cultural-geography — wyrd-x8r2.2-.5) — one per quarter once domains start. Year 2+.

LICENSE: CC-BY-SA 4.0 by default. Aligns with Wikipedia (CC-BY-SA), keeps the methodology corpus growing as commons, prevents proprietary absorption without share-back. Switch to CC-BY only when a specific venue (JOHD, JOSS, PLOS, Frontiers, Nature OA) requires it; arXiv preprint and venue version can have different licenses — common.

CITATION DISCIPLINE:
- Every new preprint cites prior wyrd-* preprints by arXiv ID
- Reference list balance: aim for ≤25% self-cites, ≥75% external (mitigation against citation-cartel-flag)
- Each preprint must be a node in the broader research graph, not an island

QUALITY GUARDRAILS:
- Each preprint stands alone as a substantive contribution. Salami-slicing inoculation: each paper explicitly states scope + what's left to sibling papers / future work.
- v2/v3 revisions used for corrections/extensions of existing preprints; new preprints used for new contributions.
- arXiv moderation passes when paper is competently written; indie-affiliation explicit is fine ('521 Studios' or 'Independent Researcher').

ACADEMIC CO-AUTHOR OUTREACH:
- Begin cold-emailing relevant academics AFTER ~3-4 preprints are up (gives them something concrete to engage with)
- Per Paper D's docstring: Kawahara, Dingemanse, Lockwood are the dream contacts for the registers paper
- Target: 1-2 papers with academic co-authors within 12-18 months

OUTPUT: ongoing strategic anchor. This ticket stays open across the publication cycle and is updated with status.

title: arXiv account setup + endorsement + CC-BY-SA default — DO FIRST
description:
DO NOW. One-time setup that gates everything else. If you wait until the first preprint is ready and then hit the endorsement gate, you lose 3-7 days waiting for a response.

STEPS (~1-2 hours total, mostly waiting):

1. Create arXiv account at https://arxiv.org/user/register
   - Use Devon Jones + a real institutional-style email (e.g. work@521studios.com if available, or personal gmail is fine for indie)
   - Affiliation: '521 Studios' OR 'Independent Researcher' — both work; pick one and stay consistent across all papers
   - Time: ~10 min

2. Get an ORCID identifier at https://orcid.org/register
   - Free, links all your papers under one canonical author entry
   - Add it to arXiv account when prompted
   - Time: ~10 min

3. Set the default license to CC-BY-SA 4.0
   - User profile → submission preferences → license default
   - Confirms each submission can override (some venues will require CC-BY later; default just sets the most common case)
   - Time: ~5 min

4. Get arXiv endorsement for cs.CL (computation + language)
   - First-time submitters to a new category need a current arXiv author in that category to endorse
   - Cold-email candidates (3-4 to try in parallel):
     a. Shigeto Kawahara (Keio, applied phonaesthetics) — kawahara@icl.keio.ac.jp or check his Keio page
     b. Mark Dingemanse (Radboud Nijmegen, iconicity) — mark.dingemanse@ru.nl
     c. Damián Blasi (Harvard, cross-linguistic sound-symbolism) — check Harvard linguistics page
     d. Gwilym Lockwood (UCL, sound-symbolism replication) — check UCL page
   - Email template: 'Dear Prof X, I am preparing a preprint titled <title> for arXiv (cs.CL) on <one-sentence-topic>. Would you be willing to endorse me as a first-time submitter? The work develops methodology in <area-of-your-research>; I attach a brief abstract.' Keep it ~5 sentences.
   - At least one will say yes; takes 1-7 days
   - Also consider endorsement for cs.HC (HCI) or cs.AI if you anticipate cross-listing

5. Cross-list strategy (optional now, useful later):
   - cs.CL is primary for the onomastics work
   - cs.HC for the methodology / cultural-bias-audit angle
   - cs.AI for the generative-systems angle
   - Cross-listing extends visibility within arXiv's category navigation

6. Verify everything works by uploading a draft / test paper as 'unpublished' to confirm the workflow

OUTPUT: arXiv account + ORCID + endorsement(s) in place. Subsequent preprints can be posted within hours (vs days if blocked on endorsement).

This is the lowest-effort/highest-leverage ticket in the publication epic. Doing it first unblocks the next 6 months of work.

title: Paper D: scholarly-grounded phonaesthetic registers with three-tier audit
description:

title: Paper C: cross-language adaptation — donor-to-recipient loanword phonology
description:
~8-12 page paper. The synchronic-language-contact paper. Takes a donor-language lexicon (Old Norse, Norman French, Brittonic, fantasy-substrate like Khuzdul) and adapts each lemma into a recipient-language phonological inventory via documented loanword-adaptation rules.

CONTRIBUTION:
- Cross-language adaptation as a generative operation. Takes lemma X in source-phonology S and recipient-language R, produces adapted form X_R according to documented loanword phonology rules.
- The Khuzdul-as-Norse / Quenya-as-French / Sindarin-as-Goidelic worked example. Demonstrates the same architecture works for fantasy substrate languages — you anchor fantasy lemmas in real loanword-adaptation literature instead of inventing transformation rules ad-hoc.

CONTRIBUTION FOR THE FIELD: bridges procedural worldbuilding with loanword phonology. Most fantasy-naming work invents transformation rules per-project; this approach grounds them in published loanword adaptation patterns. Tolkien's manual approach formalized.

DEPENDS ON: wyrd-v2gm.3.1/.2/.3 (same as Paper B), wyrd-ialp wave-2 corpus expansion (for the donor-language inventories — currently limited to English-default sources; need Old Norse + Norman French + Brittonic + Goidelic etymon corpora). Total gate: 2-4 months at your build pace.

VENUE: Names: A Journal of Onomastics OR Journal of Pragmatics (loanword integration angle) OR Lingua. Possibly JIPA (Journal of the International Phonetic Association) if the loanword-phonology framing is sharp.

- Cite Haugen 1950 'The analysis of linguistic borrowing' — the foundational paper
- Cite Paradis & LaCharité 1997 'Preservation and minimality in loanword adaptation' — the canonical phonological-adaptation reference
- Cite Kang 2011 'Loanword phonology' Wiley review
- Cite Hock & Joseph 'Language History, Language Change, and Language Relationship' on contact-induced change

title: Paper B: through-time etymology — era-staged phonological transformation
description:

- Worked example: take a hypothetical proto-form, project through 4 eras, show the surface forms that would result + alternative outcomes if substrate dialect varies.

CONTRIBUTION FOR THE FIELD: most procedural-name generators produce names at a single time-slice. This paper introduces the operation of taking a generated (or real) name and projecting it backward / forward through historical phonological evolution. title: Cross-domain integration architecture: audit trails + downstream-consumable schemas
description:
The methodological architecture that holds the whole stack together. Each domain emits citation-bearing metadata + downstream-consumable schemas; each subsequent domain consumes upstream metadata via documented contracts. The audit-trail format that lets you say 'this kingdom's economic structure is X because climate is Y because tectonics is Z, citing papers A/B/C at each step.'

THIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING METHODOLOGICAL CONTRIBUTION of the whole research program. Per the meta-epic strategy: individual domain implementations don't have to be world-class; the integration architecture does. This is what 'scholarly-grounded procedural worldbuilding' MEANS in practice.

REQUIRED DELIVERABLES:

1. Audit-trail format specification.
   - Per-feature: 'this feature was produced by mechanism X (citing paper Y at page Z) given inputs U from upstream layer V.'
   - Machine-readable (JSON Schema or equivalent)
   - Human-readable (each generated world has an 'explain why this region is what it is' query interface)

2. Cross-domain schema contracts.
   - Geology→Climate: heightmap + plate metadata + rock-age contract documented and versioned.
   - Climate→Economics: per-tile climate + biome + river-network contract.
   - Economics→Cultural: settlement-graph + trade-network + economic-history contract.
   - Cultural→Onomastics: language-family distribution + substrate/superstrate metadata per region per era contract.
   - Each contract is a published artifact (versioned, with backwards-compatibility policy).

3. Audit-aware querying.
   - 'Why is this settlement here?' should produce a citation chain (climate → biome → arable land → settlement, with paper trace).
   - 'Why does this language family exist here?' should produce a chain.
   - The querying layer is what makes the system AUDITABLE in the formal sense.

4. Cultural-bias auditing generalized.
   - The three-tier UNIVERSAL/IE-CONVENTIONAL/IDENTITY-MARKING move from REGISTERS.md (wyrd-2166) generalizes: every parameter choice in every domain should be tagged with its cultural-assumption provenance.
   - 'This climate-classification system is Köppen, a European-developed taxonomy; an alternative would be Holdridge or local indigenous classifications.'
   - 'This kinship-system taxonomy is Murdock, criticized as Eurocentric; alternative typologies cite Trautmann.'

PUBLICATION OUTPUT:
- The architecture itself becomes a paper (target: a software-engineering-for-research venue, OR the manifesto paper subsumes it)
- Open-source reference implementation across the 4-5 domain layers
- Versioned schema repository (cite-able artifact like a data dictionary)

DEPENDS ON: at least 2-3 domain layers landing (to demonstrate the architecture actually works cross-domain, not just within one layer).

OPTIONAL FUTURE: split this out into a JOSS (Journal of Open Source Software) paper — JOSS specifically accepts research-software papers, exactly the right venue for documenting the integration architecture as a citable artifact.

The publishable contribution is the integration with the geology layer's audit trail + the per-tile climate/biome metadata for the downstream economics layer.

description:
Agent-based economic simulation over the geology + climate + biomes substrate. Produces emergent: settlement patterns, trade routes, regional specialization, wealth distributions, frontier zones, urban-rural gradients.

DELIBERATE QUALITY BAR: 'defensible enough to publish.' Use existing agent-based-modeling frameworks (NetLogo, MASON, Mesa) rather than rolling a bespoke simulator. title: Phase 1 (worldbuild): plate-tectonics-grounded procedural geology with citation trace

description:

We propose <name-the-field>, demonstrate its methodological architecture via onomastics (citing wyrd-kz2b papers), and articulate the open research program across geology, climate, ecology, economics, and cultural geography.'

FOURTH OVER-CLAIM CAUGHT (per .35): wyrd's 'citation chains ARE meaning' framing is overclaim under Bender & Koller 2020 strict reading. SOFTENED FRAMING (drop in verbatim):

title: Paper A: vector-driven generation architecture (ICCC 2027 target)
description:
6-8 page system+evaluation paper. The first peer-review-bound paper in the publication stack.

DELIBERATELY-NARROWED SCOPE: this paper covers the VECTOR-DRIVEN GENERATION ARCHITECTURE specifically — D36.2 canonical composition rule, eligibility gate, per-axis scoring, empirical-priors integration. Through-time evolution, cross-language adaptation, and scholarly-register grounding are EXPLICITLY out of scope; each gets its own paper (B/C/D).

CONTRIBUTION:
- Vector-driven generation as a procedural-content-generation primitive. To our knowledge, this is the first procedural-name generator that uses composable per-axis vector scoring + eligibility-gated candidate pools. Most generators are Markov n-gram, weighted-template, or grammar-based. Vector-driven scoring with separable per-axis composition (D36.2) is structurally different. (Confirm with literature review.)
- Empirical priors from PD scholarly corpus. The generator scores against statistical baselines extracted from real toponym data (EPNS county volumes), not internet name lists.
- Composable register effects. Operators specify combinations like '--register grim,harsh' and the effects vector-sum + clamp into a composed request vector that the per-axis scorers consume.

DIFFERENTIATOR (foreground in paper): not LLM-driven. The PCG / computational-creativity audience is fatigued with LLM-saturation; the architecture is interpretable, deterministic-given-seed, reproducible, and audit-traceable per weight.

REQUIRED EMPIRICAL EVALUATION:
- Statistical baseline comparison vs held-out real-toponym distribution (per wyrd-kz2b.3 ticket): per-tag distribution shift, top-100 morpheme overlap, decomposition-pattern overlap, era-classifier accuracy. Demonstrates the generator produces statistically-plausible output, not just superficially-plausible output.
- Optional but stronger: human-rating Prolific study (per wyrd-kz2b.2 ticket): bipolar-scale ratings on register-claim-vs-perception. Demonstrates the generator's claimed effects align with rated perception.

SECTIONS:
1. Introduction — vibes-driven procedural naming + the LLM saturation; the vector-driven alternative.
2. Background — PCG procedural-naming landscape (Markov, template, grammar); composable register theory; D36.2 composition rule.
3. Architecture — eligibility gate, per-axis scorers, empirical priors, register-effect composition.
4. Evaluation — statistical baseline comparison + (optional) human ratings.
5. Discussion — interpretability, reproducibility, applications beyond fantasy naming.
6. Open-source release — repo + corpus link.

OUT OF SCOPE (explicit in paper to inoculate against salami-slicing accusations):
- Through-time etymology (Paper B, wyrd-kz2b.10)
- Cross-language adaptation (Paper C, wyrd-kz2b.11)
- Scholarly-grounded registers (Paper D, wyrd-kz2b.12)

DEPENDS ON:
- wyrd-ecjp.5 NameGenerator
- wyrd-kz2b.2 evaluation harness OR wyrd-kz2b.3 baseline comparison harness
- wyrd-kz2b.1 arXiv preprint (cited as architectural reference)
